the Dōngjīng Rear-guard Office requested an increase in the number of hostages from its officials and commoners, and a rotation.
The Emperor disallowed it,
saying:
"The various hostages have already each received land and dwellings.
If they were to be rotated again,
there would be constant movement and instability.
They can all remain as they are."
In the twelfth month,
Sòng again sent Mǎ Zhèng to request the land of Xījīng.
In the first month of spring in the fifth year,
Wòlǔ defeated Shílǐgǔdá at Hétálàshān,
executed the four principal culprits,
and pacified all the rest.
In the second month,
Yù and Zōngxióng were dispatched to divide the ten thousand households of the various *méng'ān* and *móukè* from various routes to garrison Tàizhōu.
Pólúhuǒ was placed in command,
and fifty ploughing oxen were bestowed.
On the *yǐchǒu* day, the first day of the fourth month,
Zōnghàn requested to campaign against Liáo.
An imperial edict was issued to the various routes to prepare military matters.
In the fifth month,
the Liáo Commander Yēlǜ Yú Dǔ and others went to Xiánzhōu and surrendered.
On the *xīnsì* day of the intercalary month,
the Guólùn Húlǔ Bójíliè Sāgǎi passed away.
On the *guǐsì* day of the sixth month,
Yú Dǔ and his generals and officials came to meet.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
the Qianhu Húlí Dá was found guilty of unauthorized appointment of tribesmen as Púlíyǎn,
received one hundred strokes of the rod,
and was dismissed.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
an imperial edict appointed Ānbǎn Bójíliè Wúqǐmǎi to assist in governing the state.
Bójíliè Xiáyě was made Húlǔ Bójíliè,
Pújiānú was made Bójíliè,
and Zōnghàn was made Yílái Bójíliè.
On the *gēngchén* day of the seventh month,
an imperial edict was issued to the Xiánzhōu Dūtǒngsī, stating:
"Since Yú Dǔ arrived,
We have clearly seen the circumstances of the Liáo state,
and have already decided to personally lead the campaign.
You should prepare the army to await the campaign date."
Soon after, due to continuous rain, the personal campaign was suspended.
Bójíliè Yù was appointed Commander,
and Yílái Bójíliè Zōnghàn was his deputy,
to lead the army westward.
On the *xīncǒu* day of the twelfth month,
〔一二〕Húlǔ Bójíliè Gǎo was made Commander of all internal and external armies,
with Yù, Zōnghàn, Zōnggàn, Zōngwàng, Zōngpán, and others as his deputies.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
an imperial edict stated:
"The Liáo government is without discipline,
and both heaven and men have abandoned it.
Now We desire the unification of the central and outer regions,
therefore We order you to lead a great army to undertake this punitive expedition.
You must be cautious in military affairs,
select good strategies,
ensure rewards and punishments are carried out,
ensure provisions are continuously supplied,
not disturb those who surrender,
not permit plunder and capture,
advance when it is advantageous,
and not delay the campaign schedule.
In matters requiring expediency,
there is no need to report for approval."
On the *wùshēn* day,
an imperial edict stated:
"If Zhōngjīng is captured,
the acquired ritual music, ceremonial guards, maps, books, and documents
shall all be immediately expedited to the capital."
On the *guǐyǒu* day of the first month of the sixth year,
Commander Gǎo captured the three cities of Gāo, Ēn, and Huíhé.
On the *yǐhài* day,
Zhōngjīng was taken,
and subsequently Zézhōu was captured.
On the *gēngyín* day, the first day of the second month,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the *jǐhài* day,
Zōnghàn and others defeated Liáo Xī King Xiámò at Běi'ānzhōu,
who surrendered.
The Xī tribe's Western Military Governor, Élílà, surrendered with his own division.
On the *rényín* day,
Commander Gǎo sent an envoy to report the victory,
and presented the captured goods and treasures.
An imperial edict stated:
"You and others, leading troops outside,
have fulfilled your assignments,
captured cities and towns,
and pacified the people.
We greatly commend you.
Regarding your suggestion to dispatch generals and officers to call for the surrender of the various tribes in front of the mountains,
We assume they have all been pacified.
Continue to send reports.
If the area behind the mountains is not yet approachable,
then establish fields and graze horses,
and await the autumn harvest
before planning a major campaign.
You must deliberate thoroughly,
and act when it is advantageous.
If you wish for more troops,
report the numbers.
You must not rely on a single victory
and become lax.
Those newly surrendered must be well-treated and preserved.
Proclaim Our intentions to the generals and officers."
Zōnghàn was stationed at Běi'ān,
and dispatched Xīyǐn and others to scout the territory.
They captured the Liáo guard Yēlǜ Xíníliè,
who reported that the Liáo ruler hunted at Yuānyāng Luò,
and because his son, Prince Jìn Xián, was popular among the people,
the ruler hated him and killed him,
causing the masses to become even more disaffected.
Although there were troops from the northwest and southwest routes,
they were all weak.
Therefore, Nòuwǎnwēndū and others were sent to report to Commander Gǎo to advance and attack them.
In the third month,
Dūtǒng Gǎo (都統杲) went out from Qīnglǐng (青嶺),
Zōnghàn (宗翰) went out from Piáolǐng (瓢嶺),
and pursued the Liáo (遼) ruler to Yuānyāngluò (鴛鴦濼).
The Liáo ruler fled to Xījīng (西京).
Zōnghàn (宗翰) again pursued him to Báishuǐluò (白水濼),
but did not catch him,
and captured his treasures.
On the Jǐsì (己巳) day,
they arrived at Xījīng (西京).
On the Rénshēn (壬申) day,
Xījīng (西京) surrendered.
Xīyǐn (希尹) pursued the Liáo ruler in the Yǐshìbù (乙室部),
but did not catch him.
On the Yǐhài (乙亥) day,
Xījīng (西京) rebelled again.
In this month,
Liáo Qínjìnguówáng (遼秦晉國王) Yélǜ Niēlí (耶律捏里) ascended the throne in Yān (燕).
In the fourth month, on the Xīnmǎo (辛卯) day,
they recaptured Xījīng (西京).
On the Rénchén (壬辰) day,
Túdān Wújiǎ (徒單吳甲) and Gāo Qìngyì (高慶裔) were sent to Sòng (宋).
On the Wùxū (戊戌) day,
Dūtǒng Gǎo (都統杲) went from Xījīng (西京) towards Báishuǐluò (白水濼).
Bójíliè Yù (勃極烈昱) attacked Píshìbù (毗室部) in Tiělǚchuān (鐵呂川),
and was defeated by the enemy.
He returned to join the Chálà (察剌) troops,
and pursued them to the north of Huángshuǐ (黃水),
where he inflicted a great defeat.
Yélǜ Tǎn (耶律坦) rallied the various southwestern tribes.
Westward to Xià (夏),
their zhāotǎoshǐ (招討使) Yélǜ Fódǐng (耶律佛頂) surrendered.
The Hàn (漢) army of four thousand men from Jīn (金) Sù (肅) and Xīpíng (西平) prefectures rebelled and departed.
Yélǜ Tǎn (耶律坦) and others attacked and recaptured them.
Shèmǔ (闍母) and Lóushì (婁室) persuaded Tiāndé (天德), Yúnnèi (雲內), Níngbiān (寧邊), Dōngshèng (東勝) and other prefectures to surrender,
and returned with Āshū (阿踈) captured.
At this time,
although the cities and tribes of Shānxī (山西) had surrendered,
the people's loyalty was not yet firm.
The Liáo ruler held Yīnshān (陰山),
and Yélǜ Niēlí (耶律捏里) was in Yānjīng (燕京).
Dūtǒng Gǎo (都統杲) sent Zōngwàng (宗望) to report to the court,
requesting the emperor to personally lead the army.
In the fifth month, on the Xīnyǒu (辛酉) day,
Zōngwàng (宗望) came to report the victory.
All officials entered to congratulate,
and a banquet was given with great joy.
Previously,
the Liáo shūmìshǐ (樞密使) Délǐdǐ (得里底),
jiédùshǐ (節度使) Héshang (和尚), Yǎlǐsī (雅里斯), Yúlíyě (余里野) and others had been captured.
Dūtǒǒng Gǎo (都統杲) ordered Ālín (阿隣) to escort them to the capital.
Délǐdǐ (得里底) escaped on the way,
and Ālín (阿隣) was executed for it.
Yélǜ Niēlí (耶律捏里) sent an envoy to request a cessation of hostilities.
On the Wùyín (戊寅) day,
Yáng Miǎn (楊勉) was sent with a letter to admonish Niēlí (捏里),
to make him surrender.
Móugěshī (謀葛失) sent his son Zūnìguāshī (菹泥刮失) to present local products as tribute.
In the sixth month, on the Wùzǐ (戊子) day, the first day of the month,
the emperor personally campaigned against Liáo (遼),
departing from Shàngjīng (上京).
Ānbān Bójíliè Wúqǐmǎi (諳班勃極烈吳乞買) supervised the state.
On the Xīnhài (辛亥) day,
an edict was issued to the officials and people of Shàngjīng (上京), saying:
"We, in accordance with Heaven, have undertaken a punitive expedition,
and have already pacified the Three Capitals.
However, because the Liáo ruler has not yet been captured,
the military operations cannot cease.
Now, We personally lead the expedition.
We intended to advance via the Shàngjīng (上京) road,
but fearing that it would alarm the newly pacified people
and cause them to lose their livelihoods,
We have instead departed from Dūmìlǚ (篤密呂).
As for those who surrendered earlier but then rebelled and fled into dangerous terrain,
after this edict, if they come forward to surrender,
all their crimes will be pardoned.
If they still resist Our command,
they and their families will be executed without mercy."
In this month,
Yélǜ Niēlí (耶律捏里) died.
Wòlǔ (斡魯) and Lóushì (婁室) defeated the Xià (夏) people at Yěgǔ (野谷).
In the seventh month, on the Jiǎzǐ (甲子) day,
an edict was issued to all generals not to travel far to welcome,
so as not to disrupt military affairs.
On the Yǐchǒu (乙丑) day,
Máo Bāshí (毛八十), a Hàn (漢) man from Shàngjīng (上京), led over two thousand households to surrender,
[一三] and was ordered to command them.
On the Bǐngyín (丙寅) day,
because the number of those persuaded to surrender by Wòdálà (斡荅剌) was large,
he was ordered to command eight thousand households,
with Hūxuē (忽薛) as his deputy.
On the Rénwǔ (壬午) day,
Xīyǐn (希尹) presented Āshū (阿踈) to the emperor,
who had him flogged and then released.
In the eighth month, on the Jǐchǒu (己丑) day,
the emperor arrived at Yuānyāngluò (鴛鴦濼).
Dūtǒng Gǎo (都統杲) led his officials to meet him.
On the Guǐsì (癸巳) day,
the emperor pursued the Liáo ruler to Dàyúluò (大魚濼).
Yù (昱) and Zōngwàng (宗望) caught up with the Liáo ruler at Shílián Duó (石輦鐸),
and engaged in battle,
defeating him.
The Liáo ruler fled.
On the Jǐhài (己亥) day,
the emperor arrived north of Jūyán (居延).
On the Xīnchǒu (辛丑) day,
Zhōngjīng (中京) general Wányán Húnchù (完顏渾黜) defeated sixty thousand Qìdān (契丹), Xī (奚), and Hàn (漢) troops at Gāozhōu (高州).
Bójǐn Máji (孛菫麻吉) died there.
Délǐdé Mǎnbù (得里得滿部) surrendered.
Yù (昱) and Zōngwàng (宗望) pursued the Liáo ruler to Wūlǐzhì Duó (烏里質鐸),
but did not catch him.
In the ninth month, on the Gēngshēn (庚申) day,
the emperor arrived at Cǎoluò (草濼).
Shèmǔ (闍母) pacified the Zhōngjīng (中京) tribes who had previously rebelled,
and persuaded the coastal prefectures and counties to surrender.
Jiédùshǐ (節度使) Yélǜ Shènsī (耶律慎思) led various tribes into the interior.
On the Yǐchǒu (乙丑) day,
an edict was issued to the six tribes of Xī (奚), saying:
"You have surrendered and then rebelled again,
inciting the hearts of the multitude.
Your crime is unforgivable.
However, as the time since your submission is short,
We fear that the methods of pacification have not been fully effective,
and therefore We again order persuasion.
If you can surrender quickly,
your crimes will be pardoned,
and all officials will retain their former positions."
Guīhuàzhōu (歸化州) surrendered.
On the Wùchén (戊辰) day,
the emperor arrived at Guīhuàzhōu (歸化州).
On the Jiǎxū (甲戌) day,
Zōngxióng (宗雄) died.
On the Dīngchǒu (丁丑) day,
Fèngshèngzhōu (奉聖州) surrendered.
In the tenth month, on the Bǐngxū (丙戌) day, the first day of the month,
the emperor arrived at Fèngshèngzhōu (奉聖州).
An edict stated:
"We have repeatedly instructed Our generals and ministers
to pacify and reassure those who have submitted,
and not to disturb them.
However, ignorant common people
still mostly flee and hide in mountains and forests.
To immediately impose military force
is something We deeply cannot bear.
Now, as for the scattered people who have fled,
regardless of the severity of their crimes,
all shall be pardoned.
Those who can lead their multitude to submit
shall be granted hereditary official positions.
Or if slaves surrender before their masters,
they shall all be released as commoners.
Let this be proclaimed,
to make Our intentions known."
Wèizhōu (蔚州) surrendered.
On the Gēngyín (庚寅) day,
Yúdú (余覩) and others sent Wèizhōu (蔚州) surrendered officials Zhái Zhāoyàn (翟昭彥), Xú Xīng (徐興), and Tián Qìng (田慶) to meet the emperor.
Zhāoyàn (昭彥) and Qìng (慶) were both appointed cìshǐ (刺史),
and Xīng (興) as tuánliànshǐ (團練使).
An edict stated:
"Previously, the region of Yōu (幽) and Jì (薊) was invited to submit but refused.
Now, We intend to lead Our army there,
and therefore We first pacify the various tribes of Shānxī (山西).
Since you have already submitted,
you should be treated with greater kindness.
Before officials and people have fully submitted,
regardless of the severity of their crimes and outstanding official debts,
all shall be pardoned and exempted,
and all officials shall be promoted."
On the Dīngyǒu (丁酉) day,
Zhái Zhāoyàn (翟昭彥) and Tián Qìng (田慶) of Wèizhōu (蔚州) killed Zhīzhōushì (知州事) Xiāo Guānníng (蕭觀寧) and others, and rebelled.
On the Bǐngwǔ (丙午) day,
they surrendered again.
In the eleventh month,
an edict was issued to the officials and people of Yānjīng (燕京),
stating that wherever the royal army reached,
those who surrendered would be pardoned of their crimes,
and all officials would retain their former positions.
In the twelfth month,
the Emperor attacked Yānjīng.
Zōngwàng led seven thousand soldiers as the vanguard.
Dígǔnǎi departed from Déshènglǐ,
Yínzhúgē from Jūyōngguān,
Lóushì was the left wing,
Pólúhuǒ was the right wing,
and they took Jūyōngguān.
On the *Dīnghài* day,
they reached Guīzhōu.
On the *Wùzǐ* day,
they reached Jūyōngguān.
On the *Gēngyín* day,
Liáo Army Overseer Dūjiān Gāoliù and others came to offer submission.
The Emperor arrived at Yānjīng,
entered through the south gate,
ordered Yínzhúgē and Lóushì to set up their formations on the city walls,
and then encamped south of the city.
Liáo Zhīshūmìyuàn Zuǒ Qǐgōng, Yú Zhòngwén,
Shūmìshǐ Cáo Yǒngyì,
Fùshǐ Zhāng Yànzhōng,
Cānzhīzhèngshì Kāng Gōngbì,
Qiānshū Liú Yánzōng presented a memorial and surrendered.
On the *Xīnmǎo* day,
the Liáo officials went to the army gate, kowtowed, and pleaded for forgiveness.
An imperial edict released them all.
On the *Rénchén* day,
the Emperor presided over Déshèngdiàn,
and the assembled officials offered congratulations.
On the *Jiǎwǔ* day,
Zuǒ Qǐgōng and others were ordered to pacify and settle the various prefectures and counties of Yānjīng.
An imperial edict to the officials of Xījīng stated:
"When our army arrived at Yāndū,
all has already been pacified and settled.
Only Concubine Xiāo and a few officials fled;
troops have already been dispatched in pursuit.
Should they reach that path,
they are to be captured and brought here."
Huánglóngfǔ rebelled,
and Zōngfǔ suppressed it.
In the seventh year, first month, on the *Dīngsì* day,
Liáo Xīwáng Huílíbǎo presumptuously declared himself emperor.
On the *Jiǎzǐ* day,
Liáo Píngzhōu Jiédùshǐ Shí Lì'ài surrendered.
An imperial edict granted a partial amnesty to Píngzhōu.
Another edict to Ānbānbójíliè stated:
"Previously, Āng was sent to move the people of various tribes to the east of the ridge,
but Āng was disobedient and rebellious,
causing commotion and trouble,
leading to much resentment and rebellion.
For defying orders and losing the populace,
he must be severely punished.
If there is any doubt,
he should be imprisoned and await judgment."
On the *Gēngwǔ* day,
an edict to Zhōngdū Dūtǒng Wòlún stated:
"I hear that you have pacified and settled the people,
each in their own occupation;
I greatly commend this.
Huílíbǎo has gathered followers and defied orders;
you should plan carefully,
and not let it spread."
On the *Rénshēn* day,
an edict was issued to summon and persuade Huílíbǎo.
On the *Guǐyǒu* day,
based on Shí Lì'ài's words, orders were given to pacify and recruit the various tribes.
On the *Jǐmǎo* day,
Song envoys arrived to discuss the territories of Yānjīng and Xījīng.
On the *Gēngchén* day,
Yí, Jǐn, Qián, Xiǎn, Chéng, Chuān, Háo, Yì and other prefectures all surrendered.
On the *Jiǎshēn* day,
an imperial edict stated:
"The tribes of the various prefectures have only recently submitted,
and the people's hearts are not yet settled.
Now that farming season is approaching,
officials in charge of soldiers should be dispatched to explain and instruct them
not to allow soldiers to disturb the people,
so as not to disrupt agriculture."
In the second month, on the *Yǐyǒu* day, the first day of the month,
Sābā was ordered to issue an edict and persuade Xīngzhōngfǔ,
which then surrendered.
Liáo Láizhōu Jiédùshǐ Tián Hào, [一四] Xízhōu Cìshǐ Dù Shīhuí, Qiānzhōu Cìshǐ Gāo Yǒngfú, and Rùnzhōu Cìshǐ Zhāng Chéng all surrendered.
On the *Rénchén* day,
an edict to Ānbǎnbójíliè stated:
"The commanderies and counties are now all pacified.
For those who have fled and not yet surrendered,
their crimes have been forgiven,
and they should be further summoned and persuaded.
For the households and people moved earlier and later,
it has not been long since they left their homes;
how can they not long for their native land?
Local authorities should be ordered
to show deep concern and care for them,
and not to cause any disturbance.
For those lacking food and clothing,
the government shall provide relief and loans."
On the *Guǐsì* day,
an imperial edict stated:
"Previously, due to the ongoing military affairs,
traffic was cut off at the passes and ferries on all routes.
Now that the world is one family,
to still prohibit it
would not benefit the people.
From now on, traffic on the Xiǎn, Xián, Dōngjīng and other routes
is permitted to proceed as convenient.
Those among them who were captured or sold themselves
are all allowed to redeem themselves and become free citizens."
It also ordered that this be proclaimed by express post.
Xīngzhōng and Yízhōu rebelled again.
Song envoy Zhào Liángsì arrived,
requesting an increase in annual tribute in place of the Yān tax,
and to discuss border demarcation, the sending of envoys to congratulate on New Year's Day and birthdays, and the establishment of trading markets,
as well as discussing matters concerning Xījīng and so forth.
On the *Guǐmǎo* day,
Wòlú and Zōngwàng went to Song.
On the *Yǐsì* day,
an edict to Dūtǒng Gǎo stated:
"Talented individuals among the newly attached people
may be recruited and employed."
On the *Wùshēn* day,
an edict ordered the officials of Píngzhōu to jointly divide the territory of Yānjīng's six prefectures with the Song envoys.
On the *Guǐchǒu* day,
a general amnesty was granted.
This month,
Píngzhōu was renamed Nánjīng,
and Zhāng Jué was appointed Liúshǒu.
In the third month, on the *Jiǎyín* day, the first day of the month,
Āng was to be executed,
but due to Xíbùshī's remonstrance,
he was flogged seventy times,
and still detained in Tàizhōu.
On the *Wùwǔ* day,
Dūtǒng Gǎo and others reported that Yélǜ Mázhé had accused Yú Dǔ, Wú Shí, Duólà and others of plotting rebellion,
[一五] and that measures should be taken early.
The Emperor summoned Yú Dǔ and others,
[一六] and calmly said to them:
"I have obtained the world,
all by the concerted efforts and shared virtue of my ruler and ministers, thereby accomplishing this great achievement,
certainly not by your strength alone.
Now I hear that you are plotting rebellion.
If it is indeed true,
then all the saddles, horses, armor, helmets, weapons and the like
shall all be handed over to you;
I will not go back on my word.
If you are captured by me again,
you cannot hope to escape death.
If you wish to remain and serve me,
harbor no disloyal intentions;
I will not doubt you."
Yú Dǔ and the others trembled and could not reply.
Duólà was ordered to be flogged seventy times,
and the rest were all released.
Song envoys Lú Yì, Zhào Liángsì, and Mǎ Hóng arrived with a state letter.
In the fourth month, on the *Dīnghài* day,
Wòlú and Zōngwàng were dispatched to attack the Liáo Emperor at Yīnshān.
On the *Rénchén* day,
a reply letter was sent to Song.
When the army first entered Yān,
Liáo troops again attacked Fèngshèngzhōu.
Línyá Dàshí was twenty-five *lǐ* east of Lóngmén.
Dūtǒng Wòlú heard of this
and dispatched Zhàolì, Lóushì, Mǎhéshang and others to lead troops to suppress them.
Dàshí was captured alive,
and all his followers surrendered.
On the *Guǐsì* day,
an imperial edict stated:
"From now on, if all military matters are centrally reviewed,
there will inevitably be delays.
Affairs concerning this route should be reported to the Dūtǒngsī;
all other matters shall be decided by the Shūmìyuàn."
Qìdān Jiǔjīn gathered a party and caused trouble in Xīngzhōngfǔ.
He was captured,
and Jiǔjīn committed suicide.
Xígǔnǎi and Pólúhuǒ were ordered to supervise the Chángshèng Army,
as well as the prominent families and artisans of Yānjīng,
who were moved inland via Sōngtíngguān.
On the *Jǐhài* day,
they reached Rúzhōu.
Wòlú, Zōngwàng and others attacked Liáo Quánliùyuànsī Hēlíchì at Báishuǐluò,
and captured him.
His relatives, including Qínwáng, Xǔwáng, and fifteen others, surrendered.
Hearing that the Liáo Emperor had left his baggage train at Qīngzǒng,
and with ten thousand soldiers gone to Yìngzhōu,
Zhàolǐ, Bèidá, Zōngwàng, Lóushì, Yínzhúgē and others were dispatched to pursue him.
Zōngwàng caught up with the Liáo Emperor,
engaged in a decisive battle,
and utterly defeated him,
capturing his son Zhàowáng Xíníliè and the imperial seal.
On the *jiǎyín* day of the fifth month,
Zhāng Jué (張覺), the Southern Capital (Nánjīng 南京) garrison commander, rebelled, seizing the city.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
the army reached Yěhú Lǐng (野狐嶺).
On the *jǐsì* day,
they reached Luòlí Luò (落藜濼).
Wòlǔ (斡魯) and others brought Xi Níliè (習泥烈), Prince of Zhào (趙), Línyá Dàshí (林牙大石), Fùmǎ Rǔnú (駙馬乳奴) and others as captives,
and also presented the captured imperial seal.
Zōngjùn (宗雋) brought Qín Wáng (秦王) and Xǔ Wáng (許王), sons of the captured Liáo (遼) ruler,
and the woman Àoyě (奧野) and others to audience.
Tálǎn (撻懶), commander of the Xī (奚) tribes, attacked Sùgǔ (速古), Chuòlǐ (啜里), and Tiěnǐ (鐵尼)'s thirteen *yán* (巖) territories,
subduing them all.
He also dispatched Xī (奚) Mǎ Héshàng (馬和尚) to attack Xiàpǐn (下品) and Dálǔgǔ (達魯古), along with the various tribes of the Wǔyuàn Sī (五院司),
〔一七〕capturing their *jiédù* (節度) Yǐliè (乙列).
Huí Lí Bǎo (回离保) was killed by his subordinates.
On the *xīnsì* day,
an edict was issued to the officials and common people of the Southern Capital (Nánjīng 南京).
On the *rénwǔ* day, the first day of the sixth month,
the army reached Yuānyāng Luò (鴛鴦濼).
On this day,
Zhē Mǔ (闍母) defeated Zhāng Jué (張覺) at Yíngzhōu (營州).
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
His Majesty became unwell,
and decided to return to the Supreme Capital (Shàngjīng 上京).
He commanded Yí Lài Bójíliè Zōnghán (移賚勃極烈宗翰) to be the commander-in-chief,
with Bójíliè Yù (勃極烈昱) and Diébójíliè Wòlǔ (迭勃極烈斡魯) as his deputies,
to station troops in Yúnzhōng (雲中)
to guard the border.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
the army reached Wòdúshān Yì (斡獨山驛).
Ānbān Bójíliè Wúqǐmǎi (諳班勃極烈吳乞買) was summoned.
On the *xīnyǒu* day of the seventh month,
the army reached Niúshān (牛山).
Zōnghán (宗翰) returned to his army.
On the *xīnsì* day, the first day of the eighth month,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
the army reached north of Húnhé (渾河).
Ānbān Bójíliè Wúqǐmǎi (諳班勃極烈吳乞買), leading the imperial clan and all officials, came to pay respects.
On the *wùshēn* day,
His Majesty passed away at the traveling palace west of Bùdǔ Luò (部堵濼),
aged fifty-six.
On the *guǐchǒu* day of the ninth month,
the imperial coffin arrived at the Supreme Capital (Shàngjīng 上京).
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
he was buried southwest of the palace city,
and the Níngshén Diàn (寧神殿) was established.
〔一八〕On the *bǐngchén* day,
Ānbān Bójíliè (諳班勃極烈) ascended the imperial throne.
In the third month of Tiānhuì (天會) 3,
he was honored with the posthumous title Wǔyuán Huángdì (武元皇帝)
and the temple name Tàizǔ (太祖).
His ancestral temple was built in the Western Capital (Xījīng 西京).
On the *xīnyǒu* day of the second month of Tiānhuì (天會) 13,
he was reburied at Hélíng (和陵),
and the stela Kāitiān Qǐzuò Ruìdé Shéngōng (開天啟祚睿德神功) was erected south of Yānjīng (燕京) city, at the place where he once stopped.
In Huángtǒng (皇統) 4,
Hélíng (和陵) was renamed Ruìlíng (睿陵).
In the tenth month of year 5,
his posthumous title was expanded to Yìnggān Xīngyùn Zhāodé Dìnggōng Ruìshén Zhuāngxiào Rénmíng Dàshèng Wǔyuán Huángdì (應乾興運昭德定功睿神莊孝仁明大聖武元皇帝).
In the eleventh month of Zhēnyuán (貞元) 3,
he was reburied at Dàfáng Shān (大房山),
still called Ruìlíng (睿陵).
An encomium says: Tàizǔ (太祖)'s brilliant strategies and sagacious plans
were broad-minded and magnanimous.
He understood people and was good at employing them,
and people were happy to serve him.
Shìzǔ (世祖) secretly harbored the ambition to conquer Liáo (遼).
Therefore, his brothers succeeded each other,
the succession passed to Kāngzōng (康宗),
and then to Tàizǔ (太祖).
Before his death, he entrusted Tàizǔ (太祖) to Mùzōng (穆宗);
such was his long-held ambition.
When he first pacified the Eastern Capital (Dōngjīng 東京),
he immediately abolished Liáo (遼) laws,
reduced rents and taxes,
and implemented the institutions of his own state.
The Liáo (遼) ruler fled,
and Sòng (宋) paid annual tribute.
He ceded the prefectures of Yōu (幽), Jì (薊), Wǔ (武), Suò (朔), etc., to Sòng (宋),
and established the Southern Capital (Nánjīng 南京) in Píngzhōu (平州).
The Sòng (宋) people ultimately could not hold Yān (燕) and Dài (代).
In the end, the Liáo (遼) ruler was captured,
and the Sòng (宋) ruler was seized.
Although his achievements were completed during the Tiānhuì (天會) era,
the grand design and operations truly began from this point.
The Jīn (金) held the empire for one hundred and nineteen years.
In a few years, Tàizǔ (太祖) made no miscalculations,
his armies never paused,
and he established the great enterprise,
passing it on to his descendants.
Alas,
how heroic!
Collation notes
Tàizōng (太宗), honored as Tǐyuán Yìngyùn Shìdé Zhāogōng Zhéhuì Rénshèng Wénliè Huángdì (體元應運世德昭功哲惠仁聖文烈皇帝),
his personal name was Shèng (晟),
originally Wúqǐmǎi (吳乞買),
the fourth son of Shìzǔ (世祖),
his mother was Empress Yìjiǎn Nálǎn (翼簡皇后拏懶氏),
and he was the younger brother of Tàizǔ (太祖) by the same mother.
He was born in the *yǐmǎo* year, the first year of Liáo Tàikāng (遼太康).
Initially, he was an adopted son of Mùzōng (穆宗).
In the seventh month of Shōuguó (收國) 1,
he was appointed Ānbān Bójíliè (諳班勃極烈).
During Tàizǔ (太祖)'s campaigns,
he often remained to guard the capital.
In Tiānfǔ (天輔) 5,
an imperial edict was bestowed upon him, stating:
"You are truly my younger brother by the same mother,
our bond is like one body.
Therefore, I appoint you to assist me in state affairs.
Regarding military matters, if there are transgressions,
investigate their crimes thoroughly
and deal with them appropriately.
For all other matters, great or small,
follow the old regulations of our dynasty."
In the sixth month of Tiānfǔ (天輔) 7,
Tàizǔ (太祖) reached Yuānyāng Luò (鴛鴦濼)
and fell ill.
Upon reaching Wòdúshān Yì (斡獨山驛),
he summoned him to the imperial temporary residence.
An edict stated:
"Now the Liáo (遼) ruler has lost his entire army
and fled to the Xià (夏) state.
The Liáo (遼) officials Tèliè (特列) and Yáoshè (遙設) and others seized his son Yǎlǐ (雅里) and enthroned him.
I have already left Zōnghán (宗翰) and others to manage the situation.
I have been on this imperial inspection for a long time,
and great achievements have been made.
The captured prefectures and territories
require pacification and governance.
Therefore, I shall return to the capital.
In mid-eighth month,
I expect to reach Chūnzhōu (春州).
You, leading the imperial relatives, should welcome me.
It would be even better if you could meet me at Bàozǐ Yá (豹子崖)."
On the *yǐwèi* day of the eighth month,
they met north of Húnhé (渾河).
On the *wùshēn* day,
Tàizǔ (太祖) passed away.
On the *yǐmǎo* day of the ninth month,
Tàizǔ (太祖) was buried west of the palace city.
Guólùn Bójíliè Gǎo (國論勃極烈杲), Yùn Wáng Áng (鄆王昂), Zōngjùn (宗峻), and Zōnggàn (宗幹), leading the imperial relatives and all officials, requested him to formally ascend the imperial throne,
but he refused.
They insisted again,
but he still refused.
Zōnggàn (宗幹), leading his younger brothers, draped the ochre robe over him
and placed the imperial seal in his bosom.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
he ascended the imperial throne.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
he announced sacrifices to Heaven and Earth.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the empire.
The seventh year of Tiānfǔ (天輔) was renamed the first year of Tiānhuì (天會).
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
grain from Chūnzhōu (春州) was distributed
to relieve the surrendered people who had been relocated to the Supreme Capital (Shàngjīng 上京).
On the *wùyín* day,
an edict ordered the *měngān* (猛安) to levy rice
to provide for those households lacking provisions in the interior.
Shē Mǔ (闍母), commander of the southern route army,
defeated Zhāng Jué (張覺) at Lóufēng Kǒu (樓峯口).
On the *rénchén* day of the tenth month,
an edict bestowed one hundred blank appointment slips to Zōnghán (宗翰), commander-in-chief of both the southwest and northwest routes,
saying:
"Now I entrust you with authority over a region.
If there is a need for promotion or transfer, having to wait for my report and approval
might cause delays.
Therefore, act according to your discretion."
On the *jǐhài* day,
monks from Qìngyuán Sì (慶元寺) in the Supreme Capital (Shàngjīng 上京) presented Buddha relics,
but he refused them.
Zhē Mǔ (闍母) and Zhāng Jué (張覺) fought at ●ěr Shān (●耳山),
and Zhē Mǔ (闍母) was defeated.
In the eleventh month, on the day Rénzǐ,
Wánýán Zōngwàng was ordered to investigate Zhāmǔ's crimes,
and to use his troops to attack Zhāng Jué.
On the day Rénxū,
blank commendation certificates and silver plaques were again issued to the military commanders of Shàngjīng Lù, Shígǔnǎi, Pólúhuǒ, and others.
On the day Guǐhài,
Wánýán Zōngwàng's troops, with Zhāmǔ's army, departed from Guǎngníng,
bringing down the coastal prefectures and counties.
An imperial edict was issued to Nánjīng,
ceding Wǔ and Shuò prefectures to Sòng.
Lóushì defeated Xīshān in Shuò Prefecture,
capturing its commander Zhào Gōngzhí.
Bójǐn Wòlúbié and Bólàsù defeated Yǐshì Báidá at Guīhuà.
On the day Jǐsì,
the people from Qiān, Rùn, Lái, and Xí prefectures were relocated to Shěn Prefecture.
On the day Gēngwǔ,
Wánýán Zōngwàng and Zhāng Jué fought east of Nánjīng,
and Zhāng Jué was utterly defeated.
Zhāng Jué fled to Sòng,
and the people in the city seized his father and two sons and presented them,
executing them in the army camp.
On the day Rénshēn,
Zhāng Zhōngsì and Zhāng Dūngù surrendered Nánjīng.
An envoy was sent with Zhāng Dūngù to persuade the city dwellers,
but the envoy was killed, and they rebelled again.
On the day Jǐmǎo,
an imperial edict was issued to the Nǚzhí people:
"Those who previously defected to Liáo
and are now captured again,
shall all be reinstated to their desired residences.
As for their slaves and personal retainers,
even if they fled in the past,
those who can return now
shall all be allowed to become commoners."
In the twelfth month, on the day Xīnsì,
interest on private loans was waived.
An edict stated that from Xián Prefecture southward,
and Sū and Fù prefectures northward,
where the year's harvest was poor,
the military grain that should have been transported to Nánjīng was to be exempted.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
an imperial edict said:
"It has recently been heard that commoners lack food,
to the extent that some sell their children.
They shall be allowed to redeem them by providing labor."
On this day,
Guólùn Bójíliè Gǎo was appointed Ānbān Bójíliè,
and Wánýán Zōnggàn was appointed Guólùn Bójíliè.
Bójǐn Lǐ Jìng was sent to Sòng to announce the emperor's passing.
In the second year, spring, first month, on the day Gēngxū, the first day of the month,
Màn Dūhē was appointed Āshě Bójíliè,
participating in state governance.
On the day Rénzǐ,
Wánýán Zōngwàng and his officers and soldiers were ordered to be rewarded for their meritorious service in conquering Nánjīng,
and Zhāmǔ's crimes were pardoned.
On the day Jiǎyín,
fifty blank commendation certificates and ten silver plaques were given to Wánýán Zōngwàng.
On the day Wùwǔ,
an imperial edict was issued to Bóyǐn Wánýán Āshílái, saying:
"The late emperor, seeing that people of the same clan sold or mortgaged themselves,
ordered officials to redeem them.
It is now heard that some have not yet been restored;
all of them shall be thoroughly reviewed and redeemed."
On the day Guǐhài,
as Dōngjīng had experienced poor harvests for several years,
an edict was issued to reduce land rent and market rent by half.
On the day Jiǎxū,
Zōnghàn and Zōngwàng, the Dūtǒng of the Southwest and Northwest Routes, requested not to cede the prefectures and counties of Shānxī to Sòng.
The Emperor said:
"This violates the command of the late emperor;
quickly give them."
The State of Xià presented a memorial acknowledging vassalage,
and the land south of Yīnshān, north of Xiàzhài, and west of Yǐshì Yēlā Bù Tǔlù Luò was given to it.
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
a letter was sent to Sòng,
requesting the return of captives and defectors.
On the day Dīngchǒu,
postal stations were first established every fifty *lǐ* from the capital to Nánjīng.
In the second month,
an edict stated that those who robbed the Liáo imperial tombs
would be sentenced to death.
On the day Gēngyín,
an imperial edict ordered 700 horses, 1,000 *shí* of seeds, and 7,000 *shí* of rice to be given to Zōnghàn,
to relieve the newly attached people.
On the day Dīngyǒu,
the Dū Bójǐn of Yílǎnlù, Wánýán Zhōng, was ordered to be relocated to Sūbīshuǐ.
On the day Yǐsì,
an edict was issued to the officials of Nánjīng, stating that
all matters, great and small,
must be reported to the military commander,
and none should be directly reported to the imperial court.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
Zōnghàn requested reinforcement,
and an edict ordered the relevant authorities to select 5,000 elite soldiers and give them to him.
On the day Dīngwèi,
Wánýán Zōngwàng was ordered that
for all vacant positions, including the Nánjīng留守 (liúshǒu - military commissioner),
worthy and respected individuals should be selected and proposed,
with their names and official ranks reported.
In the third month, on the day Jǐyǒu, the first day of the month,
Wánýán Zōngwàng was ordered to distribute the annual tribute of silver and silk from Sòng among the meritorious officers and soldiers.
On the day Gēngxū,
the rebel Huóbóndài surrendered,
and an edict pardoned him.
Wánýán Zōngwàng requested to select upright officials to recruit and pacify the people of Qiān, Rùn, Lái, and Xí who were holding mountain fortresses,
and this was granted.
On the day Jǐwèi,
Wánýán Zōngwàng stated that Nánjīng had repeatedly changed allegiance,
and requested that all plans for attack and capture
be decided in consultation with Liú Yànzōng, the Zhī Shūmìyuànshì.
Liú Gōngzhòu and Wáng Yǒngfú abandoned their homes and scaled the city walls to surrender.
Liú Gōngzhòu was made the Yin of Guǎngníng,
and Wáng Yǒngfú was made the Jiédùshǐ of Fèngxiān Commandery.
On the day Xīnwèi,
Lǐ Qiánshùn, the King of Xià State, sent an envoy to present a sworn memorial.
In the intercalary month, on the day Wùyín, the first day of the month,
a sworn edict was granted to Xià State.
On the day Xīnsì,
postal stations were ordered to be established between Shàngjīng, Chūn, and Tài.
On the day Jǐchǒu,
the Wūhǔlǐ and Dílièdǐ tribes surrendered.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
having already agreed to cede the various garrisons of Shānxī to Sòng,
this decision was revoked based on Zōnghàn's words.
In this month,
Xiéyě attacked Yáolián Zhāogǔyá,
putting him to flight,
and captured his wife, children, followers, and prominent clans.
Bójǐn Húnchuò and others conquered Xī Qīyán and pacified its people.
In the fourth month, on the day Jǐyǒu,
for Zōnghàn's strategy against Xīxià and his meritorious service in defeating Liáo,
he was granted ten horses,
from which he could choose two himself,
and the rest were to be distributed among the other commanders.
Relief was provided to the surrendered people of Shàngjīng Lù and Xīběi Lù, and to those newly relocated to Lǐngdōng.
On the day Wùwǔ,
the new city built by Shígǔnǎi in Shàngjīng was named Huìpíng Zhōu.
On the day Yǐhài,
an edict ordered the redemption of over six hundred people who had sold themselves among the households newly moved to Níngjiāng Zhōu in Shàngjīng Lù.
Sòng sent an envoy to offer condolences for the emperor's passing.
Gāo Shùpúgǔ and others were appointed emissaries of national trust for remaining affairs,
and Gāo Xīngfǔ, Liú Xīngsì, and others were appointed emissaries of national trust to announce the emperor's enthronement,
and sent to Sòng.
In the fifth month, on the day Dīngchǒu, the first day of the month,
Shígǔnǎi, the military commander of Shàngjīng, presented twenty-two captured seals and ribbons, and silver plaques.
On the day Guǐwèi,
an imperial edict said:
"Among the newly surrendered people, there are many litigants.
Now is the farming season,
and some might lose their livelihoods.
Their cases can be heard and decided after the farming season."
On the day Dīnghài,
Púlúgǔ, the Méng'ān of Pósù Lù, was dismissed for corruption,
and Xíníliè, the Mǒukè, replaced him.
On the day Yǐsì,
Wánýán Hūlágǔ and others, military commanders of Hélǎn Lù, reported:
"In the past years, we captured sea dogs, gyrfalcons, crows, and falcons in the territory of Gāolì.
Recently, two boats were sent,
but they used fourteen warships to intercept and attack them,
killing everyone on board the two boats
and seizing their weapons."
The Emperor said:
"To start a war over a small matter
is highly inappropriate.
Henceforth, unless ordered,
do not presumptuously go there."
Zhāmǔ conquered Nánjīng,
killing Dūtǒng Zhāng Dūngù.
In the seventh month, on the day Rénwǔ,
Imperial Prince Zōngjùn passed away.
On the day Bǐngxū,
excessive attendance of foreign envoys was prohibited.
On the day Rénchén,
Húshídá said:
"Gāolì is harboring our defectors
and increasing its border defenses,
it must have other intentions."
The Emperor said:
"If they harbor our defectors and do not return them,
the fault lies with them.
For all communications,
do not deviate from the usual customs.
If they come to invade,
arrange your ranks
and engage them.
Those who dare to preemptively attack them,
even if victorious, will be punished."
On the day Yǐwèi,
due to the rebellion of the Wūhǔ tribe and various camps,
Bójíliè Yù and others were ordered to suppress them.
Eighth month, on the *yǐsì* day, the first day of the lunar month,
Bó Jǐn Wūzhǎonǎi and others were appointed as envoys to congratulate Sòng on the Emperor's birthday.
On the *dīngsì* day,
the Méng'ān of Sālígǎi, Chúsī, was dismissed for corruption.
Xījīn Jiānú replaced him.
The Liùbù Dūtǒng, Tàlǎn, defeated and drove away Zhāogǔyá,
killing his unit commanders Hélǔzào, Báisāhé, and others.
He also defeated and received the surrender of various armies from Luòtuoshān, Jīnyuán, and Xīngzhōng.
An imperial edict granted him ten additional silver tablets.
Tenth month, on the *jiǎchén* day, the first day of the lunar month,
the Xià Kingdom sent envoys to express gratitude for the oath-edict.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
on Tiānqīng Jié,
Sòng and Xià sent envoys to offer congratulations.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
an imperial edict ordered the distribution of millet from Níngjiāng Zhōu
to relieve the people of Tàizhōu affected by autumn floods.
Yáoniǎn Zhāogǔyá led his followers to surrender.
Xīngzhōng Fǔ surrendered.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
an imperial edict instructed the authorities to transport fifty thousand *shí* of rice to Guǎngníng,
to supply the garrison troops of Nánjīng and Rùnzhōu.
The Nánlù Jūnshuài, Shēmǔ, was ordered
to reinforce Bó Jǐn Wányán Āshílái of Hésūguǎnlù with one thousand armored soldiers,
in preparation for Gāolí.
On the *wùchén* day,
Wòlǔ, the Acting Dūtǒng of the Southwest and Northwest Routes, reported:
"The Liáo Xiángwěn, Tābùyě, defected and came,
saying that Yēlǜ Dàshí has proclaimed himself King,
appointed northern and southern officials,
and has ten thousand warhorses.
The Liáo Emperor's followers are no more than four thousand households,
with over ten thousand infantry and cavalry,
wishing to advance towards Tiāndé,
and camp at Yúdū Gǔ."
The imperial edict stated:
"Pursuing and attacking the Liáo Emperor
must be done according to circumstances.
As for attacking Dàshí,
we shall await further reports."
Eleventh month, on the *guǐwèi* day,
Shēmǔ captured Yízhōu,
seized Chāyá Shān,
and killed the Jiédù Shǐ, Hán Qìngmín.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
an imperial edict granted fifty thousand *shí* of rice to Tàlǎn and Shígǔnǎi.
Twelfth month, on the *wùshēn* day,
Bó Jǐn Gāo Jūqìng and others were appointed as envoys to congratulate Sòng on New Year's Day.
Third year, first month, on the *guǐyǒu* day, the first day of the lunar month,
Sòng and Xià sent envoys to offer congratulations.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
Hán Zīzhèng, Tóngzhī Xuānhuīyuàn Shì, was promoted to Shàngshū Zuǒ Púyè,
and made Dū Bùshǔ of all palaces.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
the Xià Kingdom sent envoys to offer tribute and congratulate on the enthronement.
Sòng sent envoys to congratulate on the enthronement.
Second month, on the *rénxū* day,
Lóushì captured the Liáo Emperor at Yúdǔ Gǔ.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
the land of Pánggě Chéng was distributed to the relocated Wūhǔlǐ and Wūlièdǐ tribes, as well as the Qìdān people.
Third month, on the *yǐhài* day,
Āshě Bójíliè Màndūhē passed away.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
relief was provided to the newly surrendered Xī and Qìdān people.
On the *xīnsì* day,
Qiányuán Diàn was built.
Wòlǔ presented the Imperial Seal,
and because Móugěshī had come to defect,
requested that he be granted seals and ribbons.
On this day,
Wányán Lóushì was granted an iron certificate.
Fourth month, on the *rényín* day, the first day of the lunar month,
an imperial edict ordered the Liáo Emperor to be sent to the Jīngshī.
On the *dīngsì* day,
Chálà, the Nánlù Jūnshuài, was dismissed for a crime.
Fifth month, on the *jǐchǒu* day,
Xiāo Bājīn captured the Liáo jade seal and presented it.
Sixth month, on the *gēngshēn* day,
on account of capturing the Liáo Emperor,
Lǐ Yònghé and others were dispatched as envoys to announce the victory to Sòng.
Seventh month, on the *rénshēn* day,
internal and external officials and imperial relatives were forbidden from privately conscripting common people.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
the commander of Nánjīng reported that wild silkworms in Jǐnzhōu had formed cocoons,
and presented their silk floss.
An order was given to reward its chief official.
An imperial edict forbade powerful families from buying poor people as slaves.
Those who coercively purchased one person had to compensate fifteen people.
Those who fraudulently purchased one person had to compensate two people.
All were to be flogged one hundred times.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
an imperial edict ordered Nánjīng to confiscate horses kept by wealthy officials,
taking them according to their grade,
and distribute them among the various armies.
Yēlǜ Gù and others were appointed as envoys to convey gratitude to Sòng.
Eighth month, on the *guǐmǎo* day,
Wòlǔ brought the Liáo Emperor to the Jīngshī.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
reported to the Tàizǔ Miào.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
Liáo Emperor Yánxǐ was presented for an audience.
He was demoted and enfeoffed as Hǎibīn Wáng.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
an imperial edict instructed the authorities to select skilled archers and strong, brave men in preparation for Sòng.
Ninth month, on the *rénwǔ* day,
Guǎngníng Fǔ presented auspicious grain.
On the *guǐsì* day,
Jiāgǔsāhé, the Dū Bójǐn of Bǎozhōulù, was executed for his crimes.
Bó Jǐn Túdān Wūliè replaced him.
Tenth month, on the *jiǎchén* day,
an imperial edict ordered all generals to attack Sòng.
Ānbān Bójíliè Gǎo was concurrently appointed Dū Yuánshuài.
Yílái Bójíliè Zōnghàn was concurrently appointed Zuǒ Fù Yuánshuài and vanguard.
Jīnglüè Shǐ Wányán Xīyǐn was appointed Yuánshuài Yòu Jiānjūn.
Zuǒ Jīnwú Shàngjiāngjūn Yēlǜ Yúdǔ was appointed Yuánshuài Yòu Dūjiān.
They were to enter Tàiyuán from Xījīng.
Liùbùlù Jūnshuài Tàlǎn was appointed Liùbùlù Dūtǒng.
Xiéyě was his deputy.
Zōngwàng was appointed Nánjīnglù Dūtǒng.
Shēmǔ was his deputy.
Zhī Shūmìyuàn Shì Liú Yànzōng was concurrently appointed Hànjūn Dūtǒng.
They were to enter Yānshān from Nánjīng.
An imperial edict ordered the construction of a Tàizǔ Miào in Xījīng.
Yēlǔ was summoned to the Jīngshī to teach Nǚzhí script.
On the *wùshēn* day,
the authorities reported that Húshídá, the Acting Nánlù Jūnshuài, and his officials were corrupt and abusive.
An imperial edict ordered an investigation.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
on Tiānqīng Jié,
Sòng and Xià sent envoys to offer congratulations.
On the *dīngsì* day,
Shēmǔ was appointed Nánjīnglù Dūtǒng.
Sǎohē was his deputy.
Zōngwàng was appointed to supervise the battles of Shēmǔ's and Liú Yànzōng's two armies.
On the *rénxū* day,
an imperial edict stated:
"Now that there is a great harvest,
without reserves, how can we prepare for famine?
Therefore, let each *niú* (a unit of land) be taxed one *shí* of grain,
and each Móukè unit shall store it as one *yǐ*."
The Sòng garrison commander of Yìzhōu, Hán Mínyì, surrendered with his army.
He was settled in Yùzhōu.
Eleventh month, on the *gēngchén* day,
it was announced to all within and outside the court, by imperial edict, that the demoted Liáo Emperor was enfeoffed as Hǎibīn Wáng.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
the Nánlù Jūnshuàisī requested a ban on Qìdān, Xī, and Hànrén carrying weapons.
The imperial edict refused the ban.
Zhāng Zhōngsì was appointed Acting Nánjīng Zhōngshū Shūmìyuàn Shì.
Twelfth month, on the *gēngzǐ* day,
Zōnghàn captured Shuòzhōu.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
Zōngwàng's various armies fought against Sòng's Guō Yàoshī, Zhāng Qǐhuī, and Liú Shùnrén at Báihé.
They utterly defeated them.
Púxiàn defeated Sòng troops at Gǔběikǒu.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
Guō Yàoshī surrendered.
All prefectures and counties in Yānshān were pacified.
On the *wùshēn* day,
Zōnghàn conquered Dàizhōu.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
Zhōngshān surrendered.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
Zōngwàng defeated five thousand Sòng troops at Zhēndìng.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
Zōnghàn besieged Tàiyuán.
Yēlǜ Yúdǔ defeated Sòng's reinforcement troops from Hédōng and Shǎnxī north of the Fén Hé.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
Zōngwàng conquered Xìndé Fǔ.
Fourth year, first month of spring, on the *dīngmǎo* day, the first day of the lunar month,
began the morning audience.
The surrendered officials Guō Yàoshī and Dǒng Cái were both granted the Wányán surname.
On the *wùchén* day,
Zōngbì took Tāngyīn.
Dàgǔ attacked and captured Jùnzhōu.
Dígǔbǔ took Líyáng.
On the *jǐsì* day,
all armies crossed the river.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
took Huázhōu.
Zōngwàng sent Wú Xiàomín and others into Biàn,
to demand from Sòng the masterminds behind the pacification of (Yi)shān: Tóng Guàn, Tán Zhěn, Zhān Dù, and Zhāng Jué.
The Sòng Tàishàng Huángdì fled.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
all armies besieged Biàn.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
Sòng envoy Lǐ Zhuó came to apologize,
and requested to restore friendly relations.
Zōngwàng granted Sòng's request to restore friendly relations,
stipulating hostages,
ceding the land of three garrisons,
increasing annual tribute,
and in official documents, referring to each other as "uncle" and "nephew".
On the *wùyín* day,
Sòng offered Kāng Wáng Gòu and Shǎo Zǎi Zhāng Bāngchāng as hostages.
On the *xīnsì* day,
Sòng submitted the oath-document and maps,
referring to themselves as "Nephew Emperor of Great Sòng" and "Uncle Emperor of Great Jīn".
On the *guǐwèi* day,
all armies lifted the siege.
On the *dīngyǒu* day of the second month, the first day of the lunar month,
at night,
Sòng general Yáo Píngzhòng (姚平仲) with 400,000 troops came to raid Zōngwàng’s (宗望) camp,
but was defeated.
On the *jǐhài* day,
the army advanced again to besiege Biàn (汴).
Sòng envoy Yǔwén Xūzhōng (宇文虛中) arrived with a letter,
changing the hostage to Sù Wáng (肅王) Zhū (樞) and
sending Kāng Wáng (康王) Gòu (構) back.
The army returned.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
Huá (滑) and Jùn (濬) prefectures were given to Sòng.
Zōnghàn (宗翰) pacified Wēishèng Jūn (威勝軍)
and captured Lóngdé Fǔ (隆德府).
On the *dīngsì* day,
the army reached Zézhōu (澤州).
The enslaved commoner of the Prince of Hǎibīn (海濱王), Jiānu (家奴), falsely accused his master of wanting to flee.
An imperial edict ordered the execution of the principal culprit,
and the others were flogged.
On the *guǐwèi* day of the third month,
Yínzhúkě (銀术可) besieged Tàiyuán (太原),
and Zōnghàn (宗翰) returned to Xījīng (西京).
On the *guǐmǎo* day of the fourth month,
Zōngwàng (宗望) sent Zōngbì (宗弼) to report a victory.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
Gěng Shǒuzhōng (耿守忠) and others decisively defeated the Sòng army at Xīdū Gǔ (西都谷).
On the *xīnwèi* day of the fifth month,
Sòng’s Zhǒng Shīzhōng (种師中) led troops out of Jǐngxíng (井陘).
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
Wányán Huónǚ (完顏活女) defeated him at Shāxióng Lǐng (殺熊嶺),
beheading Shīzhōng (師中) on the battlefield.
On the same day,
Bálísù (拔离速) defeated Sòng’s Yáo Gǔ (姚古) army at Lóngzhōu Gǔ (隆州谷).
On the *bǐngshēn* day of the sixth month, the first day of the lunar month,
the King of Gāolí (高麗), Wáng Kǎi (王楷), submitted a memorial to declare himself a vassal.
On the *gēngxū* day,
Zōngwàng (宗望) presented three captured elephants.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
Zōngwàng (宗望) was appointed Right Deputy Commander-in-Chief.
On the *bǐngyín* day of the seventh month,
Gāo Bóshú (高伯淑) and others were dispatched to convey an imperial edict to Gāolí (高麗).
On the *rénshēn* day,
a golden plaque was issued,
commanding Bó Jǐn Dàkē (孛菫大●) to lead the eight *méng'ān* of the Bóhǎi (渤海) army under his command as *wànhù*.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
because the head of the Tiělè (鐵勒) tribe, Duólílà (奪离剌), did not follow his brother Kuílíběn (夔里本) in rebellion,
he was bestowed eleven horses, one hundred pigs, and five million coins.
Xiāo Zhònggōng (蕭仲恭) returned from his mission to Sòng,
and presented a secret letter in wax he carried from the Sòng Emperor to Yēlǜ Yúdǔ (耶律余睹).
On the *gēngzǐ* day of the eighth month,
an imperial edict commanded Left Deputy Commander-in-Chief Zōnghàn (宗翰) and Right Deputy Commander-in-Chief Zōngwàng (宗望) to attack Sòng.
Sòng’s Zhāng Hào (張灝) led troops out of Fénzhōu (汾州),
and Bálísù (拔离速) attacked and drove them away.
Liú Zhēn (劉臻) led troops out of Shòuyáng (壽陽),
and Lóushì (婁室) defeated them.
On the *gēngxū* day,
Zōnghàn (宗翰) departed from Xījīng (西京).
On the *xīnhài* day,
Lóushì (婁室) and others defeated Sòng’s Zhāng Hào (張灝) army at Wénshuǐ (文水).
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
Zōngwàng (宗望) departed from Bǎozhōu (保州).
On the same day,
Yēlǜ Duó (耶律鐸) defeated the Sòng army at Xióngzhōu (雄州),
and Nàyě (那野) and others defeated the Sòng army at Zhōngshān (中山).
On the *jiǎyín* day,
Xīnchéng Xiàn (新城縣) presented a white crow.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
Tūniǎn (突撚) captured Xīnlè (新樂).
On the *bǐngyín* day of the ninth month,
Zōnghàn (宗翰) conquered Tàiyuán (太原)
and captured the Commissioner of Military Affairs, Zhāng Xiàochún (張孝純).
Húshāhǔ (鶻沙虎) captured Píngyáo (平遙), Língshí (靈石), Xiàoyì (孝義), and Jièxiū (介休) counties.
On the *jǐsì* day,
Nánjīng (南京) was restored to Píngzhōu (平州).
On the *xīnwèi* day,
Zōngwàng (宗望) defeated Sòng’s Zhǒng Shīmǐn (种師閔) army at Jǐngxíng (井陘),
captured Tiānwēi Jūn (天威軍),
conquered Zhēndìng (真定),
and killed its defender Lǐ Miǎo (李邈).
In the tenth month,
Lóushì (婁室) conquered Fénzhōu (汾州),
and Shízhōu (石州) surrendered.
Púchá (蒲察) conquered Píngdìng Jūn (平定軍),
and Liáozhōu (遼州) surrendered.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
on Tiānqīng Jié (天清節),
Gāolí (高麗) and Xià (夏) sent envoys to congratulate.
Zhōngjīng (中京) presented auspicious grain.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day of the eleventh month,
Zōnghàn (宗翰) marched from Tàiyuán (太iyuán) to Biàn (汴).
On the *bǐngyín* day,
Zōngwàng (宗望) marched from Zhēndìng (真定) to Biàn (汴).
On the *wùchén* day,
Zōnghàn (宗翰) took Wēishèng Jūn (威勝軍).
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
Sālálá Dá (撒剌荅) broke through Tiānjǐng Guān (天井關).
On the *yǐhài* day,
Zōnghàn (宗翰) conquered Lóngdé Fǔ (隆德府).
Huónǚ (活女) crossed the Méngjīn (盟津).
Xījīng (西京), Yǒng'ān Jūn (永安軍), and Zhèngzhōu (鄭州) all surrendered.
On the *gēngchén* day,
Zōnghàn (宗翰) conquered Zézhōu (澤州).
Zōngwàng’s (宗望) various armies crossed the river,
and Línhé (臨河), Dàmíng (大名) two counties, Déqīng Jūn (德清軍), and Kāidé Fǔ (開德府) all submitted.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
Huáizhōu (懷州) was conquered.
On the same day,
Zōngwàng (宗望) arrived at Biàn (汴).
On the *rénchén* day of the intercalary month, the first day of the lunar month,
Sòng sent out troops to engage in battle,
but Zōngwàng (宗望) and others defeated them.
On the *guǐsì* day,
Zōnghàn (宗翰) arrived at Biàn (汴).
On the *bǐngchén* day,
Biànchéng (汴城) was conquered.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
Gāo Suí (高隨) was appointed envoy for the Gāolí (高麗) Birthday celebration.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
Sòng ruler Huán (桓) moved to live in Qīngchéng (青城).
On the *guǐhài* day of the twelfth month,
Sòng ruler Huán (桓) surrendered,
and on the same day,
returned to Biànchéng (汴城).
On the *gēngchén* day,
an imperial edict stated:
“We believe that in our nation,
although the four borders are distant, warfare has not ceased;
although the fields are vast, the furrows have not been opened;
although all crafts are generally established, salaries and ranks are not yet equitable;
although tribute is barely maintained, guest houses are not yet sufficient.
All of these rely on the strength of the people.
If we do not diligently cultivate the fundamental occupations and suppress idlers,
how can both superiors and inferiors be content?
This is impossible.
Therefore, let the local chief officials
diligently encourage agricultural work.”
On the *xīnmǎo* day of the first month of the fifth year, the first day of the lunar month,
Gāolí (高麗) and Xià (夏) sent envoys to congratulate.
On the *guǐsì* day,
Zōnghàn (宗hàn) and Zōngwàng (宗望) sent envoys to present the Sòng surrender memorial.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
Liú Yánzōng (劉彥宗), who held the position of Privy Council Commissioner, submitted a memorial
requesting the restoration of the Zhào (趙) clan,
but it was not heeded.
On the *dīngsì* day,
the Khagan of the Huíhú (回鶻), Hēlǐ (喝里), sent envoys to present tribute.
On the *bǐngyín* day of the second month,
an imperial edict demoted the two Sòng emperors to commoners.
On the *dīngyǒu* day of the third month,
Sòng Grand Tutor Zhāng Bāngchāng (張邦昌) was enthroned as Emperor of Great Chǔ (大楚).
Territory was ceded and bestowed upon the Xià (夏) Kingdom.
On the *yǐyǒu* day of the fourth month,
Shǎn Fǔ (陝府) was conquered,
and Guózhōu (虢州) was taken.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
Tàlǎn (撻懶), Commander-in-Chief of the Six Departments Route, was appointed Left Inspector-General of the Marshal,
and Zhāmǔ (闍母), Commander-in-Chief of the Nánjīng (南京) Route, was appointed Left Supervisor-General of the Marshal.
Zōnghàn (宗翰) and Zōngwàng (宗望) returned with the two Sòng emperors.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
an imperial edict stated:
“Among the various tribes of Hésūguǎn (合蘇館) and the newly attached people,
those who, after their surrender and submission, have married persons of the same surname,
shall be separated.”
On the *gēngyín* day of the fifth month, the first day of the lunar month,
Sòng’s Kāng Wáng (康王) Gòu (構) ascended the throne at Guīdé (歸德).
Sòng killed Zhāng Bāngchāng (張邦昌).
Lóushì (婁室) received the surrender of Jiě (解), Jiàng (絳), Cí (慈), Xí (隰), Shí (石), Hézhōng (河中), Kělán (岢嵐), Nínghuà (寧化), Bǎodé (保德), and Huǒshān (火山) cities.
Tàlǎn (撻懶) campaigned in Shāndōng (山東),
and captured Mìzhōu (密州).
Díhǔ (迪虎) captured Dānzhōu (單州),
and Guǎngxìn Jūn (廣信軍) surrendered.
On the *gēngshēn* day of the sixth month,
an imperial edict stated:
“North of the River,
now that the division has been made,
we again consider that the people may have seen their cities and towns destroyed,
and it is not without doubt and fear,
thus we ordered them to hold fast.
If we were to immediately launch a punitive expedition,
the common people would be pitiable.
Therefore, let us explain with reason,
and recruit and reassure them.
If they persist in not complying,
then a punitive expedition will naturally be launched.
If any of the armies dare to profit from looting or wantonly destroy,
they shall be punished.”
On the *gēngchén* day,
Right Deputy Commander-in-Chief Zōngwàng (宗望) passed away.
King of Hànguó (漢國) Zōngjié (宗傑) also passed away shortly after.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day of the seventh month,
Zōnghàn (宗翰) was granted a charter,
stating that, except for rebellion,
all other offenses would be forgiven and not pursued.
Because Shízhōu (石州) garrison commander Wūhǔ (烏虎) abandoned the city and lost his troops,
he was flogged
and stripped of his office.
In the eighth month, on the day Wùyín,
due to the victory over Sòng,
Yēlǜ Jūjǐn and others were dispatched as Xuānqìng envoys to Gāolì.
On the day Bǐngxū,
Zōngfǔ was made Right Vice Grand Marshal.
An edict stated:
"Many county and prefecture officials in Héběi and Hédōng are absent.
It is appropriate to open up civil service examinations to recruit scholars
to pacify the new populace.
Let scholars from the north and south
each be tested according to their field of study."
In the ninth month, on the day Dīngwèi,
an edict stated:
"In the various circuits of the interior,
for every plough ox, five dòu of grain shall be levied
to prepare for lean years."
On the day Xīnhài,
Wányán Xīyǐn, Right Army Supervisor to the Grand Marshal, and Yínzhúkě, Wànhù, were granted exemption certificates.
Those offenses not pardoned by the amnesty were excluded;
all others were not to be discussed.
Zhēmǔ captured Héjiān,
and heavily defeated Sòng troops at Mòzhōu.
Xióngzhōu surrendered.
Tàlǎn conquered Qízhōu.
Yǒngníngjūn, Bǎozhōu, and Shùn'ānjūn all surrendered.
In winter, the tenth month, on the day Dīngmǎo,
Huólàsǎn Kèhán of the Shāzhōu Uighurs sent an envoy to pay tribute.
On the day Xīnwèi,
on Tiānqīngjié,
Gāolì and Xià sent envoys to offer congratulations.
The two Sòng emperors moved from Yān to reside in Zhōngjīng.
In the twelfth month, on the day Bǐngyín,
Right Vice Grand Marshal Zōngfǔ attacked Sòng,
and plundered the territories of Zī and Qīng.
Wúlíndá Tàiyù defeated Sòng general Lǐ Chéng at Zīzhōu.
Zhàozhōu surrendered.
Ālǐguā plundered the territory of Jùnzhōu,
defeated the enemy troops,
and then captured Huázhōu.
On the day Yǐhài,
Wòlǔ, Commander-in-chief of the Southwest Circuit, passed away.
On the day Jǐmǎo,
Sàilǐ captured Rǔzhōu.
In the sixth year, the first month, on the first day, Bǐngxū,
Gāolì and Xià sent envoys to offer congratulations.
Zōngbì routed Sòng general Zhèng Zōngmèng's army at Qīngzhōu.
Yínzhúkě captured Dèngzhōu.
Sàmóulǔ entered Xiāngyáng.
Bálísu entered Jūnzhōu.
Mǎ Wǔ captured Fángzhōu.
On the day Guǐsì,
Qīngzhōu was conquered.
On the day Guǐmǎo,
Zhēmǔ conquered Wéizhōu.
On the day Dīngwèi,
Dígǔbǔ defeated the troops of Sòng general Zhào Zǐfǎng.
Sālīhē defeated Sòng troops by the river.
On the day Jiǎyín,
Sòng general Mǎ Kuò's troops arrived at Lè'ān;
Zōngfǔ attacked and defeated them.
Hearing that the Sòng ruler was in Wéiyáng,
he returned the army due to the farming season.
Zōngbì defeated Sòng troops by the river.
In the second month, on the first day, Yǐmǎo,
Bálísu captured Tángzhōu.
On the day Guǐhài,
Càizhōu was captured.
On the day Jǐsì,
Yílàgǔ defeated the troops of Sòng general Tái Zōngjùn and others at Dàmíng.
On the day Gēngwǔ,
their army was again defeated,
and Tái Zōngjùn and Sòng Zhōng were captured.
On the day Jiǎxū,
Bálísu captured Chénzhōu.
On the day Guǐwèi,
Yǐngchāngfǔ was conquered.
Zhèngzhōu rebelled and sided with Sòng,
but Zhèngzhōu was recaptured.
The people of Luòyáng, Xiāngyáng, Yǐngchāng, Rǔ, Zhèng, Jūn, Fáng, Táng, Dèng, Chén, and Cài were relocated to Héběi.
Zōnghàn again dispatched Lóushì to attack and capture Tóng, Huá, Jīngzhào, and Fèngxiáng,
and captured Sòng Military Administrator Fù Liàng.
Ālín routed Hézhōng.
Wòlǔ entered Féngyì.
In the third month, on the day Rénchén,
Southern Circuit Army Commander Shígǔnǎi was ordered
to register the various tribes under the command of Jíedùshǐ Wányán Shènsī and the households not yet designated as Měng'ān Móukè, and submit the report.
On the day Jǐyǒu,
Tàlǎn captured Ēnzhōu.
In the fifth month, on the day Wùxū,
Yíshātǔgǔsī came to surrender with his department.
In the sixth month, on the day Jǐwèi,
an edict was issued to solicit records of ancestral affairs.
Tàlǎn sent troops to plunder and capture Cízhōu and Xìndéfǔ.
The bandit from Zhēndìng, who called himself Grand Marshal and Prince of Qín,
was suppressed by Sālīhē.
In the seventh month, on the day Yǐsì,
the Sòng ruler sent an envoy to present a memorial requesting peace,
but an edict was issued to advance the army and attack them.
The two Sòng commoners were sent to Shàngjīng.
In the eighth month, on the day Yǐmǎo,
Lóushì defeated Sòng troops at Huázhōu.
Ètèlà defeated the enemy at the Wèishuǐ River,
and then captured Xiàguī.
On the day Dīngchǒu,
the two Sòng commoners in plain clothes paid respects at the Tàizǔ Temple,
and then had an audience in the Qiányuándiàn Hall.
Their father was enfeoffed as Hūndégōng and their son as Zhònghūnhóu.
On this day,
the event was reported at the Tàizǔ Temple.
An edict on the changes in names and salaries of prefecture and county officials was announced to the entire realm.
In the ninth month, on the day Xīnchǒu,
Shéngguǒ and others defeated Sòng troops at Púchéng.
On the day Jiǎshēn,
they again defeated the enemy at Tóngzhōu.
On the day Yǐchǒu,
Dānzhōu was captured.
In the tenth month, on the day Bǐngyín,
on Tiānqīngjié,
Gāolì and Xià sent envoys to offer congratulations.
On the day Guǐyǒu,
Liú Yànzōng, Administrator of the Bureau of Military Affairs, passed away.
On the day Dīngchǒu,
Púchá Lóushì defeated Sòng troops at Línzhēn.
On the day Wùyín,
Hūndégōng and Zhònghūnhóu were relocated to Hánzhōu.
On the day Gēngchén,
Zōnghàn and Zōngfǔ met at Pú,
and attacked Sòng.
In the eleventh month, on the day Gēngyín,
Púchá and Lóushì captured Yán'ānfǔ.
On the day Rénchén,
Yílǎnlù was relieved.
On the day Yǐwèi,
Púzhōu was captured.
Suídéjūn surrendered.
Lóushì again attacked Jìnníngjūn,
but its defender Xú Huīyán held firm,
and it could not be conquered.
In the twelfth month, on the day Bǐngchén,
Zōngbì captured Kāidéfǔ.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
Zōngfǔ conquered Dàmíngfǔ.
Húshāhǔ defeated Sòng troops at Gǒng.
In the seventh year, the first month, on the first day, Gēngchén,
Gāolì and Xià sent envoys to offer congratulations.
On the day Xīnsì,
Wúguówáng Zhēmǔ passed away.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
Hán Qǐxiān, Western Capital Defender, was appointed Concurrent Chancellor and Administrator of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
In the second month, on the day Wùchén,
Zhé Kěqiú, Sòng Línfǔlù Pacification Commissioner, surrendered with Lín, Fǔ, and Fēng three prefectures.
On the day Jǐsì,
Lóushì, Sàilǐ, Húshāhǔ and others routed Jìnníngjūn,
but its defender Xú Huīyán resisted from the inner city.
On the day Gēngwǔ,
he led his forces to break through the encirclement and flee,
but was captured.
He was ordered to bow,
but did not bow.
He was threatened with soldiers,
but did not move.
He was ordered by the surrendered general Zhé Kěqiú to surrender,
but he pointed at Kěqiú and cursed him loudly,
uttering disrespectful words,
whereupon he was killed.
His commander Sūn Áng and the soldiers all refused to yield,
and were all killed.
On the day Jiǎxū,
an edict prohibited cutting wood or gathering firewood in the Líoyáo Mountains and Imperial Tombs of Yīwúlǘ Shān.
In the third month, on the first day, Jǐmǎo,
there was a sunspot.
On the day Rénnyín,
an edict was issued that since the start of the military campaign,
for good people who were captured and forced into servitude,
their parents, husbands, wives, and children were permitted to ransom them.
Gāo Zhēn, Left Grand Counselor of the Department of State Affairs, was dismissed.
In the fourth month,
Púchá and Lóushì captured Fū and Fāng two prefectures.
In the fifth month, on the day Yǐmǎo,
Bálísu and others raided the Sòng ruler at Yángzhōu.
In the ninth month, on the first day, Bǐngwǔ,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the day Gēngwǔ,
Zōngbì defeated Sòng troops at Suīyáng.
On the day Xīnwèi,
the city surrendered.
In this month,
Cáozhōu surrendered.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day of the tenth month, which was the first day of the month,
Jīngzhào Fǔ surrendered.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
Gǒngzhōu surrendered.
On the *gēngyín* day,
the Tiānqīng Festival,
Gāolí (Goryeo) and Xià (Western Xia) sent envoys to offer congratulations.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
Ālǐ, Dānghǎi, and Dàbì defeated the enemy at Shòuchūn.
On the *jǐhài* day,
Pacification Commissioner Mǎ Shìyuán surrendered the city.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
Lúzhōu surrendered.
On the *gēngxū* day of the eleventh month,
the Hésūguǎn Dūtǒngsī was relocated to Níngzhōu.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
Gāolí sent envoys to present tribute.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
Zōngbì captured Hézhōu.
On the *rénxū* day,
Zōngbì crossed the river
and defeated the Sòng (Song) Assistant Grand Marshal Dù Chōng's army at Jiāngníng.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
the defending official Chén Bāngguāng surrendered the city.
On the *bǐngxū* day of the twelfth month,
Zōngbì captured Húzhōu.
On the *dīnghài* day,
Hángzhōu was captured.
Ālǐ and Púlúhún pursued the Sòng Emperor to Míngzhōu.
Yuèzhōu surrendered.
Dàbì defeated the Sòng Privy Council Commissioner Zhōu Wàng at Xiùzhōu,
and also defeated Sòng forces northeast of Hángzhōu.
On the *wùxū* day,
Ālǐ and Púlúhún defeated Sòng forces at Dōngguān,
and then crossed the Cáozé Jiāng.
On the *rényín* day,
Sòng forces were defeated at Gāoqiáo.
The Sòng Emperor fled to sea.
On the *jiǎchén* day of the first month of the eighth year, which was the first day of the month,
Gāolí and Xià sent envoys to offer congratulations.
On the *dīngsì* day,
Hán Qǐxiān, Concurrent Grand Councilor of the Central Secretariat, was appointed Left Grand Minister of the Department of State Affairs and Concurrent Attendant Censor.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
Ālǐ and Púlúhún captured Míngzhōu
and seized its defending official Zhào Bó'è.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
an edict stated:
"People evading corvée,
who sold themselves to powerful families for a meager price,
shall all be returned to their native districts."
Ālǔbǔ and Xiélǐyě pacified Tàipíng, Shùnchāng, and Háozhōu.
In this month,
Sòng Assistant Grand Marshal Dù Chōng surrendered with his troops.
On the *yǐhài* day of the second month,
Zōngbì returned from Hángzhōu.
On the *gēngyín* day,
Xiùzhōu was captured.
On the *wùxū* day,
Píngjiāng was captured.
As Biànjīng was in turmoil,
on the *dīngmǎo* day of the third month,
Dàdílí recaptured it.
Zōngbì and the Sòng general Hán Shìzhōng fought at Zhènjiāng,
with unfavorable results for Zōngbì.
On the *bǐngshēn* day of the fourth month,
they fought again at Jiāngníng,
and Zōngbì defeated him.
All armies crossed the river.
On this day,
Ālǔbǔ fought at Tuò.
On the *jǐhài* day,
Zhōu Qǐ fought at Shòuchūn.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
Lóushì fought at Chúnhuà.
All were victorious.
Lǐzhōu surrendered,
and then Bīnzhōu was captured.
On the *guǐmǎo* day of the fifth month,
private ordinations of Buddhist monks and nuns were prohibited, as well as marriages between step-parents' children.
On the *wùshēn* day,
an edict stated:
"For the conscripted soldiers from Héběi and Hédōng,
whose family members were displaced to Hénán and captured as slaves,
the officials shall redeem them
and allow them to resume their livelihoods."
On the *rénshēn* day of the sixth month,
an edict ordered the dispatch of ten individuals, including Liáo (Liao) Military Commissioner Yēlǜ Gélǐzhì and Regional Commander Xiāo Biélílà,
to separately govern the newly annexed prefectures and garrisons.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
an edict ordered the six daughters of Duke Hūndé to become imperial clan women.
On the *xīnhài* day of the seventh month,
an edict ordered the provision of fifty sets of armor and helmets to each *móukè* (company) under Bólúhuǒ, the Commander of Tàizhōu.
Lóushì had previously been dispatched to manage Shǎnxī,
but the cities and towns he had pacified frequently rebelled and submitted.
His Supervising General Ālúbǔ requested more troops.
The Marshal's office convened the generals to discuss, saying:
"Our military might is not insufficient;
rather, there is something lacking in the methods of pacification and appeasement.
If someone of high status and prestige, capable of both benevolence and might, were to go,
it could be settled in a short time.
It would be appropriate to send the Imperial Prince, Right Assistant Grand Marshal Zōngfǔ."
This was reported to the emperor.
The edict stated:
"Wherever Lóushì went, he was victorious.
Now, specializing in campaigning in Shǎnxī,
he has been delayed and it remains unsettled.
Is he perhaps weary of war and saving himself?
Guānzhōng and Shǎnxī are vital territories;
you all must exert yourselves there."
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
the Emperor traveled to Tōkyō (Dongjing) Wēntāng.
Duke Hūndé and Marquis Chónghūn were relocated to the Húlígǎi Circuit.
On the *wùshēn* day of the ninth month,
Liú Yù was enthroned as Emperor of the Great Qí (Qi),
who would forever serve as a son to the Jīn (Jin) dynasty,
and established his capital at Dàmíng Fǔ.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
Ānbānbójíliè, Grand Marshal Gǎo, passed away.
On the *guǐhài* day,
Zōngfǔ and others defeated Sòng Zhāng Jùn's army at Fùpíng.
Yàozhōu surrendered.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
Fèngxiáng Fǔ surrendered.
On the *yǐhài* day of the tenth month,
the Emperor returned from Tōkyō.
Emperor Liú Yù of Qí sent an envoy to express gratitude for the enfeoffment.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
the Tiānqīng Festival,
Qí, Gāolí, and Xià sent envoys to offer congratulations.
Tiělí Tūlílà was appointed Concurrent Grand Councilor of the Central Secretariat.
An edict ordered officials of Liáo and Sòng to submit their respective imperial decrees
and exchange them for new appointments based on their ranks.
On the *jiǎchén* day of the eleventh month,
Zōngfǔ pacified Jīngzhōu.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
Wèizhōu surrendered.
Sòng Liú Ní's army was defeated at Wǎtíng.
On the *wùshēn* day,
Yuánzhōu surrendered.
Sòng Jīngyuán Lù Pacification Commissioner Zhāng Zhōngfú and Prefect of Zhènrong Jun Lǐ Yànqí surrendered with their troops.
Mǎ Wǔ and others attacked Sòng Wú Jiè's army at Lǒngzhōu.
On the *gēngxū* day,
Yāozhèn Jiédùshǐ Wūkèshòu and others were appointed envoys for Emperor Liú Yù of Qí's birthday.
On the *guǐhài* day,
Zōngfǔ reported on the situation in Shǎnxī,
and an edict praised and encouraged him.
On the *dīngchǒu* day of the twelfth month,
Wányán Lóushì passed away.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
Zōngfǔ defeated Sòng Liú Wéifǔ's army.
On the *rénchén* day,
Xīzhōu surrendered.
On the *jǐhài* day of the first month of the ninth year, which was the first day of the month,
Qí, Gāolí, and Xià sent envoys to offer congratulations.
On the *wùshēn* day,
an order was issued to grant idle land west of Túmén Shuǐ
and north of the three rivers, Húntuǎnr, Xīngxiǎn, and Chànchǔn,
to the *móukè* (companies) of Hélǎnlù.
On the *xīnhài* day,
Púchá Gúbálǔ and Wányán Tèlǐ attacked Zhāng Wàndí at Báimǎ Hú
and fell into enemy hands.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
Shí Lì'ài, Concurrent Grand Councilor of the Central Secretariat, was appointed Attendant Censor,
and Zhāng Zhōngsì, Administrator of the Bureau of Military Affairs, was appointed Grand Academician of Xuānzhèng Hall and Administrator of the Three Judicial Bureaus.
Zōngbì and Ālúbǔ pacified and settled Gǒng, Táo, Hé, Lè, Xīníng, Lán, Kuò, Jīshí, and other prefectures.
Both the Jīngyuán and Xīhé circuits were pacified.
On the *jǐmǎo* day of the fourth month,
an edict stated:
"For newly relocated border households
who are lacking food and clothing
and have pawned their relatives or slaves,
officials shall redeem them.
For households with only two or three members,
official slaves shall be added to them
to make each household four members.
Those lacking plowing oxen
shall be provided with official oxen,
and officials shall be separately appointed to encourage and supervise farming.
If border households and border garrisons lack provisions,
grain shall be purchased from the people and distributed as relief.
As for border households continuously relocated in the central regions,
they shall be temporarily stopped
and allowed to plant and cultivate in their current locations,
proceeding after the harvest is complete
and reaching their garrison posts in the spring farming season."
On the *bǐngwǔ* day of the fifth month,
envoys were separately dispatched to various circuits to promote agriculture.
On the *rénchén* day of the sixth month,
Duke Hūndé and Marquis Chónghūn were each granted two sets of seasonal clothing.
On the *xīnsì* day of the eighth month,
Huíhú Wēiyù (Uyghur Weiyu) sent envoys to present tribute.
On the *jǐyǒu* day of the ninth month,
Uyghurs of Hézhōu captured Sābā, Dílí, and Tūdié, associates of Yēlǜ Dàshí, and presented them to the court.
In the tenth month, on the day Wùyín,
the Tiānqīngjié (Celestial Purity Festival) was observed.
Qí, Gāolí, and Xià sent envoys to offer congratulations.
Sālìhē attacked and captured Qìngyáng.
Mùwèi surrendered Huánzhōu.
Zōngbì battled Sòng's Wújiè at Héshàngyuán,
and was defeated.
In the eleventh month, on the day Jǐwèi,
Zhào clan's distant relatives were moved to Shàngjīng.
The land of Shǎnxī was bestowed upon Qí.
In the tenth year, in the first month, on the first day Guǐsì,
Qí, Gāolí, and Xià sent envoys to offer congratulations.
On the day Jǐyǒu,
Qí presented a memorial to express gratitude for the bestowed land.
On the day Rénzǐ,
an edict stated:
"In the past, the Liáo people divided the commoners and officials into different classes,
with unequal taxation and corvée.
Let all be made equal."
In the second month, on the day Gēngwǔ,
relief was provided to the Měng'ān people stationed on the border of Shàngjīng Lù.
In the fourth month, on the day Dīngmǎo,
an edict declared:
"If a free woman knowingly marries a slave,
she may remain his wife as before.
If she marries unknowingly,
she may choose to stay or leave as she wishes."
Yíláibó jíliè and Zuǒfùyuánshuài Zōnghàn were transferred to the capital, Jīngshī.
On the day Gēngwǔ,
Tàizǔ's grandson Dǎn was appointed Ānbānbó jíliè;
the imperial prince Zōngpán was appointed Guólùn Hūlǔbó jíliè;
Guólùnbó jíliè Zōnggàn was appointed Guólùn Zuǒbó jíliè;
Yíláibó jíliè and Zuǒfùyuánshuài Zōnghàn were appointed Guólùn Yòubó jíliè concurrently with Dūyuánshuài;
Yòufùyuánshuài Zōngfǔ was appointed Zuǒfùyuánshuài.
On the day Gēngyín,
upon hearing that the Yālù and Húntóng rivers had flooded,
an order was given to provide relief and resettle the border households along the Húntóng River.
In the intercalary month, on the day Xīnmǎo,
an edict ordered the dispatch of Húshāhǔ and twelve others to inspect the able-bodied men in various circuits,
and enlist them for military service.
In the seventh month, on the day Jiǎwǔ,
relief was provided to the border households of Tàizhōu Lù.
The Emperor went to Zhōngjīng.
In the ninth month,
Yuánshuài Yòudūjiān Yēlǜ Yúdǔ plotted rebellion
and fled.
His accomplice, Yànjīng Tǒngjūnshǐ Xiāo Gāoliù, was executed;
Wèizhōu Jiédùshǐ Xiāo Tèmóugé committed suicide.
In the tenth month, on the day Rényín,
the Tiānqīngjié was observed,
and a general amnesty was granted.
Qí, Gāolí, and Xià sent envoys to offer congratulations.
The Emperor went to Xīngzhōng Fǔ.
An envoy from Qí came to report the death of his mother.
In the eleventh month, on the day Guǐhài,
Wǔ Liángmó was appointed as Qí's envoy for condolences and sacrifice.
On the day Guǐwèi,
Sālìhē requested to take the thirteen prefectures beyond Jiàn.
This was granted.
Bùzú Jiédùshǐ Tǔgūsī captured and beheaded Yúdǔ and his sons,
and presented their heads in a box.
In the twelfth month, on the day Gēngzǐ,
Sālìhē captured Jīnzhōu.
The Emperor returned from Xīngzhōng Fǔ.
In the eleventh year, in the first month, on the first day Dīngsì,
Qí, Gāolí, and Xià sent envoys to offer congratulations.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
Sālìhē defeated Sòng's Wújiè at Ráofēng Guān.
On the day Wùchén,
Yángzhōu was captured.
On the day Jiǎxū,
Xīngyuán Fǔ was entered.
In the second month, on the day Jǐhài,
the Yuánshuàifǔ reported:
"Upon receiving the edict to provide relief to the soldiers,
your servant fears that the treasury's funds may not be sufficient.
We request that those with salaries, from the Yuánshuài downwards, contribute money to assist in the provision."
The edict stated:
"The state has its treasuries, why should it take from its subjects?
What kind of principle is this?
Let everything be provided by the state."
In the eighth month, on the day Jiǎshēn,
the Qiánbósī (Finance Department) was established in Huánglóng Fǔ.
On the day Wùzǐ,
Zhào Suǐ falsely accused his father, Hūndégōng, of treason.
Suǐ and his son-in-law Liú Wényàn were executed.
On the day Wùxū,
an edict stated:
"Previously, due to the unsettled military situation,
the Marshal's office was permitted to select and appoint officials independently.
Now, all appointments shall be made by the imperial court."
In the tenth month, on the day Bǐngshēn,
the Tiānqīngjié was observed.
Qí, Gāolí, and Xià sent envoys to offer congratulations.
In the eleventh month, on the day Bǐngyín,
relief was provided in Yílǎnlù.
Zōngbì captured Héshàngyuán.
In the twelfth month, on the day Guǐwèi,
relief was provided in Hélǎnlù.
In the twelfth year, in the first month, on the first day Xīnhài,
Qí, Gāolí, and Xià sent envoys to offer congratulations.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
new regulations and systems were first established and revised,
and an edict was issued to the entire empire.
On the day Bǐngyín,
the Emperor went to Dōngjīng.
In the second month, on the day Dīngyǒu,
Sālìhē defeated Sòng's Wújiè's army at Gùzhèn.
In the fourth month,
the Emperor returned from Dōngjīng.
In the sixth month, on the day Jiǎwǔ,
Ālúbǔ was appointed Yuánshuài Yòudūjiān.
In the tenth month, on the day Gēngyín,
the Tiānqīngjié was observed.
Qí, Gāolí, and Xià sent envoys to offer congratulations.
In the thirteenth year, in the first month, on the first day Bǐngwǔ,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the day Jǐsì,
the Emperor passed away in Míngdé Gōng,
at the age of sixty-one.
On the day Gēngwǔ,
the Ānbānbó jíliè ascended to the imperial throne before the coffin.
In the third month, on the day Gēngchén,
the Emperor was granted the honorable posthumous title Wénliè Huángdì,
with the temple name Tàizōng.
On the day Yǐyǒu,
he was buried in Hélíng.
In the fourth year of Huángtǒng,
the tomb name was changed to Gōnglíng.
In the fifth year,
his honorable posthumous title was further extended to Tǐyuán Yìngyùn Shìdé Zhāogōng Zhéhuì Rénshèng Wénliè Huángdì.
In the eleventh month of the third year of Zhēnyuán, on the day Wùshēn,
he was reburied at Dàfáng Shān,
still known as Gōnglíng.
Eulogy: During Tiānfǔ's initial establishment,
there was no time for matters of rites and music.
Tàizōng entrusted Xiéyě and Zōnggàn with state administration,
and Zōnghàn and Zōngwàng with military affairs.
After destroying Liáo and seizing Sòng,
he immediately deliberated on rites and systems,
regulated the calendar to clarify seasons,
inherited military achievements,
and developed cultural endeavors.
The blueprint for governing the nation
was finally established at this time.
He reigned for thirteen years,
without any additions to palaces, chambers, or gardens.
Finally,
he heeded the advice of his ministers
and passed the throne to Xīzōng,
ensuring that the legitimate lineage of Tàizǔ's successors was not lost.
This can be said to be an extremely difficult act.
Collation Notes
Annals Fourth: Xīzōng
Xīzōng Hóngjī Zànbǔ Zhuāngjìng Xiàochéng Huángdì,
whose personal name was Dǎn,
originally Hélà,
was Tàizǔ's grandson
and Jǐngxuān Huángdì's son.
His mother was of the Púchá clan.
He was born in the year Jǐhài, the third year of Tiānfǔ.
In the eighth year of Tiānhuì,
Ānbānbó jíliè Gǎo passed away.
Tàizōng remained undecided for a long time.
In the tenth year,
Zuǒfùyuánshuài Zōnghàn, Yòufùyuánshuài Zōngfǔ, and Zuǒjiānjūn Wányán Xīyǐn came to court,
and discussed with Zōnggàn, saying:
