"The position of Ānbānbó jíliè has been vacant for a long time.
If it is not settled soon,
we fear it might be given to the wrong person.
Hélà,
the legitimate grandson of the former Emperor,
should be enthroned."
They repeatedly requested this from Tàizōng,
who then consented.
In the fourth month, on the day Gēngwǔ,
an edict stated:
"You are the legitimate grandson of Tàizǔ,
therefore I appoint you as Ānbānbó jíliè.
Do not consider yourself young and immature,
or indulge in childish play;
rather, respect your virtue."
Regarding the Ānbānbó jíliè:
Tàizōng himself once held this office,
and upon ascending to the great throne,
he bestowed it upon his younger brother Gǎo.
After Gǎo's death,
the Emperor decided to designate him as the heir apparent,
hence this appointment.
In the thirteenth year, in the first month, on the *jǐsì* day,
Tàizōng collapsed.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
he ascended the imperial throne.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
an edict was issued to the internal and external administrations.
An edict prohibited alcohol for both public and private consumption.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
envoys were dispatched to Qí, Gāolì, and Xià to announce the mourning and to report his ascension,
and an edict was also issued to Qí, stating that from now on they should refer to themselves as subjects and not as sons.
In the second month, on the *yǐsì* day,
the posthumous title of Empress Tángkuò, the empress of Tàizǔ, was changed to Shèngmù Empress,
and Empress Péimǎn's was changed to Guāngyì Empress.
The posthumous title of Concubine Púsǎn, a consort of Tàizǔ, was changed to Dè Concubine,
and Concubine Wūgǔlún's was changed to Xián Concubine.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
Tàizǔ was reburied at the Hélíng Mausoleum.
In the third month, on the *jǐmǎo* day,
envoys from Qí and Gāolì arrived to offer condolences and sacrifices.
On the *gēngchén* day,
the deceased Emperor was posthumously titled Wénliè,
with the temple name Tàizōng.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
Tàizōng was buried at the Hélíng Mausoleum.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
Zōnghàn, the Guólùn Yòu Bójíliè and Dū Yuánshuài, was appointed Tàibǎo,
given charge of the affairs of the Three Departments,
and enfeoffed as the King of Jìn.
On the *wùxū* day,
an edict granted a banquet to the envoys from various states,
without musical entertainment.
In the fourth month, on the *wùwǔ* day,
envoys from Qí and Gāolì were dispatched to congratulate his ascension.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
Hūndégōng Zhào Jí died.
Envoys were dispatched to offer sacrifices and funeral gifts.
In this month,
sweet dew fell in Xióngyuè Prefecture.
In the fifth month, on the *jiǎshēn* day,
Zuǒ Fù Yuánshuài Zōngfǔ died.
In the ninth month, on the *rénshēn* day,
his imperial father Fēng Wáng was posthumously honored as Jǐngxūan Emperor,
with the temple name Huīzōng,
and his imperial mother Púchá as Huìzhāo Empress.
On the *wùyín* day,
Empress Hèshíliè, consort of Tàizǔ, and Empress Tángkuò, consort of Tàizōng, were both honored as Tàihuáng Tàihòu,
and an edict was issued to the internal and external administrations.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
Huīzōng and Empress Huìzhāo were reburied at Xīnglíng Mausoleum.
In the eleventh month,
Sòng Guówáng Zōngpán, the Shàngshū Lìng, was appointed Tàishī.
On the *yǐhài* day,
the calendar was first promulgated.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
Wányán Xīyǐn, the Yuánshuài Zuǒ Jiānjūn, was appointed Shàngshū Zuǒ Chéngxiàng and concurrently Shìzhōng;
Gāo Qìngyì, the Tàizǐ Shàobǎo, was appointed Zuǒ Chéng;
and Xiāo Qìng, the Píngyáng Yǐn, was appointed Yòu Chéng.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
the Tiānkāi Hall was built at Yáolà.
In the twelfth month, on the *guǐhài* day,
the ceremonies for imperial audiences, banquets, and farewells for Qí, Gāolì, and Xià were first established.
The imperial deer park in Jīngxī was bestowed upon farmers.
In the fourteenth year, in the first month, on the *jǐsì* day, the first day of the month,
the Emperor paid respects to the Tàihuáng Tàihòu at the two palaces.
Envoys from Qí, Gāolì, and Xià arrived to offer congratulations.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
the calendar was promulgated to Gāolì.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
Tàihuáng Tàihòu Hèshíliè collapsed.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
the Wànshòu Festival occurred,
and envoys from Qí, Gāolì, and Xià arrived to offer congratulations.
The Emperor was originally born on the seventh day of the seventh month,
but as this coincided with the death anniversary of his imperial father,
it was changed to the seventeenth day of the first month.
In the second month, on the *guǐmǎo* day,
the honored posthumous title Qīnxiàn Empress was conferred upon her,
and she was buried at Ruìlíng Mausoleum.
In the third month, on the *rénwǔ* day,
Tàibǎo Zōnghàn, Tàishī Zōngpán, and Tàifù Zōnggàn were all given charge of the affairs of the Three Departments.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
an envoy from Gāolì arrived to offer condolences.
In the eighth month, on the *bǐngchén* day,
his ancestors for nine generations and below were posthumously honored as Emperor and Empress,
and it was decreed that the temples of Shǐzǔ, Jǐngzǔ, Shìzǔ, Tàizǔ, and Tàizōng would never be moved.
On the *guǐhài* day,
an edict was issued that for litigation cases between the state of Qí and this dynasty's military and civilians,
documents and transfers for the year
should only use Tiānhuì.
In the tenth month, on the *jiǎyín* day,
Wú Jī was appointed envoy for the Gāolì king's birthday,
and Xiāo Zhònggōng was appointed envoy for Qí's Liú Yù's return gratitude and for the New Year's Day.
In the fifteenth year, in the first month, on the *guǐhài* day, the first day of the month,
the Emperor paid respects to the Tàihuáng Tàihòu at Míngdé Palace.
Envoys from Qí, Gāolì, and Xià arrived to offer congratulations.
The Dàmíng calendar was first used.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
the Wànshòu Festival occurred,
and envoys from Qí, Gāolì, and Xià arrived to offer congratulations.
In the sixth month, on the *gēngxū* day,
Shàngshū Zuǒ Chéng Gāo Qìngyì and Zhuǎnyùnshǐ Liú Sī were found guilty and executed.
In the seventh month, on the *xīnsì* day,
Tàibǎo, in charge of the Three Departments, and King of Jìn Zōnghàn died.
On the night of the *bǐngxū* day,
an earthquake struck the capital.
His imperial uncles Zōngjùn and Zōnggù,
and great-uncle Hūn were all enfeoffed as kings.
On the *dīnghài* day,
excessive enfeoffments and titles for soldiers were curtailed.
In the tenth month, on the *yǐmǎo* day,
Tàlǎn, the Yuánshuài Zuǒ Jiānjūn, was appointed Zuǒ Fù Yuánshuài,
and enfeoffed as the King of Lǔ.
Zōngbì was appointed Yòu Fù Yuánshuài,
and enfeoffed as the King of Shěn.
Shí Lì'ài, the Zhī Shūmìyuàn Shì concurrently Shìzhōng, retired.
In the eleventh month, on the *bǐngwǔ* day,
the state of Qí was abolished,
Liú Yù was demoted and enfeoffed as the King of Shǔ,
and an edict was issued to the internal and external administrations.
The Xíngtái Shàngshūshěng was established at Biàn.
In the twelfth month, on the *wùchén* day,
Liú Yù submitted a memorial expressing gratitude for his enfeoffment.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
an edict changed the next year to Tiānjuàn first year.
A general amnesty was proclaimed.
Hán Fǎng, Yēlǜ Shàowén, and others were ordered to compile the national history.
Xù was appointed Shàngshū Zuǒ Chéng and concurrently Tóng Zhōngshū Ménxià Píngzhāng Shì.
King of Shǔ Liú Yù was transferred to Línhuáng Prefecture.
In the first year of Tiānjuàn, in the first month, on the *wùzǐ* day, the first day of the month,
the Emperor paid respects at Míngdé Palace.
Envoys from Gāolì and Xià arrived to offer congratulations.
The Jurchen small script was promulgated.
Dà Sīkōng Yù was enfeoffed as a king.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
the Wànshòu Festival occurred,
and envoys from Gāolì and Xià arrived to offer congratulations.
In the second month, on the *rénxū* day,
the Emperor proceeded to Yáolà for the spring hunt.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
he visited the Tiānkāi Hall.
On the *jǐsì* day,
an edict ordered the abolition of the Lái Liúshuǐ and Hùntóngjiāng patrol lands,
and that they be given to the people for farming and grazing.
In the third month, on the *gēngyín* day,
the vacant lands of the imperial garden were distributed to the common people.
On the *wùshēn* day,
Hán Fǎng was appointed Hànlín Xuéshì.
In the fourth month, on the *dīngmǎo* day,
Lú Yànlún, the Shàofǔ Jiān, was ordered to construct palaces,
only adhering to frugality and simplicity.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
an ancestral sacrifice was performed at Tiānyuán Hall.
Empress Péimǎn was established as Guìfēi.
In the fifth month, on the *jǐhài* day,
an edict decreed the selection of officials through two examinations: classics and poetic prose.
In the sixth month, on the *wùwǔ* day,
the Emperor returned from Tiānkāi Hall.
In the autumn, seventh month, on the *xīnmǎo* day,
Zuǒ Fù Yuánshuài Tàlǎn and Dōngjīng Liúshǒu Zōngjùn arrived to pay respects.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
the Ànchū Hú River overflowed,
destroying houses,
and many people drowned.
On the *rénwèi* day,
Zuǒ Chéngxiàng Xīyǐn was dismissed.
In the eighth month, on the *jiǎyín* day, the first day of the month,
the official system was promulgated.
On the *guǐhài* day,
the Huíhú dispatched envoys to pay tribute.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
the land in Hénán was ceded to Sòng.
Zhāng Tōnggǔ and others, the Yòu Sī Shìláng, were sent as envoys to Jiāngnán.
The capital was designated as Shàngjīng,
the prefecture as Huìníng,
and the former Shàngjīng as Běijīng.
In the ninth month, on the *jiǎshēn* day, the first day of the month,
Shì was appointed Huìníng Mù,
and enfeoffed as the King of Dèng.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
an edict decreed that for official patents of appointment,
Jurchen, Khitan, and Han people should each use their native script,
and Bohai should follow the Han people.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
the Yānjīng Shūmìyuàn was changed to Xíngtái Shàngshūshěng.
On the *wùxū* day,
the Emperor paid respects at Míngdé Palace.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
Yì was appointed Píngzhāng Zhèngshì.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
the three capitals of Yānzhōngxī and the prefectures and counties of Píngzhōu Dōngxī and other circuits were abolished.
On the *xīnhài* day,
Quán Xíngtái Zuǒ Chéngxiàng Zhāng Xiàochún retired.
In the tenth month, on the *jiǎyín* day, the first day of the month,
Lǐ Déɡù, supervisor of Khitan documents at the imperial front, was appointed *Cānzhī Zhèngshì*.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
Shūzōngqiáng was enfeoffed as Jì Wáng.
Zōngmǐn as Xíng Wáng.
Thirteen sons of Tàizōng, including Hú lǔ bǔ, were enfeoffed as princes.
On the *jǐsì* day,
it was decreed that princes and those below them were forbidden from carrying swords into the palace.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
the system for enfeoffing states was established.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
Zōngjùn, the Grand Guardian of Dōngjīng, was appointed *Shàngshū Zuǒ Chéngxiàng* concurrently *Shìzhōng*,
and enfeoffed as Chén Wáng.
In the eleventh month, on the *bǐngchén* day,
the portraits of Kāngzōng and earlier emperors were completed,
and offered with sacrifices in the Qiányuán Diàn.
In the twelfth month, on the *guǐhài* day,
the new palace was completed.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
Gāolí sent envoys to offer tribute.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
Consort Pēimǎn Shì was established as Empress.
In the second year, first month, on the *rénwǔ* day, the first day of the month,
Gāolí and Xià sent envoys to offer congratulations.
On the *wùxū* day,
on the Wànshòujié (Emperor's birthday),
Gāolí and Xià sent envoys to offer congratulations.
Zuǒ Chéngxiàng Zōngjùn was appointed *Tàibǎo* and oversaw the affairs of the Three Departments,
and his title was advanced to Yǎn Guó Wáng.
Wányán Xīyǐn, the governor of Xìngzhōng, was reinstated as *Shàngshū Zuǒ Chéngxiàng* concurrently *Shìzhōng*.
In the second month, on the *yǐwèi* day,
the Emperor visited the Tiānkāi Diàn.
In the third month, on the *bǐngchén* day,
officials were ordered to meticulously determine ritual regulations.
In the fourth month, on the *jiǎxū* day,
officials attended court,
wearing court attire for the first time.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
Sòng sent envoys to express gratitude for the lands south of the Yellow River.
In the fifth month, on the *wùzǐ* day,
Venus was visible in broad daylight.
On the *yǐsì* day,
the Emperor returned from the Tiānkāi Diàn.
In the sixth month, on the *jǐyǒu* day, the first day of the month,
the Emperor wore the imperial crown and robes for the first time.
On the *xīnhài* day,
Wú Shí plotted rebellion
and was executed.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
the Emperor casually said to his attendants:
"Each time I read the *Zhēnguān Zhèngyào*,
I see the discussions between the ruler and his ministers,
which are very much worth emulating."
Hànlín Xuéshì Hán Fǎng replied:
"This was all due to Tàizōng's gentle demeanor in seeking advice,
and Fáng and Dù and others exhausting their loyalty and sincerity.
Although the book is concise,
it is sufficient as a model."
The Emperor said:
"Tàizōng was indeed a virtuous ruler of his generation,
how about Mínghuáng?"
Fǎng replied:
"Since Tàizōng, among Tang emperors,
only Mínghuáng and Xiànzōng can be counted.
Mínghuáng is what is called 'having a beginning but no end.'
He initially gained the throne through hardship,
employed Yáo Chóng and Sòng Jǐng,
and acted only with rectitude,
thus he was able to achieve the governance of Kāiyuán.
In his later years, he grew lax in handling myriad affairs,
entrusting governance to Lǐ Línfǔ,
allowing sycophants to be employed,
leading to the chaos of Tiānbǎo.
If he had been able to be as cautious at the end as at the beginning,
it would not have been difficult to rival the prosperity of Zhēnguān."
The Emperor praised this.
He further said:
"What kind of ruler was King Chéng of Zhōu?"
Fǎng replied:
"A virtuous ruler of antiquity."
The Emperor said:
"Although King Chéng was virtuous,
it was also due to the assistance of Duke of Zhōu.
Later generations questioned the Duke of Zhōu for killing his elder brother;
in my opinion,
for the grand plan of the state,
it should not be considered wrong."
In the seventh month, on the *xīnsì* day,
Sòng Guó Wáng Zōngpán and Yǎn Guó Wáng Zōngjùn plotted rebellion
and were executed.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
Yòu Fù Yuánshuài Zōngbì was appointed *Dū Yuánshuài*,
and his title was advanced to Yuè Guó Wáng.
On the *dīnghài* day,
an edict regarding the execution of Zōngpán and others was proclaimed throughout the empire.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
Zuǒ Fù Yuánshuài Tàlǎn was appointed *Xíngtái Zuǒ Chéngxiàng*,
Dù Chōng was appointed *Xíngtái Yòu Chéngxiàng*,
Xiāo Bǎo and Yēlǜ Huī as *Xíngtái Píngzhāng Zhèngshì*.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
Xíanzhōu Xiángwěn Yí Wáng Yūn was implicated in plotting rebellion with Zōngpán
and was executed.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
Tàifù, Zōnggàn, who oversaw the affairs of the Three Departments, was appointed *Tàishī*,
continued to oversee the Three Departments as before,
and his title was advanced to Liángsòng Guó Wáng.
In the eighth month, on the *xīnhài* day,
Xíngtái Zuǒ Chéngxiàng Tàlǎn, Yì Wáng Húlǎn, along with Huólí Hútǔ, Tàlǎn's son Wòdài, and Wūdábǔ, plotted rebellion
and were executed.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
Venus was visible in broad daylight.
In the ninth month, on the *wùyín* day, the first day of the month,
the titles of Tàizōng's sons were demoted.
Dà Sīkōng Yù was dismissed.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
the Emperor moved into the new palace for the first time.
The ancestral temple of Tàizǔ was established at Qìngyuán Gōng.
On the *rényín* day,
Sòng sent Wáng Lún and others to request the return of the deceased father and mother Wéi Shì and others;
Wáng Lún was detained and not sent back.
Wēndū Sīzhōng was appointed Imperial Inspector for various circuits.
In the tenth month, on the *guǐyǒu* day,
envoys from Xià Guó came to announce a death.
In the twelfth month,
Yù Guó Gōng Yù passed away.
In the third year, first month, on the *dīngchǒu* day, the first day of the month,
Gāolí and Xià sent envoys to offer congratulations.
On the *guǐsì* day,
on the Wànshòujié,
Gāolí and Xià sent envoys to offer congratulations.
Dū Yuánshuài Zōngbì was appointed to oversee the affairs of the *Xíngtái Shàngshū Shěng*.
In the fourth month, on the *yǐsì* day, the first day of the month,
Wēndū Sīzhōng, inspecting various circuits,
found 124 honest officials, including Dù Zūnhuì,
each promoted one rank,
and 21 corrupt officials, including Zhāng Zhěn, were all dismissed.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
Shǔ Guó Gōng Wányán Yínzhútā passed away.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
the Emperor traveled to Yānjīng.
In the fifth month, on the *bǐngzǐ* day,
an edict ordered the Marshal's Office to retake the lands of Hénán and Shǎnxī.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
an edict officially enfeoffed Lǐ Rénxiào as Xià Guó Wáng.
Dū Yuánshuài Zōngbì was ordered to lead troops from Líyáng towards Biàn,
and Yòu Jiānjūn Sālíhé to lead troops from Hézhōng towards Shǎnxī.
This month,
Hénán was pacified.
In the sixth month,
Shǎnxī was pacified.
The Emperor arrived at Liángxíng.
There was a great drought.
Xiāo Yànràng and Tián Jué were sent to release prisoners in Xījīng.
In the autumn, seventh month, on the *guǐmǎo* day, the first day of the month,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
Zōngbì sent envoys to report victories in Hénán and Shǎnxī.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
an edict allowed civil and military officials of the fifth rank and above to retire,
providing half their salary,
and those of the third rank were still provided with attendants.
In the eighth month, on the *xīnsì* day,
a proclamation of appeasement was issued to the five circuits of Shǎnxī.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
the official ranks of princesses, commandery princesses, and imperial sons-in-law were first established.
In the ninth month, on the *rényín* day, the first day of the month,
Zōngbì came to court.
On the *wùshēn* day,
the Emperor arrived at Yānjīng.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
he personally offered sacrifices at the Tàizǔ Temple.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
Zōngbì returned to his army.
Xià Guó sent envoys to express gratitude for condolences and gifts.
On the *guǐhài* day,
Zuǒ Chéngxiàng Wányán Xīyǐn and Yòu Chéng Xiāo Qìng
were executed, along with Xīyǐn's son Zhāowǔ Dàjiāngjūn Bǎdā and Fúbǎo Láng Màndài.
On the *wùchén* day,
Xià Guó sent envoys to express gratitude for the enfeoffment edict.
In the eleventh month, on the *guǐchǒu* day,
Kǒngzǐ's 49th generation descendant Fán was granted the hereditary title of Yǎnshèng Gōng.
On the *guǐhài* day,
Dū Diǎnjiǎn Xiāo Zhònggōng was appointed *Shàngshū Yòu Chéng*,
and former Xījīng Grand Guardian Áng was appointed *Píngzhāng Zhèngshì*.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
Xíngtái Shàngshū Yòu Chéngxiàng Dù Chōng passed away.
In the twelfth month, on the *yǐhài* day,
Dū Yuánshuài Zōngbì reported that Sòng generals Yuè Fēi, Zhāng Jùn, and Hán Shìzhōng were leading troops across the river;
an edict ordered them to be attacked.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
there was an earthquake.
On the *jǐhài* day,
Yuánshuài Zuǒ Jiānjūn Ālíbǔ was appointed *Zuǒ Fù Yuánshuài*,
and Yòu Jiānjūn Sālíhé was appointed *Yòu Fù Yuánshuài*.
In the first year of Huángtǒng, on the *xīnchǒu* day of the first month,
Gāolí and Xià sent envoys to offer congratulations.
On the *gēngxū* day,
the assembled officials offered the Emperor the honorary title of Chóngtiān Tǐdào Qīnmíng Wǔwǔ Shèngdé Huángdì.
He first wore the ceremonial robes and crown.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
he gave thanks at the Tàimiào.
A general amnesty was declared.
The reign title was changed.
On the *dīngsì* day,
the Wànshòu Jié was celebrated,
and Gāolí and Xià sent envoys to offer congratulations.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
the titles for the empress dowager and other imperial consorts were first established.
The state of Xià requested the establishment of customs markets,
which was granted.
On the *jǐsì* day,
Píngzhāng Zhèngshì Áng was enfeoffed as the Jīshuǐ Jùnwáng.
In the second month, on the *wùyín* day,
an edict was issued that all retired officials whose rank had reached the third grade
should receive half of their salary and labor.
Zōngbì captured Lúzhōu.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
Yēlǜ Yánxǐ, the King of Hǎibīn, was re-enfeoffed as the King of Yù;
Zhào Jí, the Hūndégōng, was re-enfeoffed as the Tiānshuǐ Jùnwáng;
and Zhào Huán, the Chónghūnhóu, was re-enfeoffed as the Tiānshuǐ Jùngōng.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
the Emperor personally offered sacrifices at the temple of Kǒngzǐ,
bowing twice facing north.
He withdrew and said to his attendants:
"In my youth, I was idle
and did not devote myself to study.
As the years passed,
I deeply regretted it.
Although Kǒngzǐ held no official position,
his Way is worthy of respect,
and causes admiration for ten thousand generations.
In general, in doing good,
one must not fail to exert oneself."
From then on, he frequently read the Shàngshū, Lúnyǔ, and various histories of the Five Dynasties and the Liáo dynasty,
sometimes continuing late into the night.
In the third month, on the *jǐwèi* day,
the Emperor hosted a banquet for his officials in the Yáochí Diàn.
It happened that Zōngbì sent an envoy to report a victory,
and many attending officials presented poems to celebrate.
The Emperor, after reviewing them, said:
"In an era of great peace,
culture and military achievements should be valued.
From ancient times, to achieve good governance
has always been through these means."
In the fourth month, on the *bǐngzǐ* day,
Hán Fǎng, the Yin of Jìnán, was made Cānzhī Zhèngshì.
On the *xīnsì* day,
Zōngbì requested to attack Jiāngnán,
which was granted.
In the fifth month, on the *jǐyǒu* day,
Tàishī, Lǐng Sānsheng Shì, and King of Liáng-Sòng Guó, Zōnggàn, died.
On the *gēngxū* day,
the Emperor personally attended.
The court astrologer reported that
it was inappropriate to weep during the *xū* and *hài* hours.
The Emperor said:
"The righteousness between ruler and minister,
and the closeness of flesh and blood,
how can one avoid it?"
Thereupon, he wept bitterly,
and ordered the suspension of court for seven days.
In the sixth month, on the *jiǎxū* day,
an edict was issued for Dū Yuánshuài Zōngbì to consult on matters with the chief ministers.
On the *gēngyín* day,
Xíngtái Píngzhāng Zhèngshì Yēlǜ Huī retired.
On the *rénchén* day,
the relevant authorities requested a musical performance,
but the Emperor disallowed it due to Zōnggàn's recent death.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
King of Wèi, Zōngqiáng, died.
The Emperor personally attended and suspended court as he did for Zōnggàn's funeral.
In the seventh month, on the *guǐmǎo* day,
on the anniversary of Jǐngxuān Huángdì's death,
the Emperor ordered the imperial kitchen to remove meat.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
Zōngbì was appointed Shàngshū Zuǒcéngxiàng concurrently Shìzhōng,
and Dū Yuánshuài, Lǐng Xíngtái, as before.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
Zōngbì returned to the army.
On the *xīnhài* day,
Cānzhī Zhèngshì Yēlǜ Ràng was dismissed.
In the ninth month, on the *wùshēn* day,
the Emperor returned from Yānjīng.
He paid respects to the Tàihuáng Tàihòu at Míngdé Gōng.
An edict granted two bolts of silk and three *jin* of floss
to each of the widowed, lonely, orphaned, and those unable to support themselves.
This autumn,
there was a locust plague.
Dū Yuánshuài Zōngbì attacked Sòng,
crossing the Huái River.
He sent a letter of reproach to Sòng,
and Sòng replied requesting a cessation of hostilities.
Zōngbì, acting on his own discretion, demarcated the Huái River as the border.
In the eleventh month, on the *jǐyǒu* day,
the state of Gāolí sent congratulations on the Emperor's acceptance of the honorary title.
The Jīgǔ Diàn caught fire.
In the twelfth month, on the *guǐsì* day,
the state of Xià sent congratulations on the Emperor's acceptance of the honorary title.
Tiānshuǐ Jùngōng Zhào Huán requested his original official salary,
and an edict was issued to provide relief to him.
Zuǒcéng Xù presented three scrolls of the chronicles of the previous reign.
The Emperor burned incense and received them standing.
In the second year, on the *yǐwèi* day of the first month,
Gāolí and Xià sent envoys to offer congratulations.
On the *jǐhài* day,
the Emperor hunted at the Láiliú Hé.
On the *yǐsì* day,
an order was given to enfeoff Gāolí.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
the Emperor returned from the Láiliú Hé.
On the *xīnhài* day,
the Wànshòu Jié was celebrated,
and Gāolí and Xià sent envoys to offer congratulations.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
Yǎnshènggōng Kǒng Fán died,
and his son Zhěng succeeded him.
In the second month, on the *dīngmǎo* day,
the Emperor went to the Tiānkāi Diàn.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
relief was distributed in the Xīhé Lù.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
the imperial prince Jì'ān was born.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
Sòng envoy Cáo Xūn came and agreed to an annual tribute of 250,000 *liang* of silver and bolts of silk,
to make the Huái River the border,
and that descendants of both sides
would forever abide by the oath.
Liú Yù, King of Shǔ, was re-enfeoffed as King of Cáo.
On the *rénchén* day,
due to the birth of the imperial prince,
a general amnesty was issued throughout the realm.
In the third month, on the *xīnchǒu* day,
the Emperor returned from the Tiānkāi Diàn.
There was a heavy snowfall.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
Zōngbì was appointed Tàifù.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
Zuǒ Xuānhuīshǐ Liú Guō was sent with ceremonial robes, a crown, a jade tablet, and an imperial decree to enfeoff Sòng Kāngwáng as Emperor.
The Emperor's mother, Wéi Shì, and his deceased wife, Xíng Shì, as well as the deceased wife Zhèng Shì of the Tiānshuǐ Jùnwáng, were returned to Jiāngnán.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
Prince Jì'ān was established as the Crown Prince.
In the fourth month, on the *bǐngyín* day,
〔一０〕the subjugation of Sòng was announced to all within and outside the court.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
the Wǔyún Lóu, Chóngmíng Diàn, and other halls were completed.
In the fifth month, on the *guǐsì* day,
the Emperor did not hold court.
From the previous year, the Emperor had become addicted to alcohol,
drinking with close officials,
sometimes continuing into the night.
When prime ministers entered to remonstrate,
he would always offer them wine,
saying:
"I know your intentions,
but since I have already drunk,
I shall be cautious tomorrow."
And then he would drink again.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
the oath edict was bestowed upon Sòng.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
the Emperor hosted a banquet for his officials in the Wǔyún Lóu,
and they all left completely drunk.
In the seventh month, on the *jiǎwǔ* day,
Huíhú sent envoys to offer tribute.
Běijīng and Guǎngníng Fǔ suffered from locusts.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
Zōngbì was granted a golden tally.
In the eighth month, on the *dīngmǎo* day,
an edict ordered the return of Zhū Biàn, Zhāng Shào, and Hóng Hào to Sòng.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
Tàizōng's son Húlú was reinstated as King.
Relief was provided in Shǎnxī.
In the ninth month, on the *rénchén* day,
an edict ordered the provision of salaries to the sons, nephews, sons-in-law, and sons of the Tiānshuǐ Jùnwáng.
In the eleventh month, on the *jiǎyín* day,
Píngzhāng Zhèngshì Jīshuǐ Jùnwáng Áng died,
and was posthumously enfeoffed as King of Yùn.
In the twelfth month, on the *yǐchǒu* day,
the King of Gāolí sent envoys to thank for the enfeoffment.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
Sòng sent envoys to thank for the return of the three coffins and mother Wéi Shì.
On the *rénshēn* day,
the Emperor hunted at the Hèyē Dāimǐ Lù.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
he returned to the palace.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
Crown Prince Jì'ān died.
In the first month, *jǐchǒu* day, of the third year,
due to the mourning for the Crown Prince, the Emperor did not preside in the main hall.
His officials went to the private hall to offer congratulations.
Envoys from Sòng, Gāolì, and Xià went to the Huángjí Hall to offer remote congratulations.
On *yǐsì* day,
the Wànshòu Festival was observed
with the same ceremony as New Year's Day.
In the third month, on *xīnmǎo* day,
Xù, Assistant Administrator of the Left in the Department of State Affairs, was appointed Píngzhāng Zhèngshì.
Zōngxiàn, Grand Commissioner of the Palace Guard, was appointed Assistant Administrator of the Left in the Department of State Affairs.
On *dīngyǒu* day,
the Grand Empress Dowager, of the Tángkuò clan, passed away.
On *jǐyǒu* day,
his son Dàojì was enfeoffed as King of Wèi.
In the fifth month, on *dīngsì* day,
Jīngzhào presented auspicious wheat.
On *guǐhài* day,
the Emperor offered sacrifices to the Grand Empress Dowager.
On *jiǎshēn* day,
the Grand Ancestral Temple and Altars of Soil and Grain were first established.
In the sixth month, on *jǐyǒu* day,
the Xiāoyì Army was first established.
In the seventh month, on *bǐngyín* day,
the Emperor offered sacrifices to the Grand Empress Dowager.
On *gēngchén* day,
Tàiyuán Circuit presented a *xièzhì* and auspicious wheat.
In the eighth month, on *xīnmǎo* day,
an edict granted stipends to the grandson of the Prince of Tiānshuǐ Commandery and the son-in-law of the Duke of Tiānshuǐ Commandery.
On *bǐngshēn* day,
the Old Man Star (Canopus) was seen.
On *yǐsì* day,
the Grand Empress Dowager was given the posthumous title Empress Qīnrén.
On *wùshēn* day,
she was interred in Gōng Mausoleum.
In the twelfth month, on *guǐwèi* day,
there was a solar eclipse.
In the first month, on *guǐchǒu* day, of the fourth year,
envoys from Sòng, Gāolì, and Xià came to offer congratulations.
On *jiǎyín* day,
an edict bestowed the Sòng tribute of the previous year upon the imperial clan members from Shǐzǔ downwards.
On *jǐwèi* day,
Wáng Lún, the Sòng envoy, was appointed as Transport Commissioner for Píngzhōu.
After accepting the appointment,
he later resigned.
For his duplicity, he was punished
and executed.
On *yǐchǒu* day,
Shǎnxī presented auspicious grain with twelve stalks,
each stalk bearing seven ears.
On *jǐsì* day,
the Wànshòu Festival was observed,
and envoys from Sòng, Gāolì, and Xià came to offer congratulations.
On *yǐhài* day,
the Emperor sacrificed to Empress Qīnrén,
weeping with utmost sorrow.
In the second month, on *guǐwèi* day,
the Emperor went to Dōngjīng.
On *bǐngshēn* day,
he stopped at Bǎibóhé Spring Water.
On *dīngyǒu* day,
an envoy from Huíhú came to offer congratulations.
Niánhé Hánnú was sent to respond to him.
In the fifth month, on *xīnhài* day,
he stopped at Xūnfēng Hall.
In the sixth month, on *xīnsì* day,
there was a solar eclipse.
In the seventh month, on *gēngwǔ* day,
the Yuán Ancestral Temple was built in Dōngjīng.
In the eighth month, on *guǐwèi* day,
King Wèi, Dàojì, was killed.
In the ninth month, on *yǐyǒu* day,
the Emperor went to Dōngjīng.
On *rénzǐ* day,
he hunted in Shāhé,
and shot and captured a tiger.
On *yǐmǎo* day,
envoys were sent to sacrifice at the mausoleum of the Liáo ruler.
On *xīnyǒu* day,
an edict granted a one-year tax exemption within twenty *lǐ* of Xūnfēng Hall and within five *lǐ* of the imperial procession's route.
All were granted a one-year exemption.
On *guǐyǒu* day,
Zhāng Xiàochún, Left Chancellor of the Traveling Chancellery, passed away.
In the tenth month, on *rénchén* day,
rewards were established for those lending to famine victims.
On *jiǎchén* day,
due to earthquakes in the various commanderies north of the Yellow River,
an edict granted the common people a one-year exemption.
For those crushed to death with no one to bury them,
officials were to arrange their interment.
In Shǎnxī, Pú, Jiě, Rǔ, Cài, and other places, due to the famine,
migrants who had sold themselves into servitude
were redeemed by the government with silk and restored to commoner status,
then sent back to their hometowns.
In the eleventh month, on *jǐyǒu* day,
the Emperor hunted on an island.
In the twelfth month, on *jiǎwǔ* day,
he arrived at Dōngjīng.
In the first month, on *dīngwèi* day, of the fifth year,
envoys from Sòng, Gāolì, and Xià came to offer congratulations.
On *guǐhài* day,
the Wànshòu Festival was observed,
and envoys from Sòng, Gāolì, and Xià came to offer congratulations.
In the second month, on *yǐwèi* day,
he stopped at Jìzhōu Spring Water.
In the third month, on *wùchén* day,
he stopped at Tiānkāi Hall.
In the fifth month, on *wùwǔ* day,
the Emperor's personally composed small script was first used.
On *rénshēn* day,
due to the remonstrance of Xù, Píngzhāng Zhèngshì,
the Emperor stopped drinking alcohol,
and this was announced to the court officials.
In the sixth month, on *yǐhài* day,
there was a solar eclipse.
In the eighth month, on *wùxū* day,
he departed from Tiānkāi Hall.
In the ninth month, on *gēngshēn* day,
he arrived back from Dōngjīng.
In the tenth month, on *xīnmǎo* day,
Tàizǔ's posthumous title was expanded.
In the intercalary month, on *wùyín* day,
Dàmíng Prefecture presented an ox that gave birth to a *lín*.
On *rénchén* day,
Huáizhōu presented auspicious grain.
In the twelfth month, on *wùshēn* day,
the posthumous titles of the ten emperors from Shǐzǔ downwards, as well as Tàizōng and Huīzōng, were expanded.
On *dīngsì* day,
a general amnesty was proclaimed.
In the first month, on *xīnwèi* day, of the sixth year,
envoys from Sòng, Gāolì, and Xià came to offer congratulations.
On *rénshēn* day,
Tàizǔ's grandsons were enfeoffed as kings.
On *yǐhài* day,
he hunted at Móulè.
On *jiǎshēn* day,
he returned to the capital.
On *dīnghài* day,
the Wànshòu Festival was observed,
and envoys from Sòng, Gāolì, and Xià came to offer congratulations.
On *gēngyín* day,
borderlands were bestowed upon the Xià kingdom.
On *rénchén* day,
he went to Spring Water.
The Emperor pursued game,
and his guide mistakenly led his cavalry into a great marsh.
The Emperor's horse became stuck,
so he dismounted and walked out,
but did not punish the guide.
On *yǐwèi* day,
Wēihē was enfeoffed as a king.
In the second month, on *bǐngyín* day,
Hán Qǐxiān, Right Chancellor, passed away.
In the third month, on *rénshēn* day,
Ālíbǔ was appointed Right Chancellor of the Traveling Chancellery.
In the fourth month, on *gēngzǐ* day,
the Emperor arrived back from Spring Water.
Zōnggù, acting co-administrator of the Imperial Clan Court, was appointed Grand Tutor and Right Chancellor concurrently Minister of the Secretariat.
On *wùwǔ* day,
Ālíbǔ, Right Chancellor of the Traveling Chancellery, passed away.
In the fifth month, on *rénshēn* day,
Kǎi, King of Gāolì, passed away.
On *xīnmǎo* day,
Liú Kè, Left Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, was appointed Right Chancellor of the Traveling Chancellery.
In the sixth month, on *yǐsì* day,
Yǔwén Xūzhōng and Gāo Shìtán were killed.
On *yǐchǒu* day,
envoys were sent to offer condolences and sacrifices to Gāolì,
and to reinstate the heir apparent, Xiàn.
In the ninth month, on *wùchén* day,
due to Xǔ Wáng's capture of Biàn,
Ruìzōng's pacification of Shǎnxī,
Zhèng Wáng's conquest of Liáo, and Lóushì and Yínshùkě all having great achievements,
steles were erected for them all.
On *wùyín* day,
Liú Yù, Prince of Cáo, passed away.
In this year,
Niángē Hánnú was sent to summon Yélǜ Dàshí,
but was killed.
In the first month, on *yǐchǒu* day, of the seventh year,
envoys from Sòng, Gāolì, and Xià came to offer congratulations.
On *xīnsì* day,
the Wànshòu Festival was observed,
and envoys from Sòng, Gāolì, and Xià came to offer congratulations.
On *guǐwèi* day,
the deer park in Xījīng was converted into farmland for the people.
On *dīnghài* day,
Venus traversed the sky.
In the third month, on *wùyín* day,
Gāolì sent envoys to express gratitude for the condolences, sacrifices, and reinstatement.
In the fourth month, on *wùwǔ* day,
a banquet was held in the private hall.
The Emperor became drunk
and killed Zōnglǐ, Minister of Revenue.
In the sixth month, on *dīngyǒu* day,

Tián Jué, Military Commissioner of Hēnghǎi Army; Xī Yì, Director of the Left Bureau of Operations; Xíng Jùzhān, Hanlin Academician in Waiting; and Wáng Zhí, Gāo Fèngtíng, Wáng Xiào, Zhào Yìxīng, Gōng Yíjiàn, and others were killed.
In the seventh month, on *jǐsì* day,
Venus traversed the sky,
and a partial amnesty was granted within the capital region.
In the ninth month,
Tàibǎo (Grand Protector) and Yòuchéngxiàng (Right Chancellor) Zōnggù passed away.
Zōngbì, the Dūyuánshuài (Grand Marshal), was appointed Tàishī (Grand Preceptor) and Líng Sānxǐng Shì (Controller of the Three Departments),
retaining his former positions as Dūyuánshuài and Xíngtái Shàngshūshěng Shì (Acting Executive of the Department of State Affairs).
Píngzhāng Zhèngshì (Councillor of State) Xù was made Zuǒchéngxiàng (Left Chancellor) concurrently Shìzhōng (Palace Attendant).
Dūdiǎnjiǎn (Chief Inspector) Zōngxián was made Yòuchéngxiàng (Right Chancellor) concurrently Zhōngshūlìng (Director of the Central Secretariat).
Xíngtái Yòuchéngxiàng (Acting Right Chancellor) Liúkuì and Yòuchéng (Right Assistant) Xiāo Zhònggōng were made Píngzhāng Zhèngshì.
Lǐ Déɡù was made Shàngshū Yòuchéng (Right Assistant of the Department of State Affairs).
Mìshūjiān (Director of the Palace Library) Xiāo Yì was made Cānzhī Zhèngshì (Participating in Determining Governmental Affairs).
On the *rénzǐ* day of the tenth month,
Píngzhāng Xíngtái Shàngshūshěng Shì (Councillor of State and Acting Executive of the Department of State Affairs) Xī Bǎo passed away.
On the *guǐyǒu* day of the eleventh month,
Púsǎn Tàiwān, the Gōngbù Shìláng (Vice Minister of Works), was appointed Yùshǐ Dàfū (Grand Censor).
On the *yǐhài* day,
Bīngbù Shàngshū (Minister of War) Bǐngdé presented a three-horned sheep.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
an edict was issued to reduce the daily ration of sheep and pigs by two-fifths.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
Shàngshū Zuǒchéng (Left Assistant of the Department of State Affairs) Zōngxiàn was appointed Xíngtái Píngzhāng Zhèngshì (Acting Councillor of State).
Liàng, who concurrently served as Pàn Dàzōngzhèng Shì (Judge of the Imperial Clan Court), was appointed Shàngshū Zuǒchéng (Left Assistant of the Department of State Affairs).
On the *wùwǔ* day of the twelfth month,
Cānzhī Zhèngshì (Participating in Determining Governmental Affairs) Hán Fǎng was dismissed.
Bīngbù Shàngshū (Minister of War) Bǐngdé was appointed Cānzhī Zhèngshì.
In the first month, on the *gēngshēn* day, the first day of the eighth year,
envoys from Sòng, Gāolí, and Xià came to offer congratulations.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
during the Wànshòu Jié (Emperor's Birthday),
envoys from Sòng, Gāolí, and Xià came to offer congratulations.
On the *rénzǐ* day of the second month,
Gēlǔgé Bōgǔ and others were appointed envoys to bestow gifts upon Gāolí and Xià kingdoms.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
Dàlǐ Qīng (Minister of the Court of Judicial Review) Zōng'ān and others were appointed envoys to enfeoff and enthrone King Xiàn of Gāolí.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
the Emperor went to Tiānkāi Diàn (Hall of Heavenly Opening).
On the *wùzǐ* day, the first day of the fourth month,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
Cānzhī Zhèngshì (Participating in Determining Governmental Affairs) Bǐngdé and others were dispatched to inspect officials.
On the *gēngxū* day,
the Emperor returned from Tiānkāi Diàn.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
the *History of Liáo* was completed.
On the *yǐmǎo* day of the sixth month,
Píngzhāng Zhèngshì (Councillor of State) Xiāo Zhònggōng was made Xíngtái Zuǒchéngxiàng (Acting Left Chancellor).
Zuǒchéng (Left Assistant) Liàng was made Píngzhāng Zhèngshì.
Dūdiǎnjiǎn (Chief Inspector) Tángkuò Biàn was made Shàngshū Zuǒchéng (Left Assistant of the Department of State Affairs).
〔一四〕The King of Gāolí sent an envoy to express gratitude for the enfeoffment and enthronement.
On the *yǐhài* day of the seventh month,
Yùshǐ Dàfū (Grand Censor) Púsǎn Tàiwān was dismissed.
Ālúdài, the Shìwèi Qīnjūn Dūzhīhuīshǐ (Commander-in-Chief of the Palace Guards), was appointed Yùshǐ Dàfū.
On the *wùyín* day,
Shàngshū Zuǒchéng (Left Assistant of the Department of State Affairs) Tángkuò Biàn was flogged
for negligence in his duties.
On the *wùxū* day of the eighth month,
Zōngbì presented the *Shílù* (Veritable Records) of Tàizǔ (Emperor Tàizǔ),
and the Emperor, burning incense, stood to receive it.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
Shàngshū Zuǒchéngxiàng (Left Chancellor of the Department of State Affairs) Xù was appointed Líng Xíngtái Shàngshūshěng Shì (Controller of the Acting Department of State Affairs).
Yòuchéngxiàng (Right Chancellor) Zōngxián was made Tàibǎo (Grand Protector) and Shàngshū Zuǒchéngxiàng.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
Xíngtái Zuǒchéngxiàng (Acting Left Chancellor) Xiāo Zhònggōng was appointed Shàngshū Yòuchéngxiàng (Right Chancellor of the Department of State Affairs).
On the *gēngshēn* day of the intercalary month,
the prime ministers requested the Emperor to hunt
in Xīlín due to the abundance of deer.
The Emperor, fearing damage to the crops,
did not approve.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
the Tàimiào (Imperial Ancestral Temple) was completed.
On the *bǐngshēn* day of the ninth month,
Shàngshū Zuǒchéng (Left Assistant of the Department of State Affairs) Tángkuò Biàn was dismissed.
Bǐng, the Zuǒxuānhuīshǐ (Left Commissioner of Military Affairs), was appointed Shàngshū Zuǒchéng.
On the *xīnyǒu* day of the tenth month,
Tàishī (Grand Preceptor), Líng Sānxǐng Shì (Controller of the Three Departments), Dūyuánshuài (Grand Marshal), and Yuè Guówáng (King of Yuè) Zōngbì passed away.
On the *rénchén* day of the eleventh month,
Venus traversed the sky.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
Zuǒchéngxiàng (Left Chancellor) Zōngxián and Zuǒchéng (Left Assistant) Bǐng and others stated
that chief officials of prefectures and commanderies should all be appointed from people of this country.
The Emperor said:
"Within the Four Seas,
all are my subjects.
If they are treated discriminatorily,
how can unity be achieved?
Does the proverb not say,
'Do not use a person you doubt;
do not doubt a person you use'?
From now on, people from this country and all other groups
shall be employed universally according to their talents."
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
Shàngshū Zuǒchéngxiàng (Left Chancellor of the Department of State Affairs) Zōngxián was appointed Zuǒfùyuánshuài (Left Deputy Marshal).
Píngzhāng Zhèngshì (Councillor of State) Liàng was appointed Shàngshū Zuǒchéngxiàng concurrently Shìzhōng (Palace Attendant).
Cānzhī Zhèngshì (Participating in Determining Governmental Affairs) Bǐngdé was appointed Píngzhāng Zhèngshì.
On the *gēngxū* day,
Zuǒfùyuánshuài Zōngxián was reinstated as Tàibǎo (Grand Protector),
retaining his former positions as Zuǒchéngxiàng and Zuǒfùyuánshuài.
On the *yǐmǎo* day of the twelfth month,
Yòuchéngxiàng (Right Chancellor) Xiāo Zhònggōng was appointed Tàifù (Grand Tutor) and Líng Sānxǐng Shì (Controller of the Three Departments).
Zuǒchéngxiàng (Left Chancellor) Liàng was appointed Shàngshū Yòuchéngxiàng (Right Chancellor of the Department of State Affairs).
On the *yǐhài* day,
Zuǒchéngxiàng Zōngxián was appointed Tàishī (Grand Preceptor), Líng Sānxǐng Shì concurrently Dūyuánshuài (Grand Marshal).
On the *jiǎshēn* day, the first day of the first month of the ninth year,
envoys from Sòng, Gāolí, and Xià came to offer congratulations.
On the *wùxū* day,
Tàishī (Grand Preceptor), Líng Sānxǐng Shì (Controller of the Three Departments), and Dūyuánshuài (Grand Marshal) Zōngxián was dismissed.
Líng Xíngtái Shàngshūshěng Shì (Controller of the Acting Department of State Affairs) Xù was appointed Tàishī and Líng Sānxǐng Shì.
Chōng, who concurrently served as Pàn Dàzōngzhèng Shì (Judge of the Imperial Clan Court), was appointed Shàngshū Zuǒchéngxiàng (Left Chancellor of the Department of State Affairs).
Yòuchéngxiàng (Right Chancellor) Liàng concurrently served as Dūyuánshuài.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
during the Wànshòu Jié (Emperor's Birthday),
envoys from Sòng, Gāolí, and Xià came to offer congratulations.
On the *rénshēn* day,
Zuǒchéngxiàng (Left Chancellor) Chōng passed away.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
Yòuchéngxiàng (Right Chancellor) Liàng was appointed Zuǒchéngxiàng.
Zōngběn, the Pàn Dàzōngzhèng Shì (Judge of the Imperial Clan Court), was appointed Shàngshū Yòuchéngxiàng (Right Chancellor of the Department of State Affairs).
Zuǒfùyuánshuài (Left Deputy Marshal) Zōngmǐn was appointed Dūyuánshuài.
Zōngxián, the Nánjīng Liúshǒu (Resident Commissioner of Nánjīng), was appointed Zuǒfùyuánshuài concurrently Xījīng Liúshǒu (Resident Commissioner of Xījīng).
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
Zōngxián was reinstated as Tàibǎo (Grand Protector) and Líng Sānxǐng Shì (Controller of the Three Departments).
On the *jiǎyín* day of the second month,
Huìníng Mù (Prefect of Huìníng) Tángkuò Biàn was reinstated as Shàngshū Zuǒchéng (Left Assistant of the Department of State Affairs).
Shàngshū Zuǒchéng Bǐng was appointed Xíngtái Píngzhāng Zhèngshì (Acting Councillor of State).
On the *guǐwèi* day, the first day of the third month,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
Sīkōng (Minister of Works) Zōngběn was appointed Shàngshū Yòuchéngxiàng (Right Chancellor of the Department of State Affairs) concurrently Zhōngshūlìng (Director of the Central Secretariat).
Zuǒchéngxiàng (Left Chancellor) Liàng was appointed Tàibǎo (Grand Protector) and Líng Sānxǐng Shì.
On the night of the *rénshēn* day of the fourth month,
there was a great storm with wind and rain.
Thunder and lightning shattered the *chīwěi* (owl-tail ornaments) of the sleeping palace.
Fire entered the Emperor's bedchamber,
burning the curtains and drapes.
The Emperor hastily moved to another palace to avoid it.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
dragons fought above the Yúlín Hé (Yulin River) in Lìzhōu.
Strong winds destroyed civilian residences and official buildings.
Tiles, wood, people, and livestock were all swept away for dozens of *lǐ*.
Hundreds of people were killed or injured.
On the *wùzǐ* day of the fifth month,
due to the celestial anomalies on the *rénshēn* and *dīngchǒu* days of the fourth month,
a general amnesty was proclaimed.
Hànlín Xuéshì (Academician of the Hanlin Academy) Zhāng Jūn was ordered to draft the edict.
Cānzhī Zhèngshì (Participating in Determining Governmental Affairs) Xiāo Yì singled out some of his words, accusing them of slander.
The Emperor was enraged
and had Jūn executed.
On this same day,
a partial amnesty was granted to prisoners in Shàngjīng.
On the *gēngyín* day,

Tàibǎo (Grand Protector) and Líng Sānxǐng Shì (Controller of the Three Departments) Liàng was sent out to serve as Líng Xíngtái Shàngshūshěng Shì (Controller of the Acting Department of State Affairs).
On the *wùshēn* day,

Yēlǜ Bājīn, the Wǔkùshǔ Lìng (Director of the Imperial Armory), falsely accused the Emperor, claiming that Sùzhí Jiāngjūn (General of the Imperial Guard) Xiāo Róng was in a faction with Zuò Wáng (Prince of Zuò) Yuán.
He was executed.
On the *jǐwèi* day of the sixth month,
Dūyuánshuài (Grand Marshal) Zōngmǐn was appointed Tàibǎo (Grand Protector) and Líng Sānxǐng Shì (Controller of the Three Departments) concurrently Zuǒfùyuánshuài (Left Deputy Marshal).
Zuǒchéngxiàng (Left Chancellor) Zōngxián concurrently served as Dūyuánshuài.
On the *gēngshēn* day of the eighth month,
Liúkuì was appointed Sīkōng (Minister of Works),
retaining his former position as Xíngtái Yòuchéngxiàng (Acting Right Chancellor).
The prime ministers deliberated on relocating the people of Liáoyáng and Bóhǎi to the south of Yān,
and this was approved.
Shìcóng (Imperial Attendant) Gāo Shòuxīng and others were to be moved
and appealed to the Empress.
The Empress informed the Emperor.
The Emperor was enraged at those who proposed the relocation,
flogged Píngzhāng Zhèngshì (Councillor of State) Bǐngdé,
and executed Zuǒsī Lángzhōng (Director of the Left Bureau of the Department of State Affairs) Sānhé.
On the *bǐngshēn* day of the ninth month,
Líng Xíngtái Shàngshūshěng Shì (Controller of the Acting Department of State Affairs) Liàng was reinstated as Píngzhāng Zhèngshì.
On the *wùxū* day,
Yòuchéngxiàng (Right Chancellor) Zōngběn was appointed Tàibǎo (Grand Protector) and Líng Sānxǐng Shì.
Zuǒfùyuánshuài (Left Deputy Marshal) Zōngmǐn was appointed Líng Xíngtái Shàngshūshěng Shì.
Píngzhāng Zhèngshì Bǐngdé was appointed Shàngshū Zuǒchéngxiàng (Left Chancellor of the Department of State Affairs) concurrently Zhōngshūlìng (Director of the Central Secretariat).
Sīkōng (Minister of Works) Liúkuì was appointed Píngzhāng Zhèngshì.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
Yùshǐ Dàfū (Grand Censor) Zōngpǔ was appointed Cānzhī Zhèngshì (Participating in Determining Governmental Affairs).
On the *yǐchǒu* day of the tenth month,

Běijīng Liúshǒu (Resident Commissioner of Běijīng) Zuò Wáng Yuán and his younger brother Ānwǔ Jūn Jiédùshǐ (Military Commissioner of Ānwǔ Commandery) Zhálà, and Zuǒwèi Jiāngjūn (General of the Left Guard) Tèsī were executed.
A general amnesty was proclaimed.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
Hànlín Xuéshì (Academician of the Hanlin Academy) Jīng was appointed Yùshǐ Dàfū.
On the *guǐwèi* day of the eleventh month,
Empress Péimǎn Shì was executed.
Zuò Wáng Fēi (Princess Consort of Zuò) Sāmǎo was summoned to the palace.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
the former Dèng Wángzǐ (Prince of Dèng) Ālǎn and Dálǎn were executed.
On the *guǐsì* day,
the Emperor hunted at Hūlàhúntǔwēn.
Envoys were dispatched to execute Défēi (Consort Dé) Wūgǔlún Shì, as well as Jiágǔ Shì and Zhāng Shì.
On the *jǐyǒu* day of the twelfth month, which was the first day of the lunar month,
the Emperor arrived back from his hunting grounds.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
he killed Consort Péimǎn Shì in her sleeping chamber.
Liàng, who was a Píngzhāng Zhèngshì, seized the opportunity of the officials being terrified,
and plotted a rebellion with his close associates, Fùmǎ Tángkuò Biàn, the palace attendant Xiǎodǐ Dà Xìngguó, the ten-man guard commander Hūtǔ, and Ālǐchūhǔ.
On the *dīngsì* day,
he assigned Hūtǔ and Ālǐchūhǔ to inner guard duty,
and ordered the Sěng Lìngshǐ Lǐ Lǎosēng to speak to Xìngguó.
At the second drum of the night,
Xìngguó secretly stole a tally,
fabricated an imperial edict to open the palace gates,
and summoned Biàn and the others.
Liàng, with a knife in his bosom, and his brother-in-law Tèsī, followed Biàn into the palace gates.
The guards, seeing Biàn was a Fùmǎ,
had no suspicions
and let them in.
When they reached the palace hall gate,
the guards became aware,
drew their blades, and threatened them;
none dared to move.
Hūtǔ and Ālǐchūhǔ arrived before the Emperor.
The Emperor searched for the saber he usually kept by the bed,
unaware that Xìngguó had already replaced it.
Hūtǔ and Ālǐchūhǔ then advanced and assassinated the Emperor.
Liàng again stepped forward and personally dealt the fatal blow,
blood splattering all over his face and clothes.
The Emperor died,
at the age of thirty-one.
Zuǒ Chéngxiàng Bǐngdé and others then enthroned Liàng,
bowed in unison, shouted "Long live!",
and established him as Emperor.
They demoted the deceased Emperor to Dōnghūn Wáng,
and buried him in the tomb of Empress Péimǎn Shì.
In the third year of Zhēnyuán,
he was reburied in Liáoxiāng Diàn in Dàfáng Shān,
sharing a burial ground with other princes.
In the early Dàdìng era,
he was posthumously given the imperial title Wǔlíng Huángdì,
the temple name Mǐnzōng,
and his mausoleum was named Sīlíng.
A separate temple was established for him.
In the nineteenth year,
he was elevated and enshrined in the Tàimiào,
and his posthumous title was augmented to Hóngjī Zuǎnwǔ Zhuāngjìng Xiàochéng Huángdì.
In the twenty-seventh year,
his temple name was changed to Xīzōng.
In the twenty-eighth year,
due to Sīlíng being narrow and small,
he was reburied in Éméi Gǔ,
still named Sīlíng,
and this was announced throughout the realm.
The eulogy states: During Xīzōng's time,
the four directions were peaceful.
He respectfully treated the imperial clan and high officials,
entrusting them with state affairs.
His rule, which involved succeeding and upholding established practices,
was quite remarkable.
In his later years, he indulged in heavy drinking and made arbitrary killings,
causing people to live in fear.
It is said that "slander existed before him but he did not see it,
and traitors were behind him but he did not know it,"
which gradually led to his downfall.
[一五]This was not the fault of a single day or night.
Collation Notes
Annals Chapter 5: Hǎilíng
The deposed Emperor Hǎilíng Shùrén Liàng,
courtesy name Yuángōng,
originally named Dígǔnǎi,
was the second son of Liáo Wáng Zōnggàn.
His mother was Lady Dà.
He was born in the *rényín* year, the sixth year of Tiānfǔ.
In the third year of Tiānjuàn,
at the age of eighteen,
as a member of the imperial clan, he was appointed Fèngguó Shàngjiāngjūn,
and dispatched to serve in Liáng Wáng Zōngbì's army,
where he was made Xíngjūn Wànhù,
then promoted to Piàojí Shàngjiāngjūn.
In the fourth year of Huángtǒng,
he was promoted to Lónghǔwèi Shàngjiāngjūn,
served as Zhōngjīng Liúshǒu,
and then promoted to Guānglù Dàfū.
He was impetuous and quick-tempered,
prone to suspicion,
cruel, and manipulative.
Initially,
Xīzōng succeeded to the throne as the legitimate grandson of Tàizǔ.
Liàng believed that since Zōnggàn was Tàizǔ's eldest son,
and he himself was also a grandson of Tàizǔ,
he harbored ambitions for the throne.
In Zhōngjīng,
he focused solely on establishing his authority,
to subdue lesser individuals.
Měng'ān Xiāo Yù was treacherous, cunning, and decisive.
Liàng befriended him,
and often discussed state affairs with him.
Yù understood Liàng's intentions
and consequently encouraged Hǎilíng to undertake a major endeavor.
The details are in Yù's biography.
In the fifth month of the seventh year,
he was summoned to serve as Tóngpàn Dàzōngzhèng Shì,
and given the additional title Tèjìn.
In the eleventh month,
he was appointed Shàngshū Zuǒchéng,
endeavoring to seize control of power,
and placing his trusted confidants in key positions within the government ministries.
He brought Xiāo Yù in as Bīngbù Shìláng.
One day, during an audience,
when the topic turned to Tàizǔ's difficult founding of the dynasty,
Liàng began to weep bitterly,
which Xīzōng took as a sign of loyalty.
In the sixth month of the eighth year,
he was appointed Píngzhāng Zhèngshì.
In the eleventh month,
he was appointed Yòuchéngxiàng.
In the first month of the ninth year,
he concurrently held the position of Dūyuánshuài.
Xīzōng sent the palace attendant Xiǎodǐ Dà Xìngguó to bestow a birthday gift upon Liàng.
Empress Dào also attached gifts.
Xīzōng was displeased,
had Xìngguó flogged one hundred times,
and reclaimed the gifts.
Hǎilíng became uneasy because of this.
In the third month,
he was appointed Tàibǎo and Lǐng Sānshěng Shì,
and increasingly sought public praise,
promoting descendants of powerful and influential families,
to gain their favor.
In the fourth month,
Xuégùn Zhāng Jūn drafted an edict that displeased the Emperor and he was killed.
Xīzōng asked,
"Who made him do it?"
Zuǒ Chéngxiàng Zōngxián replied,
"It was truly Tàibǎo."
Xīzōng was displeased,
and consequently sent him out as Lǐng Xíngtái Shàngshūshěng Shì.
Passing through Zhōngjīng,
he made an agreement with Xiāo Yù before leaving.
Upon reaching Liángxiāng,
he was recalled.
Hǎilíng could not fathom the reason for his recall
and was greatly afraid.
Upon his arrival,
he was reinstated as Píngzhāng Zhèngshì,
which made him feel even more precarious.
Xīzōng had once flogged Zuǒchéng Tángkuò Biàn and Yòuchéngxiàng Bǐngdé for certain matters.
Biàn then conspired with Dàlǐ Qīng Wūdài to depose and enthrone someone,
and Wūdài first informed Hǎilíng of this plan.
Another day,
Hǎilíng discussed the matter of deposition and enthronement with Biàn,
saying,
"If we undertake this great endeavor,
who can be enthroned?"
Biàn replied,
"Perhaps Zuò Wáng Chángshèng?"
He asked who else,
and Biàn said,
"Dèng Wángzǐ Ālǎn."
Liàng said,
"Ālǎn is distantly related;
how can he be enthroned?"
Biàn said,
"Do you perhaps have an intention?"
Hǎilíng said,
"If it truly comes to that,
who else but me!"
From then on, they secretly conspired day and night.
Hùwèi Jiāngjūn Tèsī suspected them,
and reported to Empress Dào, saying,
"Biàn and the others always gather secretly to talk after official duties.
I suspect them."
The Empress reported this to Xīzōng.
Xīzōng was enraged,
summoned Biàn, and said,
"What are you plotting with Liàng? What do you intend to do to me?"
He had him flogged.
Because of this, Liàng became wary of Chángshèng and Ālǎn,
and also hated Tèsī.
Then, a soldier from Hénán, Sūn Jìn, claimed to be the Emperor's brother, Ànchá Dàwáng.
Since Xīzōng's brothers were only Chángshèng and Chálà,
Hǎilíng seized this opportunity to frame Chángshèng, Chálà, Ālǎn, and Dálǎn.
Xīzōng ordered Tèsī to investigate,
but found no evidence.
Hǎilíng said,
"Tèsī did not investigate truthfully."
Consequently, they were all killed.
The ten-man leader of the guards, Pú Sǎn Hūtǔ (僕散忽土), had previously received favors from Zōng Gàn (宗幹).
Tú Dān Ālǐ Chūhǔ (徒單阿里出虎) was related by marriage to Hǎilíng (海陵).
Dà Xìngguó (大興國), a palace attendant,
would often, by night, take the tally and keys from the master and return home,
making it a regular practice.
Xìngguó (興國) had once entrusted the old monk Lǐ (李) to Hǎilíng (海陵),
who managed to get him appointed as a clerk in the Secretariat-Chancellery.
Therefore, Hǎilíng (海陵) had the old monk Lǐ (李) ally with Xìngguó (興國) to be an inside helper.
And Xìngguó (興國), for his part, resented Xī Zōng (熙宗) because he had been flogged,
so he made an agreement with Liàng (亮).
On the *dīngsì* day of the twelfth month,
Hū Tǔ (忽土) and Ālǐ Chūhǔ (阿里出虎) were on night duty in the palace.
That night,
Xìngguó (興國) took the tally and keys, opened the gates, and let Hǎilíng (海陵), Bǐng Dé (秉德), Biàn (辯), Wū Dài (烏帶), Tú Dān Zhēn (徒單貞), and the old monk Lǐ (李) enter the sleeping quarters,
where they then assassinated Xī Zōng (熙宗).
Bǐng Dé (秉德) and the others had not yet declared their allegiance.
Hū Tǔ (忽土) said:
"At first, we discussed establishing a *Píngzhāng* (平章).
What is there to doubt now?"
Thereupon, they seated Hǎilíng (海陵) on the throne,
all bowed,
and cried "Long Live!"
They falsely claimed that Xī Zōng (熙宗) wished to discuss the establishment of an empress,
summoned the high ministers,
and then killed Cáo Guó Wáng Zōng Mǐn (曹國王宗敏)
and Left Chancellor Zōng Xián (宗賢).
On that day,
Bǐng Dé (秉德) was made Left Chancellor concurrently with Grand Mentor and Left Vice Marshal;
Biàn (辯) was made Right Chancellor concurrently with Grand Councilor;
Wū Dài (烏帶) was made Grand Councilor;
Hū Tǔ (忽土) was made Left Vice Inspector of the Palace Guards;
Ālǐ Chūhǔ (阿里出虎) was made Right Vice Inspector of the Palace Guards;
Zhēn (貞) was made Left Palace Guard General;
Xìngguó (興國) was made Administrator of Guǎngníng (廣寧).
Thereupon, twenty individuals, from Tài Shī (太師) concurrently in charge of the Three Departments Xù (勗) downwards, were promoted in noble rank and office, each according to their station.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
a general amnesty was issued.
The ninth year of Huángtǒng (皇統) was changed to the first year of Tiāndé (天德).
Cānzhī Zhèngshì (參知政事) Xiāo Yì (蕭肄) was dismissed from office.
Zhènnán Tǒngjūn (鎮南統軍) Bó Jí (孛極) was made Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs.

The Left Chancellor Bǐng Dé (秉德), Right Chancellor Biàn (辯), Grand Councilor Wū Dài (烏帶), Administrator of Guǎngníng (廣寧) Xìngguó (興國), Inspectors of the Palace Guards Hū Tǔ (忽土) and Ālǐ Chūhǔ (阿里出虎), Left Palace Guard General Zhēn (貞), Clerk of the Secretariat-Chancellery old monk Lǐ (李), and Biàn (辯)'s father, Minister of Punishments Ālǐ (阿里), were all granted money, silk, horses, cattle, and sheep, each in varying amounts.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
an oath was sworn at Tàizǔ (太祖)'s temple,
and Bǐng Dé (秉德), Biàn (辯), Wū Dài (烏帶), Hū Tǔ (忽土), Ālǐ Chūhǔ (阿里出虎), and Xìngguó (興國)—the six men—were summoned and given the oath documents.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
Liú Lín (劉麟), Superintendent of Transport for Yānjīng Lù (燕京路), was made Cānzhī Zhèngshì (參知政事).
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
Tài Fù (太傅) concurrently in charge of the Three Departments Xiāo Zhònggōng (蕭仲恭)
and Right Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs Bǐng (禀) were dismissed.
Wēn Dū Sīzhōng (溫都思忠), Left Assistant Director of the Traveling Department of State Affairs, was made Right Assistant Director.
On the *yǐhài* day,
the posthumous title bestowed on the late Emperor's father was Huángkǎo Tàishī Xiàngǔ Hóngdào Wénzhāo Wǔliè Zhāngxiào Ruìmíng Huángdì (皇考太師憲古弘道文昭武烈章孝睿明皇帝),
his temple name Dézōng (德宗),
and his former residence was named Xīngshènggōng (興聖宮).
Envoys from Sòng (宋), Gāolí (高麗), and Xià (夏) for the New Year's congratulations were sent back midway.
In the first month of the second year, on the *xīnsì* day,
Xiāo Yù (蕭裕), Assistant Prefect of the Central Capital, was made Secretary-General.
On the *guǐsì* day,
the legitimate mother, the Tú Dān (徒單) clan, and the birth mother, the Dà (大) clan, were both honored as Empress Dowagers.
The Tú Dān (徒單) clan's palace was named Yǒngshòu (永壽),
and the Dà (大) clan's palace was named Yǒngníng (永寧).
On the *yǐsì* day,

an imperial edict was issued to officials both inside and outside the capital regarding seven matters: to encourage officials in their duties, to attend to agricultural seasons, to be cautious in punishments, to promote the humble and obscure, to sympathize with the poor, to economize finances, and to carefully select talented individuals.
Wán Yán Sīgōng (完顏思恭), Commander of the Imperial Guard Foot Soldiers, and others were dispatched to Sòng (宋), Gāolí (高麗), and Xià (夏) to report on the deposition and enthronement.
The Left Chancellor concurrently Left Vice Marshal Bǐng Dé (秉德) was put in charge of the Traveling Department of State Affairs.
On the *wùshēn* day, the first day of the second month,
his son Yuán Shòu (元壽) was enfeoffed as King Chóng (崇).
On the *gēngxū* day,
the former emperor was demoted to King of Dōnghūn (東昏).
Two granddaughters of the Duke of Tiānshuǐ (天水) Commandery were granted monthly stipends.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
Wán Yán Yuán Yí (完顏元宜), Minister of War, and others were appointed as envoys to congratulate Sòng (宋) on the emperor's birthday.
On the *wùchén* day,
the assembled officials presented an honorific title: Fǎtiān Yīngyùn Ruìwǔ Xuānwén Dàmíng Shèngxiào Huángdì (法天膺運睿武宣文大明聖孝皇帝),
and an edict was issued to both inside and outside the capital.
The fathers and grandfathers of the two empress dowagers, Yǒngshòu (永壽) and Yǒngníng (永寧), were posthumously granted official titles of varying ranks.
Right Chancellor Táng Kuò Biàn (唐括辯) was made Left Chancellor,
and Grand Councilor Wū Dài (烏帶) was made Right Chancellor.
In the third month, on the *bǐngxū* day,
Sòng (宋) and Gāolí (高麗) sent envoys to congratulate the emperor on his enthronement.
His younger brother Yǎn (兗) was made Grand Minister of Education concurrently Grand Marshal.
An edict was issued that the Jade Belt of the Prince of Tiānshuǐ (天水) Commandery be returned to Sòng (宋).
In the fourth month, on the *wùwǔ* day,
Tài Fù (太傅) concurrently in charge of the Three Departments Zōng Běn (宗本),
Left Chancellor of the Department of State Affairs Táng Kuò Biàn (唐括辯),
and Administrator of the Great Clan Affairs Office Zōng Měi (宗美) were killed.
Envoys were sent to kill Bǐng Dé (秉德), in charge of the Traveling Department of State Affairs,
Zōng Yī (宗懿), Prefect of the Eastern Capital,
Biàn (卞), Prefect of the Northern Capital, and over seventy descendants of Tàizōng (太宗),
over thirty descendants of Zōng Hán (宗翰), King of Zhōu (周) and Sòng (宋),
and over fifty other imperial clansmen.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
Xiāo Yù (蕭玉), interpreter in the Department of State Affairs, was made Minister of Rites;
Xiāo Yù (蕭裕), Secretary-General, was made Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs;
Sītú (司徒) Yǎn (兗) was put in charge of the Three Departments and enfeoffed as a Prince,
his position as Grand Marshal remaining unchanged;
Right Chancellor Wū Dài (烏帶) was made Grand Minister of Works, Left Chancellor concurrently Grand Mentor;
Grand Councilor Liú Guǎ (劉筈) was made Right Chancellor of the Department of State Affairs concurrently Grand Councilor;
Left Assistant Director Zōng Yì (宗義) and Right Assistant Director Wēn Dū Sīzhōng (溫都思忠) were made Grand Councilors;
Cānzhī Zhèngshì (參知政事) Liú Lín (劉麟) was made Right Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs;
Pú Sǎn Hū Tǔ (僕散忽土), Left Vice Inspector of the Palace Guards, was made Commander of the Palace Guards.
In the fifth month, on the *wùzǐ* day,
Dà (大)●, Grand Councilor of the Traveling Department of State Affairs and Right Vice Marshal, was made Right Chancellor of the Traveling Department of State Affairs,
his position as Marshal remaining unchanged.
On the *rénchén* day,
Sā Lí Hē (撒离喝), Left Vice Marshal, was made Left Chancellor of the Traveling Department of State Affairs,
his position as Marshal remaining unchanged.
Zōng Ān (宗安), concurrently Administrator of the Great Clan Affairs Office, was made Imperial Censor-in-chief.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day, the first day of the sixth month,
Gāolí (高麗) sent envoys to congratulate the emperor on his enthronement.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
the Tàimiào (太廟) was first equipped with four spirit gates and four corner screens.
In the seventh month, on the *jǐchǒu* day,
Sītú (司空) and Left Chancellor concurrently Grand Mentor Wū Dài (烏帶) was dismissed.
Wēn Dū Sīzhōng (溫都思忠), Grand Councilor, was made Left Chancellor;
Xiāo Yù (蕭裕), Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs, was made Grand Councilor;
Liú Lín (劉麟), Right Assistant Director, was made Left Assistant Director;
Wán Yán Sīgōng (完顏思恭), Commander of the Imperial Guard Foot Soldiers, was made Right Assistant Director.
Cānzhī Zhèngshì (參知政事) Zhāng Hào (張浩) observed mourning,
but was reinstated to his former position.
On the *wùxū* day,
Xià Guó (夏國) sent envoys to congratulate the emperor on his enthronement and the acceptance of his honorific title.
In the eighth month, on the *wùshēn* day,
Sītú (司徒) Yǎn (兗) was made Grand Commandant,
his positions in charge of the Three Departments and Grand Marshal remaining unchanged.
Xiāo Yù (蕭玉), Minister of Rites, was made Cānzhī Zhèngshì (參知政事).
In the ninth month, on the *jiǎwǔ* day,
Consort Huì (惠妃) Tú Dān (徒單) was established as Empress.
In the tenth month, on the *guǐmǎo* day,
Tài Shī (太師) concurrently in charge of the Three Departments Xù (勗) retired from office.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
Grand Empress Dowager Xiāo (蕭) and her son, Prince Rèn Wéi Hē (任王偎喝), were killed.
Envoys were sent to kill Sā Lí Hē (撒离喝), Left Chancellor of the Traveling Department of State Affairs and Left Vice Marshal, in Biàn (汴),
and also killed Grand Councilor Zōng Yì (宗義), former Minister of Works Móu Lǐ Yě (謀里野), and Imperial Censor-in-chief Zōng Ān (宗安),
all of whose clans were exterminated.
Huó Lǐ Jiǎ (活里甲), grandson of King Wèi Wáng Wò Dài (魏王斡帶), was fond of extravagant decoration,
and his clan was also exterminated.
In the eleventh month, on the *guǐwèi* day,
Liú Guǎ (劉筈), Right Chancellor of the Department of State Affairs, was dismissed.
Tú Dān Gōng (徒單恭), Prefect of Huìníng (會寧), was made Grand Councilor.
Liú Lín (劉麟), Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs, and Wán Yán Sīgōng (完顏思恭), Right Assistant Director, were dismissed.
Cānzhī Zhèngshì (參知政事) Zhāng Hào (張浩) was made Right Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
Zhāng Tōnggǔ (張通古), Left Assistant Director of the Traveling Department of State Affairs, was made Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
a white rainbow pierced the sun.
On the *dīnghài* day,
the Empress Dowager's decrees were to be called *lìngzhǐ* (令旨).
On the *wùzǐ* day,
twelve matters were decreed to admonish officials.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
ordinary officials were permitted to seek two secondary wives,
and common people were also permitted to keep concubines.
On the *guǐmǎo* day, the first day of the twelfth month,
an edict ordered the removal of the honorific title presented by the assembled officials.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
the standard for the hereditary stipend of the Duke Yǎnshèng (衍聖公) was first established.
Officials outside the capital residing more than one hundred *lǐ* away were not permitted to participate in court visits;
those within one hundred *lǐ* were not allowed to stay for more than three days for their round trip.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
a monument commemorating Tàizǔ (太祖)'s archery was erected in the Hégēlì (紇石烈) tribe's territory,
and the Emperor and Empress offered sacrifices below the monument.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
barbarians came to offer exotic incense,
but it was refused.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
the proper authorities reported the sighting of auspicious clouds,
and the Emperor said:
"What virtue do I possess to warrant this?
From now on, auspicious omens should not be reported to me.
If there are any strange or ominous occurrences,
they should be reported to me
so that I may be warned."
On the *jǐwèi* day,
the Traveling Department of State Affairs was abolished.
The Grand Marshal's Office was renamed the Bureau of Military Affairs.
An edict was issued to revise the law on continuing broken lineages.
Dà (大)●, Right Vice Marshal, was made Right Chancellor of the Department of State Affairs concurrently Grand Councilor;
Zhāng Zhōngfú (張中孚), Cānzhī Xíngtái Shàngshūshěng Shì (參知行臺尚書省事), was made Cānzhī Zhèngshì (參知政事);
Yǎn (兗), Grand Marshal, was made Commissioner of Military Affairs,
his positions as Grand Commandant and in charge of the Three Departments remaining unchanged;
Áng (昂), Left Supervisor of the Marshal's Army, was made Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs;
Zhào Zīfú (趙資福), Minister of Punishments, was made Imperial Censor-in-chief.
In the first month of the third year, on the *guǐyǒu* day,
the Sòng, Xià, and Gāolì sent envoys to offer congratulations.
On the *yǐhài* day,
Cānzhī Zhèngshì Xiāo Yù observed mourning,
but was reinstated to his former position.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
it was the Beginning of Spring,
and the ceremony of "beating the clay ox" was observed.
On the *dīnghài* day,
the creation of a "lantern mountain" within the palace began.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
it was His Majesty's birthday,
and the Sòng, Gāolì, and Xià sent envoys to offer congratulations.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
the Guózǐjiān was established for the first time.
His Majesty said to Yùshǐ Dàfū Zhào Zīfú:
“You all often indulge in private sentiments;
I have not heard of any impeachments,
which I find most unacceptable.
From now on, if any of the hundred officials act unlawfully,
you must impeach and denounce them,
without fear of the powerful and influential.”
On the *yǐwèi* day,
His Majesty went out hunting,
and the prime ministers and officials below him bid farewell in the near suburbs.
His Majesty reined in his horse and admonished them, saying:
“I do not begrudge high ranks and generous stipends to employ you all.
Recently, I have heard that many matters are stagnant.
Is it that you are content to seek your own comfort and do not care for the affairs of the people?
From now on, I will observe your diligence and idleness,
and based on that, award rewards and punishments.
Each of you should strive your best.”
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
a white rainbow pierced the sun.
In the second month, on the *dīngsì* day,
His Majesty returned to the palace.
In the third month, on the *gēngyín* day,
Hànlín Xuéshì Liú Chángyán and others were appointed as envoys for the Sòng emperor's birthday.
On the *rénchén* day,
an edict was issued to expand Yānchéng
and construct palaces.
On the *jǐhài* day,
His Majesty said to his attendant ministers:
“Yesterday, on the Crown Prince’s birthday,
the Empress presented me with an object,
which is truly precious and extraordinary.
You, ministers, please take a look.”
He then took it out from a crimson pouch;
it was a painting depicting farming scenes.
“The Empress means that since the Crown Prince was born in the deep palace,
he does not know the hardships of people’s farming.
Therefore, she offered this.
I commend her greatly.”
In the fourth month, on the *bǐngwǔ* day,
an edict was issued to move the capital to Yānjīng.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
the relevant authorities presented drawings of the palace layout in Yānchéng,
along with recommendations for construction based on Yīnyáng and the Five Phases.
Hǎilíng said:
“The nation’s fortune
lies in virtue, not in location.
If Jié and Zhòu lived there,
what benefit would a well-chosen site bring?
If Yáo and Shùn lived there,
what need would there be for divination?”
On the *bǐngyín* day,
the annual tribute of hawks and falcons was abolished.
A man from Yízhōu, Wú Zhēn, committed a crime
punishable by death.
The authorities requested mercy because his mother was old and ill and had no one to care for her.
An official was ordered to provide for her care and support,
and this was established as a regulation.
In the intercalary month, on the *xīnwèi* day,
Shàngshū Yòuchéng Zhāng Hào was ordered to manage the selection process for Yānjīng,
and he was admonished not to show favoritism.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
it was ordered that the Grand Provisioner's daily meals should only include fish and meat,
and the former tributes of geese, ducks, etc., were all abolished.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
the birds and beasts kept in the imperial park during the Huángtǒng era were released.
Guīdéjūn Jiédùshǐ Ālǔbǔ was sentenced to death
for dismantling official residences’ timber to build a private mansion.
On the *wùxū* day,
an edict was issued that for court officials who claimed illness and did not attend to affairs,
the Shàngshūshěng should order Supervising Censors to diagnose them together with imperial physicians.
Those without genuine illness would be punished.
In the fifth month, on the *rénzǐ* day,
an edict was issued to the court and beyond,
admonishing officials from the prime ministers down.
On the *wùchén* day,
the prime ministers requested an increase in imperial concubines to expand the imperial lineage.
His Majesty ordered Túdān Zhēn to tell the prime ministers
that among the women of the previously executed partisans, many were His Majesty's maternal or paternal cousins,
and he wished to take them into the palace.
Píngzhāng Zhèngshì Xiāo Yù disapproved,
but His Majesty did not heed him.
Consequently, the wives of Zōngběn’s son Shāchùchuài,
Zōnggù’s sons Húlìlà and Húshīdá,
Bǐngdé’s younger brother Cílí, and others were taken into the palace.
In the sixth month, on the *bǐngzǐ* day,
Tàifǔjiān Wányán Fēngliù was executed.
The Sòng sent envoys to request permission to visit the imperial mausoleums,
but it was not granted.
In the ninth month, on the *gēngxū* day,
silk was bestowed upon the laborers in Yānjīng,
one roll per person.
Tōngjīnglù Bīngmǎ Dōuzǒngguǎnfǔ Pànguān Xiāo Zǐmǐn was appointed as the Gāolì emperor's birthday envoy,
and Xiūqǐjūzhù Xiāo Pénggē as the Xià kingdom's birthday envoy.
In the tenth month, on the *jǐsì* day,
Lánzǐshān Méng'ān Xiāo Gǒng was executed.
Yòufù Diǎnjiǎn Bùshùlǔ Āhǎi and others were appointed as Sòng New Year envoys.
In the eleventh month, on the *guǐhài* day,
an edict was issued to abolish the hereditary Wànhù official positions,
and all those previously granted surnames were to revert to their original surnames.
In the twelfth month, on the *wùchén* day,
Shòuníng Xiànzhǔ Xú Niǎn was flogged.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
His Majesty hunted in the near suburbs.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
His Majesty returned to the palace.
This year,
Prince Chóngwáng Yuánshòu died.
In the first month of the fourth year, on the *dīngyǒu* day,
the Sòng, Gāolì, and Xià sent envoys to offer congratulations.
The assembled officials requested the establishment of a Crown Prince,
which was granted.
On the *wùxū* day,
the officials of the Eastern Palace were formally appointed for the first time.
A reward system for capturing bandits was established.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
Venus traversed the sky.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
it was His Majesty's birthday,
and the Sòng, Gāolì, and Xià sent envoys to offer congratulations.
On the *guǐhài* day,
His Majesty paid respects at the mausoleums of Shìzǔ, Tàizǔ, Tàizōng, and Dézōng.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
His Majesty returned to the palace.
In the second month, on the *dīngmǎo* day,
His son Guāngyīng was established as the Crown Prince.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
an edict was issued to the court and beyond.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
His Majesty traveled to Yānjīng.
Zhāoyìjūn Jiédùshǐ Xiāo Zhòngxuān's domestic slave accused his master of resentment and slander.
His Majesty said:
“Zhòngxuān's nephew, Díniǎn Ābù, was recently executed for slander,
so this person dares to make a false accusation.”
He ordered the accuser to be killed.
Díniǎn Ābù was
also known as Xiāo Gǒng.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
His Majesty arrived at Tàizhōu.
In the third month, on the *bǐngshēn* day,
Xíngbù Shàngshū Tián Xiùyǐng and others were appointed as Sòng emperor's birthday envoys.
In the fourth month, on the *bǐngyín* day,
the relevant authorities requested that this year, candidates from Hénán and Héběi should all go to Zhōngjīng for selection and appointment,
which was granted.
On the *rénchén* day,
His Majesty traveled from Tàizhōu to Liángxìng.
In the fifth month, on the *dīngyǒu* day,
His Majesty hunted at Lìlièzhīshān.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
the hunters were given rewards,
one sheep per person.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
His Majesty arrived at Línhuángfǔ.
On the *dīngsì* day,
Venus traversed the sky.
In the sixth month, on the *jiǎzǐ* day,
His Majesty camped at Miánshān.
On the *wùyín* day,
Quánchǔ Dìbù Méng'ān Nàyě was executed.
In the seventh month, on the *guǐmǎo* day,
His Majesty ordered Chóngyìjūn Jiédùshǐ Wūdài's wife Tángkuò Dìnggē to kill her husband, and then took her into the palace.
In the eighth month, on the *guǐhài* day,
His Majesty hunted at Túníshān.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
Shìyùshǐ Bǎolǔ was flogged
for conducting an investigation inaccurately.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
His Majesty arrived at Duówǎ.
In the ninth month, on the *jiǎwǔ* day,
His Majesty arrived at Zhōngjīng.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
Shàngshū Yòuchéngxiàng Dàlù was dismissed.
Tàifǔ Shàojiān Liú Jǐng was executed.
Dūshuǐshǐzhě Wányán Mápō was appointed as the Gāolì emperor's birthday envoy,
and Lìbù Lángzhōng Xiāo Zhōnglì as the Xià kingdom's birthday envoy.
In the tenth month, on the *rénxū* day, the first day of the month,
envoys were dispatched to respectfully move the spirit tablets of the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
Yùshǐ Dàfū Zhào Zīfú was dismissed.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
Taìzǐ Zhānshì Zhāng Yòngzhí and others were appointed as envoys to congratulate the Sòng dynasty on the New Year.
Taìzǔ's eldest princess, Wūlǔ, was killed.
Her husband, Píngzhāng Zhèngshì Túshàn Gōng, was beaten with a staff and dismissed.
Her maidservant Hūtá was enfeoffed as Guófūrén.
Gōng's elder brother, Dìnggē, was initially married to Wūlǔ.
After Dìnggē died,
Gōng forcibly took her,
but they were not compatible.
He also did not get along with the maidservant Hūtá.
Hūtá gained favor with the Empress,
and then slandered Wūlǔ to the Emperor.
Thus, Wūlǔ was killed,
and Gōng was also dismissed.
In the eleventh month, on the *wùxū* day,
Xiánpíng Yǐn Lǐ Déhù was appointed Píngzhāng Zhèngshì.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
pearls were purchased from the Wūgǔdíliè tribe and Púyǔ Lù.
The common people were forbidden from private trading among themselves.
Furthermore, commoners from both *lù* were conscripted
to collect pearls for one year.
On the *wùshēn* day,
former Píngzhāng Zhèngshì Túshàn Gōng was appointed Sītú.
In the twelfth month, on the *jiǎzǐ* day,
the madman Qiāo Xiān was beheaded in the market of Zhōngjīng.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
Biànjīng Lù Dū Zhuǎnyùnshǐ Zuǒ Yíng and others were appointed as envoys to congratulate the Sòng dynasty on the New Year.
On the *gēngyín* day,
Taìwèi, Lǐng Sānshěng Shì, Shūmìshǐ Yǎn passed away.
In the first year of Zhēnyuán, on the first month, *xīnmǎo* day, the first day of the month,
the Emperor did not hold court.
An imperial edict instructed the relevant officials to accept tribute from Sòng, Gāolí, Xià, and Huíhè.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
the Emperor's birthday,
envoys from Sòng, Gāolí, and Xià came to offer congratulations.
Zhōngjīng Liúshǒu Gāo Zhēn was appointed Yùshǐ Dàfū.
In the second month, on the *gēngshēn* day,
the Emperor traveled from Zhōngjīng to Yānjīng.
In the third month, on the *xīnhài* day,
the Emperor arrived at Yānjīng,
where the imperial cortege was prepared for the first time.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
