more than one hundred and thirty daughters from good families were personally selected to fill the imperial harem.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
an edict on the relocation of the capital was issued to both inside and outside the court.
The reign title was changed to Zhēnyuán.
Yānjīng was renamed Zhōngdū,
its prefecture called Dàxīng;
Biànjīng was renamed Nánjīng;
Zhōngjīng was renamed Běijīng.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
Sītú Túshàn Gōng was appointed Taìbǎo and Lǐng Sānshěng Shì;
Píngzhāng Zhèngshì Xiāo Yù was appointed Yòuchéngxiàng and concurrently Zhōngshū Lìng;
Yòuchéng Zhāng Hào and Zuǒchéng Zhāng Tōnggǔ were appointed Píngzhāng Zhèngshì;
Cānzhī Zhèngshì Zhāng Zhōngfú was appointed Zuǒchéng;
Xiāo Yù was appointed Yòuchéng;
Píngzhāng Zhèngshì Lǐ Déhù was appointed Sīkōng;
Zuǒ Xuānhuīshǐ Liú Wò was appointed Cānzhī Zhèngshì;
Shūmì Fùshǐ Áng was appointed Shūmìshǐ;
Gōngbù Shàngshū Púsàn Shīgōng was appointed Shūmì Fùshǐ.
In the fourth month, on the *xīnyǒu* day,
Yòuxuānhuīshǐ Hèshíliè Sāhén and others were appointed as envoys to congratulate the Sòng dynasty on its Emperor's birthday.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
Tángkuò Dìnggē was specially enfeoffed as Guìfēi.
On the *wùyín* day,
Empress Dowager Dàshì passed away.
In the fifth month, on the *xīnmǎo* day,
the Emperor's younger brother, Xījīng Liúshǒu Pújiā, was killed.
Xījīng Bīngmǎ Wányán Mólúwǎ, Biānxiūguān Yuánfúnú, and Tōngjìn Bódiē were implicated for their friendship with Pújiā,
and were also killed.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
vacant land in the capital city was bestowed upon court officials and imperial guards.
In the sixth month, on the *yǐchǒu* day,
Ānguó Jūn Jiédùshǐ Yēlǜ Shù was appointed Cānzhī Zhèngshì.
In the seventh month, on the *wùzǐ* day, the first day of the month,
the vacant land in the capital city that was originally bestowed upon court officials
was subject to varying monetary levies.
In the eighth month, on the *rénxū* day,
Sīkōng Lǐ Déhù passed away.
The hunting of deer and rabbits in the Zhōngdū Lù was prohibited.
On the *wùyín* day,
silk was bestowed upon the artisans and laborers constructing the palaces and residences.
In the ninth month, on the *dīnghài* day, the first day of the month,
Hànlín Dàizhì Móuliánghǔ was appointed as an envoy for the Xià kingdom's birthday,
and Lìbù Lángzhōng Wāhéshān was appointed as an envoy for Gāolí's birthday.
In the tenth month, on the *dīngsì* day,
the Emperor hunted at Liángxiāng.
The spirit of Liàoshígāng was enfeoffed as Língyìng Wáng.
Initially,
Hǎilíng had once passed by this shrine,
and holding a divination cup, prayed, saying:
"If I am destined to possess the Mandate of Heaven,
I shall receive an auspicious divination."
He cast it,
and it was auspicious.
He then prayed again, saying:
"If it is truly as divined,
I shall offer a reward another day;
otherwise, I will destroy your shrine."
He cast it,
and it was again auspicious,
hence the enfeoffment.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
the Emperor returned to the palace.
On the *rénxū* day,
officials reported that
the Empress Dowager's tomb was not yet completed,
and therefore the winter sacrifices and combined ancestral rites should be suspended;
this was approved.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
it was decreed that internal and external officials who heard of a mourning of great mourning grade or higher
would only be granted leave for that day.
If it was a parent's mourning,
they would be allowed three days' leave.
This was established as a regulation.
In the eleventh month, on the *bǐngxū* day, the first day of the month,
Dìngzhōu presented auspicious grain.
An imperial edict stated that from now on, such presentations were not to be made again.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
Yaóchí Diàn was completed.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
Hùbù Shàngshū Cài Sōngnián and others were appointed as envoys to congratulate the Sòng dynasty on the New Year.
On the *wùxū* day,
Zuǒchéngxiàng Nòuwǎnwēndūsīzhōng retired.
On the *gēngxū* day,
Shūmìshǐ Áng was appointed Zuǒchéngxiàng,
and Shūmì Fùshǐ Púsàn Shīgōng was appointed Shūmìshǐ.
In the twelfth month,
Venus crossed the sky.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
Guìfēi Tángkuò Dìnggē's household slave Sūn Méi was specially granted the *jìnshì* degree.
On the *rénxū* day,
Qiānshū Shūmìyuàn Shì Nánsā was appointed Shūmì Fùshǐ.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
the Emperor's uncle Cáo Guówáng Zōngmǐn's concubine Ālán, whom the Emperor had taken, was enfeoffed as Zhāofēi.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
Guìfēi Tángkuò Dìnggē was found to have committed adultery with her former slave,
and was granted death.
In the intercalary month, on the *yǐyǒu* day, the first day of the month,
Hùwèi Tèmógé was killed.
On the *guǐsì* day,
the system for the altars of state was established.
Venus crossed the sky.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
Taìbǎo, Lǐng Sānshěng Shì Túshàn Gōng was appointed Taìshī,
with his position as Lǐng Sānshěng Shì remaining as before.
Tárténg Lù Tǒngjūn Tàlán, Xīběi Lù Zhāotǎo Xiāo Huáizhōng, Línhuáng Fǔ Zǒngguǎn Mǎ Héshàng, Wūgǔdíliè Sī Zhāotǎo Xiáyě, and others were ordered to patrol the northern regions.
In the second year, first month, *jiǎyín* day, the first day of the month,
the Emperor was unwell,
and did not hold court.
Envoys from Sòng, Gāolí, and Xià were granted a banquet at their residences.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
Venus crossed the sky.
Shàngshū Yòuchéngxiàng Xiāo Yù, along with former Zhēndìng Yǐn Xiāo Féngjiānú, former Yùshǐ Zhōngchéng Xiāo Zhāozhé, Bózhōu Tóngzhī Yáoshè, and others conspired in rebellion,
and were executed.
An imperial edict was issued to both inside and outside the court.
On the *jǐsì* day,
the Emperor's birthday,
envoys from Sòng, Gāolí, and Xià came to offer congratulations.
In the second month, on the *jiǎshēn* day, the first day of the month,
Píngzhāng Zhèngshì Zhāng Hào was appointed Shàngshū Yòuchéngxiàng and concurrently Zhōngshū Lìng.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
Shàngshū Yòuchéng Xiāo Yù was appointed Píngzhāng Zhèngshì;
former Hénán Lù Tǒngjūnshǐ Zhāng Huī was appointed Shàngshū Yòuchéng;
Xīběi Lù Zhāotǎoshǐ Xiāo Hǎohú was appointed Shūmì Fùshǐ.
In the third month, on the *wùchén* day,
Xià sent an envoy to congratulate on the relocation of the capital.
In the fourth month, on the *bǐngxū* day,
the Emperor visited Dàxīng Fǔ and the Dū Zhuǎnyùnshǐ Sī.
Ripened cherries were sent as offerings to Yǎnqìng Gōng.
In the fifth month, on the *guǐchǒu* day, the first day of the month,
there was a solar eclipse.
The Emperor avoided the main hall,
and ordered all officials not to attend to state affairs.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
an imperial edict stated that from now on, on the seventh day of each month, criminal cases would not be presented,
and the imperial kitchen would not serve meat.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
the Jiāochāo Kù (Banknote Office) was first established,
and officials including an Administrator and Vice Administrator were appointed.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
Taìyuán Yǐn Túshàn Ālǐchūhǔ was executed.
His son Shùsīlà was further ordered to travel by post, burn his bones,
and throw them into the water.
In the seventh month, on the *gēngshēn* day,
the Salt, Banknote, Incense, and Tea Certificates Printing Office, with an Administrator and Vice Administrator, was first established.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
Cānzhī Zhèngshì Yēlǜ Shù was dismissed.
In the eighth month, on the *bǐngwǔ* day,
since Zuǒchéngxiàng Áng had stripped and beaten his sister-in-law,
an order was given to beat him with a staff.
On the *wùshēn* day,
Yùshǐ Dàfū Gāo Zhēn was appointed Sīkōng,
retaining his position as Yùshǐ Dàfū.
In the ninth month, on the Jǐwèi day,
a game of polo was played at Chángwǔ Diàn,
and the common people were allowed to watch.
On the Xīnyǒu day,
Xiāo Zé, Shàngshū of the Lìbù, was appointed Cānzhī Zhèngshì.
On the Guǐhài day,
there was a hunt in the nearby suburbs.
On the Dīngmǎo day,
the Emperor reached Shùnzhōu.
Tàishī and Lǐng Sānshěng Shì Túshā Dāngōng passed away.
That night,
the Emperor returned to the palace.
On the Yǐhài day,
there was another hunt in the nearby suburbs.
In the tenth month, on the Gēngchén day, which was the first day of the month,
Hán Wáng Hēng, the Yǐn of Guǎngníng, was executed.
On the Gēngyín day,
the Emperor returned to the palace.
On the Gēngzǐ day,
Wēndū Sīzhōng, who had retired from his post as Zuǒ Chéngxiàng, was reinstated as Tàifù and Lǐng Sānshěng Shì.
Bái Yàngōng, Shìláng of the Xíngbù, and others were appointed as envoys to offer congratulations to Sòng on the New Year.
In the eleventh month, on the Wùchén day,
the Emperor commanded that all his female cousins be assigned to various imperial concubines,
to enter and exit the Forbidden City,
and engage in promiscuous activities with them.
The inner chambers were covered with mats,
and they played games naked.
That month,
the Huìmín Jú was established for the first time.
Gāolí sent envoys to express gratitude for the birthday gifts.
In the twelfth month, on the Yǐyǒu day,
Tàifù Wēndū Sīzhōng was appointed Tàishī,
retaining his position as Lǐng Sānshěng Shì.
Zhāng Tōnggǔ, Píngzhāng Zhèngshì, was appointed Sītú,
retaining his position as Píngzhāng Zhèngshì.
In the third year, in the first month, on the Jǐyǒu day, which was the first day of the month,
Sòng, Gāolí, and Xià sent envoys to offer congratulations.
On the Xīnyǒu day,

Dà** (a character with a grass radical on top, and a '口' radical on the left and a '咢' radical on the right, which is difficult to transcribe, so I'm leaving it as 'Dà●'), Pàn Dōngjīng Liúshǒu, was appointed Tàifù,
and Lǐng Sānshěng Shì.
On the Jiǎzǐ day,
it was the Emperor's birthday,
and Sòng, Gāolí, and Xià sent envoys to offer congratulations.
In the second month, on the Rénwǔ day,
Āng, the Zuǒ Chéngxiàng, was appointed Tàiwèi and Shūmìshǐ.
Zhāng Hào, the Yòu Chéngxiàng, was appointed Zuǒ Chéngxiàng and concurrent Shìzhōng.
Púshàn Shīgōng, the Shūmìshǐ, was appointed Yòu Chéngxiàng and concurrent Zhōngshū Lìng.
Zhāng Zhōngfú, Shàngshū Zuǒ Chéng, was dismissed.
Zhāng Huī, the Yòu Chéng, was appointed Píngzhāng Zhèngshì.

Liú** (a character with a grass radical on top, and a '口' radical on the left and a '咢' radical on the right, which is difficult to transcribe, so I'm leaving it as 'Liú●'), Cānzhī Zhèngshì, was appointed Zuǒ Chéng.
Xiāo Zé, Cānzhī Zhèngshì, was appointed Yòu Chéng.
Cài Sōngnián, Shàngshū of the Lìbù, was appointed Cānzhī Zhèngshì.
In the third month, on the Rénzǐ day,
Zuǒ Chéngxiàng Zhāng Hào and Píngzhāng Zhèngshì Zhāng Huī were each flogged twenty times
for sitting below the monk Fǎbǎo whenever they met him,
thus losing the dignity of high officials.
Monk Fǎbǎo was flogged two hundred times for his presumptuousness.
On the Yǐmǎo day,
the Emperor ordered Yúnfēng Sì in Dàfáng Shān to be designated as the imperial mausoleum,
and a temporary palace to be built at its foot.
On the Gēngwǔ day,
Lǐ Tōng, Zuǒ Sī Lángzhōng, was appointed as an envoy to offer congratulations to Sòng on its birthday.
In the summer, in the fourth month, on the Dīngchǒu day, which was the first day of the month,
a dim fog filled all directions,
and the sun had no light,
for a total of seventeen days.
In the fifth month, on the Dīngwèi day, which was the first day of the month,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the Guǐchǒu day,
the great palace in Nánjīng caught fire.
On the Yǐmǎo day,
the Emperor ordered Jīng, Pàn Dàzōngzhèng Shì, and others to go to Shàngjīng
to respectfully move the imperial coffins (zǐgōng) of Tàizǔ and Tàizōng.
On the Bǐngyín day,
the Emperor went to Dàfáng Shān
to construct the imperial mausoleum.
In the sixth month, on the Bǐngxū day,
the Emperor ascended Bǎochāng Mén to watch wrestling,
and the common people were allowed to watch.
On the Yǐwèi day,
the Emperor ordered Yòu Chéngxiàng Púshàn Shīgōng and Dàzōngzhèng Chéng Hú Bálǔ to go to Shàngjīng
to respectfully move the imperial mausoleum and welcome the Empress Dowager from Yǒngshòu Gōng.
In the seventh month, on the Guǐchǒu day,
Venus was seen in daylight.
On the Xīnyǒu day,
the Emperor went to Dàfáng Shān
and flogged Yēlǜ Ānlǐ, Tíjiǔ Yíngzào Guānlìbù Shàngshū, and others.
On the Yǐhài day,
the Emperor returned to the palace.
In the eighth month, on the Rénwǔ day,
the Emperor went to Dàfáng Shān.
On the Jiǎshēn day,
the earth was broken,
and each worker was given
one bolt of silk.
That day,
the Emperor returned to the palace.
On the Jiǎwǔ day,
Píngzhāng Zhèngshì Xiāo Yù was sent to Guǎngníng to welcome and sacrifice to the ancestral imperial coffins.
On the Yǐwèi day,
the number of performers in the Jiàofáng was increased.
On the Gēngzǐ day,
Jìng Sìhuī, Zuǒ Xuānhuī Shǐ, Wū Jūrén, Tóngzhī Xuānhuī Shì, and officials of the Shàngshí were flogged.
In the ninth month, on the Wùshēn day,
Píngzhāng Zhèngshì Zhāng Huī welcomed and sacrificed to the imperial coffins in Zōngzhōu.
On the Yǐmǎo day,
the Emperor said to the prime ministers and officials of the Zuǒ Sī:
"Affairs of the court
are especially dependent on discretion and secrecy.
Yesterday, when Zhāng Zhōngfú and Zhào Qìng were granted hereditary official positions,
the official document had not yet arrived,
but it was already known.
This was all revealed by you.
Dare anyone do it again,
they will be executed without pardon."
On the Jǐwèi day,
the Emperor went to Dàfáng Shān.
On the Gēngshēn day,
the Emperor returned to the palace.
On the Bǐngyín day,
Nàhé Chūnnián, Diànqián Dū Diǎnjiǎn, was appointed Cānzhī Zhèngshì.
On the Dīngmǎo day,
the Emperor personally welcomed the imperial coffins and the Empress Dowager at Shāliú Hé,
and ordered two bundles of staffs to be held by his attendants.
Kneeling before the Empress Dowager,
he said:
"Your son is unfilial,
and has long neglected your comfort and care.
I wish to be severely flogged."
The Empress Dowager helped him up,
and said:
"Even common people cherish
a son who can manage the household;
how much more so do I cherish a son like this."
She shouted at those holding the staffs to retreat.
On the Gēngwǔ day,
the Emperor hunted,
and personally shot a roe deer to offer to the imperial coffins.
On the Rénshēn day,
the Emperor arrived from Shāliú Hé.
In the tenth month, on the Bǐngzǐ day,
the Empress Dowager arrived in Zhōngdū,
residing in Shòukāng Gōng.
On the Wùyín day,
the ancestral tablets (shénzhǔ) were temporarily enshrined in Yánshèng Sì.
A libation was offered to the imperial coffins in the eastern suburbs,
and mourning was observed.
On the Jǐmǎo day,
the imperial coffins arrived in Zhōngdū.
Dà'ān Diàn was renamed Pīchéng Diàn,
and the coffins were placed there.
On the Rénwǔ day,
the Emperor ordered officials of the provincial and departmental bureaus to handle affairs in informal attire,
and no death sentences were to be reported for one month.
On the Xīnmǎo day,
an announcement was made at Pīchéng Diàn.
On the Yǐwèi day,
the Emperor went to the temporary palace (zōugōng),
and conferred the posthumous title Cíxiàn Huánghòu upon Yǒngníng Huáng Tàihòu.
On the Dīngyǒu day,
the temporary palace at Dàfáng Shān was completed,
and named Pánníng.
On the Wùxū day,
the Emperor returned to the palace.
On the Jǐhài day,
Yēlǜ Guīyī, Hànlín Xuéshì Chéngzhǐ, and others were appointed as envoys to offer congratulations to Sòng on the New Year.
In the eleventh month, on the Yǐsì day, which was the first day of the month,
the imperial coffins departed from Pīchéng Diàn.
On the Wùshēn day,
the ceremony for the imperial mausoleum was completed.
On the Jiǎyín day,
an edict was issued to grant a universal promotion of one rank to all civil and military officials, both inside and outside the court.
The rent and taxes for the fourth year of Zhēnyuán were all exempted.
Soldiers who had been stationed in garrisons for a long time without rotation
were each granted three bolts of silk and three taels of silver.
All officials offered congratulations.
On the Bǐngchén day,
a banquet was held for all officials at Tàihé Diàn.
On the Dīngmǎo day,
the ancestral tablets were enshrined in Tàimiào.
On the Wùchén day,
all officials offered congratulations.
On the Xīnwèi day,
there was a hunt in the nearby suburbs.
In the twelfth month, on the Jǐchǒu day,
the Emperor returned to the palace.
The trees were covered in ice (Mùbīng).
On the Yǐwèi day,
the Emperor paid homage to the Empress Dowager at Shòukāng Gōng.
On the Jǐhài day,
Tàifù and Lǐng Sānshěng Shì Dà● passed away.
The Emperor personally attended his mourning and wept,
and ordered the relevant departments to suspend work and prohibit music for three days.
In the first month of the first year of Zhènglóng, on the day guǐmǎo (the first day of the month),
Song, Gāolí, and Xià sent envoys to offer congratulations.
On the day jǐyǒu,
the assembled ministers respectfully presented the honorable title Shèngwén Shénwǔ Huángdì to the emperor.
Since the ninth month, the emperor had suspended court audiences,
often not appearing for several months.
When there were urgent memorials,
he would summon the directors of the Left and Right Bureaus to review them in his bedchamber.
On the day gēngxū,
he began to hold court audiences again.
On the day wùwǔ,
his birthday,
Song, Gāolí, and Xià sent envoys to offer congratulations.
On the day yǐchǒu,
he watched a wrestling performance.
The Secretariats of the Central and Gatekeeper Departments were abolished.
Tài Shī and Líng Sānshěng Shì Wēndū Sīzhōng was appointed Shàngshū Lìng;
Tài Wèi and Shūmì Shǐ Áng was appointed Tài Bǎo;
Yòuchéngxiàng Púsàn Shīgōng was appointed Tài Wèi and Shūmì Shǐ.
Zuǒchéng Liú Wō and Yòuchéng Xiāo Zé were dismissed.
Cānzhī Zhèngshì Cài Sōngnián was appointed Shàngshū Yòuchéng.
Shūmì Fùshǐ Xiāo Huáizhōng was dismissed.
Lìbù Shàngshū Yēlǜ Ānlǐ was appointed Shūmì Fùshǐ.
Píngzhāng Zhèngshì Xiāo Yù was appointed Yòuchéngxiàng.
Píngzhāng Zhèngshì Zhāng Huī was dismissed.
The office of Píngzhāng Zhèngshì was no longer filled.
In the second month, on the day guǐyǒu (the first day of the month),
the reign title was changed to Zhènglóng,
and a general amnesty was declared.
On the day gēngchén,
the emperor watched the Buddha procession from Xuānhuá Mén,
and bestowed five hundred bolts of silk, fifty rolls of colored fabric, and five hundred taels of silver upon the monks of various temples.
On the day xīnsì,
the seals of all internal and external government offices were revised and re-established.
On the day yǐwèi,
Sītú Zhāng Tōnggǔ retired.
On the day gēngzǐ,
the emperor visited the imperial tombs.
On the day xīnchǒu,
he returned to the capital.
In the third month, on the day rényín (the first day of the month),
regulations for official duties and court attendance were first established.
The military guard was also abolished.
On the day gēngshēn,
Zuǒ Xuānhuī Shǐ Jìng Sìhuī and others were appointed envoys to congratulate Song on its emperor's birthday.
In the fourth month,
Tài Wèi and Shūmì Shǐ Púsàn Shīgōng was reinstated to his former position due to his father's mourning.
In the fifth month, on the day xīnhài,
Xiūróng Ānshì, a court lady, was possessed by a demon,
dancing and shouting in the palace.
An order was given to execute her.
In this month,
the Zhènglóng official system was promulgated and implemented.
In the sixth month, on the day gēngchén,
Tiānshuǐ Jùn Gōng Zhào Huán passed away.
On the day bǐngxū,
Shàngshū Yòuchéng Cài Sōngnián was appointed Zuǒchéng;
Shūmì Fùshǐ Yēlǜ Ānlǐ was appointed Yòuchéng;
Fùmǎ Dūwèi Wūgǔlún Dānghǎi was appointed Shūmì Fùshǐ.
In the seventh month, on the day jǐyǒu,
Tài Bǎo Áng was ordered to go to Shàngjīng
to escort the coffins of the founder and his descendants.
In the eighth month, on the day dīngchǒu,
the emperor went to Dàfáng Shān to inspect the imperial tombs.
In the tenth month, on the day yǐyǒu,
the founder and ten subsequent emperors were buried at Dàfáng Shān.
On the day dīngyǒu,
the emperor returned to the palace.
In the intercalary month, on the day jǐhài (the first day of the month),
the imperial tomb ceremony was completed,
and the assembled ministers offered congratulations.
On the day jiǎchén,
the Huíhú envoy Yīnshù Wūlónggǔ came to offer tribute.
On the day gēngyín,
Yòuchéngxiàng Xiāo Yù, Zuǒchéng Cài Sōngnián, Yòuchéng Yēlǜ Ānlǐ, Yùshǐ Zhōngchéng Mǎ Fěng, and others were flogged.
In the eleventh month, on the day jǐsì (the first day of the month),
Yòusī Lángzhōng Liáng Qiú and others were appointed envoys to congratulate Song on the New Year.
On the day guǐsì,
the reception of the Buddha on the eighth day of the second month was prohibited.
In the first month of the second year, on the day wùchén (the first day of the month),
Song, Gāolí, and Xià sent envoys to offer congratulations.
On the day gēngchén,
Venus was seen in broad daylight.
On the day guǐwèi,
his birthday,
Song, Gāolí, and Xià sent envoys to offer congratulations.
On the day gēngyín,
Gōngbù Shìláng Hán Xī was appointed Tóngzhī Xuānhuīyuàn Shì.
As Xī did not express gratitude,
he was flogged one hundred and twenty times
and stripped of his conferred office.
In the second month, on the day xīnchǒu,
the rituals for the seasonal sacrifices of animals at the Imperial Ancestral Temple were first established.
On the day guǐmǎo,
the ranks of enfeoffment for imperial princes and below were revised.
An office was ordered to be established to reclaim the credentials of both living and deceased officials.
For those living, officials of the second rank and above;
for those deceased, officials of the first rank.
These were to be reviewed and ranks reduced as appropriate.
All public and private documents
that contained the character for "king" (王)
were ordered to be destroyed within a set deadline.
Even tomb monuments and epitaphs were exhumed and destroyed.
In the third month, on the day bǐngyín (the first day of the month),
Gāolí sent envoys to congratulate the emperor on receiving his honorable title.
In the fourth month, on the day wùxū,
Jǐngxuān Huángdì was posthumously demoted to Fēng Wáng.
Qiānshū Xuānhuīyuàn Shì Zhāng Zhé was appointed envoy to Gāolí for special bestowals.
Sùzhí Jiāngjūn Wēndūn Wòhē was appointed envoy to Xià for special bestowals.
In the sixth month, on the day yǐwèi,
Cānzhī Zhèngshì Nàhé Chūnnián passed away.
Lǐbù Shàngshū Yēlǜ Shǒusù and others were appointed envoys to congratulate Song on its emperor's birthday.
In the eighth month, on the day guǐmǎo,
the Dēngwényuàn was first established.
On the day jiǎyín,
the Shàngjīng Liúshǒusī was abolished.
In the ninth month, on the day yǐchǒu,
Sùzhí Jiāngjūn Púsàn Wūlǐhēi was appointed envoy to Xià for its emperor's birthday.
On the day wùzǐ,
the Hùjià Jūn was abolished,
and the Lóngxiáng Hǔbù Jūn was established.
The clerical officials of the Shàngshūshěng were dismissed from their posts and sent out as local officials.
That autumn,
locusts plagued Zhōngdū, Shāndōng, and Hédōng.
In the tenth month, on the day rényín,
an imperial edict ordered Huìníng Fǔ to demolish old palaces, residences of prominent families, and Chǔqìng Sì,
and to level their sites for cultivation.
On the day dīngwèi,
the sale of ancient artifacts to other territories was prohibited.
On the day yǐmǎo,
copper coins were first minted.
In the eleventh month, on the day xīnwèi,
Shìwèi Qīnjūn Fùzhǐhuīshǐ Gāo Zhùbùgǔ and others were appointed envoys to congratulate Song on the New Year.
In the twelfth month, on the day jǐhài,
Shìwèi Qīnjūn Dūzhǐhuīshǐ Gēshíliè Liángbì was appointed Cānzhī Zhèngshì.
In the first month of the third year, on the day rényǐn (the first day of the month),
Song, Gāolí, and Xià sent envoys to offer congratulations.
On the day bǐngyín,
as his son, Shěnsī Ābùsǐ, did not recover,
Tài Yī Fùshǐ Xiè Yǒuzhèng and the wet nurse were executed.
On the day dīngchǒu,
his birthday,
Song, Gāolí, and Xià sent envoys to offer congratulations.
On the day jǐmǎo,
Yòu Jiànyì Dàfū Yáng Bóxióng was flogged.
In the second month, on the day réchén (the first day of the month),
coin minting offices were first established in the capital and Jīngzhào.
On the day jiǎwǔ,
envoys were dispatched to inspect the gold, silver, copper, and iron smelters along the routes.
In the third month, on the day xīnyǒu (the first day of the month),
the Imperial Astronomy Bureau reported a solar eclipse,
but it was not observed.
An order was issued that henceforth, upon a solar eclipse,
it should be reported directly to the emperor
and not publicly announced.
On the day xīnsì,
Bīngbù Shàngshū Xiāo Gōng and others were appointed envoys to congratulate Song on its emperor's birthday.
In the fourth month, on the day bǐngchén,
Shūmì Fùshǐ Wūgǔlún Dānghǎi was dismissed.
Běijīng Liúshǒu Zhāng Huī was appointed Shūmì Fùshǐ.
In the sixth month, on the day rénchén,
locusts entered the capital.
In the seventh month, on the day gēngshēn,
his son Guǎngyáng was enfeoffed as Téng Wáng.
On the day jiǎshēn,
Yòuchéngxiàng Xiāo Yù was appointed Sītú;
Shàngshū Zuǒchéng Cài Sōngnián was appointed Yòuchéngxiàng;
Yòuchéng Yēlǜ Ānlǐ was appointed Zuǒchéng;
Cānzhī Zhèngshì Gēshíliè Liángbì was appointed Yòuchéng;
Zuǒ Xuānhuī Shǐ Jìng Sìhuī and Lìbù Shàngshū Lǐ Tōng were appointed Cānzhī Zhèngshì.
〔一一〕
In the ninth month, on the day jǐwèi,
Venus transited the sky.
On the day jiǎzǐ,
Téng Wáng Guǎngyáng passed away.
On the day gēngwǔ,
Sùzhí Jiāngjūn Ālǔbǎo was appointed envoy to Xià for its emperor's birthday.
On the day dīngchǒu,
Jiàofāng Tídiǎn Gāo Cúnfú was appointed envoy to Gāolí for its emperor's birthday.
On the day xīnsì,
two meng'an (military units) stationed in Zhōngdū were relocated to Nánjīng,
and Lìbù Shàngshū Lǐ Dūn and others were dispatched to allocate land for their settlement.
In the tenth month, on the day wùxū,
an imperial edict was issued to the Shàngshūshěng:
"For all matters that are deemed inappropriate,
permission is granted to submit a petition to the Dēngwén Jiǎnyuàn.
The court shall classify and present these for imperial review,
after which they shall be handed over to the Yùshǐ Tái for investigation."
In the eleventh month, on the day Xīnyǒu,
Sū Bǎohéng, Grand Secretary of the Ministry of Works, and others were appointed envoys to congratulate the Sòng on the New Year.
On the day Guǐhài,
an edict was issued to officials to diligently govern and bring peace to the people.
On the day Guǐwèi,
Yēlǜ Ānlǐ, Assistant Administrator of the Left in the Department of State Affairs, was dismissed.
Lǐ Tōng, Participant in Political Affairs, was recalled from mourning leave
and reinstated to his former position.
An edict ordered Zhāng Hào, Grand Administrator of the Left, and Jìng Sìhuī, Participant in Political Affairs, to construct palaces in Nánjīng.
In the twelfth month, on the day Yǐmǎo,
Zhāng Huī, Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs, was appointed Assistant Administrator of the Left in the Department of State Affairs.
Gāo Zhàohé, formerly Administrator of Guīdé and retired, was recalled to serve as Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs.
In the fourth year, in the first month, on the day Bǐngchén, the new moon,
envoys from Sòng, Gāolì, and Xià came to offer congratulations.
The Emperor paid respects to the Empress Dowager at Shòukāng Gōng.
On the day Dīngsì,
Gāo Zhēn, Grand Censor, passed away.
On the day Gēngshēn,
the law concerning private border crossings was revised
and made punishable by death.
On the day Xīnyǒu,
the trade markets in Fèngxiáng, Táng, Dèng, Yǐng, Cài, Gǒng, Táo, and Jiāoxī were abolished,
and a market was established in Sìzhōu.
On the day Xīnwèi,
the Emperor's birthday,
envoys from Sòng, Gāolì, and Xià came to offer congratulations.
In the second month, on the day Jǐchǒu,
Xǔ Lín, Left Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Merit, was appointed Grand Censor.
On the day Dīngwèi,
the walls of Zhōngdū were repaired.
Warships were built in Tōngzhōu.
An edict was issued to the Grand Ministers regarding the campaign against the Sòng.
All *méng'ān móukè* soldiers in various circuits, aged between twenty and fifty,
were registered.
Even those with elderly parents or many able-bodied men in the family were not permitted to stay and attend to them.
In the third month, on the day Bǐngchén, the new moon,
Xiāo Gōng, Grand Secretary of the Ministry of War, was dispatched to plan the border with the Xià state.
Envoys were dispatched separately to various circuits' General Administration Offices to supervise the manufacture of weapons.
In the fourth month, on the day Xīnchǒu,
it was ordered to increase the stipends for the soldiers of Quánshuǐ and Bìkuò camps in the Shāndōng Circuit.
On the day Gēngxū,
an edict ordered all old military equipment stored in various circuits to be brought to Zhōngdū.
At this time, palaces were being built in Nánjīng,
and the cost of military equipment and supplies manufactured in Zhōngdū and other regions was all levied from the people.
A foot of arrow feather cost up to a thousand cash,
and in villages, oxen were often slaughtered to provide sinews and hides.
Even magpies, dogs, and pigs were not spared.
On the day Xīnhài,
Zhāng Huī, Assistant Administrator of the Left in the Department of State Affairs, and Xǔ Lín, Grand Censor, were dismissed.
Túdān Zhēn, Administrator of Dàxīng, was appointed Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs.
Wáng Kědào, Supervisor of the Imperial Library, and others were appointed envoys to congratulate the Sòng on their birthday.
In the eighth month,
an edict ordered the requisition of horses from various circuits,
based on household population.
Over 560,000 horses were counted,
with some wealthy households possessing up to sixty.
Households were ordered to feed and care for them themselves while awaiting further orders.
On the day Jǐmǎo,
Cài Sōngnián, Grand Administrator of the Right in the Department of State Affairs, passed away.
In the ninth month,
Wányán Dájì, Academician in Attendance at the Hanlin Academy, was appointed envoy to Gāolì for their birthday,
and Jiāgǔ Tàlǎn, General of the Palace Guard, was appointed envoy to the Xià state for their birthday.
In the tenth month, on the day Yǐhài,
the Emperor hunted in the near suburbs
and observed shipbuilding in Tōngzhōu.

Hégěliè Liángbì, Assistant Administrator of the Right in the Department of State Affairs, and Túdān Zhēn, Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs, were granted ceremonial swords for entry into the palace.
In the eleventh month, on the day Jiǎchén,
Shī Yíshēng, Academician in Attendance and Lecturer at the Hanlin Academy, and others were appointed envoys to congratulate the Sòng on the New Year.
In the twelfth month, on the day Yǐmǎo,
an envoy from Sòng announced the mourning for their mother, Lady Wèi.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
Venus was seen in broad daylight.
On the day Yǐchǒu,
Dà Huáizhōng, Left Deputy Grand Inspector, and others were appointed envoys to offer condolences to the Sòng.
On the day Yǐhài,
Qí Zǎi, Chief Imperial Physician, submitted a memorial advising against attacking the Sòng,
[一二] and was executed.
In the fifth year, in the first month, on the day Gēngchén, the new moon,
envoys from Sòng, Gāolì, and Xià came to offer congratulations.
On the day Yǐwèi,
the Emperor's birthday,
envoys from Sòng, Gāolì, and Xià came to offer congratulations.
In the second month, on the day Rénzǐ,
an envoy from Sòng presented relics left by the Empress Dowager.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
Venus was seen in broad daylight.
On the day Xīnwèi,
there was an earthquake in Hédōng and Shǎnxī.
In Zhènrong and Déshùn prefectures, there was a great wind
that destroyed houses,
and many people were crushed to death.
On the day Jiǎxū,
Gāo Zhí, Envoy of Introduction, and Hǎigǒu, Senior Clerk of the Ministry of Punishments, were dispatched to supervise the captured bandits separately.
All were to be executed by slow slicing,
or by sawing, burning, skinning, and severing hands and feet.
Furthermore, *qiānhù* and *móukè* of garrisons were warned that
if any future captures occurred,
they too would be executed,
and officials of the General Administration Offices would also be punished.
In the third month, on the day Xīnsì,
Zhāng Wàng and Xú Yuán, commoners of Dōnghǎi County, rebelled.

Xú Wén, Supervisor of Waterways; Zhāng Hóngxìn, Commander of Infantry; Lǐ Wéizhōng, acting Administrator of Dàxīng; and Xiāo Awā, General of the Palace Guard, were dispatched with a fleet of nine hundred ships
to suppress them by sea.
The Emperor instructed them,
"My intention is not merely for one district,
but to test the navy."
On the day Gēngzǐ,
Xiāo Yù, Grand Minister of Education and Administrator of Imperial Clan Affairs, was appointed Grand Censor,
retaining his position as Grand Minister of Education.
Hégěliè Liángbì, Assistant Administrator of the Right in the Department of State Affairs, was appointed Assistant Administrator of the Left.
Liú Chángyán, formerly Commissioner of the Hénghǎi Army and retired, was recalled to serve as Assistant Administrator of the Right.
In the fourth month, on the day Gēngxū,
Concubine Zhāo Púchá Ālǐhū was found guilty and granted death.
On the day Jiǎyín,
Yēlǜ Yì, Defense Commissioner of Sùzhōu, was found to have acted improperly during an embassy to Sòng.
He was flogged two hundred times
and stripped of his title.
On the day Jiǎxū,
Venus was seen in broad daylight.
In the sixth month,
Xú Wén and others defeated the rebels Zhāng Wàng and Xú Yuán,
and Dōnghǎi was pacified.
In the seventh month, on the day Xīnsì,
an edict ordered that those misled by Xú Yuán and Zhāng Wàng in Dōnghǎi County
should all be released.
On the day Rénwǔ,
Zhāng Hóngxìn, who had been ordered to suppress the rebels,
feigned illness and lingered in Láizhōu,
drinking and feasting with courtesans.
He was flogged two hundred times.
On the day Guǐmǎo,
envoys were dispatched to conscript Han Chinese soldiers from various circuits.
In the eighth month, on the day Bǐngwǔ, the new moon,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the day Xīnhài,
it was ordered that the Monopoly Bureau and the Printing and Issuing Office for paper currency should relocate to Nánjīng.
On the day Jǐsì,
Túdān Zhēn, Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs, was dismissed.
Túdān Yǒngnián, Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, was appointed Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs.
On the day Xīnwèi,
the Emperor visited the imperial tombs,
and seeing harvesters in the fields,
asked about their harvest,
and bestowed clothing upon them.
In the ninth month, on the day Jǐmǎo,
the Emperor returned to the palace.
In the tenth month, on the day Gēngwǔ,
Wányán Púlián, Imperial Guard, and twenty-four others were dispatched to supervise the capture of bandits in Shāndōng, Hédōng, Héběi, and Zhōngdū.
Thirty thousand sailors were registered from various circuits.
In the eleventh month, on the day Yǐyǒu,
Púsǎn Wúzhě, Administrator of Jǐnán, and others were appointed envoys to congratulate the Sòng on the New Year.
Liú Chángyán, Assistant Administrator of the Right in the Department of State Affairs, was dismissed.
The Imperial Guard Office was ordered to transfer its responsibilities to the Dàxīng Prefecture.
Commanders and Deputy Commanders of the Left and Right Elite Cavalry were established,
subordinate to the Grand Inspectorate.
Commanders and Deputy Commanders of Infantry were established,
[一三] subordinate to the Bureau of Military Merit.
In the twelfth month, on the day Guǐchǒu,
military personnel and civilians in Zhōngdū, Héběi, Shāndōng, Hénán, Hédōng, and Jīngzhào were forbidden from trapping birds and beasts, and from keeping eagles and falcons.
On the day Wùchén,
court officials were forbidden from drinking alcohol.
Violators would be executed.
Envoys from the Three States were exempt from this prohibition when feasting.
[一四]
In the first month of the sixth year, on the *jiǎxū* day,
Sòng, Gāolì, and Xià sent envoys to congratulate.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
the Administrator of the Imperial Clan Court, Túdān Zhēn, the Yìdū Prefect, Jīng, the Military Commissioner of Ānwǔ Commandery, Shuǎng, and the Grand General of the Imperial Guard, Āsù, drank wine.
Because they were close relatives,
Zhēn was beaten with seventy strokes,
and all others received a hundred strokes.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
the Emperor was about to visit Nánjīng.
Sītú and Grand Censor Xiāo Yù was made Prefect of Dàxīng,
and his Sītú title remained as before.
The Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, Túdān Yǒngnián, was dismissed.
Héshíliè Zhìníng, the Metropolitan Inspector-General, was made Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
it was the Emperor's birthday,
and Sòng, Gāolì, and Xià sent envoys to congratulate.
On the *guǐsì* day,
the Emperor ordered the Chancellor of Political Affairs, Lǐ Tōng, to instruct the Sòng envoy, Xú Dù, and others, saying:
"I once followed King Liáng's army
and enjoyed the customs and climate of Nánjīng.
I have always wished to tour there.
Now the construction work is nearing completion,
and I plan to go to Hénán by the end of the second month.
Imperial tours of inspection
have existed since ancient times.
As there are many open lands to the west of the Huái River,
I wish to hunt there.
My retinue will not exceed ten thousand men.
Moreover, the mausoleums of my ancestors are here;
how could I stay there for long?
You all should return and inform your lord,
ordering the relevant officials to proclaim my intention,
so that the people of Huáinán do not harbor doubts or fears."
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
an edict ordered that the prefectures and counties from Zhōngdū to Hénán Fǔ through which the Emperor would pass should provide two thousand cavalrymen for the hunt.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
Púchá Āhǔdié Yìchá was executed.
Yìchá,
born of Princess Qìngyí,
was raised in the palace since childhood.
The Emperor repeatedly wished to take her as a consort,
but the Empress Dowager disapproved.
By this time,
she was executed for a crime.
In the second month, on the *yǐsì* day,
the consort of Prince Wèi, Xiāng, and the Left Commissioner of the Bureau of Xuanhui, Xǔ Lín, were flogged.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
the Chancellor of Political Affairs, Lǐ Tōng, was made Right Grand Councilor of the Department of State Affairs.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
it was forbidden for the imperial retinue to hunt indiscriminately and disturb the populace.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
sailors from all circuits were conscripted to transport warships.
On the *guǐhài* day,
the Emperor departed from Zhōngdū.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
he arrived at Ānsù Zhōu.
In the third month, on the *jǐmǎo* day,
Hénán's Běimáng Shān was renamed Tàipíng Shān.
Those who used the old name would be punished for violating the regulation.
On the *dīnghài* day,
as the Emperor was approaching Huòjiā,
a man submitted a memorial concerning affairs.
He was beheaded,
and what he said was not heard.
On the *guǐsì* day,
the Emperor arrived at Hénán Fǔ.
He then went out hunting
and visited the hot springs of Rǔ Zhōu,
inspecting the site for an interim palace.
From Zhōngdū to Hénán,
the wheat in all passing areas was completely trampled.
It was again forbidden for the imperial retinue to leave their posts arbitrarily or to tour, enjoy, and drink wine.
Violators were all to be executed,
but none complied.
An edict ordered the *móu'ān* of the interior to go to the mountains beyond to graze horses,
and to depart together in the autumn.
The wife of his brother Yǎn, Wūyán Shì, committed a crime
and was granted death.
Wūyán Shì's brother, Xíníliè, the Vice Commander of Cavalry and Infantry of Nánjīng, was also executed for a crime.
In the fourth month, on the *dīngwèi* day,
an edict ordered all officials to proceed to Nánjīng first to handle affairs.

The Department of State Affairs, the Bureau of Military Affairs, the Imperial Clan Court, the Bureau of Agricultural Promotion, the Grand Treasury, and the Lesser Treasury all accompanied the Emperor.
One official each from the Ministries of Personnel, Revenue, War, and Justice,
the Four Quarters Bureau,
and the Directorate of Waterways
were to remain.
Gāo Jǐngshān and others, who were Assistant Executive of the Bureau of Military Affairs, were made envoys to congratulate Sòng on its birthday.
On the *wùshēn* day,
an edict ordered the prefectures and counties within 150 *lǐ* of Rǔ Zhōu to appropriately dispatch merchants to the hot springs to set up a market.
An edict ordered the relevant officials to inquire with the Sòng people
regarding the establishment of forts and garrisons along the border in Cài, Yǐng, and Shòu prefectures.
On the *gēngxū* day,
the Emperor departed from Hénán Fǔ.
Qìdān Bùbǔ dashed down from a mountain
and lay in ambush by the roadside,
claiming he had rendered meritorious service in defeating the pirates of the Eastern Sea,
but was suppressed by Lǐ Wéizhōng.
He was immediately ordered to be beheaded.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
the Emperor arrived at Wēntāng.
The imperial retinue was cautioned not to cross the Rǔ River arbitrarily.
While the Emperor was hunting,
a fleeing deer charged him, causing him to fall off his horse,
and he vomited blood for several days.
Envoys were dispatched to conscript soldiers from all circuits.
In the fifth month, on the *gēngchén* day,
Grand Tutor and Grand Councilor of the Department of State Affairs, Nòuwǎn Wēndūsīzhōng, passed away.
The Qìdān tribes revolted,
and Xiāo Tūlà, a Right Guard General, and others were dispatched to suppress them.
In the sixth month, on the *guǐmǎo* day,
the Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, Púsàn Shīgōng, and the Grand Administrator of Xījīng, Xiāo Huáizhōng, were ordered to lead an army of ten thousand to suppress the Qìdān tribes.
The Emperor went from Rǔ Zhōu to Nánjīng.
On the *rénxū* day,
he arrived in the outskirts of Nánjīng,
where Left Chancellor Zhāng Hào led all officials to greet him.
That night,
a great wind
damaged the *chīwěi* ornament on Chéngtiān Mén.
On the *guǐhài* day,
the Emperor entered Nánjīng with the imperial ceremonial carriage.
In the seventh month, on the *dīnghài* day,
Left Chancellor Zhāng Hào was made Grand Tutor and Grand Councilor of the Department of State Affairs.
Sītú and Prefect of Dàxīng, Xiāo Yù, was made Left Grand Councilor of the Department of State Affairs.
Minister of Personnel, Bái Yàngōng, was made Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, Héshíliè Zhìníng, was made Prefect of Kāifēng.
Military Commissioner of Ānwǔ Commandery, Túdān Zhēn, was made Grand Censor.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,

money and silk were bestowed upon those who accompanied the Emperor on his journey, those who accompanied him on military campaigns, and *qiānhù* and *mòkè* (leaders of a thousand and a hundred households).
A large requisition of all horses in the realm was ordered.
More than 130 male descendants of the deceased Liáo Yēlǜ clan and the Sòng Zhào clan were executed.
In the eighth month, on the *rén'yín* day,
the bandit Dù Kuí from Shàn Zhōu rebelled and occupied the city.
Metropolitan Inspector-General Yēlǜ Zhàn and Vice Commander-in-chief of the Right Agile Cavalry, Dà Pán, were dispatched to suppress him.
Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, Bái Yàngōng, was made Commander-in-chief of the Northern Front Army,
with Prefect of Kāifēng, Héshíliè Zhìníng, as his deputy.
Grand Administrator of Zhōngdū, Wányán Gòuyīng, was made Commander-in-chief of the Northwestern Front Army,
to suppress the Qìdān.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
because she advised against the invasion of Sòng, the Empress Dowager Túdān Shì was assassinated in Níngdé Palace.
It was also ordered that she be immediately cremated within the palace,
her bones cast into the water,
and more than ten of her serving maids were also executed.
On the *guǐhài* day,
Right Guard General Xiāo Tūlà

and the leader of ten imperial guards, Wòlúbǎo, were executed. The families of Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs Púsàn Shīgōng, Grand Administrator of Běijīng Xiāo Zé, and Grand Administrator of Xījīng Xiāo Huáizhōng were exterminated.
Grand Councilor of the Department of State Affairs Zhāng Hào and Left Chancellor Xiāo Yù were flogged.
Grand Master of Ceremonies Zhāng Chóng was made envoy to congratulate Gāolì on its birthday,
and Xiāo Yìzhōng was made envoy to congratulate Xià Guó on its birthday.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
Gāo Fúniáng, a serving maid of the favored Empress Dowager, was enfeoffed as Lady of Yún Guó.
In the ninth month, on the *gēngwǔ* day,
Grand Protector and Administrator of the Imperial Clan Court, Áng, was made Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
His title of Grand Protector remained as before.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
the former Prefect of Shòu Zhōu, Máo Liánghǔ, was executed.
On the *gēngyín* day,
the bandit Wáng Jiǔ from Dàmíng Fǔ rebelled and occupied the city,
with his followers numbering tens of thousands.
Wherever he went, bandits rose up like bees,
some occupying cities and towns,
others securing mountains and marshes.
Some, with just tens of cavalry, would fly banners and march,
and the government troops dared not approach.
The Emperor also disliked hearing about banditry,
and those who reported it were immediately punished.
The Emperor personally led an army of thirty-two military superintendents to attack Sòng,
advancing from Shòuchūn.
Grand Protector and Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, Áng, was made Grand Commander of the Left Vanguard Army,
with Right Grand Councilor of the Department of State Affairs, Lǐ Tōng, as his deputy.
Left Grand Councilor of the Department of State Affairs, Héshíliè Liángbì, was made Grand Commander of the Right Vanguard Army,
with Administrator of the Imperial Clan Court, Wūyán Púlúhún, as his deputy.
Grand Censor Túdān Zhēn was made Left Army Inspector,
and Co-Administrator of the Imperial Clan Court, Túdān Yǒngnián, was made Right Army Inspector.
Left Commissioner of the Bureau of Xuanhui, Xǔ Lín, was made Left Chief Overseer,
and Prefect of Hénán, Púchá Wòlún, was made Right Chief Overseer.
All accompanied the expedition.
Minister of Works, Sū Bǎohéng, was made Commander-in-chief of the Naval Forces of the Eastern Zhè Circuit,
with Prefect of Yìdū, Zhèng Jiā, as his deputy,
to proceed directly to Lín'ān by sea.
Prefect of Tàiyuán, Liú É, was made Commander-in-chief of the Mobile Forces of the Hànnán Circuit,
with Prefect of Jìnán, Púsàn Wūzhě, as his deputy,
to advance from Cài Zhōu.
Prefect of Hézhōng, Túdān Héxǐ, was made Commander-in-chief of the Mobile Forces of the Western Shǔ Circuit,
with Prefect of Píngyáng, Zhāng Zhōngyàn, as his deputy,
to take Sànguān via Fèngxiáng,
and garrison troops to await further orders.
The three armies of Wǔshèng, Wǔpíng, and Wǔjié were the vanguard.
Túdān Zhēn separately led twenty thousand soldiers into Huái'yīn.
On the Jiǎwǔ day,
the Emperor departed from Nánjīng,
and decreed that the Empress and Crown Prince Guāngyīng should remain to guard the capital.
Shàngshū Lìng Zhāng Hào, Zuǒ Chéngxiàng Xiāo Yù, and Cānzhī Zhèngshì Jìng Sìhuī were to remain and manage provincial affairs.
On the Bǐngshēn day,
Venus was seen in daylight.
Soldiers and officers deserting from the army were continuously seen on the road.
Hésūguǎn Měng'ān Fúshòu and Dōngjīng Móukè Jīn Zhù and others first took up arms in Dàmíng,
and immediately led their units to desert and return.
Their followers numbered over ten thousand,
all publicly declaring on the road:
“We are now going to Dōngjīng
to establish a new Emperor!”
On the Yǐsì day of the tenth month,
due to gloomy weather, they lost their way,
and only reached the camp at the second drum (watch).
On the Bǐngwǔ day,
auspicious clouds were seen.
The Dōngjīng Liúshǒu and Cáoguógōng, Wūlù, ascended the throne in Liáoyáng,
changed the era name to Dàdìng,
and issued a general amnesty.
He enumerated Hǎilíng's misdeeds: assassinating Empress Dowager Túdān Shì,
killing Tàizōng, the descendants of Zōnghàn and Zōngbì, and the princes including Zōngběn,
destroying the palaces of Shàngjīng,
killing Prince Yù of Liáo, Prince of Tiānshuǐ Commandery of Sòng, and the descendants of other princes, amounting to dozens of offenses.
On the Dīngwèi day,
the grand army crossed the Huái River,
and when approaching Lúzhōu,
a white deer was captured,
which was taken as an omen like King Wǔ's white fish.
Liú È of Hànnán Dào captured Tōnghuà Jūn, Jiǎngzhōu, and Xìnyáng Jūn.
Túdān Zhēn defeated Sòng general Wáng Quán at Xūyí,
and advanced to capture Yángzhōu.
The vanguard army reached Duànzhài;
all the Sòng garrison soldiers fled.
They defeated the Sòng army at Wèizǐqiáo,
and defeated the Sòng army at Cháoxiàn,
beheading two hundred.
They then reached Hézhōu.
Wáng Quán attacked during the night with over a thousand soldiers,
but was repelled by arrows.
The next day,
it rained.
The Sòng people burned their supplies and fled during the night.
At dawn, they pursued them,
but the Sòng people counter-attacked.
Měng'ān Hán Táng's army retreated,
and they suffered a defeat.
Wēndū Àolà fled north.
Āsàn, Deputy Commander of the Wǔjié Jūn, led the Měng'ān and Móukè to fight fiercely,
and repelled them.
Wáng Quán retreated and secured the south bank.
On the Guǐhài day,
the Emperor arrived at Hézhōu.
Āsàn and others were promoted and rewarded according to their achievements.
Túdān Héxǐ of Xīshǔ Dào was stationed at Sǎnguān.
The Sòng people attacked Làjiāchéng in Qínzhōu and Déshùnzhōu,
and captured them.
Sū Bǎohéng of Zhèdōng Dào fought the Sòng people on the sea route,
suffered a defeat,
and Deputy Commander Zhèng Jiā died.
On the Gēngwǔ day of the eleventh month,
Zuǒsī Lángzhōng Wūbùhē and others, upon hearing of the amnesty,
reported to the Emperor about the enthronement and change of era name in Dōngjīng.
The Emperor patted his thigh and sighed:
“I originally intended to conquer Sòng first and then change the era name to Dàdìng.
Is this not the will of Heaven?”
He then produced his document and showed it to them,
which indeed recorded his prior intention to change the era name.
He appointed Agricultural Promotion Commissioner Wányán Yuányí as Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs for Zhèxī Dào,
with Minister of Punishments Guō Ānguó as his deputy.
The Emperor garrisoned his army north of the river.
He sent Wǔpíng Zǒngguǎn Ālín to cross the river first to the south bank,
but they suffered a defeat.
The Emperor returned to Hézhōu,
and then advanced his troops to Yángzhōu.
On the Jiǎwǔ day,
the naval forces assembled at Guāzhōu Dù,
planning to cross the river the next day.
On the Yǐwèi day,
the army of Zhèxī Bīngmǎ Dūtǒngzhì Wányán Yuányí and others mutinied.
The Emperor was assassinated
and died,
at the age of forty.
Hǎilíng reigned for over ten years,
and always put on a façade to control his officials.
He refused geese presented by the Chief Steward of Imperial Cuisine to show frugality.
Yet, during hunting expeditions and stops,
he would make untimely demands,
and for a single goose or a single quail,
the people might pay tens of thousands to acquire it,
some even exchanging an ox for a quail.
Sometimes he would cover his clothes with a worn quilt
to show his close officials.
Sometimes he would wear patched clothes,
making sure the chroniclers saw it.
Sometimes he would take the stale rice of soldiers and eat it with the Chief Steward of Imperial Cuisine,
finishing almost all of the soldiers' rice first.
Sometimes, seeing a civilian cart stuck in a muddy swamp,
he would order his guards to get down and pull it out,
only proceeding after the cart was free.
When conversing casually with his close officials,
he would always cite virtuous rulers of antiquity to compare himself with.
He openly criticized high officials,
encouraging them to speak frankly.
He appointed people like Zhāng Zhòngkē as censors,
yet Qí Zǎi eventually died for his frank remonstrance.
He favored petty individuals,
and his official rewards were excessive.
If any of his attendants were idle officials,
and someone happened to call them by name,
he would immediately grant them a prominent rank.
He often placed gold between his cushions and mattresses;
if anyone expressed fondness for it,
he would allow them to take it themselves.
Yet he indulged in debauchery without regard for kinship,
and executed people without questioning their guilt.
When constructing the palaces in Nánjīng,
the cost of transporting a single timber reached twenty million (cash),
and the labor for pulling one cart required up to five hundred people.
The decoration of the palaces
was entirely covered in gold, then interspersed with five colors;
gold dust flew through the air like falling snow.
The cost of a single palace was in the hundreds of millions,
and after completion, it would be torn down again,
striving for the utmost opulence.
For his southern campaign, when building warships on the river,
he destroyed civilian houses for timber,
and boiled human fat for oil.
He exhausted the people's strength like horses and oxen,
and wasted financial resources like dirt and straw.
He emptied his own country to conquer another,
and consequently met his defeat.
The Dūdūfǔ placed his coffin in the Bānjīngguǎn in Nánjīng.
In the second year of Dàdìng,
he was demoted and enfeoffed as Hǎilíng Jùnwáng,
and given the posthumous name Yáng.
In the second month,
Shìzōng ordered Xiǎodǐ Lóushì and officials from Nánjīng to move his coffin to Níngdé Gōng.
In the fourth month,
he was buried in the burial ground of the princes in Lùmén Gǔ of Dàfáng Shān.
Twenty years later,
after Xīzōng was enshrined in the ancestral temple,
the relevant authorities reported:
“The crimes of Prince Yáng have not yet been rectified.
According to the precedent of Sīmǎ Lún, Prince of Zhào of Jìn, who deposed Emperor Huìdì and enthroned himself;
when Emperor Huìdì was restored,
Lún was executed
and reduced to a commoner.
Emperor Yáng's crimes surpassed those of Lún,
so he should not hold a princely enfeoffment,
nor should he be in the burial grounds of the princes.”
A decree was then issued to demote him to Hǎilíng Shùrén,
and he was reburied forty *lǐ* southwest of the imperial tombs.
Eulogy says: Hǎilíng possessed enough cunning to reject remonstrance,
and enough eloquence to whitewash his wrongs.
Wishing to be a ruler, he murdered his sovereign;
wishing to invade a country, he murdered his mother;
wishing to seize another's wife, he made her kill her husband.
The Sāngāng were utterly severed;
how can other matters even be discussed?
As for massacring his clan,
and eliminating loyal and good people,
wives, aunts, sisters, all were taken into his harem.
He was just about to use the armies of thirty-two commander-in-chiefs to conquer the world.
In the end, his perverse nature brought retribution,
and his life ended badly,
causing all future generations to name Hǎilíng as the foremost among immoral rulers.
How could one not be warned?
How could one not be warned?
Collation Notes
Annals Six: Shìzōng, Part One
Emperor Shìzōng Guāngtiān Xīngyùn Wéndé Wǔgōng Shèngmíng Rénxiào,
whose taboo name was Yōng,
originally named Wūlù,
was the grandson of Tàizǔ
and the son of Ruìzōng.
His mother was Empress Zhēnyì Lǐ Shì.
In the Guǐmǎo year, the seventh year of Tiānfǔ,
he was born in Shàngjīng.
His physique and appearance were remarkable.
He had a beautiful beard,
which extended past his abdomen.
On his chest, there were seven moles resembling the Big Dipper constellation.
He was benevolent and filial by nature,
calm and discerning.
He excelled at horsemanship and archery;
the people of the country regarded him as the best.
Whenever he went hunting,
the elders would all follow to watch him.
During the Huángtǒng reign,
he was, by imperial clan precedent, granted the title of Guānglù Dàfū,
and enfeoffed as Gē Wáng.
He served as Bīngbù Shàngshū.
At the beginning of the Tiāndé reign,
he was appointed judge of Huìníng Prefecture.
The following year,
he was appointed judge of the Grand Imperial Clan Affairs,
then transferred to be the Resident-General of Zhōngjīng,
and shortly thereafter transferred to Yānjīng.
Not long after,
he became the Administrator of Jìnán.
At the beginning of the Zhēnyuán reign,
he served as Resident-General of Xījīng.
In the third year,
he was transferred to Dōngjīng
and further enfeoffed as Zhào Wáng.
In the second year of Zhènglóng,
he was, by precedent, demoted in title to Zhèngguó Gōng,
and then promoted to Wèiguó Gōng.
In the third year,
he was again appointed Resident-General
and transferred to be enfeoffed as Cáoguó Gōng.
In the fifth month of the sixth year,
he was observing mourning for Empress Zhēnyì.
One day, as he was sleeping,
a red light illuminated the room,
and a yellow dragon appeared above his bedroom.
Also, he once saw a large star flow into the Resident-General's residence at night.
That year,
the Dōngliáng River swelled and overflowed,
abruptly reaching the city walls.
The water level was equal to the city,
and it breached through gaps in the parapet stones, flowing into the city.
The torrent was rushing like a surge.
The people in the city were terrified.
The emperor personally ascended the city wall,
raised a cup of wine and poured a libation,
and the water receded.
Hǎilíng marched south,
and the whole empire was in turmoil.
At this time,
able-bodied men from the Qìdān tribes were conscripted into the army.
The tribesmen were unwilling to go
and informed the envoy.
The envoy, anxious and fearing Hǎilíng, did not report it.
Consequently, the tribesmen rebelled.
At this point,
the leader of the regiment, Kuòlǐ, from Xiánpíng Prefecture, captured Hán Zhōu,
occupied Xiánpíng,
and was about to invade Dōngjīng.
In the eighth month,
he was reinstated as Resident-General of Dōngjīng.
Four hundred soldiers from Pó Sù Lù came to join in suppressing Kuòlǐ,
and he also recruited several hundred city youths who wished to be soldiers.
The emperor's maternal uncle, Lǐ Shí, the Assistant Sub-Prefect of Xīngzhōng, had been discharged due to illness,
and was residing in Liáoyáng.
On the day of Wùwǔ,
he departed from Dōngjīng,
leaving Shí in charge of the residence affairs.
Rebel scouts heard the drums shaking the heavens
and saw banners covering the fields.
They spread the word that the Duke's army of 100,000 was about to arrive.
The rebel multitude, upon reaching Shěnzhōu,
fled.
Coincidentally, Wūyán Chálà and others defeated the rebel army
and returned to Cháng’ān County.
Hǎilíng sent Wányán Móuyǎn, the Grand Administrator of Pó Sù Lù, to suppress the rebels,
and placed the troops under his command.
In the ninth month,
he arrived at Dōngjīng.
The Vice Resident-General Gāo Cúnfú,
whose daughter was in Hǎilíng's harem,
was ordered by Hǎilíng to monitor his daily life.
It happened that he had used surplus materials from making weapons to produce dozens of suits of armor.
Cúnfú openly declared,
"Why is the Resident-General making armor?"
He secretly sent someone to inform Hǎilíng.
Then, with the Judicial Officer Lǐ Yànlóng, under the pretext of playing polo,
he plotted treason.
Cúnfú's family member came to report their plot.
Lǐ Púsùyuè, the military administrator of Píngdìng, also reported the matter.
Hǎilíng had heard that the emperor was ill,
and had sent close attendants to observe his situation.
At this time,
he also sent Móuliánghǔ to make plans concerning the princes north of the Huái River.
The emperor knew of this
and was constantly troubled by hidden worries.
When he returned from suppressing Kuòlǐ and reached Qīnghé,
he met his former subordinate Liùjīn, who was traveling by post-horse from the south.
Liùjīn fully reported that Hǎilíng had killed his mother,
and killed his nephews Tánnú and Ālǐbái, as well as the Military Affairs Commissioner Púsàn Hūtǔ, etc.
He also said,
"He will also send people to harm the imperial clan brothers."
Upon hearing this,
the emperor became even more frightened.
When he heard that Cúnfú was plotting against him,
and that the matter already had evidence,
Lǐ Shí advised the emperor to take action early.
Thereupon,
under the pretext of discussing defenses against the rebels,
he summoned his officials to meet at Qīng'ān Temple.
Yànlóng arrived first.
Cúnfú only came after repeated summons,
and they were both apprehended in their seats.
That month,
clouds again came from the west,
and a yellow dragon appeared in the clouds.
On the day of Xīnchǒu in the tenth month,
Wányán Fúshòu, Gāo Zhōngjiàn, Lú Wànjiānú, and others, the commanders of the southern expedition, led their 20,000 troops from Shāndōng,
and Wányán Móuyǎn led 5,000 troops from Cháng’ān, all came to pledge allegiance.
Móuyǎn immediately paid his respects as a subject.
On the day of Yǐsì,
all the armies entered the city
and jointly attacked and killed Cúnfú and others.
That night,
the armies, clad in armor, guarded the imperial city.
On the day of Bǐngwǔ,
auspicious clouds appeared.
The officials and various armies urged him to ascend the throne.
He firmly declined for a long time.
Thereupon, he personally announced it at the Tàizǔ Temple,
returned to take his seat in the Xuānzhèng Hall,
and ascended the imperial throne.
He appointed Wányán Móuyǎn as Vice Grand Marshal of the Right,
Gāo Zhōngjiàn as Grand Marshal's Left Military Supervisor,
Wányán Fúshòu as Right Military Supervisor,
and Lú Wànjiānú as Jiedushi of Xiǎndé Commandery.
On the day of Dīngwèi,
a general amnesty was proclaimed,
and the reign era was changed to Dàdìng.
An imperial edict was issued, publicly enumerating dozens of Hǎilíng's crimes.
On the day of Jǐyǒu,
he feasted the generals and soldiers,
and bestowed official ranks and rewards, each according to their merits,
and further granted three years of tax exemption.
The southern expedition armies from Huìníng, Húlǐgǎi, Sùpín, and other routes,
met at the Shàngshū Province,
and petitioned to appoint those who had followed the army to fill vacancies in various bureaus, departments, and as officials.
The emperor said:
"The old soldiers who went on the southern expedition will return.
How will they be accommodated?
If there are absolutely indispensable vacancies,
it is permissible to sparingly use new recruits."
On the day of Xīnhài,
he appointed Dújí Yì, the Jiedushi of Lìshè Commandery, as Cānzhī Zhèngshì.
Wányán Gòuyīng, the Resident-General of Zhōngdū and Commander-in-Chief of the Northwest Marching Army, led 30,000 troops stationed at Guīhuà,
and was made Vice Grand Marshal of the Left.
On the day of Dīngsì,
he distributed gold and silver artifacts from the imperial treasury to supply the army,
and many officials and common people contributed wealth to aid government expenses.
On the day of Rénxū,
he appointed Yàn, the former Administrator of Línhuáng, as Left Chancellor.
On the day of Guǐhài,
an imperial edict was issued to instruct Zhāng Hào, the Grand Tutor of Nánjīng and President of the Department of State Affairs.
On the day of Jiǎzǐ,
Zhāng Xuánsù, the Jiedushi of Xīngpíng Commandery, came to pay respects.
The Shàngshū Province reported that,
after the military campaigns of Zhènglóng,
it was appropriate to grant official positions to those who had contributed money and grain,
which was approved.
An imperial edict was issued to send Yílà Zhābā to recruit the Qìdān tribes who had rebelled.
He appointed Shéntǔ Mǎn, the former Defense Commissioner of Zhàozhōu, as Right Grand Supervisor of the Marshal.
On the *jǐsì* day of the eleventh month, which was the first day of the month,
Yàn, the Left Chancellor, was concurrently appointed Grand Marshal.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
Lǐ Shí, the Minister of Revenue, was appointed Assistant Administrator of Political Affairs.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
an edict was issued to requisition horses from the populace for military use.
Upon completion of the task, they were to be returned to their owners,
and compensation was to be given for those that died.
Āsuǒ and Zhāng killed Shālízhī, the Concurrent Administrator of the Central Capital Retainership.
Āsuǒ proclaimed himself Central Capital Retainer,
and Zhāng proclaimed himself Concurrent Administrator of the Retainership.
They sent Shíjiānú and others to present a memorial of congratulations.
On the *xīnsì* day,
an edict was issued to the various ministers regarding the planned date of entry into the Central Capital.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
an edict was issued to Zuǒ Yuān, the Central Capital Commissioner of Transport:
"No new additions should be made to the palace decorations and furnishings.
Do not requisition a single laborer to disturb the populace.
Only strengthen the perimeter defenses and strictly control entry and exit."
Wányán Wùgūchū, a Supernumerary Official of the Right Bureau of the Department of State Affairs, was appointed envoy to Gāolí to issue an edict.
On the *guǐwèi* day,

Wúzháhū, Provisional Marshal and Left Superintendent of the Circuit Army, Shéntǔmàn, Right Superintendent, and Púsǎn Húntǎn, Governor of Guǎngníng, were dispatched to suppress the various Qìdān tribes.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
the Imperial Father, Bīn Wáng, was posthumously honored as Emperor,
with the posthumous title Jiǎnsù,
and the temple name Ruìzōng.
The Imperial Mother, Púchá Shì, was honored as Qīncí Empress,
and Lǐ Shì as Zhēnyì Empress.
The ministers presented the honorific title Rénmíng Shèngxiào Emperor.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
the imperial title of Dōnghūn Wáng was posthumously restored,
with the posthumous title Wǔlíng,
and the temple name Mǐnzōng.
This was proclaimed throughout the empire.
His sons, Shílǔlà, was enfeoffed as Xǔ Wáng,
and Hútǔwǎ as Chǔ Wáng.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
he paid respects at the ancestral temple of Tàizǔ and the imperial garden tomb of Zhēnyì Empress.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
he proceeded to the Central Capital.
He stopped at Xiǎoliáokǒu.
Zōngxiàn, the Central Capital Retainer, was sent ahead.
On the *rénchén* day,
he stopped at Liángyúwù.
Bái Yànjìng, Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs and Grand Commander of the Northern Route Mobile Army,
and Gěshíliè Zhìníng, Nanjing Retainer and Vice Commander of the Northern Route Mobile Army, arrived to report the number of troops under their command.
Shuǎng, the Military Governor of Ānwǔ Jūn, submitted to the court.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
Wányán Yuányí and others assassinated Hǎilíng in Yángzhōu.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
he stopped at Yìzhōu.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
Song forces captured Shǎozhōu.
Zhékězhí, the Defense Commissioner, surrendered,
and Lǐ Róulì, the Concurrent Administrator of Defense Affairs, died in the fighting.
On the *yǐmǎo* day of the twelfth month,
he stopped at Sānhé Xiàn.
Wányán Gòuyīng, the Left Vice Marshal, came to court.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
he stopped at Tōngzhōu.
Tángkuò Déwēn, Governor of Yán'ān, came to court.
On the *dīngsì* day,
he arrived at the Central Capital.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
he paid respects at the ancestral temple of Tàizǔ.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
he held court in the Zhēnyuán Hall
and received the obeisance of the various ministers.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
Gāo Zhōngjiàn, Left Supervisor of the Marshal's Army, and others were appointed envoys to Sòng Guó to convey a message.
On the *rénxū* day,
an edict was issued granting a three-year exemption from corvée to soldiers who had escorted him from Dōngjīng to the capital.
Gāo Chāngfú, the Concurrent Administrator of Héjiān, submitted a memorial detailing beneficial measures.
The Emperor read it repeatedly.
An edict was issued to all officials, great and small, within and outside the capital, to present beneficial measures.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
an edict was issued to Wányán Gòuyīng, the Left Vice Marshal, to formulate plans for the southern border and the various routes in Shǎnxī.
On the *wùchén* day of the first month of the second year, which was the first day of the month,
there was a solar eclipse.
Drums were beaten and offerings were made.
The Emperor halted music, reduced his meals,
and did not hold court.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
the Emperor said to the Chancellors:
"Promoting the worthy and demoting the unworthy
is the duty of Chancellors.
When there are those whose talent surpasses their own,
fearing that they might share power,
they often refuse to introduce them into their ranks.
I greatly disapprove of this.
You, my lords, should not harbor such thoughts."
Zhái Yǒnggù, formerly Grand Academician of the Hanlin Academy who had retired, was appointed Left Chancellor of the Department of State Affairs,
and Púsǎn Zhōngyì, Governor of Jǐnán, was appointed Right Chancellor.
Xiégē, the Commander-in-Chief, and Wányán Bùhuī, the Vice Commander, were punished for arbitrarily changing the officials in the Central Capital.
Xiégē was stripped of his name,
Bùhuī was demoted by two ranks,
and both were dismissed.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
he held court in the Tàihé Hall
and hosted a banquet for all officials.
Gifts were bestowed upon imperial relatives and noblewomen according to their rank.
On the *rénshēn* day,
an imperial command was issued to the Censorate to inspect documents from the Six Ministries.
If they were delayed and not implemented,
or implemented inappropriately,
they were all to be impeached.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
the prohibition against welcoming and sacrificing to gods and buddhas was abolished.
On the *yǐhài* day,
he proceeded to Dàfáng Shān.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
he offered sacrifices at the imperial tombs.
After the ceremony,
he wished to hunt before returning,
but Yàn, the Left Chancellor, and others advised:
"With the border unrest,
it is not appropriate to engage in pleasure excursions."
On the *wùyín* day,
he returned to the palace.
He then instructed Yàn and others, saying:
"I have always admired the ancient emperors
who humbly accepted remonstrance.
You, my lords, should speak your mind immediately if you have anything to say.
Do not remain silent for your own convenience."
On the *xīnsì* day,
Kěxǐ, the Minister of War, and others were executed
for plotting rebellion.
An edict was issued throughout the empire.
On this day,
gifts were bestowed upon the *méng'ān móukè* armored soldiers and down to the *ālǐxǐ* who had escorted him, according to their rank.
Púchá Ābóhàn, the Left Vice Inspector, and others were dispatched to reward the generals and soldiers in Hénán.
Yílà Yuányí, formerly the Commissioner for Encouraging Agriculture, was appointed Grand Censor.
An edict was issued to Sū Bǎohéng, formerly Minister of Works, and Gāo Sīlián, Junior Guardian of the Crown Prince, to distribute grain and silk to the people of Shāndōng,
and to report the names of those without wives.
On the *gēngyín* day,
the law of obtaining official positions by donating grain was implemented.
Wányán Móuyǎn, the Right Vice Marshal, was dispatched to lead troops to suppress Xiāo Wòwò.
On the *rénchén* day,
the Emperor said to the Chancellors and Executive Councilors:
"It has not been half a year since I ascended the throne,
and there are many matters that need to be addressed.
Recently, there have been no memorials or reports at all.
I dwell deep within the nine layers of the palace,
and I rely precisely on you, my lords, to assist me.
Each of you should consider your strengths and report them.
How could I ever be tired or lazy?"
On the *guǐsì* day,
Venus was seen in broad daylight.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
the Emperor said to the Chancellors and Executive Councilors:
"You, my lords, should investigate the advantages and disadvantages among the populace,
and whether current affairs are appropriate or not,
and report them in a timely manner.
You must not simply indulge yourselves and relax after your official duties,
merely passing the time."
An order was issued to dismiss all southern expeditionary infantry troops from Héběi, Shāndōng, Shǎnxī, and other routes, allowing them to return home.
Twenty thousand troops from Xiánpíng and Jìzhōu were moved to garrison the capital.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
Wányán Sījìng, the Southwestern Route Pacification Commissioner, and Ālín, the Minister of War, were appointed to oversee the generals and soldiers on the northern border.
On the *jǐhài* day of the second month,
former Hanlín Dàizhì Dàyǐng (大穎) was flogged and dismissed for criticizing Hǎilíng (海陵) regarding bandits.
He was then appointed Mìshū Chéng (秘書丞).
Bǔquē Mǎ Qīn (馬欽), who had gained favor by flattering Hǎilíng (海陵),
was dismissed.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
an edict ordered former Hùbù Shàngshū Liáng Qiú (梁銶)
and Hùbù Lángzhōng Yēlǜ Dào (耶律道) to pacify the people of Shāndōng (山東).
Bandits, those who had fled from bandits, or those who had absented themselves from corvée labor and were elsewhere, were
all ordered to return to their occupations
and resume farming in due season.
Regardless of the severity of their crimes,
all were to be pardoned and exempted.
On the *rényín* day,
Tàifù (太傅) and Shàngshū Lìng (尚書令) Zhāng Hào (張浩) came to an audience.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
as the Emperor had just ascended the throne,
Shīmò Yídié (石抹移迭), the Registrar of Liáoyáng (遼陽), and Yílà Gěbǔ (移剌葛補), the Dūjiān (都監) of the Qūyuàn (麴院) in Dōngjīng (東京), were sent to recruit rebel Khitans.
They were killed by Bái Yànjìng (白彥敬) and Gěshíliè Zhìníng (紇石烈志寧).
Both were posthumously granted the title Zhènguó Shàngjiāngjūn (鎮國上將軍),
and their families were each to receive a fifth-rank stipend.
Their sons were also to be taken in.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
Zhāng Hào (張浩) was appointed Tàishī (太師),
retaining his position as Shàngshū Lìng (尚書令).
Yílà Yuányí (移剌元宜), the Yùshǐ Dàfū (御史大夫), was appointed Píngzhāng Zhèngshì (平章政事).
On the *xīnhài* day,
regulations for the hereditary succession and appointment of Méng'ān Móukè (猛安謀克) were established.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
Bēndǔ (奔睹), the Tàibǎo (太保) and Zuǒ Lǐngjūn Dàdūdū (左領軍大都督), was appointed Dū Yuánshuài (都元帥),
retaining his title as Tàibǎo (太保).
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
an edict decreed the demotion of Xiāo Yù (蕭玉), Jìng Sìhuī (敬嗣暉), Xǔ Lín (許霖), and others,
and their release to return to their hometowns.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
scholars were again appointed as Shàngshūshěng Lìshǐ (尚書省令史).
On the *bǐngchén* day,
Shīmò Shùtūlà (石抹术突剌), the Cìshǐ (刺史) of Sōngzhōu (嵩州), and others defeated Sòng (宋) troops at Shòu'ān Xiàn (壽安縣).
On the *dīngsì* day,
Púchá Shìjié (蒲察世傑), the Fángyùshǐ (防禦使) of Zhèngzhōu (鄭州), captured Shǎnzhōu (陝州).
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
an edict ordered Dū Yuánshuài (都元帥) Bēndǔ (奔睹) to establish an office in Shāndōng (山東)
to manage border affairs.
Tè mògē (特末哥), the Cìshǐ (刺史) of Zézhōu (澤州), and his wife Gāo Fúniáng (高福娘) were executed.
On the *jiǎxū* day of the intercalary month,
the Emperor said to his chief ministers:
"Recently, I have heard external comments saying
that presenting memorials is very difficult.
I have never failed to comply with what is feasible.
From now on, do not conceal anything in your presentations;
I am certainly pleased to hear it."
On the *wùzǐ* day,
the Emperor said to his chief ministers:
"Many subjects who submit memorials
are often ordered to have them reviewed in detail by the Shàngshūshěng (尚書省),
and they are not immediately presented to me.
The empire will then think that I merely receive their words but do not act on them.
Present them to me immediately and in detail."
On the *gēngyín* day,
an edict ordered Píngzhāng Zhèngshì (平章政事) Yílà Yuányí (移剌元宜) to plan border affairs in Tàizhōu Lù (泰州路).
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
the Tàihé (太和) and Hòudé (厚德) Halls caught fire.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
Wēndūn Shùtūlà (溫敦术突剌), Shàngshū Bīngbù Shìláng (尚書兵部侍郎), and others engaged Wōwò (窩斡) in battle
and were defeated at Shèngzhōu (勝州).
On the *guǐmǎo* day of the third month,
Cānzhī Zhèngshì (參知政事) Dújí Yì (獨吉義) was dismissed.
Tuódān Héxǐ (徒單合喜), the Yuánshuài Zuǒ Dūjiān (元帥左都監), defeated Sòng (宋) general Wú Lín (吳璘) at Déshùnzhōu (德順州).
On the *jiǎchén* day,
Lǐ Tōng's (李通) official position was posthumously revoked.
On the *yǐsì* day,
the corvée exemption money for the Zhènglóng (正隆) *dīngfū* (丁夫) in Nánjīng (南京) was waived.
On the *xīnhài* day,
officials at home and abroad were admonished to be honest and fair.
On the *guǐhài* day,
an edict was issued regarding Hénán (河南), Shǎnxī (陝西), and Shāndōng (山東):
previously, during bandit suppression,
innocent civilians who were captured and became bandits
were to be rectified.
On the *jǐsì* day of the fourth month,
Wányán Móuyǎn (完顏謀衍), the Yòu Fù Yuánshuài (右副元帥), and others defeated Wōwò (窩斡) at Chángluò (長濼).
On the *xīnwèi* day,
the deposed Emperor Liàng (亮) was demoted to Hǎilíng Jùnwáng (海陵郡王).
On the *yǐhài* day,
an edict ordered a reduction of half the imperial meals and food in the palace.
The state of Xià (夏) sent envoys to congratulate the Emperor on his accession
and to present local products
and congratulations for the Wànchūn Jié (萬春節).
Wányán Móuyǎn (完顏謀衍), the Yòu Fù Yuánshuài (右副元帥), again defeated Wōwò (窩斡) at Míngmù Hé (霿●河).
On the *xīnsì* day,
a banquet was held for the Xià (夏) envoys in the Zhēnyuán Diàn (貞元殿).
According to custom,
foreign envoys, regardless of rank, sat in the corridors and were granted food.
The Emperor, noticing that their food was not refined or abundant,
said:
"How can we win over distant people's hearts with this?"
The officials in charge of food were all flogged sixty times.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
the Xià (夏) envoys had their farewell audience
and requested mutual trade,
which was granted.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
Zuǒ Chéngxiàng (左丞相) Yàn (晏) was appointed Tàiwèi (太尉).
On the *rénchén* day,
an edict was issued to the Khitan (契丹) tribal generals and soldiers, stating:
"Any Khitan who surrenders before engaging in battle with the grand army
shall not be killed or injured,
and shall be pacified.
For those who are later persuaded to surrender,
their slaves and captives shall be determined as already captured.
Their relatives shall be allowed to return to their homes,
and the government shall redeem them."
On the *dīngyǒu* day, the first day of the fifth month,
Bái Yànjìng (白彥敬), the Jiédùshǐ (節度使) of Hésùguǎn (曷速館), was appointed Yùshǐ Dàfū (御史大夫).
On the *wùxū* day,
Gāo Zhōngjiàn (高忠建), the Yuánshuài Zuǒ Jiānjūn (元帥左監軍), was sent to meet the generals and commanders of the northern expedition to suppress the Khitans.
On the *jǐhài* day,
Gěshíliè Zhìníng (紇石烈志寧), the Jiédùshǐ (節度使) of Línhǎijūn (臨海軍), was appointed Yuánshuài Yòu Jiānjūn (元帥右監軍).
Wányán Móuyǎn (完顏謀衍), the Yòu Fù Yuánshuài (右副元帥), and Wányán Fúshòu (完顏福壽), the Yuánshuài Yòu Jiānjūn (元帥右監軍), were summoned back to the capital
for delaying (operations),
and both were dismissed.
On the *rényín* day,
Yǔndí (允迪), the King of Chǔ (楚), was established as the Crown Prince,
and an edict was issued to the whole empire.
On the *dīngsì* day,
Péimǎn Ānlá (裴滿按剌), the Yājūn Wànhù (押軍萬戶), and Yílà Shālǐlà (移剌沙里剌), the Méng'ān (猛安), defeated Sòng (宋) troops at Huázhōu (華州).
On the *wùchén* day of the sixth month,
Yùshǐ Dàfū (御史大夫) Bái Yànjìng (白彥敬) was ordered to buy horses in the northwest region.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
Pú Sànzhōngyì (僕散忠義), the Shàngshū Yòu Chéng (尚書右丞), was appointed Píngzhāng Zhèngshì (平章政事) and concurrently Yòu Fù Yuánshuài (右副元帥),
to manage the Khitan (契丹) situation.
An edict ordered the release of gold and silver from the imperial treasury to be used for the Khitan (契丹) expeditionary army.
On the *wùyín* day,
an edict ordered the detection and capture of Khitan (契丹) spies at Jūyōng Guān (居庸關) and Gǔběi Kǒu (古北口),
and rewards were to be given to those who captured them.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
an edict ordered the defense of Gǔběi Kǒu (古北口) and Shímén Guān (石門關).
On the *gēngchén* day,
Sòng (宋) sent envoys to congratulate the Emperor on his accession.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
Pú Sànzhōngyì (僕散忠義), the Yòu Fù Yuánshuài (右副元帥), engaged Wōwò (窩斡) in battle at Huādào (花道).
On the *wùzǐ* day,
Gěshíliè Liángbì (紇石烈良弼), the Nánjīng Liúshǒu (南京留守), was appointed Shàngshū Yòu Chéng (尚書右丞).
On the *gēngyín* day,
Pú Sànzhōngyì (僕散忠義), the Yòu Fù Yuánshuài (右副元帥), inflicted a great defeat on Wōwò (窩斡) at Niǎolǐng Xīxiànquán (裊嶺西陷泉),
capturing his brother Niǎo (裊).
On the *rénchén* day,
Wányán Sījìng (完顏思敬), the Xīnán Lù Zhāotǎoshǐ (西南路招討使), was appointed Yuánshuài Yòu Dūjiān (元帥右都監).
On the *dīngyǒu* day of the seventh month,
Yuánzhōu (原州) was recaptured.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
the Sòng (宋) ruler abdicated in favor of his son.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
an edict was issued to the Khitans (契丹).
On the *dīngsì* day,
