Shùlǐgǔ (术里古) and other soldiers from the Sùpín Jūn (速頻軍) falsely accused Wányán Móuyǎn's (完顏謀衍) son, Xiégē (斜哥), of sending a letter to his father inciting rebellion,
and they presented the letter to the Emperor.
The Emperor, after reading the letter, said:
"This is a false accusation;
only interrogate the accusers."
When questioned,
it was indeed a false accusation.
Shùlǐgǔ (术里古) was executed.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
Tàiwèi (太尉) and Shàngshū Zuǒ Chéngxiàng (尚書左丞相) Yàn (晏) retired.
On the *rénxū* day,
an edict ordered five thousand troops from Jìzhōu (濟州) and Huìníng Fǔ (會寧府) who were in the capital
to proceed to Běijīng Dūtǒng Fǔ (北京都統府).
Zhāng (璋), the Shǎnxī Dūtǒng (陝西都統), defeated Sòng (宋) general Wú Lín (吳璘) at Zhāngyì Bǎo (張義堡).
On the *yǐchǒu* day of the eighth month, which was the first day of the lunar month,
Xī people, including the *mòbái móukè* Xú Liè, surrendered.
The Left Supervisor of the Army, Gāo Zhōngjiàn, defeated the Xī at Kǎoláo Mountain
and persuaded six nearby Xī camps to surrender.
Those who did not surrender
were attacked and defeated,
all their men were killed,
and their women and children were distributed among the various armies.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
Yǒngxīng County presented auspicious grain.
On the *rénshēn* day,
*wànhù* Wēndíhǎn Ālǔdài fought the Xī at Gǔběikǒu
and was defeated.
An imperial edict ordered the Co-Director of the Imperial Clan Court, Wányán Móuyǎn, and others to repel them.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
the Emperor addressed the chief ministers, saying:
"When the common people submit memorials discussing current policies,
their words can still be helpful.
You, my ministers, hold positions of vital importance,
yet you rarely offer suggestions or critiques.
How can this be acceptable?
As for hearing and deciding lawsuits,
managing documents, and setting deadlines,
who cannot do these things?
Even the sages of Táng and Yú
still made it their business to observe broadly and reflect widely,
only then were they able to achieve good governance.
Zhènglóng relied solely on his own limited views,
and thus brought about defeat and ruin.
I work diligently day and night,
hoping to hear upright counsel.
You, my ministers, should understand my intentions."
An imperial edict stated:
"Officials of all bureaus,
if they submit memorials concerning affairs of state and are suppressed by the authorities,
are permitted to present memorials directly to the Emperor,
which I will personally examine,
to observe the strengths and weaknesses of talent."
The state of Xià sent envoys to congratulate on the imperial title.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
relatives of Qíguó Fēi, Hán Wáng Hēng, *shūmì* Hūtǔ, and *liúshǒu* Zé, who were registered in the palace, were pardoned.
An imperial edict ordered *yuánshuài yòudūjiān* Wányán Sījìng to join the main army with his troops to suppress Wōwò.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
an imperial edict ordered Left Censor-in-chief Shí Jū and Surveillance Censor Féng Zhòngyǐn to investigate Héběi Dōnglù.
On the *dīnghài* day,
an imperial edict was issued to the Censorate, saying:
"What you, my censors, have impeached
are only the delays in official documents between bureaus,
and those who are slow in reporting to bureaus.
These are minor matters.
From the Three Dukes downward,
you should carefully scrutinize the good and evil, the upright and corrupt, among officials.
If you only deal with minor tasks and neglect the major ones,
I will punish you for your crimes."
The Qìdān old monk surrendered.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
taxes at all passes were abolished.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day of the ninth month, which was the first day of the lunar month,
Wányán Móuyǎn captured the Xī *mèng'ān* Hézhù.
Left Supervisor of the Army Túdān Héxǐ greatly defeated the Sòng general Wú Lín at Déshùn Prefecture.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
an imperial edict ordered Vice Director of the Right of the Department of State Affairs Gésīliè Liángbì to expediently pacify rebellious Xī and Qìdān.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
*yuánshuài yòudūjiān* Wányán Sījìng captured Qìdān Wōwò,
and the remaining rebels were all pacified.
Wányán Zhèngchén, Assistant Director of the Left Department of the Department of State Affairs, was made envoy for the birthday of the state of Xià.
On the *rénchén* day,
a hunt was held in the near suburbs.
On the *yǐsì* day,
with the pacification of Yílà Wōwò,
an imperial edict was issued to the court and the provinces.
On the *gēngxū* day,
Emperor Ruìzōng was reburied.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
*yuánshuài yòudūjiān* Wányán Sījìng was made Right Assistant Marshal.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
an imperial edict ordered Sījìng to manage the southern border.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
Emperor Ruìzōng's coffin was moved to Pánníng Palace.
On the *guǐhài* day,
Left Supervisor of the Army Túdān Héxǐ and others defeated Sòng troops at Déshùn Prefecture.
The Military Commissioner of Hénán, Zōngyǐn, recaptured Rǔ Prefecture.
On the *dīngmǎo* day of the tenth month,
Left Assistant Marshal Wányán Gòuyīng was made Manager of Governmental Affairs.
On the *wùchén* day,
the Emperor went to the imperial tomb,
paid respects to Emperor Ruìzōng's coffin,
and wept sorrowfully.
Manager of Governmental Affairs and Right Assistant Marshal Púsǎn Zhōngyì and others returned from the army
and paid their respects to the Emperor.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
Púsǎn Zhōngyì was made Right Chancellor of the Department of State Affairs, and Left Supervisor of the Army Gésīliè Zhìníng was made Left Assistant Marshal.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
Emperor Ruìzōng was buried at Jǐng Mausoleum,
and a general amnesty was granted.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
an imperial edict ordered Left Assistant Marshal Gésīliè Zhìníng to manage the southern border.
On the *rénchén* day,
the Defense Commissioner of Huá Prefecture, Púchá Shìjié, and the Prefect of Dān Prefecture, Chìzhǎn Húsùlǔ Gǎi, defeated Sòng troops at Déshùn Prefecture.
On the *guǐsì* day of the eleventh month, which was the first day of the lunar month,
an imperial edict ordered Right Chancellor Púsǎn Zhōngyì to attack Sòng.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
officials were ranked.
Those who were honest and capable, those who were corrupt and abusive, and those who were incompetent were each divided into three grades for demotion or promotion.
On the *yǐyǒu* day of the twelfth month,
Minister of Punishments Liú Zhòngyuān and others were sent to investigate and proclaim imperial decrees in Dōngjīng, Běijīng, and other circuits.
On the *rénchén* day of the first month of the third year, which was the first day of the lunar month,
Gāolí and Xià sent envoys to offer congratulations.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
Venus was seen in broad daylight.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
*kèshěngshǐ* Wū Jūlián was sent to reward and console the Hénán troops.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
Déshùn Prefecture was recaptured.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day of the second month,
an imperial edict ordered太子少詹事 Tàizǐ Shàozhānshì Yáng Bóxióng and others to investigate the Shānxī Circuit.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
the Emperor said to the prime ministers:
"The starving people of Luán Prefecture,
who have scattered to seek food,
are very pitiable.
They should be moved to Shānxī,
where the wealthy families will provide for them,
and food should be distributed along the roads according to the number of mouths."
On the *rénshēn* day,
an imperial edict was issued to pacify Shǎnxī.
On the *gēngchén* day,
Grand Protector and Grand Marshal Bēndǔ passed away.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
Zhào Jǐngyuán and others were executed for their disruptive words.
On the *gēngyín* day,
Gāolí and Xià sent envoys to congratulate on Wànchūnjié.
Gāolí sent envoys to congratulate on the Emperor's accession.
The monk Fǎtōng from Dōngjīng disturbed the populace with sorcery;
the Dutong Mansion suppressed him.
On the *bǐngshēn* day of the third month,
eight circuits south of Zhōngdū suffered from locusts.
An imperial edict ordered the Department of State Affairs to send officials to catch them.
On the *rénchén* day,
an imperial edict ordered Vice Minister of Revenue Wèi Zǐpíng and nine others
to go separately to the *mèng'ān móukè* units in various circuits
to promote agriculture and conduct investigations.
An imperial edict stated that the Hàn people from Línhuáng were seeking food in Jì and Xìn Prefectures of Huìníng Prefecture.
On the *gēngxū* day,
an imperial edict granted an exemption from last year's taxes.
On the *xīnyǒu* day of the fourth month, which was the first day of the lunar month,
Right Assistant Marshal Wányán Sījìng was dismissed.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
Manager of Governmental Affairs Wányán Gòuyīng and Grand Censor Bái Yànjìng were dismissed.
*Cānzhī Zhèngshì* Lǐ Shí was made Grand Censor.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
an imperial edict stated that officials who committed bribery
would not be pardoned even if a general amnesty was declared.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
*yǐnjìnshǐ* Hán Gāng was made envoy to Gāolí for special grants.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
relief was provided to the poor people of the *mèng'ān móukè* units in the Shānxī Circuit,
with sixty days' rations.
In this month,
Shāng, Guó, and Huán Prefectures were retaken.
All sixteen prefectures that Sòng had encroached upon were now recovered.
On the *xīnmǎo* day of the new moon of the fifth month,
Right Chancellor Púsǎn Zhōngyì came to the capital.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
for the Double Fifth Festival,
the Emperor visited Guǎnglèyuán Park to shoot willows,
ordering the Crown Prince, imperial princes, and all officials to shoot.
Winners were granted gifts of varying degrees.
The Emperor then returned to Chángwǔdiàn Hall,
granted a banquet and played *jīqiú*.
From this year on, this became a regular practice.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
the Sòng people attacked and breached Língbì and Hóngxiàn County.
On the *jǐhài* day,
the Hénán, Shāndōng, and Shǎnxī Military Commands were abolished,
and Area Commanders and Deputy Commanders were established.
As Crown Prince's Household Administrator Wányán Shǒudào was accompanying the Crown Prince,
the Emperor summoned Shǒudào and instructed him, saying:
"You are a high official,
your responsibilities are not light.
From now on, do not accompany [the Crown Prince]."
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
Right Chancellor Púsǎn Zhōngyì was concurrently appointed Grand Marshal.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
Púsǎn Zhōngyì returned to the army.
Xī Tàbùyě, Area Commander of Hénán Circuit, rebelled and defected to Sòng.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
the Sòng people attacked and breached Sùzhōu.
On the *xīnhài* day,
the laws regarding desertion for expeditionary forces were revised.
The Department of State Affairs requested to register all slaves of ministers executed during the Tiāndé reign, and those who followed Wō'à in rebellion, to be soldiers.
The Emperor, considering that the four directions had just been pacified
and public sentiment was somewhat recovering,
deemed that conscripting soldiers
was not a long-term strategy,
and did not approve.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
an edict was issued to the remnants of the Qìdān faction, Púsùyuè and others,
stating that if they could reform themselves,
all their crimes would be pardoned.
If someone captured Púsùyuè and his son and brought them,
they would still be granted official positions and rewards.
Left Deputy Marshal Gēshíliè Zhìníng recaptured Sùzhōu,
and Bóshùlǔ Dìngfāng, Deputy Commander of Hénán, died in battle.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
Wányán Sījìng, Resident Administrator of Běijīng, was again appointed Right Deputy Marshal.
Zhōngdū was afflicted by locusts.
An edict ordered Councillor Wányán Shǒudào to investigate the locust-catching officials of Dàxīng Prefecture.
On the *gēngshēn* day of the new moon of the sixth month,
there was a solar eclipse.
Sū Bǎohéng, Minister of Punishments, was appointed Councillor.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
an edict stated:
"At the end of the Zhènglóng reign,
the soldiers who fled from Jìzhōu Circuit and returned, and were ambushed and killed by the imperial army of Zhōngdū,
shall be officially collected and buried."
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
the Emperor inspected the crops in the nearby suburbs.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
Grand Preceptor and Director of the Department of State Affairs, Zhāng Hào, was dismissed.
Alègēn Héyǎn, General of the Imperial Guard, was appointed envoy to the Xià state for presenting gifts.
On the *gēngxū* day of the seventh month,
Venus was visible in daylight.
Zōngxiàn, Grand Preceptor of the Crown Prince, was appointed Administrator of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
Kǒng Zǒng was appointed Inheritor of the title Duke Yǎnshèng.
On the *bǐngyín* day of the eighth month,
Venus traversed the sky.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
an edict stated:
"For those who performed meritorious service during the reigns of the ancestors but have not yet been promoted or rewarded,
those of fifth rank and above shall be reported to the Emperor;
those of sixth rank and below, and those without official positions, shall be assessed by the Department of State Affairs for promotion or appointment."
On the *jiǎxū* day,
an edict ordered Councillor Wányán Shǒudào to pacify the remnants of the Qìdān faction.
On the *wùyín* day,
an edict abolished the Qìdān *měng'ān móukè*;
their households were assigned to the Nǚzhí *měng'ān móukè*.
It was ordered that old officials
were allowed to keep one or two horses;
the rest were all seized and purchased by the government.
An imperial decree was issued to Tángkuò Déwēn, Grand Inspector of the Palace Guards, saying,
"Hunting on the Double Ninth Festival
is an old custom of our dynasty.
Now, with two thousand accompanying troops,
can they avoid disturbing the populace?
They should be strictly disciplined.
And ten thousand strings of cash shall be distributed among them."
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
the Emperor went to Dàfángshān.
On the *dīnghài* day,
sacrifices were offered at Ruìlíng.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
the Emperor returned to the palace.
On the *guǐsì* day of the ninth month,
〔一０〕Púsǎn Xíníliè, General of the Imperial Guard, was appointed envoy to the Xià state for its birthday celebration.
〔一一〕On the *dīngyǒu* day,
there was an autumn hunt.
For the Double Ninth Festival,
sacrifices to Heaven were offered in the northern suburbs.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
an edict ordered Liú Zhònghuǐ, Academician-in-Waiting, and others, to investigate the prefectures and counties through which the imperial carriage had passed.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
the Emperor returned to the palace.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day of the tenth month,
grand sacrifices were offered at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
Yílà Tiānfóliú, Chief Administrator of the Prince of Xǔ's Establishment, was appointed envoy to Gāolí for its birthday celebration.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
there was a winter hunt.
On the *gēngyín* day of the eleventh month,
Venus was visible in daylight
and traversed the sky.
On the *rénchén* day,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
On the *wùshēn* day,
an edict stated:
"Those seeking official positions who frequently enter the gates of influential figures
shall have one official rank withdrawn
and be demoted or dismissed.
As for those who make requests by offering gifts, and those who receive them,
a detailed report shall be submitted for imperial decision."
On the *gēngxū* day,
all officials requested to bestow an honorific title upon the Emperor;
this was not approved.
An edict stated:
"In Zhōngdū, Píngzhōu, and famine-stricken areas that have also suffered plunder by the Qìdān,
if there are those who have mortgaged or sold their wives and children,
the government shall redeem them."
On the *rénzǐ* day,
Zhái Yǒnggù, Left Vice Chancellor of the Department of State Affairs, was dismissed.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
the tribute of gold-threaded silk fabrics was abolished.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
Gēshíliè Liángbì, Right Vice Chancellor of the Department of State Affairs, was appointed Left Vice Chancellor,
and Shí Jū, Minister of Personnel, was appointed Councillor.
On the *dīngchǒu* day of the twelfth month,
during the Winter Solstice hunting ritual,
the Emperor hunted in the nearby suburbs,
presenting the game caught to the imperial tombs.
From this year on, this became a regular practice.
An edict concerning displaced people who had not yet returned to their livelihoods
extended the deadline for enticing them back.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
Councillor Sū Bǎohéng arrived from the army.
On the *xīnsì* day,
he was appointed Right Vice Chancellor of the Department of State Affairs.
On the *dīnghài* day of the new moon of the first month of the fourth year,
Gāolí and Xià sent envoys to offer congratulations.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
the tributes from circuits, prefectures, and departments for New Year's Day and the Wànchūnjié were abolished.
The Emperor said to his attendants:
"Prince Zōnghàn of Qín rendered meritorious service to the state.
Why did he have no heir?"
None knew how to respond.
The Emperor said:
"I once heard that Zōnghàn, in Xījīng, buried alive a thousand beggars.
Could this not be his retribution?"
On the *guǐsì* day,
all officials again requested to bestow an honorific title upon the Emperor;
this was not approved.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
the Emperor went to Ānzhōu for spring fishing.
On the *rényín* day,
the Emperor arrived at Ānzhōu.
There was heavy snow.
An edict stated that those accompanying the Emperor who lodged in civilian homes
should pay their hosts one hundred cash per person per day.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
the Grand Marshal's Office reported:
"Sòng sent Investigator Hú Fǎng with a letter to the Right Executive Assistant of the Department of State Affairs
to negotiate peace.
Since his words were untrustworthy,
Hú Fǎng was detained in the army
and a letter was sent in reply."
When the letter was presented,
the Emperor read it and said:
"The Sòng's untrustworthiness—
what crime has the envoy committed?
He should be immediately sent back.
As for border affairs, let the Grand Marshal's Office make appropriate plans."
On the *yǐsì* day,
the Department of State Affairs reported:
"Cáo Guī, a commoner from Xúzhōu, pursued the bandit Jiāng Zhì.
His son Bì was also among the bandits,
and he killed them both.
By law, he should be appointed to two official positions
in miscellaneous ranks."
The Emperor considered the report inappropriate,
and ordered him to be promoted one rank
and appointed to a regular rank.
On the *xīnhài* day,
the first wild goose of the season was captured.
Envoys were sent to present it to the imperial tombs.
From this year on, this became a regular practice.
On the *dìngsì* day of the second month,
the taxes and labor service for this year in Ānzhōu were remitted.
Also, for the two villages, Wú and Èr, in Bǎosài County, located on the border of the imperial city, all those who had accompanied the emperor and had stayed in their homes
were also granted a one-year exemption.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
a hunt was held north of Gāoyáng.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
the emperor returned to the capital.
On the *gēngchén* day,
due to the surging price of millet in Běijīng,
an edict was issued to remit this year's *kèjiǎ* (tax).
On the *bǐngxū* day, the first day of the third month,
on Wànchūn Jié,
Gāolí and Xià sent envoys to offer congratulations.
An edict was issued to remit Běijīng's annual tax of silk cloth for one year.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
there was an earthquake in the capital.
On the *rényín* day,
the hundred officials again requested to confer an honorable title upon the emperor,
which was not approved.
On the *dìngsì* day of the fourth month,
Píngzhāng Zhèngshì Wányán Yuányí was dismissed.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
twenty-one palace women were released.
In the fifth month,
there was a drought.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
an imperial order was issued to the relevant authorities to review unjust lawsuits,
to prohibit music within the palace,
and to release the laborers of the polo grounds.
On the *yǐsì* day,
an edict ordered Lǐbù Shàngshū Wáng Jìng to pray for rain at Běiyuè.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
Cānzhī Zhèngshì Shí Jū and others were commanded to offer sacrifices and pray for rain at the northern suburb.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
it rained.
Púsùyuè, a remaining partisan of Wōwò, was executed.
On the *jiǎyín* day, the first day of the sixth month,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the *rénxū* day,
Shàngshū Zuǒchéng Géshíliè Liángbì arrived from the Zhēngnán Yuánshuàifǔ.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
as there was sufficient rain,
the relevant authorities were ordered to offer sacrifices of gratitude to the five sacred mountains, four rivers, seas, and lakes at the northern suburb.
On the *jǐsì* day,
the emperor visited the Eastern Palace
to check on the illness of the Crown Prince.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
the rites for sacrificing to the five sacred mountains and four rivers were first established.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
the crops in the nearby suburbs were inspected.
On the *gēngchén* day,
an edict was issued to the Yuánshuàifǔ, stating:
"Regarding the request for fifteen thousand troops to attack Sòng,
three thousand cavalry and four thousand infantry shall now be dispatched."
An edict was issued to the Shǎnxī Yuánshuàifǔ to deliberate on the advantages and disadvantages of entering Shǔ and report.
On the *rénchén* day of the seventh month,
the late Wèi Wáng Xiāngfēi and her son Héshang were executed for sorcery and delusion.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
Shàngshū Zuǒchéng Géshíliè Liángbì was made Píngzhāng Zhèngshì.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
there was a great wind, thunder, and rain,
uprooting trees.
On the *jiǎyín* day, the first day of the eighth month,
an edict was issued to the Zhēngnán Yuánshuàifǔ, stating:
"Previously, you requested to recover the old territories,
and asked to wait until autumn was cooler to advance.
Now that autumn is cooler,
how long more will you wait?"
On the *wǔwǔ* day,
Cānzhī Zhèngshì Wányán Shǒudào was made Shàngshū Zuǒchéng,
and Dàxīng Yǐn Tángkuò Ānlǐ was made Cānzhī Zhèngshì.
On the *rénshēn* day,
the emperor said to his chief ministers:
"Your every memorial concerns ordinary matters.
Regarding governing the country, bringing peace to the people, or court policies that are inconvenient for the people,
you have never touched upon them.
If this is the case,
then who cannot perform the duties of a prime minister?"
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
the emperor went to Dàfáng Shān.
On the *xīnsì* day,
sacrifices were offered at the imperial tombs.
On the *guǐwèi* day, the first day of the ninth month,
the emperor returned to the capital.
On the *yǐyǒu* day, the emperor said to his chief ministers:
"When powerful families and their relatives and acquaintances are involved in lawsuits,
they often request intervention through connections.
Officials often bend the law and yield to personal feelings.
This must be absolutely forbidden."
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
the emperor said to his chief ministers:
"The roads of Běijīng, Yìzhōu, Línhuáng, and others
have previously suffered from Khitan raids.
Píng and Jì prefectures have recently again suffered from locusts and drought.
The people are struggling for food,
parents and siblings cannot protect each other,
and many are illegally selling themselves into slavery.
I am deeply saddened by this.
Envoys should be swiftly dispatched to verify their numbers,
and money from the inner treasury should be used to redeem them."
On the *yǐwèi* day,
the emperor visited the Eagle House.
The superintendent had placed the hawks and falcons in the main hall of the inner province.
The emperor angrily said:
"This is where the prime ministers conduct their business.
How can it be a place for placing hawks and falcons?"
He severely reprimanded the person
and ordered them to be moved elsewhere.
On the *jǐhài* day,
Sùzhí Jiāngjūn Wūlǐyǎ was appointed as the envoy for the Xià state's birthday.
On the *xīnhài* day,
Tàizǐ Shǎozhānshì Wūgǔlún Sānhé was appointed as the envoy for Gāolí's birthday.
On the *guǐchǒu* day, the first day of the tenth month,
〔一二〕a hunt was held in Mìyún County.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
the emperor returned to the capital.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
Tàiníngjūn Jiédùshǐ Zhāng Hóngxìn and twenty-four others were ordered to inspect the resources of various circuits by dividing the routes.
On the *yǐyǒu* day of the eleventh month,
Zhēngnán Dūtǒng Túdān Kèníng defeated the Sòng forces
and captured Chǔzhōu.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
the emperor's son Yǒnggōng was enfeoffed as Zhèng Wáng.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
a winter hunt was held.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
an edict was issued to advance troops to attack Sòng.
On the *wùxū* day,
the emperor arrived at Héjiān Fǔ.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
there was a fire in the Shàngshū Shěng.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
the emperor arrived at Qīngzhōu.
On the *rénzǐ* day, the first day of the intercalary month,
the emperor returned to the capital.
On the *dīnghài* day of the twelfth month,
the Shàngshū Shěng reported that Dūtǒng Gāo Jǐngshān had captured Shāngzhōu.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
on the Làyuè festival,
a hunt was held in the nearby suburbs.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
Venus was seen in broad daylight,
traversing the sky.
This year,
there was a great harvest.
Seventeen death sentences were decided.
On the *xīnhài* day, the first day of the first month of the fifth year,
Gāolí and Xià sent envoys to offer congratulations.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
an edict ordered that seventy border forts be established
on the border between Tàizhōu and Línhuáng〔一三〕, garrisoning thirteen thousand troops.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
the Sòng envoy for communication, Wèi Shí, and others arrived with a state letter.
The letter did not use
"great,"
but referred to
"nephew Sòng Emperor,"
and used the personal name,
"bows twice and respectfully presents this letter to uncle Dàjīn Emperor."
The annual tribute was two hundred thousand.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
an edict was issued to the whole country.
The relevant authorities were again ordered
to remit taxes and levies in areas suffering from drought, locusts, or floods.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
the Yuánshuàifǔ's various new and old armies were ordered to leave sixty thousand men to garrison,
and the rest were all dismissed and returned home.
All the annual tribute from the Sòng state was to be awarded to the various armies.
On the *rénwǔ* day of the second month,
Zuǒfù Dūdiǎnjiǎn Wányán Zhòng and others were appointed as envoys to return the Sòng's greetings.
On the *rényín* day,
the policy of granting official positions in exchange for grain was abolished.
On the *wùshēn* day,
on Wànchūn Jié,
〔一四〕Sòng, Gāolí, and Xià sent envoys to offer congratulations.
On the *rénshēn* day of the third month,
the assembled officials respectfully conferred an honorable title upon the emperor as Yìngtiān Xīngzuò Réndé Shèngxiào Huángdì,
and an edict was issued to the whole country.
On the *guǐmǎo* day of the fourth month,
the rebellion planned by Xījīng Liúshǒu Shòuwáng Jīng
was brought to justice.
He was specially exempted from the death penalty,
given a beating,
stripped of his title,
and placed in Ānzhōu.
On the *yǐsì* day,
Yòufù Yuánshuài Wányán Sījìng was dismissed.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
Yòuchéngxiàng and Dū Yuánshuài Púsǎn Zhōngyì returned from the army.
In the fifth month, on the day Rénzǐ,
the Left Vice Marshal Hēshíliè Zhìníng was summoned for an audience.
On the day Dīngsì,
Púsàn Zhōngyì was appointed Shàngshū Zuǒ Chéngxiàng,
Hēshíliè Zhìníng was appointed Píngzhāng Zhèngshì,
and the army returned.
On the day Yǐchǒu,
Zōngxiàn, the Píngzhāng Zhèngshì, was appointed Shàngshū Yòu Chéngxiàng.
On the day Guǐyǒu,
the Shāndōng Lù Dūtǒng Fǔ was abolished,
and its troops were each attached to a Zǒngguǎn Fǔ.
In the sixth month, on the day Jiǎchén,
ganoderma lucidum grew on a pillar of the Dà'ān Diàn.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
there was an earthquake in the capital,
and it rained hair.
In the seventh month, on the new moon day Wùshēn,
the capital experienced another earthquake.
The Shǎnxī Dūtǒng Fǔ was abolished,
and the Tǒngjūn Sī Jīngzhào was re-established,
while the Shǎnxī Yuánshuài Fǔ was moved to Hézhōng.
In the eighth month, on the day Jǐmǎo,
the former Sùzhōu Defense Commissioner Wūlíndá Lāsā, for colluding with Lǐ Shìfǔ of Sòng,
was executed.
On the day Guǐsì,
Sòng and Xià sent envoys to congratulate on the emperor's honorary title.
In the ninth month, on the new moon day Dīngwèi,
Gāo Kàn, the Lìbù Shàngshū, and others were appointed envoys to celebrate the Sòng emperor's birthday.
On the day Wùshēn,
there was an autumn hunt.
On the day Gēngxū,
Zhúhǔ Púchá, the Sùzhí Jiāngjūn, was appointed envoy to the Xià kingdom for its emperor's birthday.
On the day Jiǎxū,
the emperor returned to the capital.
In the tenth month, on the new moon day Dīngchǒu,
there was an earthquake.
On the day Xīnsì,
Zhāng, the Dàzōngzhèng Céng, was appointed envoy to Gāolí for its king's birthday.
On the day Yǐwèi,
there was a winter hunt.
On the day Xīnchǒu,
the emperor returned to the capital.
In the eleventh month, on the new moon day Bǐngwǔ,
the emperor said to his chief ministers:
"I have been on the throne for a short time,
and have not been able to fully discern the worthiness or unworthiness of my officials.
I rely entirely on you all to recommend them impartially.
Currently, there is a severe lack of talent among officials of the sixth rank and below.
How can I fulfill my desire to seek out the worthy?"
On the day Guǐchǒu,
the emperor visited the Eastern Palace.
On the day Wùwǔ,
Wūgǔlún Niánmòhé, the Yòu Fù Dū Diǎnjiǎn, was appointed envoy to Sòng to celebrate the New Year.
On the day Guǐhài,
a new tax law for various routes based on land inspection and grading was established.
On the day Guǐyǒu,
there was a great fog,
and it was dark during the day.
In the twelfth month, on the day Jǐchǒu,
the emperor hunted in the nearby suburbs.
Gāolí sent envoys to congratulate on the emperor's honorary title.
In the sixth year, first month, on the new moon day Bǐngwǔ,
Sòng, Gāolí, and Xià sent envoys to offer congratulations.
On the day Gēngwǔ,
an imperial edict was issued to the relevant officials,
stating that decorations in the palace should not be adorned with gilding.
In the second month, on the day Dīnghài,
Púsàn Zhōngyì, the Shàngshū Zuǒ Chéngxiàng and concurrent Dū Yuánshuài of Yíguó Gōng, passed away.
On the day Rényín,
the Wànchūn Jié,
Sòng, Gāolí, and Xià sent envoys to offer congratulations.
In the third month, on the day Jiǎyín,
the emperor went to Xī Jīng.
On the day Gēngshēn,
upon arriving at Guīhuà Zhōu,
Tángkuò Déwēn, the Xī Jīng Liúshǒu, came to pay respects.
On the day Wùchén,
the emperor arrived at Xī Jīng.
On the day Gēngwǔ,
the emperor performed a morning sacrifice at the Tàizǔ Miào.
On the day Rénshēn,
a polo game was played,
and the common people watched.
In the fourth month, on the new moon day Jiǎxū,
an edict was issued prohibiting slaughter on the new moon.
On the day Wùxū,
Yílà Dào, the Shàngshū Yòusī Lángzhōng, was appointed envoy to Gāolí for special gifts,
and Xiámǎo Guólà, the Sùzhí Jiāngjūn, was appointed envoy to the Xià kingdom for special gifts.
On the day Xīnchǒu,
Venus was visible in daylight.
In the fifth month, on the day Wùshēn,
the emperor visited Huáyán Sì,
observed the bronze statues of the former Liáo emperors,
and issued an edict to the head monk to carefully guard them.
On the day Rénzǐ,
an edict was issued to grant a one-year exemption from taxes and labor for Yúnzhōng Dàtóng Xiàn and the Jǐngxún Yuàn.
On the day Rénxū,
an edict was issued announcing the emperor's impending visit to Yín Shān,
and that all accompanying soldiers would be granted 50,000 strings of cash,
and anyone who dared to damage crops
would be required to compensate for them.
In the sixth month, on the day Xīnsì,
Venus was visible in daylight,
crossing the sky.
On the day Bǐngxū,
the emperor departed from Xī Jīng.
On the day Gēngzǐ,
the emperor hunted at Yín Shān.
In the seventh month, on the day Xīnyǒu,
the emperor arrived at Sānchākǒu.
In the eighth month, on the new moon day Xīnwèi,
the emperor arrived at Liángxíng.
On the day Gēngchén,
the emperor hunted in the southern mountains of Wàngyún.
In the ninth month, on the new moon day Xīnchǒu,
the emperor returned from Xī Jīng.
On the day Dīngwèi,
Wèi Zǐpíng, the Hùbù Shàngshū, was appointed envoy to Sòng to celebrate the emperor's birthday.
On the day Xīnhài,
Yílà Xīzài, the Hànlín Dàizhì, was appointed envoy to the Xià kingdom for its emperor's birthday.
Liú Déyù, the Zézhōu Cìshǐ, and others were executed for embezzling government funds.
On the day Rénzǐ,
Venus was visible in daylight.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
Zōngxiàn, the Shàngshū Yòu Chéngxiàng, passed away.
On the day Bǐngchén,
Venus was visible in daylight,
crossing the sky.
In the tenth month, on the day Jǐmǎo,
Yílà Àndá, the Shàngshū Bīngbù Shìláng, was appointed envoy to Gāolí for its king's birthday.
On the day Jiǎshēn,
a morning sacrifice was offered at the Tàimiào.
An edict was issued to exempt Xióng and Mò and other prefectures from this year's rent.
On the day Rénchén,
Venus was visible in daylight,
crossing the sky.
On the day Dīngyǒu,
the emperor went to Ānsù Zhōu.
There was a winter hunt.
In the eleventh month, on the day Bǐngwǔ,
the emperor returned to the capital.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
Wūgǔlún Yuánzhōng, the Yòu Fù Dū Diǎnjiǎn, was appointed envoy to Sòng to celebrate the New Year.
The emperor said to his chief ministers:
"Court officials must be carefully selected,
so as to inspire the rest.
If they are not worthy,
it will incite covetous desires.
You all must know the strengths and weaknesses of talents,
and employ those who are truly capable."
On the day Gēngshēn,
Venus was visible in daylight,
crossing the sky.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
Shí Jū, the Cānzhī Zhèngshì, was dismissed due to a period of mourning for his mother.
In the twelfth month, on the day Jiǎxū,
an edict was issued to the relevant officials,
stating that on the first and fifteenth days of each month and the first seven days of the month, criminal cases should not be presented.
On the day Wùzǐ,
Venus was visible in daylight,
crossing the sky.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
Hé Zhù, a commoner from Tàizhōu, plotted rebellion,
and was executed.
On the day Bǐngshēn,
Hēshíliè Liángbì, the Píngzhāng Zhèngshì, was appointed Shàngshū Yòu Chéngxiàng,
and Hēshíliè Zhìníng was appointed Shūmì Shǐ.
In the seventh year, first month, on the new moon day Gēngzǐ,
Sòng, Gāolí, and Xià sent envoys to offer congratulations.
On the day Xīnhài,
Shí Jū was reinstated as Cānzhī Zhèngshì.
On the day Rénzǐ,
the emperor wore the ceremonial robe and crown,
presided over the Dà'ān Diàn,
and received the ceremony of the honorary title and imperial seal.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
a general amnesty was proclaimed.
On the day Gēngshēn,
Túshān Héxǐ, the Yuánshuài Zuǒ Jiānjūn, was appointed Shūmì Fùshǐ.
In the second month, on the day Gēngyín,
Sū Bǎohéng, the Shàngshū Yòu Chéng, passed away.
On the day Bǐngshēn,
Shí Jū, the Cānzhī Zhèngshì, was appointed Shàngshū Yòu Chéng.
In the third month, on the new moon day Jǐhài,
the Wànchūn Jié,
Sòng, Gāolí, and Xià sent envoys to offer congratulations.
In the fourth month, on the new moon day Wùchén,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the day Rénchén,
Lǐ Shí, the Yùshǐ Dàfū, was appointed Sītú,
retaining his title of Dàfū.
In the fifth month, on the day Bǐngwǔ,
the prison of Dàxīng Fǔ was empty;
an edict was issued granting 300 strings of cash for a celebratory feast,
to reward them.
On the day Jiǎyín,
Nòuwǎn Wēndūn Wùdài, the Běijīng Liúshǒu, was appointed Cānzhī Zhèngshì.
On the *guǐyǒu* day of the sixth month,
an order was issued to discontinue the use of dragon patterns on court carpets.
On the *wùshēn* day of the seventh month,
the wearing of clothes embroidered with gold thread was forbidden.
Those who wove or sold them
were all to be punished.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
His Majesty visited the Eastern Palace.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
His Majesty visited the Eastern Palace to see the illness of the Crown Prince.
On the *dīngmǎo* day of the intercalary month,
the emperor inspected the crops in the near suburbs.
On the *wùchén* day,
Prince Yǒngzhōng (永中) was permitted to be enfeoffed as Prince of Yuè (越王),
Prince Yǒnggōng (永功) was enfeoffed as Prince of Suí (隨王),
and Yǒngchéng (永成) was enfeoffed as Prince of Shěn (瀋王).
On the *jiǎxū* day,
an imperial edict was issued, dispatching Mìshūjiān (秘書監) Yílà Zǐjìng (移剌子敬) to manage the northern frontier.
On the *wùyín* day,
His Majesty visited the Eastern Palace.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
auspicious clouds encircled the sun.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
the emperor inspected the crops in the near suburbs.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
the emperor inspected the crops in the northern suburbs.
On the *xīnhài* day of the eighth month,
auspicious clouds encircled the sun.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
Shàngshū Yòuchéngxiàng (尚書右丞相) and Jiānxiū Guóshǐ (監修國史) Hégǔliè Liángbì (紇石烈良弼) presented the *Tàizōng Shílù* (太宗實錄),
and the emperor stood to receive it.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
he went to Dàfángshān (大房山).
On the *rénxū* day,
sacrifices were offered at Ruìlíng (睿陵).
On the *yǐchǒu* day, the first day of the ninth month,
he returned to the palace.
On the *jǐsì* day,
Hán Zàn (韓贊), a Jiǎnfǎguān (檢法官) of the three right departments, was
dismissed from office for accepting bribes while capturing locusts.
An edict was issued stating that if officials or commoners committed embezzlement or bribery,
even if a general amnesty was declared,
they would not be pardoned without a special imperial decree.
Púchá Shāluwō (蒲察莎魯窩) and others, who were Quànnóngshǐ (勸農使), were appointed as envoys to congratulate Sòng (宋) on its emperor's birthday.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
Cānzhī Zhèngshì (參知政事) Tángguō Ānlǐ (唐括安禮) was dismissed.
On the *yǐhài* day,
Sùzhí Jiāngjūn (宿直將軍) Tángguō Húlǔ (唐括鶻魯) was appointed as an envoy for the emperor's birthday to the Xià (夏) Kingdom.
On the *gēngchén* day,
there was an earthquake.
On the *xīnsì* day,
Dūshuǐjiān (都水監) Lǐ Wèiguó (李衞國) was appointed as an envoy for the emperor's birthday to Gāolí (高麗).
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
there was an autumn hunt.
On the *gēngyín* day,
the emperor arrived at Bǎozhōu (保州).
An edict ordered Xiū Qǐjūzhù (修起居注) Wáng Tiānqí (王天祺) to investigate officials in the prefectures and counties he passed through.
On the *yǐwèi* day, the first day of the tenth month,
the emperor told his attendants:
"Recently, I heard that in the prefectures and cities I have visited,
the halls and chambers where I have feasted or rested
are subsequently avoided by people.
This is utterly pointless.
An edict should be proclaimed
to allow people to reside there as before."
On the *wùshēn* day,
he returned to the capital.
On the *dīngsì* day,
the emperor told the chief ministers:
"Hǎilíng (海陵) did not distinguish between talented and untalented people,
but only indulged his own desires,
promoting many.
Since I ascended the throne,
I have taken this as a warning,
only employing truly capable individuals.
Recently, I heard that Yílà Yánshòu (移剌延壽), the Tóngzhī (同知) of Lízhōu (蠡州), was corrupt in office.
Upon inquiring about his background,
it turned out he was an 'Eagle House man' from the Zhènglóng (正隆) era.
How can a person from the 'Eagle House' category
be suitable to govern a city and shepherd the people?
From now on, such people,
by their categorization,
must not be appointed to positions overseeing the people."
Yùshǐ Zhōngchéng (御史中丞) Mèng Hào (孟浩) was appointed Cānzhī Zhèngshì (參知政事).
On the same day,
Cānzhī Zhèngshì (參知政事) Nòuwǎnwēndūn Wùdài (耨盌溫敦兀帶) passed away.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
an imperial decree ordered the relevant authorities to build an additional palace hall in front of the cool pavilion of the Eastern Palace.
Mèng Hào (孟浩) remonstrated, saying:
"Although the Crown Prince is the heir apparent,
he should be shown the virtue of frugality,
and his palace should not be equal to that of the emperor."
So, the plan was abandoned.
On the *yǐchǒu* day, the first day of the eleventh month,
the emperor told the chief ministers:
"I hear that many county magistrates are not suitable for their positions.
Order the Lìbù (吏部) to investigate their conduct, good or bad,
and clearly promote or demote them."
On the *xīnwèi* day,
Héjiān Yǐn (河間尹) Túshàn Kèníng (徒單克寧) and others were appointed as envoys to congratulate Sòng (宋) on New Year's Day.
On the *rénshēn* day,
Venus was seen in daylight.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
Jupiter was seen in daylight.
On the *dīnghài* day,
Shūmì Fùshǐ (樞密副使) Túshàn Héxǐ (徒單合喜) was dismissed.
On the *wùxū* day of the twelfth month,
Tōukyō Liúshǒu (東京留守) Túshàn Héxǐ (徒單合喜), Běijīng Liúshǒu (北京留守) Wányán Móuyǎn (完顏謀衍), and Zhàozhōu Fángyùshǐ (肇州防禦使) Púchá Tōng (蒲察通) came for their farewell audience.
Tōng (通) was bestowed a golden belt,
and the emperor instructed him, saying:
"Although you are talented,
your mind is often deceitful.
I need loyal and honest people around me,
so I am ordering you to a provincial post.
The golden belt is bestowed upon you
in recognition of your long service."
Then, looking at Zuǒ Xuānhuīshǐ (左宣徽使) Jìng Sìhuī (敬嗣輝), he said:
"One cannot say you lack talent,
but what you lack is pure honesty."
On the *jiǎchén* day,
Běijīng Liúshǒu (北京留守) Wányán Sījìng (完顏思敬) was appointed Píngzhāng Zhèngshì (平章政事).
In this year,
twenty death row prisoners were executed.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day, the first day of the first month of the eighth year,
envoys from Sòng (宋), Gāolí (高麗), and Xià (夏) came to offer congratulations.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
the emperor told the chief ministers:
"I govern the realm
and am sharing it with you all.
If there is anything improper,
each of you should state it directly to my face
to assist me where I am deficient.
Be careful not to flatter me to gain favor.
You all have attained the position of chief ministers;
this is precisely the time to practice the Way and spread your names.
If you merely seek ease and self-convenience,
though it may be fortunate for today,
what will later generations think of it?"
All the officials exclaimed, "Long live the Emperor!"
On the *xīnwèi* day,
he told Mìshūjiān (秘書監) Yílà Zǐjìng (移剌子敬) and others:
"In the time of Táng (唐) and Yú (虞) of old,
there were no lavish decorations.
The Hàn (漢) Emperor Xiàowén (孝文) alone strove for pure frugality.
Regarding my palaces, I only fear excess.
If there is any construction or repair,
I would reduce the annual expenses of the palace women to fund it.
Now, I no longer build anything.
As for banquets,
recently I only drank alcohol on the Crown Prince's birthday and New Year's Day.
In the past, I only drank on the Yuánxiāo (上元) and Mid-Autumn festivals,
and I never became drunk.
As for Buddhist teachings,
I am even less inclined to believe them.
Emperor Liángwǔ (梁武) became a slave to the Tóngtài Temple (同泰寺),
and the Liáo Dàozōng (遼道宗) bestowed common households upon temple monks,
and furthermore granted them the titles of Sāngōng (三公).
Their delusion was profound."
On the *gēngchén* day,
the investiture ceremony for the Crown Prince was held.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day, the first day of the second month,
a decree was issued that children should observe three years of mourning for their mothers who remarried.
The emperor instructed Zuǒ Xuānhuīshǐ (左宣徽使) Jìng Sìhuī (敬嗣輝), saying:
"Any minister who,
above, seeks to exploit the emperor's favor,
and below, seeks to gain the people's praise,
will inevitably compromise his loyalty and integrity.
You should beware of this."
On the *guǐhài* day, the first day of the third month,
on Wànchūnjié (萬春節),
envoys from Sòng (宋), Gāolí (高麗), and Xià (夏) came to offer congratulations.
On the *jǐsì* day,
an order was given to appoint sons of officials to fill clerical posts.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
an order was given that Hùwèi Qīnjūn Bǎihù (護衞親軍百戶) and Wǔshíhù (五十戶)
were not permitted to carry swords into the palace unless on duty.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
Venus was seen in daylight.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day of the fourth month,
an edict stated:
"Horses are used for military purposes,
and cattle are resources for farming.
Killing cattle is forbidden,
and horses are no different.
Therefore, a ban on killing them should be enforced."
On the *wùshēn* day,
polo was played in the Chángwǔ Hall (常武殿).
Sītiān (司天) Mǎ Guìzhōng (馬貴中) remonstrated, saying:
"Your Majesty is the lord of the realm,
bearing the heavy responsibility of the state,
and is also advanced in years.
Hunting and playing polo are dangerous activities;
they should all be discontinued."
The emperor said:
"I do this to demonstrate the practice of martial arts."
In the fifth month, on the *jiǎzǐ* day,
looking north towards Diàndà, there was a great earthquake, wind, and hail,
ten *lǐ* wide
and sixty *lǐ* long.
An imperial edict was issued to the Ministries of Revenue and Works, stating,
“From now on, for palace decorations,
no gold shall be used.”
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
the emperor went to Liángxíng.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
Jupiter was seen in daylight.
On the *gēngyín* day,
Wàngguóyá was renamed Jìngníngshān,
and Hélǐhú Dōngchuān was renamed Jīnliánchuān.
In the sixth month,
the Yellow River breached its banks at Lǐgùdù,
and the water flooded Cáozhōu.
In the seventh month, on the *jiǎzǐ* day,
a decree was issued that those who stole horses from the imperial herds would be executed,
and those who reported such crimes would be given three hundred strings of cash.
On the *wùchén* day,
the emperor said to Grand Counselor Wányán Sījìng and others,
“I think of obtaining worthy scholars,
never forgetting them, whether awake or asleep.
From now on, when court officials go out,
they should investigate honest and capable local officials
and talented commoners who can assist in governance,
and report their names to me.”
On the *jiǎxū* day,
there was an autumn hunt.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
they arrived at Sānchākǒu.
The emperor instructed the Diǎnjiǎnsī, saying,
“The crops along the road are excellent.
If any of the attendants tread on them,
you will be held responsible.”
In the eighth month, on the *yǐmǎo* day,
the emperor returned from Liángxíng.
In the ninth month, on the *xīnyǒu* day,
the emperor instructed Shàngshū Yòuchéng Shí Jū and Cānzhèng Mèng Hào, saying,
“I heard that hundreds of thousands of laborers were employed in Wèizhōu to gather mushrooms.
How much do I use myself,
yet there is such disturbance?
From now on, any corvée labor designated for imperial use
must be reported to me
and recorded in a register.”
On the *guǐhài* day,
Yílà Shéndúwò and others, who were Right Xuānhuīshǐ, were sent as envoys to congratulate Sòng on its emperor’s birthday.
On the *jǐsì* day,
Gāo Xīfǔ, the Yǐnjìnshǐ, was sent as an envoy to Xiàguó for its emperor’s birthday.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
the emperor visited the Eastern Palace.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
the emperor instructed the chief ministers, saying,
“When you recommend talented people,
if you yourselves know them,
you always make others recommend them,
which I dislike greatly.
If they are truly worthy,
why should you avoid them due to personal closeness or distance?”
Wèi Zǐpíng, the Hùbù Shàngshū, was appointed Cānzhī Zhèngshì.
On the *xīnsì* day,
the emperor said to Yùshǐ Dàfū Lǐ Shí,
“The Censorate is certainly for distinguishing between the wicked and the upright,
but how can it be said that there are no worthy people among the hundred offices, both inside and outside the court?
I only see you impeach people for their crimes,
but I do not hear of you commending the good.
From now on, you should order the Jiānchá Yùshǐ to go to various circuits and investigate both good and bad deeds and report them to me.”
The emperor had once ordered Zuǒwèi Jiāngjūn Dàpán to search for good bows,
but Pán took many for himself.
Hùwèi Lóushì reported this.
The emperor ordered the Diǎnjiǎnsī to interrogate Pán.
Pán’s sister was a Báolín.
Pán instructed the eunuch Sēng'ér to speak to Báolín about it.
Báolín reported it to the emperor.
Sēng'ér was ordered to be flogged a hundred times,
and Pán was exiled to be the Fángyùshǐ of Lǒngzhōu.
In the tenth month, on the *jǐchǒu* day, the first day of the month,
an edict was issued to officials inside and outside the court,
admonishing them against greed and corruption.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
the Cìshǐ of Zhuōzhōu was appointed concurrently Tídiǎn Shānlíng,
to offer sacrifices on the first and fifteenth day of each month.
On the first day, plain offerings were to be used,
and on the fifteenth day, meat offerings,
starting from the first month of the following year.
And it was ordered to paint portraits of meritorious officials in the Tàizǔ Temple,
and to erect steles for those who did not yet have them.
Jìng, the Hànlín Dàizhì, was sent as an envoy to Gāolí for its king’s birthday.
The emperor said to the chief ministers,
“During the time of Hǎilíng,
the scribes of the daily records were not honest officials,
so much of what they wrote was untrue.
You should investigate and find the truth,
and record it in detail.”
Cānzhèng Mèng Hào stepped forward and said,
“A good historian writes truthfully,
recording every action of the ruler.
From ancient times, emperors did not personally review history,
and this is precisely why.”
On the *xīnhài* day,
an edict abolished the annual tribute of deer tendons from Fùzhōu.
In the eleventh month, on the *yǐchǒu* day,
the emperor visited the Eastern Palace.
Pìhétǔ and others, who were Tóngqiān Dàzōngzhèngshì, were sent as envoys to congratulate Sòng on New Year’s Day.
In the twelfth month, on the *wùzǐ* day, the first day of the month,
Wǔdìngjūn Jiédùshǐ Yílà Àn and others were dispatched to persuade the rebels to surrender.
In the ninth year, in the first month, on the *wùwǔ* day, the first day of the month,
Sòng, Gāolí, and Xià sent envoys to offer congratulations.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
the emperor discussed ancient and modern affairs with Xuānhuīshǐ Jìng Sìhuī and Mìshūjiān Yílà Zǐjìng,
and then said,
“When the Liáo dynasty fell, three hundred sheep were slaughtered and eaten daily.
How could they all be used?
It was merely a waste of life.
Though I am in the highest position,
whenever I eat,
I often think of the hunger and deprivation of the poor,
as if it were my own.
How can those who act wickedly but pray for blessings verbally
benefit from it?
Like Hǎilíng, who appointed Zhāng Zhòngkē as Jiànyì Dàfū,
how could he hear loyal advice?
When I discuss a matter with my ministers,
I only speak what is right.
If you do not respond truthfully,
how can that be the way of a minister?”
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
an edict ordered that in the collection of grain taxes in various prefectures and counties,
the common people should not be coerced into forced contributions.
On the *wùyín* day,
Qìdān Wàishīlà and others plotted rebellion
and were executed.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
a decree allowed Han and Bohai women,
whose brothers’ wives had completed mourning and returned to their families,
to remarry according to proper rites.
In the second month, on the *gēngyín* day,
a decree stipulated that those who spread false rumors about border troops
would be sentenced to two years of penal servitude.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
an edict ordered the reburial of the two Han Yan kings to the east of the city.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
due to floods in Zhōngdū and other circuits,
taxes were remitted,
and an edict was issued to this effect both inside and outside the court.
Furthermore, as Cáozhōu and Shànzhōu were particularly severely affected by the floods,
they were granted a one-year tax exemption.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
an edict stipulated that if Nǚzhēn people were involved in public matters with people of various other ethnicities,
the case should only be handled by Nǚzhēn officials.
In the third month, on the *dīngsì* day, the first day of the month,
it was Wànchūnjié,
and Sòng, Gāolí, and Xià sent envoys to offer congratulations.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
the Shàngshūshěng had set up a law for hunting wild animals with nets,
which could lead to penal servitude.
The emperor said,
“To punish people with penal servitude for the sake of animals
is to value animals more than human lives.
This is not my intention.
From now on, offenders shall be flogged and released.”
An edict ordered Yùshǐ Zhōngchéng Yílà Dàolián to inspect Shāndōng and Hénán.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
it was forbidden for commoners to use the term
“xiāojīn” (melted gold),
and any existing regulations internally that used it
were to be changed to
“míngjīn” (bright gold)
character.
On the *xīnsì* day,
because the *qiānhù* households of various *méng'ān* in Dàmíng Lù were experiencing food shortages,
envoys were sent to open the granaries and sell grain at reduced prices.
In the fourth month, on the *jǐchǒu* day,
the emperor said to the chief ministers,
“I observe that officials in power,
when they first enter service,
compete to gain reputation to achieve rank and position.
Once they achieve prominence,
they then pursue silence and acquiescence as a means of self-preservation,
which I greatly disapprove of.
You should issue a proclamation to all officials
so they may understand my intention.”
On the *guǐsì* day,

Hànlín Xiūzhuàn Púchá Wùhǔ and Jiānchá Yùshǐ Wányán Húshā were dispatched separately to Héběi Xīlù, Dàmíng, Hénán, Shāndōng, and other circuits to encourage the *méng'ān* and *móukè* to engage in agriculture.
On the *bǐngchén* day of the fifth month,
Tuóndān Huáizhēn (徒單懷貞), a Palace Guard Officer, was appointed as the envoy to Gāolí (高麗) for the bestowal of gifts.
Wányán Sàiyě (完顏賽也), a General of the Imperial Guard, was appointed as the envoy to Xiàguó (夏國) for the bestowal of gifts.
On the *wùchén* day,
the Department of State Affairs reported that the princely establishments of Yuèwáng Yǒngzhōng (越王永中) and Suíwáng Yǒnggōng (隋王永功) had commenced construction projects,
requiring the conscription of laborers.
The Emperor said:
"I saw some wilting bamboo in the palace
and wanted to have it replanted,
but I refrained, fearing it would burden the people.
The two princely establishments each have their own retinues,
and many servants and slaves.
How can they further conscript the common people?
You merely make requests based on precedent.
Hǎilíng (海陵) conscripted laborers without restraint;
can all such practices be considered precedents?
From now on, for temporary labor in the capital,
those long established as precedents shall remain so;
for others, the government shall provide wages,
and serious cases must be reported to me."
On the *gēngyín* day of the sixth month,
Zhāng Hé (張和) and others from Jìzhōu (冀州) rebelled
and were executed.
On the *wùxū* day,
due to the prolonged drought,
an order was given that no fans should be used in the palace.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
it rained.
On the *yǐmǎo* day, the first day of the seventh month,
pearl collection in the Northeast Circuit was abolished.
On the *rénshēn* day,
the Emperor inspected the crops in the nearby suburbs.
On the *jiǎshēn* day, the first day of the eighth month,
the competent authorities reported a solar eclipse.
Since it was not visible due to rain,
drums were beaten and offerings were made according to the usual rites.
On the *jiǎyín* day, the first day of the ninth month,
Gāo Déjī (高德基), Minister of Justice, and others were appointed as envoys to Sòng (宋) to congratulate them on the Emperor's birthday.
Pú Sànshǒuzhōng (僕散守中), a General of the Imperial Guard, was appointed as the envoy to Xiàguó (夏國) for the Emperor's birthday.
Mǎ Guìzhōng (馬貴中), Controller of the Imperial Astronomical Bureau, was appointed as the envoy to Gāolí (高麗) for the Emperor's birthday.
The Crown Prince's monthly allowance was abolished,
and he was given 50,000 strings of cash annually.
The Emperor said to his ministers:
"Recently I heard that some court officials were appropriating eunuchs' property to seek profit.
Why did you not speak of this?"
They all replied:
"We were unaware."
The Emperor said:
"Even I know of it;
how can you be unaware?
If I were to pursue this matter,
what use would you be?"
On the *rénxū* day,
there was an autumn hunt.
On the *dīnghài* day of the tenth month,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
Hégélìe Liángbì (紇石烈良弼), Right Chancellor of the Department of State Affairs, was appointed Left Chancellor.
Hégélìe Zhìníng (紇石烈志寧), Commissioner of Military Affairs, was appointed Right Chancellor.
An edict was issued that for sacrifices in the imperial ancestral temple,
deer should replace oxen,
and this was established as a regulation.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
a grand banquet was held in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
On the *xīnhài* day,
Wányán Sījìng (完顏思敬), Administrator of Governmental Affairs, was appointed Commissioner of Military Affairs.
On the *jǐwèi* day of the eleventh month,
Wányán Shǒudào (完顏守道), Left Assistant of the Department of State Affairs, was appointed Administrator of Governmental Affairs.
Shí Jū (石琚), Right Assistant, was appointed Left Assistant.
Méng Hào (孟浩), Counciler of State Affairs, was appointed Right Assistant.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
the Emperor visited the Eastern Palace.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
Yì (毅), Prefect of Jīngzhàofǔ (京兆尹), and others were appointed as envoys to Sòng (宋) to congratulate them on the New Year.
On the *rénxū* day,
there was a winter hunt.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
On the *bǐngxū* day of the twelfth month,
an edict was issued to provide relief to the *móu'ān* people in Línhuáng (臨潢), Tàizhōu (泰州), Shāndōng Dōnglù (山東東路), and Héběi Dōnglù (河北東路).
Tuóndān Héxǐ (徒單合喜), Garrison Commander of Dōngjīng (東京), was appointed Administrator of Governmental Affairs.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
Venus was seen in broad daylight.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
there was a hunt in the nearby suburbs.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
a decree was issued stating that if officials committed public offenses,
and had already confessed while in office,
they would still be prosecuted even after leaving office.
On the *rénzǐ* day, the first day of the first month of the tenth year,
envoys from Sòng (宋), Gāolí (高麗), and Xià (夏) arrived to offer congratulations.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
an order was given that no lanterns should be displayed in the palace during the Lantern Festival.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
Lǐ Shí (李石), Minister of Works and Censor-in-Chief, was appointed Grand Commandant and Grand Chancellor.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day of the second month,
Tuóndān Zǐwēn (徒單子溫), Military Commissioner of Ānhuà Jūn (安化軍), and his deputy, Lǎojūnnú (老君奴), were executed
for embezzlement.
On the *wùshēn* day,
the Emperor said to his close ministers:
"All Imperial Guards will eventually become officials governing the people;
therefore, instruct them to study books."
On the *rénzǐ* day, the first day of the third month,
during the Wànchūnjié (萬春節) festival,
envoys from Sòng (宋), Gāolí (高麗), and Xià (夏) arrived to offer congratulations.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
the Emperor then ordered skilled archers from the Imperial Guard to oversee a archery banquet for the Sòng (宋) envoy.
The Sòng (宋) envoy hit the target fifty times,
while those overseeing the banquet only hit it seven times.
The Emperor said to the generals on his left and right:
"Imperial Guards, after ten years, become fifth-rank officials.
They are on duty every three days,
and their duties are light.
Is it merely for them to eat their fill and sleep soundly?
If they do not practice archery,
what use will they be?"
On the *wùwǔ* day,
Zōng (宗), Commander of the Hénán (河南) Army, was appointed Counciler of State Affairs.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
the Emperor said to Counciler Zōng (宗):
"When you were Commander of Hénán (河南) last year,
you spoke of the advantages and disadvantages of the Yellow River dikes and fascines,
which greatly pleased me.
I constantly think of the corvée labor imposed on the common people,
and how officials conspire in corrupt practices.
If no plans are made early,
when the time comes, levies are collected urgently like wildfire,
costing several times more,
causing no small harm.
Now that you participate in court affairs,
you must reform all abuses
and implement beneficial policies."
He then instructed Left Assistant Shí Jū (石琚):
"Jurchens directly hold important positions
and do not understand the suffering of the common people.
You, having served from clerks to your current positions,
what affairs of the people do you not know?
Whenever there are advantages or disadvantages,
you should fully articulate them."
On the *dīngyǒu* day of the fourth month,
a decree was issued regarding noblewomen who committed adultery:
those who did not rely on their husband's favor to have their sons enfeoffed
were not subject to this law.
On the *yǐmǎo* day of the fifth month,
the Emperor went to Liǔhéchuān (柳河川).
On the *gēngchén* day of the intercalary month,
Rèn Déjìng (任得敬) of Xiàguó (夏國) coerced his lord, Lǐ Rénxiào (李仁孝),
to submit a memorial
requesting to divide his country.
The Emperor asked his chief minister Lǐ Shí (李石),
who, along with others, thought that since the matter concerned their country,
it would be better to permit it.
The Emperor said:
"He is merely coerced by a powerful minister."
An edict was issued to refuse,
and their tribute items were also rejected.
On the *rénwǔ* day of the seventh month,
there was an autumn hunt.
On the *wùxū* day,
the laborers at the hunting ground were dismissed.
An edict was issued that all provisions for the imperial retinue would be supplied by the government.
On the *yǐsì* day,
an imperial order was issued that those in the imperial retinue who allowed their livestock to trample crops
would be flogged
and still had to compensate for the damage.
On the *jǐwèi* day of the eighth month,
the Emperor returned from Liǔhéchuān (柳河川).
On the *rénshēn* day,
Counciler of State Affairs Zōng (宗) was dispatched to inspect the northern region.
On the *gēngchén* day of the ninth month,
Hégélìe Liángbì (紇石烈良弼), Left Chancellor of the Department of State Affairs, left office due to mourning
but was reinstated to his former position.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
Yílà Zǐjìng (移剌子敬), Deputy Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, was appointed as envoy to Sòng (宋) for the Emperor's birthday.
On the *gēngyín* day,
Jiágǔ Ālǐbǔ (夾谷阿里補), Director of the Ministry of Revenue, was appointed as envoy to Xiàguó (夏國) for the Emperor's birthday.
On the *jǐyǒu* day of the tenth month,
Cí (辤), Assistant Grand Clan Elder, was appointed as envoy to Gāolí (高麗) for the Emperor's birthday.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
the Emperor went to Bāzhōu (霸州)
for a winter hunt.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
the Emperor said to his ministers:
"Recently, during the imperial hunt,
I heard that Gāo Chāngyì (高昌裔), Magistrate of Gù'ān (固安) County, was incompetent,
and I have already ordered his dismissal.
Chéng Fèngxiān (成奉先), Surveillance Officer of Bāzhōu (霸州), has performed his duties diligently and respectfully;
he may be promoted one rank
and appointed Magistrate of Gù'ān (固安)."
On the *xīnwèi* day,
the Emperor said to his chief ministers:
"Whenever I discuss matters and cannot thoroughly investigate their advantages and disadvantages,
you should all carefully deliberate and articulate them,
and not outwardly agree only to voice objections later."
In the 11th month, on the day of Xīnsì
, it was decreed that those who stole objects from the Tàimiào temple would be judged the same as those who stole objects from the palace.
On Jiǎshēn
, the Emperor visited the Eastern Palace.
On Dīnghài
, Púchá Púsùyuè and others, as Prince’s Chamberlain, were appointed envoys to congratulate the Sòng court on the New Year.
On Guǐsì
, the Xià kingdom sent an envoy to apologize for executing Rèn Déjìng,
and an imperial edict was issued to comfort and reassure them.
In the 12th month, on Bǐngyín
, the Emperor said to his chief ministers:
“Recently, my health has not been good
, which has hampered state affairs.
Now, looking at the matters you have presented,
they all merely follow regulations and precedents
, and there is nothing that truly benefits the nation.
If one act could be performed each day
, by the end of the year, there would be a surplus,
and the benefits would be extensive.
I reside deep within the palace
, how can I know all external affairs?
You all should pay particular attention.”
In the 11th year, 1st month, on Bǐngzǐ, the first day of the month
, envoys from Sòng and Xià arrived to offer congratulations.
On Dīngchǒu
, his son Yǒngshēng was enfeoffed as Xú Wáng,
Yǒngdǎo as Téng Wáng,
and Yǒngjì as Xuē Wáng.
On Rénwǔ
, an imperial edict stipulated that officials aged seventy or above who retired
, regardless of their rank,
would all be granted half of their salary.
On Bǐngshēn
, an order was given to provide relief to the Měng'ān屯田 (agricultural garrisons) in Nánjīng who suffered from flood disasters.
On Wùxū
, the Shàngshūshěng (Department of State Affairs) reported that Niú Xìnchāng, the Deputy Military Commissioner of Fènyáng Jūn, had received gifts on his birthday
, which by law warranted his dismissal.
The Emperor said:
“If the court’s actions are not just in themselves
, how can it govern the world justly?
The Shàngshūshěng and the Shūmìyuàn (Bureau of Military Affairs) receive no fewer gifts on birthdays and festivals.
If these go unquestioned
, yet minor officials who receive gifts are immediately impeached
, is this the way to govern the world justly?
From now on, gifts to Chief Councillors and Privy Councilors should also be abolished.”
The Emperor said to his chief ministers:
“In previous years, when I spent the summer west of the mountains
, the fields along the road were very extensive
, leaving almost no land for livestock.
Therefore, I ordered that cultivation should only be allowed beyond five *lǐ*.
Now I hear that the people have all moved elsewhere
, which is very regrettable and pitiable.
Let them resume cultivation as before.
If there are similar cases
, you should immediately report them to me.”
In the 3rd month, on Yǐhài, the first day of the month
, on Wànchūnjié
, envoys from Sòng and Xià arrived to offer congratulations.
On Xīnsì
, the authorities were ordered to bury the coffin of the Duke of Tiānshuǐ Jùn according to the rites of a first-rank official, at Gǒnglào zhī Yuán.
In the 4th month, on Dīngwèi
, Zāng Ān'ér, a resident of Guīdé Fǔ, plotted rebellion
and was executed.
Lǐ Chāngtú, the Grand Judge, despite having found clear evidence of corruption and unlawful conduct by Túshán Zhēn, the Prefect of Zhēndìng, and Shímò Āmòlà, the Prefect of Xiánpíng
, did not immediately dismiss them
, and was given forty strokes of the cane.
On Guǐhài
, Wèi Zǐpíng, Assistant Administrator of the Bureau of Military Affairs, was dismissed.
The younger brother of King Xiàn of Gāolì
, Hào, deposed his sovereign and enthroned himself
, falsely claiming to have ceded the throne
, and sent an envoy with a memorial to present.
In the 5th month, on Xīnmǎo
, an edict was issued to send Jìng, the Vice Minister of Personnel, as an envoy to Gāolì to investigate the matter.
On Guǐsì
, Yílà Chéng, the Defender-in-chief of Nánjīng, was appointed Vice Privy Councillor.
In the 6th month, on Jǐyǒu
, an imperial edict stated:
“Among the regular tributes from all circuits
, the sheep from Shāyuàn in Tóngzhōu are not urgently needed
, and only trouble the people.
From now on, this is abolished.
I reside deep within the palace
, how can I know all matters that trouble the people?
Matters such as this should be reported in detail.”
On Wùwǔ
, the Emperor inspected the crops in the nearby suburbs.
On Jiǎzǐ
, Túshān Héxǐ, Administrator of the Bureau of Military Affairs, passed away.
In the 7th month, on Jiǎshēn
, Zōng, Assistant Administrator of the Bureau of Military Affairs, passed away.
In the 8th month, on Guǐmǎo, the first day of the month
, Venus was seen in broad daylight.
The Emperor issued an edict to his court officials, saying:
“I have often told you
that regarding the nation’s advantages and disadvantages
, and deficiencies in governance
, all can be spoken of directly.
Even officials and common people in outer circuits have sometimes offered opinions
, yet you have never uttered a single word.
How can all administrative actions taken
be always correct?
From now on, speak directly about successes and failures
, without any concealment.”
On Yǐsì
, the Emperor said to his chief ministers:
“Officials attending court
think that after one evaluation, they should attain a certain position,
and after two evaluations, another.
They merely strive to follow established routines
, doing nothing more than that.
From now on, for officials from outer circuits and those appointed internally
, if their diligence and public service are observed, they will be promoted and employed.
But if they are simply perfunctory in their duties
, there is no need to wait for their term to expire;
they will be dismissed at their current rank.
If rewards and punishments are not clear
, how can people be encouraged?”
On Gēngxū
, an imperial edict stated:
“All Jurchen and people of other ethnic groups who were abducted by Wōwò and have not yet been released
shall be redeemed and set free by the government.
Those who conceal them
shall be judged for violating the decree.
For those who are young and cannot state their place of residence
, they may settle wherever convenient.”
The Emperor said to his chief ministers:
“There are many vacant positions below the fifth rank
, yet it is difficult to find suitable people.
I know those above the third rank
, but I cannot know those below the fifth rank.
You all have never offered a single recommendation.
If I wish to devise long-term stability plans
and promote the welfare of the people
, but lack good assistants
, everything I do will be ordinary matters.
Even if I hold court every day
, what benefit will it have?
You all should strive to ponder this.”
On Jǐsì
, Wūlíndá Tiānxī, Vice Minister of Punishments in the Department of State Affairs, and others, were appointed envoys to congratulate the Sòng court on the Emperor’s birthday,
and Liú Chōng, the Director of the Palace Attendants Bureau, was appointed envoy to the Xià kingdom for their Emperor’s birthday.
In the 9th month, on Guǐwèi
, the Emperor hunted at Héngshān.
On Gēngyín
, he returned to the capital.
In the 10th month, on Rényín, the first day of the month
, Jìng Sìhuī, the Left Director of the Bureau of Imperial Acclamations, was appointed Assistant Administrator of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
On Jiǎyín
, the Emperor said to his chief ministers:
“Regarding matters I have already acted upon
, you consider them established decrees that cannot be altered
, merely complying
, without any objection or advice.
Moreover, whenever you have made a recommendation
, when have I ever not followed it?
From now on, even if my decree has been issued
, you should deliberate before acting.
If anything is found to be inconvenient
, report it immediately for revision.
Or, if those in lower positions say that the actions of the Shàngshūshěng are inconvenient
, you should also comply and revise them
, not refuse to do so.”
On Bǐngyín
, Gēshíliè Liángbì, Left Chancellor of the Department of State Affairs, presented the Veritable Records of Ruìzōng.
On Wùchén
, the Emperor said to his chief ministers:
“The portraits of meritorious officials in Yǎnqìng Gōng
have been ordered to be increased to twenty.
For example, Chancellor Hán Qǐxiān,
since the founding of our dynasty
, many constitutional laws and regulations
came from his hand.
As for resolving major state policies
, he only discussed and deliberated with senior ministers
, never letting outsiders know.
Among Han Chinese chancellors
, none before or since have been comparable.
If he is praised and honored
, it will also serve as encouragement.
Be careful not to overlook him.”
On the *dīngchǒu* day of the eleventh month,
Zōng Níng and others, who were pacification commissioners for the Southwest Circuit, were appointed envoys to felicitate the Sòng court on the New Year.
On the *wùyín* day,
the emperor visited the Eastern Palace.
The emperor said to the Crown Prince:
"My son, you are in the position of heir apparent.
I have arranged the empire for you,
and there should be no more matters requiring your efforts.
You need only not forget the pure and generous customs of your ancestors,
diligently cultivate virtue and morality as a display of filial piety,
and clearly administer rewards and punishments for governance, and that is all.
In the past, Táng Tàizōng said to his son Gāozōng: 'I began the campaign against Gāolì but could not finish it;
you should continue it.'
Such matters
I will not leave to you.
Take the case of the Hǎibīn Wáng of Liáo,
who, because the people loved his son,
was jealous and killed him.
What kind of principle is this?
For a son to be loved by the multitude
is an even more beautiful thing.
If one acts like that,
how can one not perish?
Táng Tàizōng was a sagely ruler,
yet he said to his son Gāozōng: 'You have no favor from Lǐ Jì.
I will now dismiss him for a certain matter.
When I die,
you should immediately appoint him as *púshè*,
and he will surely exert his utmost effort for you.'
As a ruler of men,
why resort to pretense?
If one receives favor from a father,
how can one forget to repay it to the son?
When I govern my ministers,
I rely solely on sincerity and honesty."
All the ministers acclaimed "Long live the Emperor!"
On the *bǐngxū* day,
the Grand Ancestral Temple held the grand sacrifice.
On the *dīnghài* day,
rites were performed at the Round Mound,
and a general amnesty was declared.
On the *guǐsì* day,
the ministers respectfully conferred upon the emperor the honorary title of Yìngtiān Xīngzuò Qīnwén Guǎngwǔ Réndé Shèngxiào Huángdì.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
an imperial edict was issued to the internal and external administrations.
On the *guǐmǎo* day of the twelfth month,
there was a winter hunt.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
the emperor returned to the palace.
On the *bǐngchén* day, Cāncān Zhī Zhèngshì Jìng Sìhuī passed away.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
Yǒngzhōng, Prince of Yuè, was promoted to Prince of Zhào;
Yǒnggōng, Prince of Suí, to Prince of Cáo;
Yǒngchéng, Prince of Shěn, to Prince of Bīn;
Yǒngshēng, Prince of Xú, to Prince of Yú;
Yǒngdǎo, Prince of Téng, to Prince of Xú;
Yǒngjì, Prince of Xuē, to Prince of Téng.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
Yǒngzhōng, Prince of Zhào, and Yǒnggōng, Prince of Cáo, were both granted the title of *Měng'ān*.
Yǒnggōng was furthermore ordered to personally handle affairs,
to practice governance.
Collation Notes
Basic Annals 7, Shìzōng Middle
On the *gēngwǔ* day, the first day of the first month of the twelfth year,
Sòng, Gāolì, and Xià sent envoys to offer felicitations.
On the *wùyín* day,
the emperor decreed to the relevant authorities,
“All written memorials
concerning the advantages and disadvantages of state policy,
from now on, if their suggestions are feasible,
their original copies shall be sealed and sent to the Mìshūjiān.
For those that are to be implemented, a copy shall be recorded and sent to the relevant department.”
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
due to floods and droughts,
the previous year's land tax was remitted for Zhōngdū, Xījīng, Nánjīng, Héběi, Hédōng, Shāndōng, and Shǎnxī.
On the *rényín* day of the second month,
the emperor summoned the Chief Secretaries of the various princely households and instructed them:
“I selected you all
precisely to encourage and guide the princes,
to make them do good.
If the princes do anything that is not good,
you must strongly remonstrate.
If they still do not comply,
then report the specific action taken on a specific day.
If you flatter them and remain silent,
I will hold you accountable.”
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
the Shàngshū Shěng reported
that through investigations, Shān Héshang and others, Co-administrators of Chéngyáng Prefecture, were found to be clean and capable officials.
The emperor said:
“These individuals, through both covert observation and public inquiry, have established reputations for good governance.
Their political achievements should be ranked,
and each should be promoted and rewarded.
Let their promotions and appointments be swiftly discussed.”
On the *gēngxū* day,
the emperor went to Chūnshuǐ in Shùnzhōu.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
he returned to the capital.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
an edict stated:
“From now on, if an official is unlawful,
and his subordinates cannot correct him and also fail to report him to the superior,
they shall also be punished.”
Gāo Déjī, Minister of Revenue, improperly disbursed 400,000 strings of official salaries,
and was sentenced to eighty strokes of the rod.
On the *jǐsì* day, the first day of the third month,
the Wànchūn Festival was held.
Sòng, Gāolì, and Xià sent envoys to offer felicitations.
On the *yǐhài* day,
the emperor decreed to the Shàngshū Shěng,
“Corrupt officials
who have already been investigated,
if they remain in their old posts,
will certainly harm the people again.
Send envoys to the various circuits
to immediately dismiss them.”
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
an edict was issued to send Yūgǔlún Sīliè, General of the Imperial Guard,
to enfeoff Wáng Hào as King of Gāolì.
On the *gēngyín* day,
it rained earth.
On the *guǐsì* day,
Yīlà Dào, former Pacification Commissioner of the Northwest Circuit, was appointed Cāncān Zhī Zhèngshì.
The Huíhé sent envoys to pay tribute.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
Cáo Guì and others in Běijīng plotted rebellion
and were executed.
In the fourth month,
there was a drought.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
Mèng Hào, Right Vice-Chancellor of the Shàngshū, was dismissed.
On the *dīngsì* day,
Nàhé Qījīn and others in the Northwest Circuit plotted rebellion
and were executed.
On the *guǐhài* day,
due to the prolonged drought,
prayers were ordered to the mountains and rivers.
The emperor decreed to the prime ministers:
“Many junior sub-prefects in various prefectures are lacking.
We should select *jìnshì* graduates who, though their rank is not yet sufficient, have reputations for good governance,
and promote them.”
Tángkuò Āhūlǐ, General of the Imperial Guard, was appointed envoy to bestow gifts upon the Xià state.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
Jīng Wáng Wén, Governor of Dàmíng, was stripped of his princely title due to embezzlement crimes
and demoted to Defense Commissioner of Dézhōu.
An envoy from the Huíhé came to pay tribute.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
Héshíliè Zhìníng, Right Chancellor of the Shàngshū, passed away.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
Sòng and Gāolì sent envoys to congratulate on the emperor's honorary title.
Zǔ... came to pay tribute.
On the *guǐyǒu* day of the fifth month,
the emperor went to Bǎihuā Chuān.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
an order was given to relieve the famine among the Hūlàwēn *Měng'ān* people in the Eastern Circuit of Shāndōng.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
the retinue stopped at Zǔjū.
After a long drought, it rained.
On the *wùyín* day,
the crops were inspected.
The imperial entourage was forbidden from trampling civilian fields.
All officials and attendants were forbidden from wearing pure yellow oil-cloth garments.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
the emperor instructed the prime ministers:
“Each time I take residence,
all horse equipment is borrowed from the people,
and many items are lost and not returned to their owners.
This is due to the incompetence of the enforcement officials;
suitable persons should be chosen to replace them.
Wherever we pass, immediate inquiries should be made,
and for any lost civilian property,
its value must be compensated.”
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
an edict was issued to provide cattle to households in the Northwest Circuit.
On the *jiǎyín* day of the sixth month,
the emperor went to Jīnlián Chuān.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day of the ninth month,
the emperor returned from Jīnlián Chuān.
On the *xīnsì* day,
Jiágǔ Qīngchén and others, Right Deputy Grand Inspector, were appointed envoys to congratulate Sòng on the emperor's birthday,
and Niángē Wòtèlā, General of the Right Guard, was appointed envoy to the Xià state for its emperor's birthday.
On the *dīnghài* day,
Venus was seen during the day,
in front of the sun.
Lǐ Fāng and others in Fūzhōu plotted rebellion
and were executed.
In the tenth month,
Wáng Hào (王晧), King of Gāolì (高麗) Kingdom, sent an envoy to express gratitude for the enfeoffment.
On the day Yǐwèi,
a memorial sacrifice was offered for the late Right Chancellor Hésīliè Zhìníng (紇石烈志寧).
