Zhìníng’s (志寧) wife, the Princess of Yǒng'ān (永安) County, presented armor, bows and arrows, eagles and falcons, and brocades.
On the day Rénzǐ,
the Crown Prince and Zhào Wáng Yǒngzhōng (趙王永中) were summoned to the main hall.
The Emperor looked at his chancellors and said,
"Jīng (京) once plotted rebellion.
If we do not eliminate him now,
I fear he will become a future problem."
He further said,
"The great vessel of the empire belongs to the virtuous.
Hǎilíng (海陵) lost the Way,
and thus I obtained it.
We need only diligently cultivate virtue;
what else is there to worry about?"
The Crown Prince and Yǒngzhōng (永中) both said,
"Indeed, as your sacred instruction states."
Thereupon, he was released.
On the day Bǐngchén,
the property of Wénzǐ Chǎn (文貲產), Defense Commissioner of Dézhōu (德州), was bestowed upon his elder brother’s son, Yǎozhù (咬住).
And his mother was instructed:
"For Wén's (文) crime,
all of you should have been implicated.
However, considering Sòng Wáng (宋王) had great merit for the state,
we have chosen not to pursue the matter,
and moreover, his family property is bestowed upon your son."
In the eleventh month, on the day Jiǎxū,
the Emperor said to his chancellors,
"Among the imperial clan, there are some who are not suitable for official duties.
If they are not shown favor and grace,
the Way of cherishing kin
will not be fully extended.
I wish to grant them honorary official titles
and bestow upon them a certain amount of stipend.
I wonder how this was handled in previous dynasties?"
Left Chancellor Shí Jū (石琚) replied,
"Yáo (陶唐)'s closeness to the nine clans and
the Zhōu (周) family's internal harmony with the nine clans
are seen in the 'Shī' (詩) and 'Shū' (書) classics,
and these are all beautiful deeds of emperors."
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
the Emperor, because a household slave of Princess Cáo Guó (曹國) committed an offense,
and Wǎnpíng (宛平) magistrate Liú Yánbì (劉彥弼) flogged him,
the princess then humiliated the magistrate.
The Emperor severely reprimanded the princess,
and also, because the Censorate officials indulged in their power and sought ease,
feared and dared not speak,
their salaries were withheld for one month.
Zhāng (璋), the Commander of Shǎnxī (陝西), was made Censor-in-chief.
Cáo Wàngzhī (曹望之), Minister of the Board of Revenue, was made envoy to congratulate Sòng (宋) on New Year's Day.
On the day Rénwǔ,
Qū Lì (屈立) and others, commoners of Tóngzhōu (同州), plotted rebellion
and were executed.
On the day Wùzǐ,
the Emperor dismissed his attendants
and discussed matters with his chancellors.
The historians also withdrew.
The Emperor said,
"History officials record the good and evil of the sovereign.
My words and actions, and what I discuss with you, my lords,
should all be known to them,
and there should be no concealment in their records.
You may convey my intentions to them."
In the twelfth month, on the first day Yǐwèi,
because Liú [⿳艹口咢] (劉[⿳艹口咢]), Prefect of Jìnán (濟南), was corrupt and unlawful in the Dìngwǔ (定武) Army,
Dàlǐ Shǎoqīng (大理少卿) Zhāng Jiǔsī (張九思) was ordered to investigate him.
On the day Dīngyǒu,
an edict ordered officials and twenty imperial guards
to be sent out on various routes to select men between twenty and forty years of age, from prominent families, with talent and good conduct, and skilled in archery,
to serve as imperial guards,
not to exceed one hundred men.
Wáng Qióng (王瓊) and others from Jìzhōu (冀州) plotted rebellion
and were executed.
Wén (文), Defense Commissioner of Dézhōu (德州), plotted rebellion
and was executed.
On the day Xīnchǒu,
more than twenty palace women were released.
On the day Jǐyǒu,
Yílà Chéng (移剌成), Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs, was dismissed.
On the day Xīnhài,
investigating and recording officials were prohibited from neglecting public duties for banquets.
An edict allowed commoners to mine for gold and silver,
and no taxes were to be collected.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
there was a hunt in the nearby suburbs.
Túshān Kèníng (徒單克寧), Grand Inspector of the Palace Guards, was made Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs.
On the day Jǐwèi,
an edict stated that henceforth, for descendants of renowned individuals who are already in office, all appointments should be submitted for imperial decision.
In the thirteenth year, first month, on the first day Yǐchǒu,
Sòng (宋), Gāolì (高麗), and Xià (夏) sent envoys to offer congratulations.
On the day Guǐyǒu,
the Department of State Affairs reported that
Southern merchants Chē Jùn (車俊) and others, while trading at the frontier market,
accidentally crossed the border,
a crime punishable by death.
The Emperor said,
"Since it was not intentional,
they can be pardoned and sent back.
Do not let their country know of this,
lest they pursue their crime again."
An edict strictly prohibited officials in prefectures, counties, wards, and villages from harming the common people.
In the intercalary month, on the day Rénzǐ,
the Emperor issued an edict to the Grand Preceptor of the Crown Prince, saying,
"Officials and staff of the Eastern Palace must especially be selected for their uprightness.
If anyone's conduct is not proper or if they are not competent,
report their names."
On the day Xīnyǒu,
Venus was seen during the day.
Bandits from Luòyáng (洛陽) County gathered a crowd and attacked Lúshì (盧氏) County,
killing Magistrate Lǐ Tíngcái (李庭才),
and fled into Sòng (宋) territory.
In the third month, on the first day Guǐsì,
on the Wànchūn (萬春) Festival,
Sòng (宋), Gāolì (高麗), and Xià (夏) sent envoys to offer congratulations.
On the day Yǐmǎo,
the Emperor said to his chancellors,
"Huìníng (會寧) is the place where our nation rose to power.
Since Hǎilíng (海陵) moved the capital to Yǒng'ān (永安),
the Nǚzhēn (女直) people have gradually forgotten their old customs.
I have often seen Nǚzhēn (女直) customs in my time,
and I have not forgotten them to this day.
The banquets and music of today
all follow Hàn (漢) customs,
probably for the sake of ceremony,
but it is not what my heart truly likes.
The Eastern Palace does not know Nǚzhēn (女直) customs;
only because of me
are they still somewhat preserved.
I fear that at some point, this custom will be completely changed,
which is not a long-term plan.
I very much wish to visit Huìníng (會寧) once,
so that my descendants can see the old customs,
and perhaps learn and imitate them."
Liú Zhònghuì (劉仲誨), Grand Preceptor of the Crown Prince, requested to increase the number of herdsmen and furnishings for the Eastern Palace.
The Emperor said,
"The various offices and bureaus of the Eastern Palace have their fixed numbers of personnel,
and the furnishings are already complete;
why add more?
The Crown Prince was born into wealth and nobility,
and can easily fall into extravagance;
he should only be guided towards simplicity and frugality.
Since I ascended the throne,
the clothes I wear and the objects I use
have often remained the old ones.
You should convey this intention to him."
In the fourth month, on the day Jǐsì,
it was decreed that for an adopted son who inherits property less than that of his birth family, the inherited property and the birth family's property should be combined and equally divided.
Based on the report from the relevant officials, Liú Zhèng (劉政), a filial son from Míngzhōu (洺州), was specially appointed as the Crown Prince's Assistant for Beverages.
On the day Yǐhài,
the Emperor presided over the Ruìsī (睿思) Hall
and ordered singers to perform Nǚzhēn (女直) songs.
He looked at the Crown Prince and the various princes and said,
"I constantly recall the deeds of the previous dynasty,
never forgetting them for a moment.
Thus, I sometimes listen to these songs,
also wishing to let you know of them.
From a young age, you have only accustomed yourselves to Hàn (漢) customs,
not knowing the pure and simple ways of the Nǚzhēn (女直),
even to the point that you may not understand the writing and language.
This is forgetting your roots.
You must understand my intention,
and your descendants
must also follow my teachings and admonitions."
On the day Xīnsì,
the law concerning the theft of sacrificial offerings from ancestral temples was revised.
In the fifth month, on the first day Rénchén,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the day Wùxū,
Nǚzhēn (女直) people were prohibited from translating their surnames into Hàn (漢) surnames.
On the day Rényín,
Mèng Hào (孟浩), Prefect of Zhēndìng (真定), passed away.
On the day Jiǎchén,
the Department of State Affairs reported that
Fàn Sān (范三), a commoner from Dèngzhōu (鄧州), had committed murder by beating,
and deserved death,
but his parents were old and had no one to attend to them.
The Emperor said,
"Not contending in ugliness is called filial piety,
and only after being filial can one support their parents.
Did this person, forgetting his own life in a moment of anger,
have the heart to serve his parents?
He should be judged according to the law.
As for his parents,
the officials will provide for their support."
In the sixth month,
Wányán Sījìng (完顏思敬), Commissioner of Military Affairs, passed away.
In the seventh month, on the day Gēngzǐ,
Huìníng (會寧) Prefecture was again designated as Shangjīng (上京).
On the day Gēngxū,
the annual tribute of pheasant tails was abolished.
In the eighth month, on the day Dīngmǎo,
Zhào Wáng Yǒngzhōng, who was the acting Yǐn of Dàxīng Fǔ, was made Púmìshǐ.
An edict was issued granting awards to all deserving Měng'ān and Móukè of the third rank.
On the day Jǐmǎo,
Yùshǐ Dàfū Zhāng was dismissed.
On the day Bǐngxū,
Xiāng and others, who were Zuǒ Fùdū Diǎnjiǎn, were made envoys to congratulate Sòng on its birthday.
On the day Dīnghài,
there was an autumn hunt.
In the ninth month, on the first day Xīnmǎo,
Húshílái, a Sùzhí Jiāngjūn, was made envoy to the Xià state for its birthday.
On the day Xīnhài,
the court returned to the capital.
Lǐ Zhìjiū, a monk from Dàmíng Fǔ, and others conspired in rebellion,
and were executed.
In the tenth month, on the day Yǐchǒu,
the Jupiter appeared in daylight.
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
Tángkuò Ānlǐ, formerly Liúshǒu of Nánjīng, was made Shàngshū Yòuchéng.
In the eleventh month,
Zhāng, the Yǐn of Dàxīng Fǔ, was made envoy to congratulate Sòng on the New Year's Day,
and Dàdòng, the Yǐnjìnshǐ, was made envoy to Gāolí for its birthday.
The Emperor said to his chief ministers:
"There are many vacancies in the fifth-rank official positions in the outer circuits.
Why is this?"
Tàiwèi Lǐ Shí replied:
"Few meet the qualification requirements."
The Emperor said:
"If there are worthy and capable individuals,
they should be appointed without regard to normal seniority."
On the day Rénzǐ,
Lìbù Shàngshū Liáng Sù requested a ban on slaves and maidservants wearing silk gauze.
The Emperor said:
"It has already been forbidden for them to wear bright gold fabrics.
It is acceptable to implement this gradually.
Moreover, the implementation of moral education
should begin with the noble and close to the throne.
My own palace garments and articles
are always kept frugal;
those that used to be of bright gold
have already been reduced by more than half.
Recently, the customs among the common people,
compared to the Zhènglóng period, are reportedly somewhat simpler and more frugal.
You, my ministers, should strive even more to be frugal and simple,
so that the people know what to emulate."
In the fourteenth year, the first month, on the first day Jǐchǒu,
Sòng, Gāolí, and Xià sent envoys to offer congratulations.
In the second month, on the day Rénxū,
Zhāng, the Yǐn of Dàxīng Fǔ, was found guilty in his mission to Sòng,
beaten with one hundred and fifty strokes,
dismissed from office,
and the gifts he received were confiscated by the state.
On the day Bǐngyín,
Xíngbù Shàngshū Liáng Sù and others were made envoys to Sòng for detailed inquiry.
On the day Gēngwǔ,
Tàiwèi and Shàngshū Lìng Lǐ Shí was made Tàibǎo,
and retired.
On the day Wùyín,
an edict was issued to exempt the people affected by floods and droughts last year from rent and taxes.
In the third month, on the first day Wùzǐ,
during the Wànchūnjié festival,
Sòng, Gāolí, and Xià sent envoys to offer congratulations.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
the Emperor said to his chief ministers:
"Hǎilíng was purely devoted to official business;
at that time, the chief ministers and officials considered only bureaucratic paperwork as achievement.
You, my ministers, should consider methods of governance and statecraft,
and not be complacent with old practices."
An edict also stated:
"Henceforth, the people of the Měng'ān and Móukè
are not permitted to kill animals for sacrificial prayers.
On festival days or days of sacrifice to Heaven,
they are permitted to gather for drinks.
From the first day of the second month until the end of the eighth month,
all drinking and feasting are strictly prohibited,
nor are they allowed to attend gatherings elsewhere,
lest they impede agricultural work.
Even during leisure months, excessive drinking is not permitted;
violators shall be punished.
Let this be widely proclaimed."
It was also decreed:
"All imperial guards who are not proficient in the Nǚzhí language
shall be compelled to learn and practice it,
and from now on, the use of Hàn Chinese is not permitted."
On the day Xīnchǒu,
Venus and Jupiter appeared in daylight.
On the day Jiǎchén,
the Emperor changed his personal name to Yōng,
and this was announced throughout the realm.
On the day Bǐngchén,
Venus and Jupiter appeared in daylight,
traversing the sky.
In the fourth month, on the day Yǐchǒu,
the Emperor instructed his chief ministers:
"I hear that ignorant people, seeking blessings,
often build Buddhist temples.
Although there are already regulations prohibiting this,
many still violate them.
It is appropriate to reiterate the restrictions
to prevent the wasteful expenditure of resources."
On the day Wùchén,
rituals were performed at the Tàimiào,
with the Crown Prince acting on behalf of the Emperor.
On the day Yǐhài,
Wányán Púniè, the Quànnóng Fùshǐ, was made envoy for the bestowal of gifts to Gāolí.
The Emperor was at the Chuígǒng Diàn,
and looking at the Crown Prince and the imperial princes, said:
"Of human conduct,
none is greater than filial piety and fraternal respect.
Those who practice filial piety and fraternal respect invariably receive the protection of Heaven and the sun.
You should all fully practice filial piety towards your parents
and fraternal respect towards your brothers.
Since ancient times, relations between brothers
have often been estranged by wives and concubines,
leading to discord.
Moreover, wives are but members of external families;
how can they compare to the closeness of brothers?
If one listens to the words of a wife
and becomes estranged from brothers,
it is utterly unreasonable.
You should always keep my words in your hearts."
On the day Wùzǐ,
Túdān Kèníng, the Púmì Fùshǐ, was concurrently appointed Yǐn of Dàxīng Fǔ.
In the fifth month, on the first day Bǐngxū,
Liáng Sù and the other envoys for detailed inquiry returned from Sòng.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
the Emperor went to Jīnliánchuān.
In the sixth month, on the day Jǐwèi,
Venus appeared in daylight.
In the eighth month, on the day Dīngsì,
the Emperor arrived at Cí Lǐshé.
At midday,
a white dragon was seen in a small stream east of the imperial tent.
Shortly after,
it ascended with clouds and thunder and departed.
On the day Guǐhài,
there was a hunt at Mílíbǔ.
On the day Jǐmǎo,
Venus appeared in daylight.
In the ninth month, on the day Dīnghài,
the court returned to the capital.
On the day Yǐwèi,
Wányán Ràng, Shàngshū of the Bīngbù, and others were made envoys to congratulate Sòng on its birthday,
and Chóngsù, a Sùzhí Jiāngjūn, was made envoy to the Xià state for its birthday.
On the day Guǐmǎo,
after court was dismissed, the Emperor
said to his attendant ministers:
"From the time I was in the imperial residence and ascended the throne until now,
I have never been disingenuous or biased towards my relatives and old acquaintances.
Recently, the Yùshǐ Tái reported that
Púmìshǐ Yǒngzhōng once wrote a letter to Hénán Tǒngjūnshǐ Wányán Zhòng,
on the pretext of selling horses.
I knew of this but did not question it.
My disingenuousness,
this is the only instance,
and thinking of it day and night,
it is as if I have a sickness."
On the day Jǐyǒu,
Sòng sent an envoy in return for the previous mission.
In the tenth month, on the first day Yǐmǎo,
an edict was issued to have portraits of twenty meritorious officials painted in the left and right corridors of the Shèngwǔ Diàn in Yǎnqìng Gōng.
In the eleventh month, on the first day Jiǎshēn,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the day Bǐngshēn,
Liú Zhònghuì, Yùshǐ Zhōngchéng, and others were made envoys to congratulate Sòng on the New Year's Day.
On the day Wùxū,
the director of the Shàngshíjú was summoned,
and the Emperor instructed him:
"The food of the imperial kitchen
is all the fat and cream of the people.
Lately, there have been too many dishes and flavors,
which cannot all be consumed,
leading to wasteful expenditure.
From now on, only a few palatable dishes shall be served."
On the day Wùshēn,
Cáo Shìyuán, the director of the Yíluán Jú, was made envoy to the Gāolí state for its birthday.
In the twelfth month, on the day Wùyín,
Wányán Shǒudào, Píngzhāng Zhèngshì, was made Yòuchéngxiàng,
and Túdān Kèníng, the Púmì Fùshǐ, was made Píngzhāng Zhèngshì.
In the fifteenth year, the first month.
(This section is missing.
In the seventh month, on the day Bǐngwǔ,
Niánbá'ēn and his subordinate Kānglǐ Bóɡǔ and others came to pledge allegiance.
In the ninth month, on the day Wùzǐ,
the Emperor returned from Jīnliánchuān.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
Zhào Wèichǒng, Liúshǒu of Gāolí Xījīng, rebelled against his lord,
and requested to pledge allegiance with more than forty cities west of Cíbēilǐng
and east of the Yālù Jiāng,
but this was not accepted.
On the day Bǐngshēn,
the Emperor visited the new palace.
On the *jǐyǒu* day of the intercalary month, which was the first day of the month,

a regulation was established concerning the prohibition of bows, arrows, spears, and swords for various categories of people, including *lùfēn pǐnguān* (local officials), household retainers, and travelers, while permitting the carrying of bows and arrows.
The Emperor addressed Left Chancellor Liángbì, saying:
"Those currently holding official positions
must have their positions and responsibilities match their expectations,
only then do they begin to exert themselves.
If they are even slightly displeased,
they merely focus on passing the days.
How can this be the way of a loyal minister?"
On the *dīngsì* day,
he again said to Liángbì:
"During the time of Hǎilíng,
*Lǐngshěng Bǐngdé* and Left Chancellor Yán Jiē both had reputations for ability,
yet in governing, they did not focus on long-term plans,
but merely engaged in harshness.
Speaking of Yán Jí and Kěxǐ, when they were in Huìníng,
within a single month,
they flogged and killed twenty people,
whose crimes did not warrant death.
Was this reasonable?
Hǎilíng's character was like a tiger;
these individuals still wished to control him with schemes and calculations,
even to the point of sacrificing their integrity and meeting their deaths.
Can this be considered 'able'?"
On the *jǐwèi* day,
Wányán Wángxiáng, the *Guīdé Yǐn*, and others were appointed as envoys to congratulate Sòng on its birthday,
and Xiémǎo Héshang, *Fúbǎoláng*, was appointed as envoy to the Xià state for its birthday.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
the King of Gāolí reported that Zhào Wèichǒng had been executed,
and an imperial edict was issued to console and respond.
An edict commanded that the red and purple garments worn by imperial princes and officials' attendants be changed to black and purple.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
an edict stated that elderly persons should not be appointed as county magistrates.
If an elderly person is appointed to an administrative position,
their assistants should also be chosen from among the robust.
In the tenth month, on the *yǐwèi* day,
there was a winter hunt.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
they returned to the capital.
In the eleventh month, on the *yǐmǎo* day,
the Emperor visited the Eastern Palace.
Previously,
the son of Yílā Máodé, *Jiédùshǐ* of the Tánggǔ tribe, killed his wife and fled.
The Emperor ordered his capture.
By this time,
Imperial Aunt Liángguó Gōngzhǔ requested his pardon.
The Emperor said to the chancellors:
"The Princess is a woman;
she does not understand laws and regulations,
so her offense can still be forgiven.
But Máodé sought to intercede to this extent,
how can he be pardoned?"
The request was not granted.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
Jìng, *Yòuxuānhuīshǐ*, and others were appointed as envoys to congratulate Sòng on New Year's Day.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
Venus was seen in daylight.
On the *wùchén* day,
Ādiǎn Púlǔhǔ, *Sùzhí Jiāngjūn*, was appointed as envoy to Gāolí for its birthday.
On the *wùshēn* day, the first day of the first month of the sixteenth year,
Sòng, Gāolí, and Xià sent envoys to offer congratulations.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
an edict remitted the land taxes for areas affected by floods and droughts in the previous year.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
an edict ordered that all imperial clan members not yet included in the *Yùdié* (Imperial Genealogy) be compiled and added.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
the Emperor, with imperial princes, chancellors, and attendants, leisurely discussed the rise and fall of ancient and modern times,
saying:
"The flourishing of classics
has a long history,
and they instruct future generations,
being without imperfection.
Present-day scholars,
though able to recite them,
must also put them into practice.
However, many know but cannot act.
If one cannot act,
what is the benefit of reciting them?
The old customs of the Nǚzhēn were most pure and upright;
though they did not know how to read,
yet their sacrifices to Heaven and Earth,
respect for relatives,
deference to the elderly,
reception of guests,
trust in friends,
and meticulous禮儀 (propriety)
all came naturally.
Their goodness was no different from what is recorded in ancient books.
You all should learn and practice these;
the old customs must not be forgotten."
On the *wùchén* day,
there was a fire in the palace.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
the Emperor was inspecting falcons at Gāojiáo Bridge
when he saw a drunk man fall off his donkey and lie on the side of the road.
He ordered his attendants to help him up, mount him,
and send him home.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
the Imperial Aunt invited the Emperor to her private residence;
all the imperial consorts followed,
and the banquet was very joyful.
Whenever the Princess offered wine,
the Emperor stood and drank it.
In the second month, on the *gēngyín* day,
Princess of Bīnwáng, the imperial prince's consort,
Túdān Shì, was executed
for adultery.
On the *jǐhài* day,
Túdān Kèníng, *Píngzhāng Zhèngshì*, was dismissed
due to his daughter's fault.
In the third month, on the *bǐngwǔ* day, which was the first day of the month,
there was a solar eclipse.
On this day,
the Wànchūn Jié (Emperor's Birthday Festival)
was postponed to the next day.
Sòng, Gāolí, and Xià sent envoys to offer congratulations.
On the *wùshēn* day,
beans rained down in the territory of Línhuáng.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
the Emperor was at Guǎngréndian Palace,
and the Crown Prince and imperial princes all attended the meal.
The Emperor leisurely instructed them, saying:
"Generally, expenses should be managed with frugality.
If there is a surplus,
it can be used to help relatives;
do not waste it indiscriminately."
He then pointed to the robes he was wearing, saying:
"These robes have not been changed for three years,
and they are still perfectly good.
You all should learn from this."
On the *rénshēn* day,
the Wūdūwǎn Bùtúlǐ was re-established.
In the fourth month, on the *bǐngxū* day,
an edict ordered the establishment of schools in the capital prefecture to cultivate scholars,
and set up examination grades for imperial clan members and chancellors' sons.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
a regulation prohibited merchants' boats and carts from using horses.
Chóng Yǐn, *Dōngjīng Liúshǒu*, was appointed as *Shūmì Fùshǐ*.
On the *rényín* day,
he went to Jīnliánchuān.
In the fifth month, on the *wùshēn* day,
the palace in Nánjīng caught fire.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
Venus was seen in daylight.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
envoys were sent to pray for rain to the mountain spirit of Jìngníngshān,
and shortly thereafter, it rained.
In the sixth month,
there were locusts in the two circuits of Shāndōng.
In the seventh month, on the *rénzǐ* day,
Yílā Shānzhù, *Xiàjīn Xiànlìng*, was executed
for embezzlement.
In the eighth month, on the *xīnsì* day,
they arrived at Pīlìluò.
In the ninth month, on the *yǐsì* day,
they arrived from Jīnliánchuān.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
the Emperor instructed Left Chancellor Gēshíliè Liángbì, saying:
"The western frontier has always lacked provisions.
Order local officials to purchase grain there
as preparation for emergencies."
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
Púchá Tōng, *Diànqián Dūdiǎnjiǎn*, and others were appointed as envoys to congratulate Sòng on its birthday,
and Wányán Dígǔsù, *Sùzhí Jiāngjūn*, was appointed as envoy to the Xià state for its birthday.
The Emperor instructed Left Chancellor Liángbì, saying:
"Hǎilíng's unjust killings of ministers
are most lamentable.
As for the remains of Bólúnchū and others,
search for them in their respective locations,
and the government shall provide for their burial."
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
due to the fire in the Nánjīng palace,
officials of both the *Liúshǒu* and *Zhuǎnyùn* offices were punished.
In the tenth month, on the *bǐngshēn* day,
an edict instructed the chancellors, saying:
"The imperial princes' nicknames have never been given in Nǚzhēn language.
Now they should all be changed.
You all select names and present them."
In the eleventh month, on the *rénchén* day, which was the first day of the month,
Wáng Wèi, *Cānzhī Zhèngshì*, was dismissed.
The *Shàngshūshěng* reported that
Bóshùlǔ Shèshī, a *móukè* under the command of Húlāwēn *Méng'ān* in the Eastern Héběi Circuit,
ceded his *móukè* position to his nephew Púsùliè.
The Emperor deemed this virtuous and approved it,
further ordering a discussion on granting an award to Shèshī.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
Liú Chún, *Tóngzhī Xuānhuīyuàn Shì*, and others were appointed as envoys to congratulate Sòng on New Year's Day.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
Zhāng Rǔbì, *Lìbù Shàngshū*, was appointed as *Cānzhī Zhèngshì*.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
Xiánggǔ, son of Niángē Hánnú, was appointed as *Shàngniǎnjú Zhícháng*,
and Lóushì as *Wǔqì Zhícháng*.
Previously,
Hánnú had received an imperial order to recruit Qìdān Dàshí,
but his ultimate fate was unknown.
By this time, when Sālǐyǎyīn Tèsī, head of the Niánbá'ēn tribe, and others arrived,
the details of his death as a loyal martyr were ascertained,
hence his descendants were recorded.
Yílā Ziyuán, *Bīngbù Lángzhōng*, was sent as envoy to Gāolí for its birthday.
On the *rénshēn* day of the twelfth month,
an edict was issued that those who had entered officialdom through various examinations, after forty years of service, would be appointed as county magistrates.
Considering this period too long,
henceforth, those who have served for thirty-two years,
and have no other charges of corruption or embezzlement leading to dismissal,
shall be appointed as county magistrates.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
an edict was issued that old and sick displaced persons
should be provided for by the government.
The Emperor instructed his chief ministers, saying:
"If any matter that has been reported and decided upon turns out to be inappropriate,
you, my ministers, should not consider it already done
and refrain from reporting it for correction.
With the multitude of state affairs,
how could I be without error?
You, my ministers, simply speak up,
and I will make changes;
I will certainly not be reluctant."
On the *gēngyín* day,
the laws for rewards and punishments regarding incense and tea at state monopoly markets were established.
In the first month of the seventeenth year, on the *rén'yín* day,
Song, Gāolì, and Xià sent envoys to offer congratulations.
Gāolì also submitted a memorial expressing gratitude for not harboring Zhào Wèichǒng.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
the relevant authorities reported
that the jade belt presented by Gāolì was actually stone resembling jade.
The Emperor said:
"A small country may not have those who can distinguish it,
mistaking it for jade.
Moreover, people should not easily reject gifts,
but rather value the virtue behind them.
If we were to return it,
would that be proper etiquette?"
On the *wùshēn* day,
an edict was issued to construct the Divine Ancestor's Spirit Hall to the west of the Shèngwǔ Hall in Yǎnqìng Palace,
and the Divine Halls of Tàizōng and Ruìzōng to the east.
An edict was issued concerning the Qìdān households in the Northwest Route Pacification Commission:
those who had previously rebelled had already been dealt with;
those who did not participate in the rebellion and freed slaves could be resettled in Wūgǔlǐ Shíběi Department,
so that they could begin spring farming.
The Department of State Affairs reported that
the Wūdūwǎn Department's Tǐtǔ Húlǔ Yǎlǐmìsī requested to make offerings and join.
This was granted.
On the *gēngxū* day,
an edict was issued that for those high-ranking officials' families who should be granted the title of Meritorious Official,
since their descendants were not allowed to apply themselves,
the Kǎogōng Láng of the Ministry of Personnel should thoroughly investigate their merits and achievements,
and report those who deserved the title
to the Emperor immediately.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
the Emperor said to his chief ministers:
"Among the imperial clan, many elderly individuals
often lack official titles.
Their ancestors all rendered service to the state,
and I wish to grant them some official positions,
so that they may have a distinguished name and rank.
What do you think?"
They replied:
"Cherishing relatives and rewarding merit
are the excellent principles of the former kings."
On the *dīngsì* day,
an edict was issued that court officials would be granted three days leave for weddings and marriages,
without needing to submit an application.
On the *rénxū* day,
an edict was issued to the chief ministers:
"During the time of Hǎilíng,
the families of officials who were unjustly executed and whose property was confiscated
are all to be restored to commoner status.
The descendants of Liáo Yùwáng and Sòng Tiānshuǐ Jùnwáng, who were murdered,
are each to be buried in their old tombs in Guǎngníng and Hénán."
Later, another edict was issued:
"Apart from the relatives of Tiānshuǐ Jùnwáng being buried in Dūběi,
the bones deposited in Xiánpíng
are to be officially buried at their original location.
Those relatives of Liáo Yùwáng who have not yet entered their ancestral tombs
should also be moved and interred there."
In the third month, on the *xīnchǒu* day,
Song, Gāolì, and Xià sent envoys to offer congratulations.
On the *xīnhài* day,
an edict was issued to exempt ten circuits—Héběi, Shāndōng, Shǎnxī, Hédōng, Xījīng, and Liáodōng—from last year's land and locust taxes due to drought and locust plagues.
Relief was provided to the three circuits of Dōngjīng, Pósù, and Hésùguǎn.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
the Department of State Affairs reported that
the grain in the three circuits
was insufficient for distribution.
The Emperor said:
"I often told you, my ministers,
to widely purchase grain in years of abundance to prepare for lean times.
You all said that the granaries of the realm were overflowing.
Now, when relief is needed,
you say it is insufficient.
Since ancient times, emperors have always regarded accumulation as a long-term plan for the state.
Did I hoard grain
for my sole use?
Since it is insufficient now,
you can obtain it from neighboring circuits for relief.
From now on, this preparation
shall be customary."
In the fourth month, on the *jiǎxū* day,
an imperial decree stipulated that if a hereditary Měng'ān Móukè entered officialdom,
even if he had not reached sixty years of age,
if he wished for his descendants to inherit the title,
it would be permitted.
On the *wùyín* day,
the Emperor instructed his chief ministers, saying:
"Even if county officials are dismissed due to offenses,
after one or two years,
they should still be reinstated.
Měng'ān Móukè were all diligent and meritorious individuals who contributed to the state during Tàizǔ's founding.
Their hereditary official positions
should not be revoked for minor offenses."
On the *wùzǐ* day,
Túndān Wūzhě, the Chief Scribe of the Tengwáng Residence, was dismissed for improperly bestowing gifts upon the Gāolì envoy.
In the fifth month,
the Department of State Affairs reported the establishment of the seating order for imperial banquets involving imperial relatives above the degree of *tǎnmǐan*,
all following the Táng system.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
the Emperor visited Yáocūndiàn
and observed officials of the seventh rank and below, imperial clan members, and personnel from various bureaus practicing willow-shooting,
distributing rewards accordingly.
In the sixth month, on the *jǐmǎo* day,
the Emperor said to his chief ministers:
"I am old now.
I fear that due to momentary joy or anger,
my decisions may be inappropriate.
You, my ministers, should immediately remonstrate,
and not merely comply,
thus letting my mistakes stand."
On the *yǐwèi* day,
Sīliè, son of Yīngwáng Shuǎng, was appointed as Deputy Military Commissioner of the Zhōngshùn Army.
Shuǎng came to express his gratitude.
The Emperor said:
"Because of your illness,
I have specially appointed your son,
hoping that you will recover due to joy.
I wished to grant him a higher appointment immediately,
but I fear Sīliè is young
and not yet familiar with state affairs.
You must instruct him,
so that he has commendable achievements;
then he will be promoted further."
In the seventh month, on the *rénzǐ* day,
the Department of State Affairs reported that
thirty thousand sheep were annually bestowed upon the frontier soldiers in the Northwest Route.
The Emperor asked how they were transported,
but the chief ministers could not answer.
The Emperor said:
"Although I have retired from court,
I remain attentive to state affairs,
allowing myself no peace.
You, my ministers, should not think that trivial matters are beneath an emperor's inquiry,
but rather, because you have never diligently attended to state affairs,
I asked."
In this month,
there were heavy rains,
and the river burst its banks.
In the eighth month, on the *jǐsì* day,
the Emperor inspected the crops in the nearby suburbs.
On the *rénshēn* day,
the Censorate sent an investigating censor to examine officials in the Northeast Route.
He arbitrarily accepted litigation documents
and was deemed incompetent,
receiving fifty strokes of the bamboo.
On the *gēngchén* day,
the Emperor said to his chief ministers:
"Currently, among those in office,
what is seen by colleagues,
even if reasonable,
is invariably considered wrong,
thinking that if they agree,
others might say that policies do not originate from them.
There are many such people,
and I strongly disapprove.
Now, observing the judgments made by the Grand Court of Revision,
even when there are standard regulations,
if the principle cannot be applied, they present alternative viewpoints based on circumstances,
and I only take what is beneficial from them.
Indeed, the principle of being human
is to follow the good of others;
only then can one be considered good."
On the *rénwǔ* day,
the Emperor said to his chief ministers:
"Are there no talented individuals among the lower-ranking officials today?
It is merely that those in higher positions do not promote them,
because they resent their talent surpassing their own."
On the *bǐngxū* day,
the Emperor said to the Imperial Censor-in-Chief Gěshíliè Miǎo:
"The censors' duty to investigate the competence of officials
is to eliminate those who trouble the people,
and also to hope to find worthy individuals.
Now, wherever they go, they accept litigation documents
and listen to their baseless accusations.
How can those who govern effectively do their job?"
On the *dīngyǒu* day of the ninth month,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
Zǐ Yǒngdé was enfeoffed as King of Xuē.
Wányán Xíníliè and others, Right Deputy Grand Inspector, were appointed envoys to congratulate Sòng on its birthday.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
Shímò Hútǔ, Minister of the Board of War, was appointed envoy to the Xià Kingdom for its birthday.
On the *wùshēn* day,
there was an autumn hunt.
On the *gēngxū* day,
Jìxīng (Jupiter), Yínghuò (Mars), and Tàibái (Venus) gathered in the constellation Wěi.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
On the *jǐsì* day of the tenth month,
the Xià Kingdom presented one hundred tents.
An edict ordered them to be refused at the border.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
the officials concerned memorialized,
"Among the twenty meritorious officials whose portraits are hung in Yǎnqìnggōng Palace,
only five have posthumous titles.
We have now examined the meritorious deeds of the remaining fifteen
and propose their posthumous titles for your approval."
An edict approved it.
An edict ordered 100,000 sheep to be given to the Wūgǔlǐ Shílěi tribe for pasturing,
with their offspring to be distributed to the poor.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
a decree was issued to all *méng'ān*:
if a father held another office,
his son must be at least twenty-five years old to inherit the position.
On the *xīnsì* day,
the Emperor said to his chief ministers:
"Why is it that I hear no recommendations of worthy individuals from those in office today?
In the past, Dí Rénjié rose from a humble position,
firmly supported the Táng dynasty,
and restored it from danger to peace,
extending its longevity by several hundred years.
Though Rénjié was worthy,
how could he have recommended himself without Lóu Shīdé?"
On the *guǐwèi* day,
the regulations for guarding criminals against escape were changed.
The Emperor said to his chief ministers:
"Recently, I have observed that those who submit memorials
have little regard for major national interests.
While ancient remonstrators were loyal to the state,
they also sought fame.
Today's remonstrators act solely for personal gain.
For instance, Cáo Wàngzhī, Minister of the Board of Revenue, and Liáng Sù, Governor of Jǐnán, both submitted memorials on national affairs.
They were merely coveting positions in government;
what use were they to state administration?
If high officials are like this,
what of others?
In the past, when Hǎilíng marched south,
Qí Zǎi, Superintendent of the Imperial Medical Bureau, remonstrated strongly
and was executed in the marketplace.
He was the only one in this dynasty to do so."
On the *dīnghài* day,
the Emperor commanded his chief ministers:
"Tián Zhōngrú, Censor, once submitted a memorial on national affairs.
He should now be promoted
to encourage others."
On the *wùxū* day of the eleventh month,
Túdān Kèníng, Defender of Nánjīng, was appointed Grand Councilor.
On the *gēngxū* day,
the Emperor said to his chief ministers:
"I constantly fear that heavy taxation will distress our people.
From now on, even the trivial and intricate matters of levies in all circuits
must be fully reported to me."
The officials concerned memorialized that
the envoy from the Xià Kingdom who presented the imperial tents was allowed to enter due to the earnest plea of border officials.
Shí Jū, Left Assistant Minister of the Secretariat, was appointed Grand Councilor.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
Wányán Púlàdǔ, Governor of Yán'ān, and others were appointed envoys to congratulate Sòng on its New Year.
On the *wùchén* day of the twelfth month,
due to the old customs of Bóhǎi where men and women often married without rites,
but rather by abduction and elopement,
an edict was issued to strictly forbid this practice.
Offenders would be punished as adulterers.
Púsǎn Huáizhōng, General of the Imperial Guard, was appointed envoy to Gāolí for its birthday.
On the *jǐsì* day,
Tàibái (Venus) appeared during the day.
On the *rénshēn* day,
Tángkuò Ānlǐ, Right Assistant Minister of the Secretariat, was appointed Left Assistant Minister;
Púchá Tōng, Grand Inspector of the Imperial Guard, was appointed Right Assistant Minister.
The Emperor said to his chief ministers:
"I am now fifty-five years old.
If I pass sixty,
even if I wish to act,
I will no longer be able to.
While I am still hale and strong,
the incomplete *méng'ān móukè* system for the Nǚzhēn people,
the unfinished state administration,
and the inconsistent laws and regulations
should all be rectified and improved.
Whatever is implemented,
I will not be remiss."
On the *bǐngshēn* day, the first day of the first month of the eighteenth year,
envoys from Sòng, Gāolí, and Xià came to offer congratulations.
On the *rénchén* day,

regulations were established for the crimes of killing household slaves or servants who live separately, killing juniors or inferiors who live together, wantonly killing slaves, or wantonly beating and killing a blameless wife.
On the *gēngxū* day,
Yílà Jié, Compiler of the Imperial Diary, submitted a memorial stating:
"Every time matters are discussed in private,
even the imperial historians are not present to hear them,
making it impossible to record them."
The Emperor asked Grand Councilor Shí Jū and Left Assistant Minister Tángkuò Ānlǐ about this.
They replied:
"In ancient times,
the Son of Heaven had historians by his side,
who recorded every word and action,
to admonish the ruler
and ensure he had something to fear."
On the *gēngshēn* day,
taxes and rents for the previous year's disaster-stricken areas in Zhōngdū, Héběi, Hédōng, Shāndōng, Hénán, Shǎnxī,
and other circuits were remitted.
On the *rénxū* day,
the Emperor went on a spring hunt.
On the *bǐngyín* day, the first day of the second month,
the imperial procession reached Guǎnzhuāng.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
it reached Huágǎng.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
the Emperor returned to the palace.
On the *yǐwèi* day, the first day of the third month,
it was the Wànchūnjié festival,
and envoys from Sòng, Gāolí, and Xià came to offer congratulations.
On the *yǐsì* day,
an order was given allowing Nǚzhēn people guarding the borders to brew their own liquor for sacrifices, weddings, and festivals.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
the Emperor said to his chief ministers:
"The office of county magistrate is closest to the people,
and worthy talents should be employed in it.
Recently, many have broken the law,
and I hear of no capable officials.
While on the spring hunt,
I saw the magistrates of Shíchéng and Yùtián counties;
both were old
and merely clung to their salaries.
If it is like this in the capital region,
one can imagine the distant counties."
Grand Councilor Shí Jū replied:
"Jiāo Xù, Magistrate of Liángxiāng, and Lǐ Bódá, Magistrate of Qìngdōu, are both capable officials
and can be appointed."
The Emperor said:
"If what you say is true,
they can be promoted and appointed."
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
private citizens were forbidden from establishing new temples or monasteries.
Yīn Xiǎo'èr and others from Xiànzhōu plotted rebellion
and were executed.
On the *jǐsì* day of the fourth month,
the Emperor said to his chief ministers:
"Wherever I tour,
I always order officials to investigate the good and bad conduct of local officials.
Shímò Yǎo, former Registrar of Yùtián, is a capable official,
and can be appointed magistrate of that county."
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
Ābùhǎndéfǔ, Left Advisor to the Crown Prince, was appointed envoy to bestow gifts upon the Xià Kingdom.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day of the fifth month,
the Emperor went to Jīnliánchuān.
On the *gēngwǔ* day of the sixth month,
Héshíliè Liángbì, Left Chancellor of the Secretariat, passed away.
On the *xīnchǒu* day of the intercalary month,
an order was given to relieve the famine among the people of the Southwest and Northwest Pacification Commissions,
and among the relocated households of the Wūgǔlǐ Shílěi tribe.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day of the seventh month,
the Emperor said to his chief ministers:
"When officials first commit embezzlement,
it might be an error.
But to commit it a second time
shows no intention of reforming.
From now on, those who commit it a second time,
regardless of the amount embezzled, will all be dismissed from office."
On the *yǐsì* day of the eighth month,
the Emperor returned from Jīnliánchuān.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
Wányán Shǒudào, Right Chancellor of the Secretariat, was appointed Left Chancellor;
Shí Jū, Grand Councilor, was appointed Right Chancellor.
On the *xīnchén* day of the ninth month,
Zhāng Jiǔsī, Grand Judge, and others were appointed envoys to congratulate Sòng on its birthday;
Wányán Púlǔhǔ, Supervising Censor, was appointed envoy to the Xià Kingdom for its birthday.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
Tángkuò Ānlǐ, Left Assistant Minister of the Secretariat, was appointed Grand Councilor.
On the *yǐhài* day,
Púchá Tōng, Right Assistant Minister, was appointed Left Assistant Minister;
Yílà Dào, Participator in Government, was appointed Right Assistant Minister;
Niángē Wòtèlà, Minister of Justice, was appointed Participator in Government.
On the *gēngyín* day, the first day of the tenth month,
Shímò Jìnnú, Defender of Shǎnzhōu, was dismissed from office due to misconduct.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
Liú Zhònghuǐ, Censor-in-Chief,
and Lǐ Yú, Supervising Censor, were reprimanded for failing to investigate matters concerning the Grand Princess.
Each was demoted one rank.
On the Gēngshēn day of the eleventh month, the first day of the month,
the Shàngshūshěng reported,
proposing that Ākě be appointed acting Jìedùshǐ of Yǒngníng Jūn and Cìshǐ.
The Emperor said:
"Ākě is young,
and not yet experienced in affairs.
It is acceptable to appoint him as a subordinate official."
Píngzhāng Zhèngshì Tángkuò Ānlǐ reported:
"We proposed this position for Ākě because he is of the imperial clan."
The Emperor said:
"The prefect (jùnshǒu) is responsible for the well-being of a thousand miles;
how can one not choose a suitable person but instead favor one's relatives?
If, out of familial affection,
gifts are bestowed, however generous,
they do not harm governance.
But if one is made to govern a commandery (jùn) without the talent for it,
what will an entire region rely upon?"
On the Rénshēn day,
Wūyán Zhālà, Jìedùshǐ of Jìngnán Jūn, and others were appointed envoys to felicitate the Sòng on the New Year.
On the Bǐngzǐ day,
the Shàngshūshěng reported,
stating that Shí Ānjié, the magistrate of Chóngxìn Xiàn, bought carriage materials from the local people
but failed to pay for them for three days.
He should be demoted by one rank
and dismissed from his post.
The Emperor then said:
"For all officials,
one should simply select a few of the most corrupt and the most upright to promote or demote,
and then people will naturally know to be admonished and encouraged.
The governance of the court,
if too lenient, people will not know fear;
if too harsh, even minor flaws will not escape punishment.
One must only use moderate laws."
On the Wùyín day,
the Emperor reprimanded the chief ministers (zǎichén), saying:
"Recently I asked why Zhào Chéngyuán was reappointed.
You (qīng) said
that Prince Cáo had sent someone to speak of his talent and quick competence,
and so he was reappointed.
Though the nomination of officials and ranks
rests with you,
the power to grant or revoke
must emanate from me.
If the words of Prince Cáo are followed,
then if the Crown Prince were to issue an instruction,
it is clear it would be followed.
This matter I only learned of through your words;
how many unknown matters are there besides?
Moreover, is it permissible for you to publicly accept private requests and recommendations?"
It happened that Chéngyuán was formerly the Wénxué of Prince Cáo's residence,
and had committed adultery with a maid in the prince's household,
was flogged one hundred fifty times and dismissed,
but was then re-employed.
〔一０〕On the Bǐngxū day,
Wūgǔlùn Yuánzhōng, Shàngshū of the Lìbù, was appointed Yùshǐ Dàfū.
Zuǒ Guāngqìng, Shǐ of the Dōng Shànggémén, was appointed envoy to Gāolí for the King's birthday.
On the Gēngxū day of the twelfth month,
the grandson Wúdūbǔ was enfeoffed as Wēn Guógōng,
Mádágé as Jīnyuán Jùnwáng,
and Chéngqìng as Dào Guógōng.
On the Rénzǐ day,
the assembled officials presented to the Emperor
the "Great Jīn Received Mandate Ten Thousand Generations Treasure."
On the Gēngshēn day of the first month of the nineteenth year, the first day of the month,
Sòng, Gāolí, and Xià sent envoys to offer congratulations.
On the Dīngmǎo day,
the Emperor proceeded to Chūnshuǐ.
On the Jǐyǒu day of the second month,
he returned to the palace.
On the Yǐmǎo day,
taxes on fields of people affected by floods and droughts in the past year were remitted.
On the Jǐwèi day of the third month, the first day of the month,
it was the Wànchūnjié.
Sòng, Gāolí, and Xià sent envoys to offer congratulations.
On the Yǐchǒu day,
the Shàngshūshěng reported,
stating that Yán Kuí and sixty-seven other officials of the Kuīkèyuàn responsible for taxation deficits
should each be demoted by one rank.
The Emperor said:
"To allow those appointed by hereditary privilege to manage state monopolies,
this is a Liáo (dynasty) practice.
When a law is flawed, it should be changed.
If the laws of Táng and Sòng are applicable, then they should be adopted."
On the Jǐsì day,
the Emperor discussed historical matters with the chief ministers,
and further said:
"I observe that many previous historical records are overly complimentary.
Generally, historical writings value factual accuracy in recording events;
there is no need for exaggerated flattery."
On the Xīnwèi day,
the Emperor said to the chief ministers:
"Treacherous and corrupt officials,
when seeking to gain something,
often privately conspire with their partisans
and are unwilling to speak openly,
but make it a pretext for other matters,
seemingly not involved yet secretly working for it.
I observe that ancient wicked persons,
when the state was establishing an heir,
feared that an intelligent heir would be detrimental to them,
and often subtly hinted at dark schemes
to undermine the deliberation,
choosing only the dim-witted and weak to enthrone,
hoping to manipulate power for their own benefit in the future.
For example, Emperor Wǔ of Jìn wanted to enthrone his younger brother,
but corrupt officials obstructed him,
and Emperor Huì was ultimately enthroned,
leading to chaos and disaster.
This is clear proof."
On the Dīngchǒu day,
the Emperor said to the chief ministers:
"I observe that in previous dynasties, when a subject was about to remonstrate at court,
they would bid farewell to their parents, wives, and children,
indicating their resolve to die.
Their colleagues, witnessing their death,
also disregarded their own lives
and remonstrated again.
These were truly loyal to the state,
something difficult for ordinary people to achieve."
On the Jǐmǎo day,
an edict stipulated that officials responsible for investigation and impeachment who knew of a violation of the law but failed to report it
would be punished by one degree less than the offender's crime;
those with familial relations were permitted to recuse themselves.
The Emperor said to the chief ministers:
"Many people venerate Buddhism and Daoism,
hoping to gain blessings.
In my early years, I was also quite deluded by them,
but soon realized their error.
Moreover, Heaven establishes a ruler
to govern the people.
If one indulges in pleasure and neglects duties,
and wishes to obtain blessings by chance,
it is difficult.
If one can truly love and nurture the common people,
accord with Heaven's will,
blessings will surely be returned."
On the Jǐchǒu day of the fourth month, the first day of the month,
an imperial edict ordered relief for the people under the jurisdiction of the Xīnán Lù Zhāotǎosī.
On the Jǐyǒu day,
an edict was issued to the internal and external courts regarding the enshrinement of Mǐnzōng.
(or "the ascending and enshrinement of Mǐnzōng")
On the Dīngsì day,
Jupiter was seen in daylight.
On the Wùyín day of the fifth month,
the Emperor proceeded to Tàiníng Gōng.
On the Wùzǐ day of the sixth month, the first day of the month,
an imperial edict ordered revisions to the statutes.
On the Xīnwèi day of the seventh month,
the relevant authorities proposed assigning servants to Zhào Wángzǐ Shígǔnǎi.
The Emperor did not approve,
telling the chief ministers (zǎixiàng):
"My children are still young.
If they are indulged too much,
it will make their extravagance grow,
eventually making it difficult to restrain.
This cannot be allowed to continue.
Whenever my children come to attend upon me,
even amidst their laughter and amusement,
I must remain solemn,
and treat them with severity,
so that they may understand my intention to teach and admonish them,
and always be respectful and cautious, thus committing fewer faults."
On the Guǐyǒu day,
Xǔ Tōng and other people from Mì Zhōu plotted rebellion
and were executed.
On the Bǐngzǐ day,
Venus was seen in daylight.
On the Gēngchén day,
the Emperor returned from Tàiníng Gōng.
On the Rénchén day of the eighth month,
Shí Jū, Shàngshū Yòuchéngxiàng, retired.
On the Wùxū day,
Sòng Dàguān coins were made to be worth five (of the current currency).
On the Bǐngwǔ day,
Liú Xīzhōng, a person from Jǐnán, plotted rebellion
and was executed.
On the Wùwǔ day of the ninth month,
Púchá Dǐngshòu, Zuǒ Xuānhuīshǐ, and others were appointed envoys to felicitate the Sòng on their Emperor's birthday.
Péimǎn Húlà, Shuàifǔ Shuài of the Tàizǐ Zuǒwèilǜ, was appointed envoy to the Xià state for their Emperor's birthday.
On the Guǐhài day,
there was an autumn hunt.
On the Guǐwèi day,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
On the Xīnmǎo day of the tenth month,
Zhédiǎn, Xīnán Lù Zhāotǎoshǐ, was executed
for corruption.
On the Xīnhài day,
an edict stated that those who knowingly marry within the mourning period,
even if they confess, shall still be punished according to the law.
In the eleventh month, on the day Rénxū,
Zhāodé Huánghòu was reinterred,
and a great amnesty was granted.
Yīlà Zāo and others, Censor in Chief, were appointed envoys to congratulate the Sòng on the New Year.
On the day Wùchén,
Lú Gǒng, Western Chief of the Palace Gate, was appointed envoy to Gāolí for the Emperor's birthday.
On the day Rénshēn,
the Emperor went to Héjiān for winter hunting.
On the day Guǐwèi,
he returned from Héjiān.
In the twentieth year, on the first day of the first month, Jiǎyín,
envoys from Sòng, Gāolí, and Xià came to offer congratulations.
On the day Wùwǔ,
the regulations for testing clerks (lìngshǐ) were established.
On the day Rénxū,
an edict was issued to allocate five thousand strings of cash annually to provide liquor, ice, candles, medicine, and charcoal to all officials in the court,
distributed according to their rank.
On the day Jǐsì,
he went to Spring Water (Chūnshuǐ).
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
he visited the temporary palace in Shíchéng Xiàn.

On the day Yǐsì,

"Many Nǚzhí officials say that My diet is too frugal.
I disagree.
Indeed, excessive spending on one meal,
how can that be a good thing?
Moreover, I am old,
and I do not wish to slaughter living creatures.
Though I am the Son of Heaven,
to be able to be self-restrained
is not bad either.
My clothes and personal effects are sometimes old;
I always have them washed and cleaned,
and only when they are torn
do I replace them.
Previously, the curtains and tents were often decorated with gilded ornaments,
but now they are not.
As long as they are sufficient for use,
why must they be elaborate?"

On the day Rénwǔ,
the Emperor said to the Chief Ministers:
"To investigate minor details

and I know this.
However, since you gentlemen are so unmindful,
I occasionally investigate.
For example, the land beyond the mountains (shānhòu zhī dì) is all occupied by imperial princes, princesses, and powerful families,
who then sublet it to the people.
This is all due to your lack of vigilance.
You gentlemen should exert yourselves diligently in affairs,
so as not to trouble Me."
An edict ordered the relocation of the two Měng'ān of Yáoluòhé and Yímǎhé
to Dàmíng and Dōngpíng and other circuits for settlement.
On the day Wùxū,
the Emperor said to the Chief Ministers:
"When a person is in a low position,
desiring advancement, they strive to be public-spirited and incorruptible.
How can one distinguish between the worthy and the unworthy?
When they achieve prominence,
observing their actions
then reveals their true nature.
For example, Zhédiǎn, the Pacification Commissioner,
was initially the Assistant Prefect of Dìngzhōu,
then became the Commandant of the Metropolitan Area (dū sī).
He never showed the slightest favoritism,
and wherever he served, he had a reputation for integrity.
However, when he became Pacification Commissioner,
he did not firmly defend (his position).
The human heart is more treacherous than mountains and rivers,
indeed difficult to know."
On the day Rényín,
the Emperor said to the Chief Ministers:
"Recently I read the Zīzhì Tōngjiàn,
which compiles the rise and fall of successive dynasties,
providing excellent lessons and warnings.
Sīmǎ Guāng's diligence was such that
no good historian of ancient times could surpass him.
Máo Huī, the Compiler,
I have repeatedly asked him about affairs,
and he is excellent at responding.
He is truly a learned elder scholar.
He can be appointed to the duties of the Grand Minister of Sacrifices,
to be available for discussion."

In the twelfth month, on the day Xīnsì,
the Emperor said to the Chief Ministers:
"Qí Guó, when appointing people,
would promote them if a single word was agreeable to his intentions,
and punish them for a single misspoken word.
In human speech,
there are gains and losses;
even the worthy are not exempt.
From ancient times, people have always been tested by affairs.
If one relies solely on their responses in audiences,
how can one know whether a person is worthy or not?
When I select people,
I employ those whom the public approves,
and do not consider My own judgment as solely correct."

There was a man named Yílà Yúlǐyě,

He had one wife and one concubine.
His wife had six sons,
and his concubine had four sons.
When his wife died,

"She was our principal mother,

"Is it forbidden because of the consort's mourning?
The common people work daily for their food.
If it is forbidden, it would disrupt their livelihood.
Do not forbid it.
When I was about to go to Xìngdégōng earlier,

I noticed that some gates and shops on the streets

The Emperor said to his chief ministers:

Many high-ranking officials and powerful figures act unreasonably,

Púsàn Nàyě, the Vice Commissioner of the General Livestock Bureau, took two polo mallets from his subordinates,

Can this be called fulfilling one's duty?
No!
From now on, those censors whose duties are diligently performed will be promoted,

Jupiter was seen in broad daylight.
On the *rénshēn* day,
Chóng Yǐn, Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, was appointed Chancellor of the Department of State Affairs.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day of the intercalary month,
the Emperor said to his chief ministers:
“The governance of emperors and kings
is indeed founded on benevolence and compassion as virtues.
However, if one, like Emperor Wǔ of Liáng, focuses solely on benevolence and compassion,
it leads to a great breakdown of the established order.
I have often reflected on this:
if rewards and punishments are not abused,
that itself is benevolent governance.
What more needs to be done?”
He appointed Xiāng, the Left Executive of the Department of State Affairs, as Administrator of Governmental Affairs (*Píngzhāng Zhèngshì*);
Zhāng Rǔbì, the Right Executive, as Left Executive;
Niángē Wòtèlá, Participator in Governmental Affairs (*Cānzhī Zhèngshì*), as Right Executive;
and Zhāng Rǔlín, Minister of Rites, as Participator in Governmental Affairs.
He appointed Póluóhuǒ, Guardian of Xījīng, and others as envoys to congratulate the Sòng on the New Year.
A decree was issued that for officials serving in outer posts who had previously been chief ministers or executives,
when their official documents were submitted to the imperial secretariat or ministries,
they would, following the precedent for imperial princes,
be exempt from signing their names.
On the *wǔwǔ* day,
Jupiter was seen in broad daylight.
The Emperor said to his chief ministers:
“Jurchen *jìnshì* may be appointed as clerks in the imperial secretariat, just like Han *jìnshì*.
Scholars, by their conduct, are clean and upright,
and do not act contrary to ritual.
Those who rise from clerkship,
having been clerks from a young age,
become accustomed to greed and corruption.
When they become officials,
their ingrained habits cannot be changed.
The rise and fall of governance
is truly due to this.”
On the *gēngshēn* day,
Xú Wěi, Assistant Director of the Left Bureau of the Department of State Affairs, presented a memorial.
The Emperor said to his chief ministers:
“This person is pure and capable;
Guō Bāngjié, Director of the Right Bureau, is upright but somewhat impetuous.”
On the *guǐyǒu* day of the twelfth month,
the Emperor said to his chief ministers:
“Hǎilíng, perceiving his own deviation from the proper path,
feared that the imperial clan in Shàngjīng would rise up and plot against him.
Therefore, without distinguishing between close and distant relatives,
he moved them all south.
Was this not because he considered that Emperor Guāngwǔ of Hàn and King Kāng of Sòng, though of distant branches, were able to succeed to the great lineage,
and thus held this thought?
Such excessive worry,
how erroneous it was!”
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
Gāolì sent a messenger to report a royal mother's death.
On the *dīnghài* day,
Wūgǔlùn Yuánzhōng, Governor of Zhēndìng, was reinstated as Right Grand Councilor of the Department of State Affairs.
On the *xīnmǎo* day, the first day of the first month of the twenty-fourth year,
Sòng and Xià sent envoys to offer congratulations.
Xúzhōu presented eighteen stalks of auspicious *zhī* grass;
Zhēndìng presented two stalks of auspicious grain,
with six ears,
growing from different fields but having the same spikelets.
On the *wùxū* day,
the Emperor went for spring fishing at Chángchūn Gōng.
On the *rénshēn* day of the second month,
he returned to the capital.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
the Emperor said:
“I am going to Shàngjīng.
Considering that the customs of our dynasty highly value the Duānwǔ Festival,
when I arrive in Shàngjīng by Duānwǔ,
I will host a banquet for the elderly imperial clan members from the countryside.”
On the *jiǎxū* day,
a decree was issued that illegitimate sons of officials of the first rank, when receiving hereditary privilege,
would no longer require an imperial audience.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
Wányán Jìnr, Commissioner of the East Upper Gate, and others were appointed as envoys to offer imperial sacrifices to Gāolì;
Dà Zhòngyǐn, Commissioner of the West Upper Gate, as envoy to convey condolences;
Yǒngmíng, Chief Clerk of the Prince of Yú’s Household, as envoy for the resumption of duties;
and Mǒu, Commissioner of the Bureau of Utensils, as envoy to bestow gifts upon Xià.
On the *gēngyín* day, the first day of the third month,
on the Wànchūn Festival,
Sòng and Xià sent envoys to offer congratulations.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
as the Emperor was about to go to Shàngjīng,
the Department of State Affairs presented and settled
“All the Ceremonies for the Crown Prince’s Guardianship of the State.”
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
the Department of State Affairs presented
the “Imperial Seal for the Crown Prince’s Guardianship of the State.”
The Emperor summoned the Crown Prince and bestowed it upon him,
and admonished him, saying:
“Shàngjīng is the land where our ancestors rose to power.
I wish to visit it once with all the princes,
and perhaps stay for two or three years,
leaving you to guard the state.
This is like a farmer tending his fields,
or a merchant managing his wealth:
if one can simply not lose the family inheritance,
he is considered a worthy son.
How much more so for the heavy responsibility of the state,
where even greater caution is required.
I usually observe your great diligence,
and today, being able to relieve my worries,
shows your true filial piety from the heart.”
The Crown Prince repeatedly declined,
citing his unfamiliarity with governmental affairs,
and requested to accompany the Emperor.
The Emperor said:
“Governmental affairs are not very difficult;
just apply your mind with fairness and justice,
and do not accept slanders or evil,
and in time you will become proficient.”
The Crown Prince shed tears,
and all those around were moved by it.
The Crown Prince then accepted the seal.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
the Emperor went to the imperial mausoleums.
On the *jǐhài* day,
he returned to the capital.
On the *rénchén* day,
he departed for Shàngjīng.
Crown Prince Yǔngōng guarded the state.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
the chief ministers and executives, and those below them, bid farewell in Tōngzhōu.
The Emperor said to his chief ministers and executives:
“You are all veteran officials.
When the Crown Prince guards the state,
you should wholeheartedly assist him,
to fulfill my intentions.”
He also said to Túdān Kèníng, the Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs:
“After my inspection tour,
if something should happen,
you must attend to it personally.
Do not overlook minor details;
major difficulties are hard to resolve.”
He then looked at the officials of the Six Ministries and said:
“I hear that many documents from the secretariat and ministries are rejected for minor discrepancies,
seeking self-convenience,
which causes cases to remain unresolved for years.
I detest this greatly.
From now on, if something is actionable, act on it;
if it can be dismissed, dismiss it.
Do not let those below suffer from the lament of stagnation.”
At this time, all the princes accompanied the Emperor,
except for Zhào Wáng Yǒngzhōng, who remained to assist the Crown Prince.
On the *jǐwèi* day, the first day of the fourth month,
Venus was seen in broad daylight.
Yílà Dào, Governor of Xiánpíng, passed away.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
the Emperor arrived at Guǎngníng Fǔ.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
he arrived at Dōngjīng.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
he paid respects at Xiàoníng Gōng.
One year’s summer and autumn taxes and rents were remitted for the area within one hundred *lǐ* of Dōngjīng.
Those within the city walls who were seventy years old and without office were appointed to one official post.
A partial amnesty was granted for crimes punishable by two years of penal servitude or less, within one hundred *lǐ*.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
the Emperor observed fishing on the Húntóng Jiāng.
On the *jǐchǒu* day of the fifth month,
he arrived at Shàngjīng,
and resided in Guāngxīng Gōng.
On the *gēngyín* day,
he paid respects at Qìngyuán Gōng.
On the *wùxū* day,
a banquet was held at Huángwǔ Diàn.
The Emperor said to his imperial relatives:
“I have yearned for my homeland
for many days now.
Now that I am here,
we can enjoy ourselves to the fullest.
The sovereign and his ministers shall share in this.”
Gifts were bestowed upon the princesses, imperial consorts,
and wives of chief ministers, executives, and all officials, each according to their rank.
The imperial relatives all became happily drunk and danced,
and the celebration ended only at the close of day.
On the *xīnyǒu* day of the sixth month,
the Emperor visited Línyī Tíng by the Ànchūhǔ Shuǐ.
On the *rénxū* day,
he reviewed horses at Lǜyě Diàn.
On the *yǐwèi* day of the seventh month,
the Emperor said to his chief ministers:
“When the Son of Heaven conducts an inspection tour, he should promote good and punish evil.
All filial, fraternal, and harmonious commoners and scholars should be promoted and employed,
while those who disregard integrity and shame and lack moral conduct should be admonished and instructed.
If they do not repent, they should be punished.”
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
he hunted at Bóyě Diàn.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
the Emperor said to his chief ministers:
“People nowadays,
if they commit a crime and are not questioned,
after the event, they claim ignorance.
If a crime is definitely punished,
they say that every matter is scrutinized for faults.
Such is the decline of customs.
If we do not transform them with civil virtue,
we cannot return to ancient ways.
You, my ministers, assisting with virtue,
should ensure that the ancient customs are restored.”
In the eighth month, on the day Guǐhài,
Zhāng Dàjié (張大節), Supervisor of the Privy Treasury (Tàifǔjiān), and others were dispatched as envoys to congratulate Sòng on its emperor's birthday.
Yáolǐ Tèkèmògē (遙里特末哥), Palace Censor (Shìyùshǐ), was dispatched as envoy to the Xià (夏) Kingdom for its emperor's birthday.
On the day Yǐhài,
an imperial edict exempted Shàngjīng (上京) from market taxes for the current year.
In the ninth month, on the day Jiǎchén,
Jupiter was seen in broad daylight.
In the tenth month, on the day Dīngmǎo,
there was a hunt in the near suburbs.
In the eleventh month, on the day Xīnmǎo,
he returned to the palace.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
an imperial edict stated that due to the cold weather and distant location of Shàngjīng (上京),
there was no longer a need to send envoys for the Sòng (宋) New Year and emperor's birthday,
nor for the Gāolì (高麗) and Xià (夏) Kingdoms' emperors' birthdays.
The relevant authorities were
ordered to issue a notification.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
the Department of State Affairs (Shàngshū Shěng) memorialized to relocate three *mèng'ān* (猛安) and twenty-four *móukè* (謀克) from Sùpín (速頻) and Húlígǎi (胡里改) to populate Shàngjīng (上京).
In the twelfth month, on the day Bǐngchén,
there was a hunt in the near suburbs.
On the day Jǐmǎo,
he returned to the palace.
The twenty-fifth year, first month, on the day Yǐyǒu (the first day of the month).
On the day Dīnghài,
an imperial banquet was held for consorts, imperial princes, princesses, and civil and military attendant officials at Guāngdé Diàn (光德殿).
Imperial kinsmen, their wives, and ladies of the fifth rank and above,
numbering over 1,700 guests,
received various rewards.
In the second month, on the day Guǐyǒu,
Wūgǔlún Sīliè (烏古論思列), Administrator of Dōngpíng (東平 Yǐn), was executed
for harboring resentment and discontent.
On the day Dīngchǒu,
he went to Chūnshuǐ (春水).
In the fourth month, on the day Jǐwèi,
he arrived back from Chūnshuǐ (春水).
On the day Guǐhài,
he went to Huángwǔ Diàn (皇武殿) to play polo,
allowing soldiers and common people to watch freely.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
an imperial edict ordered the selection of thirty *móukè* (謀克) from the *mèng'ān* (猛安) of Sùpín (速頻) and Húlígǎi (胡里改) Routes to form three *mèng'ān* (猛安),
to be moved to the lands bordering Shuàidūpànkū (率督畔窟),
to populate Shàngjīng (上京).
On the day Rénshēn,
Huìníng Fǔ (會寧府) received a partial amnesty,
and its rent and taxes for the current year were exempted.
Common people aged seventy and above were granted one official rank.
On the day Jiǎxū,
one official from Huìníng Fǔ (會寧府) was concurrently appointed Grand Director of the Imperial Clan (Dàzōngzhèngchéng),
to manage affairs of the imperial clan.
The Emperor said to his officials:
"I truly enjoy the scenery and customs of Shàngjīng (上京).
Each time I return to the capital,
I feel a pang of sadness.
This is the ancestral homeland,
and I cannot bear to leave it.
After a myriad of years,
I wish to be laid beside Tàizǔ (太祖).
You, my ministers, must not forget my words."
On the day Dīngchǒu,
a banquet was held for imperial kinsmen and their wives at Huángwǔ Diàn (皇武殿).
Those in the *dàgōng* (大功) mourning degree were personally granted three official ranks,
those in *xiǎogōng* (小功) two ranks,
and those in *sīmá* (緦麻) one rank.
Those of high age and close kinship were additionally granted the title of Xuānwǔ Jiāngjūn (宣武將軍).
Imperial clan women were enfeoffed,
and silver and silk were distributed in varying amounts.
He said,
"I usually do not drink wine,
but today I truly wish to get drunk;
such joy is not easily found."
The imperial clan women, officials, and elders rose in turn to dance
and offered wine.
The Emperor said,
"In the past few months,
not one person has sung an indigenous song.
I shall sing one for you all."
He ordered the imperial clan youths who were seated below the hall to all be seated above the hall,
to listen to the Emperor sing himself.
His lyrics spoke of the difficulty of establishing an imperial enterprise
and the challenge of carrying on the legacy.
When he reached the line,
"With deep emotion I recall our ancestors,
as if I behold them clearly,"
he was so filled with fervor and sorrow
that he could not complete the song,
and after finishing, tears streamed down.
The Right Chancellor (Yòuchéngxiàng) Yuánzhōng (元忠), leading all officials and imperial relatives, offered a toast to the Emperor,
all exclaiming "Long Live!"
Thereupon,
the various ladies in turn sang indigenous songs,
like a private family gathering.
Once he was drunk,
the Emperor continued to play music
until the first drum roll ended the festivities.
On the day Jǐmǎo,
he departed Shàngjīng (上京).
On the day Gēngchén,
the imperial kinsmen and relatives bid farewell.
The Emperor said,
"I have long yearned for my homeland,
and deeply wished to stay for one or two years.
However, the capital is the foundation of the empire,
so I cannot remain here long.
For many years, there has been peace,
and the country has been free from levies and corvée.
You all have become extravagant and indulgent,
often falling into poverty.
I pity you greatly.
You must practice frugality;
do not forget the hardships of your ancestors."
Upon this, several lines of tears streamed down,
and the imperial kinsmen and relatives, all moved to tears, withdrew.
In the fifth month, on the day Gēngyín,
Xiāng (襄), Executive of the Department of State Affairs (Píngzhāng Zhèngshì), Píngshān (平山), Palace Attendant (Fèngyù), and others shot a pregnant rabbit.
The Emperor, enraged, had Píngshān (平山) flogged thirty strokes,
and summoned Xiāng (襄) to admonish him,
then issued an edict prohibiting the hunting of pregnant rabbits.
On the day Rényín,
he stopped at Hǎoshuǐ Chuān (好水川) by Tiānpíng Shān (天平山).
On the day Guǐmǎo,
envoys were dispatched to Línhuáng (臨潢) and Tàizhōu (泰州) to encourage agriculture.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
officials from the Department of State Affairs (Shàngshū Shěng) were ordered to wear narrow purple robes when submitting memorials.
In the sixth month, on the day Jiǎyín,
when hunting in the nearby mountains,
he saw neglected field ridges
and ordered the field workers flogged.
On the day Gēngshēn,
Imperial Crown Prince Yǔngōng (允恭) passed away.
On the day Bǐngyín,
Wūgǔlún Yuánzhōng (烏古論元忠), Right Chancellor of the Department of State Affairs (Shàngshū Yòuchéngxiàng), was dismissed.
On the day Gēngwǔ,
Tángkuò Dǐng (唐括鼎), Left Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs (Zuǒxuānhuī Shǐ), was dispatched to the capital (Jīngshī)
to offer sacrifices to the Imperial Crown Prince.
On the day Wùyín,
the Imperial Crown Prince's consort and all imperial grandchildren were ordered to observe mourning,
following Han (漢) rites.
In the seventh month, on the day Wùshēn,
he departed Hǎoshuǐ Chuān (好水川).
In the ninth month, on the day Xīnsì (the first day of the month),
he stopped at Xiáshā Hé (轄沙河),
and bestowed silk upon a centenarian old woman.
On the day Jiǎshēn,
he stopped at Liáo Shuǐ (遼水),
and summoned a 120-year-old Nǚzhēn (女直) elder,
who was able to recount the founding deeds of Tàizǔ (太祖).
The Emperor praised him,
bestowed food,
and also silk.
On the day Jǐyǒu,
he arrived back from Shàngjīng (上京).
On this day,
the Emperor personally offered sacrifices to Xuānxīao Huáng Tàizǐ (宣孝皇太子) at Xīchūn Yuán (熙春園).
In the tenth month, on the day Bǐngchén,
the Department of State Affairs (Shàngshū Shěng) memorialized that the number of imperial guards (qīnjūn) was too high
and should be slightly reduced.
An edict set the fixed number at three thousand.
After the chief ministers withdrew,
the Emperor said to his attendants,
"The chief ministers are old and find it difficult to stand for long.
A small couch should be placed in the corridor for them,
to allow them a little rest."
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
the hunting and gathering of game in Shàngjīng (上京) and other routes during heavy snow and when pregnant was prohibited.
The Emperor said to the chief ministers,
"When old guards are retired from their positions and appointed to govern the people,
if they cannot even draw characters by hand,
how can they govern the people?
One cannot know the brightness or darkness within a person's heart from the outside,
but when their spirit is confused and senile, it is evident externally.
This is forcing them to do what they cannot.
The Son of Heaven regards the myriad people as his children,
but cannot personally attend to every household.
It all depends on employing the right people.
If one knows they are incapable yet still appoints them,
what will the common people say of me?"
On the day Dīngchǒu,

officials of the Hanlin Academy (Xuéshì Yuàn), Censorate (Jiàn Yuàn), Secretariat (Mìshū Jiān), Astronomical Bureau (Sītiān Tái), Bureau of Historiography (Zhùzuò Jú), Bureau of Palace Gates (Gémén), Bureau of Palace Communications (Tōngjìn), Palace Guard (Gǒngwèi), and Armory (Zhíwǔqì Shǔ),
who were on duty in the palace,
were permitted to retire before noon.
On the *gēngchén* day of the eleventh month, which was the first day of the month,
an edict stated:
“Until the *chái* (jackal) has offered its sacrifices to the beasts,
hunting and fishing are not permitted.
In the winter months,
when snow accumulates to a *chǐ* or more,
nets and quick-cast seines are not permitted for use in the sea,
lest animal species be exhausted.”
The Planet Jupiter was seen in daylight.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
Táibái (Venus) was seen in daylight.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
Púsàn Shǒuzhōng, the Yin of Línchuáng, and others were appointed as envoys to congratulate the Sòng on the New Year.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
the Xià Kingdom sent an envoy to inquire about the emperor’s well-being.
On the *wùxū* day,
Cáo Wáng Yǒnggōng was appointed as Yùshǐ Dàfū.
On the *rényín* day,
Yílà Lǚ, a Yuánwàiláng of the Lǐbù, was appointed as an envoy to Gāolí for the king's birthday.
On the *wùwǔ* day of the twelfth month,
the imperial grandson Mā Dá Gē, King of Jīnyuán Jùn, was appointed to govern Dàxīng Yǐn,
and was promoted to be King Yuán.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
Táibái (Venus) was seen in daylight,
traversing the sky.
On the *bǐngyín* day,

Zuǒ Chéngxiàng Wányán Shǒudào, Zuǒ Chéng Zhāng Rǔbì, Yòu Chéng Niángē Wòtèlá, and Cānzhī Zhèngshì Zhāng Rǔlín were punished for unilaterally increasing the food allowance for the imperial grandsons of the Eastern Palace,
each being demoted one rank.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
an imperial decree increased the monthly stipends of Liúshǒu, Tǒngjūn, Zǒngguǎn, Zhāotǎo, Dū Zhuǎnyùn, Fǔyǐn, Zhuǎnyùn, and Jiédùshǐ.
The emperor said to his chief ministers:
“Tàiwèi Shǒudào, in discussing affairs, only seeks to be lenient,
and often wishes to reappoint those who were dismissed from office for crimes.
If the principal offenders are punished,
those who come after will know fear.
If they are reappointed after committing crimes,
how can this serve as a warning?”
On this day,
an order was given to cast a copper seal
named “Lǐxìn Zhī Bǎo” (Seal of Propriety and Trust),
which was to be used whenever
gifts were sent to foreign regions, for sealing the gift bags.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
the emperor asked his chief ministers:
“How is King Yuán performing his duties in Dàxīng?”
Yòu Chéng Wòtèlá replied:
“I hear that all the people of the capital praise him.”
The emperor said:
“I ordered an investigation among the populace,
and they all said he is very clear-sighted in handling affairs,
and his decisions on rewards and punishments are always appropriate.
Kings Cáo and Bīn cannot match him.
I also heard that when a Nǚzhēn person presented a grievance,
