he questioned them in Nǚzhēn language; when a Hàn person presented a grievance,
he questioned them in Hàn language.
Generally, it is good to practice the language of our dynasty;
if not practiced,
then the pure customs will be abandoned.”
Rǔbì replied:
“Not forgetting one's origins is
the way of the sages.”
Wòtèlá said:
“Even Xi Xià, a small state,
by adhering to old customs,
was able to preserve its state for several centuries.”
The emperor said:
“Affairs must be handled with truthfulness.
If there is falsehood in one matter, a hundred truths will be lost.
Therefore, for all matters, nothing is better than truthfulness.”
On the *gēngchén* day of the first month of the 26th year, which was the first day of the month,
envoys from Sòng, Gāolí, and Xià came to offer congratulations.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
the emperor went to Chángchūn Gōng for the spring hunt.
On the *guǐyǒu* day of the second month,
he returned to the capital.
On the *yǐhài* day,
an edict stated:
“Every quarter, seek out scholars,
ask them difficult questions,
and let them resolve them.
Those whose talent and insight are commendable
should then have their administrative records investigated,
and if their words and actions correspond,
they shall be promoted and employed.”
On the *jǐmǎo* day of the third month, which was the first day of the month,
on the Wànchūnjié festival,
envoys from Sòng, Gāolí, and Xià came to offer congratulations.
On the *dīnghài* day,
as the position of Dàlǐ Qīng was vacant,
the emperor asked who would be suitable.
Yòu Chéng Niángē Wòtèlá said
that the former Lìbù Shàngshū Tángguō Gòng would be suitable,
so he was appointed to that office.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
when the Shàngshūshěng presented a proposal for appointments,
the emperor said:
“You, my ministers, in the ministry, have never recommended worthy individuals;
you are only limited by rank and seniority.
How can you obtain competent people?
In ancient times, there were commoners who became prime ministers.
I hear that the Sòng also frequently employs obscure people from Shāndōng and Hénán who are far from the center of power,
and are not restricted by nobility or closeness to the court.
Given the vast territory of our dynasty,
how can there be no such people?
It is difficult for me to know all of them,
and you do not recommend them.
Since ancient times, has there ever been anyone who served as prime minister for life?
Among external officials of the third rank or higher,
there must be capable individuals,
but they just don't have a reason to be promoted.”
Zuǒ Chéng Zhāng Rǔbì said:
“Even if those in lower positions possess talent,
it must be tested to be seen.”
Cānzhèng Chéng Huī said:
“Even if an external official has a reputation,
once they enter the court,
they might not prove competent for the position,
and would also need to be eliminated.”
On the *guǐsì* day,
the Xiāngshān Sì was completed.
The emperor visited the temple,
bestowed upon it the name Dà Yǒng'ān,
and granted it two thousand *mǔ* of land,
seven thousand chestnut trees,
and twenty thousand strings of cash.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
based on the words of the imperial guard Wányán Qǐnú,
an edict was issued that all Měng'ān and Móukè must first read Nǚzhēn script historical classics before inheriting their positions.
The emperor then said:
“If they are just somewhat conversant with ancient and modern affairs,
they will not be willing to do wrong.
You, a rough common soldier of the imperial guard,
can say this;
if it is indeed beneficial,
why hesitate to follow it?”
On the *rénzǐ* day of the fourth month,
the Shàngshūshěng presented a memorial finalizing the law on compensation for shortfalls by supervisory officials in the Yuànwù and the rules for Héngbān.
The emperor then said:
“My daily imperial meals are also reduced and frugal.
Once a princess arrived,
and there was no leftover food to give her;
the duty officers all witnessed this.
If I wished for abundance,
even consuming fifty sheep daily would not be difficult,
but all that is the fat and toil of the people,
and I cannot bear to do it.
Supervisory officials only know how to benefit themselves,
not knowing where their profits come from.
I have served in external posts,
and am thoroughly aware of the affairs of the common people.
I imagine that many rulers of previous dynasties,
though enjoying wealth and status, did not know the hardship of farming,
and their loss of the empire
all stemmed from this.
The Liáo emperor, hearing that the people lacked food,
asked why they did not eat dried meat.
This was because he lost the instruction of his teachers and guardians in his youth,
and when he ascended the throne,
he consequently did not know the suffering of the common people.
During the reign of Suí Yángdì,
Yáng Sù wielded exclusive power and acted arbitrarily,
which was the fault of not carefully entrusting responsibilities.
If one associates with upright people,
what one knows will certainly be the right path,
and what one hears will certainly be righteous words;
one must not be careless.
Now, for the officials and subordinates of King Yuán’s residence,
those who are pure, cautious, and inherently upright should be selected,
and those with manipulative schemes should not be used.”
On the *wùwǔ* day,
Shàngshū Zuǒ Chéng Zhāng Rǔbì was dismissed.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
the emperor visited Shòu'ān Gōng.
On the *rénxū* day,
Tàiwèi and Zuǒ Chéngxiàng Wányán Shǒudào retired.
Lǐ Pán, the Kèshěng Shǐ, was appointed as the envoy to Gāolí for the special bestowal of gifts.
The Shàngshūshěng memorialized that
“the Běijīng Zhuǎnyùn Shǐ was dismissed for corruption.”
When the Shàngshūshěng reported on affairs,
the emperor said:
“Recently there was a memorial stating
that officials dismissed for crimes should not be re-employed,
and I believe this statement is extremely apt.
In cases of urgent military necessity,
they may be temporarily employed.
But now that the empire is at peace,
if we re-employ such people,
how will we warn future generations?”
It was further memorialized
that “in previous years, due to floods and droughts in various circuits,
out of over 210,000 *qǐng* of military and civilian land,
it was proposed to exempt over 490,000 *shí* of tax,”
which was approved.
An edict stated:
“The current taxes
are administered according to ancient practices,
but in cases of disaster or damage,
exemptions are always granted.”
In the fifth month, on the day Jiăshēn,
Túdān Kèníng, Sītú and Shūmìshǐ, was appointed Tàiwèi and Shàngshū Zuǒchéngxiàng.
Zhào Wáng Yǒngzhōng, Pàn Dàzōngzhèng Shì, was reinstated as Shūmìshǐ.
Yuán Wáng Mádágé, Dàxīng Yǐn, was appointed Shàngshū Yòuchéngxiàng,
and granted the name Jǐng.
Cānzhī Zhèngshì Chéng Huī retired.
On the day Wùzǐ,
the Lúgōu River burst its banks at Shàngyáng Cūn.
The turbulent waters formed a river,
which was then utilized.
On the day Gēngyín,
Yùshǐ Dàfū Cáo Wáng Yǒnggōng was dismissed.
Bīn Wáng Yǒngchéng was appointed Yùshǐ Dàfū.
On the day Wùxū,
Niángē Wòtèlà, Shàngshū Yòuchéng, was appointed Zuǒchéng.
Zhāng Rǔlín, Cānzhī Zhèngshì, was appointed Yòuchéng.
In the sixth month, on the day Guǐhài,
the Shàngshūshěng reported on the hereditary mòkè of Sùpín and Húlígǎi.
The Emperor said:
"These people are all brave and fierce.
In the past, Shìzǔ neighbored them,
and after years of bitter fighting,
was barely able to subdue them.
Thereafter, they would submit and then rebel.
It was not until the time of Mù and Kāng
that they finally submitted to civilization.
In recent times, they have also been partially relocated.
I wish to gradually move their people to Shàngjīng.
This is a long-term plan for the state."
On the day Jǐsì,
the Emperor said to the prime ministers and executive officials:
"Qí Huán was a mediocre ruler,
but by obtaining a Guǎn Zhòng,
he achieved hegemony.
I reflect day and night,
only fearing the loss of talent.
Since I do not know,
and you gentlemen do not recommend,
it will be difficult to await completely talented individuals before promoting them.
Indeed, it is difficult.
If someone is recommended as being skilled in a certain matter,
I will employ them according to their ability.
I and you gentlemen are both growing old.
The world is vast,
how can there be no talent?
Recommending talented individuals
is the urgent task of today."
He further said:
"While capable and competent individuals
are indeed not easy to come by,
they are still not as good as those of virtuous conduct."
The Emperor said to Yòuchéngxiàng Yuán Wáng:
"Have you ever read the Tàizǔ Shílù?
When Tàizǔ campaigned against Má Chǎn,
he ambushed him.
Upon reaching a muddy swamp, the horses could not advance.
Tàizǔ dismounted and proceeded on foot.
Huāndū shot and wounded Má Chǎn,
and thus captured him.
The difficulty of founding an enterprise is like this,
should it not be pondered?"
On the day Jiǎxū,
an imperial edict stated:
"All submissions and documents of proposals should be sent to the Dēngwén Jiǎnyuàn, then forwarded to the Xuéshìyuàn for reporting to the Emperor,
without passing through the Shěngtíng."
In the seventh month, on the day Rénwǔ,
an imperial edict granted concurrent office salaries to officials both inside and outside the court.
On the day Bǐngshēn,
Mǎ Huìdí, Yùshǐ Zhōngchéng, was appointed Cānzhī Zhèngshì.
On the day Gēngzǐ,
the Emperor heard that Zhào Xīruì, Tóngzhī Zhōngdū Lù Dōuzhuǎnyùnshǐ Shì,
often failed to sign documents concerning financial and grain matters while in office,
only thinking of his own safety.
He was demoted to Jīshí Zhōu Cìshǐ.
In the intercalary month, on the day Jǐwèi,
the capital was returned to.
In the eighth month, on the day Dīngchǒu,
the Emperor said to his chief ministers:
"Even if the imperial guards are illiterate,
they should be appointed to office according to regulations.
However, if they are involved in corruption,
they must be severely punished."
Tàiwèi Zuǒchéngxiàng Kèníng said:
"According to the law, that is permissible."
The Emperor said:
"I have never failed to treat the Nǚzhí people with kindness and solicitude.
However, if they are involved in corruption,
even my own children and younger relatives cannot be excused.
The Tàiwèi's intention
is to be lenient towards the Nǚzhí people."
On the day Wùyín,
the Shàngshūshěng reported
that the river had burst its banks,
and Wèizhōu was damaged.
Wáng Jì, Hùbù Shìláng, and Wáng Rǔjiā, Dūshuǐ Shàojiān, were ordered to relocate Zàochéng Xiàn of Wèizhōu.
On the day Dīnghài,
the Shàngshūshěng reported
that Lǐ Yàn, Lìbù Shìláng, and twenty-five others were dispatched to various circuits to assess the resources of each circuit.
This was approved.
On the day Jǐchǒu,
Lǐ Dákkě, Sùzhí Jiāngjūn, was appointed envoy for the Xia Kingdom's birthday.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
Zōng Hào, Yìdū Yǐn, and others were appointed envoys to congratulate the Song on their birthday.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
there was an autumn hunt.
On the day Gēngzǐ,
they reached Jìzhōu.
On the day Xīnchǒu,
they visited Xiāndòng Sì.
On the day Rényín,
they visited Xiānglín and Jìngmíng monasteries.
In the ninth month, on the first day Jiǎchén,
they visited Pánshān Shàngfāng Sì,
and then toured Zhōngpán, Tiānxiāng, and Gǎnhuà monasteries.
On the day Gēngshēn,
they returned to the capital.
On the day Bǐngyín,
the Emperor said to his chief ministers:
"The Wūdígǎi have rebelled and fled.
People have already been sent to suppress them.
Reinforce them with armored soldiers
and destroy their boats."
Cānzhī Zhèngshì Mǎ Huìdí said:
"Their people are not worth employing,
and their land is not worth inhabiting.
Perhaps it is not worth troubling Your Majesty's thoughts."
The Emperor said:
"I also know that this kind of people is useless.
The reason for destroying their boats
is to prevent them from again eyeing the border."
In the tenth month, on the day Wùyín,
the law was established for officials involved in corruption to supervise each other.
On the day Gēngyín,
the Emperor said to his chief ministers:
"The Southwest and Northwest Lù Zhāotǎosī territories are narrow,
and the mèng'ān households have no place for hunting,
thus they cannot practice horsemanship and archery.
Each mèng'ān and mòkè official is entrusted to drill them regularly.
Those who are slack, exceed the deadline, or do not personally supervise
shall all be punished with a beating."
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
an edict was issued to increase the number of river defense troops.
On the day Wùxū,
Chóngsù, Níngchāngjūn Jiédùshǐ, and Zhōngdào, Xíngjūn Dūtǒng, for returning from suppressing the Wūdígǎi without waiting for victory,
Chóngsù was flogged seventy times and
demoted one rank.
Zhōngdào was flogged eighty times and
demoted three ranks.
In the eleventh month, on the *jiǎchén* day, the first day of the month,
the rituals for the ancestral temple offerings to Mǐnzōng were finalized.
The Emperor said to his chief ministers:
"Among the Nǚzhēn people, truly outstanding individuals
whom I have known since I was young
are indeed hard to find.
The newly appointed *jìnshì*, such as Túshān Yì, Jiágǔ Ālǐbǔ, and Nímánggǔ Jiàn, are all capable men.
Those who rose through clerical work,
though their talent and ability may be useful,
their integrity and uprightness
can never equal that of the *jìnshì*.
Now, there are many vacancies at the fifth rank and above,
and even if one's rank is appropriate,
some may not attain it even in old age.
How much more difficult is it then to become a minister?
In ancient times, prime ministers generally retired after no more than three to five years;
it was rare for anyone to serve for twenty or thirty years.
You, my ministers, simply do not recommend people,
which is not at all My intention."
The Emperor looked at Chóngbì, who compiled the imperial daily records, and said:
"This man is frail and weak;
if entrusted with affairs,
he may not be able to manage them.
However, because of his cautious, honest, and venerable character,
I keep him by My side,
hoping that other officials will emulate his conduct."
On the *xīnhài* day,
Yílā Zǐyuán, the Minister of Justice, and others were appointed as envoys to congratulate Sòng on New Year's Day.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
Húshā Tōngmǐn, the Vice Commissioner of the Left Patrol, was promoted
to Palace Censor and concurrently Director of the Right Three Departments for his decisive judgment.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
Yuán Wáng Jǐng, the Right Chancellor, was established as the Imperial Grandson.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
the Emperor said to his chief ministers:
"I hear that the Sòng army has always trained without interruption.
Now, Our army is solely engaged in idleness and leisure.
You, my ministers, must not think that because the world is now peaceful, there is no need for preparedness.
Should an alert suddenly arise,
and the army be unusable,
would that not lead to disaster?
Issue orders for timely training."
On the *bǐngyín* day,
the Emperor said to his attendant ministers:
"The actions of Crown Prince Chéngqián of Táng were often beyond measure.
Tàizōng indulged him and did not restrain him,
which eventually led to his deposition.
If he had been prohibited early,
it would not have come to this.
I cannot deeply understand the sacred scriptures,
but as for historical accounts,
I always gain something whenever I open them.
I often see that good people never forget loyalty and filial piety,
and they conduct themselves with integrity and honesty;
these all stem from their innate nature.
As for ordinary people, many are prone to wrongdoing.
If those who possess the realm have no means to punish them,
how can governance be achieved?
Kǒngzǐ (Confucius) governed for seven days and then executed Shǎozhèng Mǎo.
If even a sage was like that,
how much more so for others?"
On the *wùchén* day,
the Emperor said to his chief ministers:
"Although I am old,
I never tire of hearing good advice.
Kǒngzǐ said, 'See good as if you cannot attain it;
see evil as if you are exploring boiling water.'
What profound words!"
Zhāng Rǔbì, the Right Chancellor, replied:
"Knowing is not difficult;
acting is the real difficulty."
Hán Jǐngmào, the Vice Commander of the Palace Guards, was appointed as an envoy to Gāolí for the King's birthday.
Nímánggǔ Jiàn, the Director of the Bureau of Attendants, was promoted
to Imperial Grandson's Attendant-Minister for his pure uprightness and quick understanding.
On the *jǐsì* day,
there was a hunt in the nearby suburbs.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
the Emperor said to his chief ministers:
"Compared to the enlightened rulers of antiquity,
I certainly cannot reach their level.
However, as for not accepting slanderous words from close officials
and not receiving private requests from relatives of the imperial family,
I am not ashamed.
I have often reflected that
how can I be without faults?
The problem is having faults and not correcting them.
If one can correct faults,
one may then be without blame.
Reflecting on My faults,
I have been rather fond of commencing construction projects.
From now on, I shall no longer undertake them."
In the twelfth month, on the *jiǎshēn* day,
after the Emperor had retired from court,
he visited the Fragrant Pavilion.
Huáng Jiǔyuē, the Left Grand Master of Remonstrance, spoke against the delivery of litchis,
and the Emperor instructed him, saying:
"I was unaware of this.
I now order it to be stopped."
On the *bǐngxū* day,
the Emperor said to his chief ministers:
"The officials, in serving the Emperor,
only seek to gain a reputation for efficiency,
without considering the advantages or disadvantages.
I once desired fresh litchis,
and the Ministry of War immediately set up special relay stations along the roads.
It was only recently, when the remonstrating official Huáng Jiǔyuē spoke about it,
that I became aware.
Indeed, if a person lacks understanding,
they will inevitably stumble
when faced with an urgent matter.
Regardless of the size of matters within the palace,
I often personally examine them
because I do not have suitable people.
If I had suitable people,
why would I have other concerns?"
On the *dīnghài* day,
the Emperor said to his chief ministers:
"In recent years, I have made frugality My priority.
My daily meals consist of only four or five dishes,
and I am already tired of them.
Compared to when I first ascended the throne, the amount has decreased by seven or eight tenths."
The chief ministers said:
"The Son of Heaven has his own regulations;
he is not like other people."
The Emperor said:
"The Son of Heaven is also human.
What is the use of extravagant waste?"
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
the Emperor said to his chief ministers:
"I recently heard that the river overflowed,
and the people who suffered from it lost all their property.
Now, why are officials again sent there to conduct assessments?"
Zhāng Rǔlín, the Right Chancellor, replied:
"The current assessments
are not being conducted in the areas affected by the disaster."
The Emperor said:
"It must be in adjacent areas.
Since they live near the water,
how could there be no one disturbed or forced to move?
When their property is accounted for,
how could there be any surplus?
What is the point of further assessments?"
He further said:
"In normal times, when appointing people,
one should value straightforwardness.
However, for military positions,
stratagem should be employed,
making it difficult for others to predict,
thus allowing affairs to be accomplished.
Táng Tàizōng was skilled in military strategy from a young age.
Later, even when he held the imperial throne,
he still could not change this habit.
Sucking pus from wounds and cutting beards [of his soldiers] were all tactics."
In the twenty-seventh year, in the first month, on the *guǐmǎo* day, the first day of the month,
envoys from Sòng, Gāolí, and Xià came to offer congratulations.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
Zhào Fēng, the Magistrate of Xiāngchéng, was appointed as an Attendant Calligrapher of the Hànlín Academy.
When Fēng came to express his gratitude,
the Emperor asked his chief ministers:
"Was he recommended by Dǎng Huáiyīng?"
They replied:
"The Grand Master of Remonstrance, Huáng Jiǔyuē, also once recommended him."
The Emperor said:
"The Hànlín Academy now lacks talented individuals compared to the past.
Why is that?"
Zhāng Rǔlín, the Right Chancellor, replied:
"Talented individuals need to be nurtured.
If they are allowed to serve for a long time and practice,
suitable people will naturally emerge."
On the *gēngxū* day,
the Emperor went to the Chángchūn Palace for the Spring Hunt.
In the second month, on the *yǐhài* day,
returned to the capital.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
changed Mǐnzōng's temple name to Xīzōng.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
ordered Qǔyáng Xiàn to establish a money mint,
and bestowed upon it the name
"Lìtōng".
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
the Emperor addressed the Chief Councillors, saying:
"Since I ascended the throne,
although those who speak on affairs have been sometimes wild and reckless,
I have never punished them.
Yet you, my lords, have never been willing to speak your minds fully.
Why is this?
To fail to speak when one should speak
is to harbor suspicion of each other.
When ruler and ministers have no suspicions,
then it is called a harmonious assembly.
When matters involve advantage or disadvantage,
you should speak of them with utmost sincerity.
I do not wish to see those who remain silent and do not speak."
On the *dīnghài* day,
ordered the senior and junior officials of the various prefectures, departments, and counties along the river,
to concurrently manage river embankment affairs.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
instructed the Chief Councillors, saying:
"Officials of the Near Attendants Bureau must be selected from among those who are loyal, upright, and experienced.
Although I do not heed slanderous words,
if sycophants are kept at my side,
I fear I may gradually become accustomed to and follow them."
The Emperor addressed the Chief Councillors, saying:
"I hear that Měngkuò Tèmòyě, the commandant of Bǎochí, is very clean and upright.
How is his governance?"
The Left Grand Councillor, Wòtèlá, replied:
"His local people also praise him,
but I do not know for what specific deeds he is praised."
The Emperor said:
"For an official, it is enough to be clean and upright;
how can one expect a person of complete talent?
He may be promoted one rank
and made a magistrate."
He further said:
"Sometimes I am not well,
yet I have never failed to attend court.
Princes and all officials, however, if they have a slight illness,
immediately neglect their duties.
From now on, this should be prevented."
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
ordered that if a prisoner in custody fell ill,
their relatives would be permitted to visit them.
In the third month, on the *guǐmǎo* day, the first day of the month,
on the Wànchūn Jié,
the Sòng, Gāolí, and Xià sent envoys to offer congratulations.
On the *xīnhài* day,
the Imperial Grandson received his enfeoffment
and a general amnesty was proclaimed.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
the Department of State Affairs reported:
"The Mèngjiāshān Jīnkǒu sluice is more than 140 *chǐ* lower than the capital,
and there is a risk of damage from flash floods.
We request that it be closed."
This was granted.
The Emperor addressed the Grand Ministers, saying:
"Even in a village of ten households,
there must be loyal and trustworthy people.
Now, with the vastness of the realm
and the multitude of its people,
how can there be no such individuals?
In the Táng dynasty, Yán Zhēnqīng and Duàn Xiùshí were both ministers of integrity and righteousness,
yet they were never promoted or employed,
also because the grand ministers of their time obstinately obstructed and did not recommend them.
You, my lords, must not show favoritism to relatives or acquaintances,
but specifically recommend loyal and upright individuals,
and I shall employ them."
He further said:
"In the early days of our dynasty, customs were pure and frugal.
At home, people only wore plain cloth clothes,
and unless there was a grand gathering of guests,
they never rashly cooked sheep or pigs.
I often recall the frugal customs of that time
and do not wish for extravagant expenditure.
Thus, the number of officials in the palace and the food bestowed upon them
are all fixed."
In the fourth month, on the *bǐngxū* day,
Zōng Hào, Minister of Punishments, was appointed as Cānzhī Zhèngshì.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
the Emperor went to Jīnliánchuān.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
there was an earthquake in the capital.
In the fifth month, on the *rénzǐ* day,
an edict was issued to abolish the sea onions presented by Hélǎnlù and the daily seasonal fruits presented by the Grand Treasury.
It stated:
"How many onions and fruits can be used?
It merely exhausts the people.
Only the fruits from the Imperial Gardens
are to be presented once every three days."
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
as the taste of the imperial meals presented was not well-adjusted,
an order was issued to inquire about it.
The Director of the Imperial Kitchens said:
"I heard that my aged mother is severely ill,
and my private thoughts are in turmoil,
as if I have lost my soul.
Because of this, I made an error in tasting and inspecting.
My crime deserves ten thousand deaths."
The Emperor praised his filial piety,
and immediately ordered him to return home to attend to his mother's illness,
and to return only after she had recovered.
In the sixth month, on the *wùyín* day,
the military and civilian rents and taxes in Zhōngdū, Héběi, and other circuits that had suffered from river breaches and floods were remitted.
On the *gēngchén* day,
Venus was seen during the day.
In the seventh month, on the *bǐngwǔ* day,
Venus was seen during the day,
traversing the sky.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
there was an autumn hunt.
In the eighth month, on the *bǐngxū* day,
reached Shuāngshānzi.
In the ninth month, on the *jǐhài* day, the first day of the month,
returned to the capital.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
the Emperor addressed the Chief Councillors, saying:
"This year, in the prefectures and counties traversed by the spring floods,
many minor officials were diligent in their duties.
This is because I previously offered rewards and promotions,
so they all exerted themselves.
From this, it is evident that exclusive reliance on responsibility and punishment
is not as effective as using rewards for encouragement."
Tián Yàngāo, Governor of Hézhōng, and others were appointed as envoys to congratulate the Sòng on their birthday,
and Xié Mǎo Ātǔ, Director of the Weapons Bureau, was appointed as envoy to the Xià state for their birthday.
In the tenth month, on the *yǐhài* day,
the former ruler of Sòng, Gòu, passed away.
On the *gēngchén* day,
a joint sacrifice was offered at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
On the *gēngyín* day,
the Emperor addressed the Chief Councillors, saying:
"I have observed in the History of Táng
that only Wèi Zhēng was skilled in remonstrance,
and what he said were all major affairs of the state,
which perfectly embodied the role of a remonstrating minister.
Recently, the Censors and Remonstrance Officials only point out one or two trivial matters,
merely to fulfill their duty perfunctorily,
and have never touched upon matters of great benefit or harm to the state.
Do they know but not speak,
or do they perhaps not know at all?"
The Chief Councillors had no reply.
In the eleventh month, on the *gēngxū* day,
Chóng Ān, Deputy Commander-in-Chief of the Left, was appointed as envoy to congratulate the Sòng on the New Year.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
an edict stated:
"For farmers who suffered disaster due to the overflowing river waters,
their service and taxes are remitted for one year.
The labor for damming the river in the four prefectures of Wèi, Huái, Mèng, and Zhèng
is also remitted for this year's service and taxes."
On the *gēngshēn* day,
Chóng Yǐn, Grand Councillor, retired.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
the Emperor addressed the Chief Councillors, saying:
"You, my lords, are old.
Is there truly no one who can succeed you,
must I wait until I know them before they are promoted?"
He looked at the Right Grand Councillor, Zhāng Rǔlín, and said:
"As for the Right Grand Councillor, he was also recommended by Chancellor Shí."
Grand Councillor Xiāng and Rǔlín replied:
"If we, your servants, knew of such individuals,
how would we dare not to speak?
But there is simply no one."
The Emperor said:
"During the Spring and Autumn period, various states were fragmented,
with small territories,
yet all claimed to have worthy individuals.
You, my lords, simply do not recommend them.
Now I strive myself,
hoping to achieve good governance,
but in the future, my descendants,
who will govern with them?"
All the Chief Councillors showed signs of shame.
In the twelfth month, on the *gēngwǔ* day,
Zhào Kě, a Hanlin Academician in Waiting, was appointed as the birthday envoy to Gāolí.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
there was a hunt in the near suburbs.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
the Sòng sent an envoy to announce mourning.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
the Emperor issued an edict to his chief ministers, saying:
"People all consider performing Daoist rituals, revering Buddhism, holding fasts, and reading scriptures as blessings.
But if I ensure that the common people have no grievances
and that the world is peaceful and joyful,
is that not superior to those things?
You, holding the positions of輔相 (fǔxiàng),
if you can truly assist and benefit the state,
and enable the common people to receive advantages,
not only will you personally enjoy the rewards,
but it will also extend to your descendants."
The Left Censor, Wòtèlà, said:
"How would Your Majesty's humble servants dare not to exert their utmost effort?
It is merely that our talent is insufficient,
and we are unable to fulfill our duties as required."
The Emperor said:
"How can a person be perfect in every matter?
Just add encouragement, and it will be fine."
On the *wùzǐ* day,
it was forbidden for Nǚzhēn people to change to Han surnames
or to adopt the clothing and customs of the southerners.
Violators would be punished.
In the twenty-eighth year, on the *dīngyǒu* day, the first day of the first month,
envoys from Sòng, Gāolí, and Xià came to offer congratulations.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
the Xuanhui envoy Púchá Kèzhōng was dispatched as the Sòng mourning envoy.
On the *jiǎchén* day, he went to Chūnshuǐ.
In the second month, on the *yǐhài* day,
he returned to the capital.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
the Sòng sent an envoy to present items left by the former Emperor.
On the *guǐsì* day,
the Sòng envoy took leave after his audience.
Among the gifts presented, five jade artifacts,
twenty glass artifacts,
and bows, swords, and other items were returned to the Sòng envoy,
with the words:
"These are all cherished possessions of your former ruler,
which should be treasured
so as not to forget remembrance and longing.
To accept them now
would be an act of unrighteousness I cannot bear.
Go and inform your ruler,
so that he may know my intention."
In the third month, on the *dīngyǒu* day, the first day of the month,
it was Wànchūnjié.
Envoys from Sòng, Gāolí, and Xià came to offer congratulations.
The Emperor received audience from his assembled officials at Qìnghé Diàn,
and then held a banquet at Shénlóng Diàn.
Princes and princesses in turn offered wine to wish long life.
The Emperor was greatly joyful,
and composed a tune himself in the national language.
It spoke of having ruled for a long time,
being advanced in years,
and contemplating with deep thought the重 (zhòng) of the foundation of the state,
and the trust for ten thousand generations.
It was to admonish the Imperial Grandson
to cultivate his character and virtue,
and be good at preserving and upholding,
and also to instruct the Grand Commandant and Left Chancellor Kèníng to wholeheartedly assist and guide him.
Thereupon,
the Emperor sang it himself,
and the Imperial Grandson and Kèníng harmonized with him.
They concluded in extreme joy.
On the *wùshēn* day,
it was commanded that officials of the sixth rank and above in the court, and those of the fifth rank and above in outer circuits,
〔一０〕who were already in office as *jìnshì* and had the talent to serve in the Hanlin Academy,
should be tested on three essays, such as imperial edicts and pronouncements.
Those with superior literary style and reasoning would be appointed to positions in the Academy of Scholars.
As for those seeking office through the ministries,
the old, sick, or confused
were ordered to retire,
receiving only half their salary,
and would no longer be promoted.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
he visited Shòu'ān Gōng.
In the fourth month, on the *guǐyǒu* day,
it was ordered to increase the salaries of minor officials in outer appointments and those serving in busy and difficult departments.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
Bóshùlǔ Ālǔhǎn, Commander of the Shǎnxī Circuit Army, was made Cānzhī Zhèngshì.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
it was ordered to establish a Nǚzhēn Grand University.
In the fifth month, on the *bǐngwǔ* day,
it was decreed that all professors must be filled by seasoned scholars of high talent,
and their salaries would be equal to those of Assistant Prefects and Registrars.
On the *wùshēn* day,
a Sòng envoy came to express gratitude for the mourning condolences.
In the seventh month, on the *xīnhài* day,
Zhānggē Wòtèlà, Left Chancellor of the Department of State Affairs, was dismissed.
In the eighth month, on the *jiǎzǐ* day, the first day of the month,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
he returned to the capital.
On the *gēngchén* day,
the Emperor said to his chief ministers:
"Recently I heard that the Wūdǐgǎi harbor intentions of disobedience.
If we send an envoy to question them,
they might resist defiantly and be insolent,
then border affairs could escalate beyond control.
I have often thought that
attracting distant peoples
brings little benefit to the state.
If they come, let them;
if they don't come, do not force them.
This is the long-term strategy of previous generations for loose control."
Cānzhī Zhèngshì Bóshùlǔ Ālǔhǎn was dismissed.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
Wányán Pólúhuǒ, Commander of the Shāndōng Circuit Army, was made Cānzhī Zhèngshì.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
the Emperor said to his chief ministers:
"The way to employ people
is to use them when they are in their prime, with strong minds and vigorous energy.
If one is constrained by qualifications,
one often reaches old age,
which is extremely thoughtless.
If Ālǔhǎn had been employed earlier,
the court would certainly have received his assistance;
it is a pity that he is already old and infirm.
Whenever there is usable talent,
you should think about it early."
In the ninth month, on the *jiǎwǔ* day, the first day of the month,
Chóng Kuí, the Supervisor of the Imperial Falconry, was made the birthday envoy to Xià Guó.
〔一一〕On the *bǐngshēn* day,
Wáng Kèwēn, Military Commissioner of Ānwǔ Commandery, and others were appointed as envoys to congratulate the Sòng on their birthday.
〔一二〕On the *jǐhài* day,
there was an autumn hunt.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
he returned to the capital.
In the tenth month, on the *yǐchǒu* day,
the Liúquán Wù (Floating Spring Bureaus) were established in the capital, prefectures, and military commissioner's prefectures,
a total of twenty-eight locations.
Kāng Chán (Bran Chan) and Piáo Chán (Gourd Chan) were prohibited;
households that continued these practices would be punished.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
the Department of State Affairs presented a memorial proposing appointments and dismissals but was constrained by qualifications.
The Emperor said:
"Seniority and evaluations are for ordinary people.
If one's talent and conduct surpass others,
how can one be constrained by ordinary rules?
All state affairs require capable people,
and you are unable to assign duties according to talent,
which is why many matters are not well managed.
I may not know the art of employing people,
but you only adhere to seniority and rules,
and do not consider promoting talented individuals.
Is it because talented individuals, once employed,
will seize your emoluments and positions?
If not,
then it shows a lack of discerning insight into people."
All the ministers said:
"How would your humble servants dare to conceal worthy individuals?
It is merely that our talent and discernment are insufficient."
The Emperor looked at Right Chancellor Zhāng Rǔlín and said:
"Why were there so many ministers of honest counsel in previous generations,
and so few today?"
Rǔlín replied:
"When the world is in chaos, honest counsel is advanced;
when there is peace, honest counsel has no place to be applied."
The Emperor said:
"What age is without matters that need to be spoken of?
It is just that people in ancient times spoke whatever they knew,
while people today are unwilling to speak."
Rǔlín could not respond.
In the eleventh month, on the *wùxū* day,
due to the reburial of Xīlíng (熙陵),
an imperial edict was issued to the inner and outer courts.
The Emperor said to his attendant ministers:
"For anyone cultivating their character, joy and anger should not be excessive.
Extreme anger exhausts the mind,
and extreme joy dissipates the *qì*.
Achieving moderation is very difficult,
and thus one should regulate one's joy and anger
to ensure peace of mind.
This year, no one in the palace has been reprimanded or punished even once."
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
Tàibái (太白) (Venus) was seen in daylight.
An edict commanded that for those in Nánjīng (南京), Dàmíng Fǔ (大名府), and other places who had fled due to floods and could not resume their occupations,
the government should provide them with travel and relief money,
and also distribute plowing oxen according to the acreage of their land.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
Tían Yàn'gāo (田彥臯), the governor of Hézhōng (河中), and others were appointed as envoys to offer congratulations to Sòng (宋) on the New Year's Day.
On the *wùshēn* day,
the Emperor said to his chancellors:
"The established regulations are constrained by old laws,
and occasionally contain difficult-to-understand phrases.
Laws have been modified and improved through successive generations.
If there are instances where the original intention is not met due to inadequate foresight,
what is wrong with making revisions and corrections
to make them easily understandable to the public?
They should be revised,
making sure they are clear."
An official reported on the proposed renovation of the Yùróng Diàn (御容殿) in Shàngjīng (上京).
The Emperor said to his chancellors:
"If palace buildings
are merely built for lavish decoration,
they will certainly not be sturdy.
The Rénzhèng Diàn (仁政殿), built during the Liáo (遼) dynasty,
has no lavish decoration at all.
I see other places being repaired annually,
but only this hall remains as it was.
From this, one can see that what is superficial and without substance
cannot last long.
Currently, civil engineering work
is particularly shoddy.
At the lower level, officials and artisans conspire to commit fraud,
embezzling materials.
At the upper level, officials of the Hùgōng Bù (戶工部) disburse funds and allocate materials,
only striving to get things done carelessly.
There are even cases where work is barely finished
before it starts to lean or leak.
Such deceitful and careless practices,
which exhaust the people and waste resources,
are unparalleled.
From now on, investigate such cases
and punish them severely."
On the *gēngxū* day,
the Emperor said to his chancellors:
"I recently read the *Hànshū* (漢書)
and saw the deeds of Guāngwǔ (光武),
which were difficult for ordinary people to accomplish.
Gēngshǐ (更始) had already killed his elder brother Bóshēng (伯升).
In a time of chaos and separation,
he did not think of revenge,
but served Gēngshǐ as he did in normal times,
and people did not see any mournful expression.
Is this not something difficult for people to accomplish?
This indicates that his magnanimity was such that he was destined for great achievements.
How could other ordinary rulers compare?"
The Right Chancellor Zhāng Rǔlín (張汝霖) said:
"Húyáng Gōngzhǔ's (湖陽公主) slave killed a person
and hid in the princess's carriage.
Luòyáng Lìng (洛陽令) Dǒng Xuān (董宣) dragged the slave out from the carriage
and killed him.
The princess reported this to the Emperor,
and Guāngwǔ wanted to kill Xuān.
But upon hearing Xuān's words,
his anger dissipated.
He ordered Xuān to apologize to the princess,
but Xuān did not obey the edict.
The princess provoked Guāngwǔ with her words,
but Guāngwǔ merely laughed,
and instead bestowed Xuān with 300,000 *qián*."
The Emperor said:
"Guāngwǔ's anger dissipating upon hearing honest words can be called a wise ruler.
However, ordering Xuān to apologize to the princess was wrong.
Gāozǔ (高祖) was a heroic and magnanimous figure,
who managed brave and outstanding individuals.
Rising from commoner status,
he established an imperial legacy in a few years,
which Guāngwǔ could not match.
However, upon ascending the throne,
he still retained some of the coarse and unrestrained character of a commoner,
which Guāngwǔ would not have done."
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
the Emperor visited Tàiwèi (太尉) Kèníng's (克寧) residence.
In the twelfth month, on the *bǐngyín* day,
Yílà Yàngǒng (移剌彥拱), the Grand Judge, was appointed as envoy to Gāolì (高麗) for the King's birthday.
On the *yǐhài* day,
the Emperor fell ill.
On the *gēngchén* day,
a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the empire.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
an edict appointed the Imperial Grandson Jǐng (璟) as regent,
residing in the east wing of the Qìnghé Diàn (慶和殿).
On the *bǐngxū* day,
Tàiwèi (太尉) and Zuǒchéngxiàng (左丞相) Túshàn Kèníng (徒單克寧) was made Tàiwèi (太尉) concurrently Shàngshū Lìng (尚書令).
Píngzhāng Zhèngshì (平章政事) Xiāng (襄) was made Shàngshū Yòuchéngxiàng (尚書右丞相).
Yòuchéng (右丞) Zhāng Rǔlín (張汝霖) was made Píngzhāng Zhèngshì (平章政事).
Cānzhī Zhèngshì (參知政事) Wányán Pólúhuǒ (完顏婆盧火) was dismissed,
and Hùbù Shàngshū (戶部尚書) Liú Wěi (劉暐) was made Cānzhī Zhèngshì (參知政事).
On the *wùzǐ* day,
an edict ordered Shàngshū Lìng (尚書令) Túshàn Kèníng (徒單克寧), Yòuchéngxiàng (右丞相) Xiāng (襄), and Píngzhāng Zhèngshì (平章政事) Zhāng Rǔlín (張汝霖) to spend the night in the inner palace.
On the first day of the first month of the 29th year, *rénchén*,
the Emperor's illness worsened dramatically,
and he could not hold court.
An edict was issued to send back the envoys from Sòng (宋), Gāolì (高麗), and Xià (夏) who had come to celebrate New Year's Day.
On the *guǐsì* day,
the Emperor passed away in the Fú'ān Diàn (福安殿),
aged sixty-seven.
The Imperial Grandson immediately ascended the throne.
On the *jǐhài* day,
the coffin was interred in the Dà'ān Diàn (大安殿).
On the first day of the third month, *xīnmǎo*,
〔一三〕the Emperor was posthumously honored with the full imperial title of Guāngtiān Xīngyùn Wéndé Wǔgōng Shèngmíng Rénxiào Huángdì (光天興運文德武功聖明仁孝皇帝),
and his temple name was Shìzōng (世宗).
In the fourth month, on the *yǐyǒu* day,
he was buried in Xīnglíng (興陵).
The encomium says: Although Shìzōng's (世宗) ascension
was due to persuasion to ascend the throne,
it was also where Heaven's mandate and the people's will converged.
Even ancient sagely and virtuous rulers
could not decline it.
Indeed, since Tàizǔ (太祖),
there had been continuous warfare within the empire,
with few years of peace.
Compounded by Hǎilíng's (海陵) misrule,
taxes and labor services were rampant,
bandits filled the fields,
and armies rose in rebellion.
The myriad common people were anxious,
the country was in turmoil.
The elderly had no able-bodied sons to support them,
the young had no parents to care for them.
They were in dire distress and sorrow,
awaiting their demise morning and night.
Shìzōng (世宗) had long administered outer prefectures,
understood the causes of disaster and chaos,
and knew the merits and demerits of official governance.
Five years after his enthronement,
peace was established between the north and south,
and the people were given respite.
Thereupon, he personally practiced frugality,
promoted filial piety and fraternity,
was reliable in rewards and punishments,
emphasized agriculture and sericulture,
carefully selected local officials,
and strictly enforced the responsibilities of upright inspectors.
He rejected Rèn Déjìng's (任得敬) request to divide the country,
and refused Zhào Wèichǒng's (趙位寵) offerings of prefectures and counties.
He diligently worked for good governance,
continuing day and night.
He can be said to have understood the way of a ruler.
During this time,
ministers fulfilled their duties,
superiors and subordinates lived in harmony,
households were provided for, people were content,
and granaries had surplus.
The Ministry of Justice sentenced seventeen
or twenty people to death annually,
and he was hailed as
"Little Yáo Shùn (堯舜)."
These were the manifest results.
However, despite his urgent need for worthy talents
and earnest desire for honest counsel,
which he ceaselessly expressed in his instructions,
his ministers were complacent and content with their salaries,
unable to align with his virtues
to achieve great order.
What a pity!
Proofreading Notes
Basic Annals, Chapter 9, Shìzōng (世宗) 1
Zhāngzōng Xiàntiānguāngyùn Rénwén Yìwǔ Shénshèng Yīngxiào Huángdì,
personal name Jǐng,
with the informal name Mádágé,
was the legitimate son of Xiǎnzōng.
His mother was Xiàoyì Huánghòu, of the Túdān clan.
In the eighth year of Dàdìng (1168),
Shìzōng visited Jīnliánchuān.
In the autumn, in the seventh month, on the day of Bǐngxū,
when he was at Bīngjǐng,
the emperor was born.
The next day,
Shìzōng visited the Eastern Palace,
where he feasted and rejoiced greatly.
He said to Xiǎnzōng:
"The accumulated blessings of our ancestors have brought about this day;
it is a fortune for the state."
He then said to Sītú Lǐ Shí and Shūmìshǐ Gēshíliè Zhìníng and others:
"Though I have many sons,
the empress only has the crown prince.
I am fortunate to see a legitimate grandson born at Mádágéshān.
I have always liked this place for its spaciousness and clear air,
so let him be named after the mountain."
All the officials exclaimed "Long live!"
In the eighteenth year (1178),
he was enfeoffed as Jīnyuán Jùnwáng.
He began to learn the native language and small characters of the present dynasty,
as well as Chinese characters and classics,
with the Jìnshì Wányán Kuāng, Sījīng Xú Xiàoměi, and others serving as his tutors.
In the twenty-fourth year (1184),
when Shìzōng was on an eastern tour,
and Xiǎnzōng was guarding the country,
the emperor sent a memorial to Shàngjīng to inquire about the emperor's health,
and also requested the imperial carriage to return to the capital.
Shìzōng praised his intentions
and sent an imperial edict in reply.
In the third month of the twenty-fifth year (1185),
on the Wànchūnjié festival,
he again sent a memorial to offer congratulations.
In the sixth month,
Xiǎnzōng passed away.
Shìzōng dispatched Téngwángfǔ Zhǎngshǐ ● and Yùyuàn Tōngjìn ● to provide care and supervision.
In the twelfth month,
he was advanced to be Yuánwáng
and appointed to manage the affairs of Dàxīngfǔ.
He entered and offered thanks in the national language.
Shìzōng was pleased
and even moved by this.
He said to his chief ministers:
"I have often ordered my sons to learn our dynasty's language;
only Yuánwáng is very proficient in it.
I commend him greatly."
The imperial decree stated:
"I certainly know you are young,
and during your mourning period, it is not yet suitable to entrust you with an office.
However, you must also learn about governmental affairs.
For the task in the imperial capital,
I will test your talent for a while.
Exert yourself."
In the fourth month of the twenty-sixth year (1186),
an edict granted him the name Jǐng.
In the fifth month,
he was appointed Shàngshū Yòuchéngxiàng.
Shìzōng said to him:
"In the palace, there is a map of the world.
By observing it, you can fully understand the distances, difficult passes, and strategic points of the empire."
He also said to his chief ministers:
"The reason I have placed Yuánwáng in a position close to the auxiliary capital
is to allow him to personally witness court deliberations
and become familiar with the principles of governance."
In the eleventh month,
an edict established him as Huáng Tàisūn.
He offered thanks at Qìnghédiàn.
Shìzōng instructed him, saying:
"You are still young,
and you are the only legitimate grandson of Míngdé Huánghòu.
When tested with affairs,
you show great potential for learning.
I hereby officially establish you as Huáng Tàisūn.
The establishment rests with me,
but the preservation rests with you.
You should cultivate proper conduct and virtue;
do not associate with corrupt and flattering individuals.
Serve me with utmost loyalty and filial piety,
and do not fail the expectations of the populace,
for only then will you be commended."
In the third month of the twenty-seventh year (1187),
Shìzōng presided at Dà'āndiàn
and presented the imperial grand-son with the official seal,
granting amnesty throughout the empire.
On the day of Dīngsì,
he paid respects at the Tàimiào and the imperial mausoleums.
He then began to receive congratulatory memorials from all officials.
In the twelfth month of the twenty-eighth year (1188), on the day of Yǐhài,
Shìzōng became unwell.
An edict ordered him to act as regent
and to hear appointments for officials of the fifth rank and below.
On the day of Dīnghài,
he received
the "Seal of Regency."
In the spring, the first month of the twenty-ninth year (1189), on the day of Guǐsì,
Shìzōng passed away.
He immediately ascended the imperial throne before the coffin.
On the day of Bǐngshēn,
an edict was issued throughout the empire.
Internal and external officials were granted a double degree of general grace,
while those of the third rank and above received a single degree.
This year's land taxes were remitted,
along with all outstanding debts to the government.
For widows, the lonely, and orphans, one roll of silk and two shí of rice were granted.
On the day of Jǐhài,
the coffin of the late emperor was moved to Dà'āndiàn.
On the day of Guǐmǎo,
by order of the empress dowager, an imperial decree was issued.
On the day of Jiǎchén,
Dàlǐ Qīng Wáng Yuándé and others were sent to report the mourning to Sòng, Gāolí, and Xià.
On the day of Yǐmǎo,
a white rainbow pierced the sun and spanned the sky.
On the day of Dīngsì,
Cānzhīzhèngshì Zōng Hào was dismissed.
The Shandong Tǒngjūn Yì, for privately passing through the capital without attending the mourning,
was flogged fifty times
and demoted to Zhānghuàjūn Jiédùshǐ.
On the day of Wǔwǔ,
the empress dowager's palace was named Rénshòu,
and officials such as Wèiwèi were established.
On the first day of the second month, Xīnyǒu,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the day of Guǐhài,
he began to attend to government affairs.
The deceased emperor, his father, was posthumously honored as emperor,
and his mother was honored as empress dowager.
On the day of Jiǎzǐ,
the Xuéshìyuàn was ordered to present reports on matters that benefited the people of Hàn and Táng,
as well as urgent current affairs.
On the day of Yǐchǒu,
a white rainbow spanned the sky.
An imperial edict stated that the purpose of the Dēngwéngǔyuàn was to address injustices;
previously its gate was often locked,
so it was ordered to be opened.
On the day of Wùchén,
the Rénshòugōng was renamed Lóngqìng.
An edict ordered that all slaves and bondservants in the palace registers who previously belonged to Ruìzōng, the late emperor, or the imperial father
were all to be freed.
On the day of Jǐsì,
an imperial edict was given to the Yùshǐtái:
from now on, Cècálìng are to be appointed by this office,
and if they are not competent in their term, they can also be dismissed upon memorial.
On the day of Dīngchǒu,
the salaries of all officials were increased and revised.
On the day of Yǐyǒu,
an edict ordered the relevant officials to examine historical precedents
and allowed the citation of Sòng dynasty affairs.
This month,
the Sòng emperor abdicated internally,
and his son Dūn succeeded him.
In the third month, on the day of Rénchén,
he held court at Lóngqìnggōng.
This month, there were five such courts.
On the day of Jǐyǒu,
an edict declared his birthday to be the Tiānshòujié.
On the day of Guǐchǒu,
the Xià state sent envoys to offer condolences.
In summer, the fourth month, on the day of Jǐsì,
the Xià state sent envoys to offer sacrifices.
On the day of Xīnwèi,
Sòng sent envoys to offer condolences and sacrifices.
On the day of Yǐyǒu,
Shìzōng Guāngtiānxīngyùn Wéndé Wǔgōng Shèngmíng Rénxiào Huángdì was buried at Xīnglíng.
On the day of Wùzǐ,
he held court at Lóngqìnggōng.
In the fifth month, on the first day, Gēngyín,
Venus was visible in daylight.
On the day of Rén'yín,
the Sòng emperor sent envoys to report his succession.
The Xià state sent envoys to congratulate him on his ascension.
On the day of Bǐngwǔ,
as the ceremony of enshrinement in the ancestral temple was completed,
a general amnesty was granted.
On the day of Dīngwèi,
white hair grew on the ground.
On the day of Gēngxū,
an edict abolished the practice of "sending Xuān money."
Henceforth, all guards who complete their term shall be granted two thousand strings of official money.
On the day of Rénzǐ,
an imperial edict ordered the recruitment of the descendants of meritorious officials,
who were to be assigned to various offices according to their talents.
On the day of Wùwǔ,
he held court at Lóngqìnggōng.
Wēndíhǎn Sùkě, the Northeast Route Zhāotǎoshǐ, and others were appointed as envoys to congratulate the Sòng emperor on his ascension.
The river overflowed at Cáozhōu.
On the *gēngshēn* day of the intercalary month, the first day of the month,
his elder brother Xún [珣] was enfeoffed as Fēng Wáng [豐王];
Cóng [琮] as Yùn Wáng [鄆王];
Huí [瓌] as Yíng Wáng [瀛王];
Cóngyí [從彝] as Yí Wáng [沂王].
His younger brother Cóngxiàn [從憲] was enfeoffed as Shòu Wáng [壽王];
Jiè [玠] as Wēn Wáng [溫王].
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
an edict was issued that all starving people who had sold themselves should be redeemed and set free as commoners.
Furthermore, any males and females born to slaves
were also allowed to become commoners.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
he inspected the crops in the near suburbs.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
Tángguō Gòng [唐括貢], Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, was made Censor-in-Chief.
On the *rénshēn* day,
his wet nurse, Lady Sūn [孫氏], was enfeoffed as Xiāo Guó Fūrén [蕭國夫人],
and Lady Yáo [姚氏] as Xīn Guó Fūrén [莘國夫人].
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
Zhào Wáng Yǒngzhōng [趙王永中] was promoted to Hàn Wáng [漢王];
Cáo Wáng Yǒnggōng [曹王永功] to Jì Wáng [冀王];
Bīn Wáng Yǒngchéng [豳王永成] to Wú Wáng [吳王];
Yú Wáng Yǒngshēng [虞王永升] to Suí Wáng [隨王];
Xú Wáng Yǒngdǎo [徐王永蹈] to Wèi Wáng [衞王];
Téng Wáng Yǒngjì [滕王永濟] to Lù Wáng [潞王];
Xuē Wáng Yǒngdé [薛王永德] to Shěn Wáng [瀋王].
On the *gēngchén* day,
Sòng [宋] dispatched an envoy to congratulate him on his ascension to the throne.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
he held court at Lóngqìng Gōng [隆慶宮].
An imperial edict instructed the Hanlin Academy [學士院] that
from now on, all official pronouncements (gàocí) should employ the "four-six" parallelism style.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
an edict ordered that all individuals who had obtained official status and were serving
and were to be appointed to posts involving the people,
should be instructed by their superiors to study.
For those in the Imperial Guard, Bureau of Talismans, Bureau of Ceremonial, and Bureau of Services,
who attended closely,
persons of virtue and learning should be selected to teach them.
On the *jǐchǒu* day of the sixth month, the first day of the month,
officials concerned reported:
"Those who take the law examinations only know how to read laws
but do not understand the origin of education and transformation.
They must be made to thoroughly understand the *Lúnyǔ* [論語] and *Mèngzǐ* [孟子]
to cultivate their character and capacity.
During the prefectural and metropolitan examinations,
the examining officials for classical exegesis should set separate questions
and determine their passing or failing status together with the main subject. This would be appropriate."
This was adopted.
An edict instructed the relevant officials
that each imperial prince arriving at his post should be given 200,000 cash.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
Wányán Wūzhě [完顏烏者], Compiler of the Diaries of Activity and Repose, and Sūn Duó [孫鐸], Associate Administrator of the Bureau of Appeals, both submitted memorials advising against hunting excursions.
The emperor accepted their advice.
Mǎ Shēng [馬升], Remonstrance Official, submitted "Agnosticism on Frugality" (*Jiǎndé Zhēn* [儉德箴]).
On the *yǐwèi* day,
the Bureau of Judicial Review (Tíxíng Sī [提刑司]) was first established,
divided into nine circuits,
also concurrently managing agricultural promotion and investigation.
All military colonies and garrisons were subordinate to it.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
he visited Qìngshòu Sì [慶壽寺].
The Lúgōu Shíqiáo [瀘溝石橋] was constructed.
On the *jǐhài* day,
he held court at Lóngqìng Gōng [隆慶宮].
On the *jiǎchén* day,
the practice of sending gifts and money for amnesty ceremonies was abolished.
He held court at Lóngqìng Gōng [隆慶宮].
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
Gāolí Guówáng Hào [高麗國王晧] sent an envoy to offer condolences and attend the funeral.
An imperial order instructed the relevant officials to notify Sòng [宋], Gāolí [高麗], and Xià [夏]
that the Tiānshòu Jié [天壽節] (Emperor's Birthday) should be celebrated on the first day of the ninth month.
On the *dīngsì* day,
it was ordered that after the appointment of judicial review officials, they should receive instructions in the Imperial Ante-chamber.
Every tenth month, one of the deputy officials should be ordered to enter and discuss affairs.
If there was only one deputy, then the registrar should be ordered to enter.
The registrar, whose duties were heavy and complex, could be promoted to a court official position.
In the seventh month of autumn, on the *xīnyǒu* day,
the land tax for the people was reduced by one-tenth;
for the eastern and northern parts of Hédōng [河東], by two-tenths;
for low-grade land, by three-tenths.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
he held court at Lóngqìng Gōng [隆慶宮].
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
an imperial order stated that close attendant officials appointed to external posts of the third or fourth rank
should be granted one golden belt
and differing amounts of valuable silks.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
Túdān Kèníng [徒單克寧], Grand Commandant and Chancellor of the Secretariat, and Prince of Dōngpíng [東平郡王], was made Grand Tutor [太傅],
and his title was changed to Prince of Jīnyuán [金源郡王].
On the *xīnwèi* day,
Gāolí [高麗] sent an envoy to congratulate him on his ascension to the throne.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
he accompanied the Empress Dowager to Shòu'ān Gōng [壽安宮].
On the *xīnsì* day,
an edict ordered the establishment of schools to support scholars in the capital, prefectures, military governorships, and defense prefectures.
The *Jīngtóng Kē* [經童科] (Classic-Reading Boy Examination) was first established.
Tángguō Gòng [唐括貢], Censor-in-Chief, was dismissed.
Yílà Lǚ [移剌履], Minister of Rites, was made Assistant Administrator of Political Affairs.
Wányán Shǒuzhēn [完顏守貞], Minister of Justice, and others were appointed as envoys to congratulate Sòng [宋] on the emperor's birthday.
On the *wùzǐ* day of the eighth month, the first day of the month,
he accompanied the Empress Dowager to Shòu'ān Gōng [壽安宮].
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
an imperial order instructed the relevant officials
that in places where schools were established in the capital, prefectures, states, and garrisons,
the chief and deputy officials, or their staff, should each have a *jìnshì* official supervise the affairs,
and their titles should be formally included.
On the *rénchén* day,
the criteria for testing and appointing officials' descendants as clerks were first established,
as were the thirty-two articles managed by the Bureau of Judicial Review.
Guō Ānmín [郭安民], Left Remonstrance Official, submitted a memorial discussing three matters: namely, advocating frugality,
eliminating desires,
and expanding learning.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
he went to Dàfáng Shān [大房山].
On the *wùxū* day,
he visited and offered sacrifices at the imperial mausoleums.
On the *jǐhài* day,
he returned to the capital.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
he held court at Lóngqìng Gōng [隆慶宮].
In this month, he held court three times in total.
On the *rénchén* day,
an edict ordered the Bureau of Judicial Review to appoint one *Nǚzhí* [女直], one *Qìdān* [契丹], and one *Hàn'ér* [漢兒] legal expert each.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
Liú Wěi [劉瑋], Assistant Administrator of Political Affairs, was dismissed.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
Sòng [宋], Gāolí [高麗], and Xià [夏] sent envoys to congratulate him on the Tiānshòu Jié [天壽節].
On the *wùwǔ* day of the ninth month, the first day of the month,
it was the Tiānshòu Jié [天壽節],
but due to Shìzōng's [世宗] mourning period,
no court was held.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
an edict ordered an increase in the number of mausoleum guards to twenty families [丁],
and granted them ten *qǐng* of land.
On the *rénxū* day,
an edict abolished the reward for reporting seditious speech.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
an edict stipulated that if ten or more bandits gathered,
or five or more rode horses,
the relevant officials for bandit suppression should apprehend them,
and report it to the provincial and departmental authorities.
If thirty or more gathered, it should be reported to the throne.
Violators would be punished with one hundred strokes of the rod.
On this day,
he held court at Lóngqìng Gōng [隆慶宮].
In this month, he held court four times in total.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
an edict prohibited powerful clans and prominent families from associating with local officials.
Violators would be punished.
On the *wùchén* day,
Bǎ Sīzhōng [把思忠], Commander of the Lóngqìng Gōng [隆慶宮] Guards, was appointed as envoy for the Xià [夏] Emperor's birthday.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
Chóngdé [崇德], Commissioner of the Imperial Palanquin Bureau, was appointed as envoy for the extraordinary gifts to Gāolí [高麗].
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
he hunted in the near suburbs.
On the *wùyín* day,
Jiāo Xù [焦旭], Supervising Censor, impeached Grand Tutor Kèníng [克寧] and Right Chancellor Xiāng [襄] for improperly requesting the imperial hunting excursion.
The Emperor said:
"This is a minor matter,
there is no need to prosecute it."
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
he went to Dàfáng Shān [大房山].
On the *dīnghài* day of the tenth month of winter, the first day of the month,
he visited and offered sacrifices at the imperial mausoleums.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
he returned to the capital.
On the *gēngyín* day,
he held court at Lóngqìng Gōng [隆慶宮].
In this month, he held court four times in total.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
the Emperor turned to the chief ministers and said,
"The Hanlin Academy [翰林] is short of personnel."
Rǔlín [汝霖], Administrator of Political Affairs, replied,
"Hǎo Yǔ [郝俁], Administrator of Fèngxiáng [鳳翔], would be suitable."
Rǔlín [汝霖] advised against hunting.
The emperor replied in an edict:
"If you can be like this in every matter,
what else would I have to worry about?
However, times change and circumstances differ,
so moderation is appropriate."
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
he went on a winter hunt.
On the *jǐhài* day,
he stopped at Luó Shān [羅山].
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
he stopped at Yùtián [玉田].
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
Qìn Zhōu [沁州] and Dān Zhōu [丹州] presented auspicious grain.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
he stopped at Bǎochí [寶坻].
On the *gēngxū* day,
Shímò Āgǔ [石抹阿古], an attendant, mistakenly brought a knife into the Forbidden Gates.
His crime warranted death,
but an edict commuted it to eighty strokes of the rod.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
he arrived back from Bǎochí [寶坻].
In the eleventh month, on the day Jǐwèi,
the Emperor held court at Lóngqìnggōng.
On the day Xīnyǒu,
Péimǎn Yúqìng and others, who were Administrators of the Right Xuānhuīyùan, were appointed as envoys to offer New Year's congratulations to Sòng.
On the day Guǐhài,
the Emperor addressed his chief ministers, saying:
"Currently, in the selection of officials,
there is too much adherence to seniority and qualifications.
The system of promotion based on seniority
originated in the Táng dynasty.
How can we obtain talented people if we follow this?"
Píngzhāng Zhèngshì Rǔlín replied:
"Not being restricted by qualifications
is the way to await extraordinary talents."
The Emperor said:
"When Cuī Yòufǔ was Chancellor,
in less than a year he recommended eight hundred people.
Were they all extraordinary talents?"
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
an edict was issued to the Shàngshūshěng, stating:
"The Grand Tutor is advanced in years.
Each time he attends court and then goes to the ministry,
it may be difficult for him.
From now on, in addition to the regular ten-day breaks,
he shall rest one day out of every four.
This should allow him to recuperate.
For routine matters, other chancellors may handle them,
and only major issues need to be reported to him."
On the day Wùchén,
an edict was issued to the Shàngshūshěng,
stating that from now on, officials of the fifth rank and above shall each recommend those they know to be capable.
There shall be an annual limit on the number of recommendations.
Those who fail to recommend shall be punished for obscuring talent.
Furthermore, in accordance with the Táng system,
internal officials of the fifth rank and above shall recommend their successors upon assuming office.
All such recommendations shall be subject to investigation by the Tíxíngsī.
On the day Jǐsì,
the system for transmitting documents was first established.
On the day Rénshēn,
the Emperor held court at Lóngqìnggōng.
On the day Yǐhài,
Cānzhī Zhèngshì Yílà Lǚ was ordered to supervise the compilation and revision of the Liáoshǐ.
On the day Dīngchǒu,
Yílà Bǐng, who was Administrator of the Western Shànggémén, was appointed as an envoy to Gāolí for the Emperor's birthday.
The Yùshǐtái memorialized:
"According to past practice,
Censorate officials were not permitted to meet with others.
This was primarily to prevent favoritism towards princes, chancellors, and powerful families.
However, this makes it impossible to inquire about the benefits and harms among the common people, or the good and bad conduct of officials. "
An imperial edict was issued, allowing them to meet with officials of the fourth rank and below from now on,
while meetings with officials of the third rank and above remain as before.
On the day Xīnsì,
an edict was issued to the relevant authorities,
stating that if any famine should occur in various places in the future,
the Zǒngguǎn, Jiédùshǐ, or Tíxíngsī shall first provide relief loans or aid,
and then report to the Emperor.
In the twelfth month, on the first day, Bǐngxū,
the Emperor held court at Lóngqìnggōng.
In this month, there were five court sessions in total.
An edict was issued to cease minting coins.
On the day Dīnghài,
Mìzhōu presented a white pheasant.
On the day Rénchén,
an edict was issued to the relevant authorities,
stating that Nǚzhí people and commoners are not allowed to use nets to catch wild animals,
nor are they allowed to release flocks of eagles to unjustly harm living creatures,
also fearing that Nǚzhí people might neglect archery.
On the day Wùxū,
the Běijīng and Liáodōng Salt Commissionerates were re-established,
and the Xījīng and Jiěyán Salt Patrol Commissioners were abolished.
Based on the report from the Hédōng Southern and Northern Circuit Tíxíngsī,
relief was provided for the famine in Nínghuà, Bǎodé, and Lánzhōu.
Those who had relocated and returned to their occupations
were granted a one-year tax exemption.
On this day,
officials on duty and performers in the palace were prohibited from drinking alcohol.
On the day Yǐsì,
a memorial sacrifice was offered at Xīnglíng.
On the day Rénzǐ,
an edict was issued to the Censorate officials, saying:
"The Tíxíngsī's impeachments often concern minor transgressions.
If carried out, it may compromise the overall situation;
if not, it might appear to be obstructed.
Therefore, this intention should be conveyed to them."
On the day Jiǎyín,
Sòng, Gāolí, and Xià sent envoys to offer New Year's congratulations.
This winter,
there was no snow.
In the first year of Míngchāng, in spring, on the first day of the first month, Bǐngchén,
the reign title was changed.
Due to the mourning for Shìzōng,
no court congratulations were received.
The Emperor held court at Lóngqìnggōng.
In this month, there were four court sessions in total.
On the day Dīngsì,
a decree was issued allowing princes serving in external regions to hunt for five days.
Beyond this, it was prohibited.
Their entourages were also ordered to be disciplined,
so as not to disturb the people.
On the day Xīnyǒu,
an edict was issued to the Shàngshūshěng,
stating that chancellors, who oversee the nation,
must not accept gifts from others.
However, on their birthdays,
the value of gifts accepted should not exceed ten thousand cash.
For relatives within the dàyīng mourning period and above,
and officials of the second rank and above,
there is no prohibition.
On the day Rénxū,
Wáng Wèi, who was Prefect of Hézhōngfǔ, was appointed as Shàngshū Yòuchéng,
and Wányán Shǒuzhēn, who was Minister of Punishments, was appointed as Cānzhī Zhèngshì.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
the Emperor went to Dàfángshān.
On the day Yǐchǒu,
memorial sacrifices were offered at Xīnglíng and Yùlíng.
On the day Bǐngyín,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
On the day Wùchén,
a decree was issued prohibiting self-ordination as Buddhist monks or Daoist priests.
An imperial order was issued to various regions to seek out Shìzōng's imperial writings.
On the day Xīnwèi,
the Emperor went to the spring hunt in the near suburbs.
On the day Jǐmǎo,
the Emperor went to the spring hunt.
In the second month, on the day Dīnghài,
Venus was seen in daylight.
On the day Bǐngshēn,
an envoy was sent to instruct the princes
that when hunting, they must not cross their own borders.
On the day RénYín,
an edict was issued to the relevant authorities,
granting a five-day holiday for Hánshí,
to be enacted into law.
On the day Jiǎchén,
the Emperor returned from the spring hunt.
The Emperor held court at Lóngqìnggōng.
In this month, there were four court sessions in total.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
white hair grew from the ground.
On the day Jiǎyín,
the Emperor went to Dàfángshān.
In the third month, on the first day, Yǐmǎo,
memorial sacrifices were offered at Xīnglíng.
On the day Bǐngchén,
the Emperor returned to the capital.
The Emperor held court at Lóngqìnggōng.
In this month, there were six court sessions in total.
On the day Jǐwèi,
an imperial order was issued to the Diǎnjiǎnsī,
stating that all candidates for imperial guards must meet physical standards.
However, if descendants of meritorious officials are exceptionally skilled in archery,
even if they do not meet the standards,
they should still be allowed to be presented.
On the day Guǐhài,
the Rites Officials reported:
"If commoners have triplets,
and there are those among them with talent and conduct who can be utilized, they should be observed and recommended,
and employed according to their abilities.
As for those born to female slaves,
the old system provided a hundred strings of cash from the government
to support their upbringing.
The Shàngshūshěng requests an additional forty strings of cash
to redeem them as free people."
The decree was approved.
On the day Bǐngyín,
the relevant authorities reported:
"According to the old system,
court officials of the sixth rank and below were allowed to have their retainers pay for labor service,
but officials of the fifth rank and above were not allowed to have them pay for labor service,
as it was feared to compromise propriety.
For those who have reached the third rank in official positions and are sixty years old or above upon retirement,
half of their labor service is provided.
We humbly request that without distinction between internal and external officials,
those who wish to pay for labor service be allowed to do so."
This was granted.
On the day Jǐsì,
polo was played in the Western Park,
and all officials attended to watch.
On the day Guǐyǒu,
an edict was issued that internal and external officials of the fifth rank and above
shall annually recommend one honest and capable official.
Those who fail to recommend shall be punished for obscuring talent.
On the day Yǐhài,
the examinations for 'Yìngzhì' and 'Hóngcí' were first established.
On the day Dīngchǒu,
a decree was issued that internal and external officials, as well as performers from various bureaus,
shall be granted one day of leave on the death anniversaries of their grandparents and parents.
On the day Xīnsì,
an edict was issued to repair the Kǒngzǐ Temple and Academy in Qūfù.
On the day Rénwǔ,
the Emperor went to Shòu'āngōng.
In summer, in the fourth month, on the first day, Jiǎshēn,
the Emperor held court at Lóngqìnggōng.
In this month, there were four court sessions in total.
On the day Wùxū,
the Emperor went to Shòu'āngōng.
In the fifth month,
there was no rain.
On the day Yǐmǎo,
prayers were offered at the northern suburb and the Tàimiào.
The court assembled at the Lóngqìnggōng;
this month there were three such assemblies.
On the day Bǐngchén,
Yílà Níng, the Superintendent of the Imperial Hawk Kennels, was appointed as the Envoy for Granting Gifts to the Xià Kingdom.
On the day Wùwǔ,
Heaven was worshipped in the Xīyuàn.
Willow-shooting and polo were held,
and the common people were permitted to watch.
On the day Rénxū,
prayers for rain were offered at the Shèjì.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
it was decreed that candidates who passed the provincial examinations and those who passed the four final examinations should be granted imperial favor.
On the day Jǐsì,
prayers for rain were again offered at the Tàimiào.
On the day Gēngwǔ,
one person was appointed as Zhī Dēngwéngǔ Yuàn Shì.
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
due to the prayers for rain,
distant sacrifices were made to the Yuèzhèn Hǎidú at the northern suburb.
On the day Wùyín,
officials, both inside and outside the court, of the fifth rank and above,
were ordered to recommend one talented official whom they knew within their jurisdiction to succeed them.
On the day Rénwǔ,
Cānzhī Zhèngshì Yílà Lǚ was appointed as Shàngshū Yòuchéng;
Yùshǐ Zhōngchéng Túdān Yì was appointed as Cānzhī Zhèngshī;
Shàngshū Yòuchéngxiàng Xiāng was dismissed.
In the sixth month, on the day Jǐchǒu,
it was decreed that if a family member of an imperial prince committed an offense,
their Chief Clerk and subordinate officials would be held guilty for failing to detect it or for deliberately conniving at it.
On the day Rénchén,
the Empress Dowager was escorted to Qìngshòusì.
On the day Jiǎchén,
an imperial edict stipulated that Buddhist and Daoist monks should be tested once every three years.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the day Jǐsì,
Lǐbù Shàngshū Wáng Xiāo and others were appointed as envoys to congratulate Sòng on its emperor's birthday.
On the day Gēngwǔ,
the court assembled at the Lóngqìnggōng.
On the day Dīngchǒu,
an imperial edict abolished the Xiāyá Shān market in the northwest circuit.
In the eighth month, on the first day, Guǐwèi,
it was forbidden for slaves of imperial princes and princesses to claim imperial boats, encroach on merchants, or demand money and debts under false pretenses.
On the day Yǐyǒu,
an imperial edict established Changpíngcāng.
On the day Dīnghài,
the emperor returned from the Shòu'āngōng.
On the day Wùzǐ,
the court assembled at the Lóngqìnggōng;
this month there were three such assemblies.
On the day Jǐchǒu,
Zōng Níng, acting as Pàn Dàmùqīnfǔ Shì, was appointed as Píngzhāng Zhèngshì.
On the day Rénchén,
the emperor visited Yùquánshān,
and returned to the palace on the same day.
On the day Guǐsì,
the Liúquán Wù in various prefectures and garrisons were abolished.
Talented officials were selected to be prefects of various zhōu,
and all were summoned for an audience and admonished.
On the day Wùxū,
the Emperor instructed the chief ministers, saying:
“How can we make the people abandon secondary pursuits and focus on fundamental ones
to expand their savings?”
He ordered all officials to convene and discuss this.
Hùbù Shàngshū Dèng Yǎn and others said:
“Currently, customs are extravagant and wasteful.
It is appropriate to establish regulations,
distinguish between high and low,
so that clothing, utensils, and residences
each have their proper distinctions.
Excessive rites for weddings and funerals should be suppressed,
and the pursuit of nameless expenses should be prohibited.
With moderation in spending,
accumulations will naturally increase.”
Yòuchéng Lǚ, Cānzhī Zhèngshì Shǒuzhēn, and Yì said:
“It is human nature
to desire beauty when seen.
If not restrained by regulations,
extravagance will know no bounds,
expenditures will be excessive,
and the poverty of the people
will mostly be caused by this.
Now, in a time of peace,
it is precisely appropriate to investigate this matter
and establish a lasting law.”
The Emperor approved Lǚ’s proposal.
On the day Rén'yín,
an imperial edict ordered Májí, as a relative exempted from mourning rites for the imperial family,
to be specially recruited as Zhīhòu Lángjūn in the Shàngshūshěng,
and this was made a permanent regulation.
On the day Dīngwèi,
there was a hunt in the nearby suburbs.
On the day Jǐyǒu,
Sòng, Gāolì, and Xià sent envoys to congratulate on the Tiānshòujié.

it was Tiānshòujié,

the court did not assemble.

eighteen officials, including Běihǎi Xiànlìng Zhāng Áo, were promoted for their integrity and ability.

Wǔwèijūn Fù Dūzhīhuīshǐ Wūlín Dá Móujiǎ was appointed as the Envoy for the Xià Kingdom's Emperor's Birthday.

the court assembled at the Lóngqìnggōng.

the emperor went to Qiūshān.

the emperor returned from Qiūshān.
On the day Wùzǐ,
the court assembled at the Lóngqìnggōng.
On the day Bǐngshēn,
an imperial edict granted Zhái Xùn, a filial son from Guìdézhōu, and Lady Zhāng, a virtuous widow from Suìzhōu, ten rolls of silk and twenty shí of grain each.

according to the report of the relevant department,
the Dēngwéngǔ Yuàn should be on par with the Jìzhù Yuàn,

On the day Dīngwèi,
there was a hunt in the nearby suburbs.

the court assembled at the Lóngqìnggōng;

Quánzhēn and Wǔxíng Pílú were forbidden and abolished.

it was decreed that if any official wished to yield their inherited privilege (yìn) to their brothers, sons, or nephews,

you, the censors and ritual officials, should immediately discuss and analyze them.
Even if it is the words of common people,
if there is anything commendable, I still follow it,
how much more so for you, my lords.
From now on, your discussions should not merely conform to the Shàngshūshěng.”

Xīshànggéménshǐ Yílà Tābùyě was appointed as the Envoy for Gāolì's King's Birthday.
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
there was a winter hunt.
On the day Jǐmǎo,
the emperor arrived at Xióngzhōu.
Wúwáng Yǒngchéng, acting as Pàn Zhēndìngfǔ Shì, and Suíwáng Yǒngshēng, acting as Pàn Dìngwǔjūn Jiédùshǐ, came to pay respects.
In the twelfth month, on the day Rénwǔ,
the current year's taxes on hunting grounds were remitted.
On the day Dīnghài,
the emperor arrived at Ráoyáng.
On the day Jǐchǒu,
Píngzhāng Zhèngshì Zhāng Rǔlín passed away.
On the day Dīngyǒu,
the emperor returned from Ráoyáng.
On the day Jiǎchén,
the emperor visited Tàifù Túdān Kèníng's residence to inquire about his illness.
Kèníng was appointed as Tàishī and Shàngshūlìng,
enfeoffed as Zīwáng,

On the day Yǐsì,
the court assembled at the Lóngqìnggōng.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
an imperial edict ordered the relevant department
that on New Year's Day, congratulations should first be offered at the Lóngqìnggōng,
and then wine presented.
On the day Dīngwèi,
Sòng, Gāolì, and Xià sent envoys to congratulate on New Year's Day.
In the second year, in spring, the first month, on the *gēngxū* day,
due to the mourning for Shìzōng,
no audience was held.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
an edict was issued to the relevant authorities,
stating that Xìa [xià] envoys could be allowed to trade in their lodges for one day.
The Shàngshū Shěng [shàngshū shěng] reported,
"According to precedent, trade was permitted for three days."
This was followed.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
