it was first permitted to address the emperor as Shèngzhǔ [shèngzhǔ] within the palace.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
the Empress Dowager was unwell.
From that day on, he went to attend to her illness,
and only returned late at night.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
the Empress Dowager passed away.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
Zuǒfù Dūdǐanjiǎn [zuǒfù dūdǐanjiǎn] [placeholder character] and others were sent to report the national mourning to Sòng [sòng], Gāolí [gāolí], and Xìa [xià].
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
Tàishī [tàishī], Shàngshū Lìng [shàngshū lìng], Zī Wáng [zī wáng] Túshān Kèníng [túshān kèlìng] passed away.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
all officials jointly petitioned for him to attend to state affairs,
but this was not granted.
On the *wùyín* day,
an imperial edict bestowed upon the Kuòlǐ [kuòlǐ] tribe thirty thousand sheep, five hundred bolts of heavy silk, and two thousand bolts of plain silk,
to relieve their destitution.
Wú Wáng [wú wáng] Yǒngchéng [yǒngchéng] and Suí Wáng [suí wáng] Yǒngshēng [yǒngshēng] were punished for missing the deadline when rushing to the capital upon hearing of the national mourning,
with a deduction of one month's salary,
and their Chángshǐ [chángshǐ] were given fifty strokes of the rod.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
the relevant authorities reported
that Hán Wáng [hán wáng] Yǒngzhōng [yǒngzhōng] missed the deadline due to illness.
The Emperor ordered him to return.
In the second month, on the *rénwǔ* day,
all officials again petitioned for him to attend to state affairs,
but this was not granted.
On the *rénchén* day,
the Emperor first held court.
An imperial decree prohibited monks, nuns, and Daoist priests
from entering and exiting the homes of imperial princes and officials of the third rank or higher.
An edict was issued to the relevant authorities,
stating that for the civil service examinations, as long as the essays of the *jìnshì* candidates were up to standard, they should be admitted,
without limiting the number of people.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
Jiágǔ Qīngchén [jiágǔ qīngchén], the Pīnmì Fùshǐ [pīnmì fùshǐ], was appointed Shàngshū Zuǒchéng [shàngshū zuǒchéng].
On the *wùxū* day,
the law regarding slaves enticing free people was revised.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
the Wáng Fùfǔ Wèiguān [wáng fùfǔ wèiguān] office was first established.
In the third month, on the *dīngsì* day,
Xìa [xià] sent envoys to offer condolences.
On the *guǐhài* day,
an imperial decree was issued to the relevant authorities,
stating that state titles that clashed with the names of Hàn [hàn], Liáo [liáo], Táng [táng], Sòng [sòng], etc., should not be conferred upon subjects.
The relevant authorities deliberated,
proposing Liáo [liáo] be changed to Yǎn [yǎn],
Sòng [sòng] to Bìan [bìan],
Qín [qín] to Hào [hào],
Jìn [jìn] to Bìng [bìng],
Hàn [hàn] to Yì [yì],
Líang [líang] to Shào [shào],
Qí [qí] to Péng [péng],
Yīn [yīn] to Qíao [qíao],
Táng [táng] to Jiàng [jiàng],
Wú [wú] to È [è],
Shǔ [shǔ] to Kuí [kuí],
Chén [chén] to Wǎn [wǎn],
Suí [suí] to Jīng [jīng],
Yú [yú] to Zé [zé].
The decree was approved.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
Xìa [xià] sent envoys to offer sacrifices.
On the *yǐhài* day,
Gāolí [gāolí] sent envoys to offer condolences and sacrifices.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
Sòng [sòng] sent envoys to offer condolences and sacrifices.
In the fourth month, on the *wùyín* day,
the Shàngshū Shěng [shàngshū shěng] reported:
"Among the common people and the military colonist households, there are often disharmonies.
If they are allowed to intermarry,
this would indeed be a plan for the long-term peace and stability of the state."
This was followed.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
Empress Xiàoyì [xiàoyì] was interred in Yùlíng [yùlíng].
On the *wùzǐ* day,
a decree was issued that for natural disasters and damages within various departments,
officials in charge who ought to report but do not, or who report falsely, shall be punished with seventy strokes of the rod.
Those who inspect inaccurately shall be punished similarly.
Those who cause loss of life as a result shall be judged for violating decrees.
Those who cause innocent individuals to be wrongfully exempted from taxes shall be judged for embezzlement.
Those who make false reports shall have their household head judged for fraud by not reporting truthfully,
and the severity of the punishment shall be determined by the amount embezzled, following the law against fraudulent concealment and non-payment.
On the *gēngyín* day,
it was prohibited for commoners to wear pure yellow or silver-brown clothing.
Women were not subject to this prohibition.
This was established as a permanent regulation.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
the Emperor visited the Shòuníng Gōng [shòuníng gōng].
Jiànvì Dàfū [jiànvì dàfū] Zhāng Wěi [zhāng wěi] and others submitted a memorial requesting him to stop his journey,
but it was not granted.
On the *guǐsì* day,
an edict was issued to the relevant authorities,
stating that from now on, Jurchen characters should be directly translated into Chinese characters,
and those in the Guóshǐ Yuàn [guóshǐ yuàn] who specialized in writing Khitan characters should be dismissed.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
Yǒngzhōng [yǒngzhōng] was re-enfeoffed as Bìng Wáng [bìng wáng],
Yǒnggōng [yǒnggōng] as Lǔ Wáng [lǔ wáng],
Yǒngchéng [yǒngchéng] as Yǎn Wáng [yǎn wáng],
Yǒngshēng [yǒngshēng] as Cáo Wáng [cáo wáng],
Yǒngdǎo [yǒngdǎo] as Zhèng Wáng [zhèng wáng],
Yǒngjì [yǒngjì] as Hán Wáng [hán wáng],
and Yǒngdé [yǒngdé] as Bīn Wáng [bīn wáng].
On the *wùxū* day,
the number of lecturers and assistant lecturers at the Tàixué [tàixué] was increased.
On the *jǐhài* day,
the Xuéshì Yuàn [xuéshì yuàn] newly acquired twenty-six collections by Táng [táng] poets Dù Fǔ [dù fǔ], Hán Yù [hán yù], Líu Yǔxī [líu yǔxī], Dù Mù [dù mù], Jǐa Dǎo [jǐa dǎo], Wáng Jiàn [wáng jiàn],
and Sòng [sòng] poets Wáng Yǔchēng [wáng yǔchēng], Ōuyáng Xīu [ōuyáng xīu], Wáng Ānshí [wáng ānshí], Sū Shì [sū shì], Zhāng Lěi [zhāng lěi], Qín Guān [qín guān], and others.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
Shòuníng Gōng [shòuníng gōng] was renamed Wànníng [wànníng].
On the *rénwín* day,
he went to Wànníng Gōng [wànníng gōng].
An imperial decree stated that Yǎnshèng Gōng [yǎnshèng gōng] Kǒng Yuáncuò [kǒng yuáncuò], who inherited the title, should be treated with the rank of a fourth-grade official.
In the fifth month, on the *gēngxū* day,
an imperial decree stated that from now on, memorials were to be submitted every four days,
and court audiences were to be exempted.
On the *wùchén* day,

an imperial decree ordered that if the Wénxuān Wáng [wénxuān wáng] temples, temples of the Wind and Rain Masters, and altars of the Earth and Grain gods in various prefectures and counties had fallen into disrepair,
they should be restored.
An imperial decree stated that all clerks of the Yùshǐ Tái [yùshǐ tái] should be filled by successful candidates from the final round of examinations.
In the sixth month, on the *wùzǐ* day,
Píngzhāng Zhèngshì [píngzhāng zhèngshì] Zōng Níng [zōng níng] passed away.
On the *guǐsì* day,
it was prohibited to refer to people of the current dynasty
or the language of the current dynasty as "fān" [fān].
Violators would be flogged.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
Shàngshū Yòuchéng [shàngshū yòuchéng] Yílà Lǚ [yílà lǚ] passed away.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the *dīngsì* day,
Cānzhī Zhèngshì [cānzhī zhèngshì] Túshān Yì [túshān yì] was appointed Shàngshū Yòuchéng [shàngshū yòuchéng],
and Yùshǐ Zhōngchéng [yùshǐ zhōngchéng] Jiágǔ Héng [jiágǔ héng] was appointed Cānzhī Zhèngshì [cānzhī zhèngshì].
On the *jǐwèi* day,
he inspected the crops in the nearby suburbs.
On the *jǐsì* day,
officials were prohibited from accepting gifts from their subordinates on New Year's Day and their birthdays,
and this was made a permanent regulation.
Tóngqiān Dàmùqīnfǔshì [tóngqiān dàmùqīnfǔshì] Yǎn [yǎn] and others were appointed as envoys to congratulate Sòng [sòng] on the Emperor's birthday.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
an edict was issued to the relevant authorities,
stating that from now on, when princesses from outlying regions were summoned to the capital,
their Fùmǎ Dūwèi [fùmǎ dūwèi] were not to leave their posts without imperial decree.
In the eighth month, on the *guǐwèi* day,
he returned from Wànníng Gōng [wànníng gōng].
On the *jǐhài* day,
an imperial decree permitted those in famine-stricken areas of Shāndōng [shāndōng] and Héběi [héběi]
to offer grain in exchange for official appointments.
An edict was issued to the relevant authorities,
stating that from now on, if there were military garrisons
under the command of imperial princes,
the deputy officers should take overall command of military affairs.
On the *yǐsì* day,
Sòng [sòng], Gāolí [gāolí], and Xìa [xià] sent envoys to congratulate on the Tiānshòu Jié [tiānshòu jié].
In the ninth month, on the *dīngwèi* day,
it was Tiānshòu Jié [tiānshòu jié],
but due to the mourning for the Empress Dowager,
no audience was held.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
he went to Dàfáng Shān [dàfáng shān].
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
he paid his respects and offered sacrifices at Yùlíng [yùlíng].
On the *bǐngchén* day,
he returned to the capital.
On the *dīngsì* day,
Xīshàng Géménshǐ [xīshàng géménshǐ] Bái Wǎn [bái wǎn] was appointed as Xìa [xià] 's birthday envoy.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
the law regarding fraudulent imperial decrees that had not yet been implemented was established.
Shàngshū Zuǒchéng [shàngshū zuǒchéng] Jiágǔ Qīngchén [jiágǔ qīngchén] was appointed Píngzhāng Zhèngshì [píngzhāng zhèngshì] and enfeoffed as Ruìguó Gōng [ruìguó gōng].
Cānzhī Zhèngshì [cānzhī zhèngshì] Wányán Shǒuzhēn [wányán shǒuzhēn] was appointed Shàngshū Zuǒchéng [shàngshū zuǒchéng].
Zhī Dàxīngfǔ Shì [zhī dàxīngfǔ shì] Zhāng Wàngōng [zhāng wàngōng] was appointed Cānzhī Zhèngshì [cānzhī zhèngshì].
On the *gēngshēn* day,
he went to Qīu Shān [qīu shān].
In winter, the tenth month, on the *jǐchǒu* day,
he returned from Qīu Shān [qīu shān].
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
an imperial decree prohibited prison wardens from holding banquets or associating with officials of prefectures, departments, and counties.
Violators would be punished.
It was prohibited for those who received Taoist talismans from Tàiyī Hùnyuán [tàiyī hùnyuán] to privately construct monastic cells.
On the *rénwín* day,
due to the drought in Héběi [héběi] and Shāndōng [shāndōng],
all those guilty of miscellaneous offenses and previously undetected strong robbery
were to have their sentences reduced by one degree, releasing those below the level of penal servitude.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day, the first day of the eleventh month,
an edict was issued that Jǐn Nǚzhì (女直) people were not to have their surnames translated into Hàn characters.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
it was forbidden for entertainers to perform acts portraying emperors of past dynasties,
or to use the salutation 'wànsuì' (萬歲, "long live").
Offenders would be punished with severe penalties for impropriety.
On the *dīngsì* day,
Fù Zōngbì (傅宗璧), tutor to the Bīn Wáng (豳王), and others were appointed as envoys to offer New Year's greetings to Sòng (宋).
On the *wùwǔ* day,
the Xià (夏) people killed our border general Ālǔdài (阿魯帶).
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
an edict decreed that those who submitted anonymous letters
would be sentenced to four years of penal servitude.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
Wányán Kuāng (完顏匡), Vice-Commissioner of the Bureau of Imperial Attendants, was appointed as envoy to Gāolí (高麗) for the Emperor's birthday.
On the *rénshēn* day,
an imperial decree ordered that officials of the Tíxíngsī (提刑司) henceforth present themselves at court every fifteen days.
On the *yǐhài* day, the first day of the twelfth month,
an imperial decree ordered that three-rank retired officials be exempt from paying taxes for their retainers.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
regulations were set for the punishment of border garrison commanders for offenses related to banditry.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
a hunt was held in the near suburbs.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
an imperial edict abolished Qìdān (契丹) characters.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
Shàngshū Yòuchéng (尚書右丞) Túshānyì (徒單鎰) was dismissed.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
Sòng (宋), Gāolí (高麗), and Xià (夏) sent envoys to offer New Year's greetings.
In the spring of the third year, on the *yǐsì* day, the first day of the first month,
due to the mourning for the Huáng Tàihòu (皇太后),
court was not held.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
it was the Lesser Anniversary of mourning for Xiàoyì Huánghòu (孝懿皇后).
The Shàngshūshěng (尚書省) requested that, following the precedent of Shìzōng's (世宗) death anniversary in Míngchāng (明昌) year one,
princes should attend,
wearing dark purple mourning attire,
and removing gold and jade ornaments.
All officials were not to attend to their duties,
and music and slaughtering were prohibited.
This was granted.
On the *rénxū* day,
the Emperor went to Chūnshuǐ (春水).
On the *jiǎxū* day, the first day of the second month,
an imperial decree permitted *méng'ān* (猛安) and *móukè* (謀克) to lead their households on hunts twice during the winter months,
with each outing not exceeding ten days.
On the *rénchén* day,
the Emperor returned from Chūnshuǐ (春水).
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
a hunt was held in the near suburbs.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
an imperial edict restored the official ranks and titles of Tián Jú (田瑴) and others.
In the intercalary month, on the *jiǎzǐ* day,
Wūlíndá Yuàn (烏林荅愿), Commander of the Shāndōng Lù (山東路) army, was appointed Yùshǐ Dàfū (御史大夫).
In the third month, on the *yǐhài* day,
regulations for compensating for robbery, and rewards for officials and common people who personally apprehended robbers, were revised.
On the *xīnsì* day,
the positions of Zuǒ Wèi Fùjiāngjūn (左衞副將軍) and Yòu Wèi Fùjiāngjūn (右衞副將軍) were first established.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
the Lúgōu Shíqiáo (瀘溝石橋) was completed.
The Emperor visited Xīchūnyuán (熙春園).
On the *dīnghài* day,
the Emperor went to Wànnínggōng (萬寧宮).
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
an imperial edict bestowed silk and grain upon Liú Yú (劉瑜), a filial son from Dìzhōu (棣州), and Liú Qìngyòu (劉慶祐), a filial son from Jǐnzhōu (錦州),
commending their households
and exempting them from service.
The Emperor then asked his prime ministers:
"How many filial and righteous people have ever been appointed to official positions?"
Zuǒchéng (左丞) Shǒuzhēn (守貞) replied:
"During Shìzōng's (世宗) time, there was a Liú Zhèng (劉政) who was once an official,
but such individuals are often simple and honest, not suited for official affairs."
The Emperor said:
"That is not necessarily always the case.
Filial and righteous people have already perfected their conduct.
If they are even slightly capable, they should be employed.
Even if some later pretend to be filial and righteous out of ambition,
feigning filial piety and righteousness
is still not a bad thing.
Investigate all filial and righteous people reported previously.
If there are any who are capable,
report them fully."
On the *guǐsì* day,
the Shàngshūshěng (尚書省) reported:
"Those who speak on current affairs say that
Buddhist and Daoist practitioners not bowing to their parents and relatives
corrupts customs,
and nothing is worse than this.
The ritual officials state that an imperial decree from the second year of Táng (唐) Kāiyuán (開元) stated: 'It is heard that Daoists, Daoist priestesses, monks, and nuns do not bow to their parents,
which is to forget their birth as children,
and to be arrogant towards their parents while pursuing trivialities.
From now on, all are permitted to bow to their parents,
and regarding the solemnity of mourning rites and the etiquette for elders,
all shall follow ordinary customs.'
We, your ministers, believe that it is appropriate to act according to this precedent."
The decree was approved.
Zuǒchéng (左丞) Shǒuzhēn (守貞) said:
"Your Majesty once ordered me to inquire about the matters stated in the memorial submitted by Chén Yì (陳毅) from Xīnzhōu (忻州).
One of them strongly criticized the abuses of governors and magistrates.
I personally asked him about the methods to remedy this,
but he ultimately could not articulate them."
The Emperor said:
"At present, the government wishes to know its shortcomings.
Even if he has no remedy for the abuses,
merely being able to point out the abuses
is commendable enough.
As Yì (毅) stated, officials everywhere fail to implement regulations.
Even those hired as laborers still need to exert themselves,
let alone those who receive the state's emoluments and act in such a way.
How can they not fall short in their duties as ministers and subjects?
Order an investigation into the regulations previously issued and ensure their implementation."
On this day,
Wēn Wáng (溫王) Jiè (玠) passed away.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
officials were ordered to pray for rain,
and to worship the five sacred mountains, four marshy lakes, and four seas at the northern suburb.
In the fourth month, on the *rén'yín* day, the first day of the month,
the spring and autumn sacrifices at the Xuánshèng Miào (宣聖廟) were formalized.
The three sacrificial officials were to be filled by the Jìjiǔ (祭酒), Sīyè (司業), and Bóshì (博士).
The invocation began with
"Huángdì (皇帝) respectfully dispatches,"
and the ascending music was changed to be performed by the Tàicháng (太常) musicians.
The sacrificial officials, those performing duties, and those participating in the sacrifices were all to wear formal attire.
The attending academic officials were to wear official robes,
and students, scholar robes.
The Shàngshūshěng (尚書省) reported:
"The Tíxíngsī (提刑司) has recommended Liú Qìbó (劉器博), a *jìnshì* (進士) from Zhuōzhōu (涿州), Zhāng Ānxíng (張安行), a *jìnshì* (進士) from Bózhōu (博州), and Hú Guāngqiān (胡光謙) from Hézhōngfǔ (河中府).
Although Hú Guāngqiān (胡光謙) is eighty-three years old,
he is still capable of being employed."
An imperial decree granted Liú Qìbó (劉器博) and Zhāng Ānxíng (張安xing) the special designation of *tóng jìnshì chūshēn* (同進士出身),
and summoned Hú Guāngqiān (胡光謙) to the capital.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
prayers for rain were offered to the deities of soil and grain.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
copper mining beyond the northern border of Tiānshān (天山) was halted.
On the *wùshēn* day,
Yíng Wáng (瀛王) Guī (瓌) passed away.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
an imperial edict summoned all officials to discuss the matter of digging moats along the northern border.
An imperial edict bestowed ten rolls of silk and twenty *shí* (石) of grain upon Mèng Xīng (孟興), a filial son from Yúnnèi (雲內),
and posthumously honored Míng Shīshì (明師氏), a chaste widow from Tóngzhōu (同州), with the posthumous title of
"Jié" (節, "Chaste").
On the *bǐngyín* day,
due to drought,
an imperial edict was issued, blaming himself.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
again for praying for rain,
sacrifices were offered to the five sacred mountains, four marshy lakes, four seas, and mountains and rivers at the northern suburb.
On the *wùchén* day,
an imperial decree ordered that princely robes should have silver-grey purple borders.
Yùshǐ Zhōngchéng (御史中丞) Wú Dǐngshū (吳鼎樞) and others were dispatched to review and decide on wrongful imprisonment cases in Zhōngdū (中都),
while cases in other regions were entrusted to the Tíxíngsī (提刑司) for judgment.
Zuǒchéng (左丞) Shǒuzhēn (守貞), due to the drought,
submitted a memorial requesting to resign,
but it was not granted.
Cānzhī Zhèngshì (參知政事) Héng (衡) and Wàn Gōng (萬公) both came to express gratitude.
The Emperor said:
"The four matters mentioned in the previous edict – discontinuing non-urgent tasks, economizing on unnecessary expenses, deliberating on redundant officials, and adjudicating backlogged cases –
should be implemented quickly."
In the fifth month, on the *rénshēn* day, the first day of the month,
Bóshùlǔ Zǐyuán (孛术魯子元), Yuánwàiláng (員外郎) of the Shàngshū Lǐbù (尚書禮部), was appointed envoy to Gāolí (高麗) with special gifts.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
the project of digging moats along the northern border was halted.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
prayers for rain were offered to the deities of soil and grain.
On this day,
it rained.
On the *wùyín* day,
one hundred eighty-three palace women were released.
The Shàngshūshěng (尚書省) reported that,
recently due to famine in Shāndōng (山東) and Héběi (河北),
envoys had already been dispatched to pacify and provide relief,
and Fàn Wényuān (范文淵), Sīzhèng (司正) of the Yòu Sānbù (右三部), was again sent to inspect the situation.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
as there was sufficient rain,
sacrifices were offered to the deities of soil and grain.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
all officials offered congratulations for the sufficient rain.
Shàngshū Zuǒchéng (尚書左丞) Wányán Shǒuzhēn (完顏守貞) was dismissed.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
due to sufficient rain, sacrifices were offered to the five sacred mountains, four marshy lakes, and four seas.
In the sixth month, on the day Guǐmǎo,
the Chief Ministers requested the abolition of the Tíxíngsī.
The Emperor said:
"There are only a little over thirty officials in the Tíxíngsī of various circuits,
yet we still suffer from not finding suitable people.
With over three hundred zhōu and jùn,
how can we possibly find suitable people for all of them?"
He did not permit it.
On the day Jiǎyín,
due to prolonged rain,
officials were ordered to pray for clear weather.
On the day Dīngsì,
the regulations for the Tíxíngsī were established.
On the day Xīnyǒu,
an edict was issued to fix the rules for punishment regarding suspicious presentations of criminal cases by internal and external offices.
On the day Yǐchǒu,
Liú Wěi (劉瑋), who was serving as Zhī Dàmíng Fǔ Shì, was appointed Shàngshū Yòuchéng.
Officials reported that
Hézhōu (河州) suffered disasters,
and the people lacked food,
while some rent and taxes were still unpaid.
An edict was issued to exempt them.
The Hùbù was instructed,
"You may prepay the winter salaries of all officials.
Order them to sell grain from the granaries at market price to the poor when the time comes.
After the autumn harvest, they shall buy back the equivalent amount with their funds.
The profit gained from this will surely be substantial,
and it will benefit both superiors and inferiors."
Those who did not wish to participate
were permitted to decline.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the day Wùyín,
an imperial order was given to the Shàngshūshěng, saying:
"If famine victims reach Liáodōng (遼東),
I fear they will have difficulty obtaining food quickly,
and some will surely starve to death.
Order the grain distribution officials to ask them where they wish to reside,
give them documents,
and command local officials to distribute food according to the number of mouths.
Order the wealthy to provide grain to support them,
limited to two months.
This grain shall count towards their autumn taxes."
On the day Jǐmǎo,
Qízhōu (祁州) Cìshǐ Dùn Chángshòu (頓長壽) and Ānwǔ Jūn Jiédù Fùshǐ Hú Là (胡剌) were punished with fifty strokes each
for inadequate disaster relief in four counties.
On the day Guǐwèi,
an edict was issued to increase the northern border army by 1,200 men,
to be distributed among various forts.
On the day Dīnghài,
Hú Guāngqiān (胡光謙) arrived at the capital.
The Xuéshìyuàn was ordered to test him with miscellaneous essays,
and he met with imperial approval.
The Emperor said:
"I wish to personally question him."
On the day Xīnmǎo,
Diànqián Dū Diǎnjiǎn Púsàn Duān (僕散端) and others were appointed envoys to congratulate Sòng (宋) on its birthday.
On the day Jǐhài,
the Emperor said to the Chief Ministers:
"I hear that many tutors and guards of the princes are overly strict and petty,
restricting their every move.
This is not my intention.
The establishment of this office
was originally to assist and guide the princes,
to keep them on the right path
and help them grasp the essentials, and nothing more."
Píngzhāng Zhèngshì Qīngchén (清臣) replied:
"Please let Your Majesty's will be universally proclaimed."
The Emperor said:
"I have already instructed them."
In the eighth month, on the day Guǐmǎo,
an imperial order was issued that if officials who are old or ill refuse to resign,
and the authorities instruct them to retire,
they shall not be included in the list for salary provision.
Previous cases shall not be discussed.
As the Emperor noted discord between the military and civilians, and corruption among officials,
he ordered officials from the fourth rank down to the sixth rank up to convene discussions in the Shàngshūshěng,
each to present their views.
On the day Jiǎchén,
officials from the third rank down to the sixth rank up were assembled
and questioned about the gains and losses of court policies and the advantages and disadvantages for the people,
each ordered to write down their replies.
On the day Dīngwèi,
based on the report by officials regarding the filial conduct of Wáng Zhèn (王震) from Wéndēng Xiàn (文登縣) of Nínghǎizhōu (寧海州),
and because he had previously pursued the jìnshì (進士) examination,
his writing was also tested.
He was specially granted the title of Tóng Jìnshì Chūshēn,
and appointed to a first-class professorial position.
On the day Xīnhài,
the Emperor returned from Wànníng Gōng (萬寧宮).
Hú Guāngqiān (胡光qiān) was specially granted the third class of the Míngchāng (明昌) second year jìnshì degree,
and appointed Jiāngshìláng, Tàicháng Sì Fènglǐláng.
Although this position was established in the old official system,
it had never been filled.
Due to Guāngqiān's (光謙) virtue and talent,
he was specially appointed.
On the day Jǐwèi,
Wūlíndá Yuàn (烏林荅愿) was appointed Shàngshū Zuǒchéng.
On the day Xīnyǒu,
the Emperor hunted in the near suburbs.
On the day Yǐchǒu,
the Emperor said to the Chief Ministers:
"I wish to appoint officials
and let them serve in their positions for a long time.
If today one is a ritual official,
and tomorrow manages money and grain,
though there may occasionally be exceptional talents,
few can handle all matters proficiently."
They replied:
"If a person of average ability serves long in their position,
they will become familiar with the duties,
and ultimately become effective."
The Emperor asked Tàicháng Qīng Zhāng Wěi (張暐):
"In ancient times there were three kè (恪);
why are there none now?"
Wěi (暐) thoroughly explained the historical precedents.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
Sòng (宋), Gāolì (高麗), and Xià (夏) sent envoys to congratulate on Tiānshòu Jié.
In the ninth month, on the first day Gēngwǔ,
Tiānshòu Jié was observed.
Due to the mourning for the Empress Dowager,
no court audience was held.
The Shàngshūshěng was instructed:
"Last year, the rent and taxes suspended in the disaster-stricken areas of Shāndōng (山東) and Héběi (河北), as well as loaned money and grain,
if collected immediately,
may prevent the poor from recovering.
It is permissible to collect them in installments after a bountiful harvest."
He also instructed the Chief Ministers:
"The Tíxíngsī of various circuits formerly only investigated officials who were old, ill, unfit for duty, or unsuitable for direct public service.
If their condition was confirmed,
they would be reassigned to another circuit.
If the Tíxíngsī of another circuit re-investigated and confirmed the condition,
they should no longer be assigned positions involving direct public service.
You, my lords, should discuss and implement this."
On the day Jiǎxū,
Tángkuò Hédá (唐括合達), the order of Jiāoshè Shǔ, was appointed envoy for the Xià (夏) Kingdom's birthday.
On the day Jǐmǎo,
the Emperor went to Qiūshān (秋山).
Half of this year's summer and autumn rent and taxes were exempted for households passing through the hunting grounds,
and those who had previously performed corvée labor were exempted for an additional year.
In winter, the tenth month, on the day Rénwǔ,
the Emperor returned from Qiūshān (秋山).
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
an imperial order was given to the Yùshǐ Tái:
"From now on, when the Tíxíngsī recommends honest and capable officials,
they shall no longer mention requests for promotion in rank."
On the day Rénzǐ,
officials reported the completion of the expansion and renovation of the Xuánshèng Miào (宣聖廟) in Qūfù (曲阜).
An imperial order was given:
"Dǎng Huáiyīng (党懷英) shall compose the stele inscription;
I will personally conduct the ceremony of ancestral worship and offering,
so review the historical precedents and report them."
On the day Jiǎyín,
an imperial order was issued that wherever Chángpíngcāng (常平倉) were established,
zhōu and fǔ officials should oversee them in their official capacities,
and xiàn officials should concurrently manage the affairs,
adjusting the prices based on the quantity purchased,
to establish this as a permanent system.
Yóu Zǒng (游總), a hermit recommended by the Hénán (河南) circuit Tíxíngsī, was granted the Tóng Jìnshì Chūshēn.
As he was old and disinclined to official service,
he was appointed Dēngshìláng,
and given half the salary of a regular eighth-rank official for life.
On the day Wùwǔ,
the Shàngshūshěng was instructed to seek out learned and knowledgeable scholars.
On the day Guǐhài,
an envoy was sent to instruct the tutors and guards of the princes, saying:
"I have appointed the princes to govern in various regions
primarily so that in their leisure from state affairs,
they may enjoy ease and comfort,
and find their own contentment.
However, fearing that their actions might occasionally deviate from reason,
I therefore appointed tutors and guards
to encourage and guide them, to prevent them from falling into error, and nothing more.
If their leisure activities and banquets are not excessive,
what harm is there?
Now I hear that some of you are overly zealous,
interfering in every trivial matter within the princely residences
that does not impede public morality.
This is not how assistance and guidance should be provided.
You should each consider your duties,
act moderately in matters,
and not lose sight of proper decorum.
Furthermore, instruct the princes
so they understand my intentions."
On the day Bǐngyín,
an imperial order was issued that recommended officials and those tested in the Zhōngshū Pàn (中書判) should be re-examined by appointed officials.
Those whose words and actions corresponded should be proportionally promoted or transferred.
Officials in the imperial court and those of the sixth rank and above should be employed according to their strengths.
On the day Jǐsì,
the Emperor hunted in the near suburbs.
On the Gēngwǔ day of the eleventh month, the new moon,
the Grand Secretariat reported:
“Hànlín Shìjiǎng Xuéshì Dǎng Huáiyīng recommended Kǒng Duānfǔ, the 48th-generation descendant of Kǒngzǐ.
His age and virtue are both exalted,
and he is well-versed in ancient learning.
Jǐnán Fǔ recommended Wèi Rǔyì, who possesses literary talent and moral integrity,
has studied diligently for over thirty years,
and has completed the final examination four times.
Wèi Zhōu recommended Liú Zhènhēng, who excels in both scholarship and conduct,
and has served as a chief examiner.
Yìdū Fǔ recommended Wáng Shū, who is broadly learned and skilled in calligraphy,
and is extremely filial to his parents.”
An imperial edict granted Wèi Rǔyì the special title of Jìnshì Jídì.
Liú Zhènhēng and others were granted Tóng Jìnshì Chūshēn,
and all were listed on the Wáng Zé榜.
Kǒng Duānfǔ was to be summoned when the weather turned warm in spring.
On the Bǐngzǐ day,
an edict prohibited subjects from having names identical to ancient emperors if their surnames were also the same.
The names of Zhōu Gōng and Kǒngzǐ were also to be avoided.
On the Wùyín day,
Xiāng Zhōu was elevated to Zhāngdé Fǔ.
Wēndūn Zhōng and others, formerly Right Vice Dūdiǎnjiǎn, were appointed envoys to congratulate Sòng on New Year's Day.
On the Rénwǔ day,
the Grand Secretariat reported
that Chéng Yì, Zhimíng Hénán Fǔshì, requested an imperial conferment of titles for his father and grandfather.
Quán Shàngshū Lǐbù Lángzhōng Dǎng Huáiyīng said:
“Whenever a Zǎizhí is reassigned to an external chief official post,
the etiquette for their subordinate officials to meet them differs from other chief officials,
and their sons may also be provisionally appointed as Shěng Lìshǐ.
If their sons are treated thus,
it is reasonable that the conferment of titles for their fathers and grandfathers should also be different.
They should be granted conferment of titles on par with Zǎizhí.”
This was approved.
On the Jiǎshēn day,
Tíxíng Sī Lìshǐ was changed to Shūshǐ.
On the Bǐngshēn day,
acting on a report from the authorities:
“Zhāng Xiǎn, a native of Dìngqiāng in Hé Zhōu, is filial and hardworking in farming.
He burned debt bonds already collected
and further donated a thousand shí of grain to relieve the famine.
Róng Jí, a native of Dì Zhōu, donated seven hundred shí of rice and three hundred guàn of money,
and distributed three thousand bundles of firewood in winter.
None of them had any ulterior motives.”
They were specially appointed to two official positions each,
and retained their regular rank.
On the Guǐmǎo day of the twelfth month,
Zhāng Rǔyóu, Dōng Shànggémén Shǐ, was appointed envoy to Gāolí for the Emperor's birthday.
On the Xīnhài day,
the authorities were ordered to pray for snow.
On the Guǐchǒu day,
a hunt was held in the nearby suburbs.
On the Bǐngchén day,
a red vapor was seen in the north.
On the Dīngsì day,
an edict ordered the establishment of the Wǔdìng Zhèncāng in Xiàguī Xiàn, Huá Zhōu,
the Sùyì Zhèncāng in Lìyáng Xiàn, Jīngzhào,
and the Běiwǔdù Cāng in Wǔyáng Xiàn, Xǔ Zhōu.
One Cāngcǎo Dūjiān was to be appointed for each,
to be concurrently held by the county official.
On the Yǐchǒu day,
regulations for reporting retirement upon assumption of office were established.
On the Dīngmǎo day,
Sòng, Gāolí, and Xià sent envoys to offer New Year's greetings.
Collation Notes
Běnjì, Chapter 10, Zōng 2
On the Jǐsì day, the new moon of the first month of spring in the fourth year,
due to the mourning for the Empress Dowager,
no court was held.
On the Xīnwèi day,
Jiágǔ Qīngchén, Píngzhāng Zhèngshì, was appointed Shàngshū Yòuchéngxiàng,
and concurrently Jíānxiū Guóshǐ.
On the Dīngchǒu day,
Lǐ Xiànkě, Hùbù Shìláng, and others were dispatched to various routes to encourage agriculture.
On the Guǐwèi day,
the Grand Secretariat reported that Sū Déxiù, Tuīguān of Dàxīng Fǔ, was appointed Lǐbù Zhǔshì.
The Emperor said:
“I have told you before
that officials should remain in their posts for a long time.
He was just serving as a judicial official,
then changed to Hùcáo,
and soon after appointed to Lǐbù.
How can one talent encompass all?
If one remains in their post for a long time,
even mediocre talent is better than a newcomer.
Having experience in affairs,
they will certainly be effective.
In the future, do not lightly change appointments.”
The Emperor further said:
“Anyone praised for having 'extraordinary achievements in governance'
means they possess exceptional talent in decision-making.
If it's merely incorruptibility,
this is merely their duty;
it's because many are corrupt
that their 'extraordinary' quality is highlighted.
The prime minister also said, 'Recently, those who speak on affairs say
that the ways of filial piety, fraternity, integrity, and shame are currently lacking,
and request a rectification of customs.'
This is because officials are unable to uphold and propagate moral education.
Currently, those who observe and recommend officials
often demand immediate results,
prioritizing administrative efficiency.
Those who are magnanimous in heart
and wish to implement moral transformation
are often called impractical.
Thus, everyone considers moral education a secondary matter;
this is why filial piety and fraternity are neglected.
If the authorities are informed
that officials who can diligently implement moral transformation
should be promoted and employed,
then moral education can be carried out,
and filial piety and fraternity can flourish.
What is currently observed and recommended
prioritizes talent over virtue.
Cunning and dishonest individuals,
even if corrupt,
once appointed,
are still considered capable officials;
this is why integrity and shame are lost.
If the authorities are informed
that when observing and recommending officials,
truth and falsehood must be thoroughly examined,
so that those with talent but without moral conduct cannot aspire to office,
and those who seek advancement through improper means are censured,
then the custom of eager competition will cease,
and integrity and shame can flourish.”
On the Xīnmǎo day,
aid was distributed to those affected by floods in various circuits of Héběi.
On the Guǐsì day,
the Diǎnjiǎn Sī was instructed
that all land outside the imperial temporary palace and hunting grounds should be cultivated by the people.
Although restricted areas,
people were permitted to enter and exit with farm implements.
On the Bǐngshēn day,
Sānshèng, Fùshǐ of Dōngjīng Lù, presented a falcon.
An imperial message was sent to him saying:
“Your duty is not light.
You have hardly reported on the well-being of the people
or the uprightness or corruption of officials,
yet you present a falcon.
Is this your responsibility?
Do not do this again in the future.”
On the Wùxū day, the new moon of the second month,
the Emperor went to Chūnshuǐ.
It was decided that sacrifices to the altars of earth and grain would be offered on the Wù day of the middle month of spring and autumn.
On the Guǐchǒu day,
a hunt was held at Yáocūn Diàn.
On the Guǐhài day,
the Emperor returned from Chūnshuǐ.
On the Bǐngyín day,
Zhāng Wàngōng, Cānzhī Zhèngshì, was dismissed.
On the Wùchén day, the new moon of the third month,
officials from various Tíxíng Sī came for an audience.
Each was questioned about their duties,
and admonished with an imperial instruction:
“I specially established the Tíxíng Sī
with the original intention of bringing peace to the people.
It has been five years now,
but its effectiveness is not yet apparent.
This is because many do not understand the essence of their fundamental duties,
and merely attend to trivial matters,
causing prefectures and counties to universally become timid and afraid to act.
Recently, the people of Shāndōng suffered from food shortages.
I have sent envoys to provide relief.
This is due to your incompetence,
hence it came to this.
As for past mistakes,
reflect and reform.”
On the Gēngwǔ day,
when the Emperor was about to visit Jǐngmíng Gōng,
Dǒng Shīzhōng, Yùshǐ Zhōngchéng, and others submitted a strongly worded remonstrance,
but received no reply.
On the Rénshēn day,
the memorial was submitted again.
Xǔ Ānrén, Bǔquē, and Lù Duó, Shíyí, both remonstrated,
whereupon the Emperor stopped.
Regulations were established for punishing commoners who practiced jiǎodǐ and qiāngbàng.
Xū Chíguó, Gōngbù Shàngshū, was appointed Cānzhī Zhèngshì.
On the Bǐngzǐ day,
the authorities specially granted Kǒng Duānfǔ the title of Jídì,
and appointed him Xiǎoxué Jiàoshòu.
Soon after, due to his old age,
he was ordered to receive half the salary of a zhǔbù upon retirement.
On the Jiǎshēn day,
the Emperor visited Xiāng Shān Yǒng’ān Sì and Yùquán Shān.
On the Jiǎwǔ day,
the meritorious officials to be honored in imperial temples were designated.
An edict ordered that from now on, when the Yùshǐ Tái presented memorials,
and when compiling Qǐjū Zhù, avoidance must be observed.
In the summer, fourth month, on the day Dīngyǒu (1st day of the month),
the Emperor visited Cóng Fēi’s residence at Xīnglíng.
On this day,
music was played for the first time.
From the day Jǐhài to Guǐmǎo,
the hundred officials submitted three petitions requesting the Emperor to accept an honorific title.
The Emperor said:
“Among the ancestral and ancient forefathers, those who received honorific titles
possessed the corresponding virtues,
hence they had the names.
In recent years, the five grains have not ripened,
and the common people are displaced.
This is a time for self-admonition and cultivation,
how can I accept such an empty honorific name?”
He refused,
and also stopped further such submissions.
On the day Wùshēn,
the Emperor personally performed the dì sacrifice at the Tàimiào.
On the day Gēngxū,
he went to Wànníng Gōng.
On the day Xīnhài,
Right Chancellor Qīngchén led the hundred officials and elders again to request the Emperor to accept an honorific title.
Academic official Liú Jī also led seven hundred ninety-five students from the six academies, including Zhào Kǎi, to the Zǐchénmén to request the Emperor to accept an honorific title,
following the precedent of Yuánhé in the Táng dynasty.
He refused.
On the day Dīngsì,
famine relief was provided in Hézhōu.
An imperial edict ordered that after Jurchen jinshì candidates had passed the examination,
they should still be tested in archery and horsemanship,
and those who passed would be promoted.
On the day Yǐchǒu,
the amount of grain for horses in the Shànggōng office was reduced.
Fifth month, on the day Bǐngyín (1st day of the month),
Cáo Wáng Yǒngshēng and other princes requested the Emperor to accept an honorific title.
He refused.
Shímò Zhēn, the Director of the Shànggōng Bureau, was made envoy to Xī Xià with extraordinary powers of bestowal.
On the day Jǐsì,
the Emperor, because his officials repeatedly requested him to accept an honorific title and he refused,
issued an imperial edict to both inside and outside the court,
stating that punishments of penal servitude and below would be reduced by one degree,
and those of flogging and below would be pardoned.
On the day Jiǎxū,
he observed the crops in the near suburbs.
On the day Xīnsì,
he instructed the Zuǒsī
to widely inform all circuits
to report monthly the rainfall and the condition of the fields and crops.
On the day Guǐwèi,
due to prolonged rain,
a yíng sacrifice was performed.
Sixth month, on the day Guǐchǒu,

Cuī Bǐngrén from Ānzhōu, Zhái Jū from Yǎnzhōu, Qí Wényǐ from Jǐnzhōu, Sūn Kějiǔ, Chén Xìnrén, and Dǒng Kuí from Yìngzhōu, who were recommended by officials for their virtue and talent, were all granted the status of jinshì.
On the day Bǐngchén,
due to clear weather,
sacrifices were offered to the sacred mountains and rivers.
On the day Rénxū,
Shàngshū Right Chancellor Jiágǔ Qīngchén was enfeoffed as Dài Guó Gōng.
Wányán Shǒuzhēn, the Administrator of Xījīng, was made Píngzhāng Zhèngshì,
and enfeoffed as Xiāo Guó Gōng.
Shàngshū Right Chancellor Liú Wěi passed away.
Autumn, seventh month, on the day Xīnsì,
the Nánjīng Circuit Judicial Commissioner's office moved from Xǔzhōu to Nánjīng.
On the day Jǐchǒu,
an imperial decree stipulated that for officials of the third rank and above who passed away,
if they were relatives, virtuous, meritorious, or old retainers,
the Shàngshūshěng should immediately report it,
and discuss adding posthumous honors.
It was ordered that a "Lǐ Xìn Zhī Bǎo" seal
be recast in silver,
and then gilded with gold.
Xiāng, who was concurrently in charge of the Dàmùqīnfǔ, was made Pīmìshǐ.
Dǒng Shīzhōng, the Censor-in-Chief, and others were appointed envoys to congratulate the Sòng Emperor on his birthday.
Eighth month, on the day Jǐhài,
Pīmìshǐ Xiāng, leading the hundred officials, again requested the Emperor to accept an honorific title.
He refused.
On this day,
Jupiter and Venus were seen in daylight.
On the day Gēngzǐ,
a general amnesty was proclaimed.
On the day Jiǎchén,
the Emperor returned from Wànníng Gōng.
On the day Dīngwèi,
the shīdiàn ceremony was performed at the Confucius Temple,
facing north and bowing twice.
On the day Xīnhài,
the Guóshǐyuàn presented the Veritable Records of Shìzōng.
The Emperor wore his robe and belt,
presided at Rénzhèng Diàn,
descended from his seat,
and received them standing.
Ninth month, on the day Jiǎzǐ (1st day of the month),
which was Tiānshòu Jié,
the Emperor presided at Dà'ān Diàn,
and received congratulatory greetings from the princes, hundred officials, and envoys from Sòng, Gāolì, and Xià.
On the day Wùchén,
Cāizhī Zhèngshì Jiágǔ Héng was made Shàngshū Right Chancellor,
and Hùbù Shàngshū Mǎ Qí was made Cāizhī Zhèngshì.
An imperial edict instructed the Shàngshūshěng:
If scholars or commoners from the Dàdìng 29th year onwards submitted memorials,
and these concerned matters of great national or border importance that had already been implemented,
they could be specially appointed to one office;
if they benefited officials and commoners,
they would be given a reward according to the degree of benefit.
Dàgǔ, the Xīshànggéménshǐ, was made envoy for the Xià King's birthday.
On the day Gēngwǔ,
the Emperor went to Shānlíng,
and stopped at Fèngxiān Xiàn.
On the day Xīnwèi,
he worshipped Heaven west of the county seat.
On the day Rénshēn,
he offered sacrifices at the various imperial tombs.
On the day Guǐyǒu,
he went to Qiūshān.
Eleventh month, on the day Gēngwǔ,
Right Chancellor Qīngchén and Cāizhī Zhèngshì Chíguó submitted memorials requesting retirement.
An imperial edict graciously refused.
On the day Wùyín,
Hànlín Zhíxuégshì Wányán Kuāng and others were appointed envoys to congratulate Sòng on New Year's Day.
Kuāng was ordered to temporarily change his name to Bì,
to avoid a Sòng taboo.
On the day Rénwǔ,
trees were covered in ice.
On the day Bǐngxū,
an imperial edict ordered that the names of all officials who were punished for corruption or incompetence, and those who were promoted for integrity and ability,
be listed by circuit, capital, prefecture, sub-prefecture, and county,
and posted in public offices,
to serve as encouragement and warning.
On the day Gēngyín,
Lǐ Chúnyòu, the heir apparent of Xī Xià, sent an envoy to announce the death of his father.
Twelfth month, on the day Jiǎwǔ (1st day of the month),
Lǐ Chúnyòu of Xī Xià sent an envoy to present the late King Rénxiào's last memorial.
Dàxīng Fǔ was instructed to provide five shí of rice daily to Nuǎntāng Yuàn,
to aid the poor.
On the day Wùxū,
Zhèng Wáng Yǒngdǎo, the Military Commissioner of Dìngwǔ Jūn, was executed
for plotting rebellion.
On the day Jǐhài,
the relevant officials were instructed
to distribute Zhèng Wáng's assets among the princes,
and Zéguó Gōngzhǔ's assets among the princesses.
On the day Jiǎchén,
one Sīmǎ was added to each princely mansion.
Héshíliè Chéng was made envoy for Gāolì's birthday,
and Xīshànggéménshǐ Dàgǔ and others were made envoys for imperial sacrifices and condolences to Xī Xià.
On the day Gēngxū,
the Shàngshūshěng reported that many talented people had recently been obtained through the examination system,
and requested an increase in the number of jinshì to be selected in the current examination.
The Emperor approved,
and decreed that the relevant officials should not limit the number of candidates for the provincial examination.
On the day Jiǎyín,
the deity of Chángbái Shān was enfeoffed as Kāitiān Hóngshèng Dì.
On the day Bǐngchén,
the Emperor hunted in the near suburbs.
This year
was a year of great harvest.
In Xíng, Míng, Shēn, Jì, and the sixteen Mókè territories of the Héběi West Circuit,
wild silkworms formed cocoons.
Fifth year, spring, first month, on the day Guǐhài (1st day of the month),
envoys from Sòng, Gāolì, and Xià came to offer congratulations.
On the day Yǐchǒu,
Zhaórong Lǐ Shì was promoted to Shúfēi.
On the day Jǐsì,
for the first time, following the rites of the Táng and Sòng dynasties,
all governmental affairs were suspended on the Empress's death anniversary.
The Shàngshūshěng presented the "Qūtián Fǎ" (field-partitioning method).
An edict ordered that the suitability of the land be assessed,
and the convenience of the people be prioritized.
It also mentioned the disturbance caused by sending officials to encourage agriculture,
and ordered the Tíxíngsī to prohibit it.
On the day Yǐhài,
because Yèlǔ and Gǔshén first created the Jurchen script,
an imperial edict conferred additional posthumous honors upon them.
Following the precedent of Cāngjié's temple in Zhì,
sacrifices were offered to them in Nàlíhún Zhuāng in Shàngjīng.
Sacrifices were to be offered seasonally,
with their descendants performing the rites.
One official from the local circuit and the local chiliarch were to perform the spring and autumn sacrifices.
On the day Xīnsì,

former Zhōngdū Circuit Chief Transport Commissioner Wáng Jì recommended Wén Shāng from Cáizhōu, who had completed the final examination three times, stating that he was clear in his studies, upright in his conduct,
and fully qualified to provide counsel.
Former Héběi West Circuit Transport Commissioner Lǐ Yáng stated that Lǐ Jiǎng, a jinshì from Qìngyáng Fǔ, was pure in virtue and broadly learned,
and praised by his local community.
Lǐ Tiānqí from Jiàngzhōu and Kāng Jìnhóu from Yìngzhōu had repeatedly taken the palace examination,
and both possessed talent and virtue.
The Emperor said:
“Wén Shāng can be summoned.
Lǐ Jiǎng shall be granted half the salary of a master of records for life,
and the others shall be granted the status of jinshì.”
Guózǐ Jìjiǔ Liú Jī was sent
to enfeoff Lǐ Chúnyòu as King of Xī Xià.
On the day Dīnghài,
the Emperor visited the detached palace south of the city.
On the *dìngyǒu* day of the second month,
the regulations for rewarding and punishing officials based on their ability to encourage cultivation were first established.
The Shàngshū Shěng memorialized:
"The禮官 (lǐguān) say that the mourning period for Empress Xiàoyì has long passed.
It is fitting to rename Lóngqìng Gōng as Dōnggōng,
and Cíxùn Diàn as Chénghuá Diàn."
This was approved.
An edict was issued to seek out and purchase books missing from the Chóngwén Zǒngmù.
On the *wùxū* day,
sacrifices were offered to the deities of soil and grain.
Due to the death anniversary of Empress Xuānxiàn,
the *xīníng* sacrificial rites were used,
with musical instruments displayed but not played.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
Prince Yún, Cóng, passed away.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
the prime ministers requested the disbandment of the garrison troops on the northern frontier,
but this was denied.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
due to the urgent righteousness and generosity of Zhāng Juān of Qíhé Xiàn, Wáng Chēn of Jìyáng Xiàn, and Lǐ Qí of Hé Zhōu,
an edict was issued to restore their rights for life,
and it was also inscribed in the laws.
Yílà Mǐn, Xuānhuī Shǐ, and Chìzhǎn Shílǐgē, Hùbù Zhǔshì, were ordered to inspect the camps on the northern frontier,
and to plan for long-term strategies.
On the *rénshēn* day of the third month,
the restrictions on money were first established.
On the *gēngchén* day,
regular sacrifices to the masters of the sun, moon, wind, rain, and thunder were first established.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
the Hóngwén Yuàn was established
to translate and transcribe scriptures.
On the *rénchén* day, the first day of the fourth month of summer,
the emperor visited Běiyuàn.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,

an edict stated that the six gentlemen recommended from various circuits for their virtue and talent: Shí Qí of Zhuō Zhōu, Liú Zhì of Yúnzhōng, Lǐ Shēng of Zhèng Zhōu, Fù Lì of Ēn Zhōu, Zhào Zhì of Jìnán, and Tián Hùfāng of Xīngzhōng,
were all specially granted the title of *tóng jìnshì chūshēn*.
Wén Shāng was appointed Guózǐ Jiàoshòu,
and specially promoted to Dēngshì Láng.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
an edict commanded that from now on, gold and jade should not be used for the ornamentation of baskets, chests, beds, and couches.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
Wēndíhǎn Dí, Hànlín Dàizhì, was specially granted the titles of Hànlín Xuéshì Chéngzhǐ and Zhōngfèng Dàfū.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
the emperor visited Jǐngmíng Gōng.
Dǒng Shīzhōng, Jiǎ Shǒuqīan, and Lù Duó successively submitted two urgent memorials of remonstrance,
but they were not responded to.
On the *gēngwǔ* day of the fifth month,
the emperor arrived at Wūshísābā.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
Huán and Fǔ Prefectures suffered from drought,
so an envoy was sent to pray at Jìn Shān.
On the *rénchén* day of the sixth month,
the emperor went to Bīngjǐng.
On the *jǐhài* day,
the emperor went hunting.
He ascended Hútǔbái Shān,
poured wine and bowed twice.
Prince Cáo, Yǒngshēng, and others offered wine.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
the emperor worshipped Heaven,
and issued a partial amnesty for the Northwest Circuit.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
the emperor went to Cháshāqiū Shān.
In this month,
the former ruler of Sòng passed away.
On the *wùchén* day of the seventh month,
the emperor hunted at Huòchìhuǒ,
and shot two deer with one arrow.
On this day,
two hundred and twenty-two deer were caught,
and bestowed upon the accompanying officials in varying amounts.
On the *xīnsì* day,
the emperor arrived at Lǔwēnhéshībù.
On this day,
the emperor personally shot
four hundred and seventy-one wild goats.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
the emperor arrived at Bīngjǐng.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
it was Tiānshòu Jié.
A banquet was held in Shūguāng Diàn.
All accompanying officials and performers who received grace and promotion
received their imperial edicts in front of the palace.
At this time, after a long rain, the sky had just cleared,
and a dragon was seen dragging its tail among the clouds in front of the palace.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
there was hair in the imperial soup.
The emperor picked it up, looked at it, and discarded it,
warning his attendants not to speak of it.
On the *xīnhài* day of the eighth month,
the emperor returned from Jǐngmíng Gōng.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
the river breached the old dike at Yángwǔ,
flooding Fēngqiū and flowing eastward.
On the *dìngsì* day,
the imperial army accompanying the emperor to Shānhòu was granted silver and silk in varying amounts.
On the *wùwǔ* day, the first day of the ninth month,
it was Tiānshòu Jié.
Envoys from Sòng, Gāolì, and Xià came to offer congratulations.
On the *rénxū* day,
an order was given to increase and finalize the compensation for officials killed while apprehending bandits, and the official reward system.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
Wáng Rǔjiā and other officials of the Dūshuǐ Jiān were held responsible for the river breach,
each had two ranks of their official title removed,
were beaten seventy times with a rod,
and dismissed.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
the emperor held court in Ruìsī Diàn,
and the Tíxíng Shǐ from all circuits had an audience.
On the *wùchén* day,
it was first permitted for people to bid for the right to operate gold, silver, and copper mines wherever they were located.
Cānzhī Zhèngshì Mǎ Qí was ordered to inspect the river breach,
and was permitted to act according to discretion.
On the *rénshēn* day,
the Sòng ruler sent an envoy to announce his father's death.
On the *wùyín* day,
Nímánggǔ Jiàn, Zhī Dàxīng Fǔ Shì, and others were appointed as envoys to offer condolences and sacrifices to the Sòng state.
An imperial edict was sent to the Shàngshū Shěng,
ordering all officials to gather and discuss frontier defense matters.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
special grace was extended to eight former officials of Dōnggōng, including Wáng Bówēn, Sī Jīng, with promotions to varying ranks.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
an order was given to select thirty thousand troops from the nine circuits including Shàngjīng, and all other *mò* and *cí* areas,
to be dispatched next spring.
Furthermore, it was ordered that all circuits and the northern *zǔ*● should gather troops at Línhuáng in the summer of the sixth year.
In the tenth month of winter, on the *gēngyín* day,
the Yòu Chéngxiàng Jiágǔ Qīngchén and others submitted a memorial requesting the emperor to accept an honorific title,
but this was denied.
Sòng sent an envoy to present posthumous gifts.
On the *rényín* day,
Yòu Chéngxiàng Qīngchén again requested the emperor to accept an honorific title,
and Liú Jī, Guózǐ Jìjiǔ, also led the students of the Six Schools to submit a memorial requesting it,
but this was denied.
Hé Gé, Hùbù Yuánwàiláng, was dispatched to provide relief to households affected by the river breach.
On the *gēngxū* day,
Gāotuówò, wife of Zhāng Rǔbì, was executed
for plotting rebellion.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
the Shàngshū Shěng memorialized
to promote twelve upright officials observed by the Tíxíng Sī, including Lǐ Sù, the county clerk of Nánpí Xiàn.
Měngkuò Mándū, Zhǔbù of Dàxīng Fǔ, was also among those selected.
The emperor, knowing the person,
said:
"Mándū is a frivolous person.
Is it appropriate to promote him?
Rather than employing a frivolous person,
would it not be better to use someone honest and sincere?
Moreover, Mándū is a person of ordinary talent; even someone with extraordinary talent and wisdom should not be employed
for fear of corrupting customs, let alone an ordinary talent!
Investigate him again."
On the *wùwǔ* day, the first day of the intercalary month,
the Sòng ruler sent an envoy to announce his accession to the throne.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
the imperial princes and all officials each submitted memorials requesting the emperor to accept an honorific title,
but this was denied.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
Huāndū, Dài Guógōng, and four others were designated to share in the sacrifices at Shìzǔ Miàotíng.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
Wáng Qǐ, Tíxíng Shǐ for Hédōng South and North, and others, were appointed as envoys to congratulate the Sòng ruler on his accession.
On the *yǐhài* day,
the emperor hunted in the near suburbs.
On the *wùyín* day,
the emperor asked his輔臣 (fǔchén):
"How are the Confucius temples in various places?"
Shǒuzhēn, Píngzhāng Zhèngshì, replied:
"Various counties are currently discussing their establishment."
The emperor then said:
"Buddhist monks maintain their temples and images very strictly;
Daoists are next,
but only the Confucians are most neglectful of the Confucius temples."
Shǒuzhēn replied:
"Confucians cannot reside in schools for long,
unlike monks and Daoists who stay in temples and monasteries for extended periods."
The emperor said:
"Monks and Daoists exploit Buddhism and Daoism for profit,
hence they strive for grandeur and magnificence,
which encourages people to make more donations,
and thus it appears beautiful."
On the *gēngchén* day,
Cānzhī Zhèngshì Mǎ Qí returned from the xíngshěng,
and fully reported on the advantages and disadvantages of river defense.
His words are recorded in Mǎ Qí's biography.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
Àotún Zhōngxiào, Hànlín Dàizhì, was made acting Hùbù Shìláng,
and Wēn Fǎng, Tàifǔ Shàojiān, was made acting Gōngbù Shìláng,
to manage the affairs of the Hùbù and Gōngbù,
and to repair and manage river defenses.
Wányán Zhōng, Yǐnjìn Shǐ, was appointed as an envoy for the Xià state's birthday celebration.
On the *guǐsì* day of the eleventh month,
an edict was issued to abolish the hunting grounds protected at Zǐjīng Lǐng.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
Yílà Mǐn, Yòu Xuānhuī Shǐ, and others were appointed as envoys to congratulate Sòng on New Year's Day.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
Venus was seen in broad daylight.
In the twelfth month, on the day Xīnyǒu,
Píngzhāng Zhèngshì Wányán Shǒuzhēn was dismissed.
Ní máng gǔ Jiàn, who was Zhī Dàxīng Fǔshì, was made Cānzhī Zhèngshì.
Lǐ Jìngyì, Hùbù Lángzhōng, was made the envoy to Gāolí for the Emperor's birthday.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
this year's autumn tax was remitted for those affected by the Yellow River flood.
On the day Xīnsì,
an imperial decree ordered a reduction of one thousand men from the construction battalion of Xiū nèi sī
and five hundred men from Dūchéng Suǒ.
On the day Guǐwèi,
an imperial decree was sent to the Shàngshū Shěng,
stating that from now on, those who presented auspicious fungi (língzhī) or splendid grains (jiāhé) would be rewarded.
In the sixth year, on the first month of spring, Dīnghài朔,
envoys from Sòng, Gāolí, and Xià were received for the court congratulations.
On the day Gēngyín,
Venus was seen during the day.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
an imperial decree ordered the relevant authorities to grant land and residences to the household of Tiānshuǐ Jùngōng.
On the day Rénchén,
they went to Chūnshuǐ.
On the day Gēngxū,
the land expropriation in Shǎnxī was abolished.
On the day Xīnhài,
Xū Chíguó was admonished,
as the laborers gathered along the river
were feared to develop diseases and epidemics;
medical personnel should be appointed to care for them.
On the day Yǐmǎo,
they arrived at Yùlín.
In the second month, Dīngsì朔,
an imperial decree ordered the relevant authorities
not to forbid farmers from cultivating land near the temporary palace or hunting grounds.
On the day Jǐwèi,
the sacrifice to Gāoméi was first performed.
On the day Gēngwǔ,
they returned from Chūnshuǐ.
On the day Dīngchǒu,
an earthquake occurred in Jīngshī.
There was a heavy hailstorm,
the sky became dark during the day,
and the earthquake struck the owl-tail ornament on the right side of Yìngtiān Mén.
On the day Guǐwèi,
Sòng sent an envoy to express gratitude.
In the third month, Cǐxū朔,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
Bóshùlǔ Zǐyuán, Hànlín Zhíxuèshì, was concurrently appointed Yòusī Jiàn;
Tián Zhònglǐ, Jiānchá Yùshǐ, was appointed Zuǒ Shíyí;
Púsǎn Ékě, Hànlín Xiūzhuàn, was concurrently appointed Yòu Shíyí.
They were admonished, saying:
"The state establishes remonstrance officials
not for an empty name,
but to hold them responsible for actual results,
so that there may be some benefit.
You all have been selected by the imperial court
and placed in remonstrance positions.
Regarding the state's interests and harms, and the honesty or corruption of officials,
speak frankly without concealment.
Recently, Lù Duó was demoted,
which was due to other offenses.
You should not, because of his punishment,
become timid and refrain from speaking.
You must exert yourselves wholeheartedly
and not remain silent."
On the day Bǐngshēn,
they went to Wànníng Gōng.
On the day Wùxū,
for the transport of provisions to the northern frontier,
five thousand camels from Qúnmù Suǒ, the three Zhāotǎo Sī's Mèng'ān Móukè, Suící, and Diélà, Tánggǔ Bù's various Mò, Xī jīng, and Tàiyuán officials and common people were conscripted.
However, those commoners who made a living by camel transport were not to be conscripted.
Fifty thousand taels of silver and two hundred thirty-six thousand nine hundred strings of cash were provided for disbursement.

Fifty thousand taels of silver, two thousand eight hundred taels of gold bowls, one hundred taels of gold plaques, eight thousand taels of silver bowls, fifty thousand bolts of silk, one thousand lengths of miscellaneous colored fabrics, and four hundred forty-six sets of clothing were provided for rewards and incentives.
On the day Gēngzǐ,
Zái Jièrǎn and two others, who were recommended by the commandery for their talent and conduct, were specially granted the Jinshì jí dì degree;
Lǐ Zhēnggù and fifteen others were granted the Tóng Jinshì chūshēn degree.
In the summer, fourth month, on the day Guǐhài,
an imperial decree was sent to the relevant authorities,
stating that since the expansion and renovation of the Qūfù Xuānshèng Miào were complete,
the Yǎnshèng Gōng and others were granted the ritual robes for the three offerings and a complete set of ascending-song music.
Furthermore, former artisans of the Tàicháng Temple were sent to teach the Kǒng clan's descendants
to prepare for the sacrificial rites.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
Wūlíndá Yuàn, Shàngshū Zuǒchéng, was made Píngzhāng Zhèngshì;
Jiágǔ Héng, Yòuchéng, was made Shàngshū Zuǒchéng.
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
they went to Yùquán Shān.
On the day Wùyín,
since the river defense works were complete,
Xū Chíguó, Cānzhī Zhèngshì, was promoted two ranks;
Àotún Zhōngxiào, Hànlín Dàizhì, and thirty-six others were each promoted one rank;
Wáng Wéihàn, Huòjiā Lìng, and fifty-six others were each granted silver and silk of varying amounts.
On the day Gēngchén,
Jiágǔ Qīngchén, Shàngshū Yòuchéngxiàng, was made Zuǒchéngxiàng,
Jiānxiū Guóshǐ,
and enfeoffed as Mì Guógōng.
Xiāng, Pīmìshǐ, was made Shàngshū Yòuchéngxiàng,
and enfeoffed as Rèn Guógōng.
Xū Chíguó, Cānzhī Zhèngshì, was made Shàngshū Yòuchéng.
On the day Rénwǔ,
a handwritten imperial edict was given to the prime ministers,
admonishing them
for the unrefined customs
and the perfunctoriness of officials.
In the fifth month, on the day Bǐngxū,
an order was given to reduce ninety-four items of display at Wànníng Gōng.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
because troops were being dispatched,
Zhāng Wěi, Lǐbù Shàngshū, was sent to make a report to the ancestral temple and altars.
On the day Yǐwèi,
Háo Wáng Yǒngzhōng, Pàn Píngyáng Fǔshì, was granted death due to his crimes,
which also implicated his two sons.
On the day Dīngyǒu,
an imperial edict was issued throughout the realm.
On the day Yǐsì,
an imperial edict ordered all circuit's Mèng'ān Móukè to practice military skills during agricultural slack seasons;
the local Tíxíng Sī would investigate and punish those who were lazy.
On the day Gēngxū,
Zuǒchéngxiàng Jiágǔ Qīngchén was ordered to establish a traveling secretariat (xíngshěng) at Línhuáng Fǔ.
In the sixth month, on the day Bǐngchén,
Jiǎ Shǒuqīan, Yòu Jiànyì Dàfū, and Púsǎn Ékě, Yòu Shíyí, were dismissed and stripped of two ranks
for providing false answers during the inquiry regarding Háo Wáng Yǒngzhōng's case.
Sūn Jíkāng, Yùshǐ Zhōngchéng, Mēngkuò Húlà, Yòu Bǔquē, and Tián Zhònglǐ, Yòu Shíyí, were each fined twenty catties of gold.
On the day Bǐngyín,
Tángkuò Gòng, Pīmì Fùshǐ, was made Pīmìshǐ.
Due to prolonged rain,
a rain-stopping sacrifice (yíng) was performed.
On the day Gēngchén,
Venus traversed the sky.
On the day Xīnsì,
Zuǒchéngxiàng Qīngchén sent an envoy to present a victory report.
In the seventh month, on the day Bǐngshēn,
they visited Cáo Wáng Yǒngshēng's residence.
On the day Jiǎchén,
the dress regulations for civil and military officials of the sixth rank and above, attendants, those inherited from official positions, and registered literati were first established.
In the eighth month, on the day Jǐwèi,
the Chief of Yǎnzhōu was ordered to announce the completion of the newly renovated temple at Qūfù to Xuānshèng.
On the day Guǐhài,
they returned from Wànníng Gōng.
On the day Jǐsì,
based on Wēndūn Bóyīng's suggestion,
the Ministry of Rites was ordered to instruct school officials to lecture on the classics.
On the day Xīnwèi,
Wú Dǐngshū, Lìbù Shàngshū, and others were appointed as envoys to congratulate Sòng on its emperor's birthday.
On the day Rénshēn,
Dújī Yǒngzhōng, Xíngshěng Dūshì, came to report a victory.
On the day Yǐhài,
an imperial decree stipulated that if palace attendants committed bribery within three years after being assigned to an official post,
the official who originally recommended them would be implicated and punished,
not merely dismissed from office.
This was enacted as a regulation.
On the day Xīnsì,
Mùbō presented horses.
In the ninth month, Rénwǔ朔,
the Tiānshòu Festival,
envoys from Sòng, Gāolí,
and Xià came to offer congratulations.
On the day Jiǎshēn,
the spirit of Jìngníng Shān was enfeoffed as Zhèn'ān Gōng;
the spirit of Hūtú Bái Shān was enfeoffed as Ruìshèng Gōng.
On the day Bǐngxū,
Yīlà Zhòngfāng, Zhī Héjiān Fǔshì, was made Yùshǐ Dàfū.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
they went to Qiūshān.
Niángē Húshàng, Shàngshū Zuǒsī Lángzhōng, was made the envoy to the Xià state for its emperor's birthday.
In the winter, tenth month, on the day Bǐngchén,
they returned from Qiūshān.
On the day Dīngsì,
regarding the annual visits to Chūnshuǐ and Qiūshān,
where a memorial on the emperor's daily life was submitted every five days,
from now on, it would be submitted every ten days.
On the day Yǐhài,
Jiágǔ Héng, Shàngshū Zuǒchéng, was ordered to establish a traveling secretariat at Fǔzhōu;
five hundred men each from the imperial guard and the Wǔwèi army were ordered to accompany him,
and fifty million cash were also provided.
In the eleventh month, on the day Wùzǐ,
Jiágǔ Qīngchén, Zuǒchéngxiàng, was dismissed.
Xiāng, Yòuchéngxiàng, took over the duties of the traveling secretariat.
On the day Bǐngshēn,
Gēshíliè Zhēn, Xíngbù Shàngshū, and others were appointed as envoys to congratulate Sòng on the New Year.
On the day Rénzǐ,
the regulations for granting official positions to Mèng'ān Móukè who were discharged after guarding the frontier were first established.
The "shooting for grain" army was prohibited;
those performing duties were only allowed to form ranks and files,
and were not allowed to carry weapons or anything that could harm others.
On the day Jiǎchén,
a report of defeating the enemy at Wàngyún was received.
On the day Yǐsì,
Tángkuò Gòng, Pīmìshǐ, Yīlà Zhòngfāng, Yùshǐ Dàfū, Zhāng Wěi, Lǐbù Shàngshū, and twenty others were appointed as Jìyì Guān
to deliberate on all military matters.
On the day Wùshēn,
the system for promoting and dismissing county officials based on increased irrigated land was first established.
In the twelfth month, on the day Yǐmǎo,
an edict was issued to pacify the military and civilian population in the northern border regions.
Jiǎ Yì (賈益), Attendant Censor in the Court of Announcing Appeals, was appointed envoy for the Gāolì (高麗) Emperor's birthday.
Nàlán Fǎng (納蘭昉), Assistant Minister of the Board of Revenue, was appointed envoy for bestowing gifts.
On the day Wùwǔ,
Zhāng Wěi (張暐), Minister of Rites, and others presented the "Great Jīn (金) Ceremonial Rites."
On the day Dīngmǎo,
Zhào Bǐngwén (趙秉文), Attendant Hanlin Scholar, submitted a memorial discussing corruption and deceit.
On the day Yǐhài,
an edict increased the princely titles of the Five Sacred Mountains and Four Great Rivers.
On the day Gēngchén,
the Emperor visited the Imperial Garden to inspect military equipment.
This month,
Xiāng (襄), Right Chancellor, led Fùmǎ Dūwèi (駙馬都尉) Púsàn Kuí (僕散揆) and others in an advance towards Dàyánhuò (大鹽濼),
and divided their forces to attack and capture various strongholds.
In the spring, first month, on the Xīnsì new moon of Chéng'ān (承安)元年 (First Year),
envoys from Sòng (宋), Gāolì (高麗), and Xià (夏) were received in court for congratulations.
On the day Jiǎshēn,
Yīlà Dǔ (移剌覩), Prefect of the Dàyánhuò (大鹽濼) Imperial Pastures, and others were defeated by the forces of the Guǎngjílà (廣吉剌) tribe,
and died.
On the day Dīnghài,
Zhāng Shǒuyú (張守愚), Dormitory Head of the National University, submitted three essays on pacifying the borders,
and was specially appointed Professor of the same university,
and his essays were furthermore entrusted to the Imperial Historiography Office.
In the second month, on the day Jiǎzǐ,
officials were ordered to sacrifice to Gāoméi (高禖) according to the new rites.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
Xiāng (襄), Right Chancellor, and Héng (衡), Left Chancellor, returned from the front.
On the day Jǐsì,
they were again ordered to return to the army.
The Emperor went to the Southern Temporary Palace for the spring hunt.
On the day Jiǎxū,
he returned from the Temporary Palace.
This month,
the tiger tally was first created for dispatching troops.
In the third month, on the day Dīngyǒu,
the Emperor went to Wànníng Gōng (萬寧宮).
As there was no rain,
officials were dispatched to offer sacrifices from a distance to the Five Sacred Mountains, Four Great Rivers, and Four Seas in the northern suburbs.
On the day Guǐmǎo,
an imperial order was issued to the Department of State Affairs, stating:
"Although criminal cases have already been submitted and enacted,
it is feared there may be doubts or injustices among them.
Let them be deliberated upon again and reported.
Human life is of utmost importance,
and one cannot be too cautious."
On the day Jiǎchén,
Cānzhī Zhèngshì (參知政事) Ní máng Gǔ Jiàn (尼厖古鑑) was dispatched to pray for rain at the Altar of Land and Grain.
On the day Dīngwèi,
an envoy was again dispatched to pray at the Eastern Peak.
In the summer, fourth month, on the day Xīnhài,
Xū Chíguó (胥持國), Right Chancellor of the Department of State Affairs, was ordered to pray for rain at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
On the day Rénzǐ,
envoys were dispatched to review and decide on wrongful imprisonment cases.
Umbrellas and fans were prohibited in the capital.
On the day Wùwǔ,
the method of "plot farming" (qūzhǒngfǎ) was first implemented.
For commoners aged fifteen or above and under sixty who owned land,
each adult was to cultivate one *mǔ*.
On the day Yǐchǒu,
Yīlà Zhòngfāng (移剌仲方), Grand Censor, was ordered to pray for rain at the Altar of Land and Grain.
On the day Rénshēn,
Mǎ Qí (馬琪), Cānzhī Zhèngshì (參知政事), was ordered to pray for rain at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
On the day Jiǎxū,
the Department of State Affairs, based on Zhào Chéngyuán's (趙承元) words,
requested to retrieve the imperial certificate and seal of the Empress Dowager Xiàoyì (孝懿),
and then perform the posthumous title bestowing ceremony.
The ritual officials insisted that the decree honoring the Empress Dowager had already been announced domestically and abroad,
and there was no need for a retrieval ceremony;
this was followed.
On the day Wùyín,
due to the prolonged lack of rain, the Emperor
ordered Zhāng Wěi (張暐), Minister of Rites, to pray at the Northern Peak.
On the day Jǐmǎo,
officials were dispatched to offer sacrifices from a distance to the Five Sacred Mountains, Four Great Rivers, and Four Seas in the northern suburbs.
In the fifth month, on the Gēngchén new moon,
the Emperor inspected crops in the nearby suburbs,
and subsequently viewed the plot farms.
On the day Yǐyǒu,
due to the prolonged drought,
the market was moved.
On the day Gēngyín,
an edict restored the market to its usual location.
On the day Rénchén,
Niángé Zhōng (粘割忠), Vice Director of the Imperial Pharmacy, was appointed envoy for bestowing gifts to the Xià (夏) Kingdom.
On the day Yǐwèi,
Cānzhī Zhèngshì (參知政事) Ní máng Gǔ Jiàn (尼厖古鑑) passed away.
On the day Gēngzǐ,
there was sufficient rain.
In the sixth month, on the day Jiǎyín,
the Emperor, considering the people's difficulty in obtaining food,
decreed that one hundred thousand *shí* of stored grain be released and sold at a reduced price.
On the day Yǐchǒu,
in Píngjìn Xiàn (平晉縣), the silkworms of Lìtōng (利通)'s household spontaneously formed a bolt of silk,
seven *chǐ* one *cùn* five *fēn* long and
four *chǐ* nine *cùn* wide.
An edict bestowed ten bolts of plain silk.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
an imperial order was issued that from now on, elders (zhǎnglǎo), grand masters (dàshī), and great virtues (dàdé) would not be limited by age.
Elders and grand masters were permitted to ordain three disciples,
great virtues two disciples,
and ordained monks aged forty or above one disciple.
Those *shāmí* (沙彌) registered in the fifteenth year of Dàdìng (大定) who were sixty or above were all to receive ordination,
but were not permitted to ordain disciples.
Nuns (ní), Daoist priests (dàoshì), and Daoist priestesses (nǚguān) were to follow the same rules.
Yīlà Zhòngfāng (移剌仲方), Grand Censor, was dismissed.
On the day Gēngwǔ,
the Emperor visited Huánxiù Tíng (環秀亭) to inspect the crops.
On the day Guǐyǒu,
an edict stated that for areas under military equipment prohibition,
infantry archers should be selected from the grain-supplying military,
and cavalry archers should be selected from the surplus adult males in the Měng'ān Móukè (猛安謀克) military households.
If any of them caused harm to the common people,
they were to be judged and punished by their respective prefectures and counties.
In areas without Měng'ān households,
they were to be drawn from the surplus adult males of the garrisoned troops within two hundred *lǐ*,
and paid two *guàn* and one *shí* per month, like infantry archers.
In the seventh month, on the day Gēngchén,
the Emperor held court in the Zǐchén Diàn (紫宸殿),
received congratulations from the princes and all officials,
and bestowed wine upon the princes and chief ministers.
Officials were commanded
to place ten thousand jars of wine along the main thoroughfares
for the common people to drink freely.
On the day Yǐyǒu,
an imperial order stated that henceforth, when envoys from Gāolì (高麗) and Xià (夏) had an audience and made presentations,
the newly established interpreters for various countries, wearing official attire, were to ascend the hall with the Minister of the Palace Gate to monitor the proceedings.
Officials were ordered to collect and bury the bones of those who died in battle in the northwest region.
In the eighth month, on the day Jǐyǒu,
the Emperor hunted in the nearby suburbs.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
he visited Yùquán Shān (玉泉山).
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
the date for the suburban sacrifice was announced to the public.
On the day Wùchén,
the Emperor returned from Wànníng Gōng (萬寧宮).
Dǒng Shīzhōng (董師中), Transport Commissioner of the Western Shǎnxī (陝西) Circuit, was appointed Grand Censor.
On the day Guǐyǒu,
Héng (衡), Left Chancellor, went into mourning for his father.
In the ninth month, on the Dīngchǒu new moon,
on the Tiānshòu (天壽) Festival,
envoys from Sòng (宋), Gāolì (高麗), and Xià (夏) came to offer congratulations.
The Emperor visited Tiāncháng Guān (天長觀).
On the day Xīnsì,
Xiāng (襄), Right Chancellor, was appointed Left Chancellor,
supervised the compilation of national history,
and was enfeoffed as Prince of Chángshān (常山) Commandery.
On the day Rénwǔ,
Xiāng (襄) was bestowed with one hundred jars of wine.
Venus was seen in daylight.
On the day Guǐwèi,
the capital's residents presented three thousand one hundred bottles of wine,
and an edict ordered them to be bestowed upon the military officials in the northern border regions.
Zhāng Sì (張嗣), Minister of Personnel, and others were appointed envoys to congratulate the Sòng (宋) Emperor on his birthday.
On the day Guǐsì,
Héng (衡), Left Chancellor, resumed his duties.
On the day Dīngyǒu,
Biàn (卞), Prefect of Dàxīng Fǔ (大興府), and Guō Zhù (郭鑄), Vice Prefect, were each given forty strokes of the cane
for arbitrarily arresting and questioning a chief minister.
On the day Xīnchǒu,
Púsàn Kuí (僕散揆), Pacification Commissioner of the Southwest Circuit, returned from the army.
On the day Yǐsì,
Wūgǔlùn Dájíbù (烏古論達吉不), Censor of the Imperial Academy, was appointed envoy for the Xià (夏) Kingdom's birthday.
In the winter, tenth month, on the Bǐngwǔ new moon,
an edict ordered the selection of eight hundred imperial guards to garrison Fǔzhōu (撫州).
On the day Gēngxū,
Xiāng (襄), Left Chancellor, was ordered to establish a Branch Secretariat in Běijīng (北京),
and Wányán Kuāng (完顏匡), Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, to establish a Branch Bureau in Fǔzhōu (撫州).
On the day Bǐngchén,
a joint sacrifice was offered at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
In the eleventh month, on the day Wùzǐ,
Cānzhī Zhèngshì (參知政事) Mǎ Qí (馬琪) was dismissed.
On the day Gēngyín,
Tèmǎn Qúnmù (特滿羣牧) Qìdān (契丹) Suǒ (索) and Déshòu (德壽) rebelled,
but were defeated by the Tàizhōu (泰州) army.
Dǒng Shīzhōng (董師中), Grand Censor, and Yì (裔), Defender of Běijīng (北京), were both appointed Cānzhī Zhèngshì (參知政事).
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
Chóngdào (崇道), Military Commissioner of the Shǎnxī (陝西) Circuit, and others were appointed envoys to congratulate Sòng (宋) on New Year's Day.
On the day Dīngyǒu,
a morning sacrifice was offered at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
On the day Wùxū,
rites were performed in the southern suburbs,
a general amnesty was declared,
and the reign era was changed.
On the day Jǐhài,
Cáo Wáng (曹王) Yǒngshēng (永升) led the imperial princes and all officials in offering congratulations.
On the day Guǐmǎo,
officials were ordered to pray for snow,
and an official was also dispatched to pray at the Eastern Peak.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day of the twelfth month,
the Grand Councilor Tángkuò Gòng (唐括貢) led the officials in requesting that an honorary title be conferred upon the emperor,
but this was not granted.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
Lǐ Rénbuì (李仁惠), the Administrator of the Bureau of Imperial Physicians and Palace Attendants, was dispatched to reward and bestow gifts upon the soldiers on the northern frontier.
Eleven thousand people received official appointments,
and nearly twenty thousand people received awards.
In total, this cost two hundred thousand *liǎng* of silver, fifty thousand *pǐ* of silk, and three hundred and twenty thousand *guàn* of cash.
On the *gēngxū* day,
Ābùhǎn Dégāng (阿不罕德剛), the Deputy Administrator of the Court of Appeals, was appointed as the birthday envoy to the Gāolí (高麗) Kingdom.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
the Grand Councilor Tángkuò Gòng (唐括貢) again led the officials in requesting that an honorary title be conferred upon the emperor,
but this was not granted.
In the second year, on the *yǐhài* day, the first day of the first month of spring,
envoys from Sòng (宋), Gāolí (高麗), and Xià (夏) came to offer congratulations.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
an imperial edict stipulated that officials who committed corruption or embezzlement were not allowed to appeal to their colleagues.
On the *dīnghài* day,
