the emperor went to Ānzhōu (安州) for the spring hunt.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
the emperor returned from the spring hunt.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
the Sòng (宋) emperor sent an envoy to announce the mourning
for his deceased empress dowager.
On the *dīngsì* day of the second month,
an imperial edict was issued, stating that from now on, for every official rank an official loses due to corruption,
they shall be confined to the palace for one year.
On this day,
Venus was seen in broad daylight,
traversing the sky.
In this month,
Kǒng Yuáncuò (孔元措), the Yǎnshèng Gōng (衍聖公) by hereditary title, was specially commanded to also hold the hereditary position of Magistrate of Qūfù (曲阜).
On the *jǐmǎo* day of the third month,
the imperial princes and all officials again requested that an honorary title be conferred upon the emperor,
but this was not granted.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
Wēn Fǎng (溫昉), the Vice Minister of the Ministry of Revenue, was ordered to wear the golden tiger tally
and act as Minister of the Six Ministries in Fúzhōu (撫州).
On the *gēngyín* day,
the emperor visited the West Garden to inspect military weapons.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
the criteria for recommending individuals of virtue and talent were first established.
On the *guǐsì* day,
Wūlíndá Yuàn (烏林荅愿), the Minister of the Right, was dismissed.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
the Grand Councilor Tángkuò Gòng (唐括貢) led the officials in requesting that an honorary title be conferred upon the emperor,
but this was not granted.
Yì (裔), the Assistant Administrator of Governmental Affairs, was appointed as the Left Chancellor in charge of the regional administration in Běijīng (北京).
[一一]
On the *jiǎyín* day of the fourth month of summer,
the emperor went to Wànníng Gōng (萬寧宮).
On the *bǐngchén* day,
the Ministry of Rites was ordered to pray for rain
and offer sacrifices from afar to the Five Sacred Mountains, the Four Sacred Rivers, and the Four Seas in the northern suburbs.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
prayers for rain were offered to the altars of the land and grain.
The Department of State Affairs reported,
“In recent years, the northern frontier has required considerable mobilization.
We request the issuance of blank ordination certificates for Buddhist and Daoist monks and honorary titles for Purple-robed Teachers to aid military provisions.”
This was approved.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
imperial princes began to use Jùrche (女直) script for imperial edicts.
On the *jiǎxū* day, the first day of the fifth month,
the emperor instructed his chief ministers, saying:
“Recently, due to military needs,
taxes have been levied along the routes.
Local officials, disregarding the urgency,
hastened to collect taxes,
causing the people to spend several times over,
and clerks further exploited this with their oppressive actions.
Order the Judicial Intendant Office to investigate this thoroughly.”
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
officials were gathered at the Department of State Affairs,
and the imperial edict addressed them, saying:
“Currently, discipline is not established,
officials are lax,
procrastinating and negligent,
which has become a habitual malpractice.
Many officials seek fame through trivial good deeds,
calculating their own security,
but what does the state gain from this?
As for those who yield to personal feelings and bend the law,
the clerks in the ministries are particularly egregious.
The Department of State Affairs should admonish them all.”
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
Yì (裔), the Assistant Administrator of Governmental Affairs for the Běijīng (北京) regional administration, was relocated to Línhuáng Fǔ (臨潢府).
On the *gēngchén* day,
Fúzhōu (撫州) was elevated to Zhènníng Jūn (鎮寧軍).
As the rain was sufficient,
a thanksgiving sacrifice was offered to the altars of the land and grain.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
sacrifices were offered from afar to the Five Sacred Mountains, the Four Sacred Rivers, and the Four Seas in the northern suburbs.
On the *dīnghài* day,
Xiāng (襄), the Left Chancellor, went to Línhuáng Fǔ (臨潢府).
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
an imperial prince was born.
On the *gēngyín* day,
an edict was issued to those within and outside the capital,
commuting death sentences
and releasing prisoners below the rank of penal servitude.
On the *yǐsì* day of the sixth month,
Zhāng Wěi (張暐), the Minister of Rites, was ordered to perform the sacrifice to Gāoméi (高禖).
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
there was hail.
On the *wùshēn* day,
Wáng Zūngǔ (王遵古), the Governor of Chéngzhōu (澄州), was appointed as a Scholar of the Hanlin Academy for Direct Admonition.
It was further decreed that he should not be involved in drafting documents;
if he was on duty, he should report to the emperor;
and during continuous rain,
he was exempt from duty,
due to Wáng Zūngǔ’s (王遵古) old age
and his past service as an imperial lecturer.
On the *gēngxū* day,
an edict ordered the cessation of work on Yáoguāng Diàn (瑤光殿).
On the *jiǎyín* day,
the Military Commissioner of Quánzhōu (全州) Pán'ān Jūn (盤安軍) was established,
with its seat of government in Ānfēng Xiàn (安豐縣).
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
the imperial prince was enfeoffed as Shòu Wáng (壽王).
On the *jiǎwǔ* day of the intercalary month,
the emperor went out of the West Héngmén (橫門) to inspect the crops.
On the *rénchén* day, the first day of the seventh month of autumn,
the emperor visited Tiāncháng Guàn (天長觀)
to establish a grand universal ritual (*pǔtiān dàjiào*).
Slaughtering was prohibited for seven days,
no punishments were to be reported,
and all offices temporarily suspended judgments and penalties.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
Liú Kuì (劉頍), the Grand Prefect of the Western Palace Gates, was ordered to bestow a banquet upon Yì (裔), the Assistant Administrator of Governmental Affairs, at the regional administration office.
On the *wùchén* day,
on the occasion of the Tiānshòu (天壽) Festival,
the emperor held court in the Zǐchén Diàn (紫宸殿).
On the *gēngchén* day of the eighth month,
an edict stated that proposals submitted by deliberative officials
should directly address advantages and disadvantages,
without using flowery language.
On the *xīnsì* day,
due to the unsettled border situation,
an edict was issued to gather officials of the sixth rank and above at the Department of State Affairs
[一二] to discuss strategies for attack and defense.
All civilian and military officials, regardless of their rank,
if they possessed strategies, talent, or military prowess,
or were skilled in logistics,
were each to recommend three to five individuals for selection and use.
They were not to hesitate or hold back their thoughts,
and were expected to submit sealed memorials within five days.
There were eighty-four participants in the discussions;
five spoke of attack,
forty-six of defense,
and thirty-three of both attack and defense.
They were summoned for an imperial audience in the Ruìsī Diàn (睿思殿),
where discussions and debates lasted for a long time.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
the emperor returned from Wànníng Gōng (萬寧宮).
On the *bǐngxū* day,
Xiāng (襄), the Left Chancellor, was appointed as the Left Vice Marshal;
Dǒng Shīzhōng (董師中), Assistant Administrator of Governmental Affairs, was appointed as the Left Vice Minister of the Department of State Affairs;
the Left Supervisor of the Imperial Secretariat ●
[一三] was appointed as the Right Vice Minister of the Department of State Affairs;
Yáng Bótōng (楊伯通), the Minister of Revenue, was appointed as Assistant Administrator of Governmental Affairs.
Jiágǔ Héng (夾谷衡), the Left Vice Minister of the Department of State Affairs, was dismissed.
Xū Chíguó (胥持國), the Right Vice Minister, retired.
On the *gēngyín* day,
Yì (裔), the Assistant Administrator of Governmental Affairs, was dismissed.
Tángkuò Gòng (唐括貢), the Grand Councilor, retired.
On the *rénchén* day,
Xiāng (襄), the Left Vice Marshal, was appointed as Grand Councilor and Minister of the Right.
On the *xīnchǒu* day, the first day of the ninth month,
on the occasion of the Tiānshòu (天壽) Festival,
envoys from Sòng (宋), Gāolí (高麗), and Xià (夏) came to offer congratulations.
On the *rénchén* day,
officials were dispatched to various routes including Shàngjīng (上京), Dōngjīng (東京), Běijīng (北京), Xiánpíng (咸平), Línhuáng (臨潢), and Xījīng (西京) to recruit Han soldiers;
if insufficient, conscription would make up the deficit.
On the *yǐsì* day,
when the Xià (夏) envoy made his farewell,
an imperial edict was issued in reply, promising to reopen the markets in Bǎo'ān (保安) and Lánzhōu (蘭州).
On the *dīngwèi* day,
Wányán Yú (完顏愈), the Administrator of Guīdé Fǔ (歸德府), was appointed as the envoy to congratulate Sòng (宋) on the emperor’s birthday.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
Niángē Wòtèlà (粘割斡特剌), the Grand Administrator of Shàngjīng (上京), was appointed as Minister of the Right.
[一四] On the *xīnyǒu* day,
Xiāng (襄), the Grand Councilor and Minister of the Right,
and Xū Chíguó (胥持國), the Administrator of Dàxīng Fǔ (大興府), were appointed as Deputy Grand Councilors
[一五] and acting Assistant Administrators of Governmental Affairs,
respectively, to serve in the regional administration in Běijīng (北京).
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
the Bureau of Military Manufactures (*jūnqì jiān*) was first established,
responsible for managing military weapons,
ranking below the Bureau of Imperial Works (*shǎofǔ jiān*).
It established the Armory Department (*jiǎfáng shǔ*) and the Weaponry Department (*lìqì shǔ*) under its jurisdiction.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
officials were dispatched to the Eastern, Western, and Běijīng (北京) routes,
Héběi (河北) routes,
In winter, in the tenth month, on the *gēngwǔ* (庚午) day, which was the first day of the month,
the Jiǎngyìsuǒ (講議所) was initially established with ten officials.
They collectively deliberated on money and grain matters.
Sūn Duó (孫鐸), the Transporter-in-chief of Zhōngdū (中都) Circuit, and Gāo Rǔlì (高汝礪), the Assistant Minister of Revenue, were appointed to it.
On the *gēngchén* (庚辰) day,
the Shàngshūshěng (尚書省) reported
that a dispatch from the Gāolì (高麗) kingdom stated
that its king, due to old age and illness,
had ordered his younger brother, Wáng Háo (王晧), to manage the affairs of state.
On the *rénwǔ* (壬午) day,
the Shàngshūshěng (尚書省) conducted a comprehensive census (*tuīpái*).
On the *dīnghài* (丁亥) day,
the Imperial Prince Shòuwáng (壽王) passed away.
On the *rénchén* (壬辰) day,
an imperial edict commended and encouraged the meritorious officers and soldiers, including Púsǎn Kuí (僕散揆), the Pacification Commissioner of the Southwest Circuit.
On the *jiǎwǔ* (甲午) day,
there was a heavy snowfall.
A thousand *shí* (石) of rice were granted to the Pǔjìyuàn (普濟院),
with orders to make congee for the poor.
On the *bǐngshēn* (丙申) day,
Méngkuò Rénběn (蒙括仁本), an Assistant Minister of Rites, was made envoy for the Xià (夏) kingdom's birthday celebration.
In the eleventh month, on the *jiǎchén* (甲辰) day,
it was the winter solstice.
Sacrifices were offered at the Southern Suburb.
On the *yǐsì* (乙巳) day,
due to the high price of firewood,
an imperial decree ordered that there be no prohibition on gathering firewood within the imperial hunting grounds.
On the *rénzǐ* (壬子) day,
the Shàngshūshěng (尚書省) was instructed:
since the *mèng'ān* (猛安) and *móukè* (謀克) were not subordinate to the Tíxíngsī (提刑司),
the Censor-in-chief should be ordered to investigate their good and bad conduct.
On the *gēngshēn* (庚申) day,
Yì (裔), the Resident Governor of Běijīng (北京), was flogged one hundred strokes
and dismissed from office
for dereliction of duty in the Traveling Secretariat.
Nàlán Fǎng (納蘭昉), the Right Remonstrance Grand Master, was flogged ninety strokes,
demoted two ranks,
and dismissed.
On the *jiǎzǐ* (甲子) day,
the Grand Councilors were instructed, saying:
“I reside in the imperial palace,
making it difficult to know everything about the common people.
If the Grand Councilors do not receive guests,
how can they know the benefits and harms among the common people?”
In the twelfth month, on the *jǐsì* (己巳) day, which was the first day of the month,
an imperial decree ordered the Yùshǐtái (御史臺) to investigate and expose sycophantic and opportunistic individuals with proven misconduct.
On the *jǐmǎo* (己卯) day,
the "Chéng'ān Bǎohuò" (承安寶貨) [coins] were first minted.
On the *guǐwèi* (癸未) day,
Shàngguān Yú (上官瑜), Assistant Minister of Revenue, was sent to thoroughly investigate the fugitives in Xījīng (西京)
and to encourage and lead the military and civilians along the border in farming.
Lǐ Jìngyì (李敬yì), a Director in the Ministry of Revenue, was to plan and arrange agricultural affairs in the Línpáng (臨潢) and other circuits.
On the *yǐyǒu* (乙酉) day,
the Grand Councilors were instructed
that henceforth, in cases of floods, droughts, locusts, and outbreaks of banditry,
the Tíxíngsī (提刑司) should be ordered to make advance plans.
On the *wùzǐ* (戊zǐ) day,
instructions were given to the officers and soldiers of the Southwest Circuit.
On the *gēngyín* (庚yín) day,
Yùwáng Yǒngchéng (豫王永成) presented eighty horses.
An imperial edict was bestowed, commending and encouraging him,
addressing him as "Imperial Uncle Yùwáng" (皇叔豫王) without using his personal name.
Collation Notes
Basic Annals, Chapter 11, Section 3
In the third year, in spring, in the first month, on the *jǐhài* (己亥) day, which was the first day of the month,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the *xīnchǒu* (辛丑) day,
the Sòng (宋) and Xià (夏) sent envoys to offer congratulations.
On the *guǐmǎo* (癸卯) day,
the relevant authorities were instructed:
when hosting, accompanying, and dispatching envoys,
do not seek to win arguments with words,
but rather strive to maintain decorum.
The envoys dispatched must also be the right persons for the task.
On the *yǐmǎo* (乙卯) day,
an imperial edict abolished the Jiǎngyìsuǒ (講議所).
On the *bǐngchén* (丙辰) day,
they went to the spring waters south of the city.
On the *dīngsì* (丁巳) day,
the Tíxíngsī (提刑司) of the Shàngjīng (上京) and Dōngjīng (東京) circuits were merged into one.
The Tíxíngshǐ (提刑使) and its Deputy concurrently served as Ānfǔshǐ (安撫使) and Deputy.
The Ānfǔ (安撫) specialized in training in military affairs,
without changing their original customs.
On the *jǐwèi* (己未) day,
the traveling palace south of the capital was named Jiànchūn (建春).
On the *jiǎzǐ* (甲zǐ) day,
they returned from the spring waters.
On the *yǐchǒu* (乙丑) day,
the Sòng (宋) ruler, due to the mourning for his grandmother,
sent an envoy to announce the sorrow.
In the second month, on the *jǐsì* (己巳) day, which was the first day of the month,
they visited Jiànchūngōng (建春宮).
On the *xīnsì* (辛巳) day,
the Grand Councilors were instructed, saying:
“From now on, when there are vacancies for officials, both internal and external,
if there are talented individuals suitable for the position,
even if their seniority is not yet sufficient,
they should still be reported.
Even if they are relatives or old acquaintances,
there should be no avoidance.”
Wūlíndá Tiānyì (烏林荅天益) and others, including the Commander-in-chief of the Wǔwèijūn (武衞軍), were made envoys to convey condolences to the Sòng (宋).
On the *jiǎshēn* (甲申) day,
they returned from Jiànchūngōng (建春宮).
On the *bǐngxū* (丙戌) day,
Xié Chū (斜出) came and submitted to the court.
On the *xīnmǎo* (辛卯) day,
Zhāngé Wòtèlá (粘割斡特剌), the Chancellor of the Privy Council, passed away.
In the third month, on the *wùxū* (戊戌) day,
Zhāng Wěi (張暐), Minister of Rites, was made Censor-in-chief.
On the *rényín* (壬寅) day,
the salt monopoly was re-established.
On the *jiǎyín* (甲寅) day,
they went to Wànnínggōng (萬寧宮).
On the *dīngsì* (丁巳) day,
an imperial decree ordered that regarding bandits in all locations,
they should not be misrepresented as strong when they are thieves,
nor should many be reported as few,
nor should existence be reported as non-existence.
Gatherings of thirty or more people should be reported to the throne.
Violators would be flogged one hundred strokes.
On the *bǐngyín* (丙寅) day,
King Wáng Háo (王晧) of Gāolì (高麗), having appointed his younger brother, Wáng Háo (王晧), to manage the affairs of state,
sent an envoy to present a memorial and announce this.
In summer, in the fourth month, on the *wùchén* (戊辰) day, which was the first day of the month,
the relevant authorities were instructed
that if the Grand Councilors encountered rain,
they could use the palace corridors for entry and exit.
On the *bǐngshēn* (丙申) day,
the Yùshǐtái (御史臺) was instructed, saying:
“Although officials of all ranks in the court possess talent,
they are mostly perfunctory and negligent.
I detest this greatly.
Therefore, investigate and report them.
Officials who are found by the Tíxíngsī (提刑司) to be clean, capable, corrupt, or abusive
should all be reported directly to the throne.
Other matters may be reported indirectly.”
Sūn Yǔ (孫俁), an Investigating Censor, was made envoy to inquire of King Wáng Háo (王晧) of Gāolì (高麗).
In the fifth month, on the *gēngzǐ* (庚zǐ) day,
Zhāng Rǔfāng (張汝方), the Right Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, was demoted two ranks
for leaking court deliberations.
On the *rényín* (壬寅) day,
archery at willows and polo were performed,
and the common people were allowed to watch.
On the *wùshēn* (戊shēn) day,
Yílà Yù (移剌郁), the Director of the Bureau of Guests, was made envoy for the Xià (夏) kingdom's birthday celebration.
On the *jiǎzǐ* (甲zǐ) day,
Yáng Bótōng (楊伯通), the Minister of Political Affairs, submitted a memorial requesting retirement,
but it was not granted.
In autumn, in the seventh month, on the *bǐngwǔ* (丙wǔ) day,
they visited Xiāngshān (香山).
On the *jǐyǒu* (己yǒu) day,
they went to Wànnínggōng (萬寧宮).
On the *jiǎyín* (甲yín) day,
they returned to the palace.
In the eighth month, on the *xīnwèi* (辛wèi) day,
they hunted in the nearby suburbs.
On the *guǐyǒu* (癸yǒu) day,
they hunted at Xiāngshān (香山).
On the *wùyín* (戊yín) day,
they went to Wànnínggōng (萬寧宮).
On the *gēngchén* (庚chén) day,
Shí Héshang (石和尚), a bodyguard, was appointed Marshal of Ten Thousand Households,
leading eight hundred imperial guards and sixteen hundred Wǔwèijūn (武衞軍) to garrison the Northwest Circuit.
On the *guǐwèi* (癸wèi) day,
they returned to the palace.
The Sòng (宋) sent an envoy to express gratitude.
In the ninth month, on the *bǐngshēn* (丙shēn) day, which was the first day of the month,
on Tiānshòujié (天壽節),
the Sòng (宋) and Xià (夏) sent envoys to offer congratulations.
Sūn Duó (孫鐸) and others, including the Chief Transporter of Zhōngdū (中都) Circuit, were made envoys to congratulate the Sòng (宋) on their birthday.
On the *yǐsì* (乙sì) day,
they hunted in the nearby suburbs.
On the *gēngxū* (庚xū) day,
Yáng Bótōng (楊伯通), the Minister of Political Affairs, again submitted a memorial requesting retirement,
but it was not granted.
On the *wùwǔ* (戊wǔ) day,
Mù Bō (木波) presented horses.
In winter, in the tenth month, on the *gēngwǔ* (庚wǔ) day,
they hunted in the nearby suburbs.
On the *guǐwèi* (癸wèi) day,
the Xíngshūmìyuàn (行樞密院) reported that Xié Chū (斜出) and others requested to open a trade mart at Xiá Lǐniǎo (轄里裊),
which was granted.
On the *dīnghài* (丁hài) day,
the amount of cash that officials and commoners could retain was set.
Húiyìwù (回易務) were established,
and a new method for circulating paper currency was implemented.
In the eleventh month, on the Dīngyǒu day,
Púmìshǐ (Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs) concurrently Píngzhāng Zhèngshì (Grand Counselor) Xiāng arrived from the army.
On the Guǐmǎo day,
he was appointed Shàngshū Zuǒ Chéngxiàng (Left Grand Counselor of the Department of State Affairs)
and Supervisor for the Compilation of National History.
On the Dīngwèi day,
Tàicháng Qīng (Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices) Yáng Tíngyún and others were appointed envoys to congratulate Sòng on the New Year.
On the Wùshēn day,
an imperial edict commended and encouraged Púmì Fùshǐ (Deputy Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs) Jiágǔ Héng and the officers and soldiers below him.
On the Xīnhài day,
the law on private solicitations was finalized.
The regulations for promotions and rewards for officials and officers at the front were also finalized.
As border affairs were settled,
an edict was issued to all under heaven,
reducing death sentences,
and releasing those sentenced to banishment or lesser penalties.
The Left Chéngxiàng (Grand Counselor) Xiāng and the officers and soldiers below him were granted gold and silk with varying amounts.
On the Jiǎyín day,
there was a winter hunt.
In the twelfth month, on the Jiǎzǐ day, which was the first day of the month,
the hunt was held in Suānzǎo Lín.
Due to strong wind and cold,
the hunt was called off.
Over five hundred people froze to death.
On the Jǐsì day,
the court returned to the capital.
On the Bǐngxū day,
Shàngshū Yòu Chéng (Right Grand Counselor of the Department of State Affairs) ● was dismissed.
The de facto ruler of Gāolí (Goryeo), King Yǎn, sent an envoy to present a memorial announcing the news.
In the fourth year, in the first month of spring, on the Guǐsì day, which was the first day of the month,
Sòng and Xià sent envoys to offer congratulations.
On the Yǐsì day,
Shàngshū Zuǒ Chéng (Left Grand Counselor of the Department of State Affairs) Dǒng Shīzhōng retired.
On the Xīnyǒu day,
Jiānchá Yùshǐ (Investigating Censor) Jī Duānxiū was handed over to the authorities for making baseless statements.
Shàngshū Zuǒ Chéngxiàng (Left Grand Counselor of the Department of State Affairs) Xiāng was made Sīkōng (Minister of Works),
his duties remaining as before.
Púmì Fùshǐ (Deputy Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs) Jiágǔ Héng was made Píngzhāng Zhèngshì (Grand Counselor)
and enfeoffed as the Duke of Yīngguó.
Former Zhī Jìnán Fǔ Shì (Prefect of Jìnán Prefecture) Zhāng Wàngōng was reinstated as Píngzhāng Zhèngshì (Grand Counselor)
and enfeoffed as the Duke of Shòuguó.
Yáng Bótōng was made Shàngshū Zuǒ Chéng (Left Grand Counselor of the Department of State Affairs).
Qiān Púmìyuàn Shì (Manager of the Bureau of Military Affairs) Wányán Kuāng was made Shàngshū Yòu Chéng (Right Grand Counselor of the Department of State Affairs).
In the second month, on the Yǐchǒu day,
the emperor proceeded to Jiànchūn Gōng for spring fishing.
On the Jǐsì day,
he returned to the palace.
On the Gēngwǔ day,
he presided at Xuānhuá Mén
to observe the reception of the Buddha.
On the Xīnwèi day,
he proceeded to Jiànchūn Gōng.
Jī Duānxiū's crime was pardoned,
and he was ordered to remain at home awaiting further orders.
Sīkōng (Minister of Works) Xiāng reported that
Xīnán Lù Zhāotǎoshǐ (Pacification Commissioner of the Southwest Circuit) Púsǎn Kuí had achieved merit in defending the borders.
He was summoned to the court,
and Zhī Xīngzhōng Fǔ Shì (Prefect of Xīngzhōng Prefecture) Héshíliè Zǐrén was appointed to replace him.
On the Rénshēn day,
the officials concerned were instructed that
starting from the first day of the third month,
one official from the third to fifth ranks should be rotated for audience every ten days,
and officials of the sixth rank would also be granted audience in sequence.
The Tái (Censorate) and Jiàn (Remonstrance Bureau) officials were not to participate.
If there was any matter to report,
they could meet with the rotating officials.
If there was no one to meet face-to-face, submitting memorials was also permitted.
On the Yǐhài day,
the court returned to the palace.
On the Wùyín day,
the emperor proceeded to Jiànchūn Gōng.
On the Gēngchén day,
the emperor issued an edict to the Diǎnjiǎn Sī (Inspection Bureau) saying:
"From Púhé to Chánghé and east of Xìhé,
where I often travel,
officials should purchase the land through peaceful means
and let the common people cultivate it,
and their land taxes should be exempted."
On the Jiǎshēn day,
the court returned to the palace.
On the Yǐyǒu day,
Xīnán Lù Zhāotǎoshǐ (Pacification Commissioner of the Southwest Circuit) Púsǎn Kuí was appointed Cānzhī Zhèngshì (Policy Advisor).
Jī Duānxiū was reinstated as Tàixué Bóshì (Erudite of the Imperial Academy).
The emperor proceeded to Jiànchūn Gōng.
On the Wùzǐ day,
the court returned to the palace.
In the third month, on the Dīngyǒu day,
Tóngpàn Dàmùqīn Fǔ Shì (Associate Administrator of the Grand Bureau of Imperial Kin) Zōng Hào was appointed Púmìshǐ (Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs)
and enfeoffed as the Duke of Chóngguó.
On the Jǐhài day,
the emperor proceeded to Jiànchūn Gōng.
An envoy was dispatched to confer the title of King of Gāolí (Goryeo) upon King Yǎn.

Hùbù Shàngshū (Minister of the Ministry of Revenue) Sūn Duó, Lángzhōng (Director) Lǐ Zhònglüè, and Guózǐ Jìjiǔ (Libationer of the Directorate of Education) Zhào Chén began rotating for audience in the Xiāng Gé (Perfumed Pavilion).
On the Dīngwèi day,
an imperial instruction was given to the Shàngshū (Department of State Affairs) that
officials who must be transferred or appointed should be deliberated upon,
and those whose tenure was short should not be frequently transferred.
On the Yǐmǎo day,

the Shàngshū Shěng (Department of State Affairs) proposed to reduce the quota of the Qīnjūn Wǔwèijūn (Imperial Guards and Martial Guards) and the female and male students of the Tàixué (Imperial Academy)
and to abolish the positions of Xiǎoxué Guān (officials of elementary schools) and Wàilù Jiàoshòu (professors in the outer circuits).
An edict was issued that the schools should remain as they were,
the quota of the Wǔwèijūn (Martial Guards) should be deliberated upon again,
and the rest was approved.

Sīkōng (Minister of Works) Xiāng, Yòu Chéng (Right Grand Counselor) Kuāng, and Cānzhī Zhèngshì (Policy Advisor) Kuí requested the abolition of the Tídiǎn Xíngyù (Circuit Intendants of Justice) in all circuits.
This was granted.
On the Wùwǔ day,
there was a hailstorm.
In summer, in the fourth month, on the Guǐhài day,
Tíxíng Sī (Bureau of Justice) was renamed Ānchásǐ Sī (Bureau of Surveillance).
On the Wùchén day,
the emperor proceeded to Wànníng Gōng.
On the Rénshēn day,
Zuǒ Chéng (Left Grand Counselor) Yáng Bótōng retired.
Yùshǐ Dàfū (Grand Censor) Zhāng Wěi was stripped of one official rank for untruthful reporting,
and Shìyùshǐ (Censor-in-chief) Lù Duó was stripped of two official ranks.
Both were dismissed.
Jī Duānxiū received seventy strokes of the rod
and was allowed to redeem his punishment.
On the Rénwǔ day,
Prince Yīng Cóngxiàn was promoted to Prince Yíng.
An edict was issued to abolish the concurrent positions of Fùtǒngjūn (Deputy Commander) for Shǎnxī and Hénán held by Jiédùshǐ (Military Governors) of Tóngzhōu and Xǔzhōu.
In the fifth month, on the Rénchén day, which was the first day of the month,
due to drought,
an edict was issued in which the emperor reproached himself,
sought candid advice,
avoided the main hall,
reduced his meals,
reviewed unjust cases,
and ordered that memorials be presented at Tàihé Diàn.
On the Wùxū day,
officials were ordered to perform sacrifices to mountains and rivers to pray for rain.
On the Jǐhài day,
Yìngfèng Hànlín Wénzì (Academician in the Hànlín Academy) Chén Zài spoke on four matters: Firstly,
border residents suffered from banditry;
secondly,
farmers were distressed by military provisions;
thirdly,
the review and judgment of unjust and lingering cases were all too lenient,
even conniving with offenders;
fourthly,
officials of the Xíngshěng (Branch Secretariat)
were customarily granted generous rewards,
while officials in border prefectures and counties
received no benefit whatsoever,
which also disturbed the natural harmony
and led to the drought disaster.
The emperor approved of these points.
On the Rénkūn day,
Bīngbù Lángzhōng (Director of the Ministry of War) Wányán Sālǐhé was appointed as the envoy for the Xià Kingdom's birthday.
On the Wùshēn day,
the prime ministers, seeing rain in Jīngjī (the capital region),
led all officials to request the emperor to return to the main hall
and resume his normal meals.
This was not granted.
The Shàngshū Shěng (Department of State Affairs) presented a revised system for issuing tiger tallies,
which was recorded in the statutes.
On the Gēngxū day,
the emperor instructed the prime ministers:
"The drought in various circuits
may be related to the执zhízhèng (administrators).
Now only Dàxīng and Wǎnpíng counties have no rain;
is this not the fault of their prefects and magistrates?"
Sīkōng (Minister of Works) Xiāng, Píngzhāng Zhèngshì (Grand Counselor) Wàngōng, and Cānzhī Zhèngshì (Policy Advisor) Kuí submitted a memorial, accepting blame.
The emperor replied by taking the blame upon himself
and ordered them all to return to their duties.
An edict was issued to promulgate the standard for copper rods.
On the Rénzǐ day,
prayers for rain were offered at Tàimiào (Imperial Ancestral Temple).
On the Yǐmǎo day,
the reward regulations for military merits were revised.
On the Wùwǔ day,
Sīkōng (Minister of Works) Xiāng and others again requested the emperor to return to the main hall
and resume his normal meals.
This was not granted.
On the Gēngshēn day,
Píngzhāng Zhèngshì (Grand Counselor) Jiágǔ Héng passed away.
Sùzhí Jiāngjūn (General of the Imperial Guard) Túshān Zhònghuá was appointed envoy to bestow gifts upon the Xià Kingdom.
In the sixth month, on the *dīngmǎo* day,
it rained.
Sīkōng Xiāng and others again submitted a memorial requesting the emperor to hold court in the main palace
and resume his normal meals.
This was granted.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
as there was sufficient rain,
officials were ordered to offer thanks at the Tàimiào.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
Yòu Bǔquè Yáng Tíngxiù stated:
“Apart from officials allowed direct audience,
if those from the eighth rank and above in the capital court, fifth rank and above in the outer circuits, and envoys on foreign missions have anything to say,
they shall all be permitted to submit memorials to the Jiǎnyuàn to be heard.
Then, the gains and losses of current policies,
and the benefits and ailments of the people,
can be fully known.”
This was granted.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
as there was sufficient rain,

On the *dīngwèi* day,
the emperor discussed the appointment of a prime minister with his high officials, saying:
“Túshā Dānyì,
my will is already decided.
What about Jiǎ Xuàn?”
They all said:
“Sūn Jíkāng, who is Zhī Yán'ān Fǔshì, is suitable.”
Píngzhāng Zhèngshì Wàngōng also said:
“Jíkāng passed the examination
one榜 before Xuàn.”
The emperor said:
“At this point, why ask about the examination rank?

or quarterly,

The Emperor issued an edict praising and commending this.
The Imperial Genealogy (*Yùdié*) was completed.

Lǚ Qīngyún, a Compiler in the Bureau of National History (*Guóshǐyuàn Biānxiūguān*), was appointed as Junior Remonstrance Official of the Left (*Zuǒ Bǔquē*) concurrently serving as Calligrapher in the Hanlin Academy (*Yìngfèng Hàlín Wénzì*).

The Emperor admonished them, saying:
"During the Míngchāng period,
Qīngyún once submitted a memorial speaking about matters in the imperial palace,
and his words were very direct and incisive.
These were things others could not say,
which you, gentlemen, probably do not know.
For a subject to speak on matters without letting outsiders know
is an act of prudence and discretion.
He should indeed be prominently employed.
You, gentlemen, should be fully aware of this."
Wūgǔlùn Yì, Minister of Works (*Gōngbù Shàngshū*), and others were appointed as envoys to the Sòng for condolences and sacrifices.

Sūn Fù, Director of the Imperial Treasury (*Tàifù Jiān*), stated:
"Currently, there are over thirty-seven thousand officials in service,
and those appointed through privilege (*yīn*) constitute two-thirds.
Vacancies in various departments often take years to fill.
This is because there are too many appointments through privilege,
leading to a confusion of ranks and social standing,
and a reversal of priorities.
Furthermore, those who gain advancement through payment or connections,
having neither meritorious service
nor passing the imperial examinations,
also extend their privilege to their descendants
without any distinction.
If we wish to clarify this stream,
we must first purify its source."
Thereupon, the laws regarding appointments through privilege were revised and promulgated.
The Department of State Affairs (*Shàngshū Shěng*) reported:

visited Wàngjīng Diān.
On the Rén Shēn day,
went to Wànníng Gōng.
On the Jiǎ Xū day,
the law limiting money circulation was abolished.
On the Jiǎ Shēn day,
Hào Wáng Yǒngzhōng was reburied in Wēizhōu.
In the eighth month,
Dàlǐchéng Jī Duānxiū and Sīzhí Wēn Dūn, after an investigation and deliberation regarding Gěshíliè Zhízhōng, who was in charge of Dàxīngfǔ affairs,
impeached him.
Both were stripped of one official rank each
and dismissed from their posts for their inappropriate statements.
On the day Dīngyǒu,
Zōng Hào, the Shàngshū Yòuchéngxiàng, was appointed Zuǒchéngxiàng;
Púsàn Kuí, the Yòuchéng, was appointed Píngzhāng Zhèngshì;
Sūn Jíkāng, the Cānzhīzhèngshì, was appointed Shàngshū Yòuchéng;
Púsàn Duān, the Yùshǐ Dàfū, was appointed Zuǒchéng;
and Dújí Sīzhōng, the Lìbù Shàngshū, was appointed Cānzhīzhèngshì.
On the day Gēngzǐ,
an imperial edict ordered Wányán Gāng, Qiáo Yǔ, Sòng Yuánjí, and others to compile and categorize memorialized texts.
Those that involved the imperial court,
or concerned high officials, the provincial and censorate offices, or the Six Ministries,
were to be grouped by category.
There were approximately two thousand volumes in total.
On the day Xīnchǒu,
Chóngsù, the Xījīng Liúshǒu, was appointed Yùshǐ Dàfū.
On the day Guǐmǎo,
the regulations for Gémén Zhīhòu being assigned to outside posts were revised.
Previously, due to drought, an imperial edict had called for frank advice.
At this time, the Shàngshūshěng reported:
"The memorials from Lú Xiǎndá of Hénánfǔ and Wáng Dàcái of Rǔzhōu contained disrespectful language.
We request that their crimes be judged with appropriate severity based on the circumstances."
This was approved,
and a general announcement was made both domestically and abroad.
It was ordered that students in local schools whose numbers were small should cease instruction,
and only officials with literary qualifications from their respective zhōu or fǔ should supervise them.
On the day Dīngwèi,
based on the suggestion of Liú Cháng, the Ānzhōu Jūnshì Pàn Guān,
it was decreed that any Ànchásī officials who made unverified accusations
and proceeded to impeach individuals
would be punished as if they had intentionally caused innocent people to be wrongly convicted or acquitted,
and would also be dismissed.
If the matter involved personal corruption,
they would be dealt with according to the relevant existing laws.
On the day Xīnhài,
the emperor returned to the palace.
On the day Yǐmǎo,
Wányán Chāng, who was in charge of Zhēndìngfǔ affairs, and others were appointed as envoys to congratulate Sòng on the emperor's birthday.
On the day Dīngsì,
the emperor visited Tàijí Gōng.
The ban on distant areas of the imperial hunting grounds was lifted,
allowing people to farm, fish, gather firewood, and collect herbs.
Fifty attendants from the Jiàofāng and thirty from the Bóhǎi Jiàofāng were dismissed,
along with fifty female workers from the Wénxiùshǔ.
One hundred and sixty palace women were released.
On the first day of the ninth month, Gēngshēn,
which was Tiānshòu Jié,
Sòng, Gāolí, and Xià sent envoys to offer congratulations.
On the day Bǐngyín,
the emperor went to Qiūshān in Jìzhōu.
On the day Rénshēn,
regulations for self-cultivation and tenant farming by Túntián households were established.
In the winter, on the day Jiǎwǔ of the tenth month,
private laws were established.
On the day Bǐngshēn,
an imperial edict ordered that all imperial guards below thirty-five years of age should study the Xiàojīng and the Lúnyǔ.
On the day Guǐmǎo,
the emperor returned from Qiūshān.
On the day Jiǎyín,
Wányán Xiè, who was Tídiǎn Shàngyījú, was appointed as an envoy for Xiàguó's emperor's birthday.
In the eleventh month, on the day Dīngmǎo,
Wūlín Dá Yì, who was Diànqián Yòufù Dūdiǎnjiǎn, and others were appointed as envoys to congratulate Sòng on the New Year.
On the day Guǐyǒu,
rime ice formed on trees,
lasting for three days.
On the day Dīngchǒu,
regulations for recruiting and appointing Chéngyìng Réngé were established.
On the first day of the twelfth month, Jǐchǒu,
locusts were reported in Xīnpíngděng Xiàn.
On the day Jǐhài,
Zuǒchéngxiàng Zōng Hào and others requested that the emperor accept an honorific title.
This was not permitted.
On the day Xīnchǒu,
an imperial decree ordered officials to redeem children from Shǎnxī and Hénán who had been sold due to famine.
On the day Yǐmǎo,
all officials again petitioned for the emperor to accept an honorific title.
This was not permitted.
In the spring of the fifth year, on the first day of the first month, Jǐwèi,
there was heavy snow.
Sòng, Gāolí, and Xià sent envoys to offer congratulations.
On the day Gēngshēn,
the emperor visited Yǎnqìng Gōng.
On the day Yǐchǒu,
the emperor visited Tàijí Gōng.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
the emperor went to Guāngchūn Gōng for the spring hunt.
On the day Rénshēn,
a morning sacrifice was offered at Yǎnqìng Gōng.
On the day Yǐhài,
an imperial edict instructed the relevant authorities that
since Tàihé three years, counties and prefectures that had been traversed three times by the imperial procession and whose people had provided supplies
were to be granted half of their rent and taxes for the current year.
On the day Dīngchǒu,
the emperor stopped at Bàzhōu.
Troops and laborers from Shāndōng and Héběi were conscripted to dredge and repair the漕渠 (cáoqú, transport canal).
On the first day of the second month, Jǐchǒu,
the Ànchásī was instructed:
"Recently, the system held that being composed and understanding the general situation made one competent,
while being nitpicky and ignorant of the overall situation made one incompetent.
As a result, the Ànchá officials in various circuits became complacent,
not thinking of promoting or impeaching,
and counties and prefectures indulged in greed and corruption,
unable to be restrained.
From now on, if an investigation proves effective,
and the people have no unresolved grievances,
then one who can keep an entire circuit stable is considered competent.
However, if one causes confusion and prevents people from airing their grievances,
this is considered neglect of duty."
On the day Guǐsì,
the punishment for officials conducting interrogations and investigations who accepted invitations to feasts was established.
On the day Jǐhài,
the emperor went to Jiànchūn Gōng.
On the day Jiǎyín,
a decree was issued that the crime of stealing or forging imperial gate seals
would be punished one degree less severely than that of forging palace gate seals.
In the third month, on the day Gēngshēn,
the emperor returned to the palace.
On the day Guǐhài,
the deadlines for paying the two taxes were revised.
On the day Yǐchǒu,
Sòng troops entered the Qínchuān border.
On the day Gēngwǔ,
imperial princes and all officials requested that the emperor accept an honorific title.
This was not permitted.
On the day Jiǎxū,
an imperial edict instructed the relevant authorities that
candidates for the Jinshi examination whose names conflicted with the taboo name of Kǒngzǐ should avoid using those characters,
and this was to be established as a permanent regulation.
It was ordered that rice be distributed to various temples,
from the fifteenth day of the tenth month to the fifteenth day of the first month of the following year, to make porridge to feed the poor.
On the day Wùyín,
the 'prison empty money' tax was abolished.
On the day Xīnsì,
Sòng troops entered Lái Yuǎn Zhèn in Gǒngzhōu.
Those who captured Sòng spies in Tángzhōu
reported that Hán Tuōzhòu was massing troops in Èzhōu and Yuèzhōu,
planning a northern invasion.
On the first day of the fourth month, Wùzǐ,
the emperor went to Wànníng Gōng.
On the day Guǐsì,
the Pīmìyuàn was ordered to send a dispatch to the Sòng people,
demanding that they withdraw their new troops in accordance with the oath and agreement,
and not allow them to enter the border.
On the day Rénzǐ,
the method for officials of the various circuit Zhuǎnyùnsī and fǔ to inspect treasury goods quarterly was established.
In the fifth month, on the day Jiǎzǐ,
Púsàn Kuí, the Píngzhāng Zhèngshì, was appointed Hénán Xuānfǔshǐ,
and troops from various circuits were registered in preparation for Sòng.
On the day Guǐyǒu,
an imperial edict established the number of households and individuals in townships and communities in Liáodōng.
On the day Wùyín,
the regulations for examination, inspection, and retention of officials were revised.
On the day Jǐmǎo,
the emperor went to Qìngníng Gōng.

A decree was issued that officials of the Sisǔ Chéng (subordinate departments) who experienced the death of a parent would only be granted leave until the end of the mourning period for the initial burial (zúkū jiǎ),
and this was made a permanent regulation.
On the day Jiǎshēn,
Sòng troops entered Liánshuǐ Xiàn.
In the sixth month, on the day Wùzǐ,
Liánshuǐ Xiàn was recovered.
On the day Dīngyǒu,
the imperial court's wedding rituals were established.
The regulations for selling rice outside the border were revised.
On the day Jǐyǒu,
a decree established the punishment for desertion by Zhènfángjūn (garrison troops) leading to border incidents, errors, or the loss of households.
On the day Jiǎyín,
an imperial edict decreed punishment for those who did not follow the imperial court's bowing rituals.
All high officials were summoned and asked about strategies for preparing against Sòng.
All spoke of establishing defenses and avoiding aggression.
The emperor believed that the North and South had been at peace for over forty years,
and the people knew nothing of war,
so he could not bear to initiate hostilities.
In the seventh month, on the day Wùchén,
the emperor went to Jǐnpíng Shān.
On the day Rénshēn,
a morning sacrifice was offered at Yǎnqìng Gōng.
On the day Yǐhài,
Xuānfǔshǐ Kuí presented a memorial establishing regulations for the punishment and reward of spies.
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
the punishment for accidentally shooting a person in the imperial hunting grounds was established.
On the day Rénwǔ,
an imperial edict concerned the selection and appointment of patrol officers (xúnwèi) in counties where banditry was rampant.
In the eighth month, on the day Xīnmǎo,
an edict was issued to abolish the Xuānfǔsī (Pacification Commissioner's Office).

At this time, Guō Ní (郭倪), the Sòng Grand Marshal of the Palace Guards, and Tián Jùnmài (田俊邁), the defending general of Háo Zhōu, enticed Sū Guì (蘇貴) and others, commoners of Hóng Xiàn, to act as spies.
The Hénán military officials also frequently released spies,
who often profited from Jùnmài's bribes,
and in turn became lobbyists.
They all claimed that the Sòng's increased garrisons
were originally to guard against other bandits,
and upon hearing of the establishment of the Xíngtái (Traveling Bureau of the Secretariat),
they became even more fearful and intimidated, not daring to remove their defenses.
Moreover, their soldiers were all commoners,
who carried their own rations of dry food,
and were severely afflicted by poverty, hunger, and disease,
with twelve or thirteen out of every hundred dying.
Consequently, both the court and the public believed this.
The Xuānfǔsī reported on dispatches from the Sòng's Three Departments, the Bureau of Military Affairs, and Xūyí Army,
all of which listed and criticized frontier officials as a pretext.
The Xuānfǔshǐ, Kuí (揆), therefore requested the abolition of the office,
which was granted.
Kuí (揆) also memorialized to abolish the newly established archers in Líntáo, Déshùn, Qín, and Gǒng.
In the intercalary month, on the first day of Ěrmǎo,
the Diǎnwèisī (Office of Palace Guards) was abolished.
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
the emperor returned to the palace.
In the ninth month, on the first day of Jiǎshēn,
the Tiānshòu Festival,
envoys from Sòng, Gāolí, and Xià came to offer congratulations.
On the day Wùzǐ,
in the northwest, amid black clouds, there was a reddish aura like fire.
It then spread to the southwest, due south, and southeast, all becoming red,
with a white aura piercing through it.
By midnight,
the red aura filled the sky,
and dispersed only at the fourth watch.
Héshíliè Zǐrén (紇石烈子仁) and others, who were the commander of Hénán Lù forces, were appointed as envoys to congratulate Sòng on its emperor's birthday.
On the day Wùxū,
three hundred Sòng soldiers attacked Bǐyáng Sì Zhuāng.
The deputy巡檢 (Patrol Inspector) Ālǐgēn (阿里根)'s household servant died in the incident.
On the day Jiǎchén,
Sòng forces burned Huángjiàn,
and captured Patrol Inspector Gāo Hào (高顥).
In winter, in the tenth month, on the day Gēngshēn,
Lǐ Yuánzhōng (李元忠), a Yuánwàiláng (Supernumerary Secretary) of the Ministry of Justice, was appointed as the envoy for Gāolí's king's birthday.
On the day Dīngchǒu,
Sòng forces raided Bǐyáng.
Sāndù (撒覩), the military judicial officer of Táng Zhōu, died in the incident.
In the eleventh month, on the day Yǐyǒu,
Sòng forces entered Nèixiāng,
and attacked Gù Xiàn in Luònán.
Shòu Zǔ (壽祖), the prison warden of Shāng Zhōu, pursued them to Dānhé,
and defeated them.
On the day Jǐchǒu,
Zhào Zhījié (趙之傑) and others, who were Tàichángqīng (Court of Imperial Sacrifices Grand Master), were appointed as envoys to congratulate Sòng on the New Year.
On the day Guǐsì,
Shāndōng experienced food shortages,
and thirty thousand strings of cash were granted to relieve the distress.
On the day Yǐwèi,
the regulations for military examinations were first established.
On the day Dīngyǒu,
an edict was issued to the Shāndōng and Shǎnxī military commanders to train and instruct their soldiers,
to prepare for unforeseen circumstances.
Additionally, one hundred and fifty thousand taels of silver were distributed to the frontier commanders,
to recruit people for reconnaissance.
Furthermore, Wányán Tàipíng (完顏太平), the Deputy Commander of the Wǔwèijūn (Martial Guards Army), and Púchá Ālǐ (蒲察阿里), the Deputy General of the Right Palace Guard, were dispatched to the border,
to watch for their incursions,
and ambush them with concealed troops.
On the day Wùxū,
there was heavy snow,
and the morning court audience was excused.
On the day Jǐhài,
the regulations for recruitment and appointment in the palace bureaus and offices were revised.
Wú Xī (吳曦) of Sòng amassed troops in Xīngyuán,
intending to invade Guān and Lǒng.
Huángfǔ Bīn (皇甫斌) further recruited soldiers to harass Huáiběi,
giving them whatever was plundered,
to make them fight on their own.
In the sixth year, spring, in the first month, on the first day of Guǐwèi,
envoys from Sòng, Gāolí, and Xià came to offer congratulations.
On the day Dīnghài,
Sòng envoy Chén Kèjùn (陳克俊) and others took their leave from court.
Mèng Zhù (孟鑄), the Yùshǐ Zhōngchéng (Censor-in-Chief), was sent to the residence to instruct Kèjùn (克俊) and others,
saying:
"At the beginning of Dàdìng,
Emperor Shìzōng allowed Sòng to be a fraternal nation for generations.
I have adhered to the ancestral laws,
and maintained good relations until now.
How could I have expected that your nation would repeatedly have bandits violating our border?
It was because of this that I sent a high official to pacify the Hénán army and people.
And when I received official dispatches from your nation's authorities,
claiming that border officials had been dismissed
and soldiers withdrawn,
I, considering the overall situation under heaven,
did not mind minor grievances,
and thus abolished the Xuānfǔsī.
Not long after,
the banditry was worse than before.
Recently, my officials have repeatedly spoken of your nation's breach of covenant.
I, however, have only considered that the good relations have lasted for many years,
and have been accommodating and tolerant.
I fear that the fraternal Sòng emperor may not be fully aware.
If it does not cease as before,
my officials may again have something to say.
Although I cherish all living beings,
the matter cannot simply end there.
When you return to your nation,
you must fully convey my intentions to your ruler."
On the day Xīnmǎo,
a court sacrifice was offered at Yǎnqìng Gōng.
On the day Bǐngshēn,
Wú Xī (吳曦), the defending general of Xīngyuán of Sòng, sent troops to besiege Mòshú Lóng Bǎo.
His subordinate general Púxiān Cháng'ān (蒲鮮長安) attacked and routed them,
and beheaded their general.
On the day Xīnchǒu,
the Bǎowǔ Fǎ (Neighbor-Watch System) was revised.
On the day Guǐmǎo,
county officials along the river were first concurrently made managers of river transport affairs,
and zhōu and fǔ officials concurrently made chief controllers.
On the day Dīngwèi,
the emperor went to Chūnshuǐ (Spring Waters).
On the day Gēngxū,
Sòng forces entered Sāmóu Gǔ.

Wányán Guālà (完顏摑剌), the military judicial officer of Shǎnxī, and Wányán Qīyīn (完顏七斤), the commander of military and horse affairs of Gǒng Zhōu, arranged a meeting with the Sòng defending general of Xīhé Zhōu at the border.
Suddenly, an ambush was sprung,
and they were attacked.
Zhào Yànxióng (趙彥雄), the chief of Mùbō, and seven others died there.
Guālà's (摑剌) horse sank into a quagmire,
and he was struck by a stray arrow.
Qīyīn (七斤) barely escaped with his life.
In the second month, on the day Jiǎxū,
Mèng Zhù (孟鑄), the Yùshǐ Zhōngchéng, said:
"Changing Tíxíng (Justice Commissioner) to Ànchásī (Investigation Commissionerate),
and then dispatching officials for secondary inspections,
reduces their power and diminishes their prestige,
which is not convenient."
Jiǎ Xuàn (賈鉉), a Cānzhī Zhèngshì (Grand Councilor Assistant), said:
"Since the Ànchásī already dispatches监察 (Censors) for investigation and inquiry,
to again send officials for secondary inspection is truly redundant and troublesome.
I request that from now on, when Censors are dispatched, officials be sent along with them,
and no further secondary inspection be conducted."
This was granted.
This was followed.
In the third month, on the day Jiǎwǔ,
the Shàngshūshěng (Secretariat) memorialized,
requesting posthumous grants for the military officials under Shāng Zhōu Cìshǐ (Prefect) Wūgǔlún Yǎnzhōu (烏古論兗州) who died in battle against Sòng forces,
and also requested promotion for Yòu Zhènsù (Right Commissioner of Austerity) Púchá Wǔjīn (蒲察五斤),
both of which were granted.
In the early years of Míngchāng,
Wǔjīn (五斤) had once been a Fèngyù (Attendant),
and was sent on a mission to Shāndōng.
When he reached Héjiān,
seeing the suffering of the common people from hunger,
he boldly issued an order to the Tíxíngsī (Justice Commissionerate) to open the granaries and provide relief.
Upon his return, he fully reported the matter.
The emperor was initially very pleased.
However, Tàifù (Grand Tutor) Túdān Kèníng (徒單克寧) said:
"Your Majesty has just begun to personally handle major political affairs.
It is not appropriate to delegate authority to palace attendants.
I request that the crime of unauthorized decision-making be rectified."
An edict was issued to punish him with twenty strokes of the rod.
Kèníng (克寧) again spoke about it,
and so he was dismissed.
Later, the emperor remembered him,
and he was recalled from Tàizhōu Dūjūn (Military Commander of Tàizhōu) to be a Zhènsù (Commissioner of Austerity).
On the day Jǐhài,
the emperor went to Wànníng Gōng.
On the day Jiǎchén,
an imperial edict was given to the Shàngshūshěng:
"For those whose grandparents or parents have no one to attend to them,
while their children and grandchildren travel far for over a year,
it greatly harms social customs.
Although the old law prescribed a two-year penal servitude,
it seems too light.
Review previous laws,
and reconsider the matter to report back."
On the day Jǐyǒu,
Sòng forces attacked Língbì.
The Nánjīng Ànchásǐ (Investigation Commissioner of Nánjīng) was on his circuit through the county,
and avoided capture by hiding in a commoner's house.
On the *bǐngchén* day of the fourth month,
the Sòng people besieged Shòuchūn.
Shòuchūn urgently appealed to Bó,
where the Assistant Prefect of Defense, Xiánshèngnú, led 600 cavalry and infantry to their aid,
and the Sòng then retreated.
On the *guǐhài* day,
the Shàngshūshěng reported:
"The Hénán Commander's Office stated that
Commander Hégēlì Zǐrén and others dispatched Yán Zhěng, Yán Zhōng, Zhōu Xiù and their like into Xiāngyáng
to spy on the enemy's secret affairs.
They returned reporting that Huángfǔ Bīn had sent 40,000 troops to plan the taking of Dèng,
with our traitor Tián Yuán acting as a local guide;
and 30,000 men to plan the taking of Táng,
with Zhāng Zhēn and Zhāng Shèng acting as local guides,
both of whom were granted the office of commander.
Therefore, we dare not be unprepared.
So, the troops from Zhèng, Rǔ, and Yángzhái were assembled at Chāngwǔ,
under the command of Hégēlì Yì, Vice Grand Commander of Cavalry and Infantry and concurrently Vice Prefect of Nánjīng,
and the troops from Bó, Chén, and Xiāngyì were assembled at Guīdé,
under the command of Túshānduó, Vice Commander of Hénán Circuit,
while he himself, with his own troops, was stationed at Biàn.
It was also decided to assign 7,000 troops from the Shāndōng East and West Circuits to Commander Hégēlì Zhízhōng to be stationed at Dàmíng,
and 17,000 troops from the Héběi East and West Circuits to be garrisoned in Hénán.
All were to be provided with horses,
and those who were old or weak were to be replaced."
All these proposals were approved.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
the Sòng people attacked the border of Tiānshuǐ.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
they entered Dōngkē Gǔ,
but the divisional commander Liú Duó defeated them.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
an imperial edict appointed Púsǎnkúi, Administrator of the Bureau of Military Affairs, to lead the Branch Secretariat at Biàn,
granting him discretion to act as he saw fit.
The Commander's Offices of various circuits were elevated to Grand Commands of Cavalry and Infantry.
Hégēlì Zhízhōng, Commander of Shāndōng East and West Circuits, was made Grand Commander of Cavalry and Infantry for Shāndōng West Circuit.
Wányán Sālā, Military Commissioner of Dìnghǎijūn and Vice Grand Commander, served as his deputy.
The Commander of Shǎnxī Circuit, Chōng, was made Grand Commander of Cavalry and Infantry for Shǎnxī Five Circuits.
Hú Shā, Military Commissioner of Tōngyuǎnjūn, and Shímò Zhòngwēn, Prefect of Líntáo Prefecture, served as his deputies.
In Hénán, all matters remained under the control of Kúi, as before.
All registered soldiers from the various circuits were conscripted.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
Sòng's Wú Xī attacked Lánjiālǐng in Lái Yuǎn Zhèn.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
an imperial edict stipulated that all civil and military officials, both internal and external, were to contribute a certain number of horses.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
the Sòng people entered Xīnxī and Nèixiāng,
and also entered Sīzhōu.
On the *wùyín* day,
they entered Bāoxìn.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
they entered Hóngxiàn.
On the *gēngchén* day,
they entered Yǐngshàng.
On the *rénwǔ* day of the fifth month,
Sòng's Lǐ Shuǎng besieged Shòuzhōu,
Tián Jùnmài entered Qíxiàn,
and Qín Shēn attacked Cáizhōu.
The Prefect of Defense Wányán Fózhu defeated them.
They also entered Jīnchéng Hǎikǒu,
killed the commander of Chángshān,
and seized two patrol inspectors before leaving.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
Venus was visible in broad daylight.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
because Sòng had violated the alliance and launched an army,
an announcement was made to Heaven and Earth, the Imperial Ancestral Temple, and the Altars of Soil and Grain.
On the *dīnghài* day,
a personal announcement was made at Yǎnqìng Gōng.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
Púsǎnkúi, Administrator of the Bureau of Military Affairs, was concurrently appointed Left Vice Marshal.
Chōng, Grand Commander of Cavalry and Infantry for Shǎnxī, was made Right Supervisor of the Army for the Marshal.
Wūgǔlún Yì, Prefect of Zhēndìng Prefecture, was made Left Chief Supervisor for the Marshal.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
there was a military expedition to the southern kingdom, inside and outside the capital.
Wúgǔsūn Wùtún, Prefect of Tángzhōu, and Wányán Jiāngshān, Grand Overseer of Dèngzhōu military affairs, were each granted two ranks of nobility.
Wányán Fózhu, Prefect of Defense for Cáizhōu, was granted one rank of nobility.
Other rewards and gifts varied.
Furthermore, as the report from Yán Zhěng was not strictly accurate,
he must have been misled.
Zhěng was appointed Inspector of Sōngzhōu,
granted eight ranks of nobility,
and 2,000,000 cash.
The Emperor, seeing that Sòng forces were surging,
and the newly mobilized troops from the northeast had not yet assembled,
and the forces in Hénán were insufficient to resist,
ordered 15,000 troops from Héběi, Dàmíng, Běijīng, and Tiānshān to be stationed at Zhēndìng, Héjiān, Qīng, Xiàn, etc., to serve as reinforcements.
On the *rénchén* day,
an edict was issued to the Shàngshūshěng:
"Now that the state faces many difficulties,
all officials of the fifth rank and above shall successively present their views on matters of military and national interest.
I will personally question them.
Officials below the sixth rank shall submit their proposals in writing."
On the *guǐsì* day,
there was a disaster in Shāndōng Circuit.
A general amnesty was granted for all crimes below capital punishment.
Wányán Kuāng, Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, was appointed Right Vice Marshal.
Sòng's Tián Jùnmài attacked Sùzhōu.
Nàlán Bāngliè, Vice Military Commissioner of Ānguójūn, and others led troops to attack them.
Bāngliè was hit by a stray arrow.
Sòng's Guō Zhuó and Lǐ Rǔyì arrived with reinforcements,
and then besieged Sùzhōu.
On the *rén'yín* day,
Nàlán Bāngliè and others attacked and defeated them.
Jùnmài retreated to Qí for defense.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
Jùnmài was captured at Qí.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
Huángfǔ Bīn attacked Tángzhōu.
The Prefect Wúgǔsūn Wùtún resisted him.
The Branch Secretariat dispatched Nàhé Jūnshèng, Vice Patrol Inspector of Bìyáng, to provide aid,
and they subsequently defeated Huángfǔ Bīn.
On the *gēngxū* day,
Venus traversed the sky.
On the *xīnhài* day, the first day of the sixth month,
Púsǎnduān, Left Chancellor, resigned due to his mother's mourning.
Kúi, Administrator of the Bureau of Military Affairs, reported the victory at Qí,
and also sent the captured Sòng general Tián Jùnmài to the imperial court.
The Emperor issued an edict praising and commending them,
and granted Hégēlì Zhēn, Nàlán Bāngliè, Shǐ Jítā and others various ranks and rewards.
Sòng general Lǐ Shuǎng besieged Shòuzhōu with his troops.
The Prefect Túshān Xī defended the city,
and after more than a month, it could not be taken.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
Qǐzhù and Mǎigē, staff officers of the Hénán Commander's Office, arrived with troops to provide aid.
Xī led his troops out to meet them,
and Shuǎng was thoroughly defeated.
Púliègǔ, Assistant Prefect of the Military Prefecture, was hit by a stray arrow and died.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
express courier stations were first established,
with bell-waisted couriers relaying messages,
traveling 300 *lǐ* a day.
Only for military dispatches and river defense matters were horses allowed to be used.
The crime of accepting bribes for military assignments was established.
It was also legislated that even if flying locusts entered the territory but did not damage crops, it would still be considered a crime.
On the *dīngsì* day,
an imperial edict was issued to Zhāngdé Prefecture, stating that
the tombs of Sòng's Hán Tuōzhòu and Zǔ Qí must not be damaged,
and that logging and gathering firewood were prohibited.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
Wányán Sàibù, Commander of the Right Wing, defeated Sòng's Commander Cáo at Zhēnshuǐ.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
an imperial edict was issued to the relevant authorities, stating that
wherever members of the Sòng imperial clan resided,
each case should be reported.
The local officials were to exercise constant oversight.
On the *rénxū* day,
Kúi, Administrator of the Bureau of Military Affairs, reported the victory at Shòuzhōu.
On the *wùchén* day,
an imperial edict elevated Shòuzhōu to a defense prefecture,
exempted it from this year's land tax and various miscellaneous fees,
and pardoned crimes below capital punishment.
Túshān Xī was appointed Prefect of Defense.
Púliègǔ was posthumously granted the title of Zhāoyǒng Dàjiāngjūn,
given 300 *guàn* of cash,
and his son Tūlá was given an official post.
Qǐzhù was promoted to Assistant Military Commissioner of Chāngwǔjūn,
and Mǎigē to Staff Officer of the Hénán Circuit Commander's Office.
Commander Sàibù and Deputy Commander Púxiān Wànnú were each advanced one rank of nobility,
and granted varying amounts of gold and silk.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
Jupiter was visible in daylight,
and by the *wùshēn* day of the seventh month,
it traversed the sky.
On the *yǐhài* day,
Sòng's Wú Xī attacked Yánchuān.
The garrison commander Wányán Wángxǐ defeated him.
On the *guǐwèi* day of the seventh month, in autumn,
Sòng's Shāng Róng again attacked Dōnghǎi.
The county magistrate Wányán Biànsēng again defeated him.
Upon returning,
he was hit by an arrow from an ambush and died.
He was posthumously granted the title of Prefect of Hǎizhōu,
with 500 *liǎng* of silver
and 100 bolts of silk given to his family,
and one of his sons was given an official post.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
an ancestral sacrifice was offered at Yǎnqìng Gōng.
On the *dīnghài* day,
an imperial edict instructed Chén Dàrèn, Hanlin Scholar-in-Waiting, to put aside his regular duties and focus on compiling the History of Liáo.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
Sòng commander Qī Chūn attacked Pīzhōu with his naval forces.
The Prefect Wányán Cóngzhèng defeated him.
Chūn drowned himself,
and his deputy, Commander Xià, was beheaded.
Wú Xī's army of 50,000 entered Qínzhōu.
Chéngyù, Deputy Grand Commander of Shǎnxī Circuit, and others defeated them.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
Lǐ Chúnyòu, King of Xià State, was deposed.
His nephew Ānquán ascended the throne
and sent envoys to present a memorial and announce the event.
An imperial edict prohibited the sale of horses across the border,
decreeing that anyone caught attempting to sell horses at the border would be executed.
In the eighth month, on the day Gēngxū,
the Shāndōng commander reported the victory at Pízhōu.
On the day Xīnhài,
Jupiter was seen in the morning.
On the day Yǐmǎo,
Qīngyíkě, a Qiāng chieftain, was appointed Vice Grand Commandant-in-Chief of Diézhōu.
On the day Jǐwèi,
Venus was seen during the day.
On the day Bǐngyín,
Púsǎn Duān, Left Chancellor, was reinstated to his former post.
An edict established the various Pingnán generals.
On the day Xīnwèi,
Chéng Sōng of Sòng attacked and seized Fāngshānyuán.
Púchá Zhēn defeated and drove him away.
On the day Rénshēn,
Venus was seen during the day,
traversing the sky.
On the day Jiǎxū,
he returned from Wànnínggōng Palace.
On the day Yǐhài,
an amnesty was granted to the six prefectures of Táng, Dèng, Yǐng, Cài, Sù, and Sì,
and one-third of the next year's rent and taxes were remitted.
In the ninth month, on the first day Jǐmǎo,
for the Tiānshòu Festival,
Gāolì sent envoys to offer congratulations.
On the day Xīnsì,
Marshal and Right Supervisor of the Bureau of Military Affairs Púchá Zhēn captured Héshàngyuán.
The Fān tribes of Líntáo, led by Zūnníng, offered fodder, grain, and warhorses to aid the army.
On the day Yǐyǒu,
approaching the fifth watch,
several streaks of red and white vapor appeared in the north,
rising from below Wángliáng,
and moving east of the Kaiyáng and Yaoguāng stars of the Northern Dipper.
On the day Bǐngxū,
he went to Xiāngshān.
On the day Gēngyín,
an imperial order was given to the Mobile Secretariat,
that those with outstanding strategy, unparalleled martial arts, capable talent in managing affairs, or extraordinary craftsmanship,
should be recruited.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
Jiǎ Xuàn, Participant in Government Affairs, requested retirement,
which was not permitted.
On the day Wùxū,
Púsǎn Duān, Left Chancellor of the Secretariat, acted as governor in Biàn.
On the day Jǐhài,
Liáng Táng, Vice Minister of the Ministry of Revenue, acted as Minister of the Six Ministries in Shāndōng.
On the day Xīnchǒu,
Wēndíhǎn Sījìng, Left Assistant Director of the Ministry of Personnel, was sent to enfeoff Lǐ Ānquán as King of Xiàguó.
On the day Jiǎchén,
Féng Xīng, Yáng Xióng, Lǐ Guī and other generals of Wú Xī of Sòng entered Qínzhōu.
Chéngyù and others, Vice Commissioners of the Shǎnxī General Headquarters, attacked and defeated them,
beheading Yáng Xióng and Lǐ Guī.
In winter, the tenth month, on the first day Wùshēn,
Púsǎn Kuí, Censor-in-Chief and Grand Councilor, commanded the armies from various circuits to attack Sòng.
On the day Gēngxū,
Kuí led 30,000 provincial troops out from Yǐng and Shòu.
Héshíliè Zǐrén, Commander-in-Chief of the Hénán Circuit, led 30,000 troops out from Wōkǒu.
Marshal Kuāng led 25,000 troops out from Táng and Dèng.
Héshíliè Zhízhōng, Left Supervisor of the Army, led 20,000 Shāndōng troops out from Qīngkǒu.
Chōng, Right Supervisor of the Army, led 10,000 Guānzhōng troops out from Chéncāng.
Púchá Zhēn, Right Supervisor of the Bureau of Military Affairs, led 10,000 Qí and Lǒng troops out from Chéngjì.
Wányán Gāng, Pacification Commissioner of the Shǔhàn Circuit, led 10,000 Hàn and Fān infantry and cavalry out from Líntán.
Shímò Zhòngwēn, Grand Commandant-in-Chief of the Líntáo Circuit, led 5,000 Lǒngyòu infantry and cavalry out from Yánchuān.
Wányán Lín, Defense Commissioner of Lǒngzhōu, led 5,000 of his own troops out from Láiyuǎn.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
there was a hunt in the nearby suburbs.
In the eleventh month, on the first day Wùyín,
an edict fixed the regulations for land and labor services in various prefectures and subprefectures.
On the day Rénwǔ,
Wányán Kuāng captured Zǎoyáng.
On the day Yǐyǒu,
an edict allowed military households engaged in屯田 (túntián) to intermarry with local residents.
On the day Dīnghài,
Púsǎn Kuí conquered Ānfēngjūn
and took Huòqiū County.
Héshíliè Zhízhōng conquered Huáinán,
and then besieged Chǔzhōu.
On the day Jǐchǒu,
the Secretariat reported
a reduction in the monthly stipend paid in cash for court officials and those holding temporary posts.
On the day Gēngyín,
Wányán Kuāng conquered Guānghuàjūn and Shénmǎpō.
On the day Rénchén,
Púsǎn Kuí encamped at Lújiāng.
Qiū Wù, Sòng's Inspector of Jianghuai Military Affairs, sent Liú Yòu to request peace.
Héshíliè Zǐrén conquered Dìngyuǎn County.
On the day Yǐwèi,
Wányán Kuāng captured Suízhōu.
On the day Bǐngshēn,
Héshíliè Zǐrén conquered Chúzhōu.
On the day Wùxū,
an edict ordered the circulation of small notes in all circuits.
Wányán Kuāng besieged Dé'ān,
and also sent troops to capture Ānlù, Yìngchéng, Yúnmèng, Xiàogǎn, Hànchuān, Jīngshān, and other counties.
On the day Gēngzǐ,
in the late afternoon,
there were two meteors,
their light shining like torches,
almost a zhàng (ten feet) long,
rising from the northeast and disappearing in the southeast.
The tea prohibition was initially established.
Wányán Gāng besieged Yòuzhōu,
and it surrendered.
Sòng's Qiū Wù sent Lín Gǒng with a letter to request peace.
On the day Xīnchǒu,
Wányán Kuāng attacked Xiāngyáng,
breaching its outer wall.
Púsǎn Kuí conquered Hánshān.
Púchá Zhēn conquered Tiānshuǐ.
Héshíliè Zǐrén captured Láiyán and Quánjiāo counties.
On the day Rényín,
Wányán Gāng captured Lìchuān, Lǘchuān, and other cities.
On the day Guǐmǎo,
Qiū Wù again sent Sòng Xiǎn and others with letters and silks to request peace.
On the day Yǐsì,
Wányán Gāng conquered Dàngchāng.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
Púchá Zhēn conquered Xīhézhōu.
In the twelfth month, on the first day Dīngwèi,
Wányán Kuāng conquered Yíchéng.
Púsǎn Kuí attacked Hézhōu.
Shǐ Gētā died from a stray arrow.
On the day Rénzǐ,
Wányán Gāng encamped at Dàtán County,
and it surrendered.
Púchá Zhēn conquered Chéngzhōu.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
Wú Xī, Sòng's Grand Commandant, Military Commissioner of Zhaoxinjūn, and Vice Pacification Commissioner of Sìchuān, made overtures to Wányán Gāng.
On the day Wùwǔ,
Chōng, Right Supervisor of the Army, captured Dàsǎnguān.
On the day Jǐwèi,
Héshíliè Zǐrén conquered Zhēnzhōu.
Qiū Wù again sent Chén Bì and others with a letter to request peace.
On the day Xīnyǒu,
Chōng, Right Supervisor of the Army, sent Wùyán Chāohé with troops to advance on Fèngzhōu.
The city walls collapsed, and they entered.
Wányán Gāng sent Zhāng Zǐ, Scribe of Jīngzhào, to meet Wú Xī at Zhìkǒu in Xīngzhōu.
Xī fully expressed his intention to pledge allegiance to the court.
Zǐ asked for his official credentials as a pledge,
and Xī handed them all over,
also offering Jiēzhōu.
On the day Yǐchǒu,
the officials for the Dūtíkòng Jídìpù (courier stations) were established for the first time.
Púsǎn Kuí, Censor-in-Chief and Grand Councilor, returned with his army.
Wányán Gāng, by imperial decree,
temporarily appointed Mǎ Liángxiǎn, Taicang Envoy, to carry the imperial edict and a gold seal to establish Wú Xī as King of Shǔ.
On the day Wùchén,
Púchá Zhēn reported the victories at Xīhé and Tiānshuǐ.
Wányán Kuāng presented a hundred women he had plundered.
On the day Jǐsì,

Xī sent Guō Chéng, Commander of the Guǒzhōu Tuanlian, and Rèn Xīn, Commissioner for the Supervision of Xiānrénguān, to submit a memorial, a gazetteer of the Shǔ region, and the genealogy of the Wú clan.
On the day Rénshēn,
an edict appointed Wányán Kuāng as acting Left Vice Minister of the Secretariat,
with his previous duties as acting governor and Right Vice Marshal unchanged.
As Héshíliè Zhízhōng had allowed his troops to plunder,
a close official was sent to flog his secretary Ālǐbùsūn and others,
and an edict was issued to release those who had been plundered.
In the seventh year, spring, the first month, on the first day Dīngchǒu,
Gāolì and Xià sent envoys to offer congratulations.
Wányán Kuāng advanced to attack Xiāngyáng.
On the day Wùyín,
an imperial order instructed the chief ministers to recommend capable officials to jointly discuss the Southern Campaign.
On the day Xīnsì,

an edict summoned Chóng Sù, Grand Censor, Túdān Huáizhōng, Concurrent Manager of the Bureau of the Imperial Family, Fàn Jí, Minister of Personnel, Gāo Rǔlì, Minister of Revenue, Zhāng Xíngjiǎn, Minister of Rites, and Wēndíhǎn Sīqí, Prefect of Dàxīngfǔ, and fourteen others to an audience together at Qìnghédiàn Palace.
On the day Rénwǔ,
an edict summoned all officials and the previous fourteen individuals to an audience together at Guǎngréndiàn Palace.
On the day Jiǎshēn,
a court sacrifice was offered at Yǎnqìnggōng Palace.
On the day Yǐyǒu,
Wèi Quán, a soldier who died for his loyalty in Shòuzhōu, was posthumously granted the title of Xuānwǔ General and Magistrate of Méngchéng.
His wife was enfeoffed as Xiāngjūn.
His son, when he reached fifteen, was to be enrolled in the Bāguànshí Zhèngbānjú for imperial service.
Additionally, a million cash were bestowed.
Initially,
when Lǐ Shuǎng besieged Shòuzhōu,
the Prefect Xī recruited men to go and attack the enemy camp.
Quán was among those selected,
but was captured by the enemy.
The enemy ordered him to curse Xī to be spared.
Quán feigned compliance,
but when he reached the city walls,
he cursed the enemy instead,
and was consequently killed.
He cursed without ceasing until his death,
hence this grace.
On the day Wùzǐ,
Wányán Gāng was summoned to the capital.
On the day Gēngyín,
Púsǎn Kuí returned to station at Xiàcài and fell ill.
On the day Bǐngshēn,
Zōng Hào, Left Chancellor, was concurrently appointed Grand Marshal,
and acted as governor in Nánjīng to replace Kuí.
On the day Jǐhài,
the relevant authorities reported on revising the tea prohibition.
On the day Xīnchǒu,
Wányán Kuāng captured Gǔchéng.
In the second month, on the day Bǐngchén,
an amnesty was granted to the five prefectures of Fèng, Chéng, Xīhé, Jiē, and Shān.
[一一]On the day Dīngsì,
an edict was issued to posthumously restore Wáng Yǒngzhōng and Wáng Yǒngdǎo to their princely titles.
Sòng's Zhī Púmìyuàn Zhāng Yán sent Fāng Xìnrú with a letter to Píngzhāng Zhèngshì Kuí and Zuǒchéng Duān, requesting peace.
On the day Jǐwèi,
there was a hunt in the nearby suburbs.
Wányán Kuāng captured Jīngmén Jūn.
On the day Guǐhài,
the emperor went to Jiànchūn Gōng.
Wú Xī sent an envoy with three memorials: thanking for the enfeoffment,
presenting vows,
and congratulating on the annexation of the entire Shǔ region.
On the day Bǐngyín,
the emperor returned to the palace.
On the day Wùchén,
Píngzhāng Zhèngshì兼 Zuǒ Fù Yuánshuài Púsàn Kuí died in the army.
On the day Guǐyǒu,
Túhǔ Gāoqí and others, who were Tóngzhī Fǔshì, were dispatched to invest Wú Xī as the King of Shǔ.
Wèi Wáng Yǒngjì, who was Pàn Píngyáng Fǔshì, was appointed Wǔdìng Jūn Jiédùshǐ,
and concurrently Guǎnnéi Guānchásǐ of Fèngshèng Zhōu.
In this month,
Wú Xī, the King of Shǔ, was killed by Sòng minister Ān Bǐng.
In the third month, on the day Wùzǐ,
the emperor visited Tàijí Gōng.
On the day Gēngyín,
an edict was issued to pacify and comfort the military personnel in Shǎnxī.
On the day Rénchén,
the crime of landlords and neighbors failing to report the initial discovery of insect pests was established for the first time.
Sòng again attacked and captured Jiē Zhōu.
On the day Guǐsì,
Xīhé Zhōu was again attacked and captured.
On the day Yǐwèi,
Xuānfǔ Fùshǐ Wányán Gāng arrived in Fèngxiáng.
An edict was issued to withdraw troops from the five prefectures
and distribute them to guard strategic points.
Gāng recalled all the armies.
On the day Gēngzǐ,
Wányán Kuāng was appointed Zuǒ Fù Yuánshuài.
On the day Rényín,
the emperor went to Wànníng Gōng.
On the day Jiǎchén,
the emperor visited Xīyuán.
In the summer, fourth month, on the day Rénzǐ,
Yáng Xù, Fùjiān of Gōngjí, was sent as an envoy to bestow gifts upon the King of Gāolí.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
Sòng forces captured Sànguān.
Wūyán Āshī, Qiánxiá of Gǒng Zhōu, died.
On the day Bǐngchén,
Héshíliè Zǐrén was appointed Yòu Fù Yuánshuài.
On the day Wùchén,
an edict ordered the Yuánshuài Fǔ to dispatch various generals to patrol the prefectures south of the Huái River.
On the day Guǐyǒu,
Sànguān was recaptured.
In the fifth month, on the day Jǐmǎo,
the emperor visited Shùyuán to shoot willows.
[一二]On the day Jǐchǒu,
the emperor visited Yùquán Shān.
On the day Bǐngshēn,
Sòng Zhī Púmìyuàn Shì Zhāng Yán again sent Fāng Xìnrú with a letter to the Dū Yuánshuài Fǔ,
offering to increase annual tribute in exchange for peace.
Sìchuān Ānfǔshǐ Ān Bǐng sent Lǐ Xiàoyì, Ānfǔshǐ of Xīhé Zhōu, leading 30,000 infantry and cavalry to attack Qín Zhōu,
[一三]and besiege Zàojiǎobǎo.
Túhǔ Gāoqí led troops to relieve them,
and after seven battles, lifted the siege.
In this month,
twenty palace women were released.
In the sixth month, on the first day Yǐsì,
an edict ordered court officials of the sixth rank and above, and outer officials of the fifth rank and above,
as well as imperial princes, to recommend one official skilled in finance and grain management.
Those who failed to recommend would be punished;
those who recommended inappropriately would be judged according to the law.
On the day Jǐyǒu,
due to bandits in Shāndōng,
a decree was issued regarding rewards for those of the same gang who killed the leader, captured them, and reported to officials.
On the day Wùwǔ,
Wūgǔlún Yì was appointed Yuánshuài Zuǒ Jiānjūn,
and Wányán Sālà was appointed Yuánshuài Zuǒ Dūjiān.
On the day Yǐchǒu,
envoys were dispatched to capture locusts.
In the autumn, seventh month, on the day Gēngchén,
a morning offering was made at Yǎnqìng Gōng.
On the day Rénwǔ,
an edict ordered that for transactions and pawns among the common people,
amounts above one string of cash must all use jiāochāo (paper currency),
and not cash.
On the day Yǐyǒu,
an imperial order was given to the Shàngshū Shěng,
that from now on, newly appointed censors should submit memorials detailing advantages and disadvantages
in preparation for imperial audience.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
Zuǒ Fù Yuánshuài Kuāng arrived from Xǔ Zhōu.
On the day Yǐwèi,
an edict ordered a census of the Xī Xià population,
that all be redeemed and released,
and those who dared to harbor them would be punished for violating the imperial decree.
In the eighth month, on the day Wùshēn,
Sòng's Zhāng Yán again sent Fāng Xìnrú with his sovereign's oath letter to request peace.
On the day Gēngxū,
Xiāngchéng Xiàn of Rǔ Zhōu was ceded to Xǔ Zhōu.
On the day Wùchén,
the emperor returned from Wànníng Gōng.
In the ninth month, on the first day Jiǎxū,
on Tiānshòu Jié (the emperor's birthday),
Gāolí and Xià sent envoys to offer congratulations.
Zuǒ Chéngxiàng concurrent Dū Yuánshuài Zōnghào died in the army.
On the day Jiǎshēn,
the grades for Pàn Guān of various salt fields in Dìngxī, Běijīng,
and Liáodōng Yánsī, as well as the increase or decrease in duties, were fixed.
Shàngshū Zuǒchéng Púsàn Duān was appointed Píngzhāng Zhèngshì,
and enfeoffed as Shēn Guó Gōng;
Zuǒ Fù Yuánshuài Wányán Kuāng was appointed Píngzhāng Zhèngshì concurrent Zuǒ Fù Yuánshuài,
and enfeoffed as Dìng Guó Gōng.
On the day Bǐngxū,
there was a hunt in the nearby suburbs.
On the day Rénchén,
the emperor returned to the palace.
On the day Wùxū,
the punishments for forgetting or making errors in receiving imperial decrees, and for incorrectly writing imperial decrees, were revised to be more severe.
On the day Rényín,
an imperial order forbade Nǚzhí people from changing to Hàn surnames or adopting Sòng-style attire.
In the winter, tenth month, on the day Jiǎchén,
an edict stated that for families with inherited official positions (yìn),
if the collateral yìn positions were sufficient,
but the principal yìn recipient died before taking office,
one replacement yìn would be permitted.
On the day Xīnhài,
Wǔkù Lìng Tújiǎ Fǎxīn was appointed Gāolí Shēngrì Shǐ (envoy for the King of Gāolí's birthday).
On the day Bǐngchén,
there was a hunt in the nearby suburbs.
On the day Jǐsì,
an edict established the reward system for those who accompanied the army.
On the day Xīnwèi,
Shǎnxī Xuānfǔshǐ Túchán Yì dispatched Fùtǒng Bǎ Huíhǎi to capture Sūlíng Guān.
In this month,
the reward system for generals and soldiers in the southern campaign was established.
In the eleventh month, on the day Guǐyǒu,
an edict ordered that in the newly established school regulations, Xuē Jūzhèng's Wǔdài Shǐ be removed,
and only Ōuyáng Xiū's compilation be used.
On this day,
Dūtǒng Yālà captured Báhúlíng Guān and Xīndàokǒu.
[一四]Fùtǒng Huíhǎi captured Xiǎohú Guān and Yìcāng,
advanced to Yíngkǒu Zhèn,
and then took the city.
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
Sòng's Hán Tuōzhòu sent Zuǒsī Lángzhōng Wáng Nán with a letter requesting peace,
asking to be called "Uncle,"
and to again increase annual tribute and military stipends,
and to execute Sū Shīdàn, presenting his head as an offering.
On the day Bǐngxū,
the emperor heard that Héshíliè Bósūn, Fángyùshǐ of Shǎn Zhōu, prohibited the common people from selling grain,
and ordered the Shàngshū Shěng to punish him.
On the day Rénchén,
Sòng Cānzhī Zhèngshì Qián Xiàngzǔ sent a letter to the Xíngshěng regarding the execution of Hán Tuōzhòu.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
there was a hunt in the nearby suburbs.
On the day Wùxū,
Cānzhī Zhèngshì Jiǎ Xuàn was dismissed.
An edict ordered Wányán Kuāng to issue a proclamation to Sòng,
demanding Hán Tuōzhòu's head in exchange for the former Huáinán territory.
In the twelfth month, on the first day Rényín,
the Liáo Shǐ (History of Liáo) was completed.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
Fúbǎoláng Wūgǔlún Fúlíng was appointed Xiàguó Shēngrì Shǐ (envoy for the King of Xià's birthday).
On the day Wùwǔ,
an edict exempted jinshi (palace examinees) who took policy questions from archery and polo tests.
On the day Gēngshēn,
Shàngshū Yòuchéng Sūn Jíkāng was appointed Zuǒchéng,
Cānzhī Zhèngshì Dújí Sīzhōng was appointed Yòuchéng,
and Zhōngdū Lù Dū Zhuǎnyùnshǐ Sūn Duó was appointed Cānzhī Zhèngshì.
In the eighth year, spring, first month, on the first day Xīnwèi,
Gāolí and Xià sent envoys to offer congratulations.
On the day Rényīn,
a morning audience was held at Yǎnqìng Gōng.
On the day Guǐyǒu,
large denomination paper currency was recalled and destroyed,
and small denomination paper currency was issued.
Yuánshuài Zuǒ Dūjiān Wányán Sālà was appointed Cānzhī Zhèngshì.
On the day Yǐhài,
