Sòng's Ān Bǐng sent troops to attack Húlíng Guān.
Fùtǒng Bǎ Huíhǎi and Wányán Guālà repelled them,
and beheaded their general, Jǐng Tǒnglǐng.
On the day Bǐngzǐ,

Zuǒsī Lángzhōng Liú Áng, Tōngzhōu Cìshǐ Shǐ Sù, Jiānchá Yùshǐ Wáng Yǔ, Lìbù Zhǔshì Cáo Yuán, Lìbù Yuánwàiláng Túchán Yǒngkāng, Tàicāng Shǐ Mǎ Liángxiǎn, and Shùnzhōu Cìshǐ Tángguō Zhísī were all punished with a beating for privately discussing court affairs with Dàzhōng, the magistrate of Púyīn.
They were all flogged.
On the day Guǐwèi,
the emperor went to Chūnshuǐ.
On the day Bǐngxū,
the emperor went to Guāngchūn Gōng.
In the second month, on the day Yǐsì,
Sòng Grand Councilor Qián Xiàngzǔ sent Wáng Nán to come,
bearing a letter to the Xíngshěng,
again requesting the passes of Chuān and Shǎn.
On the day Jiǎyín,
went to Jiànchūngōng.
On the day Gēngshēn,
an edict was issued to the relevant authorities, saying:
"During the farming season,
even restricted areas shall be cultivated."
On the day Jǐsì,
returned to the palace.
In the third month, on the day Dīnghài,
visited Xīn Yíngwáng's residence to inquire about his illness.
On the day Gēngyín,
regarding the peace with Sòng,
an edict was issued to the Shàngshūshěng.
On the day Rénchén,
the prime ministers submitted a memorial to apologize.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
Yíngwáng Cóngxiàn passed away.
On the day Yǐwèi,
the Emperor personally attended the sacrifice.
In summer, the fourth month, on the day Guǐmǎo,
there were three sun halos,
all yellow on the inside and red on the outside.
On the day Wùshēn,
performed the Dì sacrifice at the Tàimiào.
On the day Gēngxū,
went to Wànnínggōng.
On the day Jiǎyín,
as there was no trouble on the northern frontier,
an imperial decree was issued to the Shàngshūshěng,
ordering the Northeast Circuit Pacification Commission to return to govern Tàizhōu,
and concurrently hold the post of military commissioner.
Its副招討 (vice-pacification commissioner) was to remain stationed at the border.
An imperial edict was issued to the relevant authorities,
stating that as crops were just beginning to flourish,
officials should be swiftly dispatched to巡行農事 (inspect agricultural affairs) along various routes,
to guard against insect pests.
An imperial edict was issued to revise the regulations for the succession and examinations of méng'ān-móukè.
Sòng's Qián Xiàngzǔ again sent Wáng Nán with a letter to the Xíngshěng.
On the day Gēngshēn,
an imperial edict decreed that all circuits' Ancha司 (surveillance commissions) would receive public funds annually.
In the intercalary month, on the day Xīnwèi,
an edict was issued to the Shàngshūshěng, saying:
"Hànlín Shìjiǎngxuéshì Púchá Wèiyě said
that officials sent to Sòng should be carefully selected,
and his words are very appropriate.
Although their ambassador for mutual gratitude has not yet arrived at the court,
the person for the return embassy should be deliberated and chosen beforehand.
This is a new beginning,
and all matters of propriety
depend on the envoy.
Now that it is being put into practice,
it will become a permanent precedent,
and one cannot but be cautious."
On the day Jiǎxū,
a decree prohibited all prefectures, departments, and counties from conscripting various types of artisans for construction work.
Violators would be punished according to the law on illegal conscription,
and their offense would be judged by the value of the remuneration received for their supervision.
On the day Jiǎshēn,
regulations for the age requirements for recruiting performing artists were established.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
there was rain and hail.
Rewards for the Bǎojiǎ army for killing or capturing Sòng military officers were set.
On the day Yǐwèi,
Sòng presented the heads of Hán Tuōzhòu and others to the Yuánshuàifǔ.
In the fifth month, on the day Dīngwèi,
presided at Yìntiānmén,
with the imperial yellow standard and assembled guards,
and the princes, civil and military officials paid their respects in formation.
The Zhōnglù Bīngmǎ Tíkòng and Píngnán Fǔjūn Shàngjiāngjūn Gēshíliè Zhēn presented the heads of the Sòng treacherous ministers Hán Tuōzhòu and Sū Shīdàn,
and reported this along with the Yuánshuàifǔ's written proclamation.
Their heads and portraits were displayed in the market,
and the proclamation was distributed both domestically and abroad.
On the day Bǐngchén,
Píngzhāng Zhèngshì Kuāng arrived from the army.
On the day Jǐwèi,
the Yuánshuàifǔ was changed to the Shūmìyuàn.
On the day Guǐhài,
an imperial edict moved the Tiānshòujié to the fifteenth day of the tenth month.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
envoys were dispatched to various routes to capture locusts.
In the sixth month, on the day Guǐyǒu,
Sòng's envoy for mutual gratitude, Cháoyì Dàfū and Tí Lǐbù Shàngshū Xǔ Yì,
along with Fúzhōu Guānchásǐ and Yòuwǔwèi Shàngjiāngjūn Wú Héng and others, entered to pay respects, bearing their lord's letter.
On the day Jiǎxū,
paid respects and offered thanks at Yǎnqìnggōng.
On the day Guǐwèi,
regarding the peace with Sòng,
an imperial edict was issued to all officials, both civil and military, within and outside the capital.
The summer tax for this year was exempted in Hénán, Shāndōng, Shǎnxī, and other six circuits,
and halved in Hédōng, Héběi, Dàmíng, and other five circuits.
On the day Dīnghài,
Yuánshuài Zuǒ Dūjiān Wūgǔlún Yì was appointed Yùshǐ Dàfū.
On the day Wùzǐ,
swarms of locusts entered the capital region.
On the day Yǐwèi,
regulations for the design of clothing with bright gold and elephant gold were established.
On the day Dīngyǒu,
Zuǒ Fù Dūdiǎnjiǎn Wányán Kǎn was appointed Sòng Yùchéngshǐ,
[一五] and Lǐbù Shìláng Qiáo Yǔ was his deputy.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the day Wùxū, the first day of the month,
Venus was visible in daylight.
On the day Gēngzǐ,
an imperial edict was issued to revise the law on punishment for the outbreak of locusts.
On the day Yǐsì,
offered sacrifice at Yǎnqìnggōng.
An imperial edict was issued to distribute maps for locust catching to all.
On the day Wùshēn,
the Sòng envoy took leave,
conveying the reply to the letter of mutual gratitude and the oath letter to the Sòng sovereign.
In the eighth month, on the day Rénshēn,
the regulations for the circulation of paper currency in Liáodōng were revised.
On the day Guǐyǒu,
went to Jiànchūngōng.
On the day Jǐchǒu,
Hùbù Shàngshū Gāo Rǔlì and others were appointed Sòng Shēngrìshǐ.
On the day Gēngyín,
went to Qiūshān.
In the ninth month, on the day Jiǎzǐ,
Lìbù Shàngshū Jiǎ Shǒuxiān and thirteen others were dispatched with officials from various Ancha commissions to assess the property and resources of households.
On the day Yǐchǒu,
returned from Qiūshān.
In winter, the tenth month, on the day Xīnwèi,
Lìbù Lángzhōng Guō Fú was appointed Gāolí Shēngrìshǐ.
On the day Xīnsì,
envoys from Sòng, Gāolí, and Xià came to offer congratulations.
Xià had troops,
and sent an envoy to report.
On the day Guǐwèi,
the regulations for the crime of forcible theft at anchorages were revised.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
an article on officials praised by both military and civilians for their integrity and ability was added to the law on excellent governance.
In the eleventh month, on the day Dīngyǒu, the first day of the month,
an imperial edict decreed that all circuits' Ancha envoys would concurrently serve as Zhuǎnyùn envoys.
Initially, a Sānsīshǐ was established,
responsible for managing salt and iron, financial expenditure, and promoting agriculture.
Shūmìshǐ Gēshíliè Zǐrén concurrently served as Sānsīshǐ.
On the day Guǐmǎo,
an imperial edict admonished the Shàngshūshěng, saying:
"The governance of the state
lies in its fundamental principles.
What is foremost among these principles
is that rewards and punishments must be trustworthy.
Yet now, from the highest levels of the provincial departments,
down to the various departments and counties,
laws and regulations are not followed,
and private convenience prevails.
Years are wasted in procrastination,
and perfunctory conduct has become a habit.
If this becomes the practice,
how can there be good governance?
The imperial court is the foundation for all officials,
and the capital is the model for all of China.
Therefore, strive from this day forward,
each repenting of past mistakes,
obeying laws and regulations,
exerting full effort to achieve success.
Do not distort justice by following personal feelings,
and do not waver to avoid influence.
Let all return to rectitude,
and thereby serve as a model for your people."
On this day,
held an examination for guards at Línwǔdiàn.
On the day Dīngwèi,
an imperial decree instructed Línchuáng Tàizhōulù Bīngmǎ Dūzǒngguǎn Chéngyì and others to repair frontier defenses.
On the day Yǐmǎo,
the Emperor fell ill.
On the day Bǐngchén,
passed away at Fú'āndiàn,
aged forty-one.
In the first year of Dà'ān, spring, the first month,
he was posthumously given the title Xiàntiān Guāngyùn Rénwén Yìwǔ Shénshèng Yīngxiào Huángdì,
with the temple name Zhāngzōng.
In the second month, on the day Jiǎshēn,
buried at Dàolíng.
A赞 says: Zhāngzōng was on the throne for twenty years.
He inherited Shìzōng's long period of peaceful governance,
and the country enjoyed minor prosperity.
He rectified the rites and music,
reformed the penal code,
and established the official system,
making the institutions and cultural artifacts a brilliant model for a generation of governance.
He also frequently asked his ministers about the methods of investigation and verification of names and realities by Hàn Xuān and the system of performance reviews in the Táng dynasty.
He probably wished to surpass the Liáo and Sòng and compare himself to the Hàn and Táng,
and thus could be said to have had aspirations for good governance.
However, a favored concubine dominated the court,
no heir apparent was established,
and he alienated and distrusted imperial relatives, handing over power to the wrong person.
What was previously said about maintaining and consolidating stability for a long time
became mere empty words,
and was of no use to future generations of descendants even for a single day.
The Jīnyuán clan thenceforth declined.
In ancient times, Yáng Xióng said:
"Qín's officials betrayed Qín's laws and regulations,
and Qín's laws and regulations betrayed the laws and regulations of the sages."
Indeed, there was reason for this.
Collation Notes
Annals, Volume 13: Wèi Shàowáng
Wèi Shàowáng's personal name was Yǒngjì,
his childhood name was Xīngshèng.
His personal name was later changed to Yǔnjì.
During Zhāngzōng's time, to avoid Xiǎnzōng's taboo name,
an imperial edict was issued to change
"Yǔn"
to
"Yǒng."
He was Shìzōng's seventh son,
his mother was Yuánfēi Lǐ shì.
Wèi Wáng was tall,
with a beautiful beard.
By nature, he was frugal
and disliked extravagance.
In Dàdìng 11th year (1171),
he was enfeoffed as Xuē Wáng.
In the same year,
he was promoted to Téng Wáng.
In the 17th year (1177),
he was granted a hereditary Méng'ān.
In the 25th year (1185),
he was given the honorary title Kāifǔ Yítóng Sānsī.
In the 26th year (1186),
he became Mìshūjiān.
The next year (1187),
he was transferred to Xíngbù Shàngshū.
The year after that (1188),
he was appointed Diànqián Dūdiǎnjiǎn.
In the 29th year (1189),
Shìzōng passed away.
Zhāngzōng ascended the throne,
and he was promoted to Lù Wáng.
He was recalled to office
and appointed Pàn Ānwǔjūn Jiédùshǐ.
In the fifth month,
he arrived at Jìzhōu.
He submitted a memorial of gratitude upon taking office,
and an imperial edict was issued in kind reply.
In Míngchāng 2nd year (1191),
he was promoted to Hán Wáng.
In the 4th year (1193),
he was appointed Pàn Xīngpíngjūn.
In the 5th year (1194),
he was appointed Qìnnánjūn.
In Chéng'ān 2nd year (1197),
he was enfeoffed as Wèi Wáng.
In the 3rd year (1198),
he was appointed Zhāoyìjūn.
In Tàihé 1st year (1201),
he was appointed Pàn Zhāngdéfǔ Shì.
In the 5th year (1205),
he was appointed Pàn Píngyángfǔ.
Initially,
Zhāngzōng executed Zhèng Wáng Yǒngdǎo and Zhào Wáng Yǒngzhōng.
After a long time,
he somewhat regretted it.
In the 7th year (1207),
an imperial edict was issued to posthumously restore their former enfeoffments
and bestow posthumous titles.
Since Yǒngdǎo had no heir,
Wèi Wáng's son, Ànchén, was made the heir to Zhèng Wáng.
An imperial edict was given to Wèi Wáng, saying:
"I recall that Zhèng Wáng abandoned constant heavenly principles
and violated the national laws.
His body was buried in a desolate wilderness,
and he was neglected without offerings.
Many years have passed,
and I am deeply saddened by this.
The feelings of kinship are difficult to dismiss.
I have already issued an edict to posthumously restore his former title
and rebury him with proper rites.
Consulting ancient rituals,
I appoint your son Ànchén as Zhèng Wáng's heir,
to meticulously perform the sacrifices.
You should be aware of this."
Soon after, he was appointed Wǔdìngjūn Jiédùshǐ.
In the 8th year (1208), 11th month,
he returned to the capital from Wǔdìngjūn.
At this time,
Zhāngzōng had already contracted a cough illness.
Wèi Wáng was about to take his leave,
but Zhāngzōng intended to keep him.
In Zhāngzōng's early years,
he genuinely loved his imperial relatives,
establishing the Wángfùfǔ Wèiguān to instruct them in virtue and righteousness.
However, after the executions of Yǒngzhōng and Yǒngdǎo,
he became alienated and wary of the imperial clan.
Consequently, he used the Wángfùfǔ Wèi to control the imperial households,
with strict and meticulous questioning.
All entries and exits from their residences were recorded.
Yet Wèi Wáng was Yǒngdǎo's younger brother by the same mother,
and he was gentle and lacked wisdom.
Therefore, Zhāngzōng loved him.
Having no successor,
and with many of his uncles and brothers still alive,
Zhāngzōng was unwilling to appoint any of them,
wishing only to establish Wèi Wáng.
Hence, when he took his leave,
Zhāngzōng kept him.
Not long after,
Zhāngzōng fell gravely ill.
Yuánfēi Lǐ shì, Huángmén Lǐ Xīnxǐ, and Píngzhāng Zhèngshì WánYán Kuāng decided the succession.
When Zhāngzōng died,
Kuāng and others conveyed the imperial will
to enthrone Wèi Wáng.
Wèi Wáng initially declined,
but then accepted the edict, offered his condolences,
and ascended the imperial throne before the coffin.
The next day,
all the ministers paid their respects at Dà'āndiàn.
An edict commanded all lù, fǔ, zhōu, and xiàn to mourn the deceased emperor for seven days.
In Dà'ān 1st year (1209), 1st month, on the Xīnc丑 day,
a flying star, like fire,
appeared in the Tiānshì Yuán,
with a tail,
resembling a red dragon.
On the Rénxū day,
the reign title was changed,
and a general amnesty was granted.
Yuánfēi Túdān shì was established as empress.
In the 2nd month, on the Yǐchǒu day (the first day of the month),
Táibái (Venus) was visible in daylight,
traversing the sky.
On the Rénchén day,
Zhāngzōng's inner palace lady, Fàn shì, aborted her posthumous pregnancy,
which was announced inside and outside the court by edict.
Initially,
Zhāngzōng's will stated:
"Two inner palace ladies are pregnant;
if either gives birth to a boy, he shall be established as the heir apparent."
At this time, PúSǎn Duān and other Píngzhāng Zhèngshì reported:
"Chéngyù Jiǎ shì was supposed to give birth in the 11th month,
but it has now been three months past that.
Fàn shì's expected delivery date was in the 1st month.
Doctors say her fetal qi has been damaged.
Though medication was used for treatment,
her pulse is harmonious,
but the fetal shape is lost.
Fàn shì wishes to shave her head and become a nun."
Six imperial princes were enfeoffed as kings.
In the 3rd month, on the Jiǎchén day,
the ritual at Dàolíng was completed,
and a general amnesty was granted.
An edict stated:
"From now on, characters that do not form a continuous part of my name,
and characters such as 'chǎng' and 'yǒng,'
do not need to be changed."
Píngzhāng Zhèngshì PúSǎn Duān was appointed Yòuchéngxiàng.
In the 4th month, on the Gēngchén day,
Zhāngzōng's Yuánfēi Lǐ shì and Chéngyù Jiǎ shì were executed.
Píngzhāng Zhèngshì WánYán Kuāng was appointed Shàngshū Lìng.
In the 5th month,
Gāolì sent envoys to congratulate on the ascension.
The Hóngcí examination was held.
In the 7th month,
the emperor visited Hǎiwáng Zhuāng
to offer sacrifices to Lǔguó Gōngzhǔ.
In the 8th month,
on the Wànqiū Festival,
Sòng sent envoys to congratulate.
In the 9th month,
he went to Dàfángshān
to visit and offer sacrifices at Ruìlíng, Yùlíng, and Dàolíng.
All officials petitioned to establish an heir,
but it was not approved.
In the 10th month,
Suìxīng (Jupiter) encroached upon Zuǒzhífǎ.
On the Jǐmǎo day,
an imperial edict was issued to admonish and encourage moral conduct.
In the 11th month,
an earthquake occurred in Píngyáng,
with a sound like thunder,
coming from the northwest.
In the twelfth month,
an edict was issued regarding the earthquake in Píngyáng.
Households with three deceased members were exempted from rent and taxes for one year.
Those with two deceased members or injured persons were exempted for one year.
Poor people whose family members died were given 5,000 in burial money,
and 3,000 to the injured.
Shàngshū Lìng (尚書令) Shēn Wáng Wányán Kuāng (申王完顏匡) passed away.
Yòuchéngxiàng (右丞相) Púsàn Duān (僕散端) was appointed Zuǒchéngxiàng (左丞相).
His elder brother, Yǐng Wáng Yǒnggōng (郢王永功), was promoted to Qiáo Wáng (譙王).
Yùshǐ Dàfū (御史大夫) Zhāng Xíngjiǎn (張行簡) was appointed Tàibǎo (太保).
In the second year, on the *gēngxū* day of the first month,
a meteor appeared in the sun,
as large as a basin,
its color green.
It traveled westward,
gradually becoming as large as a chariot wheel,
with a tail several *zhàng* long.
It disappeared into the turbidness,
then rose again from the ground,
its light scattering like fire.
In the second month,
a guest star entered the Zǐwēiyuán (紫微垣) constellation,
its light scattering as a red dragon.
There was a great earthquake,
with a sound like thunder.
Lǐbù Shìláng (禮部侍郎) Gěng Duānyì (耿端義) was appointed Cānzhī Zhèngshì (參知政事).
In the fourth month,
the rites of Dà Jīn (大金) were reviewed and rectified.
In the north, there was a black qi,
like a great road,
spanning the sky from east to west.
The Hé (河) river in Xú (徐) and Pī Zhōu (邳州) became clear for over five hundred *lǐ*.
This was reported to the ancestral temples and the altars of earth and grain.
In the fifth month,
an edict was issued for Confucian scholars to compile and continue the *Zīzhì Tōngjiàn* (資治通鑑).
In the sixth month,
there was a great drought.
An edict was issued, blaming himself,
and relief was given to poor people lacking food.
A partial amnesty was granted to miscellaneous offenders in the Xījīng (西京) and Tàiyuán (太原) circuits.
Death sentences were reduced by one degree,
and sentences of *tú* (徒) and below were remitted.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
there was an earthquake.
In the seventh month,
there was an earthquake.
In the eighth month,
there was an earthquake.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
his son, Zuò Wáng Cóngkè (胙王從恪), was established as the Crown Prince.
On Wànqiū Jié (萬秋節),
Sòng (宋) sent envoys to offer congratulations.
A hunt was held in the near suburbs.
The Xī (夏) people invaded Jiá Zhōu (葭州).
In the ninth month,
there was a great earthquake.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
an edict was issued to solicit honest counsel,
recruit brave individuals,
and appease the displaced.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
envoys were sent to comfort and appease the soldiers of Xuāndé Xíngshěng (宣德行省).
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
the capital was put under martial law.
The emperor went on a daily巡撫 (xúnfǔ) inspection tour,
and officials requested to hold court,
but this was not granted.
On the *xīnhài* day,
Xuāndé Xíngshěng (宣德行省) was abolished.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
an edict was issued to comfort and appease the war-affected households in Zhōngdū (中都), Xījīng (西京), Qīng (清), and Cāng (滄).
In the eleventh month,
a hunt was held in the near suburbs.
In Zhōngdū (中都), fire spontaneously emerged from the canal east of Dàbēi Gé (大悲閣),
and extinguished only after more than ten days.
Beneath the flagstaff south of the pavilion, fire spontaneously emerged from a crevice in the stone.
When people approached it, it extinguished,
but soon reappeared.
This continued for another ten days.
Fire in Zhōngdū (中都) scorched people's residences.
In the twelfth month, on the *yǐmǎo* day of the new moon,
there was a solar eclipse.
That year there was a great famine.
The common people were forbidden from spreading rumors about border affairs.
In the third year, on the *yǐyǒu* day of the first month,
Sòng (宋), Gāolí (高麗), and Xià (夏) sent envoys to offer congratulations.
Yínghuò (熒惑) entered Dī (氐) constellation.
In the second month,
Yínghuò (熒惑) encroached upon Fáng Sù (房宿).
A great wind came from the north,
unroofing houses and breaking trees.
The heavy gates of Tōngxuán Mén (通玄門) broke,
and the heavy gates of Dōnghuá Mén (東華門) broke.
In the intercalary month,
Yínghuò (熒惑) encroached upon the Jiànbì Xīng (鍵閉星).
In the third month,
Dàbēi Gé (大悲閣) suffered a fire,
which spread to people's residences.
A black qi arose from the north,
broad and long like a great embankment,
with three white qì piercing through it,
resembling dragons and tigers.
Horses among the people were requisitioned,
and officials were ordered to provide horses according to their ranks.
In the fourth month,
our Dà Yuán Tàizǔ Fǎtiān Qǐyùn Shèngwǔ Huángdì (大元太祖法天啟運聖武皇帝) came to conquer.
Niánhé Hédá (粘合合打), the Xīběi Lù Zhāotǎoshǐ (西北路招討使), was sent to sue for peace.
Píngzhāng Zhèngshì (平章政事) Dújí Qiānjiānú (獨吉千家奴)
and Cānzhī Zhèngshì (參知政事) Húshā (胡沙) acted as Xíngshěng Shì (行省事) to prepare defenses.
Xījīng Liúshǒu (西京留守) Gēshíliè Húshāhǔ (紇石烈胡沙虎) acted as Shūmìyuàn Shì (樞密院事).
Cānzhī Zhèngshì (參知政事) Àotún Zhōngxiào (奧屯忠孝) was appointed Shàngshū Yòuchéng (尚書右丞).
Hùbù Shàngshū (戶部尚書) Liáng Zhuò (梁𤨠) was appointed Cānzhī Zhèngshì (參知政事).
On the *rénchén* day of the sixth month,
the regulations for military awards and punishments were revised.
In the eighth month,
an edict was issued to commend and instruct provincial officials,
and to comfort and appease the soldiers.
Qiānjiānú (千家奴) and Húshā (胡沙) retreated from Fú Zhōu (撫州),
stationing themselves in Xuānpíng (宣平).
The soldiers of Hénán Dàmíng Lù (河南大名路) deserted and returned,
and an edict was issued to recruit and appease them.
In the ninth month,
Qiānjiānú (千家奴) and Húshā (胡沙) were defeated at Huìhé Bǎo (會河堡),
and Jūyōng Guān (居庸關) fell.
Men were forbidden from leaving the gates of Zhōngdū (中都) city without authorization.
The vanguard of Dà Yuán (大元) reached Zhōngdū (中都),
and Zhōngdū (中都) was put under martial law.
Cānzhī Zhèngshì (參知政事) Liáng Zhuò (梁𤨠) garrisoned and pacified the capital.
In the tenth month,
every night at the first watch,
the eastern and northwestern sky became bright as if the moon had just risen,
and it disappeared after a month.
Yínghuò (熒惑) encroached upon Lěibì Zhèn (壘壁陣).
Shàngjīng Liúshǒu (上京留守) Túshàn Yì (徒單鎰) sent Tóngzhī (同知) Wūgǔsūn Wùtún (烏古孫兀屯) with 20,000 troops to guard Zhōngdū (中都).
Tài Zhōu Cìshǐ (泰州刺史) Shùhǔ Gāoqí (術虎高琪) was stationed outside Tōngxuán Mén (通玄門).
The emperor inspected and comforted the various armies.
Xuāndé Xíngshěng (宣德行省) was abolished.
In the eleventh month,
Hǎo Zàn (郝贊), a person from Hénán (河南) who offered advice, was killed.
Shàngjīng Liúshǒu (上京留守) Túshàn Yì (徒單鎰) was appointed Yòuchéngxiàng (右丞相).
The army within the walls of Zhōngdū (中都) was reviewed.
Gēshíliè Húshāhǔ (紇石烈胡沙虎) abandoned Xījīng (西京)
and fled back to the capital,
and was immediately appointed Yòu Fù Yuánshuài (右副元帥)
and acting Shàngshū Zuǒchéng (尚書左丞).
At this time,
Déxīng Fǔ (德興府), Hóng Zhōu (弘州), Chāngpíng (昌平), Huáilái (懷來),
Jìnshān (縉山), Fēngrùn (豐潤), Mìyún (密雲), Fúníng (撫寧), Jíníng (集寧),
eastward past Píng (平) and Luán (灤),
southward to Qīng (清) and Cāng (滄),
from Línhuáng (臨潢) across the Liáohé (遼河),
southwestward to Xīn (忻) and Dài (代),
all submitted to Dà Yuán (大元).
Initially,
Túshàn Yì (徒單鎰) had requested to move the people of Huán (桓), Chāng (昌), and Fú (撫) into the interior.
The emperor, trusting Liáng Zhuò's (梁𤨠) advice,
reprimanded Yì (鎰), saying:
"This is shrinking our own territory."
When Dà Yuán (大元) had already taken these three prefectures,
the emperor regretted it.
At this point,
Yì (鎰) again requested to establish a Xíngshěng (行省) office in Dōngjīng (東京)
to guard against unforeseen events.
The emperor was displeased and said:
"Sending a great minister without reason
will shake people's morale."
Not long after,
Dōngjīng (東京) could not be defended,
and the emperor then greatly regretted it.
Yòu Fù Yuánshuài (右副元帥) Húshāhǔ (胡沙虎) requested 20,000 troops to be stationed in Xuāndé (宣德).
An edict granted him 3,000 men to be stationed in Guī Chuān (媯川).
Píngzhāng Zhèngshì (平章政事) Qiānjiānú (千家奴) and Cānzhī Zhèngshì (參知政事) Húshā (胡沙) were punished for losing their entire army.
Qiānjiānú (千家奴) was dismissed from office,
and Húshā (胡沙) was demoted to Xiánpíng Lù Bīngmǎ Zǒngguǎn (咸平路兵馬總管).
Wànhù (萬戶) • Tóu (●頭) was stationed at Gǔběikǒu (古北口).
In the twelfth month,
5,000 Hàn (漢) soldiers from Shǎnxī (陝西) two circuits were conscripted to Zhōngdū (中都).
Tàibǎo (太保) Zhāng Xíngjiǎn (張行簡) and Zuǒchéngxiàng (左丞相) Púsàn Duān (僕散端) stayed in the forbidden palace to discuss military affairs.
Zuǒchéngxiàng (左丞相) Púsàn Duān (僕散端) was dismissed.
In the first year of Chóngqìng (崇慶), on the *jǐyǒu* day of the first month,
the reign title was changed,
and an amnesty was granted.
Sòng (宋) and Xià (夏) sent envoys to offer congratulations.
Yòu Fù Yuánshuài (右副元帥) Húshāhǔ (胡沙虎) requested to withdraw the army and station them at Nánkǒu (南口).
An edict enumerated his crimes,
but he was pardoned.
In the third month,
there was a great drought.
Envoys were sent to officially enfeoff Lǐ Zūnxū (李遵頊) as the King of Xià Guó (夏國).
Yùshǐ Dàfū (御史大夫) Fúxīng (福興) was appointed Cānzhī Zhèngshì (參知政事).
Cānzhī Zhèngshì (參知政事) Mèng Zhù (孟鑄) was appointed Yùshǐ Dàfū (御史大夫).
The Xià (夏) people attacked Jiá Zhōu (葭州).
Yán'ān Lù Bīngmǎ Zǒngguǎn (延安路兵馬總管) Wányán Núpì (完顏奴婢) repelled them.
In the fifth month,
20,000 men from the Shǎnxī Yǒnggǎn Jūn (Brave Army) and
10,000 men from the Shèliáng Jūn (Provision-carrying Army) were conscripted
and dispatched to Zhōngdū.
Horses in Shǎnxī were requisitioned.
Jiǎ Xuàn, the retired Military Commissioner of Ānwǔ Commandery, was recalled to serve as Vice Grand Councilor.
Fúxīng, a Vice Grand Councilor, became Assistant Director of the Left in the Department of State Affairs.
An imperial edict ordered the sale of blank official commissions.
Hédōng and Shǎnxī suffered a great famine,
where a dou of rice cost several thousand cash,
and the fields were filled with corpses of the starving.
Púsǎn Duān, the Resident Commissioner of Nánjīng, was appointed Pacification Commissioner of Hénán and Shǎnxī,
in charge of military forces.
In the seventh month,
a wind came from the east,
blowing a piece of silk
tens of zhang high,
which moved like a dragon
and fell at Gǒngchén Gate.
In the eighth month,
on the Wànqiū Festival,
no banquet was held due to military affairs.
In the tenth month,
a partial amnesty was granted to Xījīng, Liáodōng, and Běijīng.
In the eleventh month,
relief was provided for the drought-stricken areas of Hédōng Southern Circuit, Nánjīng Circuit, Shǎnxī Eastern Circuit, Shāndōng Western Circuit, and Wèizhōu.
In the twelfth month,
Lǐ Zūnxū, the King of Xià, expressed his gratitude for the investiture.
In the first month of the first year of Zhìníng,
famine relief was provided for Hédōng and Shǎnxī.
In the second month,
an imperial edict was issued to pacify and conciliate Liáodōng.
Wūgǔlùn Yì, the Administrator of Dàmíng Prefecture, plotted rebellion
and was executed.
In the third month,
the Moon and Venus were seen together with the sun,
about a chi apart.
In the fifth month,
the reign title was changed.
An imperial edict was issued to persuade the Qìdān people who had gathered in armed bands in Xiánpíng Circuit.
Húshāhǔ was reappointed as Right Assistant Marshal
and commanded 3,000 men of the Wǔwèi Jūn (Martial Guard Army) to garrison outside Tōngxuán Gate.
Shǎnxī suffered a great drought.
In the sixth month,
Xià people invaded Bǎo'ān Prefecture,
killing the Prefect,
and attacked Qìngyáng Prefecture,
killing the Assistant Administrator of the Prefecture.
Xū Dǐng, Minister of Revenue, and Wáng Wéihàn, Minister of Justice, were appointed Vice Grand Councilors.
In the eighth month,
Wányán Yuánnú, Assistant Director of the Left in the Department of State Affairs, led troops to guard the border.
An imperial edict ordered that military officers and soldiers be given rewards according to their rank.
There was a heavy fog,
and it was dark during the day.
Fúhǎi, the Supervisor of Administration, led a separate force to garrison north of the city.
On the day of Xīnmǎo,
Húshāhǔ issued a forged imperial edict to execute rebels,
summoned Fúhǎi, seized and killed him,
and took his troops.
On the day of Rénchén,
Húshāhǔ entered through Tōngxuán Gate,
killing Túdān Nánpíng, Administrator of Dàxīng Prefecture, and Túdān Mòniǎn, Vice Minister of Justice, west of Guǎngyáng Gate.
Fúhǎi's son, Keeper of the Talisman and Seal Shànyáng, and Commander-in-Chief Shígǔnǎi, led their men to resist and fight,
〔一０〕and died.
Húshāhǔ knocked at Dōnghuá Gate,
sending someone to call out to Dōng'ér, Captain of the Imperial Guard on duty, and Púcài Liùjīn, Commander of Fifty Households,
but they did not respond.
He promised them hereditary Méng'ān and third-rank official positions,
but they still did not respond.
Túdān Wèihé, the Grand Inspector, climbed down and came out,
and Xiéliè, an Imperial Guard, broke the lock and opened the gate.
Húshāhǔ entered the palace with his troops,
expelled all the palace guards,
replaced them with his partisans,
and proclaimed himself Regent and Grand Marshal.
On the day of Guǐsì,
he forced the emperor to leave the palace,
carried him in a plain carriage to his former residence,
and guarded him strictly with 200 men of the Wǔwèi Jūn.
Lady Zhèng, Lady of the Left in the Palace Administration, who
was in charge of the imperial seals,
heard of the trouble,
and sat upright at the place of the seals, awaiting the turn of events.
Húshāhǔ sent eunuchs to enter and seize the seals.
Lady Zhèng said:
"The seal
is used by the Son of Heaven.
Húshāhǔ is a subject.
What will he do by taking it?"
The eunuch said:
"Now the times have greatly changed,
and the Emperor himself cannot be guaranteed,
how much less the seal?
Your Ladyship should consider a plan to save yourself."
Lady Zhèng sternly cursed, saying:
"You close attendants in the palace,
who received exceptional favor,
did not repay your sovereign's crisis with death.
Instead, you would let this rebellious wretch seize the seal?
My death is certain;
the seal will certainly not be given."
Then she closed her eyes and said nothing.
The eunuch left,
and Húshāhǔ finally took
the "Seal of Imperial Edict,"

falsely appointing his partisans Chǒunú as Defense Commissioner of Dézhōu, Wūgǔlùn Duóluō as Military Commissioner of Shùntiān Commandery, Túdān Jīnshòu, General in Charge of Imperial Bodyguards, as Military Commissioner of Yǒngdìng Commandery,
and his other partisans, totaling several tens of people,
were all promoted in office.
Then he ordered the eunuch Lǐ Sīzhōng to harm the emperor at his residence.
He enticed Héshang, an Imperial Attendant, to write a letter urgently summoning his father, Assistant Director Yuánnú, to discuss matters.
Yuánnú came with troops,
but both he and his son were killed.
On the day of Jiǎchén in the ninth month,
Emperor Xuānzōng ascended the throne.
On the day of Dīngwèi,
he went to the residence to personally offer sacrifices,
prostrated and wept with utmost sorrow.
An imperial edict ordered a reburial with proper rites.
Húshāhǔ requested that the emperor be deposed as a commoner.
An imperial edict ordered all officials to deliberate in the imperial court,
and over 200 people deliberated.
Àotún Zhōngxiào, Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince, and Púchá Sīzhōng, Academician Attendant-in-Waiting, requested to follow the deposition.
Wǔdū, Minister of Revenue, Tián Tíngfāng, Corrector of Omissions, and thirty others requested to demote him to a prince or marquis.
Zhāng Xíngjiǎn, Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince, requested to use the precedents of King Chāngyì of Hàn and Duke Hǎixī of Jìn.
Wányán Échū, Imperial Censor, and ten others requested to demote him and restore him to a princely title.
Húshāhǔ stubbornly insisted on the previous proposal.
Emperor Xuānzōng had no choice but
to demote and enfeoff him as Marquis of Dōnghǎi Commandery.
Empress consort Lǐ of Dàolíng and Imperial Concubine Jiǎ were exonerated.
On the day of Xīnhài in the tenth month,
Shúhǔ Gāoqí, Right Army Supervisor of the Marshal, killed Húshāhǔ at his residence.
Húshāhǔ
was Hèshíliè Zhízhōng.
Emperor Xuānzōng then issued an edict stripping him of his official rank and title.
Shígǔnǎi was posthumously granted the title of Prefect of Shùnzhōu,
and Shànyáng as Vice Military Commissioner of Shùntiān Commandery.
〔一一〕All those who followed the two to resist and fight,
Commanders of a Thousand Households were awarded 500 guàn,
Myoke Commanders 300 guàn,
Púliǎn irregular soldiers 200 guàn,
each promoted two ranks,
and those who died in battle were posthumously awarded, and the awards given to their families.
Dōng'ér was promoted to General of the Dragon and Tiger Guard,
and further promoted to General of Imperial Bodyguards.
Púcài Liùjīn was promoted to Grand General Pacifying Distant Lands and Commander of the Wǔwèi Jūn (Martial Guard Army).
Shígǔnǎi's son was still young,
and was given a stipend of eight guàn and shí.
The relevant officials were ordered
to report when he reached fifteen years old.
In the fourth year of Zhēnyòu,
an imperial edict posthumously restored the Prince of Wèi and gave him the posthumous title Shào.
The eulogy says: Prince Wèi Shào's rule was chaotic internally,
and his armies were defeated externally;
his downfall already had signs.
He was assassinated, and the country was constricted.
Records were lost,
and after the move south, they were no longer recorded.
In the third year of Zhōngtǒng of this Imperial dynasty,
Wáng È, Academician Grandee of the Hanlin Academy, intended to write a treatise.
He sought records of the Dà'ān and Chóngqìng eras but could not obtain them.
He collected imperial edicts and orders of that time.
Dòu Xiáng, a former clerk of the Ministry of Revenue, was eighty-nine years old
with sharp ears and eyes,
and could remember old events.
From him, over 20 items were obtained.
Zhāng Zhèngzhī, Commissioner of the Bureau of Astronomy, wrote down 16 items of calamities and anomalies.
Academician Grandee Zhāng's family notes recorded 5 items of old events.
Yáng Yúnyì, Jin Minister of Rites, had 40 items in his daily records.
Elder Chén had 30 items in his daily records.
These were stored in the Imperial History Institute.
Although there were many entries,
two-thirds were repetitions.
Only those recorded about Consort Lǐ, Wányán Kuāng's settling of the succession,
Dújí Qiānjiānú's army defeat,
Hèshíliè Zhízhōng's rebellion,
and solar eclipses, celestial anomalies, earthquakes, and ominous portents
did not contradict each other.
Now, comparing the repetitions
and deleting the redundancy,
the Veritable Records of Zhāngzōng detailed the preceding events,
and the Veritable Records of Xuānzōng detailed the subsequent events.
Also, from what was recorded by Lady Wáng, Dàmíng Jūshì, a Jin female official in charge of memorials,
the matter of Lady Zīmíng saving the seal was obtained
and appended to this chapter,
which can also preserve its general outline.
Collator's Notes
Annals, Chapter 14: Xuānzōng (Part 1)
Xuānzōng Jìtiān Xīngtǒng Shùdào Qínrén Yīngwǔ Shèngxiào Huángdì, given name Xún,
originally named Wúdūbǔ,
was the eldest son of Xiǎnzōng.
His mother was Zhaohuá Liú Shì.
He was born in the guǐwèi year, the third year of Dàdìng (1163).
Shìzōng raised him within the palace.
In the eighteenth year (1178),
he was enfeoffed as Wēnguó Gōng
and granted the title Tèjìn.
In the twenty-sixth year (1186),
he was bestowed his current name.
In the twenty-ninth year (1189),
he was promoted to Fēng Wáng
and granted the title Kāifǔ Yítóng Sānsī.
He successively served as supervising judge for the Ministries of War and Personnel,
and also for the armies of Yǒngdìng and Zhāngdé.
In the first year of Chéng'ān (1196),
he was promoted to Yì Wáng.
In the fifth year of Tàihé (1205),
his name was changed to Cóngjiā.
In the eighth year (1208),
he was promoted to Xíng Wáng,
and then enfeoffed as Shēng Wáng.
Auspicious anomalies were noted wherever he went.
In the eighth month of the first year of Zhìníng (1213),
Wèishào Wáng was assassinated.
Túdān Míng and others welcomed him at Zhāngdé Fǔ.
Upon his arrival in the capital,
the imperial princes and all officials submitted memorials urging him to ascend the throne.
On the jiǎchén day of the ninth month,
he ascended the imperial throne at Dà'ān Diàn.
He appointed Gēshíliè Húshāhǔ as Tàishī, Shàngshū Lìng, and concurrently Dū Yuánshuài,
and enfeoffed him as Zé Wáng.
On the yǐsì day,
he issued an edict to the Shàngshū Shěng,
stating that any matters requiring planning should be planned immediately,
and all should follow the precedents established by Shìzōng.
On the bǐngwǔ day,
the mansion of the駙馬 Xióng Míng was bestowed upon Húshāhǔ.
On the dīngwèi day,
he instructed his chief ministers, saying:
"Now that I have ascended the great throne,
my ministers, if you have any insights,
speak them frankly and do not conceal them."
He personally went to mourn at Wèishào Wáng's residence.
The officials in charge reported
that according to ancient rites, a seat should be set for crying.
The Emperor ordered the seat removed
and prostrated himself to weep with utmost grief.
He commanded the officials
to rebury him with proper rites.
On the wùshēn day,
he held court at Rénzhèng Diàn.
He granted Húshāhǔ a seat,
which Húshāhǔ did not decline.
On the xīnhài day,
he enfeoffed his imperial son Shǒulǐ as Suí Wáng,
Shǒuchún as Pú Wáng,
and his imperial daughter as Wēnguó Gōngzhǔ.
Kuí Wáng Yǒngshēng died,
and the Emperor personally attended the mourning.
The Great Yuán sent Yǐlǐzhī to visit.
On the rénzǐ day,
the era name was changed to Zhēnyòu,
and a general amnesty was declared.
Favors and rewards were bestowed upon officials and common people both within and outside the capital, with varying degrees.
On the bǐngchén day,
the Left Grand Remonstrance Counselor Zhāng Xíngxìn submitted a memorial discussing three matters: promoting frugality, broadly accepting advice, and clearly administering rewards and punishments.
The Shàngshū Right Chancellor Túdān Yì was promoted to Left Chancellor
and enfeoffed as Guǎngpíng Jùnwáng.
On the gēngshēn day,
Zé Wáng Húshāhǔ and others proposed to demote the former Wèi Wáng to a commoner.
The Emperor said:
"I will consider this slowly
and then inform you."
On the rénxū day,
Húshāhǔ was granted the hereditary title of Méng'ān of Héluòhūtǔ in Zhōngdū Lù.
On the bǐngyín day,
an edict was issued to officials of the sixth rank and below,
stating that if they had anything to say, they should speak it without concealment.
On the wùchén day, the first day of the intercalary month,
he worshipped the sun at Rénzhèng Diàn;
thereafter, this became a regular practice on an auspicious day each month.
The Shàngshū Left Chancellor Túdān Yì was granted the title of Diélǔ Méng'ān of Zhōngdū Lù.
On the gēngwǔ day,
the Emperor reverted to his old name Xún,
and commanded the relevant authorities
to inform Heaven, Earth, and the ancestral temples.
The two characters of the previously changed names
no longer needed to be avoided from this day forth.
On the xīnwèi day,
an edict was issued to posthumously honor his imperial mother as Huáng Tàihòu.
On this day,
the imperial consort and imperial sons arrived from Zhāngdé Fǔ.
Envoys were dispatched to Sòng.
On the jǐmǎo day,
the Left Grand Remonstrance Counselor Zhāng Xíngxìn submitted a memorial requesting the establishment of an imperial crown prince.
On the jiǎshēn day,
his son Shǒuzhōng was established as the Imperial Crown Prince.
On the bǐngxū day,
an edict demoted the former Wèi Wáng to Dōnghǎi Jùnhóu.
On the jiǎwǔ day,
the number of Censor-in-Chiefs was reduced and fixed at twelve.
On the dīngyǒu day, the first day of the tenth month of winter,
the capital declared a state of emergency.
On the xīnchǒu day,
Yǐlǐzhī of the Great Yuán arrived.
On the yǐsì day,
an edict stated that all promotions and awards,
for people of all backgrounds, would be treated equally with those of the imperial court.
On the gēngxū day,
the Emperor commanded the relevant authorities
that the investiture ceremony for the Imperial Crown Prince
should be held after the border conflict had ceased.
On the xīnhài day,
Yuánshuài Right Supervisor of the Army Shúhǔ Gāoqí fought north of the city.
After two defeats, he returned,
and then used his soldiers to kill Húshāhǔ at his residence.
He presented Húshāhǔ's head at the imperial palace, awaiting punishment.
He was pardoned
and subsequently appointed Left Vice Marshal.
On the rénzǐ day,
the Palace Grand Commandant Gēshíliè Tèmòyě and others were reassigned to posts outside the capital.
On the jiǎyín day,
Zhāng Xíngxìn submitted a sealed memorial,
discussing correcting punishments and rewards, selecting generals,
and the injustices suffered by Shànyáng and Shígǔnǎi.
The Great Yuán army descended upon Zhuōzhōu.
Officials for pacification and suppression were established for the capital city.
A Bureau for Recruiting Worthies was set up.
On the guǐhài day,
one hundred and thirty palace women were released.
On the wùchén day of the eleventh month,
the Xià people attacked Huìzhōu,
and Túdān Chǒu'ér led troops to defeat them.
On the gēngwǔ day,
intending to seek peace with the Great Yuán,
the Emperor ordered all officials to discuss the matter at the Shàngshū Shěng.
Chénghuī, the Military Commissioner of Hénghǎi Army, was appointed Shàngshū Right Chancellor,
and Gěng Duānyì was made Cānzhī Zhèngshì.
On the guǐwèi day,
an edict posthumously granted official titles to Pèimǎn Fúxīng, Shànyáng, and Shígǔnǎi, who died in service.
The Great Yuán army plundered Guānzhōu,
and its Prefect Gāo Shǒuyuē died.
They also plundered Héjiān Fǔ and Cāngzhōu.
On the yǐwèi day,
regulations for lost official documents and diplomas were established.
On the dīngyǒu day, the first day of the twelfth month,
the Emperor ascended Yìngtiān Mén,
issued an edict to the soldiers,
and distributed silver to them.
The Píngzhāng Zhèngshì Túdān Gōngbì was promoted to Shàngshū Right Chancellor.
The Shàngshū Right Chancellor Chénghuī was promoted to Dū Yuánshuài and concurrently Píngzhāng Zhèngshì.
The Left Vice Marshal Shúhǔ Gāoqí was promoted to Píngzhāng Zhèngshì and concurrently retained his former post.
On the dīngmǎo day, the first day of the first month of spring in the second year (1214),
due to ongoing border conflicts,
an edict exempted officials from offering New Year's greetings.
On the xīnwèi day,
the Great Yuán army plundered Zhāngdé Fǔ,
and the Acting Prefect Huángguá Jiǔzhù died.
The Sòng people attacked Qínzhōu,
and the Commander Shímò Zhòngwēn repelled them.
On the guǐwèi day,
the officials reported
requesting to temporarily suspend this year's dì, xiǎng, cháoxiàn, yuánmiào rituals and the investiture ceremony for the Empress Dowager.
This was approved.
On the yǐyǒu day,
the recluse Wáng Huì was summoned,
but he did not come.
The Great Yuán army plundered Yìdū Fǔ.
The authorities were ordered to re-discuss the imperial dynasty's virtue and fortune.
On the yǐwèi day,
the Great Yuán army plundered Huáizhōu,
and the Military Commissioner of Qìnnán Army, Sòng Yǐ, died.
On the bǐngshēn day, the first day of the second month.
On the rénzǐ day,
Yǐlǐzhī Zhábā of the Great Yuán arrived.
On the bǐngchén day,
the Surveillance Commissions were abolished.
On the rénxū day,
Yǐlǐzhī of the Great Yuán came again.
In the third month, on the day Xīnwèi,
Chénghuī was sent to Dàyuán to request peace.
On the day Dīngchǒu,
an amnesty was granted within the country.
On the day Guǐwèi,
the capital extensively requisitioned grain.
On the day Jiǎshēn,
Yǐlǐzhī Zhābā of Dàyuán arrived.
An imperial edict ordered all officials to deliberate in the Shàngshū Shěng.
On the day Wùzǐ,
Púwáng Shǒuchún was made Diànqián Dū Diǎnjiǎn concurrently Shìwèi Qīnjūn Dū Zhīhuīshǐ,
acting as Dū Yuánshuàifǔ Shì.
On the day Gēngyín,
Wèishàowáng's princess was sent back to Dàyuán Tàizǔ Huángdì,
who became Princess Empress.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
an imperial edict permitted all people to offer grain in exchange for official positions.
The capital was put under martial law.
On the day Rénchén,
Dàyuán troops descended upon Lánzhōu,
and Zhènxījūn Jiédùshǐ Wūgǔlún Zhòngwēn died there.
In summer, in the fourth month, on the first day Yǐwèi,
Xū Dǐng, who was Zhī Dàxīngfǔ Shì, was made Shàngshū Yòuchéng.
On the day Wùxū,
the coffin of Zhāoshèng Huánghòu was moved to Xīnsì.
At this time, various commanderies in Shāndōng and Héběi were lost,
with only a few cities remaining, namely Zhēndìng, Qīng, Wò, Dàmíng, Dōngpíng, Xú, Pī, and Hǎi.
Many prefectures and counties in Hédōng were also ruined and burned.
After the troops retreated,
Púsàn Ānzhēn and others were appointed as Zhū Lù Xuānfǔshǐ,
to settle the remaining populace.
By this time, Dàyuán had agreed to the peace negotiations,
and a general amnesty was granted nationwide.
On the day Guǐmǎo,
Zhāoshèng Huánghòu was temporarily interred at Xīnsì.
On the day Jiǎchén,
an imperial edict ordered the relevant authorities to list the descendants of those who died in battle for future employment.
On the day Dīngwèi,
Dū Yuánshuài Chénghuī was made Yòuchéngxiàng.
On the day Gēngxū,
Zuǒchéngxiàng and Jiānxiū Guóshǐ, Guǎngpíngjùn Wáng Túyú Yì, passed away.
On the day Yǐmǎo,
the Shàngshū Shěng proposed an imperial tour to Nánjīng,
and an imperial edict approved it.
On the day Jǐwèi,
Wèishàowáng was buried.
In the fifth month, on the day Guǐyǒu,
Chénghuī was promoted to Jīnzǐ Guānglù Dàfū,
and enfeoffed as Dìngguó Gōng.
Shàngshū Zuǒchéng Mòyán Jìnzhōng was promoted further,
and enfeoffed as Shēnguó Gōng.
On the day Jiǎxū,
Huòwáng Cóngyí passed away.
On the day Yǐhài,
the court was suspended.
The Emperor resolved to move south,
and an imperial edict announced it to the country.
Tàixuéshēng Zhào Fǎng and others submitted memorials strongly arguing for and against the plan,
but as the grand strategy had already been decided,
it could not be halted.
They were all consoled and dismissed.
The Emperor proceeded to the ancestral temples to bid farewell.
On the day Wùyín,
the Emperor was about to depart,
but it rained,
so the journey was not undertaken.
As Nánjīng Liúshǒu Púsàn Duān and others had previously requested an imperial visit,
when the journey was about to begin,
an edict was first issued to inform them.
On the day Xīnsì,
an imperial edict ordered the relocation of Wèishào, Hàolìwáng's families to Zhèngzhōu.
On the day Rénwǔ,
the imperial carriage departed from Zhōngdū.
It rained on this day,
and stopped on Jiǎshēn.
On the day Bǐngxū,
the entourage reached Dìngxīng.
Officials accompanying the Emperor were forbidden from trampling on people's fields.
On the day Dīnghài,
the entourage reached Ānsùzhōu,
where Yuánshuài Yòujiānjūn Wányán Bì met them with troops.
On the day Guǐsì,
the entourage reached Zhōngshānfǔ,
and an imperial order stipulated that any crops trampled by the accompanying army
should be compensated at their value.
In the sixth month, on the first day Jiǎwǔ,
Gāo Rǔlì, who was Ànchá Zhuǎnyùnshǐ, was made Cānzhī Zhèngshì.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
the entourage reached Nèiqiū Xiàn.
Yǐlǐzhī of Dàyuán arrived.
On the day Wùwǔ,
the entourage reached Zhāngdé Fǔ,
and a partial amnesty was granted within its territory.
On the day Gēngshēn,
the entourage reached Jùqiáo Zhèn.
On this day,
the Bǎozhèn Gé of the Nánjīng Xínggōng caught fire.
On the day Rénxū,
the entourage reached Yícūn.
A yellow dragon was seen in the northwest.
In autumn, in the seventh month,
the imperial carriage arrived at Nánjīng.
An imperial edict established the primary consort Wēndūn Shì as empress.
In the eighth month, on the day Jiǎwǔ,
due to the establishment of the empress,
all officials submitted memorials of congratulation.
On the day Gēngzǐ,
the Crown Prince arrived from Zhōngdū.
On the day Dīngwèi,
Xià people entered the border,
and an order was given to issue a dispatch to reprimand them.
On the day Jiǎyín,
the Jīngluè Sī was abolished.
Yīngfèng Hànlín Wénzì Wányán Sùlán submitted a memorial concerning affairs.
In the ninth month, on the first day Rénxū,
there was a solar eclipse.
The imperial grandson was born.
On the day Guǐhài,
the Shāndōng Lù reported a victory at Láizhōu.
On the day Xīnwèi,
regulations for the promotion and demotion of supervising censors were established.
On the day Gēngchén,
an imperial edict ordered the training of soldiers.
On the day Dīnghài,
the Xuānhuī Yuàn was instructed
that no gifts were necessary for New Year's Day and the imperial birthday.
Tàibái was seen in the daytime in Zhěn constellation.
On the day Wùzǐ,
military officers were forbidden from hunting in groups.
In winter, in the tenth month, on the day Jiǎwǔ,
an imperial edict ordered officials to purchase Mùbō and Xīqiāng horses.
Families of soldiers from Shǎnxī who died in battle were given grain to support them.
On the day Dīngyǒu,
Dàyuán troops attacked Shùnzhōu,
and Quànnóngshǐ Wáng Huì died there.
On the day Rényín,
Zuǒfù Yuánshuài concurrently Shàngshū Zuǒchéng Mòyán Jìnzhōng was promoted to Píngzhāng Zhèngshì.
Yùshǐ Zhōngchéng Bóshùlǔ Déyù was made Cānzhī Zhèngshì concurrently Qiān Shūmìyuàn Shì.
A partial amnesty was granted in Zhōngdū Lù.
On the day Yǐmǎo,
Cānzhī Zhèngshì Bóshùlǔ Déyù was dispatched to head the Shàngshū Shěng at Dàmíng Fǔ.
On the day Bǐngchén,
Dàyuán troops captured Chéngzhōu.
Dàmíng Xíngshěng was instructed
to reduce expenses.
Dézhōu Fángyùshǐ Wányán Chǒunú was executed.
In the eleventh month, on the day Dīngmǎo,
Yùshǐ Dàfū Púsàn Duān was made Shàngshū Zuǒchéngxiàng.
A partial amnesty was granted in Shāndōng Lù.
On the day Xīnwèi,
an imperial edict granted provisions to Wèishàowáng's family.
An imperial edict ordered the relevant authorities to reply to the Xià state's dispatch.
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
people of all occupations were permitted to take the military examination.
Lánzhōu interpreter Chéng Chénsēng rebelled,
and allied with the Xià people for support.
On the day Xīn Sǐ,
Yínghuò trespassed upon the Hóugēnxīng of Fáng constellation.
On the day Guǐwèi,
a partial amnesty was granted in Liáodōng Lù.
An imperial order abolished the Xuánfǔ Sī's arbitrary appointments of officials.
In the twelfth month, on the day Wùxū,
Zhēndìng Xíng Yuánshuàifǔ Shì Yǒngxī and others were dispatched to reinforce Zhōngdū.
An edict encouraging agriculture was issued.
On the day Dīngwèi,
as the peace negotiations were settled,
people were allowed to cross south.
On the day Yǐmǎo,
Dēngzhōu Cìshǐ Gěng Gé was executed,
and his wife and children were exiled.
Dàyuán troops attacked Yìzhōu,
and Jiédùshǐ Gāo Lǘshān died there.
In the spring, first month, *xīnyǒu* day, the first day of the month, of the third year
Sòng sent an envoy to offer congratulations.
On the *rénxū* day,
an internal attendant was dispatched to instruct Yǒngxī to guard the border,
and not to use peace talks as an excuse.
On the *guǐhài* day,
a relaxed banquet was held for the numerous officials and the Sòng envoy.
The number of civil and military officials of the fifth rank and above allowed to attend the emperor was determined,
and this became a permanent system.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
an imperial edict ordered宣撫 Āhǎi and 總管 Hézhù to suppress the rebels Liú Èrzǔ and Zhāng Rǔjí.
On the *wùchén* day,
the Shangshū Shěng reported:
"Many internal and external military personnel obtain official positions by contributing grain,
causing the ranks to become increasingly hollow.
We request that after pacification,
those eligible for supervisory duties be given three promotions,
those with hereditary official positions be promoted one rank,
and their sons and younger brothers eligible for荫* (hereditary privilege) be dismissed."
The Emperor approved the memorial.
On the *yǐhài* day,
the Xià people raided Huánzhōu.
The Běijīng army mutinied,
killing the 宣撫使 Àotún Xiāng.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
the 右副元帥 Púchá Qījīn surrendered with his army to the Dà Yuán.
On the *xīnsì* day,
the Crown Prince fell ill.
Court was suspended.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
the Crown Prince passed away.
In the second month, on the *xīnmǎo* day,
Huánzhōu Cìshǐ Wūgǔlùn Yánshòu and Xiémǎo Máoliánghǔ, among others, defeated the Xià people in the prefecture's territory,
and an imperial edict ordered varying promotions for them.
Dà Yuán Yǐlǐzhī arrived.
On the *rénchén* day,
the Emperor personally attended the Crown Prince's funeral.
The officials in charge of rites reported that it was improper to mourn on a *chén* day,
but the Emperor said:
"Father and son are intimately close;
how can one be constrained by taboos?"
He ordered 御史中丞 Lǐ Yīng and 元帥左都監 Wūgǔlùn Qìngshòu to lead troops to escort provisions to Zhōngdū,
giving them blank imperial edicts,
permitting promotion based on merit,
and stipulating that those who hesitated would be punished according to military law.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
Níngbiānzhōu was reorganized and placed under Lánzhōu.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
an imperial edict ordered that promotions for people of all classes should be treated the same as for Nǚzhí people.
Officials who arbitrarily made distinctions
would be judged as violating the regulations.
This was in accordance with the request of Hùbù Lángzhōng Àotún Āhǔ.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
an imperial decree ordered the prime ministers to provide wine and food to Yǐlǐzhī.
On the *rényín* day,
an imperial edict was issued to award and admonish officials, soldiers, and common people,
granting a general amnesty,
and appealing to those who had revolted in Běijīng to surrender.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
the Shangshū Shěng reported that after the move south,
the Lìbù held selections in Nánjīng in autumn and winter,
and in Zhōngdū in spring and summer.
This was inconvenient for those coming for selection,
so they requested that all selections be combined in Nánjīng.
This was approved.

Wǔqīng Xiàn Xúnjiǎn Liáng Zuǒ and Liǔkǒu Xúnjiǎn Lǐ Yǎozhù were promoted with varying ranks for their meritorious service in executing the treacherous rebels Zhāng Huī and Liú Yǒngchāng, among others,
and all were granted the surname Wányán.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
Shāndōng Xuānfǔshǐ Púsàn Ānzhēn dispatched Tíkòng Púsàn Liújiā and others to defeat the rebel Yáng Ān'ér's army of thirty thousand infantry and cavalry,
annihilating their forces,
and causing over three hundred pseudo-leaders and over thirty thousand coerced common households to surrender.
On the *wùshēn* day,
the official salaries and appraisals for border prefectures and sub-prefectures were reduced by varying degrees.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
regulations were established for rewards for securing garrisons and capturing traitors and rebels.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
an imperial decree ordered that urgent matters were not subject to holiday restrictions.
On the *dīngsì* day,
the sun at sunrise was red like blood,
and it was the same again at sunset.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
there was a great wind,
and the *chīwěi* (ridge ornament) of Lóngdé Diàn was damaged.
In the third month, on the *rénxū* day,
an imperial edict was issued to officials in Héběi prefectures and counties,
stating that civil and military officials of the fifth rank and above should be appointed by recommendation,
and not be allowed to be transferred or occupied by other matters.
It was also decreed that they should serve their full term.
Those with meritorious service would only be promoted to a titular position,
and those subject to demotion or punishment would also remain in their original place of residence.
At that time, Héběi was ravaged,
and many officials were perfunctory in their governance, seeking to be replaced.
Thus, this order was issued.
On the *guǐhài* day,
an imperial edict ordered all officials to memorialize on the advantages and disadvantages of border defense,
submitting their sealed reports.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
an imperial decree ordered the chief and secondary officials of Hédōng, Héběi, and Dàmíng to train local righteous militias.
If a neighboring area was alarmed,
they would be held responsible for providing assistance.
Defectors who returned to the country on their own would be promoted,
and their names would be listed
to attract others.
Officials in prefectures and counties along the river who were weak and unfit for their duties would be dismissed,
and officials of the fifth rank and above were to publicly recommend replacements,
also allowing for capable individuals among those who arrived at the ministry this season to be chosen first and replaced according to urgency.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
Ānwǔ Jūn Jiédùshǐ Zhāng Xíngxìn submitted a memorial proposing four urgent matters.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
an imperial instruction was given to Liáodōng Xuānfǔshǐ Púxiān Wànnú to select elite troops to garrison Shěnzhōu and Guǎngníng,
awaiting further orders.
On the *rénshēn* day,
Chángchūn Jié (Emperor's birthday),
Sòng sent an envoy to offer congratulations.
On the *wùyín* day,
an imperial instruction was given to the Shangshū Shěng,
stating that due to the drought,
they should discuss suspending the operation of mills in various places,
so that their water could irrigate the people's fields.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
it rained.
There had been no rain or snow since last winter,
and it only started raining now.
Quànnóng Shǐ Lǐ Gé
stated:
"Many officials in Héběi prefectures and counties seek transfer to Hénán to avoid hardship.
It would be appropriate to send those originally appointed to lead garrison troops.
If they cannot leave, they should be specially assigned to go."
On the *gēngchén* day,
the Yùshǐ Tái reported:
"Military officers in the capital and officials assigned to duties, their fodder and grain vouchers are all treated the same as those on campaigns.
We request a reduction in their provisions.
Personnel with salaries assigned by the Shūmìyuàn, if not on campaign, should not be given provisions."
All were approved.
An imperial decree was issued to the Shangshū Shěng,
stating that those who obtained official positions by contributing grain should not have their households conscripted into the army.
The relevant authorities should discuss military rewards,
and not obstruct them.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
the Shāndōng Xuānfǔ Sī reported a victory at Dàmògū.
Jiágǔ Shí Lǐgē and Mòliè captured and executed the rebel leader Liú Èrzǔ and others,
killing tens of thousands of rebels both before and after.
The military and civilians in Xījīng rebelled,
and an official was dispatched to appease them.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
prefectures and counties were forbidden from placing blades on staffs when punishing criminals.
The previous year,
Jīngzhào Zhìzhōng Lǐ Yǒuzhí secretly fled to Huázhōu,
and conspired with Tóngzhī Fángyùshǐ Féng Cháo, Hézhōu Fángyù Pànguān Hǎo Zūnfǔ, Píngliáng Fǔ Tóngzhī Zhìshì Yáng Tíngxiù, Shuǐluò Xiàn Zhǔbù Sù Huī, and others to gather the prefectural people,
calling themselves
"Zhōngyì Hùjià Dūwèifǔ" (Loyal and Righteous Imperial Escort Commandery),
inciting rebellion.
They killed the Fángyù Pànguān Wányán Bājīn and the Nǚzhí people in the city,
and sent a letter to Dūtǒng Yáng Guī,
which was intercepted by the guard's troops.
Guī concealed this,
and requested to prove his loyalty by luring Yǒuzhí and others to capture them,
and ordering the more than one thousand people he had recruited to lay down their weapons and be buried alive outside the city.
At that time, roads to the capital were cut off,
so the Ānfǔ Sī summarily executed Yǒuzhí and his relatives,
and reported it now.
Therefore, Bājīn and more than ten other officers and soldiers who were killed were each posthumously granted one official rank,
and given a funeral allowance of three hundred *guàn* of cash.
In the summer, fourth month, on the day Guǐsì,
Xū Dǐng, the Pacification Commissioner of Hédōng, reported on thirteen matters of concern.
Yáng Guī, the Military Commissioner of the Chángshèng Army, was executed.
On the day Bǐngshēn,
locusts appeared in Hénán Circuit,
and officials were dispatched to capture them.
The emperor instructed his chief ministers, saying:
“When I was in the imperial residence,
I heard that those who catch locusts only do so along the roadside,
and where the envoys are not present, they pay no attention.
This intention should be emphasized to them.”
Déshēng, Acting Grand Councilor, said:
“According to the old system, after the summer solstice, court audiences were suspended,
and reports were submitted once every four days.”
The emperor said:
“This might be acceptable in peacetime.
But at present, there are many difficulties.
Do not think I am weary,
and thus say it should be waived;
it is only good if state affairs are not neglected.”
On the day Jǐhài,
a partial amnesty was granted to Shāndōng Circuit.
On the day Guǐmǎo,
officials selected for supervisorial posts were registered as soldiers.
On the day Yǐsì,
the Six Boards in Dōunánxíng were abolished.
Hóu Zhì spoke on nine matters.
A partial amnesty was granted to the followers of Púchá Qīyǐn who were coerced,
and a reward was offered to anyone who could kill or capture Qīyǐn,
giving them his official position.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
due to insufficient resources,
all officials of the sixth rank and below attending court, and those providing services,
were exempted from contributing their own laborers' wages.
In prefectures and sub-prefectures affected by war, the number of clerks was halved;
in departments and counties, it was reduced by one-third.
For all others, except for Kāifēng Prefecture and Nánjīng Transport Office,
the reduction was generally one-third.
Officials with salaries who were appointed but did not leave their home territory had their vouchers revoked;
those who left their territory were given half.
The number of military laborers in the Bureau of Palace Construction was also halved.
On the day Dīngwèi,
the coffin of the deceased Crown Prince was moved,
and he was posthumously granted the title Zhuāngxiàn.
On the day Wùshēn,
he was temporarily buried outside Yíngshuò Gate.
An imperial edict stated that from now on, for jinshì who excelled in policy essays and rhapsodies,
the first place in the first class would be specially promoted to Fèngzhí Dàfū,
the second place and below, and the first place in classical studies, would all be Rúlín Láng,
the second class and below would be Zhēngshì Láng,
those with the title Tóng Jinshì would be Cóngshì Láng,
and classical scholars (jīngtóng) would be Jiāngshì Láng.
On the day Rénzǐ,
Cónghòu, Duke of Ruì, passed away.
An imperial edict ordered envoys to be dispatched with the Shānxī Pacification Commission to select strong and brave men from among the populace to serve as soldiers.
Officials were instructed
not to refuse refugees from Héběi,
but to provide relief wherever they arrived.
Following the advice of Wányán Bì, the Deputy Pacification Commissioner of the Western Shāndōng Circuit,
the bandit leaders Sūn Bāngzuǒ and Zhāng Rǔjí from Dàmògù were recruited with fifth-rank positions,
and an imperial edict was issued to pardon their crimes.
On the day Yǐmǎo,
an imperial edict ordered an inspection of the court's official appointment vouchers and records,
and those who deliberately delayed mid-journey without cause would be punished.
On the day Bǐngchén,
Tián Zhuó was instructed to retain the young and able-bodied displaced people from Shānxī for military service,
while the old and young were to be sent to Xíng and Míng prefectures for food,
and those who wished to go to Hénán were permitted.
The emperor discussed sending over six thousand imperial guards and two thousand seven hundred recruited men to reinforce Zhōngdū.
The chief ministers believed that the temporary imperial residence was vulnerable,
and the imperial guards could not be sent,
so the plan was abandoned.
In the fifth month, on the day Gēngshēn,
the military and civilians of Shānxī were invited to surrender,
and an imperial edict was issued to them.
On this day,
Zhōngdū fell,
and Chénghuī, Duke of Dìngguó, concurrently Grand Marshal and Right Chancellor of the Department of State Affairs, died.
Rèn Tiānchǒng, Minister of Revenue, and Gāo Lín, Prefect of Dàxīng Prefecture, also perished in the calamity.
On the day Rénxū,
blank imperial edicts, purple robes, and monk certificates (dùdié) were issued
to replenish military provisions.
On the day Xīnwèi,
Kēng, the imperial grandson, was appointed Grand Imperial Grandson.
On the day Guǐyǒu,
Liú Bǐng submitted a memorial on ten matters.
On the day Xīnsì,
the emperor instructed his chief ministers:
“In this time of many difficulties,
all submitted proposals should be sent to the province.
Fearing that you, ministers, might not have time,
I will set up a bureau in the palace,
and appoint several upright officials to select those that can be adopted for implementation.
What do you think?”
The chief ministers requested to follow the imperial instruction.
An imperial edict abolished the preferential treatment of acquiring official positions by presenting horses.
On the day Wùzǐ,
a plan to attack Xīxià was discussed,
and a high official was dispatched to pacify Jīngzhào.
In the autumn, seventh month, on the first day Wùwǔ,
the army of Dàyuán captured Jìyuán County.
On the day Jǐwèi,
bows and arrows were levied from officials of all ranks,
three sets for third rank and above,
two sets for fourth and fifth rank,
and the rest according to their grade.
On the day Gēngshēn,
officials were appointed to oversee grain transport in Chén and Yǐng,
with officials from the Ministry of Revenue dispatched to supervise.
A star like Tàibái,
blue-white in color,
with a tail,
appeared near the North Pole in the Zǐwēi asterism,
and entered Guànsuǒ.
The emperor heard that inspecting officials in Héběi were demanding money from the people before allowing them to cross the river,
and that many refugees died of starvation or drowned themselves.
He specially ordered the Censorate to investigate this.
He also prohibited attending officials from seizing people's mills for personal profit.
An imperial edict ordered the transfer of soldiers and civilians from the isolated city of Héjiān to Qīngzhōu for provisions,
and the confiscation of mules from the populace for military use,
to be used interchangeably with horses.
On the day Xīnyǒu,
it was discussed to appropriate public land and pastureland to support the military households from Héběi who had moved to Hénán,
and land already leased to civilians would be handed over after the harvest.
The ministers successively argued against its inconvenience,
and so it was shelved.
On the day Guǐhài,
an imperial edict ordered that military provisions for prefectures and counties in Héběi be halved compared to Hénán.
The various tallies created by the Department of State Affairs were designated:
deer for the Bureau of Military Affairs,
fish for the Pacification Commission,
and tiger for the Military Command.
On the day Bǐngyín,
Gāo Rǔlì, Grand Councilor, was dispatched to Hénán
to expediently manage grain storage.
The order for officials to contribute bows and arrows was enacted,
but those in mourning or who had retired were exempt.
On the day Jiǎxū,
the rent of Píngyáng residents was borrowed for one year.
An imperial edict stated that for officials whose credentials were lost during military service,
those currently in office would be reissued based on verification,
while fraudulent claims would be subject to fraud laws.
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
the Department of State Affairs proposed giving the Grand Imperial Grandson an annual stipend.
The emperor did not agree,
saying:
“What use would an infant have for it?”
An imperial edict ordered that the stipends of retired officials be halved compared to the period of the southern expedition.
On the day Dīngchǒu,
the spirit tablet of Sùzōng arrived from Zhōngdū
and was enshrined in the Míngjùn Hall.
On the day Wùyín,
the moon entered the constellation Bì,
and at night it encroached upon the main star of Bì.
On the day Jǐmǎo,
the spirit tablet of Empress Míngdé arrived from Zhōngdū.
Annual palace expenditures were reduced by varying amounts.
On the day Jiǎshēn,
an imperial edict was issued to the Department of State Affairs,
stating that the Six Boards were too many,
and ordering that the transport commissions of various circuits concurrently handle their duties.
The name of the paper currency was changed to
“Zhēnyòu Bǎojuàn”.
On the *wùzǐ* day of the eighth month, the first day of the lunar month,
Wán Yán Hédá, Administrator-in-Chief of Shǎnxī, was appointed Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
an imperial decree was issued that for all miscellaneous matters of the military prefectures, the officials of the Bureau of Military Affairs must make decisions with the *jīnglì* officials.
If the *jīnglì* officials' deliberation was correct but the bureau officials did not follow it,
they were permitted to report it directly to the throne.
On the *guǐsì* day,
an imperial edict ordered officials to be dispatched to thoroughly investigate the newly relocated military households in the Jīngxī Circuit.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
the Grand Secretariat was informed:
when officials commit crimes,
the serious cases should be dealt with immediately,
while minor cases should be registered,
and their punishment decided after the affair is settled.
The Bureau of Military Affairs was informed:
among the soldiers conscripted by Sāhén there are fully ordained monks,
they may be discharged and sent away.
On the *jǐhài* day,
an imperial edict commanded that military candidates who were not currently in office or had already joined the army
should be transferred to the capital from wherever they were,
to form a separate army
for future use.
Those recommended but not yet appointed to office
should be assigned positions according to their talents.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
the Emperor, concerned that the city of Píngyáng was too large
and that there might not be enough troops and provisions,
discussed abandoning it,
but the Chief Counselors firmly disagreed.
Zhān Gē Tèlín, former Professor of Jìzhōu, was rewarded for
gathering volunteer militias,
devising strategies,
and thwarting local bandits.
After the war, he took charge of the prefecture,
reestablished the prefectural administration,
accumulated fodder and provisions,
and attracted 50,000 households.
He was specially promoted three ranks
to a fifth-grade official position.
The Circuit Administration Office of Shāndōng Xīlù was established in Guīdé Fǔ and in Xú and Bò prefectures.
Hóu Zhì, Grand Master of Ceremonies, was appointed Assistant Administrator of the Grand Secretariat,
to administer the Grand Secretariat in Héběi Dōng and Xī circuits.
The imperial portrait of Tàizǔ arrived from Xījīng
and was reverently placed in Qǐqìng Gōng.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
a Provisional Bureau of Military Affairs was established in Xúzhōu and Guīdé Fǔ.
An imperial edict ordered that for all officials, regardless of their background,
if their talents were suitable for important duties, the Grand Secretariat should fully report them to the throne.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
Wán Yán Bì, Pacification Commissioner of Shāndōng Xīlù, reported:
"Zhāng Rǔjí, acting Assistant Prefect of Dōngpíng Fǔ, was planning to rebel again.
He secretly sent someone to recruit Sūn Bāngzuǒ, Assistant Prefect of Yìdū Fǔ.
Bāngzuǒ beheaded that person
and immediately reported to Bì.
Bì killed Rǔjí and over ten thousand of his followers.
By imperial command, Bāngzuǒ was promoted to Defender of Dézhōu,
and others who rendered meritorious service were rewarded accordingly."
The Emperor praised Bì's achievements,
granted him further promotion,
ennobled him as Duke of Mì,
and issued an imperial edict of commendation.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
an imperial edict commanded close ministers to recommend good generals.
Sūn Bāngzuǒ was promoted to Grand General of Inspiring Loyalty and Military Commissioner of Tàidìng Army,
and his son was also granted an official position.
On the *wùshēn* day,
Marshal's Offices were established in Dōngpíng, Yìdū, Tàiyuán, and Lùzhōu.
A general amnesty was declared.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
Xǔ Gǔ, Censor, presented a strategy for recovering Zhōngdū.
The Red Turban bandits plundered Chéngwǔ.
Yánzhǎn Tiānzé, Deputy Pacification Commissioner, led an expedition against them and drove them away,
beheading several hundred.
Tiānzé was promoted one rank,
and military officers and commanders who rendered meritorious service were ordered to be promoted and rewarded immediately.
Hóu Zhì was ordered to offer an official position to Chéng Bāngjié, a bandit from Xíngzhōu.
If he refused, his followers were to be enticed to conspire against him.
Four officials from the Ministry of Revenue's clerical staff and a varying number of assigned officials were dismissed.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
a Provisional Secretariat was established in Shǎnxī.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
the method of intercepting and purchasing grain along the river was intensified,
taking eight out of ten to suppress the malpractice of grain speculation,
and private crossings were strictly prohibited.
Ten thousand infantry soldiers were added
to guard west of the capital,
and forty thousand to guard east of the capital.
Two thousand cavalry from Shǎnxī were selected
to reinforce the capital guard.
Shǎnxī was instructed
to firmly defend the strategic points in Yán'ān, Líntáo, Huán, Qìng, Lán, Huì, Bǎo'ān, Suídé, Píngliáng, Déshùn, Zhènrónɡ, Jīngyuán, Fū, Fāng, Bīn, Níng, Qián, and Yào.
Infantry from Wèinán Prefecture and commanderies were stationed in Píngliáng.
The Pacification Commissioner was ordered to administer Bīnzhōu,
and the Deputy Commissioner to administer Chéngchéng in Tóngzhōu to command them.
Furthermore, infantry and cavalry were assigned to guard all crossings along the Wèi River.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
Yǒngxī, Marshal's Left Military Supervisor and concurrently Prefect of Zhēndìng Fǔ, was punished for a regulatory failure in aiding Zhōngdū.
His official titles and noble ranks were stripped,
and he was flogged eighty times.
On the *dīngsì* day of the ninth month, the first day of the lunar month,
Àotún Āhǔ, Vice Minister of the Ministry of Revenue, stated:
"The state faces many difficulties,
and officials often refuse to serve.
I request that a limit of two seasons be set;
those who violate this should not be reappointed."
The Emperor deemed it too severe,
and ordered that violators should only be deprived of three official ranks,
demoted three grades,
and permanently barred from further promotion.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
Yǒngxī, who had been removed from office, was specially promoted to General of Inspiring Trust and Prefect of Xīzhōu.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
the Chief Counselors were informed:
lands south of the Huái River embankments and roads were previously granted for private cultivation.
For those now seized by powerful individuals,
officials should be ordered to investigate.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
the Bureau of Military Affairs reported:
"The hereditary indigenous patrol commanders in Shǎnxī and Hédōng
were previously, like hereditary *móu'ān* and *móukè*, deprived of their stipends.
As border affairs are now urgent,
it is appropriate to restore their stipends,
so that their services may be utilized.
Furthermore, among the archers and crossbowmen on the western frontier, if there are individuals of outstanding talent and martial skill
who have achieved merits but have not yet been rewarded,
the Pacification Commission should verify the facts and report them."
This was approved.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
as the autumn harvest had not yet been gathered,
officials of the imperial guards were forbidden to hunt.
Wáng Huì, a recluse, was appointed Grand Master of Grand Eminence and Right Grand Remonstrant,
serving as a staff officer for the Liáodōng Pacification Commission.
On the *wùchén* day,
Túshān Wúdiǎn, acting Deputy Military Commissioner of Wǔníng Army, reported the rebellious conspiracy of Mònián Jìnzhōng, Administrator of Political Affairs.
An imperial edict ordered the relevant authorities to interrogate him.
Officials such as Supervisor-General of Troops and Horses at Tóngguān were established.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
a Provisional Circuit Administration Office for Héběi Dōnglù was established across Yuánwǔ, Yángwǔ, Fēngqiū, Chénliú, Yánjīn, Tōngxǔ, and Luò counties,
to manage the military households transferred to its seat.
Officials and monks of the Directorate of State Ceremonies were ordered to protect and administer the residence of Gǒngguó Gōng Ànchén.
The Emperor said to the Chief Counselors:
"Ànchén's conduct is not careful,
and he may commit crimes.
To ignore it would be intolerable by reason,
but to punish him would be to lose the way of cherishing relatives.
We should simply establish officials to guard against it."
Soon after, Ànchén, due to unlawful conduct,
was demoted to Defender of Bózhōu.
Lǐ Shì, the mother of Wèi Shàowáng, was stripped of her posthumous title, Empress Guāngxiàn.
Her spirit tablet in the Imperial Ancestral Temple
and her portrait in Qǐqìng Gōng
were both removed.
Duàn Zhònglián, commander of the garrison in Chénzhōu, presented three hundred sheep.
An imperial edict ordered his promotion by three ranks.
Rǔ Lì, Right Vice Grand Councilor, was ordered to go to Chénzhōu to plan for grain storage.
On the *rénshēn* day,
Sūmén County was renamed Huīzhōu.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
imperial portraits of Shìzǔ and Tàizǔ were honored and worshipped at Qǐqìng Gōng,
and sacrificial rites were performed,
for the first time with music.
Dōng Yǒngchāng was granted the surname Wēndūn Shì;
Bāo Shìxiǎn and Bāo Gēdá were granted the surname Wūgǔlún Shì;
Dǔ Lìnggū was granted the surname Hésùjiā Shì;
Hé Dìng was granted the surname Bìlán Shì;
Mǎ Fúdè and Mǎ Bǎishòu were granted the surname Jiágǔ Shì.
Each was promoted one rank.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
imperial portraits of Tàizōng, Xīzōng, and Ruìzōng were honored and worshipped,
and sacrificial rites were performed.
An imperial edict ordered the establishment of interconnected strongholds in Kāi, Huá, Jùn, Jì, Cáo, and Téng prefectures,
similar to Wèizhōu.
On the *yǐhài* day,
an imperial edict stated that in the Héběi and Shāndōng circuits, as well as Píngliáng, Qìngyáng, Líntáo prefectures,
and Jīng, Bīn, Qín, Gǒng, Déshùn prefectures that had experienced warfare,
official positions of the fourth grade and below should be considered complete after twenty months of service.
Chief commanders, imperial army officers, and volunteer militia officers and commanders were recruited from all locations:
those who could lead their forces to recapture Zhōngdū would be enfeoffed as princes,
promoted one rank,
and granted a second-grade official position.
Those able to defeat the enemy in battle, skillfully persuade people to surrender, and recover prefectures and counties attached to the capital
would be granted local chief official positions and honorary titles,
promoted according to their current ranks.
For other prefectures and counties, the reward would be successively reduced by two grades.
The Red-Jacket bandit Zhōu Yuán'ér (周元兒) seized Shēn (深), Qízhōu (祁州), Shùlù (束鹿), Ānpíng (安平), Wújí (無極) and other counties.
The Zhēndìng (真定) Marshal's Residence defeated him by stratagem,
beheading Yuán'ér (元兒) and killing more than five hundred of his followers.
On the *dīngchǒu* (丁丑) day,
an edict ordered prefectural and county officials who could recruit people to contribute five thousand *shí* (石) or more of grain
to have their service record (資考) reduced by one year.
