For ten thousand *shí* (石) or more,
they would be promoted one rank
and have their service record reduced by two years.
For twenty thousand *shí* (石) or more, they would be promoted one rank
and raised one grade,
details of which are missing.
For people of various backgrounds who were granted the imperial surname for their achievements:
those who could defeat three thousand enemy soldiers with a thousand men
were granted the imperial surname down to their *sīmá* (緦麻) relatives (mourning for three months);
those who could defeat more than two thousand men
were granted it down to their *dàgōng* (大功) relatives (mourning for nine months);
those who could defeat more than a thousand men
were granted it only to their household.
On the *gēngchén* (庚辰) day,
the Shǎnxī (陝西) Pacification Commission reported the victory of Yáng Zàixīng (楊再興), commander of the Fifth Division and myriad-household (萬戶) of the city, who repelled the Xià (夏) people.
On the *rénwǔ* (壬午) day,
blank imperial decrees were issued to the Shǎnxī (陝西) Pacification Commission,
stating that whenever the Xià (夏) people raided,
those who could achieve merits in battle,
from the fifth rank downwards, were all permitted to be promoted and appointed.
On the *yǐyǒu* (乙酉) day,
the Branch General Administration (行總管府) for Dàmíng Fǔ (大名府) was established in Zhèchéng (柘城) County,
to manage the military households moved to the new administrative seat.
In the winter, on the *bǐngxū* (丙戌) day, the first day of the tenth month,

Wūgǔlùn Déshēng (烏古論德升), Hanlin Academician Serving as Reader (翰林侍讀學士) and acting Minister of the Right (權參知政事), was appointed as Jíqìng (集慶) Military Commissioner (節度使) and Inspector of Bózhōu (亳州) Prefecture.
[一二]On the *dīnghài* (丁亥) day,
Rǔlì (汝礪), Assistant Director of the Right (尚書右丞), said:
"Regarding the military households from Héběi (河北) who have been moved to Hénán (河南),
it is fitting to grant them unused official land and cultivable grazing land
so they can farm for their own sustenance,
and cease their monthly grain allowance."
The Emperor approved his request.
Féng Kāi (馮開), Right Remonstrance Official (右司諫), was ordered to inspect the various locations,
giving each person thirty *mǔ* (畝).
The Xià (夏) people invaded Bǎo'ān (保安),
and Commander-in-Chief Wányán Guójiānú (完顏國家奴) defeated them.
They attacked Yán'ān (延安),
and the garrison commander also defeated them.
On this day,
the victory reports arrived.
On the *wùzǐ* (戊子) day,
Túdān Sīzhōng (徒單思忠), Censor-in-Chief (御史中丞), was appointed Minister of the Right (參知政事).
On the *jǐchǒu* (己丑) day,
as Prime Minister Mòlián Jìnzhōng (抹撚盡忠) had been imprisoned for a long time,
Supervising Censor Xǔ Gǔ (許古) said:
"Jìnzhōng (盡忠) has been detained by the authorities;
this must be a serious crime,
but the reason is unknown,
which greatly alarms the public.
I beg that an impartial and prominent minister be dispatched to interrogate him.
If the truth is obtained,
the charges should be clearly announced
to satisfy the hearts of those within and outside the court."
The memorial was submitted,
but no reply was given.
On the *gēngyín* (庚寅) day,
Jìnzhōng (盡忠) was executed.
On the *guǐsì* (癸巳) day,
Jìnzhōng's (盡忠) crimes were announced to the public.
An edict ordered Púsǎn Ānzhēn (僕散安貞), Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs (樞密副使), to establish a Branch Bureau of Military Affairs (行樞密院) in Xúzhōu (徐州).
On the *wùxū* (戊戌) day,
the Liáodōng (遼東) Pacification Commission reported the victory of defeating Liú Gē (留哥).
On the *jiǎchén* (甲辰) day,
an edict sought the descendants of the Prince of Guǎngpíng Commandery (廣平郡王) Chénghuī (承暉).
His nephew, Yǒnghuái (永懷), Assistant Magistrate of Lìtíng (歷亭) County, was found
and appointed as Director of Palace Supplies (器物直長).
On the *bǐngwǔ* (丙午) day,
the Xià (夏) people captured Líntáo (臨洮),
and Wányán Húshīlà (完顏胡失剌), Deputy Pacification Commissioner of Shǎnxī (陝西), was captured.
On the *gēngxū* (庚戌) day,
an edict ordered Púsǎn Duān (僕散端), Left Chancellor (尚書左丞相), to concurrently serve as Commander-in-Chief (都元帥),
and establish a Branch Secretariat (行尚書省) in Shǎnxī (陝西).
On the *xīnhài* (辛亥) day,
Měnggǔ Gāng (蒙古綱) reported:
"Yesterday, I received an imperial order to act as Deputy Pacification Commissioner of Shāndōng (山東) Circuit
and garrison at Dōngpíng (東平).
Upon reaching the northern bank of Xúzhōu (徐州),
the northern army was already pressing towards Xúzhōu (徐州),
making it impossible to proceed."
An edict ordered Púsǎn Ānzhēn (僕散安貞), Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs (樞密副使), to act along the river and deploy him.
On the *rénzǐ* (壬子) day,

the troops formerly garrisoned in Tóngzhōu (同州) and Huázhōu (華州) in Shǎnxī (陝西), as well as the infantry and cavalry transferred from Hénán (河南) who were previously subordinate to the Shǎnzhoū (陝州) Pacification Commission,
were reorganized under the Shǎnxī (陝西) Branch Secretariat (行省).
Kǒng Yuáncuò (孔元措), Grand Master of the Central Court (中奉大夫) [一三]and Inherited Duke Yǎnshèng (襲封衍聖公), was summoned to serve as Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices (太常博士).
When the Emperor first appointed Yuáncuò (元措) to the court,
some suggested that since the tomb and temple of the Illustrious Sage (宣聖) were in Qūfù (曲阜),
he should be sent to attend to the sacrifices there.
Later, the Emperor remembered that Yuáncuò (元cuò) was a descendant of the Sage,
and with bandits rampant in Shāndōng (山東),
he feared Yuáncuò (元cuò) might suffer harm.
Thus, sending him to attend to the sacrifices would in fact cut him off (from safety),
hence this new command.
Púxiān Wànnú (蒲鮮萬奴), a bandit in Liáodōng (遼東), usurped the imperial title
and changed the era name to Tiāntài (天泰).
In the eleventh month, on the *bǐngchén* (丙辰) day, the first day of the month,
Hóu Zhì (侯摯) of the Héběi (河北) Branch Secretariat (行尚書省) was granted an audience.
An edict ordered Tián Zhuó (田琢), Deputy Pacification Commissioner of the Western Héběi (河北) Circuit, to move his troops from Jùn (濬) to garrison in Shǎn (陝).
On the *wùwǔ* (戊午) day,
the Bureau of Military Affairs (樞密院) submitted Wáng Shì'ān's (王世安) strategy for taking Xūyí (盱眙) and Chǔzhōu (楚州).
Shì'ān (世安) was then appointed as Pacification Commissioner (招撫使),
and, along with personnel dispatched by the Sīzhōu (泗州) Marshal's Residence, proceeded to Huáinán (淮南) to assess the situation.
On the *wùchén* (戊辰) day,
the Xià (夏) people attacked the Kèróng (克戎) fortress in Suídé (綏德),
and the official army defeated them.
They attacked Suípíng (綏平),
and were again defeated.
Rewards were given to the meritorious generals and soldiers and to those who reported the victories.
Túdān Sīzhōng (徒單思忠), Minister of the Right (參知政事), said:
"Today, many who present memorials gather trivial matters.
I beg that they not be sent to the Secretariat (省),
but only be handled by the Palace Attendants Bureau (近侍局) to determine their feasibility and disposition."
The Emperor said:
"If so,
this would block the path of expression.
Anything concerning the state, how can it not go through the Secretariat (尚書省)?"
On the *gēngwǔ* (庚午) day,
the Emperor discussed with Rǔlì (汝礪), Assistant Director of the Right (尚書右丞), the advantages and disadvantages of dispatching officials to survey land for distribution to the military.
[一四]Rǔlì (汝礪) listed several disadvantages.
An edict was then issued to the relevant authorities to abolish the order,
and instead,
provide half of the military's grain allowance
and the monetary equivalent for the other half.
On the *rénshēn* (壬申) day,
Hóu Zhì (侯摯), Minister of the Right (參知政事), was dispatched to offer sacrifices to the River God at Yícūn (宜村).
On the *jiǎxū* (甲戌) day,
Yílà Tǎbùyě (移剌塔不也) with ten thousand soldiers defeated tens of thousands of Xià (夏) people at Shúyáng (熟羊) fortress.
On the *bǐngzǐ* (丙子) day,
an edict ordered the purchase of broken-down carts, infirm mares from the common people and placed them in imperial pastures
to encourage their breeding.
Tuómǎn Hútúmén (陀滿胡土門), Prefect of Líntáo Fǔ (臨洮府), defeated eighty thousand Xià (夏) people below the city.
On the *dīngchǒu* (丁丑) day,
Supervising Censor Chén Guī (陳規) impeached Hóu Zhì (侯摯), Minister of the Right (參知政事).
The Emperor did not accept his words
but consoled and replied to him.
On the *gēngchén* (庚辰) day,
the Emperor said to his chief ministers:
"I feared that surveying the land would disturb the people,
so I abolished that order.
Military households who wish to cultivate unused official land and grazing land are permitted to do so,
but land already cultivated by the people should not be taken.
The old custom was that officials of the Left and Right Generals, the Palace Attendants Bureau, bodyguards, and performing personnel, upon completing their terms, were all granted silk and cloth.
Although the relevant departments manufactured these,
they still involved levies on the people.
Recently, this too was abolished,
and only precious certificates (寶券) are given.
As for the clothes and articles I use,
they are also woven by the Grand Treasury (太府監) using official silk.
From now on, the people should not be burdened again."
Dà Yuán (大元) troops advanced into Zhāngdé Fǔ (彰德府),
and the prefect, Tuómǎn Xiéliè (陀滿斜烈), died there.
In the twelfth month, on the *yǐyǒu* (乙酉) day, the first day of the month,
the people of Shuòzhōu (朔州) were moved and resettled in various prefectures such as Lán (嵐), Shí (石), Xí (隰), Jí (吉), Jiàng (絳), and Xiè (解).
On the *wùzǐ* (戊子) day,
officials of the Bureau of Military Affairs (樞密院) were exempted from formal court greetings due to military affairs.
On the *jǐchǒu* (己丑) day,
Hóu Zhì (侯摯) again established the Branch Secretariat (行尚書省) in Héběi (河北).
On the *gēngyín* (庚寅) day,
Venus was visible during the day.
On the *rénchén* (壬辰) day,
an edict exempted the New Year's Day court audience.
On the *yǐwèi* (乙未) day,
an imperial decree posthumously granted official titles and ranks to the ancestors for three generations of Empress Zhāoshèng (昭聖).
Liú Quán (劉全) and Shí Wēn (時溫) from Tàikāng (太康) County, and Lǐ Níng (李寧) from Dōngpíng Fǔ (東平府), plotted rebellion
and were executed.
On the *wùxū* (戊戌) day,
the Shǎnxī (陝西) Branch Marshal's Residence (行元帥府) requested additional troops,
so Tián Zhuó's (田琢) forces were assigned to them,
and an imperial edict was issued to commend and encourage them.
On the *rén'yín* (壬寅) day,
an edict ordered Wéi Hóng (惟宏), Magistrate of Línzhōu (林州), and Dōu Tíkòng Cóng Tǎn (都提控從坦) to jointly manage border affairs,
and to expediently carry out the sequential rewards for meritorious generals.
On the *yǐsì* (乙巳) day,
Dà Yuán (大元) troops advanced into Dàmíng Fǔ (大名府).
On the *guǐchǒu* (癸丑) day,
the Imperial Grandson passed away.
As it was an untimely death,
there was no sacrificial ceremony,
and it was decreed not to burden the people.
The Xuānhuī Yuàn (宣徽院) was instructed to exempt princes and princesses from presenting wine on New Year's Day.
On the *jiǎyín* (甲寅) day,
the officials of rites reported that
Song envoys were coming to offer New Year's greetings,
and it was inappropriate to suspend court.
It was ordered that music be played and court attire be as usual.
An edict promoted Tuómǎn Hútúmén (陀滿胡土門), Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs for Líntáo (臨洮) Circuit, three ranks
and reappointed him.
On the wùzǐ day of the sixth month,
an edict was issued that anyone who privately viewed memorial documents or communications to the Shàngshū Shěng or the Shūmì Yuàn concerning important matters,
would be strangled.
Those who did so inadvertently would have their punishment reduced by two degrees.
Edicts that were meant to be secret were to be treated similarly.
On the rénchén day,
Zhāng Zhì, the self-proclaimed Prince of Yíng in Liáoxī, sent Wányán Nánhé and Zhāng Wánsēng with a memorial to pledge allegiance and surrender.
An edict was issued appointing Zhì as a Tèjìn,
to act as the Yuánshuài Fǔ of Běijīng Lù,
and concurrently as the Xuānfǔ Shǐ of that circuit.
Nánhé was made a Tóngzhī Běijīng Bīngmǎ Zǒngguǎnfǔ,
and Wánsēng a Tóngzhī Guǎngníng Fǔ.
On the bǐngshēn day,
Jupiter was visible in the daytime in the constellation Kuí,
and it remained visible for one hundred and one days before it vanished.
On the guǐmǎo day,
an edict ordered the relevant officials to pray for rain.
On the dīngwèi day,
a great locust plague in Hénán damaged the crops,
and officials were dispatched to different routes to capture them.
The Xuānfǔ Sī of the various circuits in Héběi were abolished,
and replaced with Jīnglüè Sī.
On the rénzǐ day,
due to the drought,
an edict ordered Cānzhī Zhèngshì Lǐ Gé to review and decide on wrongful imprisonment cases in the capital.
In autumn, on the guǐchǒu day, the first day of the seventh month,
Bìlán Ālǔdài, the Jiédùshǐ of Zhāoyì Jūn, recovered Wēizhōu and Huòlù Xiàn.
Swarms of flying locusts passed over the capital.
On the jiǎyín day,
the bandits Hǎo Dìng and others, captured by the Shāndōng Xíngshěng, arrived at the capital
and were executed.
On the yǐmǎo day,
due to drought and locusts,
an edict was issued to both the capital and the provinces.
On the jǐwèi day,
an imperial order reduced several dishes in the imperial kitchen and the annual supply of silk for the imperial concubines, with varying degrees of reduction.
On the xīnyǒu day,
Jiānchá Yùshǐ Chén Guī submitted a memorial outlining eight matters.
On the rénwǔ day, the first day of the intercalary month,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the xīnmǎo day,
Shēnzhōu was recovered.
On the guǐsì day,
Hànlín Xuéshì Wányán Bódié presented an account of the achievements of the Zhongxing restoration.
On the jiǎwǔ day,
an order was given to military officials to recommend individuals of extraordinary talent and strength,
and officials such as Tíkòng and Dūfùtǒng were to recommend their subordinates to each other.
Regulations for rewards and punishments for recommending officials were issued,
allowing merits and demerits to offset each other.
For ranked officials and commoners with military talent and skill,
recommendations for promotion or demotion were to follow the same rules.
On the gēngzǐ day,
an edict stated that for the garrisons in Hénán and Shǎnxī, those who qualified for inherited rank or purchased office by donating grain
should remain in service as before,
and only after the situation had stabilized would they be allowed to participate in the selection process.
In the eighth month, on the jiǎyín day,
Zhāng Xíngxìn, the Tàizǐ Shàobǎo concurrently Lǐbù Shàngshū, presented the established rites for the ancestral sacrifice by affinity.
The Emperor praised and accepted it.
The monk Guǎnghuì from Sānyuán Xiàn presented a set of rules for monks and Daoists regarding the amount of grain to be donated and the ranks of Dūfù Wēiyí and Jiānsì;
the sale was implemented according to his words.
The Xià people entered Ānsàibǎo,
and Yuánshuài Zuǒ Jiānjūn Wūgǔlún Qìngshòu dispatched troops to defeat them.
On the rénxū day,
Zhāng Xíngxìn was granted two thousand strings of precious scrolls and ten bolts of heavy silk,
to commend him for the appropriateness of his proposals for rites.
On the yǐhài day,
an edict was issued to the people of Zhōngdū,
and the Dàmíng Zhāofǔ Shǐ was ordered to recruit people to carry the edict there.
On the bǐngzǐ day,
Dà Yuán troops attacked Yán'ān.
On the jǐmǎo day,
the Xià people entered Jiéyēzuǐ Chuān,
and the government forces attacked and repelled them.
In the ninth month, on the xīnsì day, the first day of the month,
Dà Yuán troops attacked Fángzhōu.
[一六] Yǒngxī, who was Qiān Shūmì Yuàn Shì, was appointed Yùshǐ Dàfū,
and led troops to Shǎnxī,
to act at his discretion.
On the rénchén day,
Dà Yuán troops attacked Dàizhōu.
Jīnglüè Shǐ Àotún Chǒuhéshàng died in battle.
Wányán Núbì and others, who were Zhōngwèi Wèi, were appointed as envoys to celebrate the Sòng Emperor’s birthday.
[一七]
In winter, on the jǐwèi day of the tenth month,
the imperial princes and all officials reverently welcomed the ancestral spirit tablets to the Tàimiào.
Hunters who were skilled in archery and familiar with mountain paths were recruited and stationed in key strategic locations in Shǎn and Guó.
Yuánshuài Zuǒ Jiānjūn Bìlán Ālǔdài was ordered to guard Tóngguān,
and Wányán Zhòngyuán, who was remotely appointed Zhī Guīdé Fǔ Shì, garrisoned Lúshì.
Dà Yuán troops attacked Tóngguān.
Nílínggǔ Púlǔhǔ, the Jiédùshǐ of Xī'ān Jūn, died in battle.
On the xīnyǒu day,
the Emperor personally performed the ancestral sacrifice by affinity.
On the jiǎzǐ day,
the ancestral sacrifice by affinity was completed.
An amnesty was declared.
On the yǐchǒu day,
an edict was issued to the officials, soldiers, and people of Hénán,
to recruit men of merit with a reward system.
Cānzhī Zhèngshì Túdān Sīzhōng was ordered to take charge of and pacify the capital,
and Yílài Zhōulà Ābùtún was sent to Guān and Shǎn.
On the bǐngyín day,
an edict ordered the capital to prepare defensive equipment,
dig many pits and traps,
and build walls in vacant spaces.
The families of Wèi Shào and Hào Lìwáng were moved to the capital.
On the dīngmǎo day,
to install the gods of soil and grain,
officials were dispatched to make a preliminary announcement.
On the wùchén day,
Zhāng Xíngxìn was appointed acting Tàiwèi,
to install the gods of soil and grain,
and the rites and music were all reduced in number.
An edict ordered the Shàngshū of the four ministries—Lì, Lǐ, Bīng, and Gōng—to supervise the defensive works.
Dà Yuán troops made a foray into Rǔzhōu.
On the jǐsì day,
only small boats for communication were left on the river,
all others were burned.
On the gēngwǔ day,
an edict ordered the garrisoning of troops in grain-producing prefectures and counties,
and those civilians conscripted into military service were immediately appointed as squad leaders,
for self-defense.
Xú Dǐng, of the Hédōng Xíngshěng,
[一八] dispatched Bìlán Ālǔdài, Yuánshuài Zuǒ Jiānjūn of Lùzhōu, with ten thousand troops,
and Túdān Bǎijiā, Jīnglüè Shǐ of Mèngzhōu, with five thousand troops,
to cross the river via convenient routes to Guān and Shǎn,
and personally led elite troops from Píngyáng to reinforce the capital.
The Shūfǔ was ordered to oversee the army in response.
On the xīnwèi day,
officials were appointed to manage the Zhāoxián Suǒ (Bureau for Recruiting the Worthy).
Internal and external officials were ordered to seek out and report individuals with talent, knowledge, courage, and strategic ability who could plan city defenses,
and if verified, they would be promoted extraordinarily,
and their recommenders rewarded.
Those who possessed great talent but were not known to others
were permitted to go to the Zhāoxián Suǒ to state their own case.
On the rénshēn day,
Péimǎn Yánggē, who was Lóngchùwèi Shàng Jiāngjūn, was appointed Zhī Guīdé Fǔ Shì,
and acted as Shūmì Yuàn Shì.
On the guǐyǒu day,
an edict ordered the cessation of the seizure of private wagons and oxen by relevant authorities for transporting soldiers' clothing and provisions.
On the jiǎxū day,
a proclamation was issued to the people residing near the capital to move all their fodder and grain into the city,
and official stores were also to be transported.
On the bǐngzǐ day,
Wányán Hédá, who was Xíng Shūmì Yuàn Zhī Hénán Fǔ Shì, was executed
for failing to respond to a conscription order.
Wèi Qí, a Hùbù Lángzhōng, was honored as having died in royal service,
and his son was given an official post.
On the jǐmǎo day,
there was a discussion about prohibiting the lavish use of grain in the capital,
but the imperial attendants, fearing that it would hinder the circulation of the precious scrolls (currency),
did not carry it out.
Hàn Xīzǔ, a Lìbù Lìshǐ, submitted a proposal
that all those who had achieved official positions through military merit should be detained in the capital for potential deployment,
and this was followed.
On the *gēngchén* day of the eleventh month, which was the first day of the lunar month,
regulations for promoting and rewarding garrison officers and soldiers were revised.
On the *xīnsì* day,
an edict was issued to prohibit farmers attached to the capital from dismantling their own dwellings.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
Xū Dǐng, from the Hé​dōng Branch Secretariat, entered to reinforce the capital.
Following his advice, Wáng Zhì was appointed Acting Marshal and Left Inspector of Armies for Píngyáng Prefecture,
and concurrently Wányán Sēngjiānú was appointed Acting Right Inspector of Armies,
to jointly govern Hé​dōng.
Dǐng was appointed Minister of the Left in the Department of State Affairs and concurrently Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
Wányán Bójiā, Administrator of Guīdé Prefecture, was appointed Assistant Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
Because Wányán Hédá had been executed,
an imperial edict was issued to the court and the provinces.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
Wányán Sàibùlái, the Right Deputy Marshal and Inspector of Armies, reported a great victory by his commanders Shízhǎn Héxǐ and Yáng Wòliè over the Xīxià people at Dìngxī.
The Branch Secretariat was ordered to assess their merits and reward them.
When the Great Yuán army reached Miǎnchí,
Púchá Ālǐbùsūn, the Right Deputy Marshal, saw his army collapse and fled,
losing his tiger tally.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
Wányán Hédá, former Judicial Commissioner of Línhuáng Prefecture and Acting Right Inspector of Armies, returned to the country from the north with his officers, soldiers, old, and young.
He was promoted to Military Governor of Zhènnán Command
and advanced three ranks in office.
An edict ordered the release of public funds, cotton, and silk to the relevant authorities to compensate for the civilian clothing that had been requisitioned to clothe the army.
That evening,
there was a halo around Jupiter.
Jupiter was in the Kui constellation,
and the moon was in the Bi constellation.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
a law was established regarding the destruction of city defense equipment.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
an edict decreed that officials who had performed meritorious service of the fifth rank and above would be granted a meal before the emperor,
while officials of the sixth rank and below would be granted a meal at the imperial retinue bureau.
On the *guǐsì* day,
the Emperor instructed the Crown Prince:
"Some of the capital's command officers are filled by civil officials.
How can they understand military affairs?
They should be replaced quickly."
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,

all retainers and followers of various officials, as well as soldiers from various departments and bureaus who received grain rations and had previously been selected for military service, were exempted from duty.
On the *wùxū* day,
an imperial order commanded all prefectures and counties to register military and civilian personnel
to guard against local bandits.
The Huázhōu Marshal's Office recovered Tóngguān Pass.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
the civilian militias defending the capital were disbanded.
Censor Chén Guī and others were dispatched as pacification and bandit-suppression officials for the Hénán Circuit.
Gésīliè Sǎohé, Commander of the Hénán Circuit, was
executed for delaying the dispatch of troops.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
Minister Wòshàng of the Board of Works and others were appointed envoys to felicitate the Sòng court on New Year's Day.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
Tǎn, from the Hénán Branch Bureau of Military Affairs, reported
that his kinsman Dàogē wished to join the ranks and offer his service.
The Emperor commended his loyalty
and permitted it.
Nèizú Chénglì presented captured horses and camels.
The Emperor said:
"These were obtained by the soldiers;
they should be given back to them.
What use are they to me?"
He then universally instructed all commanders and generals
not to do this again in the future.
On the *xīnhài* day of the twelfth month,
Zhúhǔ Gāoqí, Chancellor of the Right, was promoted to Grand Preceptor and Minister of the Right in the Department of State Affairs.
Lǐ Gé, Policy Advisor, was dismissed.
On the *guǐhài* day,
the Great Yuán army attacked Píngyáng.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
the Crown Prince discussed campaigning against the Xīxià.
The Great Yuán army advanced to Dàmíng Prefecture.
On the *rénshēn* day,
the Great Yuán army advanced from Dàizhōu, Shénxiān Héngchéng, and the various passes of Píngdìng Chéngtiān Town,
and attacked Tàiyuán Prefecture.
Wūgǔlún Lǐ, the Pacification Commissioner, sent a messenger via a secret path with a document written on alum paper to the capital to report the emergency.
An edict ordered the dispatch of troops from the Lùzhōu Marshal's Office,
and the Píngyáng, Hézhōng, Jiàng, and Mèng Pacification Commissions to reinforce it.
On the *yǐhài* day,
Gāoqí requested the repair of Nánjīng's outer city wall.
The Emperor said:
"The people's strength is already exhausted.
If this project begins,
their suffering will become even worse.
Even if the city wall is complete and solid,
how can I alone live in peace here?"
Collation Notes
Annals, Chapter 15: Xuānzōng (Middle)
On the *jǐmǎo* day of the first month of spring in the first year of Xīngdìng, which was the first day of the lunar month,
Sòng dispatched envoys to offer congratulations.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
the Sòng envoys had their farewell audience.
The Emperor said to his chief ministers:
"I hear there are bandits in the southern border of Xīzhōu.
These are merely starving people from their territory causing trouble along the Huái River.
Why do the Sòng people attack us?"
Gāoqí requested to campaign against them to expand territory.
The Emperor said:
"My intention is otherwise.
It is sufficient to merely guard what our ancestors entrusted to us.
Why bother with external conquest?"
On the *yǐwèi* day,

an edict ordered that civil service examination candidates and military examination candidates from the Zhōngdū, Xījīng, Běijīng, and other circuits should take their provisional examinations in the Nánjīng, Dōngpíng, Pósu, Shàngjīng, and other four circuits.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
the Dōngpíng Branch Secretariat reported:
"Since the dispatch of troops,
officials and soldiers, due to their arduous service, have been promoted to as high as the fifth rank,
and are generally eligible for enfeoffment and posthumous honors.
Also, civilians aged seventy and above are all eligible for imperial grace.
If people individually come forward to declare their eligibility,
it will be costly for both public and private parties.
We request that this circuit be allowed to issue the imperial edicts and patents,
then categorize and send them to the imperial court
for official seals.
Those who receive the decrees can then pay a certain amount of goods for them to be issued.
This will spare the people labor and partially relieve the military's food supply."
This was approved.
Imperial Prince Pú Wáng Shǒuchún, Chancellor of the Right, was granted the hereditary chieftainship of the Three Tuns *Mèng'ān* in Dōngpíng Prefecture Circuit.
Xū Dǐng, Minister of the Left in the Department of State Affairs, was promoted to Chancellor of the Right
and enfeoffed as the Duke of Xīn.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
it was discussed to reduce the number of redundant civilian officials.
On the *yǐsì* day,
the Great Yuán army attacked Guānzhōu.
On the *wùshēn* day of the second month, which was the first day of the lunar month,
the "Zhēnyòu Tōngbǎo"
currency was first put into circulation.
One string of it was equivalent to
one thousand strings of "Zhēnyòu Bǎojuàn."
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
the Bureau of Military Affairs was ordered to eliminate and dismiss weak soldiers.
The Department of State Affairs was instructed
to use government horses for post stations to alleviate the burden on the people.
On the *gēngxū* day,
the Empress's birthday,
an edict exempted all officials from offering congratulations,
and further instructed:
"The times are difficult,
so the upcoming Chángchūnjié festival will also be exempt from congratulatory ceremonies."
On the *xīnhài* day,
Wányán Sàibù, the Grand Preceptor and Right Deputy Marshal and Inspector of Armies, was appointed Assistant Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
the Office for Recruiting Talents was abolished.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
an imperial grandson was born.
The Bureau of Imperial Parks requested to offer congratulations,
but an edict forbade the use of music.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
the Great Yuán army advanced into Xīn and Dài.
An edict stipulated that even if prefecture and county officials had accumulated ranks up to the third grade,
if they were found to lack military provisions,
the circuit inspector was permitted to make decisions and dismiss them.
On the *rénxū* day,
the Department of State Affairs, due to insufficient military provisions,
requested to stop providing stipends to students in prefectural and county schools.
The Emperor said:
"From ancient times, civil and military talents have been used together.
Previously in Zhōngdū,
the establishment of schools and the support of scholars were never abolished.
How much more so today?
Let the stipends continue as before."
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
the establishment of a temple for Crown Prince Zhuāngxiàn was discussed.
On the *wùyín* day of the third month,
an imperial edict stated that matters concerning criminal cases and names [of officials]
must be deliberated upon face-to-face,
and not be relayed through reports.
Lǐ Gé, the Jìngyáng Army Commander (*jiéduòshǐ*), was appointed Prefect of Píngyáng Prefecture,
concurrently serving as Grand Commander of Military Affairs for the Southeastern Hédōng Circuit,
acting *Cānzhī Zhèngshì*,
and administering the Department of State Affairs (*Shàngshū Shěng*).
On the *rénwǔ* day,
regulations were established for the common people to collect abandoned soldiers and lost horses,
and for the method of compensation for horses delivered to officials.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
the Emperor saw locusts in the palace,
and dispatched officials to various routes to supervise their capture,
while also cautioning them not to harass the people with harshness or violence.
On the *gēngyín* day,
the Chángchūn Festival was celebrated,
and the Sòng sent envoys to offer congratulations.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
an imperial edict abolished the Marshals (*yuánshuài*) of Píngyáng and Hézhōng.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
previously, Shandong troops had been mobilized to rendezvous with Miáo Dàorùn to jointly retake Zhōngdū.
However, Shí Hǎi rebelled, holding Zhēndìng,
and it was feared that this would obstruct the effort.
Therefore, the elite troops of Niángē Zhēn, Guō Wénzhèn, Wǔ Xiān, and the Dōngpíng Army were gathered to form a pincer movement
to attack them.
On the *jǐhài* day,
the Dà Yuán army attacked Xīnchéng.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
they attacked Bàzhōu.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
Wǔ Xiān, the Prefect (*cìshǐ*) of Wēizhōu, led troops and beheaded Shí Hǎi and over two hundred of his followers,
and accepted the surrender of the armies of Gě Zhòng, Zhào Lín, Zhāng Lì, and others,
seizing all the items Shí Hǎi had usurped.
Soon after, Wǔ Xiān was promoted to acting Prefect of Zhēndìng Prefecture.
On the *dīngwèi* day, the first day of the fourth month of summer,
as the Sòng annual tribute had not arrived,
Ugulùn Qìngshòu and Wányán Sàibù were ordered to conduct military operations along the southern border.
On the *wùshēn* day,
Sòng Zǐyù, the Myriad-Commander (*wànhù*) of the Mèngzhōu Military Affairs Commissioner's Office (*jīngluèsī*), led his troops in rebellion,
breaking through the passes and exiting.
The Military Affairs Commissioner Cóng Tǎn and others pursued and defeated him.
On the *gēngxū* day,
the Huāmào Army revolted in Téngzhōu,
and an imperial edict ordered the Shāndōng Branch Secretariat (*xíngshěng*) to suppress them.
Bandits arose in Wǔliàn Mountain in Nányáng,
their numbers reaching over a thousand.
Yílà Yánggē, the Assistant Commander (*fùshǐ*) of the Military Commissioner, went out to suppress them,
and encountered them at Fāngchéng.
He tried to persuade them to surrender, but they refused,
so he advanced and attacked them,
killing almost all of them.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
Wányán Dùn, the Commander of Ānhuà Army, was appointed acting Marshal of the Left Grand Supervisor (*yuánshuài zuǒdūjiān*),
administering the Marshal's Office,
and overseeing Military Affairs Commissioner Miáo Dàorùn's advance to retake the capital,
and also ordering him to coordinate with Yílà Tiěgē and other armies, the Recruitment Commissioner (*zhāofǔshǐ*) of Héjiān.
Tiěgē and Dàorùn were at odds,
each accusing the other of having ulterior motives,
so a high official was ordered to oversee them.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
hail damaged crops in Shànzhōu.
An imperial edict ordered officials to encourage farmers to replant autumn crops,
with the government providing seeds.
Yán Xiǎn, a follower of the bandit Yán Déyòng of Píngdìng Prefecture, killed Déyòng
and surrendered with his followers.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
Wányán Ālǐbùsūn, acting *Cānzhī Zhèngshì* and administrator of the Liáodōng Circuit Branch Secretariat, was appointed *Cānzhī Zhèngshì*,
administering the Department of State Affairs and Marshal's Office in Pó Sù Circuit.
Púchá Wǔjīn, acting Liaodong Circuit Pacification Commissioner (*xuānfǔshǐ*), was appointed acting *Cānzhī Zhèngshì*,
administering the Department of State Affairs and Marshal's Office in Shàngjīng.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
Lǐ Gé requested to abolish the Grand Commanders and Assistant Commanders of the Righteous Army (*yìjūn*),
and transfer their authority to the prefectures and counties.
The Department of State Affairs stated that as autumn defenses were imminent,
changing the law would be inconvenient,
so the old system should temporarily remain,
with prefectures and counties each supervising.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
Marshal Wányán Sàibù defeated Sòng troops at Xìnyáng,
and an envoy was sent to report the victory.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
bandits rose simultaneously in Jǐnán, Tàiníng, Téng, Yǎn and other prefectures.
Hóu Zhì dispatched Wányán Tíng, the Defense Commissioner (*fángyùshǐ*) of Dìzhōu, to suppress them,
and accepted the surrender of twenty thousand able-bodied men and fifty thousand old and young.
Wányán Sàibù again reported
defeating Sòng troops at Lǒngshān and other places,
capturing and beheading a great number.
On the *wùchén* day,
Venus was seen in the daytime in the well (*Jǐng* constellation).
On the *xīnwèi* day,
Cóng Tǎn, acting Mèngzhōu Military Affairs Commissioner, pursued the bandit Sòng Zǐyù to the border of Huīzhōu.
His follower Xíng Fú killed Zǐyù
and surrendered with his followers.
On the *rénshēn* day,
as Wànnú's rebellion was not yet suppressed,
an imperial edict was issued to the generals in Liáodōng.
Wányán Sàibù's army crossed the Huái River and broke through two passes in Guāngzhōu,
obtaining military supplies which were distributed to the generals and soldiers.
On the *wùyín* day of the fifth month,
the Shǎnxī Branch Secretariat defeated the Xīxià people at Dàběichà,
and the victory report arrived on that day.
On the *dīnghài* day,
the commoner Yuàn Rújì submitted a memorial discussing advantages and disadvantages.
The Emperor showed it to the Grand Counselor (*zǎichén*), saying:
"Even a humble commoner
can speak so fully.
If there is anything worth adopting, implement it."
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
the remaining followers and families of the bandit Sòng Zǐyù were all released to return to farming.
Púchá Yílàdū, Assistant Grand Counselor of the Right (*shàngshū yòuchéng*), abandoned his post and unauthorizedly went to the capital,
and was demoted to Prefect of Hénán Prefecture,
administering the Bureau of Military Affairs (*Shūmìyuàn*) concurrently with the Six Boards.
On the *rénchén* day,
hail damaged crops in Yuánwǔ County, Yánzhōu.
An imperial edict ordered officials to lend seeds to the people for replanting.
On the *guǐsì* day,
the Sòng attacked Yǐngzhōu,
burning and plundering before leaving.
On the *wùxū* day,
the Bureau of Military Affairs army defeated the Sòng at Níhéwān,
and again defeated them at Fánchéng County.
Ménggǔ Gāng, administrator of the Shandong Branch Marshal's Office, unauthorizedly arrested and shackled the Transport Commissioner (*zhuǎnyùnshǐ*) Lǐ Bǐngjūn.
The law dictated that Ménggǔ Gāng should be flogged.
Bǐngjūn, in turn, insulted Gāng,
which should be punishable by ransom.
An imperial edict released both.
The Sòng captured Liánshuǐ County.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
Lǐ Píng and other Myriad-Commanders of the Lánzhōu navy, suffering from the greed and violence of Commander (*tíkòng*) Púchá Yànjīng,
killed him.
They incited the Xīxià people to rebel,
and forced their follower Zhāng Yǐ to join them.
Yǐ used a stratagem to capture them all.
The Shǎnxī Branch Secretariat, acting on its discretion, promoted Yǐ four ranks,
and appointed him Assistant Prefect of Lánzhōu,
and rewarded the soldiers differently,
reporting the matter to the Emperor.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
the Dà Yuán army captured Miǎnchéng County,
and officer Rèn Fú died there.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
regulations were established for officials seeking posts in Héběi to cross the river.
Those who had commanded troops were to report to the Bureau of Military Affairs,
while others were to be verified before being allowed to cross.
Ugulùn Qìngshòu, administrator of the Bureau of Military Affairs, returned from the southern campaign,
and his report was not truthful.
An imperial edict ordered an investigation.
On the *jǐyǒu* day of the sixth month,
Miáo Dàorùn reported that the returned native Lǐ Chēn had again rebelled with his followers,
while Lǐ Chēn also reported that Dàorùn had ulterior motives.
An imperial edict ordered the Shāndōng Branch Secretariat to investigate.
Tóngguān Pass was repaired,
and imperial envoys were dispatched with imperial edicts and summer medicine to comfort the laborers and artisans.
Zhāng Xíngxìn, acting *Cānzhī Zhèngshì*, was promoted to *Cānzhī Zhèngshì*.
On the *gēngxū* day,
the families of officials in Liáodōng who had accepted false appointments were arrested and prosecuted.
The wife and children of Ancha Commissioner (*ànchásǐ*) Gāo Lǐ were found
and all executed.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
an edict decreed that officials of the fourth rank and below in Fū, Fāng, and Dān Prefectures and counties should follow the precedent of Huán and Qìng [Prefectures],
with their terms ending after twenty months.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
Recruitment Commissioner Wéi Hóng reported that the defending official of Zhāngdé Prefecture had unauthorizedly relocated people to mountain fortresses to avoid soldiers.
The Emperor said:
"Of what use is it to defend a city that cannot be secured?
It only harms our people.
Do not prosecute."
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
it was the memorial day of Xiǎnzōng,
and a ceremony was held at Qǐqìng Palace.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
an imperial edict ordered the Bureau of Military Affairs to dispatch experienced officials to various branch offices,
to strictly guard critical strategic points with strong troops and sharp weapons,
and also to prohibit drinking and feasting.
Violators would be punished according to military law.
The Sòng and local bandits jointly attacked the border of Dōnghǎi.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
as the Sòng had repeatedly sent troops to invade the border,
and the annual tribute had not arrived,
an imperial edict was issued along the border condemning the Sòng.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
an imperial edict stated that for all people who submitted memorials whose suggestions had been adopted,
their names should be publicized.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
as the discussions of the Presented Scholar (*jìnshì*) Zhū Gài and the commoner Lǐ Wéiyuè were commendable,
an imperial edict granted them a salary of eight *guàn* of grain.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
Commanders and Assistant Commanders were established for Tóngguān Pass,
and Overseer (*tíjǔ*) officials for Sānmén and Jí Jīn.
Púsǎn Duān, Grand Counselor of the Left and concurrent Grand Marshal, passed away,
and court was suspended.
The Liúquán Office (*wù*) was established in Nánjīng.
The Liáodōng Branch Secretariat sent an envoy to report the victory against the Qìdān in the first month.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the day bǐngzǐ (1st of the month),
there was a solar eclipse.
On the day xīnsì,
the Sòng people besieged Sīzhōu.
On the day rénwǔ,
Língbì County was besieged.
On the day guǐwèi,
Mǎ Kuān (馬寬), myriarch of the Zhènwēi Army in Àozhōu, expelled its prefect Lǐ Cè (李策),
and occupied the city, rebelling.
An envoy was sent to recruit him,
and he surrendered.
Soon after, he plotted another變 (bian - rebellion/change),
and the provincial officials captured and executed him,
wiping out his clan.
On the day jiǎshēn,
an edict was issued to admonish the various circuits of Liáodōng.
On the day yǐyǒu,
the Sòng people attacked and captured Dōnghǎi County.
On the day bǐngshēn,
the offices of Commissioner and Deputy Commissioner for Granary Administration (Tíjjǔ Cāngcháng Shǐ, Fù) were established.
On the day guǐmǎo,
auspicious grain grew on the altar of the Grand Altar of Land (Tài Shè Tán),
with one stalk bearing fifteen ears.
On the day jiǎchén,
the Xià people attacked Huánghèchà,
and the imperial army defeated them.
On the day yǐsì,
the offices of Administrator (Zhī Yuàn Shì) and Joint Administrator (Tóng Zhī Yuàn Shì) of the Jíxián Yuàn were first established.
The Sòng people and local bandits attacked Hǎizhōu,
and the Commissioner for Military Affairs (Jīnglüè Shǐ) defeated their forces.
The Xià people besieged Yánglángzhài,
and the Commander-in-Chief's residence dispatched troops from various garrisons to repel them.
In the eighth month, on the day wùshēn,
the Shǎnxī Provincial Administration reported that the Mùbō bandits attacked Táozhōu but were defeated
and fled.
Jupiter was seen during the day in the constellation Mǎo (Pleiades),
and remained visible for sixty-seven days before disappearing.
On the day jǐyǒu,
the Hǎizhōu Commissioner for Military Affairs (Jīnglüè Sī) reported that the imperial army fought the Sòng people south of Shíqiū,
fought in Liánshuǐ County,
and fought at Zhōngtǔqiáo,
where the Sòng army was defeated.
On the day rénzǐ,
the Grand Censor (Yùshǐ Dàfū) Yǒngxī (永錫) was stripped of his official rank and title.
The relevant department argued that he deserved execution for military failure,
but the emperor, considering him a close relative,
specially spared his life.
On the day guǐchǒu,
the Sòng people attacked Quèshān County
but were defeated by the imperial army.
An edict was issued to instruct the soldiers in the country,
making them aware of the Sòng people's breach of alliance,
and also commanded ministers to discuss the matter.
On the day yǐmǎo,
Zhū Gài (朱蓋), Advisory Official of the Jíxián Yuàn, submitted a memorial presenting three strategies to resist the enemy.
On the day rénxū,
Ābùhǎnnúshīlà (阿不罕奴失剌), Commissioner for Military Affairs of Hǎizhōu, defeated the Sòng people within their territory.
The Chief Commander (Tíkòng) Lǐ Yuán (李元) fought the Sòng people
and achieved repeated victories,
capturing many.
The Lántōngdù Commissioner for Military Affairs Office was moved to Huánglínggāng.
On the day yǐchǒu,
regulations were enacted to increase rewards for capturing runaway soldiers and to punish those who harbored them.
On the day bǐngyín,
Púsǎn Yìfū (僕散毅夫), Left Remonstrance Official (Zuǒ Sī Jiàn), requested a change of name for Kāifēng Prefecture,
to be bestowed with an auspicious name,
making Wèishì County an administrative prefecture (cìjùn),
and Suīzhōu a defense commissioner (fángyù shǐ),
together with Zhèng (鄭) and Yán (延) prefectures, to serve as auxiliary to the capital from the left, right, front, and rear.
The emperor said:
"The imperial tombs are in Zhōngdū (中都).
How could I be happy to stay here indefinitely?"
The matter was thus dropped.
On the day guǐyǒu,
the anniversary of Tàizǔ's (太祖) death,
offerings were made at Qǐqìnggōng.
On the day jiǎxū,
Marshal Left Chief Supervisor Chéngyì (承裔)
dispatched his generals Nàlán Jìsēng (納蘭記僧) and others,
joining with Nímánggǔ (尼厖古), commander of the Pā'é (葩俄) tribe,
to launch a surprise attack with troops on the various encampments of the Guālíyú (瓜黎餘) tribe.
They repeatedly defeated them,
slaughtering soldiers,
capturing their leaders,
and seizing many people and livestock.
News of the victory arrived on this day.
In the ninth month, on the day dīngchǒu,
the law regarding malfeasance of Censors (Jiānchá Yùshǐ) was revised.
Bìlán'ālǔdài (必蘭阿魯帶), Marshal Left Military Supervisor (Zuǒ Jiānjūn), was appointed acting Assistant Administrator of Governmental Affairs (Quán Cānzhī Zhèngshì)
and to lead the Provincial Administration (Xíngshěng) in Yìdū.
On the day wùyín,
the Xià people attacked Kèróngzhài in Suídé.
Commander-in-Chief Luó Shìhuī (羅世暉) met them in battle
and repelled them.
On the day jǐmǎo,
the Càizhōu Commander-in-Chief's residence, having scouted that the Sòng people were planning to invade Xīzhōu,
used light troops to lure them forward,
and then separately ambushed them with elite forces,
capturing their general Shěn Jùn (沈俊).
On the day rénwǔ,
due to the change of reign title to Xīngdìng,
an amnesty was granted nationwide.
On the day jiǎshēn,
a logistics bureau (Guīyùn Suǒ) was established,
and six temporary ministries (Xíng Liù Bù) were set up.
On the day xīnmǎo,
the Great Yuán (大元) army raided Xízhōu and Fénxī County.
On the day guǐsì,
they attacked Qìnzhōu.
Wányán Ālǐbùsūn (完顏阿里不孫), Head of the Liáodōng Provincial Administration, was killed by the rebel Bódéhútǔ (伯德胡土).
The moon encroached upon the second star north of the western fan of Dōngjǐng (Eastern Well constellation).
On the day yǐwèi,
the Great Yuán army attacked Bòjīzhǎngzhài in Tàiyuán.
On the day dīngyǒu,
they approached Tàiyuán city,
and attacked Jiāochéng and Qīngyuán.
On the day guǐmǎo,
ice walls and 'deer antlers' (defensive stakes) were erected along the river.
In winter, the tenth month, on the day dīngwèi,
due to continuous rain,
an edict was issued to extend the deadline for farmers' tax payments.
On the day gēngxū,
as there was to be an engagement with the Sòng,
an edict commanded military commanders to discipline their troops.
On the day xīnhài,
officials were dispatched to requisition civilian horses,
and a red reward schedule was published to encourage compliance.
On the day jiǎyín,
Gāo Rǔlì (高汝礪) and Zhāng Xíngjiǎn (張行簡) were ordered to jointly compile the Veritable Records of Emperor Zhāngzōng (Zhāngzōng Shílù).
The Xīzhōu Commander-in-Chief's residence presented news of their victory over the Sòng people at Zhōngdù.
On the day yǐmǎo,
the Great Yuán army raided Zhōngshān Prefecture and Xīnlè County.
On the day bǐngchén,
Dānzhōu presented auspicious grain,
with different stalks bearing the same ear.
On the day xīnyǒu,
regulations were established for punishing officials of prefectures, departments, and counties who failed to detect spies.
On the day rénxū,
Xǔ Gǔ (許古), Right Remonstrance Official (Yòu Sī Jiàn) and concurrently Palace Censor (Shì Yùshǐ), submitted a memorial,
requesting to first send envoys to negotiate peace with Sòng.
On the day yǐchǒu,
the Great Yuán army captured Cízhōu.
On the day bǐngyín,
laws were established for officials who did not seek office or avoided appointment.
Gāo Rǔlì submitted a memorial saying,
if the peace negotiations were initiated by us,
it might appear as a sign of weakness,
which would be inconvenient.
On the day wùchén,
the emperor ordered Xǔ Gǔ to draft a dispatch for peace negotiations with Sòng.
After it was submitted and shown to the chief ministers,
the chief ministers believed its words contained an air of supplication,
merely showing weakness,
and thus had no merit.
The discussion was then dropped.
On the day xīnwèi,
the Liúquán Affairs Office was abolished.
The Great Yuán army captured Zōupíng, Chángshān, and Zībì Prefecture.
On the day rénshēn,
the state title of Xún (郇) was changed to Guǎn (管),
to avoid using a character from the emperor's given name.
Gāo Rǔlì submitted a memorial requesting retirement,
but it was not granted.
In the eleventh month, on the day Rénwǔ,
Cóngyí Yílài Mǎinú said:
"As for the bandits of Wǔyuánshān, Yú Zhāng and others, if they are all executed,
despite repeated imperial edicts granting them exemption from punishment,
I fear it would go against the imperial grace and trust.
Furthermore, their relatives are stranded in Sòng territory,
nearby in Jūnzhōu,
and might stir up trouble.
I request that their lives be spared,
and that they be resettled in Guīdé, Suī, Chén, Jūn, and Xǔ for convenience."
An imperial edict approved this.
On the day Guǐwèi,
a halo encircled the stars Mù (Jupiter) and Huǒ (Mars);
Mù was in Wèi,
and Huǒ was in Mǎo.
On the day Bǐngxū,
Tàibái (Venus) appeared in daytime.
The Hanlin Attendant Lecturer Yáng Yúnyì was dispatched to offer sacrifice to it.
Dàyuán troops recaptured the three prefectures of Shāndōng Bīn, Dì, and Bó.
On the day Jǐchǒu,
Zīzhōu was taken.
On the day Gēngyín,
Yízhōu was taken.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
more than a thousand households from the Héxī Jūnà, Jiānnà, and other tribes surrendered.
On the day Dīngyǒu,
an imperial edict ordered the traveling marshal's offices in Táng, Dèng, and Càizhōu to raise an army to attack Sòng.
On the day Wùxū,
Dàyuán troops attacked Tàiyuánfǔ.
On the day Gēngzǐ,
the Emperor said to the prime ministers:
"I have heard that the common people are displaced,
and all outstanding taxes are assigned to existing households.
How can people endure this?
Moreover, too much money for military provisions has been added,
and those who have fled will certainly not return to their occupations.
Let this be discussed and abolished."
The prime ministers requested that officials from the touring department be ordered to inspect and verify the remissions and loans,
and that those who had already paid on behalf of others be given special favors,
either by being exempted from other corvée duties,
or by having a quarter of their household's miscellaneous levies reduced.
The Emperor said:
"I have never ceased to be concerned about this matter;
let it be carried out promptly."
In the twelfth month, on the new moon day Jiǎchén,
Dàyuán troops attacked Lùzhōu,
and Commandant Mǎ Fǔ died there.
On the day Wùshēn,
at the Yífēngzhài in Jìmò, seventy-two common people from the Dàzǎifǔ of Japan were found on a large ship.
They had encountered a storm while buying grain
and drifted to China.
The authorities verified that there was no deception,
and an imperial edict provided them with provisions
to enable their return to their homeland.
On the day Gēngxū,
Marshal Zǔojiānjūn Púchá Wǔjīn was promoted to Yòufùyuánshuài,
acting Cānzhīzhèngshì,
and appointed to the Liáodōng Xíngshěng.
On this day,
Dàyuán troops pacified Yìdūfǔ.
On the day Xīnhài,
Xú Dǐng of Shǎnxī Xíngshěng remonstrated against attacking Sòng,
but was not heeded.
On the day Jiǎyín,
the Jīngluèshǐ of Hǎizhōu reported that Tíkòng Hán Bì defeated Sòng people at Yáncāng.
On the day Jǐwèi,
Dàyuán troops attacked Yízhōu again.
Officials and common people abandoned the city and fled.
On the day Xīnyǒu,
Mìzhōu was taken,
and Jíedùshǐ Wányán Hú died there.
On the day Rénxū,
Hóu Zhì concurrently held the post of Sānsīshǐ.
On the day Gēngwǔ,
fugitive households who returned to their occupations were exempted from corvée tax.
In the second year, spring, first month, on the day Yǐhài,
an imperial edict ordered discussions on relief and compassion.
On the day Xīnsì,
an imperial order prohibited southern expedition generals from wanton killing and looting wherever they went.
On the day Rénwǔ,
Sòng people attacked Huáinán.
The Tángzhōu Marshal's Office defeated them,
capturing leaders Lǐ Xióngtāo and Chén Gāo and returning.
On the day Guǐwèi,
the Vice Commissioner of the Near Attendants Bureau, Ékě, sent an envoy to report the victory of the southern army.
On the day Yǐyǒu,
the Shǎnxī Xíngshěng captured a person returning to their homeland,
who reported that Dàyuán troops had besieged Xiàwángchéng,
and Lǐ Zūnxū had ordered his son to defend it while he himself fled to Xīliáng.
An imperial edict instructed the various marshal's offices to clearly establish scouts
and strictly prepare defenses.
On the day Wùzǐ,
Wányán Sàibù, Marshal of Táng and Dèng, reported successive victories over Sòng people.
Sòng people attacked Sìzhōu,
and were again repulsed in battle.
In the second month, on the day Guǐmǎo,
Sòng people invaded Qīngkǒu.
The traveling Privy Council dispatched troops to defeat them.
On the day Jiǎchén,
outstanding rents in Zhōngjīng, Sōng, Rǔ and other prefectures were remitted.
Xú Dǐng was instructed that if Sòng Sànguān could be held, it should be,
but if not, it should be burned down before returning.
The law for slaves rescuing their masters was established.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
Ékě defeated Sòng people at Fángshān.
Héshíliè Huánduān also sent an envoy to report victories at Guāngzhōu and Xìnyáng.
On the day Gēngxū,
the Jīngluè of Hǎizhōu defeated Sòng troops at Qúshān.
He presented a memorial requesting continued military provisions,
and ordered the Dōngpíng Marshal's Office to dispatch troops to escort supplies and provisions to support him.
Hé Miǎn and others from Chángshèxiàn, Xǔzhōu, plotted rebellion
and were executed.
On the day Xīnhài,
Zhāng Xíngxìn was appointed Jíedùshǐ of Zhānghuàjūn and concurrently Guǎnèi Guānchásǐ of Jīngzhōu.
On the day Rénzǐ,
the censor requested, due to the retreat of the northern troops,
the reduction of superfluous officials in the various traveling Privy Councils and Marshal's Offices.
The Department of State Affairs deemed it inconvenient,
and the Emperor followed the words of the Department of State Affairs,
maintaining the old system.
Wányán Sàibù reported a victory at Zǎoyáng.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
Wányán Ālín reported a victory at Zàojiāobǎo.
On the day Dīngsì,
the Shòuzhōu Traveling Privy Council destroyed the Sòng people's aquatic fort at Gāoliǔqiáo,
razed their fort, and returned.
On the day Rénxū,
Ékě dispatched troops to take the Sòng palisade at Pánlǐng,
and also defeated their forces at Péijiāzhuāng, Hánshānlǐng, Lóngmén Guān, and other places,
obtaining over two thousand shí of grain.
On the day Yǐchǒu,
the Emperor instructed the Privy Council, saying:
"The soldiers in Zhōngjīng, Shāng, and Guó prefectures are willing to cultivate military farms;
compared to previously, land was allotted to them.
I hear that the Xú and Sù armies alone are unwilling to accept,
thinking that if land is given, their stipends will surely be cut.
Would I do such a thing?
Let my intention be conveyed to them."
On the day Bǐngyín,
the Emperor instructed the Department of State Affairs, saying:
"I hear that many officials collecting grain in Zhōngdū are rejected by the Ministry of Personnel,
without considering the advantages and disadvantages when there is a shortage.
Furthermore, those who have performed meritorious service in battle
are required to be guaranteed by officials.
Such people are all volunteers and commoners;
how would they know official ranks?
If the official documents are credible,
they should be given the positions immediately.
As for those who, while in the capital,
transported firewood and charcoal into the city,
I once, out of grace, bestowed official positions upon them.
How could this be fraudulent?
Yet, sometimes they too were obstructed.
Let this be made clear to all of them;
do not let this happen again."
Héshíliè Yáwǔtǎ defeated Sòng people at Xūyí Jūn,
and the number of captives was reported.
On the day Jǐsì,
Hóu Zhì was made traveling provincial governor for Héběi,
concurrently acting as the Sānsī Ānfǔsī.
In the third month, on the day Gēngchén,
the Department of State Affairs gathered civil officials to discuss the selection of jinshi,
and an imperial edict ordered it to be carried out according to the Tàihé precedent.
On the day Guǐwèi,
Ékě defeated Sòng people at Guānghuà Jūn.
On the day Jiǎshēn,
it was Chángchūn Festival.
On the day Wùzǐ,
the Emperor instructed the prime ministers, saying:
"According to the old system,
jinshi candidates for the palace examination left the palace after dusk.
Recently, I wished to revert to the old practice,
but I fear that those who are good at writing but slow in thought
might not be able to fully demonstrate their talent.
Therefore, let them leave only after sunset."
Bǎhúlǔ, the Censor-in-Chief, was made Cānzhīzhèngshì.
Yáng Zhēn, the Shàngshū of Shǎnxī Xíngliùbù, was stripped of five official ranks,
received one hundred and seventy strokes of the rod,
and was dismissed from office.
Ékě submitted a memorial stating that
the official army, having entered Sòng territory from Tóngbǎi,
achieved many victories wherever they advanced.
On the day Guǐsì,
Sòng people contended for Zàojiāobǎo and
attacked the official army.
The army was routed,
and the commanding general Wányán Ālín died in battle.
On the day Bǐngshēn,
the system of official rewards for reporting and apprehending bandits in the capital was revised.
On the day Xīnchǒu,
Púchá Wǔjīn of Shàngjīng Xíngshěng memorialized that
Zuǒjiānjūn Gēbùǎi falsely accused Héshíliè Àndūn, the Deputy Pacification Commissioner of Fāngzhōu, of plotting rebellion and then killed him.
The matter was referred to the Department of State Affairs.
The prime ministers suggested that Àndūn's death should be followed by a gradual discussion of compassionate provisions,
and Gēbùǎi should also be temporarily reined in and kept in service.
The Emperor reluctantly agreed to their suggestion.
In the summer, fourth month, on the day Rén-yín, the first day of the month,
Púchá Wǔjīn reported:
Liáodōng Commissioner Ālǐbùsūn lent grain to Gāolí, but Gāolí did not respond.
He then plundered their border with his troops.
The Emperor ordered Wǔjīn to send an envoy with an imperial edict to Gāolí,
so they would know that raising an army was not the intent of the imperial court.
On the day Yǐ-sì,
an imperial edict was issued to officials in Hénán lù from the Commissioner-General's Office and above,
to serve as special envoys for capturing bandits.
Defensive Prefects and their deputies, and hereditary Méng'ān who were talented and martial, were appointed as their assistants.
Furthermore, Wányán Máoliáng Hǔ, the Commandant of the Púwáng Mansion,
was appointed as a special envoy for supervision,
to patrol and oversee.
On this day,
a partial amnesty was granted in Liáodōng and other circuits.
Jiágǔ Bìlán, the Minister of Revenue, was appointed as Grand Academician of the Hanlin Academy,
provisionally acting as Co-administrator of the Bureau of Military Affairs,
to preside over the provincial administration in Liáodōng.
On the day Dīng-wèi,
Chéngyì defeated Sòng people at Zàojiāo Fort.
On the day Gēng-xū,

the Censor impeached Lǐ Wéiyuè, the consultant official of the Jíxiányuàn, stating that he was originally a household slave of Zhào Xiàoxuǎn, a successful candidate in the imperial examination from Wújí County, Zhōngshān Prefecture.
They requested that the matter be rectified.
The Emperor said:
"When the state employs people,
why discriminate between noble and humble?"
He ordered that fifty taels of official silver be used to redeem him and make him a commoner,
and that his appointment remain unchanged.
On the day Rén-zǐ,
Grand Supervising Secretary Wányán Sùlán and Deputy Director of the Imperial Household Bureau Èkě Tóng were dispatched to Liáodōng,
to investigate the matter of the rebel Wànnú.
The Acting Provincial Governor Hóu Zhì led troops to recover Mìzhōu.
Commissioner Zhū Chēn recovered Gāomì County.
On the day Guǐ-chǒu,
Wányán Sùlán requested an imperial edict to Gāolí to reopen mutual markets,
which was granted.
On the day Yǐ-mǎo,
a special decree granted the degree to 140 martial examination candidates, including Wēndíhǎn Jiǎozhù.
On the day Dīng-sì,
the army of the Shǎnxī Provincial Administration defeated the Sòng at Jīgōngshān,
took Hézhōu and Chéngzhōu,
and reached Hēgǔ Pass in Héchí County.
All defenders fled.
They captured ninety thousand hú of grain
and tens of millions of cash,
with countless military supplies.
On the day Wù-wǔ,
the Red Turbans attacked Xú and Pī,
and the army of the Acting Bureau of Military Affairs thoroughly defeated them.
On the day Jǐ-wèi,
since Ālǐbùsūn's defeat at Tóngguān,
his whereabouts were unknown.
He changed his name and hid in Zhèchéng,
but was detected by the Censor.
His family members were arrested,
and he was to be thoroughly investigated.
He then sent his son to submit a letter to the Board of Civil Office to await punishment.
The court officials strongly requested his execution,
to punish disloyalty.
The Emperor eventually pardoned his crime,
and instructed him to prove his loyalty.
On the day Guǐ-hài,
important officials were dispatched to investigate unjust cases in the capital.
On the day Dīng-mǎo,
locusts infested various commanderies in Hénán.
Línláo lù reported a victory over Sòng people.
The Dōngpíng Provincial Administration defeated the Black Banner bandits,
capturing Dùxī County.
The chief bandit Lǐ Quán came to reinforce,
and was also defeated.
On the day Wù-chén,
the Héběi Provincial Administration defeated the Red Turbans,
advanced to Mìzhōu,
accepted the surrender of dozens of puppet generals and officers,
and seven hundred soldiers,
and restored them all to their former occupations.
In the fifth month, on the day Xīn-wèi, the first day of the month,
Wányán Lǘshān, Marshal of Fèngxiáng, defeated Sòng people at Bùluòguō and Xiānglú Fort and other garrisons.
On the day Jiǎ-xū,
Deputy Pacification Commissioner Huángguā Ālúdá attacked and defeated Lǐ Quán in Jǔzhōu and south of Rìzhào County,
striking from three directions,
and pursuing the fleeing enemy for forty lǐ.
On the day Bǐng-zǐ,
Xīxià people entered Fūyán from Jiāzhōu.
Marshal Chénglì dispatched troops to defeat them at Mǎjífēng.
The victory report arrived on this day.
An imperial edict was issued to dispatch officials to oversee the capture of locusts in various circuits of Hénán.
On the day Xīn-sì,
the successful candidates in the imperial examinations (on policy, essays, and classic interpretations) and the martial examination candidates were granted an audience,
and were bestowed with appointment documents and official attire.
Qǔ Guì, a commoner from Láizhōu, murdered Zhuǎn Núl, a relative of the Military Commissioner and Pacification Commissioner,
declared himself marshal,
and colluded with Sòng people to occupy the city and rebel.
The Shāndōng Pacification Bureau dispatched Commissioner Wáng Tíngyù and Deputy Pacification Commissioner Huángguā Ālúdá and others to suppress and pacify them,
beheading the puppet commander Bái Zhēn and dozens of his aides,
capturing Qǔ Guì and the puppet Military Commissioner Lǚ Zhōng and over ten others alive,
and executing them.
Then, Tíngyù was ordered to guard Lái,
Zhū Chēn to guard Mì,
and Ālúdá to guard Nínghǎi,
to pacify their people.
On the day Bǐng-xū,
the Shǎnxī Provincial Administration reported:
"In mid-fourth month,
Chéngyì, Acting Marshal of Gǒngzhōu, dispatched Commissioner Wūgǔlún Chángshòu and Nàlán Jìsēng to attack Sòng from separate routes.
Chángshòu sallied forth from Yánchuān Town,
and Jìsēng from Tiěchéng Fort.
Both achieved victories and returned."
On the day Xīn-mǎo,
the army of the Southern City under the Shòuzhōu Acting Bureau of Military Affairs attacked Xīnchéng Town,
and one army hastened to Shǐhé,
fighting and defeating the Sòng people.
On the day Rén-chén,
the Héběi Provincial Administration recovered Huángxiàn.
On the day Yǐ-wèi,
the merits of the generals and soldiers who campaigned south from Fèngxiáng, Qín, and Gǒng were assessed,
and each was promoted in official rank.
On the day Bǐng-shēn,
the salaries of officials attending the court and various attendants were increased.
On the day Wù-xū,
the Shǎnxī Provincial Administration repeatedly reported victories of Chéngyì and others entering Sòng territory.
On the day Jǐ-hài,
the troops of Dà Yuán advanced into Jǐnzhōu,
and Marshal Liú Zhònghēng died there.
On the day Gēng-zǐ,
a pack of wolves in Shǎnzhōu injured over a hundred people.
Rewards were immediately offered to recruit people to hunt and kill them.
On the *jiǎchén* day of the sixth month,
the Shūmìyuàn reported:
"Reports from various circuits state that the Great Yuán are amassing troops in Yìzhōu and Fēihú,
intending to advance southward in separate columns.
Observing their intentions, they are not aimed at Héběi,
but at Shǎnxī.
For the righteous volunteers, local troops, and Fān-Hàn archers of the various circuits in Hédōng,
it is advisable to drill them during the agricultural off-season,
to be prepared for emergencies.
Dōngpíng and Shànzhōu are strategic points.
Their farmers, grain, and livestock should be moved proactively
to defensible cities.
Water stockades near cities should be repaired,
using them for fortification.
Tónggǔ extends far to Shāng and Guó.
The two shuàifǔs should be ordered to select officials to inspect the strategic passes."
They also reported,
"Jiǎ Yǔ and others assassinated Miáo Dàorùn.
We request that Yǔ and the others be punished for the crime of unauthorized killing.
For other prefectures and counties, headmen should be appointed to their proper positions,
enabling them to govern their respective areas."
The Emperor responded to them, saying:
"Miáo Dàorùn's followers should be quickly gathered.
The right and wrong of Yǔ and others are not yet clear,
so for now, let them be unquestioned.
Headmen each governing an area
is a matter of great importance and potential harm.
It should be deliberated upon more carefully."
The bandit Féng Tiānyǔ of Shízhōu, with several thousand followers,
occupied Línquán County and caused disturbances.
The shuàifǔ ordered a general to suppress them,
but he was defeated by the bandits.
Generals from neighboring prefectures and counties planned to join them.
The prefectural governor, Gēsīliè Gōngshùn, rushed there with troops.
Tiānyǔ and dozens of others came forward to surrender,
but Gōngshùn killed them.
The remaining bandits fled to protect Jīcuìshān.
General Wáng Jiǔsī was sent to attack them,
but could not overcome them.
An imperial edict ordered Mǎ Jìliáng, a compiler in the Guóshǐyuàn, to take imperial edicts, gold, and silk to recruit them.
By the time he arrived,
Jiǔsī had already broken through the stockade,
killing two thousand bandits.
The rest again fled to difficult terrain.
Soon after,
their partisans, Ān Guóyòng and others, numbering over five thousand, surrendered to Jìliáng.
Guóyòng was immediately appointed as Acting Administrator of the Méngzhōu Defense Command,
and others were promoted in due order.
Their followers were dispersed between Jiàng and Huò.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
Bǎhúlǔ, a Cānzhī Zhèngshì, was given temporary authority as Zuǒ Fù Yuánshuài,
to cooperate with Píngzhāng Zhèngshì Xū Dǐng in defending against the autumn incursions.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
Miáo Dàorùn's troops requested to be assigned to the Lùzhōu Yuánshuàifǔ.
An imperial edict ordered the Héběi Xíngshěng to deliberate on the matter.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
the Hóng'ǎo bandits attacked Yízhōu.
The government troops defeated them,
pursuing them to Báilǐgǎng.
Dōutíkòng Qí Xìn died in battle.
An imperial edict ordered the relevant authorities to discuss posthumous honors and compensation.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
Jiānchá Yùshǐ Niángē Suōshī was sent to Hézhōng, Jiàng, Jiě, and other commanderies
to consult with the local defense officials on defensible cities.
On the *dīngsì* day,
the Emperor, due to the prolonged drought,
instructed the prime minister to investigate wrongful convictions in the capital's prisons.
He then mentioned the common people in the capital
who had collected coal.
After receiving payment for it,
a censor impeached them for excessive claims of public money
and imprisoned them.
Some argued for the death penalty.
He asked, "I wish to treat all of them leniently,
what do you think?"
Gāo Qí replied that this was not advisable,
so it was stopped.
On the *rénxū* day,
a censor reported that Zāng Bóshēng, a Yuánwàiláng of the Hùbù, had supplied Xīzhōu.
Coincidentally, government troops won a battle,
and he also presumptuously received a promotion.
The censor requested that he be punished.
The Emperor said:
"Among those on the military front,
there are many such cases, not just Bóshēng.
If he is immediately punished now,
everyone else will be uneasy.
Moreover, if we investigate his origin,
it will inevitably implicate the shuàifǔ.
In these times of many troubles,
should we, for the sake of one official,
forget the greater strategy?
Just order that it be rectified."
On the *guǐhài* day,
Gāo Rǔlì and Túshān Sīzhōng were sent to pray for rain.
In the seventh month of autumn, on the *gēngwǔ* day, the first day of the month,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
an imperial edict awarded the generals and soldiers of the southern expedition in varying degrees.
The Xià people invaded Gāngǔ.
Tíkòng Jiágǔ Ruì and his deputy Zhào Fáng attacked and drove them away.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
due to the drought,
an imperial edict was issued to the capital and the provinces.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
officials were sent to perform distant sacrifices to the Five Sacred Mountains, Four Rivers, and Four Seas in the northern suburbs,
to offer sacrifices at the Tàimiào,
to offer sacrifices to the Tàishè and Tàijì,
and to offer sacrifices to the Jiǔgōng Guìshén in the eastern suburbs,
to pray for rain.
Tàizǐ Tàibǎo Ābùhǎndégāng and Lǐbù Shàngshū Yáng Yúnyì were sent on separate routes to investigate wrongful convictions.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
there was heavy rain.
The Crown Prince, princes, and all officials presented a memorial requesting that the Emperor resume residence in the main hall
and return to his regular diet.
On the *gēngyín* day,
competent and capable officials who had no irregularities in their *tíkòng* selection were chosen for promotion.
Interpreters who were not performing their duties were
to be verified for having completed their salaried months and then discharged.
Capable individuals were to be selected instead.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
the Xià people again invaded Gāngǔ.
Jiágǔ Ruì utterly defeated them.
Following the words of Diǎnjiǎn Chéngxuán,
officials were sent to various circuits to select officials in mourning or awaiting appointments, and those from the imperial guards capable of commanding troops,
resulting in one hundred and six individuals,
who were handed over to the Shūmìyuàn for deployment.
On the *gēngzǐ* day, the first day of the eighth month,
the Héběi Xíngshěng assigned Miáo Dàorùn's army to Zhuōzhōu Cìshǐ Lǐ Quélǘ,
with Zhāng Fǔ and Zhāng Róu as his deputies.
On the *wùshēn* day,
an imperial edict granted basic salary to centurions and below in the imperial guards who were awaiting appointments,
while still having them perform duties,
to be dispatched when their assignments were due.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
an imperial edict ordered Wányán Tíng of the Héběi Xíngshěng to advance with his army to reinforce Tián Zhuó, the Zhāofǔshǐ of Shāndōng.
Henceforth, meritorious generals and soldiers should first be rewarded by Zhuó and then reported.
The Great Yuán sent Mùhuálǐ and others to lead tens of thousands of infantry and cavalry from Tàihélǐng to sweep through Hédōng.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
the Great Yuán troops captured Dàizhōu.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
Tíkòng Gēsīliè Chǒuhàn of Dìzhōu attacked the bandit Zhāng Jù,
utterly defeating his forces,
and recovered Bīn and Dì prefectures.
The treacherous person Lǐ Yí was executed.
Returning northern commoners were forbidden from crossing the river.
On the *wùchén* day,
the Great Yuán troops captured Xízhōu.
On the *yǐhài* day of the ninth month,
Tàiyuán Fǔ fell,
and Yuánshuài Zuǒ Jiānjūn and concurrently Zhīshūfǔshì Wūgǔlún Déshēng died there.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
the Emperor instructed the Crown Prince, saying:
"The speed of military affairs
is critically linked to opportune moments.
If everything is reviewed by the center,
it may be delayed.
From now on, for matters that require immediate action,
act first and then report."
Nàhé Púlàdū, Shàngshū of the Hùbù, was appointed Yuánshuài Yòu Jiānjūn,
and was to act on behalf of the Yuánshuàifǔ in Lùzhōu.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
nine defense commands were established at Qínguān and other places,
and Wányán Púchá and others were ordered to garrison the various strategic passes.
A relocation of Hǎizhōu was discussed,
but Hóu Zhì argued against it as inconvenient,
and it was stopped.
The Great Yuán troops swept through Fénzhōu,
and Jiédùshǐ Wùyán Échūhǔ died there.
On the *gēngyín* day,
Lǐ Quán captured Mìzhōu,
seizing Zhāofǔ Fùshǐ Huángguā Ālúdá and Tóngzhī Jiédùshǐ Jiágǔ Sìjiānú.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
the Great Yuán troops captured Xiàoyì County.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
officials of the Xíng Liùbù were established for various localities.
The chief officials of the Jīngfǔ Jiézhèn were appointed as Shàngshū,
followed by Shìláng, Lángzhōng, and Yuánwàiláng;
the chief officials of the Fángcì were Shìláng,
followed by Lángzhōng, Yuánwàiláng, and Zhǔshì;
the Gōudàng officials were to be employed as directed by their superiors.
All officials of prefectures and counties were to concurrently serve as Quànnóngshì.
The chief officials of the Fángcì and those at or below Tóngzhī of the Jīngfǔ Jiézhèn were to serve as Fùshǐ.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
Lǐ Quán captured Shòuguāng County.
In winter, in the tenth month, on the *Jiǎchén* day,
Lǐ Quán (李全) defeated Zōupíng (鄒平) County.
On the *Wùshēn* day,
he defeated Líqú (臨朐) County.
On the *Jǐyǒu* day,
the Dàyuán (大元) soldiers overran Jiàng (絳) and Lù (潞).
On the *Rénzǐ* day,
they attacked Píngyáng (平陽).
Tíkòng (提控) Guō Yòng (郭用) died there.
On the *Guǐchǒu* day,
Píngyáng (平陽) was taken.
Zhīfǔshì (知府事), Quán Cānzhīzhèngshì (權參知政事), Xíng Shàngshūshěng (行尚書省) Lǐ Gé (李革) and Cóng Tǎn (從坦) died there.
On the *Jiǎyín* day,
Quán Píngdìngzhōu Cìshǐ (權平定州刺史) Fàn Duó (范鐸) was executed
for abandoning the city.
An imperial edict ordered officials responsible for recording prisoners in all prefectures
to report all cases of those charged with military offenses for trial.
Shāndōng Lù Zhuǎnyùn Fùshǐ (山東路轉運副使) concurrent Tóngzhī Yízhōu Fángyùshǐ (同知沂州防禦使) Chéng Jiǎn (程戩) and Pīzhōu Fùtíkòng (邳州副提控) Wáng Rǔlín (王汝霖) and others colluded with the Sòng (宋) people to rebel,
and were executed.
The Sòng (宋) people attacked Liánshuǐ (漣水) County.
Tíkòng (提控) Liú Yīng (劉瑛) defeated them.
On the *Dīngsì* day,
the Dàyuán (大元) soldiers attacked Zézhōu (澤州).
On the *Wùwǔ* day,
the Shàngshūshěng (尚書省) reported that spies and deserters had been captured,
most of whom were Buddhist or Daoist monks.
An imperial edict stated that in border prefectures,
only those who had received their ordination there were allowed to reside in their original places.
Those who came from Héběi (河北) and Shāndōng (山東) were to be sent to inland prefectures,
and their movements were to be monitored.
On the *Jǐwèi* day,
Lǐ Quán (李全) occupied Ānqiu (安丘).
Tíkòng (提控) Wáng Zhèng (王政) camped at Chānglè (昌樂), awaiting Wáng Tíngyù’s (王庭玉) forces to advance together for suppression.
Xuānchāi Tàifǔ Shǎojiān (宣差太府少監) Bó Déwán (伯德玩) unauthorizedly led Zhèng’s (政) troops to attack Quán (全),
and was defeated by Quán (全).
Tíkòng (提控) Wáng Xiǎn (王顯) died there.
Tián Zhuó (田琢) memorialized requesting that Wán (玩) be punished.
On the *Guǐhài* day,
the moon encroached upon the lesser star in the left horn of Xuānyuán (軒轅).
On the *Jiǎzǐ* day,
an imperial edict ordered the prefectures of Xīn (忻), Dài (代), Nínghuà (寧化), and Dōngshèng (東勝) in Hédōngběi Lù (河東北路) to all be subject to the command of the Lánzhōu Shuàifǔ (嵐州帥府).
In the eleventh month, on the *Gēngwǔ* day,
a general amnesty was declared.
On the *Gēngchén* day,
the Emperor attended the Dēngxiánmén (登賢門) and summoned former officials who had retired from service, granting them food
and inquiring about the successes and failures of current policies.
On the *Xīnsì* day,
Xíng Yuánshuàifǔ (行元帥府) Héshíliè Huánduān (紇石烈桓端) was appointed Quán Qiān Shūmìyuàn Shì (權簽樞密院事),
with his Xíngyuàn (行院) at Xúzhōu (徐州).
Quán Yòudūjiān (權右都監) É Kěxíng (訛可行) was appointed Xíng Yuánshuàifǔ Shì (行元帥府事) at Xīzhōu (息州).
On the *Jiǎshēn* day,
an imperial edict ordered the prefectures of Xí (隰), Jí (吉), etc., in Hédōngnán Lù (河東南路) to be subject to the command of the Jiàngzhōu Yuánshuàifǔ (絳州元帥府).
The Dàyuán (大元) soldiers recovered Lùzhōu (潞州).
Yuánshuài Yòujiānjūn (元帥右監軍) Nàhé Púlàdū (納合蒲剌都) and Cānyìguān Xiū Qǐjūzhù (參議官修起居注) Wáng Liángchén (王良臣) died there.
On the *Wùzǐ* day,
Kāngǔ Tíkòng (龕谷提控) Jiágǔ Ruì (夾谷瑞) defeated the Xià (夏) people at Zhígūbǎo (質孤堡).
The Héběi Xíngshěng (河北行省) reported a victory at Hǎizhōu (海州).
On the *Rénchén* day,

regulations were established concerning the sons and grandsons of military officials in prefectures that had undergone warfare, prohibiting them from receiving inherited benefits if they were not from the local jurisdiction or if they missed the deadline for inheritance.
On the *Bǐngshēn* day,
the Dàyuán (大元) soldiers captured Háncūnzài (韓村砦) in Tàiyuán (太原).
Regulations for fire prevention in the capital were established.
In the twelfth month, on the *Jǐhài* day, the first day of the month,
Yùshǐzhōngchéng (御史中丞) Wányán Bójiā (完顏伯嘉) was appointed Quán Cānzhīzhèngshì (權參知政事) and Yuánshuài Zuǒjiānjūn (元帥左監軍),
with his Xíng Shàngshūshěng Yuánshuàifǔ (行尚書省元帥府) at Hézhōngfǔ (河中府),
to command Hédōngnán (河東南) and Hédōngběi (河東北) circuits and act according to expediency.
Jiàngzhōu (絳州) was elevated to Jìn'ānfǔ (晉安府),
commanding the troops of Hédōngnán Lù (河東南路).
Píngyáng (平陽) was demoted to a Sǎnfǔ (散府).
On the *Xīnchǒu* day,
Qiān Shūmìyuàn Shì (簽樞密院事) Púchá Yílàdū (蒲察移剌都) was executed.
On the *Rényín* day,
former Shāndōng Xīlù Zhuǎnyùnshǐ (山東西路轉運使) (retired) Yílà Fúsēng (移剌福僧) submitted a memorial concerning current affairs.
On the *Guǐmǎo* day,
an imperial edict appointed Dàlǐqīng (大理卿) Wēndíhǎn Dá (溫迪罕達) as Quán Tóng Qiān Shūmìyuàn Shì (權同簽樞密院事),
with his Xíngyuàn (行院) at Xǔzhōu (許州).
On the *Jiǎchén* day,
an imperial edict was issued to the internal and external courts regarding the execution of Yílàdū (移剌都).
On the *Yǐsì* day,
Túdān Sīzhōng (徒單思忠) was ordered to pray for snow.
Soon after,
there was heavy snow.
On the *Jiǎyín* day,
Kāifēngfǔ Zhìzhōng (開封府治中) Lǚ Zǐyǔ (呂子羽) and others were sent as envoys to Sòng (宋) to negotiate peace.
The Red Jacket bandits attacked Húcáizhài (胡材寨) in Péngchéng (彭城).
Xúzhōu (徐州) troops attacked and defeated them.
On the *Yǐmǎo* day,
Lǐbù Shìláng (禮部侍郎) Mǒnián Húlǔlà (抹撚胡魯剌) was appointed Fényángjūn Jiédùshǐ (汾陽軍節度使),
Quán Yuánshuài Yòujiānjūn (權元帥右監軍),
to, with Lánzhōu Yuánshuài (嵐州元帥) Gǔlǐ Jiǎshílún (古里甲石倫), recover Hédōng (河東).
On the *Dīngsì* day,
soldiers along the river embankments (*sào* 埽兵) were registered.
On the *Guǐhài* day,
the Shàngshūshěng (尚書省) stated:
“The Shūmì (樞密) commands all troops under heaven.
The Crown Prince supervises the army,
and Xíngyuàn (行院) are also established in various circuits.
Those who achieve merit or violate military discipline
must report to the Xíngyuàn (行院),
which then reports to the Crown Prince,
until approval is granted.
Only then can punishments or rewards be administered.
The relevant officials merely carry out these orders.
From now on, all military orders concerning rewards and punishments
must be clearly specified in imperial edicts and decrees,
to prevent military commanders from engaging in fraud and deception.”
The Emperor agreed to this.
Shūmì Fùshǐ Fùmǎ Dūwèi (樞密副使駙馬都尉) Púsǎn Ānzhēn (僕散安貞) was appointed Zuǒ Fùyuánshuài (左副元帥),
Quán Cānzhīzhèngshì (權參知政事),
and Xíng Shàngshūshěng Yuánshuàifǔ Shì (行尚書省元帥府事),
to campaign against Sòng (宋).
On the *Jiǎzǐ* day,
the Emperor issued an edict to the relevant officials:
“Beggars in the capital are dying from the bitter cold.
I deeply pity them.
They should be given bamboo and wood from the imperial garden
and allowed to live in warm places.”
In the third year, in spring, in the first month, on the *Gēngwǔ* day,
Lǚ Zǐyǔ (呂子羽) reached Huái (淮),
but the Sòng (宋) people did not receive him, and he returned.
