An imperial edict ordered a campaign against Sòng (宋).
On the *Bǐngzǐ* day,
a land tax on cultivated fields was imposed,
and the implementation of equal distribution was discussed.
On the *Wùyín* day,
an imperial order prohibited the distribution of military provisions to the populace, instead advocating for purchasing them through fair trade at border cities.
Regulations were established for military officers serving in garrisons or on campaigns, regarding the reduction of their seniority and monthly days.
On the *Rénwǔ* day,
there was heavy snow.
The Emperor heard the sound of tiles being removed from the eastern side wing
and asked his attendants.
He learned that laborers were repairing the storerooms and residential quarters.
The Emperor felt saddened
and admonished the supervisor, saying:
“It is snowing and cold, should the laborers not rest?
Stop them for now.”
On the *Bǐngxū* day,
Héshíliè Yáwūtǎ (紇石烈牙吾塔) reported a victory at Xiāngshāncūn (香山村) in Háozhōu (濠州).
On the *Dīnghài* day,
the Xuānhuī (宣徽) was instructed
that officials were exempt from congratulating the Empress on her birthday.
On the *Rénchén* day,
because the Dàyuán (大元) soldiers had already secured Tàiyuán (太原)
and the situation in Héběi (河北) was no longer as it had been,
all officials were gathered to discuss long-term defense plans.
News of victory against Sòng (宋) arrived.
The Emperor said to his attendant ministers:
“How could this matter have been avoided?
Recently, envoys were sent with the sincere desire for peace,
but since they did not comply,
how could we not use military force?”
Single-male households were exempted from monthly military supply payments.
On the *Jiǎwǔ* day,
the relevant officials requested to set a price to purchase horses captured by the southern expeditionary soldiers.
The Emperor feared losing popular support
and thus leading to failure,
so he did not agree.
On the *Yǐwèi* day,
an imperial order was issued to the Shàngshūshěng (尚書省):
“From now on, when the Six Ministries submit discussions on routine matters,
they may only resubmit twice;
they are not to be urgently summoned for clarification.
Other matters that should be decided by the law courts, if resubmitted
and still found to be inappropriate, shall be fully reported
and handled by the officials.
Chancellors and executive officials, down to lesser ranks, are not to summon officials from ministries or courts.
Officials from ministries or courts are also not to visit the Secretariat.
Violators shall be punished for contravening regulations.”
On the *Dīngyǒu* day,
Dèngzhōu Yuánshuàifǔ Tíkòng (鄧州元帥府提控) Lóushì (婁室) was found guilty.
His death sentence was commuted, and his title was stripped.
In the second month, on the day Gēngzǐ,
the Emperor deliberated with the Crown Prince about a commander for the southern campaign.
Being unable to find a suitable person,
he sighed, saying:
“The world is vast,
yet in times of urgency, there is no one who can be employed.
How can I not be worried?”
Hēshíliè Yáwútǎ defeated the Sòng people at Chú.
On the day Jiǎchén,
Xū Dǐng stated:
“Regarding rewards and punishments in the army,
recent regulations require consultation with the imperial court.
That rewards come from the center,
showing where imperial grace originates,
is acceptable.
But if there is a breach of discipline,
and the commanding general cannot immediately deal with the crime,
that is unacceptable.”
An edict was issued for the Shàngshū and Jūnmì bureaus to discuss this.
The Grand Councillors requested that for officers with the rank of from the seventh grade or below, involved in defending cities or fighting in the field,
they be allowed to be summarily judged and punished,
while all others must have their cases reported for imperial decision.
The Emperor said:
“To allow only those of the seventh grade and below to be dealt with [by the generals],
the generals’ authority would be too light,
potentially leading to errors.
Henceforth, those of the fourth grade and below may be summarily judged.”
On the day Yǐsì,
Guāngshān County of Sòng was attacked,
and its commander, Cài Cóngdìng, and others were captured.
Guāngzhōu sent troops to reinforce,
but they were again defeated.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
the Emperor said to his Grand Councillors:
“The people of Jiānghuái
are known as elite and strong,
yet when our imperial army attacked Mànjīngbǎo,
their multitude was severely distressed.
When threatened to surrender,
not a single one would comply.
In our prefectures and commanderies north of the Yellow River,
upon encountering an alarm from the north,
they often surrender.
What is the reason for this?”
On the day Dīngwèi,
an imperial decree was issued that any meritorious officers and soldiers in mourning should be specially allowed to resume their posts and be promoted.
On the day Wùshēn,
Xiǎojiāngzhài of Sòng was captured,
and its commander, Wáng Dàpéng, was killed.
On the day Jǐyǒu,
Wǔxiūguān of Sòng was taken.
On the day Gēngxū,
Yuánshuài Zuǒ Dūjiān Chénglì,
obtained documents and dispatches from the Xià people’s military command and submitted them.
Although their language was somewhat disrespectful,
they all contained words about protecting borders and pacifying the people.
The Shàngshūshěng was ordered to discuss them.
The Grand Councillors stated:
“The recent losses at Zhènrong and Língpíng,
and the frequent incursions by the Xià people into our territory.
These documents are merely meant to relax our vigilance;
we should strengthen our defenses
to thwart their insidious plans.”
The Emperor assented to their words.
He further said:
“Recently, a close attendant returned from Shǎnxī,
saying that Báisā had already taken Fèngzhōu.
If Wǔxiūguān were also taken,
they would then proceed to take Shǔ.
My intention is quite different.
Even if it were taken,
how could it be held?
This campaign was undertaken because the Sòng people broke their alliance;
why would we initially covet their land?
I deeply value human life,
and only an early peace agreement would be desirable.”
Gāo Rǔlì requested to retire,
but an imperial edict graciously denied it.
On the day Jiǎyín,
an edict was issued to the Shǎnxī Xíngshěng,
stating that officials from the seventh grade and below were allowed to be appointed,
and those with crimes were allowed to be judged and punished.
Those in mourning or awaiting appointments could be employed as deemed appropriate.
For military officers with crimes above transfer or those negligent in military affairs,
the Xún'àn Yùshǐ were to handle them.
On the day Jǐwèi,
Xíngshěng Ānzhēn entered Sòng territory,
defeated the armies of Liángxiàn and others,
and captured Commander Lǐ Shēnzhī.
Reports of victories from Yòufù Yuánshuài Wányán Sàibù and Zuǒ Dūjiān Yáwútǎ at Báishíguān and Píngshānzhài
all arrived.
In the third month, on the first day Dīngmǎo,
the Shǎnxī army breached Sòng’s Hǔtóuguān,
and took Xīngyuán and Yángzhōu.
When the victory report arrived,
the Emperor was greatly pleased.
On the day Gēngwǔ,
the Sòng people were defeated at Qīkǒucāng.
On the day Jiǎxū,
Gāolì had previously requested to pay tribute,
so an envoy was sent to soothe and advise them.
Upon the envoy’s return,
he reported in a memorial that the roads were impassable,
and that talks of establishing contact would await pacification.
The Xíngshěng was ordered to temporarily maintain a loose relationship,
and not sever good ties.
On the day Wùyín,
Cáizhōu Xíngyuánshuàifǔ Yòudūjiān Wányán Hédá defeated the Sòng people at Méilíngguān,
On the day Jǐmǎo,
for Chángchūnjié,
the imperial audience was excused.
Tíkòng Àotún Wúlǐbù defeated the Sòng people at Shàngjīn County.
When the army returned to Háozhōu,
the Sòng people came to resist,
and Yáwútǎ attacked and repelled them.
On the day Yǐyǒu,
for each Jiézhèn and higher in Hénán Lù, a military arsenal was established,
with one commissioner and one deputy commissioner appointed.
For each Fángcìjùn, one Dūjiān and one Tóngjiān were appointed.
Wányán Hédá defeated the Sòng people at Mǎlíngbǎo.
On the day Bǐngxū,
Xíngshěng Ānzhēn defeated the Sòng people at Shígùshān.
On the day Jǐchǒu,
the posthumous surname Wēndūn was bestowed upon Yànchāng, the father of the Empress, Taìwèi and Bìnguó Gōng.
On the day Gēngyín,
Máchéng County of Sòng was attacked,
and captured,
its magistrate Zhāng Tì and others were taken.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
Xíngshěng Ānzhēn defeated the Sòng army at Túshān.
On the day Rénchén,
Sàibù defeated the Sòng army at Lǎokǒuzhèn,
and again defeated the Sòng people at Shígǔyá.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
seventy officials who had been dismissed due to crimes, including Fùyuánshuài Púchá Ālǐbùsūn and Yùshǐ Dàfū Yǒngxī, were reinstated.
An edict was issued to Taìyuán and other circuits,
that for vacant official posts in prefectures and counties,
the people should elect their beloved as chiefs,
and the Xíngshěng would appropriately assign them duties.
Also, to transport salt into Shǎnxī
to meet requirements,
Xū Dǐng was ordered to concurrently oversee this matter.
In the intercalary third month, on the first day Bǐngshēn.
The law on the crime of slaughtering cattle was re-emphasized.
The area east of Xióng and Bà was entrusted to Quán Zhōngdū Jīnglüè Lǐ Quélǘ,
and the area west of Yìzhōu was entrusted to Quán Zhōngdū Xīlù Jīnglüè Jìng Ānmín to govern.
Wányán Héshang, who was remotely appointed as Jīn’ānjūn Jiédùshǐ, and the late Xíngjūn Fùtíkòng Jiágǔ Wúdiǎn, were both dismissed from their names.
On the day Gēngzǐ,
Imperial Prince Púwáng Shǒuchún, who was Píngzhāng Zhèngshì, was advanced to the title of Yīngwáng.
On the day Rén'yín,
the rebel Wáng Gōngxǐ conspired with the Sòng people to take Yízhōu.
On the day Jiǎchén,
due to the death of the Princess of Yíguó,
the court was suspended.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
blank imperial edicts and gold and silver tallies were issued
to Lánzhōu commander Gǔlǐ Jiǎshílún,
to recruit those who were coerced [into rebellion].
On the day Dīngwèi,
the Jūnmìyuàn was instructed to discuss strategies for garrisoning Jìn'ān, Dōngpíng, and Hézhōng commanderies.
On the day Gēngxū,
Xíngshěng Zuǒ Fùyuánshuài Púsǎn Ānzhēn arrived from the front,
and was granted an audience in the Rén'āndiàn.
On the day Xīnhài,
Shǎofǔ Shǎojiān Niángē Suōshī spoke about seven matters of advantage and disadvantage.
On the day Jiǎyín,
as the southern expeditionary army returned,
the conscription of civilians into the army in the southern border prefectures and commanderies was abolished.
On the day Wùwǔ,
the Xià people captured Tōngqínzhài in Jiāzhōu,
On the day Rénxū,
Zhīshū Shìyùshǐ Púlǔhǔ submitted a memorial
requesting the selection of tutors for the Crown Prince.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
Xū Dǐng and others were all promoted,
rewarding them for their merits in the southern campaign.
In summer, the fourth month, on the day Bǐngyín, which was the first day of the month,
Marshal's Offices were established in Yù and Sù prefectures.
Six thousand elite infantry and cavalry from Shǎnxī were selected to garrison Jīngzhào.
On the day Wùchén,
sixty thousand elite troops were selected and divided to garrison Píngliáng, Jīng, Bīn, Gān, and Yào prefectures.
On the day Gēngwǔ,
Nǚxīliè Gǔlǐjiān, the Defense Commissioner of Qínzhōu, was appointed acting Marshal of the Marshal's Office in Píngliáng.
The recruitment of civilians to transport salt was abolished.
The Jiūchéng (Forbidden City) in the capital was constructed.
Hóu Zhì was ordered to oversee the work,
and Gāo Qí was made the overall supervisor.
On the day Jiǎxū,
Shízhǎn Héxǐ, who was in charge of Línfú Prefecture, was appointed Left Supervisor-General of the Marshal,
and was to act as Marshal in Gǒngzhōu.
On the day Rénwǔ,
four imperial attendants were dispatched to inspect the laborers building the city walls,
to ensure they were fed on time,
to allow them proper rest,
and to strictly prohibit cruel supervision by officials.
On the day Guǐwèi,
a black wind rose in Shǎnxī during the day,
with a sound like thunder,
and a great earthquake occurred.
On the day Jiǎshēn,
an imperial edict stipulated that officials in the prefectures and counties of Héběi should only be appointed from local residents who were well-regarded by the people,
while those already appointed by the court would have their assignments reconsidered.
On the day Yǐyǒu,
the Xià people occupied Tōngqínzhài,
but they were defeated by Tíkòng Nàhé Mǎizhù.
On the day Jǐchǒu,
Huò Chéng, the Area Commander of Línzhōu, was accused of disloyalty and unjustly killed a surrendered man.
He was judged to deserve death,
but Marshal Wéiliáng did not wish to execute a frontier general for killing an enemy,
and requested leniency for his punishment.
He also requested the establishment of a reward system for escorting surrendered civilians
to prevent future troubles.
The Emperor pardoned Chéng on this account,
and ordered the relevant department to issue the reward scale: those who escorted ten or more people would be promoted one rank;
those who escorted fewer would receive two hundred *mín* of cash per person;
for fifty or more people, two ranks;
for one hundred or more people, two ranks and appointment to various miscellaneous posts.
On the day Gēngyín,
due to the summer heat,
an imperial edict allowed court officials to report affairs only once every four days.
Gāo Rǔlì requested that provisions for autumn defense be prepared,
and that, taking advantage of a good harvest, a system be established in the prefectures and commanderies of Hénán to purchase grain at a set price
by recruiting civilians to supply it.
The Emperor discussed and finalized the method with him and implemented it.
Wáng Sānxī, Associate Supervisor-General of the Salt and Tea Monopoly Bureau, requested a monopoly on oil,
which could generate tens of thousands of *liǎng* of silver annually.
Gāo Qí was put in charge,
but the general opinion was that it was inconvenient,
so it was stopped.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
the Xià people attacked Tōngqínzhài.
Marshal Wányán Hédá led troops from Ānsāibǎo to strike their base.
Upon reaching Lóngzhōu,
the Xià people met them in battle.
The government forces attacked them,
and their multitude scattered.
They advanced and pressed upon the city,
and shortly captured its southwest corner.
As night fell,
they returned.
On the day Rénchén,
Hú Tiānzuò, Associate Administrator of Píngyáng Prefecture, was appointed Commissioner for Expedient Pacification.
In the fifth month, on the day Yǐwèi, which was the first day of the month,
the Fèngxiáng Marshal's Office dispatched troops and defeated the Sòng people at Huángniú and other forts.
On the day Rénzǐ,
Venus was seen in broad daylight near Cān (Orion).
In the sixth month, on the day Jiǎzǐ, which was the first day of the month,
due to the summer heat,
medicine was given to sick laborers repairing the city walls.
An edict was sent to Marshal Hédá, saying:
"Because of your capability,
you were entrusted with the responsibilities in Táng and Dèng.
If there are any incursions,
it is not advisable to pursue far after a battle;
merely secure our borders."
Shízhǎn Nǚlǔhuān, General of Agile Cavalry and Area Commander of Hénán Circuit, was appointed Right Supervisor-General of the Marshal,
and was to act as Marshal of Píngliáng.
An imperial edict granted golden and silver tallies and blank imperial decrees to the Regional Branch Secretariat in Liáodōng and other places,
On the day Rénshēn,
a decree stipulated that the punishment for desertion by river patrol soldiers would be the same as for regular campaigning soldiers.
An imperial edict ordered Wányán Bójiā, Censor-in-Chief, to establish a Branch Bureau of the Bureau of Military Affairs in Xǔzhōu.
On the day Jiǎxū,
the penalties for playing *qiújū* and feasting by generals and officers for autumn defense were set.
Lǐ Quán plundered Rìzhào and Bóxīng;
Gēshíliè Wànnú defeated him.
He attacked Jìmò;
Wányán Sēngshòu again defeated him,
and recovered Láizhōu.
On the day Wùyín,
an imperial edict ordered conscripted soldiers in Shǎnxī to follow the Hénán precedent,
and granted partial amnesties in the Hédōng Southern and Northern circuits.
On the day Dīnghài,
Defense Commissioner Túdān Fúdìng and others were ordered to lead their loyalist militias,
and all old and young people from Yízhōu were relocated to Pī.
On the day Wùzǐ,
Tángkuò Gǒu'ér, General Commander and Tíkòng of Liáozhōu, led troops to retake Tàiyuán Prefecture.
There was an earthquake in Píngliáng and other places,
and an imperial edict ordered Guō Zhù, Right Policy Advisor, to reassure the military and civilians there.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the day Dīngyǒu,
loyalist militias from Pī, Hǎi and other prefectures, as well as those coerced into joining and now returned to the state and conscripted, were registered.
Each person was granted thirty *mǔ* of land,
and those capable, fifty *mǔ*.
Their taxes and levies were exempted,
and they received two *shēng* of grain daily.
They were called
"Decisive Victory Army."
On the day Wùxū,
the Emperor summoned the officials of the Bureau of Military Affairs and instructed them, saying:
"The Jiūchéng has long remained unfinished.
The Department of State Affairs wishes to mobilize more civilians,
but I fear it will hinder farming.
Moreover, if grain storage is insufficient,
what will we do?
Why not reconsider the plan?"
The officials of the Bureau of Military Affairs replied:
"The initiation of this project
was indeed a major undertaking.
Now more than half the work is done,
and it merely coincided with continuous heavy rains,
causing a delay in completion.
The Department of State Affairs' proposal to increase laborers
will necessarily involve checking household registrations, ensuring it does not hinder their livelihood.
By the time of the autumn defense,
it should be completed."
The Emperor said:
"You all must plan well,
so as not to cause me worry."
On the day Gēngzǐ,
due to the earthquake,
a partial amnesty was granted in Shǎnxī Circuit.
On the day Jiǎchén,
three Branch Bureaus of the Court of Judicial Review were established in the Jīngdōng, Jīngxī, and Jīngnán circuits.
a partial amnesty was granted in the Shāndōng Xī Circuit.
On the day Dīngsì,
Túdān Sīzhōng was dispatched to make sacrifices to the Earth Deities at the Shàngqīng Palace due to the earthquake.
In the eighth month, on the day Bǐngyín,
Xǔ Gǔ, Remonstrance Official, and others were stripped of their ranks and dismissed.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
Jupiter encroached upon the southeastern stars of Yúguǐ (Praesepe).
On the day Wùchén,
Yáng Yúnyì, Minister of Rites, was dispatched to sacrifice to the Gods of Earth and Grain,
and Zhào Bǐngwén, Academician and Attendant Reader of the Hanlin Academy, was dispatched to sacrifice to the Empress of the Earth at Hézhōng Prefecture.
Lǐ Fùhēng of the Jīngxī Branch Bureau of the Court of Judicial Review spoke of the profits from iron smelting in Rǔ and Dèng,
and from salt in Hénán and the North.
and disappeared after one hundred and nine days.
On the day Rénshēn,
the Emperor decreed to the Censorate officials:
"I issue instructions to the Department of State Affairs,
but sometimes they are not implemented for several days,
and when I inquire again, I receive artfully embellished chronological replies.
High officials may be forgetful,
but the Left and Right Bureaus are negligent.
Censorate officials should impeach them.
If this happens again in the future,
all of you will be punished together."
Thereupon, it was stipulated that Censorate officials would inspect imperial decrees and documents in the Secretariat every half-month.
Great Yuán troops captured Wǔzhōu;
Guō Xiù, Military Judicial Officer, died there.
On the day Dīngchǒu,
corvée labor in the capital was suspended.
Wáng Shàn, Administrator of Zhōngshān, killed Lǐ Zhòng, acting Prefect, and others in rebellion.
Great Yuán troops captured Héhé County;
Qiao Tiānyì, county magistrate, and others died there.
On the day Yǐyǒu,
the Bureau of Military Affairs was ordered to dispatch officials to select strong and robust soldiers from the armies beyond the passes,
and station them in the cities of Zhāngdé, Xíng, Míng, Wèi, Jùn, Huái, Mèng, and other places,
while the weak ones were to be dismissed.
On the day Wùzǐ,
the Emperor decreed to Hóu Zhì to instruct the officials of the Branch Bureaus of the Court of Judicial Review to encourage the people to plant wheat,
and to lend grain to those who had none to sow.
In the ninth month, on the *jiǎwǔ* day,
an edict was issued for Wányán Zhòngyuán (完顏仲元), Commissioner of Military Affairs for Shānzhōu, to garrison Sùzhōu,
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
Jiágǔ Tiānchéng (夾谷天成), Pacification Commissioner of Tángzhōu, defeated the Sòng people at Tóngbǎi.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
the Department of State Affairs requested to re-order Hóu Zhì (侯摯) to extensively manage grain storage.
The emperor did not permit it,
saying:
"Taxation and levies are already plentiful.
To plan further now
would merely be taking from the people again.
The autumn defense is somewhat relaxed;
we should appropriately reduce the garrison troops,
and expenditures are fortunately sufficient.
Why resort to this?"
and to act concurrently as the Marshal’s Residence Administrator with Hésīliè Dé (紇石烈德), Right Deputy Supervising Marshal.
Dà Yuán (大元) soldiers swept through Dōngshèngzhōu,
and the Military Commissioner Bódé Wāgē (伯德窊哥) died there.
On the *gēngxū* day,
Xū Dǐng (胥鼎), Acting Provincial Governor, was ordered to lead troops to Hézhōng.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
Wǔ Xiān (武仙), Pacification Commissioner of Zhēndìng, requested gold and silver talismans to reward the meritorious,
which was granted.
Warships were built along the river
and handed over to the Acting Provincial Marshal’s Residence.
In the winter, on the first day (*guǐhài*) of the tenth month,
regulations were established for the promotion and demotion of recommenders based on the capability of the county magistrates they recommended.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
based on the words of Ménggǔ Gāng (蒙古綱),
volunteer armies were recruited, and officials such as Chief Commanders and Deputy Commanders were appointed for each,
following the system of Zhēnyòu (貞祐) three years.
Píngliáng Fǔ had previously been ordered to hold a ritual of supplication due to an earthquake.
As the ceremony was being performed,
auspicious clouds appeared,
and a drawing of them was submitted.
Officials were dispatched to verify the truth,
and on that day,
all officials submitted memorials to offer congratulations.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
Wányán Kāi (完顏開) was appointed acting Left Deputy Supervising Marshal,
and Guō Wénzhèn (郭文振) acting Right Deputy Supervising Marshal,
both concurrently managing affairs of the Marshal’s Residence,
planning to recover Tàiyuán.
On the *rénshēn* day,
it was decreed that silver would be the standard for calculating punishment for corrupt officials.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
an official was dispatched to report the auspicious clouds to the Tàimiào.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
an edict regarding the auspicious clouds was issued throughout the country.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
Dà Yuán (大元) troops reached the border of Shānzhōu.
An edict was issued that for people in various circuits who should evacuate from the troops but were unwilling,
messengers should be immediately sent to explain the advantages and disadvantages to them.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
the city walls were completed,
and all officials offered congratulations.
A banquet was held for the Prime Ministers in the side hall.
The Right Chancellor, Zhì (摯), was promoted one rank,
and the Right Prime Minister, Qí (琪), Left Chancellor, Rǔlì (汝礪), and Participant in Political Affairs, Sīzhōng (思忠), were each granted one gold tripod
and three heavy bolts of silk.
During this project,
the emperor, concerned about disturbing the people,
recruited people, promising promotion by one rank for those who could provide 500,000 bricks,
and an additional rank for 1,000,000.
Wányán Ālà (完顏阿剌), Associate Judge of Píngyáng, and Huò Dìnghé (霍定和), Censor of the Left Wing, uncovered the former residence of Sòng Cài Jīng (蔡京),
acquiring over 2,000,000 (bricks),
and were rewarded according to the regulations for promotion.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
the Prime Ministers requested to erect a stele at the Huìcháo Gate commemorating the achievement of building the city walls,
which was granted.
On the *dīnghài* day,
Dà Yuán (大元) troops were garrisoned at Miánshàng.
On the *rénchén* day,
officials were ordered to repair vacant houses,
provide firewood and rice,
to aid the poor,
to cease in the second month of the following year,
and to make it a regular practice to provide for them once peace was restored.
In the eleventh month, on the first day (*guǐsì*),
Zhāng Yòu (張祐), former Granary Administrator of Lánzhōu, returned from the Xià Kingdom.
Pú Sàn'ānzhēn (僕散安貞), Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and É Kěxíng (訛可行), Concurrent Signatory of the Bureau, were appointed to oversee military affairs in Héběi.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
official donkeys were loaned to court officials who had no horses to ride,
and fodder was also provided.
On the *jǐhài* day,
Dà Yuán (大元) troops swept through Zhāngdé Fǔ.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
an edict was issued for court officials of the seventh rank and above, and outside officials of the sixth rank and above,
to recommend one county magistrate every two years.
Sū Táng (蘇唐), a clerk in the Ministry of Revenue, pressed for rent payment in Fēngqiū,
with such urgency that
some people harvested unripe grain to pay their rent.
The emperor, hearing of this,
dispatched an official to investigate,
caned Táng (唐) fifty times,
and demoted County Magistrate Gāo Xīlóng (高希隆) by two ranks.
The Department of State Affairs considered Xīlóng’s (希隆) punishment too light,
but the emperor said:
"When an imperial envoy goes to an outer circuit,
who but the most steadfast could refuse to comply?
Let it be according to the previous edict."
On the *jiǎyín* day,
Nàhé Liùgē (納合六哥), General Administrator of Xúzhōu, greatly defeated the Red Jacket bandits at Díshān.
Mònián Húlǔlà (抹撚胡魯剌), a supervising secretary in the Ministry of Rites, submitted a memorial concerning current affairs.
On the *dīngsì* day,
Gāo Qí (高琪), Right Chancellor, was imprisoned.
Zhāng Tiānyì (張天翼), Deputy Commissioner of Tài'ān Commandery, had been captured by the bandit Zhāng Lín (張林) and taken back to Sòng,
where he was held in Chǔzhōu.
He escaped and returned at this time,
and was appointed Prefect of Suīzhōu,
promoted two ranks,
and advanced one grade in office.
On the *wǔwǔ* day,
Dà Yuán (大元) troops pacified Jìn'ān Fǔ,
and Niángē Zhēn (粘割貞), Acting Marshal’s Residence Administrator and Minister of Works, died there.
In the twelfth month,
Gāo Qí (高琪) was executed.
Collation Notes
Basic Annals 16, Xiānzōng (宣宗) Part 2
In the fourth year, spring, on the first day (*rénchén*) of the first month,
an edict was issued to exempt from court attendance.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
Gǔlǐjiǎ Shílún (古里甲石倫), Military Commissioner of Jīn'ān Commandery and Acting Marshal’s Residence Administrator, was stripped of his name.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
Dà Yuán (大元) troops captured Hǎoyì Bǎo,
and Yílā Ālǐhé (移剌阿里合), Prefect of Huòzhōu, and others died there.
An edict was issued to posthumously confer differing official titles.
On the *gēngxū* day,
over one hundred thousand Sòng infantry and cavalry besieged Dèngzhōu.
Hearing of the arrival of reinforcements,
they burned their camps and departed at night.
Shúhǔ Yílá Dá (术虎移剌荅), Deputy Pacification Commissioner, pursued and overtook them,
recovering their captives.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
the sky was dark during the day,
followed shortly by great thunder and lightning,
and rain with wind.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
Zhāng Shīlǔ (張師魯), Assistant Minister of Revenue, submitted a memorial,
requesting to dispatch several thousand cavalry,
and by spring,
advance simultaneously on Huái (淮) and Shǔ (蜀),
to harass Sòng.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
Wǔ Xiān (武仙) was remotely appointed Commander of Zhōngjīng,
and promoted one rank.
In the third month, on the *xīnchǒu* day,
there was a discussion to relocate Suīzhōu.
Pú Lǔhǔ (蒲魯虎), Censor of the Imperial Household, was dispatched by edict to inspect the city walls in Jīngdōng,
and upon his return, reported that it was better not to relocate,
so the plan was halted.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
on the Chángchūn Festival,
an edict was issued to exempt from court attendance.
On the *yǐsì* day,
Wéiliáng (惟良), Marshal of Línzhōu, captured the rebels Shàn Zhòng (單仲) and Lǐ Jùn (李俊),
and executed them,
accepting the surrender of their associate Lú Guǎng (盧廣).
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
Lǐ Fùhēng (李復亨), Minister of Personnel, was appointed Participant in Political Affairs,
and Shújiǎ Sàiyě (术甲賽也), Commander of the Southern Capital Military Corps, was appointed to oversee military affairs in Huái (懷) and Mèng (孟).
On the *xīnhài* day,
Gāo Rǔlì (高汝礪), Grand Councillor, was promoted to Right Prime Minister of the Department of State Affairs,
appointed Supervisor of National History,
and enfeoffed as Duke of Shòu.
Lǐ Fùhēng (李復亨), Participant in Political Affairs, concurrently served as Compiler of National History.
Xū Dǐng (胥鼎), Grand Councillor and Acting Provincial Governor of Shǎnxī, was promoted and enfeoffed as Duke of Wēn,
and retired from office.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
Yú Máng’ér (于忙兒), a Red Jacket bandit, launched a surprise attack and occupied Hǎizhōu.
Wányán Chén’ér (完顏陳兒), Commissioner of Military Affairs, led troops to defeat Máng’ér (忙兒),
and recaptured the city.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
Jupiter encroached upon the 'Pile of Corpses' asterism in the Ghost宿 mansion.
In the summer, on the first day (*gēngshēn*) of the fourth month,
an edict was issued for Wányán Bójiā (完顏伯嘉), Censor-in-Chief, to take charge of city defense matters.
On the *guǐhài* day,
Chái Mào (柴茂), Military Commissioner of Ānwǔ Commandery, defeated the Red Jacket bandits at Zǎojiàng.
Duàn Zēngshùn (段增順), Commissioner of Military Affairs for Qízhōu, defeated the rebel Zhēn Quán (甄全) at Tángxiàn.
Xià people encroached upon the border,
and Marshal Shízhǎn Héxǐ (石盞合喜) defeated them.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
Zhāngdé, Wèi, Huī, Huá, and Jùn Prefectures were placed under the Hénán Circuit Transport Commission.
The Hénán Circuit Transport Commission was made the Metropolitan Transport Commission,
on par with the Central Capital,
and additional officials were appointed.
On the *wùchén* day,
the *dì* sacrifice was performed at the Tàimiào.
Dà Yuán (大元) dispatched Zhào Ruì (趙瑞) with troops to attack Mèngzhōu.
Tíkòng Lǔ Dé (提控魯德) and Wáng Ān (王安) recovered Dàmíng Fǔ.
Bǎ Húlǔ (把胡魯), Participant in Political Affairs, was appointed acting Right Chancellor and Left Deputy Marshal,
and Chénglì (承立), Left Deputy Supervising Marshal, was appointed Right Supervising General and acting Participant in Political Affairs,
both concurrently managing the Department of State Affairs and Marshal’s Residence in Jīngzhào.
On the *gēngchén* day,
Púchá Shān'ér (蒲察山兒), General Administrator and Tíkòng of the Dōngpíng Marshal’s Residence, defeated the Red Jacket bandits at Liáochéng.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
the Six Ministries were ordered to examine legal cases and directly present the case documents to the departmental officials,
allowing them to deliberate in person,
and the Dali Temple was to do the same.
In the fifth month, on the day Rénchén,
regulations were established for promoting officials from the second to third ranks based on meritorious service.
On Guǐsì,
the Hóng'ǎo bandits raided Lèlíng and Yánshān.
Wáng Fú, Jìedùshǐ of the Hénghǎi Army, defeated them.
Zhāng Jù came to raid,
and was again defeated.
On Jiǎwǔ,
the Emperor played polo at the Línwǔ Diàn.
On Bǐngshēn,
due to the summer heat,
the regular morning court was suspended,
and memorials were presented once every four days.
On Dīngyǒu,
an edict was issued to the Ministry of Works to halt all labor projects during the summer month.
On Guǐmǎo,
the Great Yuán army advanced into Àizhōu.
On Bǐngchén,
the Great Yuán army advanced into Yǎnzhōu.
Wūyán Wèikě, Jìedùshǐ of the Tàidìng Army, died defending it.
In the sixth month, on Bǐngyín,
messengers were sent to recruit Zhāng Ròu.
On Dīngmǎo,
an imperial edict reduced the number of Cénchá Yùshǐ by four.
On Wùchén,
five hundred able-bodied men were recruited from among the migrant populace of Shāndōng,
and added to the Yànníng Army of Duke Dōngjǔ.
The moon encroached upon Saturn.
On Jǐsì,
Venus was seen in broad daylight in Zhāng (a lunar mansion),
and remained visible for one hundred and eighty-four days before setting.
On Jiǎxū,
a decree was issued that the patrol and guard troops of all granaries, fields, storehouses, and offices
should be overseen by the Tíjué Cāngcháng Sī and the Jiān Zhīnà Guān.
As there was no rain in the Jīngjī,
an imperial order instructed the relevant officials to review prisons,
and all offenders, from those condemned to death downwards, were released.
On Dīngchǒu,
the Great Yuán dispatched Yáng Zài to attack and capture Dàmíng,
and also attacked Kāizhōu, Dōngmíng, and Chángyuán counties.
On Jǐmǎo,
prayers for rain were offered.
On Gēngchén,
Fāng Zǐxīn from the Sòng realm came to surrender.
The relevant officials settled him in Zhèngzhōu.
The Emperor said:
"Our people who fled to Sòng
were always provided with food and clothing by them.
If those who come to us
are not treated well,
they might flee back again,
and leak confidential information."
He ordered an increase in Zǐxīn's provisions,
and the officials were commanded to treat him favorably.
Yuánshuài Yòu Jiānjūn, acting Cānzhī Zhèngshì Chéng Lì, submitted a sealed memorial.
In autumn, the seventh month, on Xīnmǎo,
the Sòng people and Hóng'ǎo bandits invaded Héshuò.
All the commanderies surrendered,
except Cāngzhōu, where Jīnglüèshǐ Wáng Fú held firm.
At that time, the Yìdū bandit Zhāng Lín came to attack,
so Fú rebelled and surrendered to Lín.
The Marshal's office requested permission to punish him.
On this day,
it rained.
On Guǐchǒu,
the Línzhōu Xíng Yuánshuài Fǔ dispatched Zǒnglǐng Yán Lù and others to suppress the Hóng'ǎo bandits in Zhāngdé Fǔ,
and captured the pseudo-Ānfǔshǐ Wáng Jiǔ alive.
An edict appointed Cānzhī Zhèngshì Lǐ Fùhēng as Xuānwèishǐ,
with Yùshǐ Zhōngchéng Wányán Bójiā as his deputy,
to tour the commanderies and counties to encourage agriculture.
Wūgǔlún Zhòngduān and others were sent as envoys to the Great Yuán.
In the eighth month, on Wùwǔ, the first day of the month,
Yán Shí, Chéng Jiāng, and Wáng Yūn occupied Jǐnán.
Gāo Jūshí, Shāndōng Zhāofǔ, sent a messenger to recruit Yán Shí at Qīngyázhài,
and reported his favorable response.
Lǐ Quán attacked Dōngpíng Fǔ.
Jiānjūn Wáng Tíngyù defeated him,
and captured his pseudo-Ānhuà Jūn Jiéduóshǐ Zhāng Lín.
On Gēngshēn,
Gāoyáng Gōng Zhāng Fǔ requested to increase troops to defend Jìzhōu.
The Emperor instructed the Shūmì,
stating that there were ten villages of Yǐngzhōu people who had crossed the Huái River to become Sòng soldiers,
and ordered that their leaders be apprehended,
and one or two punished to warn the rest.
On Gēngwǔ,
an imperial order forbade military officials from nominating county magistrates.
The Xià people captured Huìzhōu,
and Cìshǐ Wūgǔlún Shìxiǎn surrendered.
On Jiǎxū,
the Shǎnxī Xíngshěng reported a victory over the Xià people at Kāgǔ.
On Yǐhài,
the Emperor instructed the Zǎichén [ministers],
stating that Hénán was experiencing floods,
especially severe in Táng and Dèng.
For the affected prefectures and counties,
their taxes had already been remitted.
For the remaining areas that were able to achieve a normal harvest,
only the regular tribute was to be collected,
while héliáo (forced grain purchases) and miscellaneous levies were all to be waived.
Furthermore, starting from the ninth month of this year,
the annual payment in mulberry bark and old paper was to be suspended.
Refugees who cultivated wasteland would receive the same generous exemptions as above.
On Bǐngzǐ,
the Shǎnxī Xíngshěng negotiated peace with the Xià people.
On Wùyín,
the method for selecting and appointing imperial guards was established.
On Jǐmǎo,
the Jiāzhōu Zhāofǔ Sī was abolished.
On Rénwǔ,
Chéng Yì of the Shǎnxī Lù Xíngshěng reported a victory at Dìngxīzhōu.
On Bǐngxū,
troops from various roads were relocated to Hénán, Jīngdōng, Jīngxī, and Jīngnán routes,
each establishing an Inspector and Deputy Inspector.
Shān Gōng Wǔ Xiān surrendered to the Great Yuán.
In the ninth month, on Wùzǐ,
an imperial edict was issued to send officials to Hénán and Shǎnxī to select imperial guards.
On Xīnmǎo,
the Zhāngzōng Shílù (Veritable Records of Emperor Zhāngzōng) was presented.
On Wùxū,
Mùhuálǐ of the Great Yuán stationed troops in Zhēndìng.
A Zǒnglǐng Yuánshuài Fǔ was established in Guīdé,
with the troops from Shòuzhōu and Chénliú Garrisons assigned to it.
On Gēngzǐ,
the Xià people entered Dìngxīzhōu.
On Rénchén,
the Sòng people garrisoned Zàojiāo Bǎo.
Xíngjūn Tíkòng Wányán Yìdū defeated them.
The Great Yuán sent Tǎhū and others.
On Guǐmǎo,
the Xià people came to invade.
On Jiǎchén,
Tiéngzhōu Zhāopǔ Tíkòng Xià Yìyǒng attacked the Hóng'ǎo bandits
and defeated them.
On Yǐsì,
an edict appointed Cānzhī Zhèngshì Lǐ Fùhēng to take charge of fodder and grain supplies.
On Jǐyǒu,
the Xià people captured Xīníngzhōu.
Púsǎn Núshībù, Dūshì of the Shàngshū Shěng, was executed for his responsibility.
Fùmǎ Dūwèi Túdān Shòuchūn was demoted one rank
and received sixty blows with the rod.
On Guǐchǒu,
the punishments for deserting soldiers from garrisons and the rewards for capturing them were revised.
On Jiǎyín,
the Sòng people marched out of Qínzhōu,
and the Xià people also came to invade.
On Bǐngchén,
Shízhǎn Héxǐ of the Gǒngzhōu Xíng Yuánshuài Fǔ reported a victory at Dìngxīzhōu.
In winter, the tenth month, on Rénxū,
the Great Yuán sent Měnggǔ Tǎhū, Érǐlà, and others.
On Jǐmǎo,
the Shǎnxī Dōnglù Xíngshěng reported a victory at Suídézhōu.
The Sìzhōu Yuánshuài Fǔ reported
that the Hóng'ǎo bandits had raided four times in one month,
plundering people and livestock before leaving.
On Gēngchén,
the Emperor played polo at the Línwǔ Diàn.
On Xīnsì,
the Hóng'ǎo bandit Shí Qīng was appointed Tiéngyáng Gōng, Zǒnglǐng of local military forces, and Yuánshuài兼Xuānfǔ.
On Guǐwèi,
each mountain stronghold in Jīngxī was assigned a Shǒuyùshǐ and Deputy,
with the Marshal's office of that route overseeing them.
An edict instructed the Shǎnxī Xíngshěng to plan the recovery of Huìzhōu.
The Emperor played polo at the Línwǔ Diàn.
In the eleventh month, on Dīnghài, the first day of the month,
Yuè Wáng Yǒnggōng was exempted from morning court on the first and fifteenth days of the lunar month.
Jìng Ānmín, Duke Yìshuǐ, was murdered by his subordinates.
On Wùzǐ,
Wūgǔlún Shíhǔ and others, Jīnglüèshǐ of Huánglíng Gāng, were executed
for failing in battle.
On Rénchén,
Jupiter was seen in broad daylight in Yì (a lunar mansion),
and set after sixty-seven days.
At night, it again encroached upon the first star north of Língtái.
On Jiǎwǔ,
there were floods in Hénán,
and officials were sent to encourage cultivation.
Fúshān County was renamed Zhōngxiào.
On Wùxū,
an edict restored Wèi Shàowáng's princely title,
and additionally granted him the honorific title of Kāifǔ Yítóng Sānsī.
On Rén'yín,
military households from Shāndōng Dōnglù were relocated to Xǔzhōu.
The Xíng Dōngpíng Zǒngguǎnfǔ was ordered to administer them,
with one Pànguān separately stationed in Línyǐng.
On Yǐsì,
an edict appointed Chái Mào as acting Yuánshuài Zuǒ Dūjiān,
and Gài Rénkuì as acting Yòu Dūjiān,
to jointly lead the Xíng Yuánshuài Fǔ in Zhēndìng.
In this month,
Mùhuálǐ, King of the Great Yuán, besieged Dōngpíng with his army.
On the *jiǎxū* day of the twelfth month,
prayers were offered for snow.
Mòniǎn Húlǔlà, an Assistant Minister of the Board of Rites concurrently serving as Left Remonstrance Official, submitted a memorial.
On the *wùyín* day,
an edict was issued allowing military officers to play polo three times a month
to practice martial skills.
On the *gēngchén* day,
the Làyì Festival was observed,
with sacrifices offered at the Tàimiào.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
Wēndíhán Sījìng, the Jìedùshǐ of Zhènnán Commandery, submitted a letter discussing currency and taxation.
In the first month of the fifth year, on the *bǐngxū* day, the first day of the month,
court was suspended.
On the *dīnghài* day,
the anniversary of Shìzōng's death,
offerings were made at Qǐqìnggōng Palace.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
arrearage households in Nánjīng and its various prefectures, who had previously cultivated government land, were registered,
and the land was allocated to military households.
On the *rénchén* day,
discussions were held regarding defending against Xīxià and the southern expedition.
The Crown Prince was instructed on the strategy for defending against enemies in Dōngpíng.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
the Privy Council was instructed that
the southern campaign was a weighty matter
and required detailed deliberation for its convenience.
An account of the deeds of the late Wèi Wáng was compiled,
following the precedent of Hǎilíng Shùrén.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
Dàyuán troops attacked Tiānjǐngguān.
On the *wùxū* day,
Sòng forces raided the west wall of Sìzhōu,
and Tíkòng Wáng Lù died there.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
Tàibái (Venus) was seen in daylight in the constellation Niú,
having been hidden for 232 days.
On the *yǐsì* day,
an edict was issued for troops from various circuits to gather at Càizhōu.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
the campaign against Sòng began.
On the *gēngxū* day,
the Shāndōng Xíngshěng reported a victory at Dōngpíng.
On the *bǐngchén* day, the first day of the second month,
a Zhāofǔsī was established in Shànzhōu.
A partial amnesty was granted to Dōngpíng Fǔ.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
an edict was issued for the campaign against Sòng.
Wéibì, a member of the imperial clan, was provisionally appointed as Co-Signatory of the Privy Council,
and the Xíngyuàn was established in Zhōngjīng;
Wòlèhédá was provisionally appointed as Right Vice Grand Marshal,
and the Xíngyuánshuàifǔ was established in Cài and Xī;
Nàhé Jiàngfú was provisionally appointed as Co-Signatory of the Privy Council,
and the Xíngyuàn was established in Sùzhōu;
Bóshùlǔ Dáā was provisionally appointed as Right Vice Grand Marshal,
Wányán Éluàn as Deputy Right Vice Grand Marshal,
and the Xíngyuánshuàifǔ was established in Táng and Dèng.
On the *wùchén* day,
the Huáizhōu Xíngyuánshuàifǔ was abolished,
and a Zhāofǔsī was re-established,
which, along with the Mèngzhōu Jīnglüèsī, was placed under the command of the Zhōngjīng Xíngshūmìyuàn.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
Púsàn Ānzhēn led troops out of Xīzhōu,
defeated Sòng forces at Jìngjūshānsì,
and captured Huángtǔguān.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
due to drought,
a partial amnesty was granted to Hénán Lù.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
weapons were prohibited in the capital city.
Marshal Hégěliè Yáwǔtà defeated Sòng troops
and recaptured Sìzhōu.
He advanced to Háo Zhōu,
reaching Guākǒu,
but returned to the west wall due to lack of provisions.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
due to drought,
an edict was issued to the court and the country.
On the *bǐngxū* day, the first day of the third month,
the Emperor proceeded to the Rénāndiàn Palace
to pray for rain,
and also offered a distant sacrifice in the northern suburbs.
On the *gēngyín* day,
Sòng forces besieged Táng and Dèng,
but Wányán Éluàn, acting as Xíngyuánshuàifǔshì, fought valiantly and repelled them.
Former Qiānhù of Dèngzhōu, Bóshùlǔ Máoliánghǔ, bravely broke through and returned to the country.
Éluàn expediently promoted him three ranks
and appointed him as Tóngzhī Tángzhōushì,
requesting formal confirmation to demonstrate trustworthiness,
which was granted.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
the Hénán Lù Xíngsānsī was abolished.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
Cānzhīzhèngshì Túshàn Sīzhōng was promoted to Shàngshū Yòuchéng and concurrently Supervisor of National History,
and Púsàn Yìfū, the Crown Prince's Junior Mentor, was appointed Cānzhīzhèngshì.
The Emperor instructed the chancellors, saying:
"Currently, many of the Fèngyù and Fèngzhí do not pay attention to gathering external information.
I heard that during Zhāngzōng's time, when close attendants completed their service,
their promotions or demotions were decided based on the information they collected.
Now, a method for examination and assessment should also be established in advance
to encourage them."
On the *wùxū* day,
the Chángchūnjié Festival was observed,
and court was suspended.
On the *jǐhài* day,
Xīxià, enticed by the rebel Dòu Zhào'ér,
occupied Láiqiāngchéng.
Bóshùlǔ Hézhù used heavy rewards to induce the coerced followers to act as an internal contingent,
urgently led troops to attack the city,
and captured it.
During the provincial examinations for classics scholars,
the examiners additionally passed more than ten people, including Qiáo Sōng, beyond the usual quota.
The authorities petitioned for their rejection,
but the Emperor had already approved it.
Soon after, he sent an envoy to instruct Sōng and others, saying:
"You were selected but then dismissed,
which cannot but affect your hearts.
Currently, there has been a long drought,
and I fear it may harm the harmonious atmosphere.
Therefore, I now grant you a special pardon."
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
Kāng Jū, an experience official of the Línzhōu Xíngyuánshuàifǔ, was granted the title of *Jìnshì Jídì*.
Jū had requested to take the palace examination as a military official,
hence this decree.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
due to drought, an altar was built to sacrifice to the masters of thunder and rain.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
it rained.
In the fourth month, on the *jǐwèi* day,
Měnggǔ Gāng of the Shāndōng Xíngshěng reported:
"Yàn Níng, Duke of Dōngjǔ, was defeated in battle and died.
Níng's stronghold, Tiānshèngzhài, was strategically located.
With Níng's death,
his followers had no one to turn to,
and change could occur at any moment.
Therefore, Sun Bāngzuǒ, who was provisionally serving as his Tíkòng, was appointed Zhāofǔshǐ,
and Huángguā Wùyě was appointed Zǒnglǐng,
to appease his followers."
An envoy was sent to request instructions,
and an imperial edict instructed the authorities to discuss it.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
prayers for rain were offered at the Tàimiào.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
Púsàn Ānzhēn defeated Sòng forces in Huáng and Qí prefectures.
On the *rénshēn* day,
over seventy male and female members of the Sòng imperial clan were captured and presented to the capital.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
an edict stated that those from the imperial army who had passed the military examinations and were awaiting appointment
should continue their former duties,
receive regular stipends,
and be dispatched when vacancies arose.
On the *xīnsì* day,
Liú Cóngyì, a Censor, was stripped of one rank
and dismissed
for improper impeachment.
An edict was issued to formalize the method for *Jìnshì* of the middle and lower grades, and officials from *Jiānguān* to *Míngwēi*, to be selected as county magistrates.
On the *jiǎshēn* day, the first day of the fifth month,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the *wùxū* day,
Sòng forces occupied Chǔqiū,
but government troops recaptured it.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
Nàlán Jìsēng was executed,
and Zhào Ruì, who reported him, was promoted four ranks.
On the *rényín* day,
Wányán Sàibù, Marshal of Shǎnxī, sent an envoy to report victories at Jìn'ān and Píngyáng.
While deliberating on his reward,
Censor Wūgǔlún Húlǔ impeached him for allowing his officers and soldiers to loot,
which did not align with the Emperor's intention to suppress disorder and save the people.
He requested that Sàibù's crime be formally punished.
The Emperor, considering Sàibù's merits,
decreed that he not be questioned,
and the discussion of rewards was also dropped.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
Éluàn, the commander of Tángzhōu, who was Marshal Sàibù's nephew,
fought Sòng forces on the border of Tángzhōu.
He was defeated by Sòng forces,
with over seven hundred casualties,
but concealed this and reported a victory.
Censor Nàlán exposed the matter.
The Emperor, for Sàibù's sake,
also did not punish Éluàn,
but conveyed this intention to him.
Then, praising Nàlán's courage in speaking out,
he recorded his merits and submitted them to the authorities,
for consideration as "most outstanding" when his term was complete.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
Dōngpíng was relocated internally.
Měnggǔ Gāng was ordered to establish the Xíngshěng in Pīzhōu,
and Wáng Tíngyù to establish the Shuàifǔ at Huánglínggāng.
In the sixth month, on the *jiǎyín* day, which was the first day of the month,
the Shàngshū Shěng (Department of State Affairs) presented a memorial regarding the rebellion of Fùmǎ Dūwèi Ānzhēn.
The Emperor reviewed the memorial, pondering its potential inaccuracy.
He said to Píngzhāng Zhèngshì (Grand Councilor) Yīng Wáng Shǒuchún:
"When the state executes a high official,
it must align with the public consensus of all under heaven and of future generations.
Let it be thoroughly re-examined."
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
an envoy was dispatched to inform Jìnyáng Gōng Guō Wénzhèn and Shàngdǎng Gōng Wányán Kāi to each guard their territories,
to unite in overcoming difficulties,
and not to initiate hostilities over minor matters,
thus harming the affairs of the state.
On the *wùyín* day,
Púsǎn Ānzhēn was executed for plotting rebellion,
and his three sons
were all put to death.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
Yuè Wáng Yǒnggōng passed away.
On the *gēngchén* day,
the court ceased its regular sessions.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
the Emperor personally offered sacrifices at the mourning hall.
In autumn, in the seventh month, on the *jǐhài* day,
the Yìyǒng Jūn (Brave and Loyal Army) rebelled,
occupying Dàngshān Xiàn.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
an imperial edict ordered an increase in clothing and rations for the garrison troops in Xúzhōu, Qīngkǒu, and other places.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
the Dàngshān rebels attacked Yǒngchéng Xiàn by night.
Xíngjūn Fù Zǒnglǐng (Deputy Commander of the Expeditionary Army) Gāo Wǎn defeated them.
Mènggǔ Gāng was ordered to join forces in the suppression.
On the *xīnhài* day,
Dānzhōu Zhāofǔ (Pacification Commissioner) Liú Qióng requested that grain from Hénán be transferred to supply his army.
An imperial edict granted this.
In the eighth month, on the *rénzǐ* day, which was the first day of the month,
the Huánglínggāng Zhāofǔ Sī (Huánglínggāng Pacification Office) was abolished.
The Emperor instructed the Shàngshū Shěng,
saying that the families of the Dàngshān rebels, imprisoned in Guīdé,
had not been given food for more than ten days,
and he feared for their lives.
The宰臣 (Grand Councilors) reported
that food had already been supplied.
He further instructed the Shūmìyuàn (Bureau of Military Affairs),
saying that Héběi was experiencing food shortages,
and the number of people wishing to come south was increasing daily.
They were to be swiftly allowed to cross,
lest they starve to death.
On the *guǐhài* day,
the marshals of Lín and Huái invited and attacked the Hóng'ǎo Zéi (Red Turban Bandits) at Fú'ēn Cūn,
and defeated them.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
an imperial edict stated that those who had returned from the southern campaign after their forces were routed, and were still capable of fighting,
should be rewarded according to the standard for achieving merit beyond the border.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
the Sòng people plundered Shěnqiū,
and killed the county magistrate.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
officials were ordered to remit outstanding rents owed by defaulting households,
and not to collect from current households.
In the ninth month, on the *jiǎshēn* day,
due to famine and numerous bandits in Jīngdōng,
Yùshǐ Dàfū (Grand Censor) Gēshíliè Húshīmén was dispatched as Xuānwèi Shǐ (Pacification Commissioner)
to soothe and pacify the region.
The method for penalizing violations by jiānchá Yùshǐ (Investigating Censors) was revised.
On the *dīnghài* day,
an imperial edict stated that if prefectures, counties, and military officers were slow in apprehending bandits,
those of fourth rank and below would be judged by the Xuānwèi Shǐ,
while those of third rank and above would have their cases submitted to the Emperor for decision.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
Xízhōu Zhāofǔ Shǐ (Pacification Commissioner of Xízhōu) Xuān Chéng was promoted in official rank,
and placed under the jurisdiction of Shǎnxī Shěng.
On the *yǐsì* day,
Chóngjìn, Fùmǎ Dūwèi Dìngguó Gōng Túshān Gōngbì passed away.
On the *gēngxū* day,
the planet Jupiter violated the left "law enforcer" (a star).
Yòuchéngxiàng (Right Grand Councilor) Gāo Rǔlì submitted a memorial requesting retirement,
but an imperial edict graciously retained him.
In winter, in the tenth month, on the *guǐchǒu* day,
Rǔlì was promoted to the official rank of Rónglù Dàfū (Grand Master for Splendid Happiness).
Púsǎn Yìfū was ordered to serve as acting Shàngshū Shěng in Jīngdōng,
supervising the fodder and rations for all armies.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
Grand Physicians Hóu Jì and Zhāng Ziyīng treated the Imperial Grandson's illness.
They used medicine that caused a severe reaction,
which the Imperial Grandson could not endure,
and thus the treatment was discontinued.
Their crime warranted death.
The Emperor said:
"While Jì and others' offense indeed merits death,
if it were the son of one of my uncles or brothers,
it should be handled according to the law.
However, to kill someone because of my grandson
is something I cannot bear."
He ordered them to be caned seventy times and dismissed from their posts.
The Shàngshū Shěng stated:
"If *sī* (judicial) and county officials are corrupt, tyrannical, and unlawful,
causing the people of their jurisdiction to flee,
there are already prescribed punishments.
If other counties harbor and conceal them,
they should also be punished.
Local people everywhere have long been burdened by corvée labor,
while transient households engaged in trade and hawking reap substantial profits.
Since the government collects nothing from them,
it is fitting to impose a slight levy on transient households as well,
to alleviate the burden on the local populace.
As for staff officers in the Xíngyuàn Shuàifǔ (Provisional Bureau of Military Affairs and Marshal's Office),
though they have no troops,
they do assist in planning military achievements.
Yet, their rewards for promotion are limited to a single rank.
It is advisable to allow their commanding generals to recommend them,
and reward them according to their merits."
The Emperor agreed to all their requests.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
the imperial guard was dispatched to suppress bandits in Hénán.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
Dà Yuán (Great Yuan) forces attacked Suídé Zhōu.
On the *rénxū* day,
the Xià (Western Xia) people again invaded Kānbì.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
an imperial order decreed that matters reported by censors
should not be known in advance by their colleagues,
establishing this as a regulation.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
the Xià people encroached upon the borders of Dìngxī and Jīshí.
On the *wùyín* day,
twelve thousand garrison soldiers from the Jīngjī (Capital Region)
and eight thousand militia from Hézhōng
were placed under the command of Xǔzhōu Yuánshuài (Marshal of Xǔzhōu) Gēshíliè Hèshòu,
to be stationed west of Tóngguān.
In the eleventh month, on the *guǐwèi* day,
the Shǎnxī Dōnglù Xíngshěng (Provisional Department of Shǎnxī Eastern Circuit) reported a victory over the Xià people at Ānsài Bǎo.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
the Tàifǔ (Ministry of the Treasury) was instructed to reduce food consumption.
On the *gēngyín* day,
people were recruited to cultivate irrigated rice fields in Nányáng.
On the *rénchén* day,
the Crown Prince, imperial princes, and all officials presented memorials congratulating the victory at Ānsài Bǎo,
but the Emperor declined their congratulations.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
the Xià people attacked Kānbì.
The Sòng people attacked Qí Xiàn.
The Hóng'ǎo Zéi plundered Sùzhōu.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
an imperial edict remitted outstanding rents in Xú, Pī, Sù, Sī, and other prefectures.
Officials and commoners who could reclaim and cultivate idle land
would be exempt from next year's levies.
In Guīdé, Bó, Shòu, and Yǐng, besides suspending the rents of defaulting households,
one-third of the remaining rent was also remitted.
The authorities were to recruit people to take over the fields and houses of defaulting households,
forbidding their destruction,
to await their eventual return.
Lǐ Wénxiù and other commoners from Púchéng Xiàn plotted rebellion
and were executed.
On the *rénchén* day,
the Sòng people burned Yǐngzhōu,
captured the Fángyù Pànguān (Deputy Defense Commissioner), and departed.
On this day,
Xiāngguó Sì caught fire.
Dà Yuán forces attacked Yán'ān.
In the twelfth month, on the *xīnhài* day, which was the first day of the month,
as Dà Yuán forces had descended upon Tóngguān and Jīngzhào,
an imperial edict ordered the *shěng* (departments) and *yuàn* (bureaus) to deliberate on this matter.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
the method of appointing county magistrates by selection and recommendation was abolished.
On the *dīngsì* day,
Lǐbù Shìláng (Vice Minister of Rites) Wūgǔsūn Zhòngduān
and Hànlín Dàizhì (Academician in Attendance) Ān Tíngzhēn returned from their mission to the north,
each being promoted one rank.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
the Hénán Yìjūn (Volunteer Army of Hénán) was disbanded.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
an imperial edict abolished the newly recruited civilian army,
reduced the number of military officials in the Shūmìyuàn and the garrison troops in the capital.
It further instructed the Xíngyuàn Shuàifǔ
not to arbitrarily increase recruitment or appointments.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
the Xíng Zǒngguǎnfǔ (Provisional Chief Military Command) and the Zhāotǎo Tǒngjūn Jiǎnchá Sī (Pacification and Expeditionary Army Inspection Bureaus) were abolished.
Regulations for rewarding Sòng people who surrendered and the law for punishing those who defrauded and enticed military personnel to desert were established.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
Marshal Hédá, Mǎizhù, and their officers and soldiers were specially rewarded for their achievements at Yán'ān,
and an imperial edict of commendation was also issued.
On *xīnsì* day in the intercalary month,
the troops of Dà Yuán attacked Fūzhōu.

Wányán Liùjīn, the Military Commissioner of Bǎodà Commandery; Hèshíliè Hèshòu, the acting Right Deputy Marshal; Púchá Lóushì, the Right Deputy Marshal; and Nǚxīliè Zīlù, the titular Military Commissioner of Jīn'ān Commandery, all died.
On *yǐyǒu* day,
commander Shùjiǎ Yǎozhù defeated the bandits of Shěnqiū at Chénwǎ.
On *bǐngxū* day,
an edict was issued to pacify and conciliate the local bandits in Hénán.
On *wùzǐ* day,
Mars encroached upon Xuānyuán.
On *jǐchǒu* day,
Sūn Yǔ and the bandit-catching officer Wúgǔchū persuaded two thousand bandits from Tàihé County to surrender.
An imperial edict ordered their ringleaders to be executed,
while the rest were released.
Guō Shù, the Co-Administrator of Bǎojìng Commandery, was executed
for failing to deliver grain on time
and falsely accusing and killing common people.
On *xīnmǎo* day,
the imperial army recovered Jiāzhōu.
On *guǐsì* day,
Bòshùlǔ Hézhù, the Military Commissioner of Tōngyuǎn Commandery, was stripped of his office.
On *jiǎwǔ* day,
the Moon encroached upon Mars.
On *bǐngshēn* day,
the Hóng'ǎo bandits entered Méngchéng County at night.
The county officials lost their seals and tallies,
and many soldiers and civilians died.
The bandits plundered extensively and then departed.
On *wùxū* day,
Saturn appeared in the sky during the day, in Zhěn.
On *jǐhài* day,
troops were dispatched to apprehend bandits in Jīngdōng.
Venus appeared in the sky during the day, in Shì.
On *rénrín* day,
grain from the Shànglín Directorate was distributed to aid the poor.
In Chénzhōu, Bózhōu, and other prefectures,
and Lùyì, Chéngfù, and other counties,
bandits rose up.
The Grand Council was urged to dispatch officials to suppress them.
An imperial censor was sent to investigate
the bandit-catching army's devastation of civilians wherever they passed.
The cattle seized by the army
were redeemed by the authorities with government funds.
On *wùshēn* day,
an edict set the reward regulations for recruiting and apprehending local bandits.
On *jǐyǒu* day,
the "Xīngdìng Bǎoquán"
currency was re-minted.
One string of it was worth
four hundred strings of "Tōngbǎo."
In the spring, first month of the first year of Yuánguāng, on *gēngxū* day,
no court audience was held.
On *xīnhài* day,
the anniversary of Shìzōng's death,
sacrifices were offered at Qǐqìng Palace.
Marshal Wéibì defeated the Hóng'ǎo bandits
at Zhāngqiān Diàn.
On *rénzǐ* day,
officials were dispatched to cultivate paddy fields in the three circuits of Jīngdōng, Jīngxī, and Jīngnán.
On *jiǎyín* day,
the use of post horses was prohibited for non-urgent border matters.
If anyone used them improperly, the prefectures and counties were to report directly to the Secretariat and Department of State Affairs.
In the four directions, the post stations were under the Censorate,
and in other circuits, they were managed by the circuit censors.
An edict ordered the traveling provincial administration of Shǎnxī Xīlù, which had moved to Jīngzhào,
to return and govern Píngliáng once the troops retreated.
Bǎyíshīlà, the Prefect of Fāngzhōu,
was executed
for abandoning the city.
Péimǎn Yánggē, the Defense Commissioner of Zhèngzhōu,
and Gǔlǐjiǎ Shílún, the Co-Administrator of the Defense Commission, were dismissed.
Bǎgǔ Yǎozhù, the Military Commissioner of Píngxī, was demoted by one rank.
On *dīngmǎo* day,
an edict was issued to pacify and conciliate the people of Jīngdōng.
In the second month, on *rénwǔ* day,

an edict ordered the garrison troops from Zhōngjīng, Tángzhōu, Dèngzhōu, Shāngzhōu, Guózhōu, Xǔzhōu, and Shǎnzhōu, as well as the families of all armies, to move to Jīngzhào, Tóngzhōu, and Huàzhōu for grain and settlement.
On *yǐyǒu* day,
the traveling provincial administration of Shǎnxī Xīlù requested to offer generous rewards to recruit the various tribal chieftains and Buddhist monks from Héxī,
with the aim of recovering Dàtōng City.
The traveling provincial administration and the Grand Council were ordered to devise a plan.
On *guǐsì* day,
the Emperor instructed the chief ministers:
"The Sòng people attacked Píngyú and Bāoxìn with heavy forces,
but our army fought valiantly and repelled them.
We also have detailed intelligence on the situation.
If we wait for the Marshal's office to submit their achievements for commendation and rewards,
how can it be as urgent as promptly encouraging and rewarding them?
Therefore, send reputable officials,
bearing blank imperial edicts,
to verify the facts and issue the rewards."
On *yǐwèi* day,
an edict was issued to Hénán and Shǎnxī.
Dà Yuán troops were stationed at Jiāzhōu.
On *rénrín* day,
the provisional provincial administration, Grand Council, and Marshal's office were authorized to punish officials of the Right and Left Bureaus and the Secretariat with caning.
On *jiǎchén* day,
the Emperor, mindful that Fūyán had suffered from warfare,
and Yán'ān had been besieged,
had previously issued civilian grain to the army.
An edict exempted Yán'ān, Fūzhōu, Fāngzhōu, Dānzhōu, Jiāzhōu, and Suídé from taxes and rents,
and further ordered the authorities to compensate them for the value of their grain.
Those who were still in need were allowed to take official positions.
On *wùshēn* day,
there was a military mutiny in Zhōujūn.
Hūyán Yù and over a thousand other *wànhù* plundered and killed in the city,
burned houses, and then departed.
On *jǐyǒu* day,
Wókě, the Left Supervisor of the Marshal's office, was dispatched to act as Marshal,
controlling the armies of the three circuits to attack Sòng.
Shí Quán, the Co-Administrator of the Bureau of Military Affairs, was to act as Administrator of the Bureau,
assisting him.
In the third month, on *xīnyǒu* day,
the Sòng people plundered Liúcūn in Quèshān County.
On *bǐngyín* day,
Jupiter encroached upon the Left Judge of Tàiwēi.
On *wùchén* day,
Jiǎ Tiān'ān, an official appointed by the Grand Council, submitted a memorial discussing advantages and disadvantages.
On *rénshēn* day,
Túshàn Sīzhōng, the Right Grand Councilor of the Department of State Affairs, was impeached by a censor
for falsely claiming a high price
when selling sick horses to the government.
The authorities sentenced him to death for stealing from his own office.
However, the Emperor, valuing the overall dignity,
demoted him to Defense Commissioner of Chénzhōu.
On *guǐyǒu* day,
commander Lǐ Shīlín defeated the Xià people at Yǒngmù Lǐng.
Guō Wénzhèn reported
that he had recently learned from captives
that the combined forces of the North and South were preparing to attack Hénán and Shǎnxī.
An edict ordered the Grand Council to prepare defenses.
In the summer, fourth month, on *xīnsì* day,
Wókě, the General-in-Chief of the Jīnwú Guard and Minister of Agriculture, was appointed Co-Administrator of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
The Great Ministry of Agriculture was established,
with a Great Minister of Agriculture, a Vice Minister, and an Assistant Minister.
Traveling bureaus were set up in the three circuits of Jīngdōng, Jīngxī, and Jīngnán,
also handling investigation matters.
On *rénwǔ* day,
Dà Yuán troops attacked Língchuān County.
On *dīngyǒu* day,
Wéiliáng, acting as Administrator of the Traveling Marshal's Office of Línhuái Circuit, was demoted by two ranks
and dismissed.
The method for appointing county magistrates was revised
and reinstated.
On *wùxū* day,
officials mourning parents, awaiting appointment, or serving titular positions were registered
to prepare for autumn defense.
On *dīngwèi* day,
the Traveling Bureau of Military Affairs reported a victory in Huáinán.
In the fifth month, on *wùshēn* day,
Dà Yuán troops were stationed in Xízhōu, Jízhōu, Yìzhōu, and other prefectures.
On *rénxū* day,
Wókě and Shí Quán's armies suffered a great defeat.
On *jiǎzǐ* day,
Wókě was liable to death for his defeat.
The Emperor interrogated and reprimanded him,
encouraged him to perform meritorious service in the future,
and demoted him by two ranks.
On *dīngmǎo* day,
retired officials like Xū Dǐng were summoned to the Secretariat to discuss advantages and disadvantages.
On *rénshēn* day,
Shí Quán was executed.
In the sixth month, on *wùyín* day,
boats were built to transport grain from Shǎnxī,
crossing through Dàqìng Pass to Húchéng.
On *guǐwèi* day,
a general amnesty was proclaimed.
Lǚ Zǐyǔ, the Defense Commissioner of Chénzhōu, committed suicide
for failing to provide military supplies.
An edict ordered that all supervisory officials and officials of the eighth rank and below,
who were in mourning, awaiting appointment, whose term had expired, or who held titular positions,
be provisionally appointed to the Imperial Guard.
The various circuit agricultural bureaus were ordered to devise strategies for apprehending bandits.
On *dīngyǒu* day,
the Hóng'ǎo bandits plundered Liǔzǐ Town,
driving away civilians and post horses.
Commander Zhāng Yǔ pursued them,
recovering what had been plundered.
Wáng Èr, a false military supervisor, occupied Líyáng County.
Commander Wáng Quán attacked him,
recovering the city.
In autumn, seventh month, on *gēngxū* day,
Ànchá'ér, a Dà Yuán general, stationed his troops on the border of Jìn'ān and Jìzhōu.
On *bǐngchén* day,
Wányán Kāi, Duke of Shàngdǎng, recovered Zézhōu.
On *jǐwèi* day,
Wáng Tíngyù of the Guīdé Traveling Bureau of Military Affairs reported a victory over the Hóng'ǎo bandits in Cáozhōu.
On *gēngshēn* day,
the selection method for supervisory officials was set.
Bandits in Héběi encroached upon the borders of Fēngqiū and Kāifēng.
The Grand Council was ordered to defend against and apprehend them.
On *jiǎzǐ* day,
Hèshíliè Yáwǔtǎ, the Grand Commander of Jīngdōng, requested that from now on, officials in the secretariat of the traveling Marshal's office
who committed offenses should be allowed to decide their own punishments.
This was not granted.
On *wùchén* day,
the Hóng'ǎo bandits attacked Shíbālǐ Zhài in Xúzhōu,
and also attacked Gǔchéng and Táoyuán.
The imperial army defeated them.
On *yǐhài* day,
Venus appeared in the sky during the day, crossing the sky
and rivaling the sun in brightness.
On the *dingchǒu* day of the eighth month,
the rewards for the officers and soldiers of the western expedition were set with distinctions.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
a comet was seen in the west.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
the penalties for harboring runaway elite troops and the rewards for reporting and apprehending them were increased and fixed.
The Fan (Tibetan) people of Jīshí Zhōu rebelled and defected to Xià.
Gǒng Zhōu Tíkòng Ní Pánggǔ Sānláng attacked them,
capturing a thousand sheep.
These were offered to the Imperial Kitchen,
but an imperial edict refused them.
As a comet had been seen,
the reign title was changed,
and a general amnesty was declared.
The emperor issued an edict to the prime ministers, saying:
“The amnesty proclamation has been issued.
At this moment, human lives are at stake.
Order the envoys to proceed quickly,
arriving within the scheduled time.”
Bǎ Húlǔ, the Grand Minister of Agriculture, was appointed Cānzhī Zhèngshì.
On the *guǐsì* day,
Yílà Zhòngjiānú, the Duke of Héjiān, and Zhāng Fǔ, the Duke of Gāoyáng, with their troops, recovered Héjiān Fǔ.
On that very day,
the bearers of the victory report finally arrived.
The emperor, noting the obstructed roads
and the reporters’ hardships,
ordered them to be generously rewarded.
The Xià people entered Déshùn.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
prayers for rain were offered.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day, the first day of the ninth month,
the Zǔoyòu Jǐngxún Shǐ were also made Dànyā.
An imperial decree instructed the Shǎnxī Xíngshěng to prepare border defenses.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
Yáwūtǎ requested to lead troops across the Huái River from Shòuzhōu
to raid the Sòng people’s strongholds,
but this was not permitted.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
strategies for governing Huáinán were discussed.
On the *jǐsì* day,
the Sòng people raided Shízhàidiàn in Suìpíng Xiàn,
and again invaded Nányáng.
Jiágǔ Jiǔzhù, Tíkòng of Tángzhōu, defeated them.
In winter, on the *dīngchǒu* day of the tenth month,
the Xià people raided Shénlínbǎo in Déshùn.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
Zhāng Huì of Sòng attacked Língzǐ Zhèn,
but was defeated by Wòlǔ Xùn,
who captured two of his deputy generals.
Sūn Zhòngwēi, Wànhù of Hézhōng Fǔ, seized Abùhān Húlǔlà, the Ānfǔ Shǐ, and rebelled by holding the city.
The Shǎnxī Xíngshěng dispatched generals to suppress the rebellion.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
Cáozhōu was recovered.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
the emperor hunted in the nearby suburbs.
An imperial edict exempted all officials from greeting and escorting him,
and also forbade them from repairing roads,
so as not to burden the common people.
On the *gēngyín* day,
Dù Xiān, the Zhāofǔ Shǐ of Zhāngdé, had his troops moved to Wèizhōu.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
the Dà Yuán army captured Húbìbǎo in Róngzhōu and Línjìn.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
an imperial edict instructed the relevant authorities to patrol and protect the property of civilians fleeing war.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
as over a million officials and common people from Jīngzhào had fled to Nánshān to avoid war,
an imperial edict ordered Wányán Tíng and others, who concurrently held the post of Tóngzhī Fǔshì, to pacify the populace.
In the eleventh month, on the *dīngwèi* day,
the Dà Yuán army swept through Tóngzhōu.
Lǐ Fùhēng, Jiédùshǐ of Dìngguó Jūn, and Ékě, Tóngzhī Dìngguó Jūn Jiédùshǐ, both committed suicide.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
Yáwūtǎ, Zǒngshuài of Jīngdōng, reported the victory of breaking the Sòng army at Línhuái.
On the *wùchén* day,
Púhuā of Dà Yuán Měnggǔ attacked Fèngxiáng Fǔ.
On the *yǐhài* day, the first day of the twelfth month,
the emperor said to the Crown Prince:
“I often reflect on affairs of the state at night;
I must light a lamp to record my thoughts,
and then act upon them immediately in the morning.
You should do the same.”
Hóu Xiǎoshū, Zhìzhōng of Hézhōng, was provisionally appointed Yuánshuài Yòudūjiān with discretionary powers.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
Shǐ Yǒnglóng, Tóngzhī Píngyáng Fǔshì, was promoted to Lónghǔwèi Shàngjiāngjūn,
and granted the title
“Shǒujié Zhōngchén” (Loyal Minister Who Upholds Integrity),
and provisionally held the affairs of the Duke of Píngyáng’s office.
On the *dīnghài* day,
Qīngyí Kě, Zǒngguǎn of Diézhōu, passed away.
His son, Jué, was specially commanded to inherit his post.
An imperial edict instructed the officials of the Jìnshì Jú, saying:
“The Fèngyù and Fèngzhí are all young
and uneducated.
I recall in the past, lecturers were appointed
to daily expound on the ancient teachings of rulers and ministers, fathers and sons,
so that they would know how to serve their superiors.
They should be reinstated.”
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
Tángkuò Fǎng, Tíkòng of Lánzhōu, defeated the Xià people at Zhígūbǎo.
The Dà Yuán army launched a major attack on Fèngxiáng.
In the second year, on the *jiǎchén* day, the first day of the first month of spring,
an imperial edict exempted the morning court greetings.
On the *yǐsì* day,
the anniversary of Emperor Shìzōng’s death,
memorial offerings were made at Qǐqìng Gōng.
Rǔ Lì, the Right Chancellor, requested to retire,
but the emperor personally decreed that he stay.
The Dà Yuán army captured Hézhōng Fǔ,
but Hóu Xiǎoshū, the provisional Yuánshuài Yòudūjiān, recovered it.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
Wányán Nǎilá, Fángyù Shǐ of Shòuzhōu, was stripped of four ranks.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
the emperor instructed the prime ministers, saying:
“Previously, someone spoke of a matter of expediency.
You repeatedly requested to implement it as an imperial decree.
It is enough for an emperor to accept advice;
how can one take credit for others’ achievements as one’s own?”
On the *wùwǔ* day,
Lǐ Quélǘ, Sīfāngguǎn Shǐ, was dismissed for a crime.
The prime ministers requested to keep him in a minor, ceremonial post to restrain him,
but the emperor said:
“These brave and outstanding individuals
must be treated with sincerity.
If you try to control them with schemes,
it will only make them suspicious.
As long as they are not given military authority,
what harm is there in assigning them to external posts?”
Lǐ Quélǘ was appointed Zhōucǐshǐ.
He further said:
“Among the precedents for selling official titles, there are cases where officials in mourning can be reinstated.
This teaches people to be unfilial.
Why was such a decree issued?”
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
the Dà Yuán army again captured Hézhōng Fǔ.
In the second month, on the *jiǎxū* day, the first day,
on the empress’s birthday,
an imperial edict exempted congratulatory ceremonies.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
Chancellor Rǔ Lì attended the court assembly.
He was exempted from bowing,
a couch was placed beneath the hall,
and after standing for a long time, he was granted rest.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
an imperial edict stated: “According to the old system, military officers who committed crimes were no longer employed.
Now, in this time of many difficulties,
talented individuals are hard to find.
Excluding major crimes,
I wish to reinstate those who received penal servitude or banishment, but possess martial skills and are adept at commanding troops,
to be re-employed according to their abilities.
Order the Shàngshū Shěng to deliberate and report.”
On the *dīnghài* day,
a general amnesty was declared.
On the *jǐhài* day,
the siege of Fèngxiáng was lifted.
Shízhǎn Héxǐ was promoted to Jīnzǐguānglù Dàfū,
and rose to Zuǒ Jiānjūn.
He was specially appointed Hǎigǔ Hūshēn Méng'ān of Dàmíng Fǔ.
Wányán Zhòngyuán was promoted to Guānglù Dàfū,
and rose to Yòu Jiānjūn.
He was specially appointed Táowěi Bìlá Méng'ān of Héběi Dōnglù.
Each was granted a golden belt with distinctions.
On the *jiǎchén* day, the first day of the third month,
the Sòng people attacked Rǔyáng.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
an imperial warning was issued to Píngzhāng Yīngwáng Shǒuchún regarding excessive drinking.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
Jí Āwài, Tuīguān of Hézhōng Fǔ, was provisionally appointed Yuánshuài Yòudūjiān,
to take command of Hóu Xiǎoshū’s army.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
the emperor said to the prime ministers:
“If a person has the talent to handle affairs
but their heart is not upright,
they are ultimately not worthy of esteem.”
Chancellor Rǔ Lì replied:
“If their heart is not upright and it is aided by talent,
it is like a tiger with wings,
even ancient sages might not easily discern it.”
The emperor concurred.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
on Chángchūn Jié,
court was exempted.
Shízhǎn Wèixīn, Shàngshū of the Ministry of Revenue, was appointed Cānzhī Zhèngshì,
and concurrently Supervisor of National History.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
tea was prohibited.
On the *rénxū* day,
an imperial edict widely proclaimed the achievements in the Fèngxiáng battle and the corresponding reward levels to all prefectures.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
Wányán Bójia was provisionally appointed Cānzhī Zhèngshì,
and was to oversee the Shàngshū Shěng affairs in Hézhōng Fǔ.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
an imperial edict stated that officials who committed crimes not punishable by death would be dismissed from office.
If they were fortunate enough to be pardoned during an amnesty,
those with talent and ability could be re-employed both within and outside the capital.
In the summer, fourth month, on the day Guǐyǒu at the new moon,
Huòzhōu and Fēnxī County were recovered.
An imperial edict ordered the issuance of blank *xuānchì* (imperial rescripts)
to promote and reward deserving generals and soldiers.
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
the Jīngzhào Nánshān Pacification Bureau was established.
On the day Dīngchǒu,
the late Fèngxiáng Myriad Household, Wányán Chǒuhé, who died in defense of his integrity, was posthumously granted the title of Grand General of Huáiyuǎn
and appointed to the post of Cìshǐ.
His father, Shù, besides receiving the customary rewards for his achievements,
was promoted two official ranks
and his position raised by two grades.
On the day Jǐmǎo,
officials were dispatched to inspect the existing troops of the Hénán Military Governor's Office
and register idle officials, powerful local gentry, their close relatives, and households from Liáodōng and Héběi to serve in the army.
On the day Gēngzǐ,
hunters from Xīshān were recruited for the army.
In the fifth month, on the day Guǐmǎo at the new moon,
the minting of
"Yuánguāng Zhòngbǎo" (Original Light Heavy Treasure) began.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
Hézhōng Prefecture and Róngzhōu were recovered,
and envoys were sent with a summons to recruit Gōng Wǔxiān from Qiánshān.
On the day Yǐmǎo,
the Acting Prince of Píngyáng, Shǐ Yǒng, recovered Huòzhōu and Hóngdòng County.
On the day Dīngsì,
the minting of
"Yuánguāng Zhēnhuò" (Original Light Precious Currency) began,
to be used alongside silver in transactions.
On the day Wùwǔ,
a summons was sent to recruit Yán Shí of Dōngpíng.
On the day Jǐwèi,
Cānzhī Zhèngshì (Assistant Administrator of Governmental Affairs) Yìfū stated:
"Those who were coerced into joining are called 'Zhōngxiào Jūn' (Loyal and Filial Army),
but those stationed along the Huái River often engage in illegal activities.
I request that measures be taken to guard against this."
The Emperor replied:
"The human heart is inconstant;
it depends on how one governs it.
If there is skill in governing,
even distant regions will obey orders,
let alone these people?
Otherwise,
even those by my side would be difficult to guard against.
It is precisely about being open-minded and magnanimous.
If, despite this, peace cannot be achieved,
it is fate."
On the day Gēngshēn,
resident officials and commoners in Hénán Circuit were conscripted into the army.
On the day Xīnyǒu,
the troops of Prince of Jìnyáng, Guō Wénzhèn, were relocated to Mèngzhōu.
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
the troops of Acting Prince of Píngyáng, Shǐ Yǒng, were relocated to Jiězhōu and Hézhōng Prefecture.
In the sixth month, on the day Yǐhài,
the General Commander of Jīngdōng, Yáwǔtǎ, reported victory in Huáinán.
〔一０〕On the day Dīnghài,
the positions of Investigating Censor and Suppressor, established by the Provisional Secretariat, were abolished.
