On the day Wùzǐ,
a discussion was held to dispatch envoys to recruit Lǐ Quán, Yán Shí, and Zhāng Lín.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
an imperial edict abolished the Hézhōng Provisional Secretariat
and established a Marshal's Office.
On the day Xīnchǒu,
Yánzhǎn Xiājiǎ and others, who were remotely appointed as Jiedushi of Jìngnán Commandery, were promoted for their meritorious service in defending Fèngxiáng.
In the autumn, seventh month, on the day Rén'yín at the new moon,
the Xià people invaded Jīshízhōu.
Many monasteries and clans in the Qiāng border region were overrun.
Only the monks Kànbū, Zhāobū, and Sīmò from Sāngbū Monastery,
and the monk Bēnjú and others from Dánà Monastery, resisted and refused to surrender.
An imperial edict awarded these monks the titles of Qiánxiá (Military Commissioner), Zhèngjiàng (Battalion Commander), and other ranks,
and provided them with official salaries.
On the day Yǐsì,
troops were dispatched to guard the salt ponds of Jiězhōu.
On the day Gēngxū,
blank *xuānchì* were issued to promote and reward the surrendered people from various tribes.
On the day Rénzǐ,
the prohibitions on using silver and privately exchanging silver for *bǎoquán* (treasury notes) in market transactions were abolished.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
an imperial decree was issued to the censors, stating:
"Trivial matters are not for the ruler to interrogate,
however, any fraud or malpractice is always related to state governance.
Recently, I heard that the monthly stipends and rations given to court officials and attendants
are often mixed with chaff and dirt.
How could the collected materials by the relevant departments ever contain such things?
Furthermore, the measures for dispensing (grain) are inconsistent.
All these are unacceptable practices,
yet the censors never questioned them.
Must I speak of every single matter?
What use are you then?"
On the day Yǐmǎo,
the Dānfèng Gate collapsed.
On the day Dīngsì,
Gǔjūmén and others of the Yīnpō tribe rebelled and defected to Xià.
Marshal Jiágǔ Ruì dispatched troops to suppress them
and reported victory.
Investigating Censor-in-chief Shī Ānshí spoke of two matters concerning repelling the enemy.
On the day Wùwǔ,
while the prime ministers were having an audience,
the relevant department reported that the former Fèngyù (Imperial Attendant), Wēndūn Tàipíng, had died.
The Emperor was greatly astonished and said:
"I repeatedly wished to bestow a position upon Tàipíng,
but each time it was hindered by affairs.
Now, I had just bestowed it upon him, but he died within a few days.
Is this not Heaven's will?!"
He then turned to the prime ministers and said:
"During the time of Hǎilíng, two imperial guards whispered privately.
One said, 'Wealth and honor are determined by Heaven,'
the other said, 'They are bestowed by the ruler.'
Hǎilíng secretly overheard this
and issued an edict to bestow a fifth-rank position upon the one who said 'bestowed by the ruler,'
thinking that it truly came from him.
However, that person fell ill and ultimately could not receive the appointment.
During the autumn hunt of Zhāngzōng,
〔一一〕he heard that Píngzhāng (Chancellor) Zhāng Wàngōng had passed away,
and sighed, 'When I return, I intended to appoint Wàngōng as丞相 (Chancellor),
but he never recovered.
It is fate.'"
On the day Yǐchǒu,
an imperial edict ordered the registration of resident officials and commoners in Shǎnxī Circuit for military service.
In the eighth month, on the day Xīnwèi at the new moon,
Nàhé Liùgē, the Pīzhōu Expediency Commissioner, and others, led Dūtǒng (Commander) Jīnshān Yánjùn and over a hundred men from Yízhōu,
entered the provincial office at dawn,
killed the Acting Shangshūshěng (Secretariat) Ménggǔ Gāng,
seized the prefecture, and rebelled.
On the day Rénshēn,
an imperial edict rewarded the meritorious service of the Jīngzhào Circuit official army for preserving the various valleys of Nánshān,
with ranks determined by the number of people preserved:
those preserving over a thousand people were promoted one rank;
over three thousand people, two ranks;
over five thousand people, three ranks,
and their official position raised by one grade.
Those who protected them through fierce fighting received an additional rank.
Those who died in battle were posthumously granted these honors.
On the day Jiǎxū,
officials were dispatched with blank *xuānchì*,
announcing generous rewards to recruit Nàhé Liùgē.
He refused the order.
Thereupon, Yáwǔtǎ was ordered to join forces with the troops of the Provisional Administration to suppress and eliminate him.
On the day Yǐhài,
Mars entered the Guǐ mansion,
eclipsing the *Jīshīqì* (accumulated corpse vapor, an astrological phenomenon).
On the day Yǐyǒu,
an imperial edict stated that whoever could capture the rebel leader Liùgē,
besides the established official position,
would also be granted a hereditary *móukè* (myriad-household).
On the day Bǐngxū,
officials were dispatched to various prefectures including Cài, Xī, Chén, Bó, Táng, Dèng, and Yù,
along with local officials from the Sīnóngsī (Ministry of Agriculture), to jointly discuss that:
for commoners who gathered and built stockades to avoid warfare,
and who relied on the local patrol armies,
if there were over fifty households, one *zhàizhǎng* (stockade chief) would be appointed;
for over a hundred households, an additional deputy would be appointed,
and they would first be promoted one official rank.
Those who could pacify the people, suppress bandits, and encourage agriculture would be appointed based on their merits.
In the ninth month, on the day Gēngzǐ at the new moon,
there was a solar eclipse.
The Sòng people entered Shòuzhōu.
Nǚxīliè Púnǎi fought bravely and repelled them.
On the day Rén'yín,
the Privy Council reported the meritorious service of Tíkòng (Controller) Shùjiǎ Cuózǐhàn in defeating the Sòng people.
On the day Jiǎchén,
the Sòng people attacked Nányáng.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
Yáwǔtǎ reported victories at Táoyuán and Huáiyáng,
and also reported Nàhé Liùgē's conspiracy with Lǐ Quán.
On the day Wùshēn,
the surrendered man Sūn Bāngzuǒ returned from Lǐ Quán's army
and was remotely appointed Zhī Dōngpíng Fǔ (Prefect of Dōngpíng Prefecture) concurrently Dū Zǒngguǎn (Grand Commander) of the Shāndōng Xī Lù (Western Shandong Circuit) Army and Horse.
The official army fought fiercely with the Sòng people at Húpō and repelled them,
but Tíkòng Shùhǔ Chūn'ér was killed.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
the pseudo-Dūtǒng Wūgǔlún Sàihàn and Jiágǔ Liúzhù, appointed by Nàhé Liùgē, surrendered.
On the day Jǐwèi,
Shùhǔ Chūn'ér was posthumously granted the title of Yínqīng Rónglù Dàfū.
On the day Bǐngyín,
Zhāyě Húlǔ and others captured the southern city of Pīzhōu.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
Acting Imperial Censor-in-chief Shī Ānshí [一二] and others impeached Prince Yīng, Shǒuchún, for dishonesty.
He was handed over to the relevant department for trial.
Soon after, an imperial edict pardoned him,
but still admonished him.
In winter, in the tenth month, on the day Guǐyǒu,
the troops of Jìnyáng Gōng Guō Wénzhèn and others were moved to Wèizhōu.
On the day Yǐhài,
an imperial decree was issued regarding the acting Bureau of Military Affairs and the Marshal's Offices:
during the months of agricultural downtime, they were to take turns patrolling and hunting,
no more than three times a month.
On the day Dīngchǒu,
the Emperor hunted in the near suburbs.
On the day Jǐmǎo,
the grand ancestral sacrifice (Xiá) was performed at the Tàimiào.
On the day Rénwǔ,
Mars trespassed against the Língtái constellation.
On the day Yǐyǒu,
the Emperor hunted in the near suburbs.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
an edict ordered the stationing of one thousand troops each at Shíháo Diàn, Miǎnchí, [and]
Yǒngníng Xiàn. On the day Rénchén,
Shí Míng of Téngzhōu plotted rebellion [and]
was executed.
On the day Wùxū,
the acting marshals of Tángzhōu and Dèngzhōu reported a victory in Huáinán.
In the eleventh month, on the day Jǐhài,
Xú Fú and others, false supervisors of the Red Scarf rebels, surrendered.
An edict promoted Yáwútǎ one rank [and]
bestowed gold and silk according to their status.
On the day Xīnchǒu,
Commander Yáwútǎ reported a victory at Pīzhōu,
presenting the head of the rebel Liù Gē in a box.
There was a tiger eating people in the district of Kāifēng Xiàn.
An edict ordered one hundred imperial guards to shoot and kill it,
rewarding the successful hunter with twenty liǎng of silver
and bestowing imperial medicine upon the injured.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
three thousand Red Scarf rebels from Pīzhōu surrendered.
Initially, it was proposed to settle them between Chénzhōu and Xǔzhōu.
The Emperor, however, said: "Although these people have surrendered,
their families are still in Héshuò,
and the remaining rebels will surely kill them.
What is gained is little, but those harmed are many.
How can we bear this?
It would be better to send envoys to pacify and appease them,
bestow official titles and rewards, and send them back.
If they are truly loyal to Us,
even if they are in Héshuò, how could they betray Us?
Moreover, the remaining multitudes, grateful for this kindness,
will come to follow and submit."
On the day Wùwǔ,
at the request of Shàngdǎng Gōng Wányán Kāi,
an edict instructed Kāi, along with Guō Wénzhèn, Shǐ Yǒng, Wáng Yù, Zhāng Dào, Lú Zhī, and others, to inspect arable land adjacent to their respective marshal's offices,
as well as land along the northern bank of the Yellow River,
divide it by boundary, and cultivate it
to provide for military provisions.
On the day Xīnyǒu,
the acting Marshal's Office of Gǒngzhōu reported a victory over the Xī Xià people at Huìzhōu.
In the twelfth month, on the first day Jǐsì,
the border troops of the Huái River patrol were moved inland.
On the day Guǐyǒu,
blank official appointments and gold and silver tallies were given to Wányán Kāi as rewards for meritorious service.
On the day Xīnsì,
an edict ordered that local people of Yán'ān serving as county officials and righteous army envoys should be replaced by selected individuals,
and their corvée and taxes should be appropriately reduced.
For the commoners of Pīzhōu who died in battle, each was posthumously promoted one rank.
The commoners of Guīdé, Xúzhōu, Pīzhōu, Sùzhōu, Sìzhōu, Yǒngzhōu, Bózhōu, Yǐngzhōu, and Shòuzhōu who had returned to their occupations or settled in new lands
were exempted from corvée and taxes for two years;
existing households for one year.
Those who had previously supplied Pīzhōu were further exempted for half a year,
while Suīzhōu, Chénliú, and Shíxiàn were exempted for one-third.
On the day Dīnghài,
the Emperor was unwell
and did not hold court.
On the day Wùzǐ,
the Crown Prince led the hundred officials, along with the imperial consorts and princesses, to inquire about the Emperor's health.
On the day Jǐchǒu,
they again entered to inquire about his health.
On the day Gēngyín,
the Emperor passed away in the Níngdé Diàn,
at the age of sixty-one.
When the Emperor's illness became critical,
late at night,
all close ministers had exited.
Only Madame Zhèng, Zīmíng Fūrén of the former court, remained at his side, old in years.
The Emperor, knowing her trustworthy,
decreed to her:
"Immediately summon the Crown Prince to manage the affairs that follow."
His words ceased, and he passed away.
Madame concealed this.
That night,
the Empress and Noble Consort Páng inquired at the sleeping quarters.
Páng Shì was cunning and intelligent,
and often, because her eldest son Shǒuchún was not made heir,
she felt resentful.
Madame, fearing she might cause trouble,
immediately deceived her, saying:
"His Majesty is currently changing clothes.
Empress and Consort may rest a while in another room."
Waiting for them to enter, she quickly locked them in,
urgently summoned the high officials,
and transmitted the imperial will to establish the Crown Prince.
Only then did she unlock the doors to release the Empress and Consort
and announce the mourning.
As the Crown Prince was entering the palace,
Yīng Wáng Shǒuchún had already entered first.
The Crown Prince, knowing this,
dispatched officials from the Bureau of Military Affairs and Imperial Guard officers from the Eastern Palace, Yílà Pú'ā, to assemble over thirty thousand troops at Dōnghuámén Jiē.
Once the deployment was complete,
he ordered four guards to confine Shǒuchún in the attendants' office,
and then immediately ascended the imperial throne before the coffin.
On the day Rénchén,
the imperial will was proclaimed.
On this day,
an edict pardoned all within and without the capital.
In the next year, in the first month, on the first day Wùxū,
the reign era was changed to Zhèngdà.
The deceased Emperor was posthumously honored with the title Jìtiān Xīngtǒng Shùdào Qínrén Yīngwǔ Shèngxiào Huángdì,
and his temple name was Xuānzōng.
In the third month, on the day Gēngshēn,
he was buried in Délíng.
The eulogy says: Xuānzōng, in the late period of the Jīn dynasty,
though lacking the talent to quell chaos and restore order,
possessed the ambition to exert himself and govern well.
Judging from his diligent administration and concern for the people,
the revival of the dynasty was perhaps within reach.
However, why did he ultimately fail?
It was precisely because his nature was inherently suspicious,
he placed great trust in his attendants,
and promoted clerks and scribes.
Harshness became the norm,
and his actions were often inappropriate.
Zhí Zhōng was a chief evil.
How could such a person be a prime minister?
Yet, out of private gratitude for his support in ascending the throne,
the distinction of a clean and honorable court was abolished,
which was extremely contrary to ritual.
Gāo Qí's execution of Zhí Zhōng,
though said to be eliminating evil,
judged by the laws of the Chūnqiū,
could hardly escape the blame of Zhào Yǎng at Jìnyáng.
Being unable to punish him and then appointing him as prime minister
was an error compounded by another.
After moving to Biànjīng,
the northern court's fortunes grew increasingly prosperous,
which discerning scholars surely foresaw.
Yet, he continued to be complacent with residual power,
constrained public opinion,
provoked conflict with the Sòng in the south,
and invited insult from the Xī Xià in the west.
With military strength divided,
achievements could not compensate for the troubles.
Not many years passed
before what was once a daily expansion of a hundred lǐ of territory
became a daily contraction of a hundred lǐ of territory.
How could it succeed?
A second relocation eventually led to the loss of the state.
Is this not deeply lamentable?
Collations and Notes
Annals, Volume Seventeen: Āizōng (Part One)
Āizōng's taboo personal name was Shǒuxù (守緒),
originally Shǒulǐ (守禮),
and also Níng Jiǎsù (寧甲速).
He was Xuānzōng's (宣宗) third son.
His mother was the Minghuì Empress Wáng (明惠皇后王氏),
who was granted the surname Wēndūn (溫敦氏).
She was the elder sister of the Rénshèng Empress (仁聖皇后).
He was born on the 23rd day of the 8th month of Chéng'ān (承安) 3 (1198 CE) at the Yìdǐ (翼邸).
As Rénshèng had no sons,
she adopted him as her own.
During the Tàihé (泰和) period,
he was appointed Jīnzǐ Guānglù Dàfū (金紫光祿大夫).
Upon Xuānzōng's (宣宗) ascension to the throne,
he was promoted to the title of Suí Wáng (遂王),
appointed Mìshū Jiān (祕書監),
and then changed to Shūmì Shǐ (樞密使).
In early Zhēnyòu (貞祐),
Zhuāngxiàn Crown Prince Shǒuzhōng (莊獻太子守忠) died.
The imperial grandson Kēng (鏗) was established as Imperial Grandson and Crown Prince,
but he also died shortly after.
On the jǐmǎo (己卯) day of the 1st month of the 4th year (1216 CE),
Shǒulǐ (守禮) was established as Crown Prince,
and he continued to oversee the affairs of the Privy Council (Shūmìyuàn).
The imperial edict briefly stated:
"A son gains honor through his mother.
Suí Wáng (遂王) Shǒulǐ (守禮), whose position is close to that of the eldest legitimate son,
has his good fortune assembled by the primary consort.
He is hereby established as Crown Prince.
As for the ceremonial rites,
the relevant authorities shall itemize and report them."
On the jiǎwǔ (甲午) day of the 4th month,
following the advice of the Crown Prince's Junior Guardian, Zhāng Xíngxìn (張行信),
he was granted the new name Shǒuxù (守緒).
On the gēngyín (庚寅) day of the 12th month of Yuánguāng (元光) 2 (1223 CE),
Xuānzōng (宣宗) passed away.
On the xīnmǎo (辛卯) day,
he ascended the imperial throne before the coffin, by imperial testament.
On the rénchén (壬辰) day,
an imperial edict declared a grand amnesty,
stating in brief:
"I shall carry out the late emperor's wishes.
Anything that was beneficial to the times and which he desired to implement but could not,
I shall fully adopt and implement.
Regarding state regulations already established,
officials often break the law due to personal feelings,
causing people to suffer unwarranted legal penalties.
Henceforth, if there are existing provisions that are not followed,
those responsible shall be punished for deliberately bringing false charges against others.
Commoners and scholars from remote areas
are permitted to speak frankly about the advantages and disadvantages of military and state affairs.
Even if their words involve satire or criticism and cannot be adopted,
they shall not be charged with any crime."
On the wùxū (戊戌) day, the first day of the 1st month of spring in Zhèngdà (正大) 1 (1224 CE),
an edict changed the reign title to Zhèngdà (正大).
On the gēngzǐ (庚子) day,
the emperor resided in a mourning hut,
and officials began to present their memorials.
Mìshū Jiān (祕書監) and Acting Lìbù Shìláng (吏部侍郎) Púchá Hézhù (蒲察合住) was demoted to Zhōu Cìshǐ (州刺史).
Zuǒsī Yuánwàiláng (左司員外郎) Nímánggǔ Huàshān (泥厖古華山) became Co-Administrator of Zhēuzhōu (楨州).
These two treacherous officials were expelled,
and the grandees and scholars congratulated each other.
Bīnzhōu Jiédùshǐ (邠州節度使) Yílà Shùnà Ābùgòng (移剌术納阿卜貢) presented a white rabbit.
An edict stated:
"When worthy ministers assist me and the harvest is abundant,
this is a supreme auspicious sign.
Why should I care for this?
Let the authorities provide travel expenses,
and release it to its native land.
The Ministry of Rites shall universally instruct the four directions
so that they know my intention."
On the dīngsì (丁巳) day,
an edict ordered the court officials to deliberate on the restoration of Hézhōng Fǔ (河中府).
Lǐbù Shàngshū (禮部尚書) Zhào Bǐngwén (趙秉文) and Tàicháng Qīng (太常卿) Yáng Yúnyì (楊雲翼) and others stated that
the people of Shǎnxī (陝西) were currently exhausted
and not yet able to endure forced labor.
So, the plan was halted.
On the wùwǔ (戊午) day,
the emperor began to hold court.
Dàsīnóng (大司農) and Shǒu Rǔzhōu Fángyùshǐ (守汝州防禦使) Lǐ Qī (李蹊) was appointed Tàicháng Qīng (太常卿),
and concurrently Acting Cānzhī Zhèngshì (權參知政事).
Píngzhāng Zhèngshì (平章政事) Jīng Wáng Shǒuchún (荊王守純) was dismissed
and appointed Pàn Mùqīn Fǔ (判睦親府).
Cānzhī Zhèngshì (參知政事) Púsǎn Wǔjīn (僕散五斤) was dismissed
and appointed Chōng Dàxíng Shānlíng Shǐ (充大行山陵使).
The Empress Wēndūn (溫敦氏) and the Primary Consort Wēndūn (溫敦氏) were both honored as Empress Dowagers,
and their palaces were named
Rénshèng (仁聖) and Císhèng (慈聖) respectively.
All officials entered to offer congratulations at Lóngdé Diàn (隆德殿).
On that day,
a strong wind blew off tiles from the Duānmén (端門).
Chìzhǎn Héxǐ (赤盞合喜) was appointed Acting Shūmì Fùshǐ (樞密副使).
A man dressed in hempen clothes
looked towards Chéngtiān Mén (承天門), laughing and crying.
When questioned,
he said:
"I laugh
because there are no competent generals or prime ministers.
I cry
because the Jīn (金) state is about to perish."
The assembled officials requested that severe punishment be meted out,
but the emperor insisted against it,
saying:
"Recently, I issued an edict allowing commoners to speak frankly,
and they shall not be punished even if their words involve satire."
The judicial authorities only ruled that the imperial gate was not a place for laughing and crying,
gave him a heavy beating with a rod, and sent him away.
Nányáng (南陽) commoner Bù Chén (布陳) plotted rebellion
and was executed.
In the 3rd month,
Yínghuò (熒惑) encroached upon Zuǒzhífǎ (左執法).
On the wùshēn (戊申) day,
Xuānzōng's (宣宗) imperial portrait was enshrined at Xiàoyán Sì (孝嚴寺).
On the xīnhài (辛亥) day,
Chancellor Gāo Rǔlì (高汝礪) passed away.
On the guǐchǒu (癸丑) day,
Xuānzōng (宣宗) was buried at Délíng (德陵).
On the jiǎyín (甲寅) day,
the retired Bīnzhōu Jiédùshǐ (邠州節度使) Zhāng Xíngxìn (張行信) was reinstated as Shàngshū Zuǒchéng (尚書左丞).
As Yán'ān (延安) Commander Wányán Hédá (完顏合達) had achieved merit in battle,
he was granted the Gold Tiger Tally,
appointed Acting Cānzhī Zhèngshì (權參知政事),
and put in charge of the affairs of the Secretariat (Shàngshū Shěng) in Jīngzhào (京兆),
also commanding the two circuits of Hédōng (河東).
In the 4th month of summer, on the guǐyǒu (癸酉) day,
Xuānzōng (宣宗) was interred in the ancestral temple,
and a grand amnesty was declared throughout the empire.
Yínghuò (熒惑) encroached upon Yòuzhífǎ (右執法).
In the 5th month, on the wùxū (戊戌) day,
Píngzhāng Zhèngshì (平章政事) Bǎ Húlǔ (把胡魯) passed away.
On the guǐmǎo (癸卯) day,
Shūmì Fùshǐ (樞密副使) Wányán Sàibù (完顏賽不) was appointed Píngzhāng Zhèngshì (平章政事).
Acting Cānzhī Zhèngshì (權參知政事) Shízhǎn Wèixīn (石盞尉忻) was appointed Shàngshū Yòuchéng (尚書右丞).
Tàicháng Qīng (太常卿) Lǐ Qī (李蹊) was appointed Hànlín Chéngzhǐ (翰林承旨),
and continued to serve as Acting Cānzhī Zhèngshì (權參政).
On the jiǎchén (甲辰) day,
more than ten successful candidates of the Cèlùn Jìnshì (策論進士) examination, starting with Bóshùlùn Chánghé (孛术論長河), were granted their degrees.
Five successful candidates of the Jīngyì Jìnshì (經義進士) examination, starting with Zhāng Jiè (張介), were granted their degrees.
On the wùshēn (戊申) day,
fifty successful candidates of the Cífù Jìnshì (詞賦進士) examination, starting with Wáng È (王鶚), were granted their degrees.
An edict was issued to the Ministry of Punishments (Xíngbù),
and the Dēngwén Jiǎn Gǔ Yuàn (登聞檢鼓院)
was not to be locked or guarded,
allowing those with grievances to make their complaints.
In the 6th month, on the jiǎxū (甲戌) day,
the Prime Ministers and Executive Councilors requested to play polo,
but the emperor, observing the period of heart-mourning, did not permit it.
On the xīnmǎo (辛卯) day,
Consort Túdān (徒單氏) was established as Empress.
The Privy Council Recorder, Yílà Pú'ā (移剌蒲阿), was dispatched to lead troops to Guāngzhōu (光州),
posting proclamations to the military and civilians along the Sòng (宋) border, stating that there would be no further southern expeditions.
In the 7th month of autumn, on the jǐhài (己亥) day,
an edict was issued to all officials, urging each to diligently perform their duties.
On the guǐmǎo (癸卯) day,
the Grand Music (Dàlè) was repaired and restored.
In the 9th month,
Privy Council Recorder Yílà Pú'ā (移剌蒲阿) recaptured Zé (澤) and Lù (潞),
and captured a thousand horses.
In the 10th month of winter, on the wùwǔ (戊午) day,
the Xià (夏) state sent an envoy to restore friendly relations.
In the 12th month, on the yǐsì (乙巳) day,
Zhōu Cìshǐ (州刺史) Púchá Hézhù (蒲察合住) was found guilty
and executed.
On the jiǎyín (甲寅) day,
on the first anniversary of Xuānzōng's (宣宗) death,
food was burned at Délíng (德陵).
The method for appointing county magistrates (xiànlìng) by recommendation
was revised, assessing county magistrates based on six criteria.
Dàsīnóng Sī (大司農司) were established in the eastern, western, and southern parts of the capital region,
and Shǎnxī (陝西),
also handling intelligence collection.
The Dàsīnóng (大司農) in the capital oversaw them all.
Zuǒchéng (左丞) Zhāng Xíngxìn (張行信) said:
"The late emperor decreed within the realm
that punishment would not extend to grandees,
and governance would be based on integrity and shame.
Chancellor Gāo Qí (高琪) had established over a hundred articles regarding crimes committed by officials,
and I request that these be reverted to the old system."
The emperor did not wish to expose the late emperor's faults,
so he implemented them in a modified way.
In the 1st month of spring in the 2nd year (1225 CE),
there was an inauspicious yellow-black celestial phenomenon.
In the 4th month of summer, on the xīnmǎo (辛卯) day, the first day of the month,
Shān Gōng (山公) Wǔ Xiān (武仙) came over from Zhēndìng Fǔ (真定府).
The retired Píngzhāng Zhèngshì (平章政事) and Xīnguó Gōng (莘國公) Xū Dǐng (胥鼎) was reinstated as Píngzhāng Zhèngshì (平章政事),
and put in charge of provincial affairs in Wèizhōu (衞州),
promoted to Yīnguó Gōng (英國公).
On the jiǎwǔ (甲午) day,
due to drought in the capital region,
envoys were sent to review prisoners.
Jūn (鈞) and Xǔ (許) prefectures experienced heavy rain and hail.
On the dīngyǒu (丁酉) day,
Sù (宿) and Zhèng (鄭) prefectures suffered rain damage to their wheat.
In the fifth month, on the day of Dīngchǒu,
due to the severe drought, the Emperor blamed himself,
moved out of the main palace hall,
reduced his regular meals,
and issued a general pardon.
Sū Chūn came from Dàmíng to seek refuge,
and an imperial edict placed Chūn in Xǔzhōu.
In autumn, seventh month,
Púchá Máohuāliǎn, director of the Dūshuǐ Bureau, committed murder,
was spared death but stripped of his rank.
In the eighth month,
Tián Ruì, Marshal of Gǒngzhōu, rebelled.
The provincial army surrounded him.
His younger half-brother, Shígē, killed Ruì and surrendered.
His crime was pardoned,
and he was made Jìngzhōu Jiedushi,
with a hereditary Meng'an position.
In the ninth month,
the peace agreement with Xiàguó was settled.
It was to serve Jīn as an elder brother,
each using its own country's reign title,
sending envoys to offer tribute,
and presenting a state letter addressing Jīn as elder brother.
In winter, tenth month,
because Xiàguó had mended relations,
an imperial edict was issued to the internal and external administrations.
The new military administration reformed the Zǒnglǐng into Dūwèi.
On the day of Jǐyǒu,
an imperial edict concerning the execution of Tián Ruì was issued to the internal and external administrations.
On the day of Guǐhài,
Ǎodūn Liángbì, Minister of Rites; Péimǎn Qīnfǔ, Grand Minister of Justice; and Wūgǔsūn Hóngyì, Palace Censor, were dispatched as envoys to Xiàguó to report on the conclusion of peace,
with the state letter addressing Xiàguó as younger brother.
On the day of Yǐhài,
the Emperor personally instructed the Censors Wányán Sùlán and Chén Guī, saying:
"The Sòng people lightly infringed upon our border.
We attacked them with light cavalry,
hoping they would learn their lesson and establish good relations,
thereby bringing peace to our people.
The Xià people have always been our subjects.
Now they call themselves younger brothers in peace,
and we do not consider it an insult.
If we can achieve good relations,
and ensure the peace of our people,
do we still want to use military force?
You, my ministers, should understand my intention."
Yílà Pú'ā battled the Sòng forces in Guāngzhōu,
capturing several thousand horses,
killing over a thousand people, and then returned.
Wáng Jiānú, a member of the imperial clan, intentionally killed clerk Xiānyú.
Many powerful figures interceded for him.
The Emperor said:
"King Yīng is my elder brother,
yet would he dare to arbitrarily flog anyone?
I am the ruler,
would I dare to harm an innocent person?
At a time when the state is weak,
how many lives are there left?
And yet a clan member, relying on his power, kills a clerk.
Our people will have no lord!"
He specifically ordered his execution.
An imperial edict commanded the relevant authorities to erect a temple of commendation for thirteen loyal martyrs.
Officials and soldiers patrolling the borders of Sùzhōu, Sìzhōu, and Qīngkǒu were forbidden
from arbitrarily killing the "Red-robed Army" that crossed the Huái River.
An imperial edict commanded Zhào Bǐngwén and Yáng Yúnyì to compile the Guī Jìng Wàn Nián Lù.
In the third year, spring, first month, on the day of Dīngsì, the new moon,
Xiàguó sent envoys to offer congratulations.
In the third month,
Shǎnxī experienced a drought.
Xū Dǐng, Grand Councilor, again requested to retire,
but was not permitted.
An imperial edict commanded the Shàngshūshěng to deliberate on reducing expenditures.
In summer, fourth month, on the day of Xīnmǎo,
the Emperor personally offered sacrifices at the Tàimiào.
Chéngguó Fūrén's carriage passed along the imperial road,
in front of the temple.
The charioteer rode on horseback,
and two maids sat inside the carriage,
none dismounting.
An imperial edict ordered them imprisoned and flogged.
On the day of Xīnchǒu,
due to drought,
officials were sent to pray at Jìdú.
On the day of Guǐmǎo,
prayers were offered at the Tàimiào.
Umbrellas and fans were prohibited.
Hénán experienced heavy rain and hail.
On the day of Jǐyǒu,
envoys were sent to review prisoners,
and envoys were sent to catch locusts.
In the fifth month, on the day of Jǐwèi,
there was heavy rain.
Sòng soldiers plundered the territory of Shòuzhōu.
On the day of Guǐhài,
the army in Táoyuán, Yǒngzhōu, suffered a defeat,
with four hundred killed.
On the day of Yǐchǒu,
there was heavy rain.
On the day of Rénshēn,
an imperial edict was issued to Zhào Fǔ and others in Àozhōu,
stating that if they could bring their land to surrender,
they would be employed.
In the sixth month, on the day of Xīnmǎo,
Jīngdōng experienced heavy rain and hail,
and all the locusts died.
On the day of Rénzǐ,
an imperial edict was issued to Gāolì and Gě Bù'ǎi of the Liáodōng Xíngshěng,
to suppress the rebel Wànnú,
pardoning those who were coerced.
In autumn, seventh month, on the day of Gēngwǔ,
Xū Dǐng, Duke of Yīngguó and Grand Councilor, passed away.
In the eighth month,
Yílà Pú'ā recaptured Qǔwò and Jìn'ān.
On the day of Xīnmǎo,
an imperial edict established the Yìzhèng Yuàn in the inner court,
appointing Yáng Yúnyì, Minister of Rites, and others as Shuōshū Guān of the Yìzhèng Yuàn,
with two on duty daily,
to be available for consultation.
In winter, tenth month, on the day of Dīngyǒu,
a Xià envoy came to report a death.
In the eleventh month, on the day of Gēngshēn,
discussion was held to mend relations with Sòng.
On the day of Wùchén,
it was discussed again.
On the day of Jǐsì,
Xià Quán, a loyal and righteous general of Sòng, defected from Chǔzhōu.
Wáng Yìshēn, Zhāng Huì, and Fàn Chéngjìn of Chǔzhōu surrendered with the city.
The four were enfeoffed as Jùnwáng.
On the day of Xīnwèi,
Chǔzhōu was renamed Pínghuái Fǔ.
Because Xià Quán and others surrendered,
an amnesty was granted to all officials, soldiers, and common people from the Sòng territories and the Huái and Chǔ regions,
including their families.
On the day of Jiǎxū,
envoys were sent to Xiàguó to congratulate them on New Year's Day.
On the day of Bǐngzǐ,
Xià reported that military affairs were urgent,
and both sides halted the exchange of envoys.
The Dàyuán army campaigned against Xīxià,
pacifying Zhōngxīng Fǔ.
The Shǎnxī Xíngshěng and Wányán Ékě, Commander-in-chief of Shǎnzhōu, and Gēshíliè Yáwǔtǎ, Commander-in-chief of Língbǎo, were summoned to Biàn to discuss military affairs.
An imperial edict was issued to the two Shǎnxī provinces,
stating that for military affairs, officials below the third rank could be rewarded or punished based on their merits and demerits,
and 250,000 liǎng of silver were allocated for their rewards.
Wányán Lǚxìn, Grand Master of Central Counsel, and others were dispatched as envoys to offer condolences to Xiàguó.
In the fourth year, spring, first month, on the day of Xīnhài, the new moon.
On the day of Rénxū,
the walls of Zhōngjīng City were expanded,
and the outer moat of Biàn City was dredged.
In the second month,
Pú'ā and Yáwǔtǎ recaptured Píngyáng,
seized Prefect Lǐ Qījīn,
and captured eight thousand horses.
In the third month,
officials with effective service were conscripted into the army,
but there were complaints,
so it was not carried out.
Captured men and women from Píngyáng were ransomed with silver,
and those distributed to officers and soldiers were allowed to choose for themselves.
The Dàyuán army pacified Déshùn Fǔ.
Jiedushi Àishēn and acting Prefect Mǎ Jiānlóng died there.
The Dàyuán army again captured Píngyáng.
On the day of Jǐsì,
the summer tax was doubled.
In summer, fifth month, on the day of Dīngchǒu,
discussion was held to seek peace with Dàyuán.
The Dàyuán army pacified Líntáo Fǔ.
Commander Mǎnhútǔmén died there.
The Shǎnxī Xíngshěng presented three strategies: the best strategy was for the Emperor to personally lead the army to battle;
the middle strategy was to move to Shǎnzhōu;
the worst strategy was to abandon Qín and defend Tóngguān.
This was not followed.
In the sixth month, on the day of Wùshēn, the new moon,
Wányán Hézhōu, former Grand Censor, was sent as a peace envoy.
On the day of Bǐngchén,
there was an earthquake.
The planet Venus entered a well.
Candidates for the jinshi degree, from Lú Yà downwards, were granted titles based on their literary compositions and understanding of the classics.
In autumn, seventh month,
the Dàyuán army advanced from Fèngxiáng to Jīngzhào.
Guānzhōng experienced a great tremor.
Shī Ānshí, Minister of Works, was appointed Vice Director of the Right of the Shàngshūshěng.
On the day of Rénchén,
Wūgǔsūn Bǔjí, Grand Censor, and Péimǎn Āhǔdài, Libationer, were concurrently appointed Ministers of Agriculture,
to conscript civilian militia,
encourage wealthy citizens to move into and defend fortified cities and towns,
and also supervise the autumn tax,
so that the people would know the plan for evacuation and relocation.
On the day of Dīngyǒu,
an amnesty was granted to the eastern and western circuits of Shǎnxī,
and the people's rent for this year was remitted.
In the eighth month, on the day Gēngxū,
an edict was issued to officials to dismiss and send home the able-bodied men assigned to defense and the laborers repairing city walls.
Military provisions and levies that were not urgent were temporarily suspended.
On the day Jǐsì,
at the Wànnián Festival,
Tóngzhī Jíxiányuàn Shǐ Gōngyì presented the "Dàdìng Yíxùn" (Great Dìng Bequests),
and Dàizhì Lǚ Zào presented the "Shàngshū Yàolüè" (Essentials of the Classic of Documents).
On that day,
a great wind blew down the chīwěi (ridge ornament) of the Left Yèmén gate,
and damaged the doors of the Dānfèngmén gate.
Frost fell,
and all the grain was damaged.
Lǐ Quán, having returned from Yìdū, re-entered Chǔzhōu and occupied it.
Commander-in-Chief Wányán Ékě and Marshal Qìngshānnú were sent to defend Xūyí.
They fought Lǐ Quán at Guīshān,
and were defeated.
In winter, the tenth month, on the day Xīnyǒu,
Right Shíyí Lǐ Dàjié and Right Sījìan Chén Guī impeached Tóngpàn Mùqīnfǔshì Sāhélián for corruption and bribery,
but there was no response.
On the day Rénxū,
an official of the Wàitái Jiānchá Yùshǐ (Censorate) admonished against hunting.
The emperor was angered,
and accused him of seeking fame and selling righteousness.
An edict was issued posthumously granting official titles to Àishēn, Mǎ Jiānlóng, and others who died in service at Déshùnfǔ.
Lǐ Quán was offered the title of Huáinán Wáng (Prince of Huáinán) to induce him to surrender.
In the eleventh month, on the day Yǐwèi,
at the hour Wèishí,
two white rainbows appeared intersecting the sun.
On the day Dīngyǒu,
a hunt was held in the nearby suburbs.
In the twelfth month,
Lǐ Xī was formally appointed Cānzhī Zhèngshì.
The Dà Yuán army advanced into Shāngzhōu.
On the day Rénzǐ,
envoys were sent to appease Shǎnxī,
and a thousand head of cattle were bestowed upon the poor.
In the fifth year, spring, the first month, on the day Dīngchǒu,
the emperor personally sacrificed at the three ancestral temples.
On the day Gēngchén,
Wányán Máqīnjī, the Zhī Kāifēngfǔshì (Prefect of Kāifēng), was sent as an envoy to Dà Yuán to express condolences.
On the day Bǐngxū,
there was a discussion about attacking Xūyí.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
due to the defeat at Guīshān,
Marshal Qìngshānnú was demoted to Dìngguó Jūnjié Dùshǐ.
In the second month, on the first day Yǐsì,
there was extreme cold,
thunder,
rain and snow,
and all flowering trees died.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
an edict ordered officials to enshrine the statue of Línfú Zǒngguǎn Mǎnhú Tǔmén in the Bāozhōng Miào (Temple of Commendation for Loyalty).
The names of the descendants of those who died for their country were inscribed on the imperial screen,
and they were given official positions according to their talents.
In the third month, on the first day Jiǎxū,
the assembled officials requested that, in accordance with ancestral precedents,
the Shūmìyuàn (Privy Council) be subject to the control of the Shàngshūshěng (Department of State Affairs),
but this was not adopted.
On the day Yǐyǒu,
Jiānchá Yùshǐ Wūgǔlùn Bùlǔlá impeached the close attendants Zhāng Wénshòu, Zhāng Rénshòu, and Lǐ Línzhī for accepting bribes,
but their crimes were leniently pardoned, and they were released.
In summer, the fourth month, on the first day Jiǎchén,
due to the censors' persistent criticism of the three corrupt officials,
the emperor did not hold court for four days.
On the eighth day,
there was a discussion about repatriating the population from Xīxià.
On the day Bǐngyín,
Right Céng Shī Ānshí passed away.
Wáng Yǎor of the Imperial Guards, in a drunken rage, killed his grandson.
The Dàlǐsì (Supreme Court) was to sentence him to penal servitude,
but an imperial order specifically decreed his execution.
In the fifth month, on the day Guǐsì,
Dìngguó Jūnjié Dùshǐ Qìngshānnú was stripped of one official rank
for accepting bribes.
In the sixth month, on the day Rénxū,
due to drought,
an amnesty was granted for miscellaneous capital crimes and lesser offenses.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the day Wùzǐ,
Tóngpàn Mùqīnfǔshì Sāhélián was appointed Zhōngjīng Liúshǒu (Resident Commissioner of the Central Capital),
and acted as Shūmìyuànshì (Affairs of the Privy Council).
In the eighth month, on the day Yǐmǎo,
due to drought,
envoys were sent to pray at the Shàngqīng Gōng (Palace of Supreme Purity).
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
Cānzhī Zhèngshì Báisā was appointed Shàngshū Yòuchéng,
and Tàicháng Qīng Yánzhǎn Shìlǔ temporarily held the position of Cānzhī Zhèngshì.
The expansion of the Guīdé Xíngshūmìyuàn (Branch Secretariat of the Privy Council in Guīdé) was planned,
estimated to require millions of laborers.
An edict dispatched Quánshūmìyuàn Pàn Guān Báihuá to explain the hardship of farmers
and reduce the labor by two-thirds.
Due to inconsistent administration,
the Wèizhōu Shuàifǔ (Commandery of Wèizhōu) was merged with the Shāngōngfǔ (Shāngong Commandery),
and Báihuá was ordered to oversee its planning.
In the ninth month, on the day Gēngyín,
there was sufficient rain,
and wheat was first planted.
In winter, the eleventh month, on the day Xīnsì,
the "Xuānzōng Shílù" (Veritable Records of Emperor Xuānzōng) was presented.
In the twelfth month, on the first day Gēngzǐ,
there was a solar eclipse.
Wányán Máqīnjī was stripped of his title and disgraced
for dereliction of duty as an envoy, but spared from death.
On the day Rénzǐ,
Wányán Núshēn was appointed Shìjiǎng Xuéshì (Academician of the Lecture Hall),
and served as Guóxìnshǐ (Envoy of State Trust).
〔一０〕Due to the severe cold in Shǎnxī,
firewood, charcoal, and silver were granted to the soldiers, with differing amounts.
The Sīzhújiān (Bamboo Office) of Jīngzhào and Fèngxiáng Fǔ returned bamboo,
and it was ordered to be distributed.
In the sixth year, spring, the second month, on the day Bǐngchén,
Shūmìyuàn Pàn Guān Yílà Pú'ā temporarily held the position of Shūmì Fùshǐ (Vice Commissioner of the Privy Council).
Yàozhōu Cìshǐ Lǐ Xīng was granted a jade rabbit and hawk belt and gold articles
for his military achievements.
As Prime Minister Wányán Sài did not perform the duties of the Shàngshūshěng in Guānzhōng,
Píngzhāng Zhèngshì Wányán Hédá was recalled to the imperial court.
Yílà Pú'ā led the Zhōngxiào Jūn (Loyal and Filial Army), with General Wányán Chénhéshàng leading one thousand cavalry, stationed at Bīnzhōu.
Báihuá was dispatched to convey to Pú'ā the intention behind the military deployment.
〔一一〕An edict ordered the Shūmìyuàn to provide fresh horses for the Zhōngxiào Jūn,
and gradually mobilize infantry from the Dūwèisī (Commandery Office) and Zhōngxiào cavalry to garrison Jīngxī.
Báihuá was exclusively assigned to prepare military supplies.
In the third month, on the day Yǐhài,
Zhōngxiào Jūn Zǒnglǐng Chén Héshàng was granted the titles of Dìngyuǎn Dàjiàngjūn (Great General who Pacifies the Distant) and Píngliáng Fǔpàn Guān (Adjutant of Píngliáng Prefecture),
and hereditary mòkè
for his military achievements.
In summer, the fifth month,
Lǒngzhōu Fángyùshǐ Shímò Dōng'ér presented a yellow parrot.
The emperor decreed:
"Presenting rare birds and exotic beasts from outside regions
violates the natural order of things
and wastes human effort.
It is ordered that such presentations should cease."
In autumn, the seventh month,
superfluous military expenses in the Shǎnxī Xíngshěng (Branch Secretariat of Shǎnxī) were abolished.
In the eighth month,
Yílà Pú'ā recovered Zé and Lù again.
In the ninth month,
Táo, Hé, Lán, and Kuàiyuánshuài Yánzhǎn Xiāchī presented two Western horses.
The emperor decreed:
"Your martial skill is extraordinary.
These horses are suitable for battle.
If I were to ride them, how could I fully utilize their strength?
Since they have been presented,
they are already valuable items.
Now I bestow them upon you;
understand my intention."
In winter, the tenth month,
Yílà Pú'ā returned east,
ordering Chén Héshàng to lead the Shǎnxī Guīshùn cavalry to garrison Jūn and Xǔ.
The Dà Yuán army was stationed at the border of Qìngyáng.
An edict ordered the Shǎnxī Xíngshěng to send envoys with sheep, wine, and silk to request a delay in the advance and to seek peace.
In the eleventh month,
envoys were sent to Jūn and Xǔ to select and test men from Shǎnxī who had submitted.
Two thousand soldiers were obtained.
Those with excellent skills were assigned to the Zhōngxiào Jūn,
and the next best were assigned to the Hélǐhé Jūn.
In the twelfth month,
an edict ordered Vice Commissioner Pú'ā, Commander-in-Chief Hégéliè Yáwútǎ, and Acting Privy Council Adjutant Wányán Ékě to relieve Qìngyáng.
The imperial hunting grounds within a hundred *lǐ* of the capital were abolished,
allowing the people to cultivate them.
In the seventh year, spring, the first month,
Vice Commissioner Pú'ā, Commander-in-Chief Yáwútǎ, and Acting Privy Council Adjutant Ékě lifted the siege of Qìngyáng.
Ékě was stationed at Bīnzhōu,
while Pú'ā and Yáwútǎ returned to Jīngzhào.
In summer, the fifth month,
an edict released three thousand captured Sòng soldiers from Qīngkǒu.
Five hundred who wished to remain
were settled in Xǔzhōu,
and the rest were all sent away.
Lǐ Táng and others were granted the *jìnshì* degree for their proficiency in classics, meaning, and prose.
In autumn, the seventh month,
Píngzhāng Zhèngshì Hédá was made acting Shūmì Fùshǐ.
In the eighth month,
the orphans of those who died in service in Shǎnxī were granted salt certificates and silk,
and were also assigned positions according to their talents.
The Dà Yuán army besieged Wǔ Xiān at the old Wèizhōu.
In winter, the tenth month,
Píngzhāng Hédá and Vice Commissioner Pú'ā led troops to relieve Wèizhōu.
The siege of Wèizhōu was lifted.
The emperor ascended the Chéngtiānmén gate to reward the army,
and Hédá and Pú'ā were both granted hereditary mòkè.
Yílà Pú'ā temporarily held the position of Cānzhī Zhèngshì,
and, together with Hédá, administered provincial affairs in Wénxiāng,
to defend Tóngguān.
In the eighth year, spring, the first month,
the Dà Yuán army besieged Fèngxiáng Fǔ.
Shūmìyuàn Pàn Guān Báihuá and Yòusī Lángzhōng Jiágǔ Bālǐmén were sent to instruct the Wénxiāng Xíngshěng to advance troops,
but Hédá and Pú'ā did not move, stating that the opportunity had not yet arisen.
Báihuá was sent again to instruct Hédá and Pú'ā to lead troops out of the pass to relieve the siege of Fèngxiáng,
but again they did not move.
In the fourth month of summer, on the *dīngsì* day, the first day of the month,
a general amnesty was proclaimed.
All military supply taxes for the Jīngxī Lù were completely waived for one year.
For prefectures and counties suffering from drought,
taxes and levies were genuinely reduced.
Dà Yuán forces pacified Fèngxiáng Fǔ.
The two traveling secretariats abandoned Jīngzhào,
relocated the residents to Hénán,
and left Qìngshānnú to defend it.
In the fifth month,
Lǐ Quán's wife Yáng Miàozhēn, due to Quán's entrapment by Sòng,
built a floating bridge north of Chǔzhōu,
intending to avenge Sòng.
Hédá and Pú'ā were dispatched to garrison Háo Hékǒu in the Táoyuán border region
to guard against incursions.
People of Bālǐ Zhuāng in Sòng resisted their commanding general
and welcomed Hédá and Pú'ā.
An imperial edict renamed Bālǐ Zhuāng to Zhènhuái Fǔ.
In the seventh month of autumn,
a Sòng general burned the floating bridge.
On the *bǐngshēn* day of the ninth month,
the Císhèng Gōng empress dowager Wēndūn Shì passed away.
Her dying injunction was that the design of her imperial tomb should be strictly economical.
Dà Yuán forces were stationed in Hézhōng Fǔ.
Qìngshānnú abandoned Jīngzhào and returned eastward.
Hédá and Pú'ā were summoned to Biàn
to discuss leading troops towards Hézhōng Fǔ,
but they were afraid and dared not proceed,
returning instead to Shǎnzōu,
advancing their army to Lěngshuǐ Gǔ before returning.
Dà Yuán forces attacked Hézhōng Fǔ.
Hédá and Pú'ā dispatched Marshal Wáng Gǎn with ten thousand soldiers to relieve it.
In the tenth month of winter,
Right Chancellor Sài Bù retired.
On the *dīngwèi* day of the eleventh month,
Dà Yuán advanced troops to Yáofēng Guān,
〔一二〕proceeding eastward from Jīnzhōu.
The Secretariats discussed waiting for the enemy to tire while they rested,
judging it not yet time to engage in battle.
The Emperor admonished them, saying:
"For twenty years since the Southern Crossing,
the people in various places
have had their fields and homes destroyed,
sold their wives and children,
and exhausted their very beings to support the army.
Now that the enemy has arrived, you cannot meet them in battle;
you only protect yourselves.
Even if the capital city survives,
how can it be a nation?
What will the world say of me?
I have pondered this deeply.
Survival or destruction is a matter of Heaven's will;
I only wish not to betray my people."
Thereupon, an edict was issued for all generals to garrison their troops in Xiāng and Dèng.
On the *jǐwèi* day of the twelfth month,
Empress Mínghuì was buried.
Hézhōng Fǔ fell.
The acting Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, Cǎohuǒ'ékě, died defending it.
Marshal Bǎnzǐ'ékě led three thousand defeated soldiers and fled to Wénxiāng.
An edict pardoned generals and their subordinates,
but Ékě was beaten with two hundred strokes of the rod and died.
Hédá and Pú'ā led all armies into Dèngzhōu.
Yáng Wòyǎn, Chén Héshàng, and Wǔ Xiān all led their troops to rendezvous,
and then camped at Shùnyáng.
On the *wùchén* day,
Dà Yuán forces crossed the Hànjiāng and advanced north.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
the crossing was completed.
Hédá and Pú'ā led their troops to defend before Yǔshān.
Dà Yuán forces split up and advanced towards Biànjīng.
The capital was placed on alert.
That night, at the second watch,
Hédá and Pú'ā led their armies back to Dèngzhōu.
Dà Yuán forces pursued them,
capturing all their baggage train.
In the first year of Tiānxīng (This year was originally the ninth year of Zhèngdà,
in the first month the era name was changed to Kāixīng,
and in the fourth month it was again changed to Tiānxīng.) In the first month of spring, on the *rénwǔ* day, the first day of the month,
there were two solar parhelia.
Dà Yuán forces advanced via Tángzhōu.
Marshal Wányán Liǎnglóushì engaged them in battle at Rǔfén in Xiāngchéng,
and suffered a crushing defeat.
Liǎnglóushì fled to Biànjīng.
Wányán Májīnchū and other departments were dispatched with ten thousand civilian laborers
to divert river water to protect the capital city.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
the Shangshu Sheng and the Bureau of Military Affairs were established within the palace
to facilitate summoning and consultation.
Former Marshal Gǔlǐjiǎ Shílún was appointed acting Military Commissioner of Chāngwǔ Commandery,
and was to manage the affairs of the Marshal's office.
Hédá and Pú'ā led their armies from Dèngzhōu to Biànjīng.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
Diǎnjiǎn Jiágǔ Sāhé was made overall commander,
leading thirty thousand infantry and cavalry to patrol the river crossing.
Túdān Chánglè, acting Director of the Imperial Household Bureau, supervised his army.
Fifty thousand members of military households from near the capital were moved into the capital.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
Dà Yuán forces, having pacified Hézhōng,
crossed the river at Báipō in Héqīng Xiàn.
On the *dīnghài* day,
Chánglè and Sāhé led their troops to Fēngqiū and then returned.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
Assistant Director of the Left Department Xiémǎo Àishí submitted a memorial requesting the execution of Chánglè and Sāhé to rectify military administration,
but it was not followed.
Dūwèi Wūlíndá Hútǔ's army, having come to reinforce from Tóngguān,
upon reaching Yǎnshī, heard that Dà Yuán forces had crossed the river,
and so fled to Shàoshì Shān in Dēngfēng.
On the *rénchén* day,
Wèizhōu Military Commissioner Wányán Xié Niàn'ābù abandoned the city and fled to Biàn.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
the capital city's watchtowers and defensive preparations were repaired.
Dà Yuán forces approached Zhèngzhōu,
united with the Báipō army,
and the garrison marshal Mǎ Bójiān surrendered the city.
Defense Commissioner Wūlíndá Yǎozhù died defending it.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
Dà Yuán cavalry patrols reached the city of Biàn.
On the *dīngyǒu* day,
there was a heavy snowfall.
Dà Yuán forces and the armies of the two Secretariats fought at Sānfēng Shān in Jūnzhōu.
The armies of the two Secretariats suffered a great rout.
Hédá, Chén Héshàng, and Yáng Wòyǎn fled to Jūnzhōu.
When the city fell, they all died.
Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs Pú'ā was captured,
and soon also died.
Wǔ Xiān fled to Mìxiàn.
From then on,
the army never recovered.
On the *jǐhài* day,
Xúzhōu Traveling Secretariat Wányán Qìngshānnú led his troops to reinforce.
Yìshèng Jūn commander Hóu Jìn, Dù Zhèng, and Zhāng Xīng led their units and surrendered to the north.
Qìngshānnú entered Suīzhōu.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
an amnesty was proclaimed at Duānmén.
The era name was changed to Kāixīng.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
Tóngguān commander Lǐ Píng surrendered the pass to Dà Yuán.
On the *rén'yín* day,
Fúgōu residents Qián Dàhēng and Lǐ Jūn rebelled,
killing county magistrate Wáng Hào and his subordinates.
On the *gēngxū* day,
there was a military mutiny in Xǔzhōu.
Marshal Gǔlǐjiǎ Shílún, Niánhé Tóngzhōu, Sū Chún, and others were killed,
and the city was surrendered to Dà Yuán.
On the *rénzǐ* day, the first day of the second month,
Qìngshānnú planned to flee to Guīdé.
At Yángyì Diàn, he encountered Dà Yuán forces.
The Xú commander Wányán Wūlǐ fought bravely and died.
Qìngshānnú was captured,
and was used to appeal to the capital city,
but it did not comply.
Suīzhōu Governor Zhāng Wénshòu abandoned the city and followed Qìngshānnú;
they all died.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
Dà Yuán forces raided Línhuàn,
and acting county magistrate Zhāng Ruòyú died.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
they reached Lúshì.
The armies of the Guān-Shǎn Traveling Secretariat and the Qín-Lán Marshal's office abandoned Tóngguān and moved east.
They encountered them,
and then there was heavy snowfall again,
and they routed without fighting.
Traveling Secretariat Túdān Wùdiǎn
and overall commander Nàhé Hélún were defeated and died.
Wányán Chóngxǐ surrendered
and was beheaded before the horses.
Dūwèi Zhèng Tì killed Dūwèi Miáo Yīng and also surrendered.
Qín-Lán Marshal's Office Administrator Shāng Héng died.
Dà Yuán forces took Suīzhōu.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
Academician of the Hanlin Academy Fēng Yándēng returned from an envoy mission to the north.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
Dà Yuán forces attacked Guīdé.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
the retired Right Chancellor Sài Bù was reinstated as Left Chancellor.
Two hundred thousand military households from the capital were conscripted and assigned to various marshals,
each person receiving one *shí* and five *dòu* of grain per month.
In the third month, on the *dīnghài* day,
the army of the Great Yuán pacified Zhōngjīng.
The Resident-General, Sāhélián, drowned himself.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
Plenipotentiary Minister Báisā was ordered to reside at the Shàngqīng Palace,
and Vice-Commissioner of Military Affairs Héxǐ to reside at the Dàfó Temple,
in preparation for emergencies.
The Great Yuán sent an envoy from Zhèngzhōu to convey a surrender ultimatum.
The envoy immediately produced a national letter and handed it to the translator,
who handed it to the Chancellor.
The Chancellor knelt and presented it,
and the Emperor rose to receive it,
and handed it to the proper authorities.
The letter demanded the surrender of the Grand Academician Zhào Bǐngwén, the Duke Yǎnshèng Kǒng Yuáncuò, and twenty-five other families,
as well as the families of those who had submitted,
Pú'ā's wife and children,
embroiderers, bow makers, and falconers, numbering several tens of people.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
Prince Ékě of Jīng was enfeoffed as King Cáo,
with the understanding that he would be a hostage.
The Duke of Mì, Shú, considering King Cáo to be young,
requested to go in his place.
The Emperor consoled him and sent him away,
not allowing him to go as a substitute.
On the *rényín* day,
Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs Lǐ Qī escorted King Cáo as a hostage.
Adviser Péi Mǎn'āhǔdài and Grand Administrator of the Imperial Treasury Guó Shìróng served as peace envoys.
Vice-Minister of Revenue Yáng Zào provisionally served as Participant in Political Affairs.
The army was divided to defend the four gates.
The Great Yuán army attacked Biànchéng.
The Emperor went out through the Chéngtiān Gate to comfort the generals and soldiers on the west side.
The Chiliarch Liú Shòu spoke disrespectfully,
but an imperial edict pardoned him without question.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
the Emperor again went out to comfort the generals and soldiers on the east side,
personally applying medicine to the wounded under the Nánxūn Gate,
and also bestowing cups of wine.
Gold, silk, and vessels from the imperial treasury were distributed to reward the warriors.
On the *yǐsì* day,
Wáng Ālǘ and Fán Qiáo, Chiliarchs of the artillery corps from Fèngxiáng Prefecture, came to submit.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
three thousand leather carts were constructed,
but were later not used.
A bureau was established to care for homeless captives.
In summer, the fourth month, on the *guǐchǒu* day,
the soldier Lǐ Xīn, for his merits,
was promoted to Ambassador of the Four Directions.
Marshal Liú Yì scolded his son, who died in battle.
On the *dīngsì* day,
Vice-Minister of Revenue Yáng Jūnrén was dispatched with gold and silk to the Great Yuán army to beg for peace.
〔一三〕On the *wùwǔ* day,
more rare treasures were sent to express gratitude for the agreement to peace.
On the *guǐhài* day,
the tomb of Empress Mínghuì was desecrated,
and the coffin was missing.
An imperial eunuch was sent to inspect it.
Only then was it recovered.
Soldiers escorted ten palace women out through the Shuò Gate to receive the coffin and bring it to the city gate.
It was placed in the imperial tent,
and reburied that night.
Zhèng Tì's wife and children were executed.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
the Emperor held a grand amnesty at the Duānmén Gate,
and the reign era was changed to Tiānxīng.
An edict was issued to officials and commoners, both inside and outside the capital,
stating that those who could fully restore prefectures and commanderies would receive graded rewards for their merits.
Gold, silk, wine, and roasted meat were distributed to feast the soldiers.
Imperial meals were reduced,
redundant officials were dismissed,
and palace women were released.
Petitions were not allowed to use the term "saint,"
and "imperial edict" was changed to "decree."
The families of King Hàolì and King Wèishào, who were imprisoned, were released,
and allowed to act as they pleased.
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
officials for the first time paid their respects in front of the Lóngdé Hall.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
the Department of State Affairs was made concurrently responsible for the Bureau of Military Affairs.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
palace women were released,
allowed to take their clothing with them,
while gold and pearls were kept to reward the soldiers.
The curfew in Biànjīng was lifted,
and foot soldiers began to go out through the Fēngqiū Gate to gather firewood and vegetables.
On the *jǐsì* day,
Commander of Martial Prestige Wányán Wùlùn entered the city with the Great Yuán envoy Mòtè.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
the envoy was received at the Lóngdé Hall.
Palace women were released as before.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
the Zhèng Gate was opened to allow men among the common people to enter and exit.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
the Emperor held a grand feast for the generals and soldiers at the Chéngtiān Gate,
and only returned to the palace upon hearing voices of grievance.
On the *yǐhài* day,
an edict was issued to stop submitting memorials.
Xǔzhōu presented cherries.
In the fifth month, on the *xīnsì* day,
tens of thousands of displaced people requested to leave the city,
but Sàibù and Báisā did not permit it.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
Prince Sīliè of Nányáng Commandery was appointed to act as the Department of State Affairs in Dèngzhōu,
and to summon reinforcements.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
sacrifices were offered to Heaven at the Dàqìng Hall.
An edict ordered Báisā to retire.
The four armies surrounding the capital were disbanded,
but Lǐ Xīn did not obey the edict.
On the *dīnghài* day,
the Wěi River was dredged to create a transport canal,
but this was soon abandoned.
Féng Yándēng, for his meritorious service as an envoy,
was appointed Vice-Minister of Rites.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
Hè Dūxǐ, a general of the garrison army from Yùzhōu, led two thousand Western soldiers to reinforce the capital.
Displaced people were allowed to leave the capital.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
there was great cold, like winter.
The Duke of Mì, Shú, passed away.
A great plague broke out in Biànjīng,
lasting for fifty days.
Over nine hundred thousand people were carried out through the gates,
and those too poor to be buried were not included in this number.
On the *guǐsì* day,
Yáng Chūn entered and occupied Bózhōu,
and Judicial Assistant Liú Jūn died there.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
the Emperor ascended the Xiānggé Pavilion,
and openly reprimanded the Chancellor.
On the *yǐsì* day,
the generals and ministers received titles and rewards for defending the city.
In the sixth month, on the *gēngxū* day, the first of the month,
an edict ordered all officials to recommend a great general.
The consensus was Liú Yì,
but he could not be used.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
two hundred soldiers of the Fēihǔ Army seized the Fēngqiū Gate and fled.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
the gates were locked due to the deployment of troops.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
Báisā opened a canal to the east of his private residence.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
imperial horses were inspected,
and the emaciated ones were slaughtered for food.
On the *dīngsì* day,
Fēng Xiān occupied Xúzhōu.
Túdān Yìdōu fled to Sùzhōu,
and appointed Zhāng Xīng to act as Head of the Provincial Government.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
the four gates of the capital were sealed
to facilitate defense.
On the *rénxū* day,
Guó Ānyòng entered Xúzhōu,
〔一四〕killed Zhāng Xīng,
and appointed Fēng Xiān as Marshal,
to take charge of the affairs of the prefecture.
On the *jǐsì* day,
an edict posthumously granted the title of Commander of the Zhènnán Army and Military Commissioner to Commander of the Guards Wányán Chénhéshàng.
A stele for the Temple of Praising Loyalty was erected.
Provisionary Participant in Political Affairs Yáng Zào was dismissed.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
the Biànchéng city wall was repaired again.
Due to the plague,
gardeners, monks, Daoist priests, physicians, and coffin sellers took excessive profits.
The authorities were ordered to double their taxes
to aid in expenditures.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
Chiliarchs Gāo Lāgē and Lǐ Xuān of the Sùzhōu garrison killed Military Commissioner Hésīliè Āhǔ and his son.
They asked Head of the Provincial Government Túdān Yìdōu to act as commander,
but Yìdōu refused.
He led his generals and officials west,
and encountered the Great Yuán army at Gǔshú,
where he died.
On the *yǐhài* day,
Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs Lǐ Qī escorted King Cáo and his son Tóng back.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
Shān Gōng Wǔ Xiān killed the scholar Lǐ Fén.
On the *gēngchén* day of the seventh month, the first day of the lunar month,
there was a fire in weapons.
On the *xīnsì* day,
soldiers beat the *dēngwéngǔ* to beg for General Liú Yì.
On the *guǐwèi* day,
the Right Chancellor of the Department of State Affairs, Yánzhǎn Shìlǔ, was dismissed.
The Minister of Personnel, Wányán Núshēn, became a Grand Councilor.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
Shēn Fú and Cài Yuán, soldiers of the Fēihǔ Army, unauthorizedly killed over thirty Northern envoys, including Táng Qìng, at the guesthouse.
An imperial edict pardoned their crime,
and the peace negotiations were consequently broken off.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
the capital's populace spread rumors of wanting to kill Báisā.
A secret edict was issued to send imperial guards to protect his family.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
soldiers destroyed Báisā's villa.
Xié Niǎn Ābù wantonly killed market people who passed by his gate
to quell the unrest.
On the *dīnghài* day,
heaven was worshipped below the Chéngtiānmén Gate.
Treasures from the imperial treasury and the two palaces were distributed to the soldiers.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
an order was issued to recruit soldiers.
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
civilians were conscripted into the army.
One hundred and twenty civilians from Gǒngchāng went to reinforce.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
the commander of Xùzhōu, Zhòngsēngnú, whose courtesy name was Guó Ānyòng, surrendered.
The attendant Zhícháng Yīnshì and others were dispatched with an imperial edict to enfeoff Ānyòng as Prince Yǎn,
to administer the affairs of the Department of State Affairs for the Jīngdōng and other circuits,
bestow upon him the surname Wányán,
and rename him Yòng'ān.
New recruits who beat the *dēngwéngǔ*
were beaten to death with a staff.
On the *yǐsì* day,
Jupiter, Mercury, Mars, and the Moon converged in the asterisms Zhěn and Yì.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
the Grand Councilor Wányán Sīliè, Duke Shān Wǔ Xiān, and the General Commander of Gǒngchāng, Wányán Hūxiéhǔ, led various generals and troops from Rǔzhōu to reinforce,
with Héxǐ appointed as the Commissioner of Military Affairs,
leading ten thousand soldiers to meet them.
Left Chancellor Lǐ Qī was ordered to persuade them to set out.
Only then did they move.
On the *jǐyǒu* day of the eighth month, the first day of the lunar month,
Héxǐ encamped at Xìnghuāyíng.
An additional five thousand soldiers were added,
and they began to advance and encamp at the old city of Zhōngmóu.
On the *gēngxū* day,
five thousand able-bodied men were dispatched to transport grain,
supplying Héxǐ's army.
On the *xīnhài* day,
Wányán Sīliè encountered the Great Yuán army at Jīngshuǐ,
and his forces consequently collapsed.
Wǔ Xiān retreated to defend Liúshān,
and Sīliè fled to Yùzhài.
The Grand Marshal of Zhōngjīng and Left Supervisor of the Army, Rèn Shǒuzhēn, died there.
Héxǐ abandoned his baggage and fled to Zhèngmén,
where he gathered his troops and entered.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
Héxǐ was dismissed as a commoner,
and his property was confiscated and bestowed upon the soldiers.
The Supervisor of the Army, Chánglè, was demoted to Keeper of the Imperial Seal.
On the *dīngsì* day,
a sacrifice was offered to Confucius.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
private grain was requisitioned.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
the family assets of Túdān Wùdiǎn, Wányán Chóngxǐ, and Nàhé Hérùn were confiscated.
The former Magistrate of Yífēng, Wèi Fán, submitted a memorial stating,
"The commander of Gǒngchāng, Wányán Zhòngdé, is resolute and has far-reaching plans.
Your subject requests to be ordered to summon him."
This was not reported.
On the *wùchén* day,
the prefectural examinations were suspended.
The former Grand Minister of Agriculture, Hóu Zhì, was reinstated as Grand Councilor,
further enfeoffed as Duke Xiāo of the State,
and administered the affairs of the Department of State Affairs for the Jīngdōng Circuit.
On the *jǐsì* day,
Zhì led his troops to Fēngqiū.
The officers and soldiers were about to mutiny,
but Zhì stopped them,
and then returned to Biàn with the masses.
On the *rénshēn* day,
families without soldiers were allowed to stay in the capital.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
Jupiter and Mercury converged.
On the *yǐhài* day,
offices were sold,
and the purchase of *jìnshì* degrees was permitted.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
an edict abolished the requisitioning of grain,
and instead it was obtained through voluntary contributions.
On the *dīngchǒu* day,
Yáng Xīng, a civilian from the capital, contributed assets
and was appointed Prefect of Yánzhōu.
On the *wùyín* day,
Liú Zhòngwēn contributed assets
and was appointed Prefect of Xǔzhōu.
〔一五〕校勘記 (Collated Notes)
本紀第十八哀宗下 (Annals, Volume 18, Emperor Aizong, Part 2)
On the *wùyín* day of the ninth month, the first day of the lunar month,
an edict ordered a reduction in the Imperial Guard.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
soldiers killed the guards at Zhèngmén and fled.
On the *rénchén* day,
Zhāng Kāi, Duke of Shàngdǎng, and Wáng Yìshēn, Prince of Línzī Commandery, and Fàn Chéngjìn, Prince of Guǎngpíng Commandery, were reinstated as Marshals.
The former Grand Censor Wányán Hézhōu was made acting Grand Councilor.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
a notice was posted to summon civilians to sell military provisions for the coming year,
with land rent for upper households treated similarly.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
there was a great thunder at night,
and the Minister of Public Works, Pú Nǎisù, was struck dead.
On the *wùshēn* day of the intercalary month, the first day of the lunar month,

an envoy was dispatched with one iron certificate, six tiger tallies, ten large credentials, one imperial robe with woven golden dragon pattern, one Jade Fish Belt of the Prince of Yuè, and two bows and arrows,
to be bestowed upon Prince Yòng'ān.
His parents and wife were also enfeoffed.
Additionally, ten hereditary proclamations, ten princely proclamations, and ten jade rabbit falcon belts
were given to Yòng'ān,
and those among his allies who were eligible were immediately rewarded.
On the *xīnhài* day,
Zhāng Kāi, Wēnsà Xīn, Liú Yì, and Gāo Xiǎn were sent to lead infantry to guard the grain routes of Chénliú and Tōngxǔ.
The requirement for poor civilians to contribute grain was abolished.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
local guides were recruited.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
arrows were shot into the palace,
with the names of treacherous officials written on them.
This happened twice in two days.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
grain in the capital was requisitioned again,
with Grand Censor Hézhōu, Inspector Túdān Bǎijiā, and others in charge.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
the grain requisitioning envoy and Commander-in-Chief of Cavalry, Wányán Jiǔzhù, because the grain contained weeds,
beat a filial woman to death with a staff at the provincial gate.
In the tenth month,
due to the slander of the former Minister of Agriculture, Lǐ Huàn,
an edict ordered Left Chancellor Lǐ Qī and Vice Minister of Revenue Yáng Zào to be imprisoned,
and they were to be punished for mismanaging military provisions.
Soon, Qī and Zào were both dismissed,
but only Zào's family assets were confiscated.
Huàn then became acting Minister of Revenue.
Soon after, remaining outstanding grain debts were pardoned,
and all those imprisoned for grain-related matters were released.
An edict summoned troops from various circuits,
with a deadline of the first day of the twelfth month for their arrival as reinforcements.
On the *dīngwèi* day of the eleventh month, the first day of the lunar month,
gruel was distributed to the poor.
Grand Councilor Hóu Zhì retired.
The Left Chief of the Ministry of Personnel, Xiémǎo Àishí, due to his words offending a close attendant,
was sent to the authorities,
and soon released.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
a military officer from Wèizhōu openly took rice from the Fēngbèicāng Granary.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
people in the capital resorted to cannibalism.
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
an edict ordered the Cáomén and Sòngmén gates to be opened for commoners and officials to leave and seek food.
On the *rénxū* day,
various generals and chancellors were summoned to discuss affairs.
Prince Yòng'ān led his troops to Xúzhōu,
but Marshal Wáng Déquán closed the city gates and refused entry.
At that time, Liú Ānguó and the commander of Sùzhōu, Zhòngsēngnú, led troops to reinforce.
Upon reaching Línhuàn,
Yòng'ān sent men to hijack and kill them.
He attacked Xúzhōu for a long time but could not conquer it,
so he retreated to defend Liánshuǐ.
The Commissioner Yīn Shìyīng, because Yòng'ān failed to reinforce,
returned to the west of Sùzhōu,
encountered the Great Yuán army,
and died.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
Zhào Wěi, the Marshal of Hé and Xiè and concurrently Military Commissioner of Quánxīngbǎo, seized Shǎnzhōu in rebellion,
killing twenty-one people including the Administrator Ābùhǎnnú Shílà.
He falsely accused Ābùhǎnnú Shílà and others of treason and reported it.
The emperor knew of their injustice
but could not rectify the matter.
He then appointed Wěi as Marshal and Left Supervisor of the Army,
concurrently Military Commissioner of Xī'ān,
and administrator of the Grand Marshal's office.
Wěi soon also defected to the north.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day, the first day of the twelfth month,
due to the urgent and perilous situation,
the emperor sent a close attendant to immediately ask Bái Huá for a plan.
Bái Huá responded with the precedent of Jì Jì entering Qí with Xié,
and was thereupon made Right Administrator of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
an imperial edict ordered a discussion about the emperor personally leading the forces.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
a second discussion was held at the Dàqìng Hall.
The emperor wished to appoint Guānnú, Gāo Xiǎn, and Liú Yì as marshals,
but this did not come to pass.
On this day,
officials accompanying the emperor and those remaining to guard the capital were appointed.
Sài Bù, Right Chancellor and Commissioner of Military Affairs, concurrently serving as Left Deputy Marshal;
Bái Sā, Administrator of Political Affairs and acting Commissioner of Military Affairs, concurrently serving as Right Deputy Marshal;
É Chū, Right Deputy Marshal, concurrently Deputy Commissioner of Military Affairs and acting Administrator for Political Affairs;
Lǐ Qī, Minister of War and acting Left Assistant Minister of the Department of State Affairs;
Túdān Bǎijiā, Left Overseer of the Marshals, acting Commander-in-Chief of the General Headquarters, and others, were to lead the various armies as escorts.
Wányán Núshēn, Administrator for Political Affairs and concurrently Deputy Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs;
Xíniē Ābù, Deputy Commissioner of Military Affairs and concurrently Administrator of Kāifēng Prefecture, acting Administrator for Political Affairs;
Wányán Zhūkē, General Commander of the four sides of the imperial city and Minister of Revenue;
Bǎsāhé, Marshal of the east side of the outer city;
Zhújiǎ Yǎozhù, Marshal of the south side;
Cuī Lì, Marshal of the west side;
Bóshùlǔ Mǎinú, Marshal of the north side, and others, were to remain to guard the capital.
Once the appointments were settled,
the capital city was entrusted to them.
Wèi Fán was promoted to Hanlin Compiler,
and sent to Dèngzhōu to summon Wǔ Xiān to reinforce the capital.
On the *dīnghài* day,
the emperor presided at the Duānmén Gate,
distributing treasury and palace utensils, as well as maids' clothing and other items to the generals and soldiers.
On the *wùxū* day,
Guānnú and Ālǐ conspired to establish Jīngwáng as emperor, but failed.
The court learned of their plot,
but did not pursue the matter.
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
the emperor departed Nánjīng,
bidding farewell to the Empress Dowager, Empress, and various concubines,
and wept greatly.
When they reached Gōngzhǔ Yuàn,
the Empress Dowager sent eunuchs with rice and meat to distribute to all the soldiers.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
they arrived outside Kāiyáng Gate,
where the emperor waved for all officials to withdraw.
An imperial edict was issued to the garrison soldiers, saying:
"The altars of the state and the imperial ancestral temples are here.
You are brave men.
Do not think that because you are not included in the number of those departing,
you will have no merit.
If you guard this place without mishap,
will your future rewards and achievements be less than those of the warriors in battle?"
Those who heard this all shed tears.
On this day,
Wányán Hūxiéhǔ, Marshal of Gǒngchāng, arrived from Jīnchāng.
He reported to the emperor that there were no wells or hearths in the three hundred *lǐ* west of the capital,
making it impossible to go that way.
The plan to travel east was thus decided.
He was made Right Assistant Minister of the Department of State Affairs to accompany the emperor,
who then proceeded to Chénliú.
On the *rényín* day,
they reached Shíxiàn.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
they reached Huángchéng.
Ānchūn, son of Chancellor Wányán Sài Bù, committed a crime
and was executed.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
they reached Huánglínggāng.
On the *yǐsì* day,
the generals requested to proceed to Héshuò,
and the emperor agreed.
In the second year, on the *bǐngwǔ* day, the first day of the first month,
they crossed the river.
A strong north wind blew,
and the rear army was unable to cross.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
Dà Yuán troops pursued and attacked on the south bank.
Marshals Wányán Zhū'ér and Hèdūxǐ died in battle,
and Jiànwēi Commander Wányán Wùlùn surrendered.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
the emperor wept and offered sacrifices to the fallen soldiers on the north bank of the river,
bestowing posthumous official ranks upon all,
and executing Wùlùn's two younger brothers as a sacrifice.
An amnesty was declared in Héshuò,
and soldiers and provisions were gathered with a view to taking Wèizhōu.
Púchá Guānnú, Marshal, led a thousand loyal and filial troops.
Gāo Xiǎn, East Marshal, and Niángē Yǎozhù, Guǒyì Commander, led ten thousand troops as the vanguard,
reaching Púchéng.
On the *gēngxū* day,
the emperor advanced to Ōumágāng.
Píngzhāng Zhèngshì Bái Sā
and Marshal Hésùjiā Wùdǐ arrived later.
On the *xīnhài* day,
Bái Sā led troops to attack Wèizhōu,
but failed to take it.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
news arrived that Dà Yuán troops had crossed the river from Hénán
and reached the southwest of Wèi,
whereupon the army retreated.
On the *dīngsì* day,
they fought at Báigōng Miào.
Bái Sā was defeated,
abandoned his army, and fled eastward.
Marshals Liú Yì and Zhāng Kāi, Duke of Shàngdǎng, also fled
and were both killed by commoners.
Wáng Quán, Liú Yì's subordinate, surrendered.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
the emperor advanced to Púchéng,
then returned to Wèilóu Cūn.
Lǐ Xīn fled from Biànjīng
and was executed.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
following Bái Sā's plan,
the emperor abandoned the six armies at night and crossed the river,
fleeing to Guīdé with Deputy Marshal Hélǐhé and six or seven others.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
the various armies first realized the emperor had departed,
and thereupon dispersed.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
Púchá Shìdá, Grand Administrator of Agriculture, and Wányán Hūtǔ, Marshal, exited the west gate of Guīdé
to welcome the emperor into Guīdé.
Prisoners in the prefecture were pardoned.
All military personnel and civilians were granted one official rank.
Sixteen *jìnshì* finalists, from Wáng Fǔ downwards, were granted official status.
Jíjiǎ Tāshībù, Imperial Attendant, and Túdān Sìxǐ, the Empress's younger brother, were sent to Biànjīng to welcome the two empresses.
Bái Sā returned from Púchéng,
gathered troops at Dàqiáo, but dared not enter.
On the *rényín* day,
an envoy was sent to summon Bái Sā.
His crimes were enumerated,
and he was imprisoned.
His family property was confiscated and bestowed upon the generals and soldiers.
The emperor said:
"You should exert your utmost loyalty,
and not be like this person who misled the country."
Each person was given one *liǎng* of gold.
Seven days later,
Bái Sā and his son Hūtǔlín both died in prison.
Sài Bù, Right Chancellor, retired.
Wányán Hūxiéhǔ, Right Assistant Minister, administered provincial affairs in Xúzhōu.
Guānnú again requested to lead troops to cross the river north,
but Nǚlǔhuān disagreed.
Púchá Shìdá, Prefect of Guīdé and acting Minister of Revenue, and Zhāng Jùnmín, Commissioner of Transport, were sent to Chén and Cài to procure grain,
with Marshals Lǐ Qí and Wáng Bì escorting them.
On the *wùchén* day,
Cuī Lì, Commander of Ānpíng and Marshal of the west side of the imperial city,
along with his confederates Hán Duó, Yào Ānguó, and others, raised an army and rebelled.
They killed Wányán Núshēn, Administrator for Political Affairs, and Wányán Xiéniē Ābù, Deputy Commissioner of Military Affairs.
They coerced troops to enter and meet the Empress Dowager,
and issued an order summoning Wèiwángzǐ Cóngkè to be Liángwáng
and supervise the state.
Cuī Lì then appointed himself Grand Preceptor, Grand Marshal of the Armies, and Director of the Department of State Affairs,
and later proclaimed himself Left Chancellor, Grand Marshal, Director of the Department of State Affairs, and King of Zhèng.
His younger brother Yǐ was made Administrator for Political Affairs,
Kǎn was made Grand Commander of the Palace Guard.
His confederate Bóshùlǔ Chánggē was made Imperial Censor-in-chief,
Hán Duó was made Deputy Marshal and concurrently Administrator of Kāifēng Prefecture,
Zhétóuxī Yán, Yào Ānguó, Zhāng Jūnnú, Wányán Hédá were all made Marshals,
Shī Sù was made Administrator of the Right and Left Bureaus of Military Affairs,
Jiǎ Liáng was made Administrator of the Ministry of War and concurrently Staff Supervisor of the Right Bureau of Military Affairs.
Wēndíhǎn Èrshí, Minister of Works, and Liú Zhòngzhōu, Vice Minister of Personnel, were both appointed Administrators for Political Affairs.
Àotún Shùnqīng, Commissioner of the Privy Council, was made Left Assistant Minister of the Department of State Affairs.
Zhāng Zhènglún, Vice Minister of Revenue, was made Right Assistant Minister of the Department of State Affairs.
Zhāng Jié, Staff Supervisor of the Right and Left Bureaus of Military Affairs, was made Administrator of the Right and Left Bureaus of Military Affairs.
Yuán Hàowèn, Clerk of the Department of State Affairs, was made Supernumerary Administrator of the Right and Left Bureaus of Military Affairs.
Wáng Tiānqí, Staff Supervisor of the General Transport Commission, and Kāng Táng, Assistant Prefect of Huáizhōu, were both made Staff Supervisors of the Right and Left Bureaus of Military Affairs.
Lǐ Yǔyì, Judicial Officer of Kāifēng, abandoned his post and left.
Zhèng Zhù, Principal of the Ministry of Revenue, was summoned but did not respond.
On this day,
Wēndūn Ālǐ, Right Deputy Grand Commander;
Niè Tiānjì, Supernumerary Administrator of the Right and Left Bureaus of Military Affairs;
Péimǎn Āhǔdài, Grand Imperial Censor;
Wūgǔsūn Núshēn, Grand Master of Remonstrance and Administrator of the Right and Left Bureaus of Military Affairs;
Wányán Āsàn, Left Deputy Grand Commander;
Mánggē, Imperial Attendant;
Púchá Qí, Lecturer, all died.
They then presented a submission to the Dà Yuán army.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
Suìbù, a Dà Yuán general, advanced troops into Biànjīng.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
Cuī Lì reviewed the imperial attendants, military personnel, and civilians' children at the Department of State Affairs' headquarters.
He also forbade marriages among the common people
and confiscated the capital's wealth.
The two empresses were unable to proceed due to the turmoil.
