Treatises, Volume 18: Rites, Volume 10: Empress Installation Ceremony; Empress Dowager Installation Ceremony; Crown Prince Installation Ceremony; Crown Prince's New Year's Day and Birthday Congratulatory Ceremony; Crown Prince's Audience with Officials Ceremony
Empress Installation Ceremony.
On the ninth day of the tenth month of Tiāndé 2nd year (1150),
Consort Túdān was installed as Empress.
The day before,
the Yíluan Command (儀鸞司) set up a seat in the Qínzhèng Hall (勤政殿),
facing south.
Seats for all officials were arranged in the court assembly hall.
The Grand Music Director (大樂令) arranged the palace orchestra (宮縣) in the hall courtyard.
The Harmonization of Rhythms Officer (協律郎) set up a banner-waving position (舉麾位) to the northwest of the orchestra,
facing east.
The Gate Keeper (閤門) arranged the ranks of all officials in the courtyard,
following the usual morning court ceremony.
Furthermore, a Master of Ceremonies (典儀) was positioned to the northeast of the ranks,
with two assistant reciters (贊者) slightly behind to the south,
both facing west.
The positions for the Principal and Deputy Envoys for the Investiture (冊使副) were set up outside the hall gate to the east.
Another position for the Principal and Deputy Envoys to receive the imperial edict (受命位) was set up in front of the ranks of officials.
Two tented areas (幄次) for the Imperial Patent (冊) and Imperial Seal (寶) were set up in the eastern antechamber behind the hall,
both facing south.
On that day,
the various Guards led their respective units,
loosely arraying the imperial yellow pennants and fine ceremonial weapons (黃麾細仗) in the courtyard.
The Talisman and Seal Officer (符寶郎) presented the Eight Treasures (八寶) and placed them to the left and right.
The Assistant Minister of Personnel (吏部侍郎) presented the Imperial Patent,
and the Assistant Minister of Rites (禮部侍郎) presented the Imperial Seal Casket.
All were placed on tables.
After this was done,
they moved out to their ranks outside the gate.
The Grand Music Director, Harmonization of Rhythms Officer, musicians, Master of Ceremonies, and assistant reciters each entered and took their positions.
All officials gathered in the court assembly hall at the appointed time,
each taking their place,
and all wearing court attire.
The Chamberlain (侍中) at the appointed time presented a tablet and announced,
"Request the 'mid-strictness' be ordered."
The Palace Aide (通事舍人) led the officials in,
to stand facing each other east and west in the courtyard,
with north being the superior position.
The Principal and Deputy Envoys were then led to stand at the eastern side gate,
facing west.

The Assistant Minister of the Palace Chancellery (門下侍郎) led the Chief Bearer of the Imperial Ensign (主節) and the Bearer of the Imperial Ensign (奉節) to stand under the hall, to the north of the cross-street in the eastern corridor.
The Grand Chancellor (中書令) and Assistant Minister of the Chancellery (中書侍郎) led the officials holding the Imperial Patent,
who presented the Imperial Patent table to stand to the south of the ensign.
The Chamberlain and Assistant Minister of the Palace Chancellery led the officials holding the Imperial Seal,
who presented the Imperial Seal table to stand to the south of the Imperial Patent table,
all facing west.
The Chamberlain presented a tablet and announced,
"All is ready outside."
Fans were requested on the dais.
The Harmonization of Rhythms Officer waved the banner,
and the palace orchestra began to play.
The Emperor, wearing the Heaven-Reaching Crown (通天冠) and Crimson Gauze Robe (絳紗袍),
emerged from the eastern chamber,
with curved and straight flowery canopies (曲直華蓋) and a guard of honor (警蹕侍衞) as in regular ceremonies.
He took his seat,
sitting facing south.
The screen was rolled up,
and the music stopped.
The Palace Aide led the Principal and Deputy Envoys in,
and the palace orchestra played.
The envoys took their position for receiving the imperial edict.

The Chamberlain, Grand Chancellor, Assistant Minister of the Palace Chancellery, Assistant Minister of the Chancellery, and the officials holding the Imperial Patent and Seal stood facing west as before.
All officials formed their ranks,
standing across, facing north,
as in the usual morning court ceremony,
and stood still.
The Master of Ceremonies said,
"Bow twice."
The assistant reciters conveyed the command,
and all officials in their positions, starting from the head of the ranks, bowed twice.
The head of the ranks inquired about the Emperor's health,
and bowed twice again.
A Gate Official (閤門官) led the Acting Chamberlain (攝侍中) out of the ranks to receive the imperial command,
descending to the northeast of the Principal and Deputy Envoys,
and facing west, announced,
"There is an imperial edict."
The envoys moved slightly forward,
bowed and bowed twice again.
The Acting Chamberlain proclaimed the edict, saying:
"You are commanded to hold the imperial ensign and present the Imperial Patent and Seal to the Empress."
After the edict was proclaimed,
they all bowed twice again,
and the Chamberlain returned to his rank.
The Assistant Minister of the Palace Chancellery led the Chief Bearer of the Imperial Ensign to the Principal Envoy.
The Chief Bearer of the Imperial Ensign handed the ensign to the Assistant Minister of the Palace Chancellery.
The Assistant Minister of the Palace Chancellery held the ensign, facing west, and presented it to the Grand Commandant (太尉).
The Grand Commandant received it, becoming the new Chief Bearer of the Imperial Ensign.
The former Chief Bearer of the Imperial Ensign stood to the left and right of the envoys.
The Assistant Minister of the Palace Chancellery retreated to his rank.
The Assistant Minister of the Chancellery led the Imperial Patent table,
and the Assistant Minister of the Palace Chancellery led the Imperial Seal table,
to stand to the northeast of the Imperial Envoys,
facing west,
and in sequence presented them to the Grand Commandant.
The Grand Commandant received both with cupped hands.
The Imperial Patent table was placed to the north,
and the Imperial Seal table was placed to the south.
The Chamberlain, Grand Chancellor, Master of Rites (禮儀使), officials holding the Imperial Patent and Seal, and those carrying the tables,
retreated to the left and right of the east and west brick paths,
standing facing each other.
The Assistant Minister of the Palace Chancellery and Assistant Minister of the Chancellery retreated to their ranks.
The Master of Ceremonies said,
"Bow twice."
The assistant reciters conveyed the command,
and all officials in their positions bowed twice.
After this,
they divided into ranks and stood facing each other east and west.
The officials holding and carrying the Imperial Patent and Seal tables advanced.
The Imperial Patent table went first,
followed by the officer who would read the Imperial Patent.
The Imperial Seal table followed,
followed by the officer who would read the Imperial Seal.
The carrying officials divided to the left and right.
The Palace Aide led the Imperial Envoys to follow.
The ensign bearers led the way.
As the Grand Commandant began to move,
the palace orchestra played.
When they exited the hall gate,
the music stopped.
The Acting Chamberlain exited his rank, ascended the dais,
and reported,
"Your humble servant, the Chamberlain, reports that the ceremony is complete."
Fans were requested on the dais,
the screen was lowered,
and the palace orchestra played.
The Emperor descended from his seat,
entered through the eastern chamber,
and the music stopped.
The Palace Aide led the officials in their positions out in sequence.
After the Grand Commandant and Grand Minister of Education (司徒) reported the completion of their mission,
the ceremony was concluded,
and they returned inside.
Prior to this,

the relevant authorities had already prepared the Grand Commandant's and Grand Minister of Education's respective ceremonial carriages and retinues (革車鹵簿) from outside the gate to the left and right of the hall gate.
When the Principal and Deputy Envoys emerged,
the drums and wind instruments played vibrantly.
The Master of Rites, the officials holding the Imperial Patent and Seal, and the ensign bearers, along with the carriers,
paused briefly with the Imperial Patent and Seal at the Tàihé Gate (泰和門).
The Grand Commandant, Grand Minister of Education, and the officials who would read the Imperial Patent and Seal temporarily retired to their waiting tents.
The Palace Attendant (內侍閤門) led them into the Tàihé Hall (泰和殿).
When they reached their positions below the hall,
the drums and wind instruments stopped.
The relevant authorities had already set up arrangements.
In the Tàihé Hall, the Empress's seat was placed in front of the screen.
A screen was lowered on the dais.
East and west chambers were also set up to the left and right of the seat, slightly to the north.
A position for receiving the Imperial Patent was set up to the south of the western steps in the hall courtyard,
facing east.
Positions for inner palace ladies (內命婦) were set up to the left and right of the hall.
The Grand Music Director set up the palace orchestra in the courtyard.
The Harmonization of Rhythms Officer set up the banner-waving position on the dais.
Positions for the Imperial Patent and Seal were set up outside the gate.
Positions for the officiating officials (行事官) were set up to the left and right of the gate.
Positions for outer palace ladies (外命婦) were set up inside the gate.
On that day,
the various Guards loosely arrayed the imperial yellow pennants and fine ceremonial weapons outside the hall gate.
The relevant authorities set up two screens (步障) on the western steps of the hall.
Fans were set up in front of the screen,
ten on each side.
One red parasol
was outside the balustrade of the western steps.
Positions for presenting the Imperial Patent and Seal (舉冊寶案) were set up in front of the Principal and Deputy Envoys,
facing north.
The Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs (宣徽使) was positioned in the northern chamber,
facing south.
The Ceremony Director (司贊) arranged the positions for the inner and outer palace ladies and below, in rows to the left and right of the brick path in the hall courtyard.
Each rank stood in double rows in different positions, facing north,
with the inner palace ladies in the rear.
The Ceremony Director was positioned to the southeast of the eastern steps,
with two assistant reciters slightly behind to the south,
both facing west.
At dawn,
the officiating officials, the Grand Music Director, and others each took their positions.
The Empress, in her usual attire,
rode in a dragon-decorated shoulder sedan (龍飾肩輿)
to the back chamber of the Tàihé Hall,
with a close guard of honor (近仗導衞) as in regular ceremonies.
The Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs announced,
"The 'mid-strictness' is ordered."
The Principal and Deputy Envoys entered the gate,
and the palace orchestra played.
When the envoys stood in the courtyard,
the music stopped.
The Imperial Patent was to the north,
the Imperial Seal to the south.
The envoys stood behind the tables.
The Master of Rites led the ensign bearers to stand in front.
The officials holding the Imperial Patent and Seal stood to the left and right of the Imperial Patent and Seal tables.
The officials who would read the Imperial Patent and Seal each stood behind them.
The Xuānhuī Shǐ reported,
"The preparations outside are complete."
The Nèishì Gémén Guān led the Empress out of the inner chambers.
Court music played.
The curtains were rolled up.
The Empress descended from the west steps,
with attendants holding screens, umbrellas, and fans accompanying her on both sides.
Upon reaching the bottom of the steps,
she stood facing the location of the imperial chambers in the Qínzhèng Diàn.
The music stopped.
The emissary for the investiture advanced
and stood to the right.
He proclaimed,
"There is an imperial edict."
The Gémén Shǐ and the Nèishì prompted,
"Bow twice."
The investiture emissary proclaimed:
"An edict dispatches Tàiwèi Chén Mǒu and Sītú Chén Mǒu
to respectfully present the Empress with the investiture scroll and seal."
The Gémén Shǐ and the Nèishì prompted,
"Bow twice."
The investiture emissary retreated slightly.

The Zhōngshū Lìng, Shìzhōng, and the officials for holding and presenting the scroll and seal led the bearers, who reverently carried the investiture scroll and seal, to advance in order to the front.
Court music played.
The stands for the scroll and seal were brought up from the east steps
and placed between the front pillars of the hall,
with the scroll stand to the north
and the seal stand to the south.
A space was left in the middle for the official who would read the investiture scroll and seal to stand.
Both the covers and lids were removed,
and the bearers held them,
retreating to stand in the west Xùdiàn.
The officials for holding and presenting divided into left and right, standing facing each other.
The officials for reading the investiture scroll and seal each stood to the east of their respective stands,
facing west.
Once they were in position,
the music stopped.
The Gémén Shǐ and the Nèishì prompted,
"Bow twice."
The official holding the memorial of thanks handed the memorial to the Nèishì standing on the left.
The Nèishì handed it to the Empress.
After receiving it,
she handed it to the Nèishì standing on the right.
The Nèishì held the memorial and stood to the right.
The Gémén Shǐ prompted,
"Bow twice."
After this was done,
the investiture emissary retreated.
Court music played.
The Nèishì holding the memorial handed it to the Gémén Guān
and followed the investiture emissary.
When the deputy investiture emissary reached the gate,
drum and wind instruments played vibrantly as when they arrived.
Upon entering the west side gate,
the drum and wind instruments stopped.
The deputy investiture emissary went to the location of the imperial chambers,
bowed low,
knelt and reported:
"Tàiwèi Chén Mǒu and Sītú Chén Mǒu
have presented the investiture scroll and seal according to the edict.
The ceremony is complete."
He bowed low,
rose,
and retreated.
The Gémén Guān holding the memorial presented it.
A close attendant received it
and presented it for reading.
After it was read,
he retreated.
Initially,
as the investiture emissary retreated
and reached the gate, the music stopped.
The Gémén Nèishì led the Empress up the west steps to the hall.
Court music played.
The umbrellas and fans stopped outside the curtains,
retreating to the left and right Xùdiàn.
The screens stopped at the bottom of the steps
and were rolled up.
The Empress stood facing south in front of her seat.
The music stopped.
The Zhōngshū Lìng went to the south of the scroll stand,
faced north,
and declared,
"Your servant, Zhōngshū Lìng Chén Mǒu,
respectfully reads the investiture scroll."
After reading, he descended from the east steps
and stood on the first terrace outside the railing,
facing west.
Next, the Shìzhōng went to the south of the seal stand,
faced north,
bowed and declared,
"Your servant, Shìzhōng Chén Mǒu,
reads the seal inscription."
After reading, he descended the steps
and stood to the north of the Zhōngshū Lìng,
facing west.
The Nèishì Gémén led her to ascend to the seat.
Court music played.
Once seated,
the music stopped.
The officials for holding and presenting sequentially motioned for the bearers to cover the scroll and seal stands with covers and lids,
and respectfully placed them on the left and right of the hall,
the scroll stand to the east
and the seal stand to the west.
After placing them,
the officials for holding and presenting sequentially descended the steps
and stood behind the Zhōngshū Lìng and Shìzhōng.
Once in position,
they formed a line facing north.
The Gémén prompted,
"Bow twice."
After bowing,
they descended the east steps
and exited the hall gate.
As for the bearers who had placed the scroll and seal stands on the east and west,
they each descended the steps from the Xùdiàn,
and exited the hall gate directly behind the Shìzhōng and other officials,
awaiting their re-entry
to carry the scroll and seal back into the palace.
After the memorial of thanks for receiving the investiture scroll was completed,
the Nèishì knelt and reported,
"The ceremony is complete."
The Gémén led the inner and outer court ladies who were attending to advance in order,
taking their places facing north.
As the head of the line began to move,
court music played.
Upon reaching their positions, the music stopped.
The Gémén said,
"Bow twice."
All the court ladies bowed twice.
The Gémén led the head of the line to ascend from the west steps.
Music played.
Upon reaching the steps, the music stopped.
They advanced to stand in front of the seat,
faced north, and bowed to offer congratulations.
After this,
they descended from the west steps.
Music played.
Upon reaching their positions, the music stopped.
The Gémén said,
"Bow twice."
The Shèrén relayed the command,
and all the court ladies bowed twice.
The Gémén Shǐ advanced to receive the command,
descended from the west steps,
went to the northwest of the court ladies,
faced east,
and declared,
"There is an imperial instruction."
All the court ladies bowed.
The Gémén Shǐ proclaimed:
"Humbly accepting the Imperial Grace,
bestowed with the investiture scroll and seal,
the honor and good fortune are immense,
and the diligence should be redoubled.
Your congratulations are acknowledged."
The Shèrén said,
"Bow twice."
All the court ladies bowed twice.
After this was done,
the Nèishì led the inner court ladies back to the palace.
As the head of the line began to move,
music played.
Upon exiting the gate,
the music stopped.
The Nèishì led the outer court ladies out to their assigned places.
The Xuānhuī Shǐ reported,
"The ceremony is complete."
She descended from her seat.
Court music played.
She entered the east chamber.
The music stopped.
She returned to her chambers.
Court music played.
Upon reaching her chambers,
the music stopped.
She changed into her normal attire.
The Nèishì received the imperial instruction
and summoned the outer court ladies to an audience,
all according to usual protocol.
After the audience,
the Gémén led the outer court ladies to descend the steps,
form a horizontal line facing north.
The Shèrén said:
"Bow twice."
After this was done,
they exited in order.
They returned to the palace
as when they arrived.
The Zhōngshū Ménxià Shìláng, along with the Yǐnjìn Sī, again led the bearers to carry the investiture scroll and seal inside.
They were handed over to the Dūdiǎnjiǎn Sī
and then retreated.
On the day of separation,
the assembled officials,
consisting of imperial consorts, princesses, members of the imperial clan, and others, were
bestowed wine,
offered food,
adorned with flowers,
and had music performed by the Jiàofāng.
The ceremony was like an inner banquet.
On the eleventh day,
court was held at the Yǒngshòu and Yǒngníng palaces.
After the Empress had received her imperial decree,
two days later,
the inner attendants set up a seat in the palace she occupied,
facing south.
On that day, she rose early.
The Xuānhuīshǐ presented a tablet, announcing
"Zhōngyán" (middle preparation).
At dawn,
all the imperial guards and palace women went to the sleeping chamber to welcome her.
The Xuānhuīshǐ presented a tablet, announcing
"Wàibàn" (outer completion).
The Empress, wearing her phoenix crown and ceremonial robe, rode in her carriage.
Inner attendants led the way.
She descended from the west steps and exited.
The imperial guard followed the usual procedure.
Upon arriving outside the palace gate of the Empress Dowager,
she alighted from the carriage.
Screen-fans and imperial guards were arranged as usual.
She entered and stood in the west wing,
facing east.
As she was about to arrive,
the Xuānhuīshǐ presented a tablet, announcing
"Qǐng Zhōngyán" (requesting middle preparation).
After she had alighted from the carriage,
the Xuānhuīshǐ presented a tablet, announcing
"Wàibàn" (outer completion).
The Empress Dowager, in ordinary attire,
was led by the Xuānhuīshǐ to ascend her seat,
facing south.
The Xuānhuīshǐ led the Empress forward.
She ascended from the west steps,
bowed twice facing north,
then advanced and knelt to offer words of gratitude.
She was consoled and bestowed with wine and food,
all in the manner of a family gathering.
When the ceremony was complete,
the Xuānhuīshǐ announced
"Zàibài" (bow again),
and it concluded.
The Xuānhuīshǐ led her to descend from the west steps and exit.
Upon exiting the gate,
the Xuānhuīshǐ announced
"Lǐ bì" (the ceremony is complete),
and she descended from the seat and entered her palace.
The ceremony for presenting the imperial decree to the Grand Empress Dowager.
In the first month of the second year of Tiāndé,
an imperial edict was issued to the relevant officials:
"Choose an auspicious day to present the imperial decrees to Táng Yīnguófēi and Qíguótàifēi.
Furthermore, establish separate palace names for them.
Regarding the ceremonies that should be performed,
the ritual officials are to examine the details and report them."
On that day, at dawn,
the relevant officials each prepared umbrellas and fans.
The imperial guards were arranged as per the regulations.
The Bīngbù (Ministry of War) assessed and dispatched military personnel.
All civil and military officials proceeded to the two palaces to welcome and invite
the Grand Empress Dowagers to enter.
They all proceeded to the Palace of Receiving the Imperial Decree,
entered the imperial tent,
with imperial guards arranged according to form.
Next, the Tàiwèi and others, who were to present the imperial decrees, placed the decrees on tables.
The Sītú and others, who were to present the imperial seals, placed the seals on tables.
All were placed in boxes,
covered with cloths,
and brought to the tent outside the gate of the separate palace.
The Jiàofāng Tídiǎn led the Jiàofāng to enter.
The imperial guards each took their positions.
The Emperor, in ordinary attire, rode in his carriage
to the tent behind the separate palace.
The Tōngshì Shèrén led the Xuānhuīshǐ to present a tablet, announcing
"Zhōngyán" (middle preparation).
He then returned to his position.
A moment later,
he again announced
"Wàibàn" (outer completion).
The tent curtains were rolled up,
the Jiàofāng music began,
the fans closed,
and the two Grand Empress Dowagers emerged from the back tent.
They immediately took their seats,
facing south.
The fans opened,
and the music stopped.
(They separated, moving slightly to the left and right.)
The Tōngshì Shèrén led the civil and military officials to enter from the left,
according to their ranks,
in double rows facing west,
and stood still.
The Tōngshì Shèrén called out
"Qǐjū" (salutation).
The officials performed the salutation according to the usual court practice,
bowing seven times.
After it concluded,
he led the civil and military officials to separate into two groups, standing east and west, facing each other.
The Tōngshì Shèrén and Tàicháng Bóshì acted as ceremonial guides.
The Tàicháng Qīng led the procession.
The officials in charge of carrying the decrees carried the decrees and proceeded.
The Tàiwèi presenting the decrees, the Zhōngshūlìng reading the decrees, and the officials holding the decrees followed in sequence.
Next, the officials in charge of carrying the seals carried the seals and proceeded.
The Sītú presenting the seals, the Shìzhōng reading the seals, and the officials holding the seals followed in sequence.
They all entered through the main gate.
The Jiàofāng music began.
They proceeded to a spot slightly east of the west steps in the palace courtyard,
facing north.
They paused briefly at the cushion seats,
and the music stopped.
The decrees were to the north,
the seals to the south.
The Tōngshì Shèrén and Tàicháng Bóshì acted as ceremonial guides.
The Tàicháng Qīng led the procession.
The officials in charge of carrying the decrees carried the decrees up.
Music began.
The Tàiwèi and others presenting the decrees followed them,
advancing to the cushion seats in front of the two Grand Empress Dowagers' seats.
Music stopped.
(The decrees and seals for the two palaces
were presented simultaneously,
and read simultaneously.)
The officials holding the decrees stood flanking them.
The Tàiwèi presenting the decrees each inserted their hù (tablet),
knelt facing north,
bowed low,
rose,
and stepped back to stand.
The Zhōngshūlìng reading the decrees advanced together,
knelt in front of the decrees and announced,
"I, the acting Zhōngshūlìng, bearing the title of [official title], your servant [name],
respectfully read the decree."
The officials holding the decrees knelt on one knee opposite them and held up the decrees.
The Zhōngshūlìngs each inserted their hù.
After reading,
they held their hù,
bowed low,
rose,
inserted their hù,
held up the decrees and rose,
turned the decree cases eastward at their positions, facing north,
and advanced together,
kneeling to place them on the cushion seats in front of the imperial seats.
The Zhōngshūlìngs and the officials holding the decrees all descended
and returned to their positions.
The Tàiwèi presenting the decrees all descended the steps,
facing east to await.
The officials in charge of carrying the seals carried the seals up.
Music began.
The Sītú and others presenting the seals followed them,
advancing to the cushion seats in front of the two Grand Empress Dowagers' seats.
Music stopped.
The officials holding the seals stood flanking them.
The Sītú presenting the seals each inserted their hù,
knelt facing north,
bowed low,
rose,
and stepped back to stand.
The Shìzhōng reading the seals advanced together,
knelt in front of the seals and announced,
"I, the acting Shìzhōng, bearing the title of [official title], your servant [name],
respectfully read the seal."
The officials holding the seals knelt on one knee opposite them and held up the seals.
The Shìzhōngs each inserted their hù.
After reading,
they held their hù,
bowed low,
rose,
inserted their hù,
held up the seals and rose,
turned the seal cases eastward at their positions, facing north,
and advanced together,
kneeling to place them on the cushion seats in front of the imperial seats, south of the decrees.
The Tōngshì Shèrén and Tàicháng Bóshì guided the Tàiwèi, Sītú, and other officials involved in the ceremony to all descend from the west steps,
and return to their original ranks.
One Xuānhuī Shǐ goes before the emperor's canopy,
bows down,
kneels and memorializes:
"Your subject [name] respectfully requests the emperor to proceed before the two empress dowagers [Liǎng Gōng Huángtàihòu]
to perform the congratulatory rite."
He bows down,
and rises.
The Zànyǐn leads the emperor in a double bow,
and then memorializes:
"Please kneel facing north."
The emperor offers congratulations, saying:
"The heir emperor, your subject [name], states thus and so..."
He bows down,
rises,
and bows again twice.
When finished,
he again memorializes:
"Please have the emperor stand for a moment."
The Nèishì Chéngzhǐ withdraws,
faces west and declares:
"The decree of the two empress dowagers states thus and so..."
The emperor bows twice.
The Xuānhuī Shǐ leads the way,
and the emperor returns to his canopy,
then in ordinary clothes and riding his palanquin returns to the inner chambers,
with guards as upon his arrival.
The civil and military officials below the steps re-form their ranks and stand firm.
The Tōngshì Shèrén shouts:
"Bow!"
All present bow twice.
The Tōngshì Shèrén leads the Tàishī to ascend the western steps,
where he bows down,
kneels, and memorializes, saying:
"We, the civil and military officials, your subjects, [names], prostrate ourselves and say:
Your Highness the Empress Dowager [Huángtàihòu Diànxià], you clearly preside over the ceremony of investiture,
and forever secure the emperor's well-being.
We look up to pray for your longevity and fortune,
to be coeval with heaven."
He bows down,
rises,
descends from the western steps,
and returns to his position.
The Tōngshì Shèrén instructs:
"All officials present bow twice!"
They perform the ceremonial dance,
thrice exclaim
"Long Live!",
and then bow twice again.
The Xuānhuī Shǐ ascends from the eastern steps,
receives the decree, and withdraws.
Approaching the steps, he faces west and declares:
"The decree of the two empress dowagers!"
The Tōngshì Shèrén instructs:
"All officials present bow twice!"
When finished,
he proclaims:
"You, the dukes and others, are loyal, respectful, and devoted.
You promote and cooperate with all your might.
We receive this auspicious ceremony,
with profound gratitude and shame."
After the proclamation,
he returns to his position.
The Tōngshì Shèrén instructs:
"Thank the proclamation,
bow!"
All officials present bow twice,
perform the ceremonial dance,
thrice exclaim
"Long Live!",
and then bow twice again.
The Tōngshì Shèrén leads the officials who are to face north to their respective east and west ranks.
The Xuānhuī Shǐ ascends from the eastern steps,
memorializes, saying:
"Your subjects, the officials, report that
the ceremony is complete."
He descends and returns to his position.
The screens close,
and the empress dowagers rise together.
The Jiàofāng music begins,
they descend from their seats,
and return to the inner tent behind the hall.
The screens open,
and the music stops.
The Tōngshì Shèrén leads the Xuānhuī Shǐ to memorialize:
"Dismiss the guard."
The Zhōngshū Shìláng and others each lead the officials carrying the book-stands up to the hall,
kneel, and place the books on the stands.
Next, the Ménxià Shìláng and others each lead the officials carrying the seal-stands up to the hall,
kneel, and place the seals on the stands.
When finished,
the Tōngshì Shèrén leads them to the Dōng Shàng Gémén,
to deliver them to the relevant department.
The civil and military officials exit in sequence.
The empress dowagers, in ordinary clothes and riding their palanquins,
each return to their respective palaces,
guided as upon their arrival.
The civil and military officials proceed to the Dōng Shàng Gémén to present memorials and congratulate the emperor,
then withdraw.
When the ceremony is complete,
they each proceed to their respective palaces
to receive congratulations from the inner and outer court ladies [nèi-wài mìngfù].
The relevant department has already set up the empress dowager's seat within the hall.
The Sībīn leads the inner and outer court ladies to stand in order, facing north, in the hall courtyard.
The Shàngyí requests,
and the empress dowager, in ordinary clothes, takes her seat.
The Sīzàn says:
"Bow twice!"
All the court ladies bow twice.
The Sībīn leads the head of the ranks to ascend the western steps,
kneels and offers congratulations, saying:
"We, your concubines, [names], respectfully state:
We humbly consider Your Highness the Empress Dowager,
naturally endowed with sagely virtue,
having clearly received a grand title.
All who are under your gaze and brilliance
are overcome with joy and excitement."
She rises,
descends the steps, and returns to her position.
The Sīzàn says:
"Bow twice!"
All the inner and outer court ladies bow twice.
The Shànggōng Chéngzhǐ,
descends from the western steps,
stands east of the court ladies, facing east.
The Sīzàn says:
"Bow twice!"
All present bow twice,
and the Shànggōng then proclaims the reply, saying:
"Receiving this ceremony,
we are profoundly grateful and ashamed."
The Sīzàn says:
"Bow twice!"
All present bow twice,
and withdraw.
They proceed to a separate hall to congratulate the emperor,
also following the ceremony for congratulating the empress dowager,
but without delivering speeches
or proclaiming a reply.
The Ceremony of Investiture of the Crown Prince [Cè Huángtàizǐ Yí].
In the first month of the eighth year of Dàdìng,
the crown prince was invested.
The ritual officials proposed that
the crown prince should ride in a palanquin to Xiánglóng Mén,
with officials of the Eastern Palace [Dōng Gōng] accompanying him,
not riding horses.
Three days before the investiture of the crown prince,
envoys were dispatched on the same day to report to Heaven, Earth, and the Ancestral Temple.
The day before the investiture,
the Xuānhuī Yuàn, leading the Yíluán Sī,
set up the imperial seat in the center of the Dà'ān Diàn,
facing south.
The crown prince's temporary resting place [Huángtàizǐ Cì] was set up outside the gate to the east,
facing west.

Furthermore, temporary resting places for the civil and military officials, the officials performing the rites, and the officials of the Eastern Palace were set up in the east and west corridors outside the gate.
Moreover, the canopy for the investiture documents and seals [Cè Bǎo Wòcì] was set up in the eastern wing behind the hall,
all facing south.
An altar for receiving the investiture documents was also set up south of the horizontal steps in the palace courtyard.
Officials of the Gōngbù and the officials supervising the manufacture of the investiture documents and seals, in official dress,
guided the stands for the documents and seals from the manufacturing workshop,
entered through Xuānhuá Mén,
approximately along with the Xuānhuī Yuàn to present them.
After completion, they were placed in the canopy.
The Dà Yuè Lìng, leading his subordinates,
arranged the musical instruments in the courtyard.
On that day,
the Bīngbù帥 (Minister of War) led his subordinates
to set up the huánghuī zhàng (yellow-plumed imperial guard) inside and outside the gates of the Dà'ān Diàn.
At dawn on that day,
all civil and military officials due to perform duties entered their waiting areas in court attire.
Officials of the Dōnggōng (Eastern Palace) each wore court attire,
rode on horseback from the Dōnggōng with an escort,
dismounted outside the Zuǒ Xiánglóng Mén,
and entered to take their positions.
Tōngshì Shèrén (Secretaries of the Bureau of Transmission) led the hundred officials in groups to stand in ranks,
facing each other east and west.

Next, they led the Shìzhōng (Grand Councilor), Zhōngshū Lìng (Director of the Central Secretariat), Ménxià Shìláng (Vice Minister of the Chancellery), Zhōngshū Shìláng (Vice Minister of the Central Secretariat), and officials carrying the imperial patent and seal
to stand before the curtained enclosure behind the hall.
After a short while,
the imperial patent and seal were brought out from the curtained enclosure,
descended from the east of the Dà'ān Diàn,
and were placed temporarily on a mat in the courtyard.
Once placed,
the officials attending the imperial patent and seal stood behind them.
The Huáng Tàizǐ (Crown Prince), wearing a yuǎnyóu guān (crown for distant travels) and zhūmíng yī (crimson bright robes), emerged from his waiting area,
holding a guī (jade tablet).
The sānshī (three grand tutors) and sānshǎo (three junior tutors) and those below them escorted him,
standing outside the gate.
The Shìzhōng announced,
"Zhōngyán" (middle stage of preparation).
The Fúbǎo Láng (Officer of Imperial Insignia) brought the bābǎo (eight imperial treasures) in through the side gates, east and west,
and placed them to the left and right of the imperial throne.
The Shìzhōng announced,
"Wàibàn" (outer preparations complete).
An Nèishì Chéngzhǐ (Eunuch Bearing Edict) requested the fans;
the fans closed.
The Huángdì (Emperor), wearing a tōngtiān guān (celestial crown) and jiàngshā páo (crimson gauze robe), emerged.
The qūzhí huágài (curved and straight ceremonial canopies) and guards attended him as per regular ceremony.
Whips cracked;
the gōngxuán yuè (palace suspended bells and chime stones music) began.
The Huángdì emerged from the east wing,
took the imperial throne,
incense smoke rose,
fans opened, curtains rolled up,
and the music stopped.
The Diǎnzàn Yí (Master of Ceremonies) led the Huáng Tàizǐ through the gate.
The gōngxuán yuè began;
it stopped when he reached his position.
The shī (grand tutors) and shǎo (junior tutors) and those below followed him in,
standing southeast of the Huáng Tàizǐ's position,
facing west.
The Diǎnyí (Master of Rites) prompted,
"The Huáng Tàizǐ performs a double bow."
He tucked in his guī,
performed the ritual dance,
then performed another double bow,
announced,
"Shènggōng wànfú" (May Your Sacred Majesty enjoy ten thousand blessings),
then performed another double bow,
was led closer to the east,
and stood facing west.
The shī, shǎo, and those below, along with the officials attending the imperial patent and seal,
each went to the eastern rank of the hundred officials.
Music began;
it stopped when they reached their positions.
The Tōngshì Shèrén led the hundred officials to form a horizontal rank, facing north.
The Diǎnyí prompted,
"Bow."
All officials in position performed a double bow,
tucked in their hù (tablets of rank),
performed the ritual dance,
then performed another double bow,
made their obeisances,
then performed another double bow.
Upon completion,
the hundred officials each returned to their east and west ranks.
The shī, shǎo, and those below, along with all officials performing duties, each returned to their standing positions.
The Diǎnzàn Yí led the Huáng Tàizǐ back to the position for receiving the patent.
Music began;
it stopped when he reached his position.
The Shìzhōng, by imperial order,
declared,
"There is an edict."
The Huáng Tàizǐ and all officials present bowed twice,
bending their bodies.
The Shìzhōng proclaimed the edict, saying,
"We hereby invest so-and-so Prince as Huáng Tàizǐ."
They bowed twice again.
The Tōngshì Shèrén and Tàicháng Bóshì (Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices) led the Zhōngshū Lìng to the position for reading the patent.
The Zhōngshū Shìláng brought the patent box and placed it in front.
The official holding the patent knelt, facing west, holding it.
The Huáng Tàizǐ knelt.
After the reading, he prostrated himself,
and rose.
The Huáng Tàizǐ bowed twice.
The Zhōngshū Lìng went to the position for presenting the patent,
offered the patent to the Huáng Tàizǐ,
who tucked in his guī,
knelt to receive the patent,
and handed it to the Yòu Shùzǐ (Right Executive Assistant).
The Yòu Shùzǐ knelt to receive it.
The Huáng Tàizǐ prostrated himself,
and rose.
The Yòu Shùzǐ, with the patent,
rose,
and placed it on a bed.
The Zhōngshū Lìng and those below withdrew and returned to their original ranks.
Next, the Tōngshì Shèrén and Tàicháng Bóshì led the Shìzhōng to the position for presenting the seal.
The Ménxià Shìláng stood to his right, holding the seal box.
The Shìzhōng offered the seal to the Huáng Tàizǐ,
who tucked in his guī,
knelt to receive it,
and handed it to the Zuǒ Shùzǐ (Left Executive Assistant).
The Zuǒ Shùzǐ knelt to receive it.
The Huáng Tàizǐ prostrated himself,
and rose.
The Zuǒ Shùzǐ, with the seal, rose,
and placed it on a bed.
The Shìzhōng and those below withdrew and returned to their original ranks.
The Diǎnyí prompted,
"Double bow."
Upon completion,
the Huáng Tàizǐ was led away.
As he first departed,
music began.
The Yòu Shùzǐ and Zuǒ Shùzǐ led their subordinates
to carry out the patent and seal bed and boxes.
Upon exiting the gate,
the music stopped.
The Shìzhōng announced,
"The ceremony is complete."
An Nèishì Chéngzhǐ requested the fans;
the fans closed.
Curtains lowered;
whips cracked;
music began.
The Huángdì descended from his throne,
returned through the west wing to the rear chambers.
Guards attended him as they had upon his arrival.
Fans opened;
music stopped.
The Shìzhōng announced,
"Jiěyán" (end of restrictions).
The relevant officials, by imperial order,
released the guards and escorts, who departed in sequence.
The Huáng Tàizǐ entered his waiting area,
changed into official attire,
and returned to the Dōnggōng,
with an escort as he had upon his arrival.
Two days after the Investiture,
the Ministry of War set up the Yellow Pennant Guard inside and outside the gates of
Rénzhèng Diàn. The arrangement was entirely
as for Dà'ān Diàn. All officials wore their court robes.
The Crown Prince, in court dress, arrived at his station,
then changed into a yuǎnyóu guān (far-ranging cap) and a zhūmíng yī (scarlet bright robe).
The Assistant Envoys led the officials to the foot of the steps, where they formed ranks,
facing each other east and west.
The Master of Ceremonies led the Crown Prince, holding a ceremonial jade tablet (guī), out of his station,
to stand outside the gate.
The Attendant Censor announced
"Zhong yán (Inner preparations complete)."
After a short while,
he again announced
"Wài bàn (Outer preparations complete)."
The Emperor emerged from the eastern chamber,
took his seat,
and the curtain was rolled up.
The Assistant Envoys led the officials to form a transverse rank facing north.
The Master of Ceremonies announced
"Bài (Bow)."
All seated officials bowed twice,
inserted their ceremonial tablets into their belts,
performed the ritual dance,
bowed twice again,
stood up,
bowed twice again,
and when finished,
separated into ranks.
The Crown Prince entered, holding a memorial,
and stood at the memorial-presenting position.
Waiting for the Director of the Palace Gate to approach,
he knelt on one knee and held up the memorial.
The Director of the Palace Gate received the memorial.
The Crown Prince prostrated himself,
rose,
and the Master of Ceremonies announced
"Zài bài (Bow twice)."
He inserted his ceremonial jade tablet,
performed the ritual dance,
and bowed twice again.
After the memorial had been read,
the Attendant Censor, having received the Imperial order, withdrew and declared
"Yǒu zhì (There is an Imperial decree)."
The Master of Ceremonies announced
"Zài bài (Bow twice)."
He rose,
bowed deeply,
and after the Attendant Censor finished proclaiming,
the Master of Ceremonies announced
"Zài bài (Bow twice)."
He inserted his ceremonial jade tablet,
performed the ritual dance,
and bowed twice again.
The Crown Prince was led to withdraw.
The Attendant Censor announced
"Lǐ bì (The ceremony is complete)."
The fans were closed,
the whip cracked,
and the Emperor entered the western chamber,
returning to the inner palace.
The Imperial Guard remained as before.
The Attendant Censor announced
"Jiě yán (Preparations are lifted)."
The guard was dismissed,
and the officials exited in order.
Two days later,
the officials presented memorials of congratulation,
following the usual custom.
New Year's Day and Birthday Rites for the Crown Prince to receive congratulations.
In the second year of Dàdìng,
Shìzōng ordered the relevant department to deliberate on the rites for Imperial Princes, officials, consorts, and titled ladies to pay respects to the Crown Prince.
The department consulted the old rites of Táng and Sòng,
and proposed that Imperial Princes and members of the Imperial Clan of the first rank congratulate the Crown Prince
according to the rites for receiving congratulations after the Investiture.
However, the Táng rites for New Year's Day also included the passage about descending the steps to see paternal uncles and returning the double bow of the officials,
and there were no rites for consorts and titled ladies to see the Crown Prince.
Upon examining the extant legal texts,
it was found that when officials who ought to show respect met,
whether there was a great difference in status,
or whether they were elders, juniors, or relatives,
they were permitted to follow private etiquette.
Henceforth, if one were to await the Crown Prince in the Eastern Palace
in informal attire,
then a private reception would be appropriate.
If those below the Three Mentors,
on the occasion of the Crown Prince's birthday,
were in the Imperial presence,
they should await the Crown Prince's completion of the initial wine offering.
All officials would then bow twice towards the Crown Prince.
The head of the rank would kneel and offer wine,
and bow twice again.
If wine were bestowed,
one should kneel in the hall and drink it,
then bow twice again.
This was established as a fixed custom,
and orders were given to follow it.
On the last day of the twelfth month,
the Crown Prince presented a memorial, stating:
"According to ritual texts,
Imperial Princes and Imperial Clan members of the first rank all bow and prostrate facing north,
while I merely return a greeting.
Although it is said to 'honor the Imperial lineage,'
it is truly unsettling in the context of respect for elders and juniors.
At that time, the decree was swiftly promulgated, and I did not have the chance to express my humility.
Tomorrow is New Year's Day,
and the relevant department will perform this rite.
I humbly hope for Your Sacred Benevolence to permit me to return the bow,
so as to foster the virtues of kinship and friendly affection."
The Emperor granted his request,
and ordered the Secretariat-Chancellery to promulgate it to the relevant departments.
If it was the Crown Prince's birthday,
he would wear court dress.
To the left, outside the railing of the elevated terrace,
he would first bow twice.
The two palace gate officials would bow in unison and enter inside the railing,
kneel and bow.
After the prayer was completed,
he would proceed to bow,
rise,
return to his position,
bow twice,
and bow twice again.
He would receive the wine offered from the terrace,
retreat and kneel,
wait for the drinking to be completed,
receive the cup,
return to his position,
pass the terrace to the attendants,
and bow twice.
The Grand Minister of the Court of Imperial Accoutrements would offer wine.
The Emperor would personally bestow the wine.
He would receive the cup, retreat slightly, and kneel to drink.
When finished,
the Grand Minister of the Court of Imperial Accoutrements would receive the cup.
He would return to his position and bow twice,
then bow and enter inside the railing again,
kneel and insert his ceremonial tablet into his belt.
After receiving the bestowed items,
he would withdraw his tablet,
rise,
return to his position,
bow twice,
retreat to change clothes,
enter the hall slightly to the east,
and stand facing west.
The Imperial Consorts and others would advance to offer birthday wine.
The Crown Prince would kneel,
and the Imperial Consorts and others would also kneel.
After drinking,
each would bow twice.
When all officials offered congratulations,
on that day, at dawn,
they all gathered outside the gate in court attire.
The Shǎo Zhānshì奏
"requested an inner preparation,"
and then requested
"an outer readiness."
The Diǎnyí 引 escorted [the Crown Prince] to ascend to his seat.
The civil and military palace officials entered and stood in the courtyard in two rows facing north.
The Diǎnyí 曰
"Bow twice,"
and all officials present bowed twice.
The head of the cohort stepped forward slightly, knelt, and奏
"May the first day of the year bring good fortune."
On a birthday, they would say
"We celebrate this auspicious day of your birth,"
"Humbly wishing His Royal Highness the Crown Prince a thousand years of blessings and longevity."
After the congratulations, they returned to their positions.
The Diǎnyí 曰
"Bow twice,"
and all palace officials bowed twice.
He [the Crown Prince] received them seated,
and they stood in two lines, east and west.
Next, the Three Grand Tutors of the Eastern Palace were led onto the hall,
and the Three Junior Tutors outside the hall pillars,
standing facing north, with the east as the superior position.
The Crown Prince went to the south-facing mat seat.
The Diǎnyí 曰
"Bow twice,"
and the Tutors and Junior Tutors all bowed twice.
The head of the cohort offered congratulations as before,
then returned to his position.
An attendant poured a cup of wine,
and the head of the cohort respectfully presented it.
Music played.
After drinking,
the music stopped.
After reciprocally encouraging the Tutors and Junior Tutors,
each returned to their position.
The Diǎnyí 贊 prompted the Tutors and Junior Tutors to bow twice,
and the Crown Prince returned the bow.
The Tutors and Junior Tutors exited,
and the Crown Prince took his seat.
Next, the Imperial Princes were led into the railing enclosure,
First-rank imperial clansmen outside the railing enclosure,
and the remaining imperial clansmen stood in ordered ranks in the courtyard.
They bowed to offer congratulations and present wine according to the previous ceremony.
After the Crown Prince returned the bow,
he took his seat.
Next, the Three Grand Tutors, Three Grand Ministers, and Chief Councilors attending court were led onto the hall,
officials of the third rank and above on the exposed steps,
and those of the fourth rank and below in the courtyard,
facing north.
Within each rank, they stood in two rows, with the east as the superior position.
The Crown Prince went to the mat seat.
The Diǎnyí 曰
"Bow twice,"
and everyone, high and low, bowed twice.
After this,
the head of the cohort stepped forward slightly to offer congratulations,
then returned to his position.
An attendant poured a cup of wine,
and the head of the cohort respectfully presented it.
Music played.
After drinking,
the music stopped.
If there were presentations, they followed the usual ceremony.
After reciprocally encouraging the Three Grand Tutors and Three Grand Ministers,
for the rest of the officials in the hall, the attendants circulated wine on trays.
After drinking,
the Diǎnyí 曰
"Bow twice,"
and everyone, high and low, bowed twice.
Then [the Crown Prince] returned the bow,
and the officials were led out in sequence.
The Shǎo Zhānshì knelt and奏
"The ceremony is complete."
From then on, the annual congratulations became a fixed system.
Ceremony for the Crown Prince meeting officials.
The Three Grand Tutors and Three Grand Ministers, within the railing enclosure, faced north and bowed.
The head of the cohort stepped forward slightly to greet him,
and the Crown Prince moved forward slightly from his seat,
standing directly south,
and returned the bow.
The Chief Councilors and First-rank executive officials knocked on the railing, faced north, and bowed.
The return of the bow was as before.
Second-rank executive officials, outside the railing enclosure and slightly to the south, bowed.
The Crown Prince rose and bowed.
Third-rank executive officials, on the exposed steps slightly to the south, bowed.
The Crown Prince bowed from his seat.
Fourth-rank and lower executive officials, in the courtyard, bowed,
knelt to greet him,
and the Crown Prince received them seated.
The Tàizǐ Tàishī, Tàifù, and Tàibǎo were the same as the Three Grand Tutors attending court.
The Three Junior Tutors of the Eastern Palace were the same as the second-rank officials attending court.
The Zhānshì and those below,
all stood in the courtyard facing north.
Within each rank, they stood in two rows, with the east as the superior position.
They bowed twice.
The head of the cohort stepped forward slightly to greet him,
〔一０〕and bowed twice again.
The Crown Prince received them seated.
This was established in the second year of Dàdìng.
In the seventh year,
it was stipulated
that when the Crown Prince attended court,
he was permitted to meet with Imperial Princes and Chief Councilors.
Other officials and imperial clansmen were to avoid him.
Later, he was also permitted to meet with the Púmìshǐ Fù, Yùshǐ Dàfū, Pàn Zōngzhèng, and the Three Grand Tutors of the Eastern Palace.
In the ninth year,
it was stipulated
that whenever the Crown Prince went out,
a mat seat would be set up three lǐ outside the capital gate.
The Three Grand Ministers, Chief Councilors, and those below would stand in court attire in two rows.
The Crown Prince would be in informal attire.
The Three Grand Ministers, Chief Councilors, and those below would bow.
The head of the cohort would offer a greeting, saying
"May the Crown Prince enjoy ten thousand blessings!"
They would bow twice,
and the Crown Prince would return the bow,

The welcoming and farewell ceremonies were the same.

Again, the deputy envoy bowed.

Arrangements for the casual banquet.
The Huángdì (皇帝) ascended the imperial seat.
After the whip-cracking and time announcement,
the officials in front of the hall performed a small audience ceremony,
and moved to their standing positions.
The officials and guest envoys were led in from the left,

Audience of Farewell ceremony.
The Huángdì (皇帝) ascended the imperial seat.
After the whip-cracking and time announcement,

and moved to their standing positions.

The deputy envoys were led up the open steps from the left,
